1.summary: God creates the heavens and the earth in six days, bringing light, sky, land, and living creatures into being by his word, and finally makes man in his own image to rule over creation. On the seventh day God rests and blesses the day.

segments.title: Creation of light
segments.gist: God creates the heavens and earth, then separates light from darkness on the first day.

segments.title: Firmament divides waters
segments.gist: God makes a firmament to divide the waters above from the waters below, calling it Heaven.

segments.title: Dry land and plants
segments.gist: God gathers the waters, brings forth dry land, and creates plants yielding seed and fruit.

segments.title: Sun, moon, and stars
segments.gist: God creates lights in the firmament to divide day and night and to rule over the day and night.

segments.title: Sea creatures and birds
segments.gist: God creates great sea creatures, every living thing in the waters, and every winged bird, then land animals.

segments.title: Creation of man
segments.gist: God creates man in his own image, male and female, gives them dominion over the earth, and declares all creation very good.

2.summary: Genesis 2 recounts the completion of creation: God rests on the seventh day and blesses it, then the chapter retells the creation of man from dust and God's planting of Eden. It describes the garden, its trees and rivers, God's command about the tree of knowledge, and the creation of woman from Adam's rib to be his companion.

segments.title: God Rests on Seventh Day
segments.gist: God finishes his work, rests on the seventh day, and blesses and sanctifies it.

segments.title: Man Formed from Dust
segments.gist: The LORD God forms man from dust, breathes life into him, and plants a garden in Eden.

segments.title: Eden's Trees and Rivers
segments.gist: God places the man in Eden and describes the garden's trees, including the tree of life and knowledge, and four rivers.

segments.title: Command About the Tree
segments.gist: God puts the man in the garden to tend it and commands him not to eat from the tree of knowledge.

segments.title: No Helper Found
segments.gist: God says it is not good for man to be alone; the man names animals but finds no helper.

segments.title: Woman Created from Rib
segments.gist: God creates woman from the man's rib, and the man recognizes her as bone of his bones and flesh of his flesh.

3.summary: The serpent persuades the woman to eat the forbidden fruit, and she gives it to the man; they realize their nakedness and hide from God. God questions them, curses the serpent, and pronounces judgments on the man and woman. He makes them garments of skins and expels them from Eden, placing cherubims and a flaming sword to guard the tree of life.

segments.title: Serpent tempts the woman
segments.gist: The serpent questions God's command and denies the penalty, and the woman eats the fruit and gives it to her husband.

segments.title: Eyes opened, they hide
segments.gist: The man and woman realize their nakedness, sew fig leaves together, and hide from God among the trees.

segments.title: God questions the man and woman
segments.gist: God calls to the man, who blames the woman, and the woman blames the serpent.

segments.title: Curse on the serpent
segments.gist: God curses the serpent to crawl on its belly and predicts enmity between its seed and the woman's seed.

segments.title: Judgments on man and woman
segments.gist: God multiplies the woman's sorrow in childbirth and curses the ground, so the man must labor for food until he returns to dust.

segments.title: Expulsion from Eden
segments.gist: The man names his wife Eve, God makes them coats of skins, and drives them out, placing cherubims and a flaming sword to guard the tree of life.

4.summary: Adam and Eve's sons Cain and Abel bring offerings to God; Cain's offering is rejected, and in anger he murders Abel. God curses Cain, who goes to live in Nod, and Eve bears Seth, through whom a line of worshipers of God begins.

segments.title: Cain and Abel's Offerings
segments.gist: Eve bears Cain and Abel; Abel keeps sheep and Cain tills the ground, and God respects Abel's offering but not Cain's.

segments.title: God Warns Cain
segments.gist: God asks Cain why he is angry and warns him that sin is crouching at the door, urging him to master it.

segments.title: Cain Kills Abel
segments.gist: Cain kills Abel in the field; when God asks where Abel is, Cain denies knowing and God says Abel's blood cries out from the ground.

segments.title: Cain's Punishment
segments.gist: God curses Cain so the ground will not yield for him and he will be a fugitive; Cain fears being killed, but God sets a mark on him, and Cain settles in Nod.

segments.title: Cain's Descendants and Lamech
segments.gist: Cain's descendants include Enoch, Irad, Mehujael, Methusael, and Lamech; Lamech takes two wives and boasts to them of killing a man.

segments.title: Seth and Enos
segments.gist: Eve bears Seth as a replacement for Abel, and Seth has a son Enos; then people begin to call on the name of the Lord.

5.summary: Genesis 5 traces the line of Adam through Seth to Noah, listing each patriarch's age at the birth of his named son, the years he lived afterward, and his total lifespan. Enoch is singled out for walking with God and being taken without dying, while Lamech names Noah in hope of comfort from the cursed ground.

segments.title: Adam to Enosh
segments.gist: The generations of Adam begin with Seth, and the record of Adam's years and death leads to Enosh and his line.

segments.title: From Kenan to Jared
segments.gist: The lineage continues through Kenan, Mahalalel, and Jared, each with the age at fatherhood, later years, and total lifespan.

segments.title: Enoch walks with God
segments.gist: Enoch lives 365 years, walks with God, and is taken away because God took him, without mention of death.

segments.title: Methuselah and Lamech
segments.gist: Methuselah fathers Lamech and lives 969 years; Lamech fathers a son and lives 777 years.

segments.title: Noah and his sons
segments.gist: Lamech names his son Noah, hoping he will bring comfort from the cursed ground, and Noah fathers Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

6.summary: As humanity multiplies, God sees that wickedness is great and resolves to destroy the earth with a flood. Noah, however, finds grace in God's eyes and is commanded to build an ark to preserve his family and pairs of every living creature.

segments.title: The sons of God and giants
segments.gist: The sons of God take wives from the daughters of men, and giants appear; God limits human days to 120 years.

segments.title: God grieves over human wickedness
segments.gist: God sees that human wickedness is great and every imagination is evil, and He regrets making humanity, but Noah finds grace.

segments.title: Noah's righteousness and God's warning
segments.gist: Noah is described as just and blameless, walking with God; God tells him He will destroy all flesh because of violence.

segments.title: Instructions for building the ark
segments.gist: God commands Noah to build an ark of gopher wood with specific dimensions and to bring his family and animals into it, and Noah obeys.

7.summary: God commands Noah to enter the ark with his family and the clean and unclean animals, because Noah is righteous before him. After seven days the flood comes, covering the earth and destroying all flesh outside the ark, and the waters prevail for a hundred and fifty days.

segments.title: God commands Noah to enter the ark
segments.gist: God tells Noah to enter the ark with his household and the animals, because Noah is righteous before him.

segments.title: Noah enters the ark before the flood
segments.gist: Noah, his family, and the animals enter the ark, and after seven days the floodwaters come upon the earth.

segments.title: The flood begins and the ark is shut
segments.gist: On the same day Noah and all with him enter the ark, and the Lord shuts him in as the waters rise.

segments.title: The waters prevail over the earth
segments.gist: The flood covers the earth, lifting the ark above the waters, which prevail greatly and cover all high mountains.

segments.title: All flesh outside the ark perishes
segments.gist: All flesh outside the ark dies, and the waters prevail on the earth for a hundred and fifty days.

8.summary: After the flood, God remembers Noah and causes the waters to recede; Noah sends out a raven and a dove to test the earth, then leaves the ark at God's command. Noah builds an altar and offers sacrifices, and God promises never again to curse the ground or destroy all flesh, setting the rainbow as a sign.

segments.title: God remembers Noah
segments.gist: God causes a wind to pass over the earth, the fountains and windows are stopped, and the waters recede for 150 days.

segments.title: Noah sends raven and dove
segments.gist: Noah opens the window, sends a raven and then a dove; the dove returns with an olive leaf, showing waters abated.

segments.title: Waters dry and Noah exits
segments.gist: By the first day of the first month the waters are dried; God commands Noah to leave the ark with his family and animals.

segments.title: Noah's altar and God's promise
segments.gist: Noah builds an altar and offers clean animals; God smells a sweet savour and promises never again to curse the ground or smite all flesh.

9.summary: After the flood, God blesses Noah and his sons, permits them to eat meat, and establishes the rainbow as a sign of his covenant never to destroy the earth by water again. Noah plants a vineyard, becomes drunk, and is shamed by his son Ham, while Shem and Japheth cover him; Noah then pronounces blessings on Shem and Japheth and a curse on Canaan, and the chapter closes with Noah's death and a genealogy of his sons.

segments.title: God blesses Noah and permits meat
segments.gist: God blesses Noah and his sons, commands them to multiply, and allows them to eat animals but forbids eating blood.

segments.title: Covenant of the rainbow
segments.gist: God establishes a covenant with Noah and all living creatures, setting the rainbow as a sign that he will never again flood the earth.

segments.title: Noah's drunkenness and Ham's sin
segments.gist: Noah plants a vineyard, becomes drunk and lies uncovered; Ham sees him and tells his brothers, who cover Noah without looking.

segments.title: Noah curses Canaan and blesses Shem
segments.gist: When Noah wakes, he curses Canaan as a servant to his brothers and blesses Shem and Japheth.

10.summary: Genesis 10 is the table of nations, tracing the descendants of Noah's sons—Japheth, Ham, and Shem—and the peoples and lands that came from them. It highlights Nimrod, the mighty hunter whose kingdom began at Babel, and concludes by noting how the nations spread abroad after the flood.

segments.title: Descendants of Japheth
segments.gist: The sons of Japheth and their descendants are listed, from whom the isles of the Gentiles were divided.

segments.title: Descendants of Ham and Nimrod
segments.gist: The sons of Ham are listed, with a focus on Nimrod, the mighty hunter whose kingdom began at Babel and extended to Assyria.

segments.title: Canaanite Nations
segments.gist: The descendants of Canaan are listed, including the Jebusites, Amorites, and other peoples who later inhabited the land.

segments.title: Descendants of Shem
segments.gist: The sons of Shem and their descendants are listed, culminating in the line that leads to Abraham.

11.summary: The chapter recounts humanity's attempt to build a tower to heaven and the resulting confusion of languages at Babel, then traces the generations from Shem to Terah, ending with Terah's family settling in Haran.

segments.title: The Tower of Babel
segments.gist: People unite to build a city and tower to make a name for themselves, but God confuses their language and scatters them.

segments.title: Genealogy from Shem to Terah
segments.gist: A linear genealogy traces Shem's descendants through Arphaxad, Salah, Eber, Peleg, Reu, Serug, Nahor, and Terah.

segments.title: Terah's Family and Journey to Haran
segments.gist: Terah's sons are Abram, Nahor, and Haran; after Haran's death, Terah takes Abram, Sarai, and Lot toward Canaan but settles in Haran.

12.summary: God calls Abram to leave his country and promises to make him a great nation and bless all families of the earth. Abram travels to Canaan with Sarai and Lot, then a famine drives him to Egypt, where he passes Sarai off as his sister and Pharaoh takes her into his house, bringing plagues on Egypt until Abram is sent away.

segments.title: God's call and promise to Abram
segments.gist: God tells Abram to leave his country and kindred for a land God will show him, promising to make him a great nation and bless all families of the earth.

segments.title: Abram journeys to Canaan
segments.gist: Abram departs Haran with Sarai and Lot, travels through Canaan to Shechem and Bethel, and God promises the land to his seed.

segments.title: Abram in Egypt with Sarai
segments.gist: A famine drives Abram to Egypt, where he asks Sarai to say she is his sister; Pharaoh takes her into his house and treats Abram well for her sake.

segments.title: Plagues and Abram's departure
segments.gist: God plagues Pharaoh and his house because of Sarai, Pharaoh confronts Abram, and Abram leaves Egypt with his wife and possessions.

13.summary: Abram and Lot return from Egypt to the Negev, where their herdsmen quarrel because the land cannot support both households. Abram offers Lot first choice of the land; Lot chooses the well-watered Jordan plain and settles near Sodom, while Abram remains in Canaan. God renews his promise of the land and countless descendants to Abram at Hebron.

segments.title: Abram returns to Bethel
segments.gist: Abram goes from Egypt to the Negev with Sarai and Lot, then back to the altar at Bethel and calls on the Lord.

segments.title: Strife between herdsmen
segments.gist: Lot also has flocks and herds, and the land cannot sustain them together, so their herdsmen quarrel.

segments.title: Abram offers Lot the choice
segments.gist: Abram asks Lot to avoid strife and offers him first pick of the land, east or west.

segments.title: Lot chooses the Jordan plain
segments.gist: Lot lifts his eyes, chooses the well-watered Jordan plain, and settles near Sodom, whose men were wicked.

segments.title: God renews the promise to Abram
segments.gist: After Lot departs, God tells Abram to look in all directions, promises him and his seed the land forever, and Abram moves to Hebron.

14.summary: Four invading kings defeat the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah and carry off Lot and his goods. Abram arms his household, pursues the captors, defeats them, and rescues Lot and the stolen property. Afterward Melchizedek blesses Abram, and the king of Sodom offers him the goods, which Abram refuses, giving a tenth to Melchizedek.

segments.title: Kings battle and Lot captured
segments.gist: Four kings defeat the kings of the plain, take Lot and his goods captive, and carry them away.

segments.title: Abram rescues Lot
segments.gist: Abram arms his trained servants, pursues the enemy, defeats them, and recovers Lot and all the goods.

segments.title: Melchizedek blesses Abram
segments.gist: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God, brings bread and wine and blesses Abram, who gives him a tenth.

segments.title: Abram refuses Sodom's goods
segments.gist: The king of Sodom offers Abram the goods, but Abram refuses to take anything, except what his men have eaten and the portion for his allies.

15.summary: God appears to Abram in a vision, promising him a great reward and a multitude of descendants despite his childlessness. Abram believes God's promise, and God formally establishes a covenant with him, foretelling his descendants' enslavement in Egypt and their eventual return. The chapter concludes with a symbolic covenant ceremony and a prophecy of the land Abram's descendants will inherit.

segments.title: Abram's Complaint and Promise
segments.gist: God promises Abram a great reward, but Abram laments his childlessness and names Eliezer as his heir; God assures him of a biological heir.

segments.title: Land Promise and Abram's Belief
segments.gist: God promises Abram the land of Canaan; Abram believes and is counted righteous, then prepares animals for a covenant ceremony.

segments.title: Prophecy of Slavery and Return
segments.gist: God tells Abram his descendants will be enslaved in a foreign land for 400 years, but will return with great possessions in the fourth generation.

segments.title: Covenant of the Pieces
segments.gist: A smoking furnace and burning lamp pass between the divided animals, and God defines the boundaries of the land promised to Abram's descendants.

16.summary: Sarai, still childless, gives her Egyptian maid Hagar to Abram as a wife; when Hagar conceives, she despises Sarai, and Sarai deals harshly with her. Hagar flees into the wilderness, where an angel of the LORD finds her, tells her to return and submit, and promises her a son named Ishmael. Hagar names the LORD who spoke to her, and Abram later names the child Ishmael when he is born.

segments.title: Sarai gives Hagar to Abram
segments.gist: Sarai, childless, gives her maid Hagar to Abram as a wife, and Hagar conceives.

segments.title: Sarai blames Abram and mistreats Hagar
segments.gist: Sarai complains to Abram about Hagar's contempt, and Abram tells her to do as she pleases; Sarai deals harshly with Hagar, who flees.

segments.title: Angel finds Hagar and promises a son
segments.gist: An angel of the LORD finds Hagar by a spring in the wilderness, tells her to return and submit, and promises her numerous descendants and a son named Ishmael.

segments.title: Hagar names the LORD and Ishmael is born
segments.gist: Hagar names the LORD who spoke to her, and Abram names the son Hagar bears him Ishmael.

17.summary: When Abram is ninety-nine, God appears to him, changes his name to Abraham, and establishes an everlasting covenant of circumcision, promising him countless descendants and the land of Canaan. God also renames Sarai to Sarah and promises she will bear a son, Isaac, though Abraham laughs in disbelief. The chapter ends with Abraham circumcising every male in his household that same day.

segments.title: God's covenant with Abram
segments.gist: God appears to Abram, promises to multiply him exceedingly, and establishes his covenant with him and his descendants.

segments.title: Circumcision commanded
segments.gist: God commands Abraham and every male in his household to be circumcised as the sign of the covenant.

segments.title: Promise of Isaac
segments.gist: God renames Sarai to Sarah, promises she will bear a son named Isaac, and Abraham laughs in disbelief.

segments.title: Abraham circumcises household
segments.gist: Abraham circumcises himself, Ishmael, and all the males of his household on the same day, as God commanded.

18.summary: Three visitors come to Abraham at Mamre, where he and Sarah show hospitality; they announce that Sarah will bear a son within a year, and Sarah laughs in disbelief. The visitors then leave for Sodom, and the LORD reveals to Abraham that Sodom and Gomorrah will be destroyed; Abraham intercedes, bargaining with God to spare the cities if righteous people are found there.

segments.title: Abraham Welcomes Three Visitors
segments.gist: Abraham sees three men near Mamre, runs to greet them, offers water, rest, and a meal, and they accept.

segments.title: Sarah Promised a Son; She Laughs
segments.gist: The visitors say Sarah will have a son within a year; Sarah laughs inwardly, and the LORD asks why she laughed.

segments.title: The LORD Reveals Sodom's Destruction
segments.gist: The men leave toward Sodom, and the LORD tells Abraham that the outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah is great and He will destroy them.

segments.title: Abraham Intercedes for Sodom
segments.gist: Abraham bargains with the LORD, asking repeatedly if He will spare the city for the sake of fifty, forty, thirty, twenty, or ten righteous people.

19.summary: Two angels arrive at Sodom and are hosted by Lot, but the men of the city surround the house demanding to abuse them; Lot offers his daughters instead and the angels strike the mob blind. The angels warn Lot to flee with his family before Sodom and Gomorrah are destroyed; Lot's sons-in-law mock him, but he, his wife, and two daughters escape, with his wife turning into a pillar of salt. Fire and brimstone destroy the cities, and Lot's daughters later bear sons by him, Moab and Ammon.

segments.title: Angels visit Lot in Sodom
segments.gist: Two angels come to Sodom; Lot hosts them, but the men of the city surround the house demanding to abuse the visitors, and the angels blind the mob.

segments.title: Angels warn Lot to flee
segments.gist: The angels tell Lot to flee with his family; his sons-in-law mock him, but he, his wife, and two daughters are led out, and Lot asks to flee to Zoar.

segments.title: Sodom and Gomorrah destroyed
segments.gist: The LORD rains fire and brimstone on Sodom and Gomorrah; Lot's wife looks back and becomes a pillar of salt, and Abraham sees the smoke.

segments.title: Lot's daughters bear sons
segments.gist: Lot and his daughters live in a cave; the daughters make him drunk and conceive, bearing Moab and Ammon, ancestors of two nations.

20.summary: Abraham journeys to Gerar and again calls Sarah his sister; Abimelech takes her, but God warns him in a dream and he returns her untouched, rebuking Abraham. Abraham explains his fear and prays, and God heals Abimelech's household.

segments.title: Abraham sojourns in Gerar
segments.gist: Abraham travels to Gerar and says Sarah is his sister, so Abimelech takes her.

segments.title: God warns Abimelech in dream
segments.gist: God tells Abimelech in a dream that he is a dead man for taking Sarah, and Abimelech protests his innocence.

segments.title: Abimelech confronts Abraham
segments.gist: Abimelech returns Sarah and rebukes Abraham, who explains his fear and his agreement with Sarah.

segments.title: Abimelech restores Sarah with gifts
segments.gist: Abimelech gives Abraham sheep, oxen, servants, and silver, and defends Sarah's honor.

segments.title: Abraham prays; household healed
segments.gist: Abraham prays, and God heals Abimelech, his wife, and maids so they can bear children.

21.summary: Isaac is born to Abraham and Sarah in their old age, and Sarah demands that Hagar and Ishmael be cast out; God preserves Hagar and Ishmael in the wilderness and promises to make Ishmael a nation. Later, Abraham makes a covenant with Abimelech at Beersheba over a well.

segments.title: Isaac's Birth and Weaning
segments.gist: Sarah bears Isaac as promised, Abraham circumcises him, and Sarah rejoices; at the feast for Isaac's weaning, Sarah sees Ishmael mocking.

segments.title: Hagar and Ishmael Cast Out
segments.gist: Sarah demands Hagar and Ishmael be expelled; Abraham is grieved but God reassures him, and he sends Hagar away with bread and water.

segments.title: God Rescues Ishmael
segments.gist: Hagar weeps when the water runs out; God hears Ishmael, opens her eyes to a well, and promises to make Ishmael a great nation.

segments.title: Covenant at Beersheba
segments.gist: Abimelech and Phicol seek a covenant with Abraham; Abraham sets apart seven ewe lambs for a well, and they swear an oath at Beersheba.

22.summary: God tests Abraham by commanding him to sacrifice his son Isaac on Mount Moriah. Abraham obeys, but an angel stops him at the last moment, and a ram is provided as a substitute. God then reaffirms His covenant blessings to Abraham.

segments.title: God Tests Abraham
segments.gist: God calls to Abraham and commands him to offer his only son Isaac as a burnt offering in the land of Moriah.

segments.title: Journey to Moriah
segments.gist: Abraham rises early, saddles his donkey, takes Isaac and two servants, and travels toward Moriah; on the third day he sees the place afar off.

segments.title: Altar and Bound Isaac
segments.gist: Abraham builds an altar, lays the wood in order, binds Isaac, and places him on the altar; then he takes the knife to slay his son.

segments.title: Angel Stops Abraham
segments.gist: The angel of the LORD calls from heaven, stops Abraham, and declares his fear of God; a ram caught in a thicket is offered instead, and Abraham names the place Jehovahjireh.

segments.title: Covenant Reaffirmed
segments.gist: The angel of the LORD calls a second time and swears by Himself to bless Abraham and multiply his seed because he obeyed; Abraham returns to Beersheba.

segments.title: Nahor's Descendants
segments.gist: Abraham is told that his brother Nahor has children by Milcah and a concubine, including Bethuel, the father of Rebekah.

23.summary: Sarah dies at Kiriath-arba (Hebron), and Abraham mourns and seeks a burial place. He negotiates with the Hittites and buys the cave of Machpelah from Ephron for four hundred shekels of silver, then buries Sarah there.

segments.title: Sarah's death and Abraham's mourning
segments.gist: Sarah dies at Kiriath-arba (Hebron), and Abraham mourns and weeps for her.

segments.title: Abraham requests a burial site
segments.gist: Abraham asks the Hittites for a burial place, and they offer him choice of their sepulchers.

segments.title: Abraham buys Machpelah cave
segments.gist: Ephron offers the cave of Machpelah, and Abraham pays four hundred shekels of silver for it.

segments.title: Sarah buried in Machpelah
segments.gist: The field and cave become Abraham's possession, and he buries Sarah there.

24.summary: Abraham sends his oldest servant to his homeland to find a wife for Isaac, swearing an oath not to take a Canaanite woman. At a well in Nahor, the servant prays for a sign and meets Rebekah, who offers water for him and his camels. She agrees to return with him, and Isaac marries her, finding comfort after his mother's death.

segments.title: Abraham Commissions Servant
segments.gist: Abraham makes his eldest servant swear to find a wife for Isaac from his own kindred, not from the Canaanites, and sends him to Mesopotamia.

segments.title: Servant Prays at Well
segments.gist: The servant arrives at a well outside Nahor and prays for a specific sign: the woman who offers water to him and his camels is the one God has chosen.

segments.title: Rebekah Shows Kindness
segments.gist: Rebekah comes to the well, gives the servant drink, and waters his camels; the servant gives her gifts and blesses God for leading him to Abraham's relatives.

segments.title: Servant Tells His Mission
segments.gist: Rebekah runs home; her brother Laban welcomes the servant, who recounts Abraham's wealth, the oath, and how the sign at the well led him to Rebekah, asking for a decision.

segments.title: Rebekah Agrees to Go
segments.gist: Laban and Bethuel accept the match as from God; the servant gives gifts, and after a request to delay, Rebekah agrees to leave with him immediately.

segments.title: Isaac Marries Rebekah
segments.gist: Isaac is in the field when the servant arrives; Rebekah covers herself with a veil, Isaac takes her as his wife, loves her, and is comforted after his mother's death.

25.summary: Abraham dies and is buried by Isaac and Ishmael; Ishmael's descendants are listed. Rebekah bears twins, Esau and Jacob, and Esau sells his birthright to Jacob for bread and pottage.

segments.title: Abraham's death and burial
segments.gist: Abraham dies, is buried by Isaac and Ishmael in Machpelah, and God blesses Isaac.

segments.title: Ishmael's descendants
segments.gist: The generations of Ishmael are listed, including twelve princes and their settlements.

segments.title: Birth of Esau and Jacob
segments.gist: Rebekah bears twins; Esau is born first, then Jacob holding Esau's heel.

segments.title: Esau sells his birthright
segments.gist: Esau, faint with hunger, sells his birthright to Jacob for bread and pottage.

26.summary: Isaac, during a famine, goes to Gerar and is told by God to stay in the land; he repeats the lie that Rebekah is his sister, but Abimelech discovers the truth. Isaac prospers, reopens his father's wells, and after disputes over wells at Esek and Sitnah, moves to Rehoboth and then Beersheba, where God renews the covenant and Abimelech makes a treaty with him. The chapter closes with Esau's marriage to two Hittite women.

segments.title: Isaac lies in Gerar
segments.gist: God tells Isaac not to go to Egypt but to stay in the land; Isaac settles in Gerar and claims Rebekah is his sister.

segments.title: Abimelech discovers the truth
segments.gist: Abimelech sees Isaac caressing Rebekah and confronts him; Isaac admits the lie, and Abimelech warns his people not to harm them.

segments.title: Isaac prospers and is sent away
segments.gist: Isaac sows and reaps a hundredfold, grows very wealthy, and the Philistines stop up his wells; Abimelech asks him to leave.

segments.title: Disputes over wells
segments.gist: Isaac reopens wells and digs new ones; herdsmen quarrel over Esek and Sitnah, but at Rehoboth there is no strife.

segments.title: Covenant at Beersheba
segments.gist: God appears to Isaac at Beersheba and renews the promise; Abimelech and his men make a treaty with Isaac, who names the well Beersheba.

segments.title: Esau's Hittite wives
segments.gist: Esau marries Judith and Bashemath, Hittite women, who bring grief to Isaac and Rebekah.

27.summary: Isaac, old and blind, asks Esau to hunt game and prepare a meal so he can bless him. Rebekah overhears and helps Jacob deceive Isaac by dressing as Esau and serving the meal, and Isaac gives Jacob the blessing. When Esau returns and learns what happened, he weeps and begs for a blessing, but Isaac confirms Jacob's supremacy; Esau vows to kill Jacob, and Rebekah sends Jacob away to Haran.

segments.title: Isaac sends Esau to hunt
segments.gist: Isaac, old and blind, asks Esau to hunt game and prepare savory meat so he can bless him before he dies.

segments.title: Rebekah and Jacob plot deception
segments.gist: Rebekah overhears and tells Jacob to bring two goats so she can cook and Jacob can deceive Isaac and receive the blessing.

segments.title: Jacob deceives Isaac and gets blessing
segments.gist: Jacob, disguised with goatskins, brings the food to Isaac, lies about being Esau, and receives the blessing of abundance and rule over his brothers.

segments.title: Esau discovers deception and begs blessing
segments.gist: Esau returns and learns Jacob took the blessing; he weeps and begs, but Isaac can only give him a lesser blessing of servitude and eventual freedom.

segments.title: Esau's hatred and Rebekah's plan
segments.gist: Esau vows to kill Jacob after Isaac's death; Rebekah warns Jacob and sends him to Haran, complaining to Isaac about Esau's wives.

28.summary: Isaac blesses Jacob and sends him to Paddan-aram to find a wife, warning him not to marry a Canaanite. On the way, Jacob dreams of a ladder reaching to heaven with angels and God's promise of land and descendants; he names the place Bethel and vows to serve God if He keeps him safe.

segments.title: Isaac blesses and sends Jacob
segments.gist: Isaac blesses Jacob, commands him not to marry a Canaanite, and sends him to Paddan-aram to find a wife from Rebekah's family.

segments.title: Esau marries Ishmael's daughter
segments.gist: Esau sees that Canaanite wives displease Isaac, so he marries Mahalath, daughter of Ishmael.

segments.title: Jacob's dream at Bethel
segments.gist: Jacob dreams of a ladder to heaven with angels, and God promises him the land and numerous descendants.

segments.title: Jacob names the place Bethel
segments.gist: Jacob wakes in awe, sets up a stone pillar, and names the place Bethel, meaning house of God.

segments.title: Jacob's conditional vow
segments.gist: Jacob vows that if God protects and provides for him, he will serve God and give a tenth of all he receives.

29.summary: Jacob flees to Haran, meets Rachel at a well, and is welcomed by her father Laban. He agrees to serve seven years for Rachel, but Laban deceives him by giving Leah first; Jacob then serves another seven years for Rachel. The chapter ends with Leah bearing four sons while Rachel remains barren.

segments.title: Jacob meets Rachel at the well
segments.gist: Jacob arrives in Haran, rolls the stone from the well for Rachel, and is received by Laban.

segments.title: Jacob agrees to serve for Rachel
segments.gist: Laban asks Jacob's wages, and Jacob agrees to serve seven years for Rachel.

segments.title: Laban deceives Jacob with Leah
segments.gist: After the wedding, Laban gives Leah instead of Rachel, then gives Rachel for another seven years' service.

segments.title: Leah bears four sons
segments.gist: The LORD sees Leah is hated and opens her womb; she bears Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah.

30.summary: Rachel, jealous of Leah's children, gives her maid Bilhah to Jacob, who bears Dan and Naphtali; Leah then gives her maid Zilpah, who bears Gad and Asher. After a dispute over mandrakes, Leah bears Issachar, Zebulun, and Dinah. Finally, God remembers Rachel, who bears Joseph; later Jacob asks Laban to let him leave, and they agree on a wage of speckled and spotted animals, which Jacob breeds to increase his own flock.

segments.title: Rachel gives Bilhah to Jacob
segments.gist: Rachel, envious of Leah, gives her maid Bilhah to Jacob; Bilhah bears Dan and Naphtali, and Rachel names them.

segments.title: Leah gives Zilpah to Jacob
segments.gist: Leah, seeing she had stopped bearing, gives her maid Zilpah to Jacob; Zilpah bears Gad and Asher.

segments.title: Mandrakes and more sons
segments.gist: Reuben finds mandrakes; Rachel and Leah argue over them, and Leah bears Issachar, Zebulun, and Dinah.

segments.title: Rachel bears Joseph
segments.gist: God remembers Rachel, opens her womb, and she bears Joseph, saying God has taken away her reproach.

segments.title: Jacob bargains with Laban
segments.gist: After Joseph's birth, Jacob asks Laban to let him return home; they agree that Jacob will take the speckled and spotted animals as wages.

segments.title: Jacob breeds speckled flocks
segments.gist: Jacob uses peeled rods to breed stronger speckled animals for himself, and his flocks multiply greatly.

31.summary: Jacob, having prospered in Laban's service, is commanded by God to return to Canaan. He secretly departs with his family and flocks, and Rachel steals her father's household gods. Laban pursues and confronts Jacob, but God warns Laban not to harm him; the two make a covenant of peace at Mizpah and part ways.

segments.title: Jacob Decides to Flee
segments.gist: Jacob hears Laban's sons complain and sees Laban's changed attitude; God tells him to return to Canaan, and he summons Rachel and Leah to explain his departure.

segments.title: Jacob Flees with Family
segments.gist: Jacob secretly leaves with his family and livestock; Rachel steals Laban's household gods; Laban pursues and overtakes Jacob, but God warns Laban in a dream not to harm him.

segments.title: Laban Confronts Jacob
segments.gist: Laban accuses Jacob of fleeing secretly and stealing his gods; Jacob denies theft, and Rachel hides the gods under her camel saddle, deceiving her father.

segments.title: Jacob's Defense
segments.gist: Jacob recounts his twenty years of faithful service and Laban's unfair treatment, declaring that God has seen his affliction and rebuked Laban.

segments.title: Covenant at Mizpah
segments.gist: Laban proposes a covenant; Jacob sets up a stone pillar and they make a heap of witness, swearing not to harm each other; Laban blesses his daughters and departs.

32.summary: Jacob, returning to Canaan, sends messengers ahead to Esau and, fearing attack, divides his company and prays for deliverance. He sends gifts to Esau, then wrestles with a man until daybreak, receives the name Israel, and leaves limping with the sun rising upon him.

segments.title: Jacob sends messengers to Esau
segments.gist: Jacob sends messengers to Esau, who return reporting Esau is coming with four hundred men, causing Jacob great fear.

segments.title: Jacob prays for deliverance
segments.gist: Jacob prays, recalling God's promise and asking to be saved from Esau, fearing he will attack.

segments.title: Jacob prepares a gift for Esau
segments.gist: Jacob selects a large gift of livestock and instructs his servants to go ahead in groups, hoping to appease Esau.

segments.title: Jacob wrestles at Peniel
segments.gist: Jacob sends his family across the Jabbok and wrestles with a man until dawn; he is renamed Israel and leaves limping.

33.summary: Jacob, still fearing Esau, bows before him, but Esau runs to embrace and kiss him, and the two are reconciled. Esau meets Jacob's family, initially declines Jacob's gift but accepts it after urging, and then offers to accompany Jacob; Jacob declines and travels slowly to Succoth and then to Shechem, where he buys land and builds an altar.

segments.title: Jacob and Esau meet
segments.gist: Jacob bows seven times; Esau runs to embrace, kiss, and weep with him.

segments.title: Esau meets Jacob's family
segments.gist: Esau asks about the women and children, and Jacob's family bows before him.

segments.title: Jacob gives Esau a gift
segments.gist: Esau initially refuses Jacob's gift but accepts it after Jacob insists.

segments.title: Jacob declines Esau's offer
segments.gist: Esau offers to accompany Jacob, but Jacob declines and travels slowly to Succoth.

segments.title: Jacob settles in Shechem
segments.gist: Jacob arrives at Shechem, buys land, pitches his tent, and builds an altar.

34.summary: Dinah, Jacob's daughter, is defiled by Shechem, a Hivite prince, who then seeks to marry her. Her brothers Simeon and Levi deceive the men of Shechem, requiring circumcision as a condition, and then slaughter them while they are incapacitated, plundering the city. Jacob rebukes his sons for making him a stench among the Canaanites.

segments.title: Shechem Defiles Dinah
segments.gist: Dinah goes out to see the daughters of the land, and Shechem takes her and lies with her, then loves her and speaks kindly to her.

segments.title: Hamor Proposes Marriage
segments.gist: Hamor the Hivite asks Jacob and his sons for Dinah as a wife for Shechem, offering intermarriage and land to dwell and trade in.

segments.title: Circumcision Deceit
segments.gist: Jacob's sons deceitfully require all males of Shechem to be circumcised, and Hamor and Shechem persuade the men of the city to agree.

segments.title: Simeon and Levi Slay Shechem
segments.gist: On the third day, Simeon and Levi kill all the males of Shechem, rescue Dinah, and plunder the city, taking wealth and families captive.

segments.title: Jacob Rebukes His Sons
segments.gist: Jacob complains that his sons have made him odious among the Canaanites, and they defend their action by citing the treatment of Dinah.

35.summary: God commands Jacob to return to Bethel, where Jacob purifies his household and builds an altar. God renews the promise of many descendants and the land, Rachel dies giving birth to Benjamin, Isaac dies and is buried by Jacob and Esau.

segments.title: Jacob returns to Bethel
segments.gist: God tells Jacob to go to Bethel; Jacob has his household purify themselves and bury their foreign gods, then builds an altar there.

segments.title: God renews promise to Jacob
segments.gist: God appears to Jacob at Bethel, blesses him, changes his name to Israel, and promises many descendants and the land.

segments.title: Rachel dies bearing Benjamin
segments.gist: Rachel dies in childbirth near Ephrath and names her son Benoni, but Jacob calls him Benjamin; she is buried there.

segments.title: Reuben sleeps with Bilhah
segments.gist: Israel journeys on and Reuben lies with his father's concubine Bilhah, and Israel hears of it.

segments.title: Jacob's twelve sons listed
segments.gist: The sons of Jacob are listed by their mothers: Leah, Rachel, Bilhah, and Zilpah.

segments.title: Isaac dies and is buried
segments.gist: Jacob comes to Isaac at Mamre; Isaac dies at 180, and his sons Esau and Jacob bury him.

36.summary: Genesis 36 records the generations of Esau, also called Edom, listing his wives, sons, and the chiefs descended from him. It describes Esau's move to Mount Seir to separate from Jacob because their possessions were too great, and it catalogs the kings and chiefs of Edom before Israel had a king.

segments.title: Esau's wives and sons
segments.gist: Esau's Canaanite wives and his sons born in Canaan are listed, including Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.

segments.title: Esau's descendants in Edom
segments.gist: The generations of Esau in Mount Seir are recorded, naming his sons and the sons of Eliphaz, including Amalek.

segments.title: Chiefs descended from Esau
segments.gist: The chiefs of the sons of Esau are listed: the chiefs of Eliphaz, Reuel, and the other sons of Esau.

segments.title: Chiefs of the Horites
segments.gist: The sons of Seir the Horite and their chiefs in the land of Edom are listed, including Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, and others.

segments.title: Kings of Edom
segments.gist: The kings who reigned in Edom before Israel had a king are named, from Bela to Hadar, with their cities.

segments.title: Chiefs of Esau by place
segments.gist: The chiefs of Esau according to their families and places are listed, ending with the record that Esau is the father of the Edomites.

37.summary: Jacob settles in Canaan and favors his son Joseph with a special coat, fueling his brothers' hatred. Joseph recounts two dreams of his family bowing to him, and his brothers sell him into slavery in Egypt, deceiving Jacob with a bloodied coat.

segments.title: Jacob Favors Joseph
segments.gist: Jacob dwells in Canaan and gives Joseph a coat of many colors, making his brothers jealous.

segments.title: Joseph's Dreams
segments.gist: Joseph dreams of his brothers' sheaves and the sun, moon, and stars bowing to him, increasing their hatred.

segments.title: Joseph Sent to Brothers
segments.gist: Jacob sends Joseph to check on his brothers, who are shepherding near Shechem; Joseph finds them at Dothan.

segments.title: Brothers Sell Joseph
segments.gist: The brothers plot to kill Joseph, but Reuben and Judah intervene, and they sell him to Ishmaelite traders for twenty pieces of silver.

segments.title: Jacob Deceived by Coat
segments.gist: The brothers dip Joseph's coat in goat's blood and show it to Jacob, who mourns; Joseph is sold to Potiphar in Egypt.

38.summary: Judah leaves his brothers and marries a Canaanite woman, Shua's daughter, who bears him Er, Onan, and Shelah. After Er dies and Onan refuses to raise up seed for his brother, Tamar tricks Judah into sleeping with her and bears twins, Perez and Zerah.

segments.title: Judah's sons born
segments.gist: Judah separates from his brothers, marries Shua's daughter, and she bears Er, Onan, and Shelah.

segments.title: Er and Onan die
segments.gist: Judah gives Tamar to Er, who dies; Onan refuses to raise up seed and dies; Judah sends Tamar to her father's house.

segments.title: Tamar deceives Judah
segments.gist: Tamar disguises herself, Judah sleeps with her, and she takes his signet, cord, and staff as pledge.

segments.title: Judah acknowledges Tamar
segments.gist: Judah's friend cannot find the harlot; Judah learns Tamar is pregnant and condemns her, but she produces his pledge and he acknowledges her.

segments.title: Twins Perez and Zerah
segments.gist: Tamar bears twins; Zerah puts out his hand, but Perez is born first.

39.summary: Joseph, sold into Egypt, serves in Potiphar's house and rises to oversee all his master's affairs. Potiphar's wife repeatedly tries to seduce him; when he refuses and flees, she accuses him falsely, and Potiphar imprisons him. In prison, the LORD is with Joseph, and the keeper puts him in charge of all the prisoners.

segments.title: Joseph Prospers in Potiphar's House
segments.gist: Joseph is bought by Potiphar, serves well, and is made overseer of all his master's household and fields.

segments.title: Potiphar's Wife Tempts Joseph
segments.gist: Potiphar's wife repeatedly urges Joseph to lie with her, but he refuses, citing his master's trust and sin against God.

segments.title: Joseph Flees and Is Accused
segments.gist: She catches Joseph's garment, he flees, and she uses it to accuse him before the household and then before Potiphar.

segments.title: Joseph Imprisoned and Prospered
segments.gist: Potiphar puts Joseph in prison, where the LORD is with him and the keeper gives him charge over all the prisoners.

40.summary: In prison, Joseph interprets the dreams of Pharaoh's butler and baker: the butler will be restored to his position in three days, while the baker will be hanged. Joseph asks the butler to remember him before Pharaoh, but the butler forgets him.

segments.title: Butler and baker imprisoned
segments.gist: Pharaoh's chief butler and chief baker offend him and are put in the prison where Joseph is confined.

segments.title: Dreams and Joseph's question
segments.gist: The butler and baker each dream on the same night, and Joseph asks why they look sad and offers to interpret.

segments.title: Butler's dream interpreted
segments.gist: The butler describes his dream of a vine with three branches, and Joseph says the three branches mean three days until he is restored.

segments.title: Baker's dream interpreted
segments.gist: The baker describes his dream of three baskets of bread, and Joseph says the three baskets mean three days until he is hanged.

segments.title: Dreams fulfilled; butler forgets
segments.gist: On Pharaoh's birthday the butler is restored and the baker is hanged, but the butler does not remember Joseph.

41.summary: Pharaoh dreams of seven fat cows devoured by seven lean cows and seven good ears of grain swallowed by seven thin ears. Joseph, released from prison, interprets both dreams as seven years of plenty followed by seven years of famine, and advises Pharaoh to store grain. Pharaoh makes Joseph governor of Egypt; Joseph stores grain during the plenty, marries Asenath, and has two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, before the famine begins and Egypt's people come to buy grain.

segments.title: Pharaoh's dreams of cows and grain
segments.gist: Pharaoh dreams of seven fat cows eaten by seven lean cows, and seven good ears of grain swallowed by seven thin ears.

segments.title: Butler recalls Joseph and Pharaoh summons him
segments.gist: The chief butler remembers Joseph, and Pharaoh sends for him from prison to interpret the dreams.

segments.title: Pharaoh recounts dreams; Joseph interprets
segments.gist: Pharaoh repeats his dreams, and Joseph says both mean seven years of plenty followed by seven years of famine, firmly fixed by God.

segments.title: Joseph advises Pharaoh and is made governor
segments.gist: Joseph recommends storing grain during plenty, and Pharaoh appoints him governor over Egypt with wide authority.

segments.title: Joseph stores grain; famine brings buyers
segments.gist: Joseph gathers grain during the seven plentiful years, has two sons, and when famine comes, sells grain to Egyptians and others.

42.summary: Jacob sends ten of his sons to Egypt to buy grain during the famine, keeping Benjamin at home. In Egypt, Joseph recognizes them but they do not recognize him; he speaks harshly, accuses them of being spies, and demands they bring Benjamin to prove their honesty. He holds Simeon hostage and sends them back with grain and their money returned, leaving the brothers fearful and Jacob grieving over the loss of his sons.

segments.title: Jacob sends sons to Egypt
segments.gist: Jacob learns there is grain in Egypt and sends ten of his sons to buy food, but keeps Benjamin at home for fear of harm.

segments.title: Joseph accuses brothers as spies
segments.gist: Joseph recognizes his brothers and speaks harshly, accusing them of being spies; they deny it and explain their family, but he insists they prove it by bringing Benjamin.

segments.title: Simeon bound; brothers sent back
segments.gist: Joseph proposes a test to prove their honesty, keeps Simeon bound, and sends the others back with grain, secretly returning their money.

segments.title: Brothers discover money in sacks
segments.gist: On the journey, one brother finds his money in his sack and the brothers are afraid, wondering what God has done to them.

segments.title: Brothers report to Jacob
segments.gist: The brothers tell Jacob everything that happened in Egypt, including the demand to bring Benjamin, and Jacob grieves over losing his children.

segments.title: Jacob refuses to send Benjamin
segments.gist: When they empty their sacks and find their money, Jacob laments that all these things are against him and refuses to let Benjamin go, fearing more loss.

43.summary: Jacob reluctantly sends Benjamin to Egypt with his other sons, fearing loss. In Egypt, Joseph receives them, weeps privately upon seeing Benjamin, and then hosts them at a feast, still concealing his identity.

segments.title: Jacob sends Benjamin to Egypt
segments.gist: Famine forces Jacob to send Benjamin with his sons, hoping for mercy from the Egyptian ruler.

segments.title: Joseph's steward reassures the brothers
segments.gist: Joseph's steward brings the brothers to his house, reassures them, and treats them kindly.

segments.title: Joseph weeps and hosts a feast
segments.gist: Joseph sees Benjamin, blesses him, weeps, and then seats the brothers by age and serves them generously.

44.summary: Joseph tests his brothers by having his silver cup planted in Benjamin's sack, then sends his steward to accuse them of theft. When the cup is found, the brothers return to Egypt and Judah offers himself as a slave in Benjamin's place to spare their father Jacob further grief.

segments.title: Joseph's Cup Plot
segments.gist: Joseph commands his steward to fill the brothers' sacks with grain and money and to place his silver cup in Benjamin's sack.

segments.title: Steward Accuses Brothers
segments.gist: The steward overtakes the brothers, accuses them of theft, and searches their sacks, finding the cup in Benjamin's sack.

segments.title: Brothers Return to Joseph
segments.gist: The brothers return to Joseph, bow before him, and Joseph declares that only the one found with the cup will be his servant.

segments.title: Judah's Plea for Benjamin
segments.gist: Judah recounts the family's history to Joseph and offers himself as a slave in Benjamin's place to protect their father Jacob.

45.summary: Joseph can no longer restrain himself before his brothers and reveals his identity to them, weeping aloud. He reassures them that God sent him ahead to preserve life, and he sends them back to Canaan to bring Jacob and their families to Egypt, where Pharaoh promises them the best of the land. The brothers return with wagons and provisions, and Jacob's spirit revives when he sees them and hears Joseph's words.

segments.title: Joseph Reveals Himself
segments.gist: Joseph weeps loudly and tells his brothers, 'I am Joseph,' asking if their father still lives; they are terrified.

segments.title: God Sent Me to Preserve Life
segments.gist: Joseph comforts them, saying God sent him ahead to preserve life and save them by a great deliverance.

segments.title: Bring Jacob to Egypt
segments.gist: Joseph instructs them to bring Jacob and all their families to Goshen, promising to provide for them during the five remaining years of famine.

segments.title: Pharaoh's Invitation
segments.gist: Pharaoh is pleased and tells Joseph to send wagons and invite Jacob's family to settle in the best of Egypt.

segments.title: Brothers Sent with Provisions
segments.gist: Joseph gives them wagons, provisions, changes of clothes, and gifts for Benjamin, then sends them away, warning them not to quarrel.

segments.title: Jacob Revived by the News
segments.gist: The brothers return to Canaan and tell Jacob that Joseph is alive and ruler of Egypt; Jacob's spirit revives when he sees the wagons.

46.summary: Jacob sets out for Egypt with his family and possessions, and God speaks to him at Beersheba, promising to go with him and make him a great nation there. The chapter lists Jacob's descendants who went to Egypt, and Jacob is reunited with Joseph, who instructs his brothers on how to present themselves to Pharaoh.

segments.title: Jacob journeys to Egypt
segments.gist: Jacob travels to Beersheba, offers sacrifices, and God speaks to him in a vision, promising to go with him to Egypt and bring him back.

segments.title: Jacob's descendants listed
segments.gist: The descendants of Jacob who went to Egypt are listed by their mothers and tribes, totaling seventy persons.

segments.title: Joseph meets Jacob and instructs brothers
segments.gist: Jacob sends Judah ahead, Joseph meets his father and weeps, and Joseph tells his brothers to say they are shepherds so they may settle in Goshen.

47.summary: Joseph presents five of his brothers and his father Jacob to Pharaoh, who grants them the land of Goshen. Jacob blesses Pharaoh and settles in Egypt, while Joseph manages the famine by buying up land and livestock for Pharaoh, reducing the Egyptians to servitude and establishing a tax of one-fifth. Jacob, nearing death, makes Joseph swear to bury him in Canaan, and Joseph swears to do so.

segments.title: Joseph presents brothers to Pharaoh
segments.gist: Joseph brings five brothers before Pharaoh, who grants them permission to settle in Goshen and appoints some as overseers of his livestock.

segments.title: Jacob blesses Pharaoh
segments.gist: Joseph brings his father Jacob to Pharaoh; Jacob blesses Pharaoh and tells him his years are few and evil compared to his ancestors.

segments.title: Joseph buys land for Pharaoh
segments.gist: Joseph collects all money, livestock, and land from the Egyptians in exchange for food, making them servants to Pharaoh and instituting a one-fifth tax on produce.

segments.title: Jacob makes Joseph swear
segments.gist: Israel dwells in Goshen and grows; Jacob, nearing death, makes Joseph swear to bury him in Canaan, and Joseph swears to do so.

48.summary: Joseph brings his sons Manasseh and Ephraim to his dying father Jacob, who adopts them as his own and blesses them. Jacob crosses his hands to give the greater blessing to the younger Ephraim, despite Joseph's objection, and foretells that Ephraim will become greater than Manasseh. Jacob then gives Joseph a special portion of land above his brothers.

segments.title: Joseph brings sons to Jacob
segments.gist: Joseph is told his father is sick and brings his sons Manasseh and Ephraim; Jacob recalls God's promise to him at Luz.

segments.title: Jacob adopts and blesses them
segments.gist: Jacob formally adopts Ephraim and Manasseh as his own sons and blesses them, then receives them from Joseph's knees.

segments.title: Jacob crosses hands to bless
segments.gist: Joseph positions his sons, but Jacob crosses his hands, giving the greater blessing to Ephraim; Joseph objects, but Jacob insists Ephraim will be greater.

segments.title: Jacob gives Joseph a portion
segments.gist: Jacob tells Joseph that God will be with them and gives Joseph a special portion above his brothers.

49.summary: Jacob gathers his twelve sons to bless them and foretell their futures, giving distinct pronouncements to Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Zebulun, Issachar, Dan, Gad, Asher, Naphtali, Joseph, and Benjamin. He then charges them to bury him in the cave of Machpelah and dies, and Joseph has him embalmed.

segments.title: Jacob Calls Sons to Bless
segments.gist: Jacob summons his sons to tell them what will befall them in the last days.

segments.title: Reuben, Simeon, Levi Rebuked
segments.gist: Reuben loses preeminence for defiling his father's bed; Simeon and Levi are cursed for their anger and violence.

segments.title: Judah's Blessing and Rule
segments.gist: Judah is praised, given dominion over enemies, and promised the scepter until Shiloh comes.

segments.title: Blessings on Six Sons
segments.gist: Zebulun, Issachar, Dan, Gad, Asher, and Naphtali receive brief prophetic blessings.

segments.title: Joseph and Benjamin Blessed
segments.gist: Joseph receives abundant blessings from God and men; Benjamin is described as a ravenous wolf.

segments.title: Jacob's Burial Charge and Death
segments.gist: Jacob commands his sons to bury him in the cave of Machpelah and then dies.

50.summary: After Jacob's death, Joseph has him embalmed and buried in Canaan, mourning with Egypt. Joseph reassures his brothers that he will not take revenge for their past betrayal, and he lives to see his great-grandchildren. The book ends with Joseph's death and his oath that God will bring Israel back to the promised land.

segments.title: Jacob's burial in Canaan
segments.gist: Joseph mourns Jacob, has him embalmed, and with Pharaoh's permission buries him in the cave of Machpelah.

segments.title: Joseph reassures his brothers
segments.gist: Fearing revenge, Joseph's brothers plead for forgiveness; Joseph weeps and promises to provide for them, saying God meant it for good.

segments.title: Joseph's old age and death
segments.gist: Joseph lives to see Ephraim's and Manasseh's children, then makes Israel swear to carry his bones to Canaan and dies at 110.

1.summary: Exodus 1 recounts the growth of Jacob's descendants in Egypt after Joseph's death, the new Pharaoh's fear of their numbers, and his escalating oppression through forced labor and the command to kill Hebrew male infants.

segments.title: Israelites multiply in Egypt
segments.gist: The sons of Israel multiply greatly in Egypt, and a new Pharaoh who does not know Joseph becomes afraid of their numbers.

segments.title: Egyptians enslave Israelites
segments.gist: Pharaoh sets taskmasters over the Israelites, forcing them into hard labor with brick and mortar, but the more they are oppressed, the more they multiply.

segments.title: Midwives defy Pharaoh's order
segments.gist: Pharaoh orders the Hebrew midwives to kill male infants, but they fear God and let the boys live, so God blesses them.

2.summary: A Levite woman hides her baby boy for three months, then places him in a basket among the reeds of the Nile, where Pharaoh's daughter finds and adopts him; the child's sister arranges for his own mother to nurse him. Grown up, Moses kills an Egyptian who was beating a Hebrew, flees to Midian, and marries Zipporah, daughter of the priest of Midian, and God hears the groaning of the enslaved Israelites.

segments.title: Baby hidden and found by princess
segments.gist: A Levite woman hides her infant son, then sets him in a basket in the Nile reeds, where Pharaoh's daughter discovers and pities him.

segments.title: Sister arranges mother as nurse
segments.gist: The baby's sister offers to find a Hebrew nurse, brings the child's own mother, and Pharaoh's daughter adopts the boy, naming him Moses.

segments.title: Moses kills Egyptian and flees
segments.gist: Grown Moses kills an Egyptian beating a Hebrew, tries to reconcile two Hebrews who expose the deed, and flees from Pharaoh to Midian.

segments.title: Moses rescues shepherdesses and marries
segments.gist: Moses helps the daughters of the priest of Midian water their flock, is invited to stay, and marries Zipporah, who bears him a son, Gershom.

segments.title: God hears Israel's groaning
segments.gist: The Israelites groan under bondage, and God hears, remembers his covenant, and takes notice of them.

3.summary: While tending his father-in-law's flock at Mount Horeb, Moses sees a bush burning without being consumed and hears God call him from it. God declares that he has seen Israel's affliction in Egypt and will send Moses to bring the people out, giving him signs and revealing his name.

segments.title: The Burning Bush
segments.gist: Moses leads the flock to Horeb, sees a bush burning but not consumed, and turns aside to look; God calls to him from the bush.

segments.title: God's Commission to Moses
segments.gist: God declares he has seen Israel's affliction, will deliver them to a good land, and sends Moses to Pharaoh to bring the people out.

segments.title: God Reveals His Name
segments.gist: Moses asks who he is and what God's name is; God promises to be with him and reveals his name as I AM THAT I AM.

segments.title: Instructions for the Elders
segments.gist: God instructs Moses to gather Israel's elders, tell them of the promised deliverance, and foretells that Pharaoh will resist until compelled by wonders and the people will plunder Egypt.

4.summary: God gives Moses three signs to convince Israel and reassures him about his slow speech, but Moses still protests; God's anger burns, and Aaron is appointed as his spokesman. Moses returns to Egypt with his family, and on the way God meets him and seeks to kill him until Zipporah circumcises her son. Aaron meets Moses, and together they gather the elders, perform the signs, and the people believe.

segments.title: Three signs given to Moses
segments.gist: God gives Moses three signs—a rod becoming a serpent, a leprous hand, and water turning to blood—so Israel may believe.

segments.title: Moses protests, Aaron appointed
segments.gist: Moses pleads that he is slow of speech; God rebukes him and appoints Aaron as his spokesman.

segments.title: Moses leaves for Egypt
segments.gist: Moses asks Jethro's leave, takes his family, and God tells him to perform signs before Pharaoh, whose firstborn will be killed.

segments.title: Zipporah circumcises her son
segments.gist: On the journey God seeks to kill Moses, and Zipporah circumcises her son, touching his feet with the foreskin.

segments.title: Aaron and Moses gather elders
segments.gist: Aaron meets Moses, they gather Israel's elders, perform the signs, and the people believe and worship.

5.summary: Moses and Aaron ask Pharaoh to let the Israelites go into the wilderness to worship, but Pharaoh refuses and accuses them of idleness. He retaliates by making the Israelites gather their own straw while maintaining the same quota of bricks, and the Israelite foremen are beaten when they fail. The foremen confront Moses, and Moses cries out to the LORD about the increased suffering of the people.

segments.title: Moses and Aaron before Pharaoh
segments.gist: Moses and Aaron tell Pharaoh that the LORD commands Israel's release for a wilderness feast, but Pharaoh denies knowing the LORD and refuses.

segments.title: Pharaoh increases the workload
segments.gist: Pharaoh accuses the Israelites of idleness and orders that they gather their own straw while still producing the same number of bricks.

segments.title: Israelites scattered for straw
segments.gist: The taskmasters force the Israelites to gather stubble for straw, and the Israelite foremen are beaten for failing to meet the daily brick quota.

segments.title: Foremen appeal to Pharaoh
segments.gist: The Israelite foremen protest to Pharaoh that they are being mistreated, but Pharaoh repeats that they are idle and insists the quota remain.

segments.title: Foremen confront Moses and Aaron
segments.gist: The foremen meet Moses and Aaron and blame them for making the Israelites odious to Pharaoh and his servants.

segments.title: Moses complains to the LORD
segments.gist: Moses returns to the LORD, asking why He has brought trouble on the people and why He sent him, since Pharaoh has only harmed them.

6.summary: God renews His covenant with Moses, promising to free the Israelites from Egyptian bondage and give them Canaan. Moses again doubts because of his poor speech, and a genealogy of Reuben, Simeon, and Levi leads to Aaron and Moses, whose mission to confront Pharaoh is restated.

segments.title: God reassures Moses with covenant promises
segments.gist: God speaks to Moses, reaffirms His covenant, and promises to deliver Israel from Egypt with great judgments.

segments.title: Moses doubts; God commands Pharaoh
segments.gist: Moses protests that Pharaoh and the Israelites won't listen, but God commands him and Aaron to bring Israel out.

segments.title: Genealogy of Reuben, Simeon, and Levi
segments.gist: The heads of Reuben, Simeon, and Levi are listed, focusing on Levi's descendants down to Aaron and Moses.

segments.title: Moses' speech impediment restated
segments.gist: God again commissions Moses, who repeats his concern about being a poor speaker.

7.summary: God reassures Moses that He has made him a god to Pharaoh and Aaron his prophet, and commands them to demand Israel's release. When Pharaoh demands a sign, Aaron's rod becomes a serpent, but Pharaoh's magicians duplicate it and his heart remains hard. God then instructs Moses to meet Pharaoh at the river and announce the first plague: the waters of Egypt will turn to blood, which happens, and the Egyptians are left unable to drink for seven days.

segments.title: God Appoints Moses and Aaron
segments.gist: God tells Moses he will be as God to Pharaoh, with Aaron as his spokesman, and commands them to demand Israel's release.

segments.title: Aaron's Rod Becomes a Serpent
segments.gist: Pharaoh asks for a sign; Aaron's rod becomes a serpent, but the magicians replicate it, and Pharaoh's heart hardens.

segments.title: God Announces the Plague of Blood
segments.gist: God instructs Moses to meet Pharaoh at the river and warn that the waters will turn to blood, killing the fish.

segments.title: The Waters Turn to Blood
segments.gist: Moses and Aaron strike the river, the water turns to blood, the magicians copy it, and Egyptians dig for drinking water for seven days.

8.summary: God continues the plagues on Egypt through Moses and Aaron: frogs cover the land, and Pharaoh asks for relief but hardens his heart once it comes; then lice and swarms of flies come, with Pharaoh bargaining and refusing to let the people go.

segments.title: Plague of Frogs
segments.gist: Moses and Aaron bring frogs upon Egypt; Pharaoh asks for prayer and relief, but hardens his heart when the frogs die.

segments.title: Plague of Lice
segments.gist: Aaron strikes the dust and lice infest man and beast; the magicians cannot replicate it and call it the finger of God.

segments.title: Plague of Flies
segments.gist: Swarms of flies fill Egypt except Goshen; Pharaoh negotiates but refuses to let Israel go, and the plague remains.

9.summary: God sends the fifth, sixth, and seventh plagues on Egypt—livestock disease, boils, and hail—after Pharaoh again refuses to let Israel go. Moses warns Pharaoh each time, and though some Egyptians fear God's word, Pharaoh's heart remains hardened after each plague.

segments.title: Plague on Livestock
segments.gist: God sends a deadly disease on Egyptian livestock, but Israel's animals are spared; Pharaoh's heart stays hard.

segments.title: Plague of Boils
segments.gist: Moses sprinkles ashes, causing boils on Egyptians and magicians, but Pharaoh remains unyielding.

segments.title: Warning of Hail
segments.gist: God warns of a devastating hailstorm and urges Egyptians to shelter their livestock; some heed the warning.

segments.title: Hail Strikes Egypt
segments.gist: Moses stretches his rod and hail destroys crops and livestock in Egypt, but Israel's land is spared.

segments.title: Pharaoh Confesses and Hardens
segments.gist: Pharaoh admits sin and asks for prayer, but once the hail stops, he and his servants harden their hearts again.

10.summary: God sends the eighth and ninth plagues on Egypt—locusts and thick darkness—after Pharaoh repeatedly refuses to let Israel go. Pharaoh's officials urge him to relent, and he offers compromises, but God hardens his heart so the signs may be told to future generations.

segments.title: Locusts announced to Pharaoh
segments.gist: God tells Moses to warn Pharaoh that locusts will cover the land and eat everything left after the hail, so Israel may know God's power.

segments.title: Pharaoh's servants object
segments.gist: Pharaoh's officials ask how long he will be a snare and urge him to let Israel go; Pharaoh offers only the men, and Moses and Aaron are driven out.

segments.title: Locusts cover Egypt
segments.gist: Moses stretches his rod and an east wind brings locusts that devour all plants; Pharaoh briefly confesses and asks for prayer, but hardens his heart again after the locusts are removed.

segments.title: Darkness and final refusal
segments.gist: Moses stretches his hand and thick darkness covers Egypt for three days; Pharaoh offers to let the people go without their flocks, then threatens Moses, who declares they will not meet again.

11.summary: God tells Moses he will bring one final plague on Egypt—the death of the firstborn—after which Pharaoh will let Israel go. Moses warns Pharaoh of this plague, and the chapter ends with Pharaoh still hardened.

segments.title: God Announces Final Plague
segments.gist: God instructs Moses to tell the Israelites to borrow jewels from the Egyptians, and promises one more plague will make Pharaoh release them.

segments.title: Moses Warns Pharaoh
segments.gist: Moses declares that at midnight God will strike dead all firstborn in Egypt, from Pharaoh's son to the slave's, and a great cry will arise.

segments.title: Pharaoh's Heart Hardened
segments.gist: The Lord tells Moses Pharaoh will not listen, so that God's wonders may multiply, and Pharaoh's heart remains hardened.

12.summary: God institutes the Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread, commanding each household to sacrifice a lamb and mark their doorposts with its blood so the destroyer will pass over them. At midnight the firstborn of Egypt are struck down, and Pharaoh finally urges the Israelites to leave. The chapter closes with instructions for a perpetual Passover observance and the record of the Israelites' departure from Egypt after 430 years.

segments.title: Passover Lamb and Blood
segments.gist: God commands each household to take a lamb, kill it, and mark their doorposts with its blood so the destroyer will pass over them.

segments.title: Feast of Unleavened Bread
segments.gist: God ordains a seven-day feast of unleavened bread and warns that anyone eating leaven must be cut off from Israel.

segments.title: Moses Instructs Elders
segments.gist: Moses relays the Passover instructions to the elders, and the people bow in worship and obey.

segments.title: Firstborn of Egypt Struck
segments.gist: At midnight the Lord strikes down all the firstborn of Egypt, and Pharaoh urgently sends the Israelites away with silver and gold.

segments.title: Israelites Depart from Egypt
segments.gist: The Israelites journey from Rameses to Succoth, and the chapter notes the 430 years and the night of watching.

segments.title: Passover Regulations
segments.gist: God gives further rules about who may eat the Passover and requires that no bone of the lamb be broken.

13.summary: God commands Moses to consecrate every firstborn male to Him and to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread as a memorial of the Exodus. Moses instructs the people to explain these practices to their children and to redeem firstborn donkeys and sons. God leads Israel out of Egypt by a pillar of cloud and fire, guiding them toward the Red Sea rather than the shorter Philistine road.

segments.title: Consecration of Firstborn
segments.gist: The LORD tells Moses to set apart every firstborn male, both man and beast, as belonging to Him.

segments.title: Feast of Unleavened Bread
segments.gist: Moses instructs the people to remember the Exodus by eating unleavened bread for seven days and keeping the feast as a memorial.

segments.title: Redeeming Firstborn Sons
segments.gist: Moses explains that firstborn males and donkeys must be redeemed, and that sons should be told how God delivered Israel from Egypt.

segments.title: Moses Carries Joseph's Bones
segments.gist: God leads Israel by the Red Sea rather than through Philistine land, and Moses takes Joseph's bones as the Israelites had sworn.

segments.title: Pillar of Cloud and Fire
segments.gist: God goes before Israel in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night, never leaving them.

14.summary: God leads Israel from Succoth to Pi-hahiroth, then hardens Pharaoh's heart so he pursues them with his army. Trapped between the Red Sea and the Egyptians, the people panic, but Moses declares God will fight for them. God parts the sea, Israel crosses on dry ground, and the returning waters destroy the Egyptian army.

segments.title: God leads Israel to Pi-hahiroth
segments.gist: God directs Moses to camp by the sea, and Pharaoh is told that Israel is entangled in the wilderness.

segments.title: Pharaoh pursues Israel
segments.gist: Pharaoh regrets letting Israel go and chases them with chariots and horsemen, overtaking them at Pi-hahiroth.

segments.title: Moses reassures the fearful people
segments.gist: The Israelites cry out in fear, but Moses tells them to stand still and see the LORD's salvation.

segments.title: God instructs Moses and the cloud moves
segments.gist: God tells Moses to stretch out his rod, and the pillar of cloud moves between Israel and the Egyptians.

segments.title: The sea parts and Egypt is troubled
segments.gist: Moses stretches out his hand, the sea divides, Israel crosses on dry ground, and the Egyptians are thrown into confusion.

segments.title: The waters return and Israel is saved
segments.gist: At God's command Moses stretches out his hand, the waters cover the Egyptian army, and Israel sees the great deliverance.

15.summary: After Israel's deliverance at the Red Sea, Moses and the Israelites sing a victory song celebrating God as a warrior who threw Pharaoh's chariots into the sea. The song is followed by the women's dance led by Miriam. The people then travel three days without water, and at Marah the bitter water is made sweet. God promises to protect them from diseases if they obey, and they camp at Elim, where there are twelve wells and seventy palm trees.

segments.title: Moses' Song of Victory
segments.gist: Moses and the Israelites sing praise to God for drowning Pharaoh's army in the Red Sea.

segments.title: God Leads and Plants Israel
segments.gist: The song continues, describing God guiding the people to his holy dwelling and planting them on his mountain.

segments.title: Miriam Leads the Women
segments.gist: Miriam the prophetess leads the women in dancing with timbrels, singing that God has triumphed gloriously.

segments.title: Bitter Water Made Sweet
segments.gist: The people travel three days without water, complain at Marah, and Moses cries to God, who shows him a tree to sweeten the water; God promises health if they obey, and they camp at Elim.

16.summary: After leaving Elim, the Israelites journey into the wilderness of Sin and complain of hunger, longing for the fleshpots of Egypt. God promises to rain bread from heaven and sends quail in the evening and manna in the morning, with instructions to gather only enough for each day and double on the sixth day. Moses rebukes their murmuring, and the chapter ends with the manna being preserved before the LORD and the people eating it for forty years.

segments.title: Israelites Murmur in Wilderness
segments.gist: The congregation journeys from Elim to the wilderness of Sin and complains to Moses and Aaron about hunger.

segments.title: God Promises Bread and Quail
segments.gist: God tells Moses He will rain bread from heaven and send quail, and His glory appears to the murmuring people.

segments.title: Quail and Manna Provided
segments.gist: Quail cover the camp in the evening, and manna appears in the morning; the people gather it, some keeping leftovers that breed worms.

segments.title: Sabbath Gathering Instructions
segments.gist: On the sixth day the people gather double, and Moses explains that the seventh day is a holy Sabbath for rest.

segments.title: Manna Described and Preserved
segments.gist: The manna is described as white and tasting like wafers with honey, and a pot of it is kept before the LORD for future generations.

17.summary: Israel camps at Rephidim with no water, and the people quarrel with Moses; God has Moses strike the rock at Horeb to bring forth water. Then Amalek attacks, and Joshua leads the fight while Moses holds up his hands with the rod, aided by Aaron and Hur, until Israel prevails; God declares war against Amalek and Moses builds an altar.

segments.title: Water from the Rock at Rephidim
segments.gist: The people thirst and quarrel with Moses; God instructs him to strike the rock at Horeb, and water comes out.

segments.title: Israel Defeats Amalek
segments.gist: Joshua fights Amalek while Moses holds up the rod; when his hands are heavy, Aaron and Hur support them, and Israel wins.

segments.title: God's War Against Amalek
segments.gist: God commands Moses to write the curse on Amalek, and Moses builds an altar called Jehovah-nissi.

18.summary: Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, visits the Israelite camp at Mount Sinai, bringing Moses' wife and sons. After hearing how God delivered Israel from Egypt, Jethro rejoices and offers sacrifice. The next day he observes Moses judging the people alone from morning to evening and advises him to delegate authority to capable men over groups of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens, reserving only the hardest cases for himself. Moses follows the counsel, and Jethro returns to his own land.

segments.title: Jethro visits Moses
segments.gist: Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, comes to the wilderness camp with Moses' wife and two sons, and Moses welcomes him.

segments.title: Moses recounts God's deliverance
segments.gist: Moses tells Jethro how the Lord delivered Israel from Egypt and sustained them in the wilderness, and Jethro rejoices and blesses God.

segments.title: Jethro sees Moses judging
segments.gist: Jethro observes Moses sitting to judge the people all day and warns that the burden is too heavy for him alone.

segments.title: Jethro advises delegation
segments.gist: Jethro counsels Moses to appoint capable men over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens to judge the people, handling only the great matters himself.

segments.title: Moses follows the counsel
segments.gist: Moses heeds Jethro's advice, appoints leaders, and then lets Jethro depart to his own land.

19.summary: Israel arrives at Mount Sinai three months after leaving Egypt. God calls Moses up the mountain and offers a covenant: if the people obey, they will be a treasured possession and a kingdom of priests. After the people agree, God descends on the mountain in fire and smoke, and Moses is told to warn the people not to break through the boundary.

segments.title: Israel camps at Sinai
segments.gist: Israel arrives at the wilderness of Sinai and camps before the mountain.

segments.title: God offers covenant at Sinai
segments.gist: God tells Moses to remind Israel of deliverance from Egypt and offers a covenant of obedience.

segments.title: People agree to obey
segments.gist: Moses relays God's words; the people promise obedience, and God plans to speak from a cloud.

segments.title: People consecrate and approach mountain
segments.gist: God commands consecration and sets bounds around the mountain; Moses instructs the people.

segments.title: God descends in fire and smoke
segments.gist: On the third day, thunder, lightning, and smoke signal God's descent; Moses is called to the top.

segments.title: Warning against breaking bounds
segments.gist: God warns Moses that the people must not break through to see, and Moses returns to warn them.
