20.summary: God speaks the Ten Commandments to Israel from Mount Sinai, forbidding other gods, idols, and misuse of His name, and commanding Sabbath rest and honor to parents. The people tremble at the thunder and smoke and beg Moses to speak to them instead of God, while Moses builds an altar and forbids carved gods.

segments.title: God's preface and first commandment
segments.gist: God identifies Himself as the deliverer from Egypt and commands Israel to have no other gods before Him.

segments.title: Commandments against idols
segments.gist: God forbids making graven images or bowing to them, describing Himself as jealous and showing mercy to those who love Him.

segments.title: Name, Sabbath, and creation
segments.gist: God forbids taking His name in vain and commands the seventh day as a Sabbath of rest, grounded in the six days of creation.

segments.title: Commands on family and neighbors
segments.gist: God commands honor to parents and forbids murder, adultery, theft, false witness, and coveting.

segments.title: People fear and Moses reassures
segments.gist: The people see thunder, lightning, and smoke and stand afar off, asking Moses to speak to them instead of God.

segments.title: Altar instructions
segments.gist: God forbids making silver or gold gods alongside Him and gives rules for building an altar of earth or unhewn stone.

21.summary: God gives Moses a set of civil ordinances for Israel: rules on Hebrew servants and their release, capital offenses and penalties for violence, injury to slaves and pregnant women, restitution for property damage and theft, and laws on oxen that gore and the responsibility of their owners.

segments.title: Laws on Hebrew servants
segments.gist: Rules for buying a Hebrew servant, his release in the seventh year, and provisions for his wife and children.

segments.title: Capital offenses and penalties
segments.gist: Death penalties for striking or cursing parents, murder, and kidnapping, with cities of refuge for unintentional killing.

segments.title: Injuries and their penalties
segments.gist: Penalties for causing injury, including striking a servant, causing a miscarriage, and the law of retaliation.

segments.title: Laws on goring oxen
segments.gist: Rules for an ox that gores a person, including the owner's liability and the penalty for a goring ox that was known to be dangerous.

segments.title: Laws on pits and oxen
segments.gist: Restitution for opening a pit or for an ox that kills another ox, with full compensation required.

22.summary: Exodus 22 continues the covenant code with case laws on property, restitution, and social responsibility. It addresses theft, damage by grazing or fire, safekeeping disputes, seduction, and the treatment of strangers, widows, orphans, and the poor. The chapter ends with commands about firstfruits, holiness, and dietary restrictions.

segments.title: Laws on Theft and Restitution
segments.gist: Rules for restitution when a thief steals an ox or sheep, including multiple-fold repayment and provisions if the thief is killed.

segments.title: Damage by Grazing and Fire
segments.gist: Laws requiring restitution when animals graze in another's field or when a fire spreads and destroys crops.

segments.title: Property Held in Trust
segments.gist: Cases of money or goods entrusted to a neighbor and stolen, lost, or injured, with rules for oaths and restitution.

segments.title: Seduction of a Virgin
segments.gist: A man who seduces an unbetrothed virgin must endow her as his wife, unless her father refuses.

segments.title: Capital Crimes and Oppression
segments.gist: Death penalties for sorcery, bestiality, and idolatry, and warnings against oppressing strangers, widows, and orphans.

segments.title: Laws on Lending, Justice, and Offerings
segments.gist: Commands about lending to the poor without interest, returning pledges, giving firstfruits, and being holy.

23.summary: Exodus 23 continues the covenant laws given at Sinai, covering judicial integrity, treatment of enemies and the poor, annual feasts, the promise of an angel to lead Israel, and the covenant conditions for possessing the land.

segments.title: Laws of Justice and Mercy
segments.gist: Rules against false reports, mob injustice, partiality to the poor, and commands to help an enemy's straying animal and to give the poor rest on the Sabbath.

segments.title: Sabbath Year and Sabbath Day
segments.gist: Instructions for letting the land rest every seventh year and for ceasing work on the seventh day, with a warning against invoking other gods.

segments.title: Three Annual Feasts
segments.gist: Commands for all males to appear before God three times a year at the Feasts of Unleavened Bread, Harvest, and Ingathering, with rules for sacrifices and firstfruits.

segments.title: Promise of an Angel Guide
segments.gist: God promises to send an angel to lead Israel into the land, warns them to obey his voice, and assures blessings of protection, provision, and health if they serve God alone.

segments.title: Conquest and Covenant Boundaries
segments.gist: God promises to drive out the inhabitants gradually, sets Israel's borders, and forbids making covenants with the land's inhabitants or serving their gods.

24.summary: God calls Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy elders up Mount Sinai, where they see the God of Israel and eat a covenant meal. Moses then goes further up to receive the stone tablets of the law, leaving Aaron and Hur in charge, and the glory of the Lord appears as a consuming fire on the mountain for forty days and nights.

segments.title: Covenant ratified and elders see God
segments.gist: Moses reads the book of the covenant, the people promise obedience, and Moses sprinkles blood; then Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy elders go up and see God and eat and drink.

segments.title: Elders behold God and feast
segments.gist: The elders see the God of Israel with a paved sapphire work under His feet, yet He does not harm them; they eat and drink in His presence.

segments.title: Moses called up for tablets
segments.gist: The Lord tells Moses to come up to receive the stone tablets of the law and commandment, and Moses leaves Aaron and Hur to judge the people while he goes up.

segments.title: Glory cloud and consuming fire
segments.gist: Moses goes up into the cloud covering Mount Sinai, and the glory of the Lord appears as a consuming fire while Moses remains on the mountain forty days and nights.

25.summary: God gives Moses instructions on Mount Sinai for building the tabernacle and its furnishings. The chapter details the collection of materials, the construction of the ark, table, and lampstand, and the pattern for the tabernacle itself.

segments.title: Offerings for the Tabernacle
segments.gist: God tells Moses to collect freewill offerings of gold, silver, bronze, and other materials for the tabernacle and its service.

segments.title: The Ark and Mercy Seat
segments.gist: Instructions for building the ark of acacia wood overlaid with gold, with a mercy seat and two cherubim above it.

segments.title: The Table for Showbread
segments.gist: Specifications for a table of acacia wood overlaid with gold, including its dishes, pans, and the showbread set before God.

segments.title: The Golden Lampstand
segments.gist: Details for making a pure gold lampstand with branches, cups, and lamps, along with the pattern for the tabernacle.

26.summary: God gives Moses detailed instructions for constructing the tabernacle, including the curtains of fine linen and goats' hair, the covering of rams' skins and badgers' skins, the boards and sockets for the walls, and the veil separating the holy place from the most holy place. The chapter concludes with specifications for the hanging at the entrance of the tabernacle.

segments.title: Curtains of fine linen
segments.gist: Instructions for making ten curtains of fine twined linen with cherubim, joined by loops and taches of gold.

segments.title: Curtains of goats' hair
segments.gist: Eleven curtains of goats' hair for the tent covering, with loops and taches of brass, plus coverings of rams' skins and badgers' skins.

segments.title: Boards and sockets
segments.gist: Instructions for the boards of shittim wood standing in sockets of silver, with bars to hold them together.

segments.title: Veil and mercy seat
segments.gist: A veil of blue, purple, and scarlet with cherubim to separate the holy place from the most holy place, where the ark and mercy seat are placed.

segments.title: Entrance hanging
segments.gist: A hanging for the tabernacle door of blue, purple, and scarlet, with five pillars and sockets of brass.

27.summary: Exodus 27 continues God's instructions to Moses on Mount Sinai concerning the tabernacle. It specifies the construction of the bronze altar for burnt offerings, the court surrounding the tabernacle with its hangings and gate, and the command to use pure olive oil for the lampstand's continual light.

segments.title: The Bronze Altar
segments.gist: Instructions for building the altar of burnt offering with its horns, grating, rings, and poles.

segments.title: The Court of the Tabernacle
segments.gist: Specifications for the court's hangings, pillars, sockets, and the gate with its curtain.

segments.title: Oil for the Lamp
segments.gist: Command for Israel to provide pure olive oil for the lampstand to burn continually before the Lord.

28.summary: God gives Moses detailed instructions for making the sacred garments of the priests: the ephod, breastplate, robe, and other items for Aaron and his sons, specifying materials, design, and the placement of the Urim and Thummim and the engraved stones.

segments.title: Set apart Aaron and sons
segments.gist: God commands Moses to bring Aaron and his sons near to serve as priests and to make holy garments for glory and beauty.

segments.title: The ephod and its stones
segments.gist: Instructions for making the ephod of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet, with two onyx stones engraved with the names of Israel's sons.

segments.title: The breastplate of judgment
segments.gist: Directions for the breastplate with twelve precious stones set in gold, holding the Urim and Thummim over Aaron's heart.

segments.title: Robe, mitre, and coats
segments.gist: Instructions for the blue robe with pomegranates and bells, the golden plate on the mitre, and the embroidered coats and bonnets.

segments.title: Garments for Aaron's sons
segments.gist: Commands to make coats, girdles, and bonnets for Aaron's sons, and a linen breeches to cover their nakedness in the tabernacle.

29.summary: God gives Moses detailed instructions for consecrating Aaron and his sons as priests, including the sacrifices, the ordination ritual, and the consecration of the altar. The chapter concludes with promises of God's presence and the perpetual nature of the priesthood.

segments.title: Consecration of Priests and Garments
segments.gist: Moses is instructed to bring Aaron and his sons, along with the garments, anointing oil, and sacrificial animals, to the door of the tabernacle to consecrate them.

segments.title: Sin Offering for the Priests
segments.gist: Aaron and his sons lay hands on a bullock, which is slain as a sin offering; its blood is applied to the altar, and its flesh is burned outside the camp.

segments.title: Burnt Offering of the Ram
segments.gist: A ram is offered as a burnt offering, with its blood sprinkled on the altar and its parts burned as a sweet savor to the Lord.

segments.title: Ram of Consecration and Wave Offering
segments.gist: The second ram is slain; its blood is applied to the priests' right ear, thumb, and toe, and parts are waved before the Lord as a wave offering.

segments.title: Perpetual Priesthood and Altar Consecration
segments.gist: The holy garments are to be worn by succeeding priests; the ram of consecration is boiled and eaten by Aaron and his sons, and the altar is cleansed and consecrated for seven days.

segments.title: Daily Offerings and God's Presence
segments.gist: Two lambs are to be offered daily, morning and evening, with meal and drink offerings; God promises to dwell among the Israelites and be their God.

30.summary: God gives Moses instructions for building the altar of incense, the bronze laver, and the anointing oil and incense. He also commands a census tax of half a shekel and specifies the composition of the holy anointing oil and the incense.

segments.title: Altar of Incense
segments.gist: Instructions for making the golden altar of incense and the ritual for burning incense on it.

segments.title: Census Tax
segments.gist: Each Israelite counted in the census must pay half a shekel as an offering to the Lord.

segments.title: Bronze Laver
segments.gist: A bronze basin for washing is to be placed between the tabernacle and the altar for the priests to wash.

segments.title: Anointing Oil
segments.gist: Recipe for the holy anointing oil and instructions for anointing the tabernacle and its furnishings.

segments.title: Incense Recipe
segments.gist: Recipe for the sacred incense to be placed before the testimony in the tabernacle.

31.summary: God designates Bezaleel and Aholiab, filled with the Spirit, to build the tabernacle and its furnishings. He repeats the command to keep the Sabbath as a sign, and gives Moses the two stone tables of testimony written by God's finger.

segments.title: God calls Bezaleel and Aholiab
segments.gist: God names Bezaleel and Aholiab, fills them with the Spirit and skill, and assigns them to make the tabernacle and its furnishings.

segments.title: Sabbath command repeated
segments.gist: God commands Israel to keep the Sabbath as a sign and a perpetual covenant, with death as the penalty for violation.

32.summary: While Moses is on Mount Sinai receiving the law, the Israelites grow impatient and persuade Aaron to make a golden calf, which they worship. God threatens to destroy them, but Moses intercedes and comes down with the tablets, breaking them in anger. Moses confronts Aaron, calls for loyalty, and about three thousand men are killed by the Levites. Moses then returns to God to seek atonement for the people's sin.

segments.title: Golden Calf Made
segments.gist: The people ask Aaron for gods, and he fashions a golden calf from their earrings, which they hail as the god who brought them out of Egypt.

segments.title: God Threatens, Moses Intercedes
segments.gist: God tells Moses the people have corrupted themselves and threatens to destroy them, but Moses pleads, reminding God of His promises to the patriarchs, and God relents.

segments.title: Moses Breaks Tablets
segments.gist: Moses descends with the two tablets, hears Joshua's report of noise, sees the calf and dancing, and in anger breaks the tablets at the foot of the mountain.

segments.title: Aaron's Excuse
segments.gist: Moses confronts Aaron about the people's sin, and Aaron blames the people's evil nature and claims the calf emerged from the fire when he cast in the gold.

segments.title: Levites Slay Idolaters
segments.gist: Moses calls for those on the Lord's side, and the Levites gather; they kill about three thousand men, and Moses declares their consecration for obedience to God.

segments.title: Moses Seeks Atonement
segments.gist: Moses tells the people he will go to God to seek atonement, offers his own life for their sin, and God replies that He will blot out the sinners and plague the people.

33.summary: God tells Moses to lead the people on to Canaan but refuses to go with them because they are stiffnecked, and the people mourn. Moses pitches the tabernacle outside the camp and speaks with God face to face; he intercedes, asking for God's presence and to see His glory, and God grants a partial revelation while declaring His mercy and justice.

segments.title: God Withdraws His Presence
segments.gist: God tells Moses to lead Israel to Canaan but will not go among them, and the people mourn and strip off their ornaments.

segments.title: Moses Meets God in Tabernacle
segments.gist: Moses pitches the tabernacle outside the camp; the pillar of cloud descends, and God speaks with Moses face to face as a friend.

segments.title: Moses Pleads for God's Presence
segments.gist: Moses asks God to show him His way and to go with the people, and God agrees to do as Moses has asked.

segments.title: Moses Asks to See God's Glory
segments.gist: Moses requests to see God's glory; God promises to proclaim His name and show His goodness, but hides Moses in a rock cleft so he sees only His back.

34.summary: God renews the covenant with Israel after the golden calf incident, commanding Moses to cut new stone tablets. Moses ascends Mount Sinai, receives the divine proclamation of mercy and justice, and the covenant stipulations are restated. Moses' face shines after speaking with God, and he wears a veil.

segments.title: New Tablets and Covenant Renewal
segments.gist: God instructs Moses to cut two stone tablets and ascend Sinai, promising to drive out the nations and warning against idolatry.

segments.title: Covenant Obligations and Warnings
segments.gist: God commands Israel to destroy pagan altars, avoid intermarriage, and keep the feasts, emphasizing exclusive worship.

segments.title: Feasts and Firstborn Regulations
segments.gist: God reiterates laws about the Feast of Unleavened Bread, firstborn offerings, Sabbath, and pilgrimage festivals.

segments.title: Moses Writes the Covenant
segments.gist: Moses writes the words of the covenant on the tablets and spends forty days and nights with God.

segments.title: Moses' Shining Face
segments.gist: Moses descends with the tablets, his face shining, and he veils it when speaking to the people.

35.summary: Moses assembles the Israelites and reiterates the Sabbath law, then calls for freewill offerings of materials and skilled labor for the tabernacle. The people respond generously, bringing abundant supplies, and Moses appoints Bezaleel and Aholiab to oversee the construction.

segments.title: Sabbath Command Reiterated
segments.gist: Moses gathers the congregation and commands them to keep the Sabbath as a holy day of rest.

segments.title: Call for Freewill Offerings
segments.gist: Moses asks the people to bring voluntary offerings of gold, silver, bronze, yarn, linen, skins, and other materials for the tabernacle.

segments.title: Skilled Workers Summoned
segments.gist: Moses calls for wise-hearted artisans to make the tabernacle, its furnishings, and the priests' garments.

segments.title: People Bring Abundant Offerings
segments.gist: The Israelites, both men and women, bring freewill offerings of materials and gold for the Lord's work.

segments.title: Bezaleel and Aholiab Appointed
segments.gist: Moses declares that God has filled Bezaleel and Aholiab with the Spirit and skill for the construction and teaching.

36.summary: Moses assembles Bezaleel, Aholiab, and the skilled craftsmen, who receive the people's freewill offerings for the tabernacle. When the offerings exceed the need, Moses commands the people to stop giving. The craftsmen then construct the tabernacle curtains, coverings, boards, bars, and pillars according to the pattern shown to Moses.

segments.title: Moses commissions the craftsmen
segments.gist: Moses calls Bezaleel, Aholiab, and all skilled workers, who receive the people's freewill offerings for the tabernacle construction.

segments.title: Curtains of fine linen
segments.gist: The craftsmen make ten curtains of fine twined linen with blue, purple, and scarlet cherubim, joined by loops and golden clasps.

segments.title: Coverings of goats' hair and skins
segments.gist: They make eleven curtains of goats' hair for the tent, plus coverings of rams' skins and badgers' skins.

segments.title: Boards, sockets, and bars
segments.gist: They construct upright boards of shittim wood with silver sockets, and bars to hold the tabernacle frame together.

segments.title: Veil and hanging for the door
segments.gist: They make the inner veil and the outer hanging for the tabernacle door, with pillars and hooks overlaid with gold.

37.summary: Bezalel constructs the ark of the covenant, the mercy seat with its two cherubims, the table of shewbread, the golden candlestick, and the altar of incense, along with their associated vessels and the holy anointing oil and pure incense. The chapter details the materials and dimensions of each item, following the pattern shown to Moses on the mount.

segments.title: Bezalel Makes the Ark
segments.gist: Bezalel builds the ark of shittim wood, overlays it with gold, and makes the mercy seat with two cherubims of beaten gold.

segments.title: Bezalel Makes the Table
segments.gist: He constructs the table of shittim wood, overlays it with gold, and furnishes it with dishes, spoons, covers, and bowls of pure gold.

segments.title: Bezalel Makes the Candlestick
segments.gist: He makes the pure gold candlestick with its branches, bowls, knops, and flowers, along with its lamps and snuffers.

segments.title: Bezalel Makes the Incense Altar
segments.gist: He builds the altar of incense of shittim wood, overlays it with gold, and prepares the holy anointing oil and pure incense.

38.summary: Exodus 38 records the construction of the tabernacle's furnishings and courtyard: the altar of burnt offering, the bronze laver, the court hangings, and a summary of the metals used. It concludes with an inventory of the gold, silver, and bronze contributed and the listing of the craftsmen's work.

segments.title: Altar of Burnt Offering
segments.gist: Bezaleel makes the bronze altar, its utensils, and the bronze grating and rings.

segments.title: Tabernacle Courtyard
segments.gist: The court is constructed with hangings, pillars, sockets, and the gate screen on the south, north, west, and east sides.

segments.title: Inventory of Tabernacle
segments.gist: The sum of the tabernacle's materials is recorded under Ithamar, with Bezaleel and Aholiab overseeing the work.

segments.title: Metals Offered
segments.gist: The amounts of gold, silver, and bronze used in the sanctuary are listed, including the silver from the census and the bronze for sockets and pins.

39.summary: The chapter describes the making of the priests' garments—the ephod, breastplate, robe, tunics, and related items—according to Moses' instructions, and concludes with Moses inspecting all the work and blessing the people because it was done as the LORD commanded.

segments.title: Making the ephod
segments.gist: Bezalel makes the ephod of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet, with onyx stones engraved with the names of Israel's sons.

segments.title: Making the breastplate
segments.gist: The breastplate is made with twelve precious stones set in gold, attached to the ephod by chains and cords.

segments.title: Making the robe
segments.gist: The robe of the ephod is woven entirely of blue, with pomegranates and bells around its hem.

segments.title: Making tunics and girdles
segments.gist: Fine linen tunics, caps, and girdles are made for Aaron and his sons.

segments.title: Making the crown plate
segments.gist: A plate of pure gold is engraved with 'Holiness to the LORD' and fastened to the mitre with a blue lace.

segments.title: Tabernacle work completed
segments.gist: All the work of the tabernacle is finished; Moses inspects it, sees it done as the LORD commanded, and blesses the people.

40.summary: God commands Moses to set up the tabernacle on the first day of the first month and to anoint it and its furnishings. After Moses completes the work, the cloud covers the tent of meeting and the glory of the LORD fills the tabernacle, guiding the Israelites on their journeys.

segments.title: God's instructions for tabernacle setup
segments.gist: The LORD tells Moses to set up the tabernacle, place the ark, table, lampstand, and altars, and anoint everything with oil.

segments.title: Moses completes the tabernacle work
segments.gist: Moses sets up the tabernacle, places all its furnishings, and finishes the work as the LORD commanded.

segments.title: Cloud and glory fill the tabernacle
segments.gist: The cloud covers the tent and God's glory fills the tabernacle; the cloud guides Israel's journeys.

1.summary: God calls to Moses from the tabernacle and gives instructions for the burnt offering, the first of the offerings Israel is to bring. The chapter details how a worshipper is to present a bull, a sheep or goat, or a bird, with the priest handling the blood and the fire consuming the offering as a sweet savour to the Lord.

segments.title: God speaks from the tabernacle
segments.gist: The Lord calls to Moses from the tent of meeting and gives the rule for offerings brought to him.

segments.title: Burnt offering of a bull
segments.gist: A man bringing a bull without blemish lays his hand on it, kills it, and the priest offers the blood and burns the parts.

segments.title: Burnt offering of a sheep or goat
segments.gist: If the offering is a sheep or goat, it must be without blemish and is killed and burned in the same way.

segments.title: Burnt offering of a bird
segments.gist: If the offering is a turtledove or young pigeon, the priest wrings off its head, drains the blood, and burns it on the altar.

2.summary: This chapter gives instructions for the grain offering (meat offering) in Israel's worship: fine flour with oil and frankincense, baked or pan-cooked cakes, and the requirement of salt and no leaven or honey, with a portion burned and the rest given to the priests.

segments.title: Uncooked grain offering
segments.gist: Fine flour with oil and frankincense is offered, and a memorial portion is burned.

segments.title: Baked and pan offerings
segments.gist: Rules for oven-baked cakes, pan-cooked cakes, and the portion burned and given to priests.

segments.title: No leaven or honey; salt required
segments.gist: No leaven or honey may be burned, but salt of the covenant must accompany the offering.

segments.title: Firstfruits grain offering
segments.gist: Green ears of corn dried, with oil and frankincense, are offered as firstfruits.

3.summary: Leviticus 3 gives the law of the peace offering, describing how a worshiper may present an animal from the herd or the flock—male or female without blemish—and how its fat portions, kidneys, and liver lobe are burned on the altar as a food offering to the LORD, while the breast and right thigh are given to the priests. The chapter emphasizes that all the fat belongs to the LORD and that the blood must not be eaten.

segments.title: Peace offering from the herd
segments.gist: If the offering is a peace offering from the herd, the worshiper lays hands on a male or female without blemish, kills it at the tabernacle door, and the priests burn the fat and entrails on the altar.

segments.title: Peace offering from the flock
segments.gist: If the offering is from the flock, a male or female without blemish is presented, killed before the tabernacle, and its fat portions are burned as a food offering to the LORD.

segments.title: Peace offering of a goat
segments.gist: If the offering is a goat, it is presented before the LORD, killed, and its fat portions are burned on the altar as a food offering, with all fat belonging to the LORD.

4.summary: Leviticus 4 gives the law of the sin offering for unintentional sins. It specifies different procedures for the anointed priest, the whole congregation, a ruler, and a common person, each requiring a bullock, goat, or lamb according to status, with blood applied to the altar and the fat burned.

segments.title: Introduction to Sin Offering
segments.gist: The LORD speaks to Moses, stating that if a soul sins through ignorance against any commandment, an offering must be brought.

segments.title: Sin Offering for the Priest
segments.gist: If the anointed priest sins, he must bring a young bullock without blemish, lay his hands on it, kill it, and apply its blood before the veil and on the altar of incense.

segments.title: Sin Offering for the Congregation
segments.gist: If the whole congregation sins ignorantly, they must bring a young bullock, the elders lay their hands on it, and the priest makes atonement with its blood and fat.

segments.title: Sin Offering for a Ruler
segments.gist: If a ruler sins ignorantly, he must bring a kid of the goats without blemish, lay his hand on it, and the priest makes atonement with its blood and fat.

segments.title: Sin Offering for a Common Person
segments.gist: If a common person sins ignorantly, they must bring a female kid or lamb without blemish, lay hands on it, and the priest makes atonement with its blood and fat.

5.summary: Leviticus 5 continues the laws for offerings, specifying the guilt offering for sins committed unknowingly or against holy things, and the trespass offering for certain offenses against God or neighbors, including the case of a witness who withholds testimony. It details the required sacrifices according to the person's ability, and concludes with the procedure for the trespass offering involving a ram and restitution.

segments.title: Sin Offerings for Unintentional Sins
segments.gist: Laws for sin offerings when someone sins unintentionally or becomes guilty through an oath, including the requirement to confess and bring a female lamb or goat.

segments.title: Confession and Offering Required
segments.gist: The guilty person must confess the sin and bring a trespass offering to the Lord for the sin committed.

segments.title: Alternative Offerings for the Poor
segments.gist: If unable to afford a lamb, the person may bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a sin offering and one for a burnt offering.

segments.title: Grain Offering for the Very Poor
segments.gist: If unable to afford birds, a tenth part of an ephah of fine flour without oil or frankincense is acceptable as a sin offering.

segments.title: Trespass Offering for Holy Things
segments.gist: When someone sins unintentionally against the holy things of the Lord, they must bring a ram without blemish and make restitution plus a fifth.

segments.title: Trespass Offering for Unknown Sins
segments.gist: If someone sins unknowingly and is guilty, they must bring a ram without blemish as a trespass offering to make atonement.

6.summary: Leviticus 6 continues God's instructions to Moses for the priests, specifying the guilt offering for trespasses against a neighbor, the perpetual burnt offering on the altar, and the grain offering brought by priests. It also details the sin offering to be eaten by priests in the tabernacle court and the handling of its ashes.

segments.title: Guilt Offering for Trespass
segments.gist: God gives laws for the guilt offering when someone sins against a neighbor and must restore plus a fifth.

segments.title: Perpetual Burnt Offering
segments.gist: The burnt offering must burn all night on the altar, and the priest tends the fire each morning.

segments.title: Priests' Grain Offering
segments.gist: The grain offering of the priests is to be burned entirely, a perpetual ordinance.

segments.title: Anointing Grain Offering
segments.gist: On the day of anointing, the priest offers a grain offering, half in the morning and half in the evening.

segments.title: Sin Offering Regulations
segments.gist: The sin offering is most holy, eaten by priests in the tabernacle court, but blood is not brought inside.

7.summary: Leviticus 7 continues the instructions for the guilt offering and the peace offering, detailing the portions reserved for the priests and the rules for eating the sacrificial meat. It concludes with a summary of the offerings and the command that the fat and blood must not be eaten.

segments.title: Guilt Offering Rules
segments.gist: The guilt offering is most holy; its blood and fat are offered, and the priest receives the skin and grain offerings.

segments.title: Peace Offering Rules
segments.gist: The peace offering may be a thanksgiving, vow, or freewill offering, with rules for eating it and penalties for uncleanness.

segments.title: Fat and Blood Forbidden
segments.gist: The Israelites are forbidden to eat fat or blood on pain of being cut off from the people.

segments.title: Priests' Portions
segments.gist: The priest who offers the peace offering receives the breast and right shoulder as a heave and wave offering.

segments.title: Summary of Offerings
segments.gist: This is the portion of the anointing of Aaron and his sons, summarizing the offerings commanded on Mount Sinai.

8.summary: God commands Moses to ordain Aaron and his sons as priests. Moses washes and clothes them, anoints the tabernacle and Aaron, and offers the prescribed sacrifices. After a seven-day ordination period at the tabernacle door, they remain to complete the consecration.

segments.title: Moses assembles and washes priests
segments.gist: God commands Moses to bring Aaron and his sons, wash them with water, and clothe them with the priestly garments.

segments.title: Moses clothes and anoints Aaron
segments.gist: Moses puts the garments on Aaron, anoints the tabernacle and its vessels, and anoints Aaron to sanctify him.

segments.title: Sin offering for the priests
segments.gist: Moses offers the bull for the sin offering, placing blood on the altar and burning the flesh outside the camp.

segments.title: Burnt offering for the priests
segments.gist: Moses offers the ram for a burnt offering, sprinkling its blood on the altar and burning the whole ram.

segments.title: Ram of consecration offered
segments.gist: Moses offers the second ram, putting its blood on Aaron and his sons and waving the breast as a wave offering.

segments.title: Anointing and seven-day consecration
segments.gist: Moses sprinkles anointing oil and blood on Aaron and his sons, who then remain at the tabernacle door for seven days.

9.summary: On the eighth day after the priests' ordination, Moses summons Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel, and Aaron offers a sin offering and a burnt offering for himself and the people. After the offerings are made, Aaron blesses the people, and the glory of the LORD appears; fire comes from the LORD and consumes the offerings on the altar, and the people shout and fall on their faces.

segments.title: Moses instructs Aaron's offerings
segments.gist: Moses tells Aaron to offer a sin offering and burnt offering for himself and the people, and to prepare offerings for the LORD's appearance.

segments.title: Aaron offers for himself
segments.gist: Aaron offers the sin offering and burnt offering for himself, and Moses directs the handling of the blood and parts on the altar.

segments.title: Aaron offers for the people
segments.gist: Aaron presents the people's sin offering, burnt offering, grain offering, and peace offerings, burning the fat on the altar.

segments.title: Glory and fire from the LORD
segments.gist: Aaron blesses the people, the LORD's glory appears, fire consumes the offerings, and the people shout and fall on their faces.

10.summary: After Aaron's sons Nadab and Abihu offer unauthorized fire before the LORD and are consumed by fire, Moses instructs Aaron and his remaining sons not to mourn publicly. Moses then rebukes Eleazar and Ithamar for not eating the sin offering in the sanctuary, and Aaron appeals that he could not have eaten it with a clear conscience after such a tragedy.

segments.title: Nadab and Abihu Die
segments.gist: Nadab and Abihu offer strange fire and are consumed by fire from the LORD; Moses tells Aaron that God will be sanctified.

segments.title: Mourning Restricted
segments.gist: Moses forbids Aaron and his sons from mourning openly so they do not die, but allows the whole house of Israel to mourn.

segments.title: Priests Forbidden Wine
segments.gist: The LORD tells Aaron that priests must not drink wine or strong drink when entering the tabernacle, so they can distinguish holy from common.

segments.title: Eating the Offerings
segments.gist: Moses instructs Aaron and his remaining sons to eat the meal offering and the wave breast and heave shoulder in a clean place.

segments.title: Sin Offering Dispute
segments.gist: Moses is angry that the sin offering was not eaten, but Aaron explains that after such a day God would not have accepted it, and Moses is satisfied.

11.summary: God gives Moses and Aaron the dietary laws for Israel, distinguishing clean from unclean animals, fish, birds, and creeping things. The chapter also addresses contact with dead carcasses and the requirement to be holy because God is holy.

segments.title: Clean and Unclean Land Animals
segments.gist: God instructs Moses and Aaron which land animals may be eaten, specifying split hooves and chewing the cud, and lists examples of unclean beasts.

segments.title: Clean and Unclean Water Creatures
segments.gist: Rules are given for creatures in the waters: those with fins and scales are clean, while others are abominable.

segments.title: Unclean Birds Listed
segments.gist: A list of birds that are detestable and must not be eaten is provided.

segments.title: Winged Creeping Things
segments.gist: Insects that walk on all fours are unclean, except those with jointed legs for leaping, which may be eaten.

segments.title: Defilement by Carcasses
segments.gist: Regulations explain how touching or carrying the carcasses of unclean animals causes defilement until evening, and rules for vessels and food.

segments.title: Creeping Things and Call to Holiness
segments.gist: Creeping things on the ground are abominable, and the chapter concludes with the command to be holy because God is holy, separating clean from unclean.

12.summary: God gives Moses regulations for women after childbirth: a woman is ceremonially unclean for a set period after bearing a son or a daughter, after which she brings a burnt offering and a sin offering to the priest, who makes atonement for her.

segments.title: Purification after a Son
segments.gist: A woman who bears a son is unclean seven days, then continues in purification thirty-three days and may not touch holy things.

segments.title: Offerings after Purification
segments.gist: When her purification days are complete, she brings a lamb for a burnt offering and a pigeon or turtledove for a sin offering.

13.summary: God gives Moses and Aaron detailed instructions for diagnosing and handling skin diseases, including raw flesh, boils, burns, and scalp or beard infections. The priest examines the person, isolates them for seven days if uncertain, and declares them clean or unclean. The chapter also covers rules for contaminated clothing, which is burned or washed depending on whether the infection has spread.

segments.title: Initial examination of skin disease
segments.gist: The priest examines a swelling, scab, or bright spot; if it appears deeper than the skin and the hair has turned white, the person is declared unclean.

segments.title: Raw flesh and healing signs
segments.gist: When raw flesh appears, the person is unclean; if the raw flesh changes and turns white, the priest declares the person clean.

segments.title: Boils and their diagnosis
segments.gist: A boil that heals but leaves a white swelling or reddish spot is examined; if it spreads, the person is unclean; if it fades, clean.

segments.title: Burns and their diagnosis
segments.gist: A burn that develops a bright spot or white or reddish patch is examined; spreading means unclean, fading means clean.

segments.title: Scalp and beard infections
segments.gist: A plague on the head or beard is examined; if it appears deeper than the skin and the hair is yellow and thin, it is a scall and the person is unclean.

segments.title: Bright spots and leprosy diagnosis
segments.gist: Bright spots that are dull white are harmless, but a white rising with white hair and raw flesh indicates leprosy, requiring the person to live outside the camp.

segments.title: Rules for contaminated clothing
segments.gist: Garments with greenish or reddish streaks are examined; if the spot spreads, the garment is burned; if it fades, it is washed and declared clean.

14.summary: Leviticus 14 gives the law for cleansing a healed leper, including two birds, cedar wood, scarlet, and hyssop, and the eighth-day offerings. It then describes the purification of a house with leprous spots and the offerings for a poor leper.

segments.title: Cleansing ritual for healed leper
segments.gist: The priest inspects the healed leper outside the camp and uses two birds, cedar wood, scarlet, and hyssop for cleansing.

segments.title: Eighth-day offerings for cleansing
segments.gist: On the eighth day the cleansed person brings lambs, flour, and oil for guilt, sin, and burnt offerings.

segments.title: Provision for poor leper
segments.gist: If the person is poor, a reduced offering of one lamb, flour, oil, and two birds is allowed.

segments.title: Law for leprous house
segments.gist: When a house has leprous spots, the priest inspects it and performs a cleansing ritual with two birds, cedar wood, scarlet, and hyssop.

segments.title: Summary of leprosy laws
segments.gist: This concludes the law for leprosy in garments, houses, and persons, to determine clean and unclean.

15.summary: Leviticus 15 gives the law for bodily discharges: a man with a running issue is unclean, along with his bed and anyone who touches him or his spit, until he is cleansed by washing and sacrifices. It also covers a man's emission of seed, a woman's monthly impurity, and a woman with an issue of blood, each with its own period of uncleanness and rite of purification.

segments.title: Law for a man's running issue
segments.gist: A man with a running issue is unclean; his bed and seat are unclean, and anyone who touches them or his spit must wash and is unclean until evening; when healed he washes and brings two birds.

segments.title: Law for emission of seed
segments.gist: A man who has an emission of seed is unclean until evening; any garment or skin touched by it must be washed, and intercourse involving seed makes both unclean until evening.

segments.title: Law for a woman's monthly impurity
segments.gist: A woman is unclean seven days during her monthly issue; anyone who touches her or her bed is unclean until evening, and if a man lies with her he is unclean seven days.

segments.title: Law for a woman's blood issue
segments.gist: A woman with a prolonged issue of blood is unclean as in her monthly impurity; her bed and seat are unclean, and when healed she brings two birds for her cleansing.

segments.title: Summary of the discharge laws
segments.gist: The Israelites are to be separated from their uncleanness so they do not defile the tabernacle and die; this is the law for all discharges and impurities.

16.summary: God gives Moses instructions for Aaron's annual Day of Atonement: after the deaths of Nadab and Abihu, Aaron must enter the most holy place with a bullock and a goat, burning incense and sprinkling blood to atone for himself and the people. The chapter details the scapegoat ritual, the cleansing of the sanctuary, and the permanent statute for the day of affliction.

segments.title: Warning and entry instructions
segments.gist: God warns Aaron not to enter the holy place at all times, and specifies he must come with a young bullock and a ram.

segments.title: Two goats chosen
segments.gist: Aaron takes two goats for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering; one goat is sacrificed and the other is sent to Azazel.

segments.title: Blood sprinkled in holy place
segments.gist: Aaron offers the bullock for his own sin, brings incense into the most holy place, and sprinkles blood to cleanse the sanctuary.

segments.title: Scapegoat sent away
segments.gist: Aaron lays his hands on the live goat, confesses Israel's sins over it, and sends it into the wilderness.

segments.title: Cleansing and burnt offerings
segments.gist: Aaron changes clothes, offers burnt offerings for himself and the people, and the bodies of the sin offerings are burned outside the camp.

segments.title: Permanent statute of atonement
segments.gist: The day of atonement is established as a permanent statute of affliction and rest, with the ritual to be performed annually by the high priest.

17.summary: Leviticus 17 sets out the law that all slaughter of oxen, sheep, or goats must be brought to the tabernacle door as a peace offering, so that Israelites stop sacrificing in the open field. It forbids eating blood, because the life of the flesh is in the blood, and it rules that anyone who eats what dies of itself or is torn by beasts must wash and remain unclean until evening.

segments.title: Slaughter at the Tabernacle Door
segments.gist: Any Israelite who kills an ox, sheep, or goat must bring it to the tabernacle door as an offering, not sacrifice it in the open field.

segments.title: Ban on Eating Blood
segments.gist: Israelites and strangers among them are forbidden to eat blood, because the life of the flesh is in the blood, given to make atonement.

segments.title: Cleansing After Eating Carcasses
segments.gist: Anyone who eats an animal that died of itself or was torn by beasts must wash and be unclean until evening, and if they do not wash, they bear their iniquity.

18.summary: God instructs Moses to warn Israel against adopting the sexual practices of Egypt and Canaan, commanding them to keep His statutes. The chapter lists forbidden sexual unions, including those with close relatives, and prohibits child sacrifice, homosexuality, and bestiality, with warnings that the land will vomit out those who commit such abominations.

segments.title: Warning Against Pagan Practices
segments.gist: God tells Moses to warn Israel not to follow the doings of Egypt or Canaan but to keep His judgments and live by them.

segments.title: Laws Against Incest
segments.gist: Various sexual relations with close relatives are forbidden, including with parents, siblings, grandchildren, half-siblings, aunts, daughters-in-law, and sisters-in-law.

segments.title: Further Sexual Prohibitions
segments.gist: Additional laws forbid intercourse during menstruation, adultery, child sacrifice to Molech, homosexual acts, and bestiality.

segments.title: Warning of Defilement
segments.gist: Israel is warned not to defile itself as the nations before them did, lest the land vomit them out; those who commit these abominations will be cut off.

19.summary: God instructs Moses to tell the Israelites to be holy as He is holy, giving a wide range of laws covering sacrifices, treatment of the poor, honesty, love of neighbor, sexual purity, and fair dealings. The chapter repeatedly ties obedience to the command 'I am the LORD your God.'

segments.title: Holiness and Sacrificial Rules
segments.gist: God commands Israel to be holy, to honor parents and Sabbaths, and gives rules for peace offerings and eating leftovers.

segments.title: Love Your Neighbor
segments.gist: Laws about leaving harvest gleanings for the poor, honesty, justice, and loving one's neighbor as oneself.

segments.title: Mixed Practices and Firstfruits
segments.gist: Prohibitions against mixing kinds, rules about sexual relations with a betrothed slave, and instructions for firstfruits.

segments.title: Occult Practices and Respect
segments.gist: Forbids pagan mourning, divination, and prostitution, and commands respect for the elderly and the sanctuary.

segments.title: Fair Treatment of Strangers
segments.gist: Commands love for the foreigner and honest scales and measures, concluding with the call to keep all God's statutes.

20.summary: God gives Moses laws prescribing capital punishment for serious offenses, including Molech worship, cursing parents, adultery, incest, and other sexual sins, and he distinguishes Israel from the nations they are displacing.

segments.title: Penalties for Molech Worship
segments.gist: Anyone who gives offspring to Molech must be put to death, and God will set his face against those who hide the offender.

segments.title: Warning Against Familiar Spirits
segments.gist: Israel must not seek out mediums or wizards, but must sanctify themselves and keep God's statutes.

segments.title: Punishments for Sexual Sins
segments.gist: Death or cutting off is prescribed for adultery, incest, homosexuality, and other forbidden unions, with details for each case.

segments.title: Israel to Be Holy and Separate
segments.gist: God commands Israel to keep his statutes, promises them the land, and warns them to distinguish clean from unclean and not follow the practices of the nations.

21.summary: Leviticus 21 gives regulations for the priests' holiness, forbidding them to mourn like others or marry certain women, and lists physical defects that disqualify a descendant of Aaron from offering sacrifices, while allowing them to eat the holy food.

segments.title: Priests' mourning and marriage rules
segments.gist: Priests must avoid ritual defilement for the dead except close relatives, must not shave or cut themselves, and must marry only virgins of Israel.

segments.title: High priest's stricter holiness
segments.gist: The high priest may not mourn at all, must not leave the sanctuary, and must marry only a virgin from his own people.

segments.title: Defects bar priests from altar
segments.gist: Any descendant of Aaron with a physical defect may not offer sacrifices, though he may still eat the holy food.

22.summary: God gives Moses regulations for the priests regarding the handling of holy offerings, specifying who may eat of them and under what conditions. The chapter also sets standards for the animals brought as sacrifices, requiring them to be without blemish and of proper age.

segments.title: Priests must avoid defilement
segments.gist: God commands Aaron and his sons to separate themselves from holy things when unclean and warns that any priest who approaches while unclean shall be cut off.

segments.title: Who may eat holy offerings
segments.gist: Only the priest's household may eat holy offerings; strangers, hired servants, and those who eat inadvertently must make restitution.

segments.title: Sacrifices must be without blemish
segments.gist: Offerings brought to the Lord must be perfect, with no blindness, broken bones, or other defects, whether from the Israelites or strangers.

segments.title: Rules for young animals and thanksgiving
segments.gist: A newborn animal must remain with its mother for seven days, and thanksgiving offerings must be eaten on the day they are offered.

segments.title: Exhortation to keep commandments
segments.gist: God calls the Israelites to keep His commandments and not profane His holy name, reminding them that He brought them out of Egypt.

23.summary: God gives Moses a calendar of Israel's appointed feasts, including the weekly Sabbath, Passover and Unleavened Bread, Firstfruits, Weeks, Trumpets, Atonement, and Tabernacles. The chapter specifies the dates, offerings, and rules for each observance, with a closing summary of Moses declaring them to the people.

segments.title: Sabbath and Feasts Introduced
segments.gist: God tells Moses to speak to Israel about His appointed feasts and holy convocations, beginning with the weekly Sabbath.

segments.title: Passover and Unleavened Bread
segments.gist: Israel must keep Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month and eat unleavened bread for seven days, with a holy convocation and offerings.

segments.title: Feast of Firstfruits
segments.gist: When Israel enters the land, they must bring a sheaf of the firstfruits to the priest, who waves it before the Lord with a lamb and meal offering.

segments.title: Feast of Weeks
segments.gist: Seven weeks after Firstfruits, Israel must bring a new meal offering, wave two loaves, and offer sacrifices, leaving gleanings for the poor.

segments.title: Feast of Trumpets and Day of Atonement
segments.gist: The first day of the seventh month is a memorial of blowing trumpets, and the tenth day is a day of atonement with affliction of soul and no work.

segments.title: Feast of Tabernacles
segments.gist: Israel must dwell in booths for seven days during the Feast of Tabernacles, with offerings and rejoicing, and Moses declares these feasts to the people.

24.summary: God instructs Moses on the continual burning of the lampstand and the weekly showbread in the tabernacle. A man blasphemes the name of the LORD and is held in custody until God gives the verdict: he is stoned by the congregation. God then states the law of retaliation—life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth—applying equally to stranger and native.

segments.title: Oil for the Lampstand
segments.gist: God tells Moses to command Israel to bring pure olive oil for the lampstand to burn continually before the LORD.

segments.title: Showbread on the Table
segments.gist: God ordains twelve cakes of showbread set in two rows each Sabbath as a memorial offering for the priests.

segments.title: Blasphemer Held in Custody
segments.gist: A man of mixed Israelite and Egyptian parentage blasphemes the Name and is held until God's will is declared.

segments.title: Verdict Against Blasphemy
segments.gist: God rules that the blasphemer must be stoned by the congregation, and that any blasphemer, stranger or native, shall be put to death.

segments.title: Law of Retaliation
segments.gist: God sets the principle of life for life and eye for eye, with one law applying to both stranger and native.

25.summary: Leviticus 25 sets out the sabbatical year, when the land rests and debts are released every seventh year, and the Year of Jubilee every fiftieth year, when liberty is proclaimed and ancestral property returns to its original owners. It gives rules for redeeming land and for the fair treatment of poor Israelites who sell themselves as servants, ending with instructions on the redemption of servants and the status of foreign slaves.

segments.title: The Sabbath of the Land
segments.gist: God commands Israel to let the land rest every seventh year, neither sowing nor pruning, and to live off its spontaneous produce.

segments.title: The Year of Jubilee
segments.gist: Every fiftieth year liberty is proclaimed, property returns to its owners, and God promises provision in the sixth year.

segments.title: Redemption of Land and Houses
segments.gist: The land belongs to God and must not be sold permanently; rules are given for redeeming land, houses in walled cities, and Levite property.

segments.title: Care for the Poor
segments.gist: Israelites are told to support a poor brother without charging interest, so that he may live among them.

segments.title: Servants and Slaves
segments.gist: A poor Israelite who sells himself serves as a hired servant until Jubilee and may be redeemed; foreign slaves may be held permanently.

segments.title: Redemption of Israelite Servants
segments.gist: Rules are given for redeeming an Israelite who has sold himself to a resident foreigner, and for his release in the Year of Jubilee.

26.summary: Leviticus 26 sets out the blessings Israel will receive for obeying God's statutes—rain, harvests, peace, and God's presence—and the escalating curses for disobedience, including disease, defeat, wild beasts, famine, and exile. It ends with a promise that God will remember his covenant and restore a humbled people who confess their sins.

segments.title: Against Idols and Images
segments.gist: God forbids making idols, setting up graven images, or bowing to stone pillars, and commands keeping his sabbaths and reverencing his sanctuary.

segments.title: Blessings for Obedience
segments.gist: God promises rain in season, abundant harvests, peace in the land, victory over enemies, fruitfulness, and his presence among his people.

segments.title: First Curses for Disobedience
segments.gist: If Israel disobeys, God will bring terror, disease, defeat, and wild beasts that destroy their children and cattle.

segments.title: Escalating Curses and Exile
segments.gist: Continued disobedience brings sword, pestilence, famine so severe that parents eat their children, destruction of high places, and scattering among the nations.

segments.title: Land Enjoys Its Sabbaths
segments.gist: While Israel is exiled, the land will rest and enjoy its sabbaths, and those left will waste away in their enemies' lands because of their iniquity.

segments.title: Confession and Covenant Remembered
segments.gist: God promises to remember his covenant and restore the land when the people confess their sins and humble their hearts, for he will not utterly reject them.

27.summary: Leviticus 27 sets out the rules for vows and dedications to the LORD, including the monetary valuation of persons by age and sex, the redemption of animals and houses, and the special status of firstborn animals and devoted things. It closes with the principle that a tithe of the land's produce and of herds and flocks belongs to the LORD and cannot be redeemed without adding a fifth.

segments.title: Valuation of Persons
segments.gist: The LORD gives Moses valuations in silver shekels for persons vowed to him, scaled by age and sex.

segments.title: Vows of Animals
segments.gist: Clean animals vowed become holy and cannot be exchanged; unclean animals are valued and may be redeemed with a fifth added.

segments.title: Vows of Houses
segments.gist: A man may dedicate his house to the LORD; the priest sets its value, and redemption requires adding a fifth.

segments.title: Vows of Land
segments.gist: Fields are valued by seed and years to the jubilee; redemption adds a fifth, and fields not redeemed or sold remain the LORD's.

segments.title: Firstborn and Devoted Things
segments.gist: Firstborn animals already belong to the LORD and cannot be vowed; devoted things are most holy and cannot be redeemed.

segments.title: Tithes and Conclusion
segments.gist: A tithe of produce and herds is the LORD's; it may be redeemed with a fifth added, and these are the commandments given at Sinai.

1.summary: In the wilderness of Sinai, God commands Moses to take a census of all Israelite men aged twenty and above who are able to go to war, organized by tribe and ancestral house. Moses and Aaron, with a leader from each tribe, count the people, and the total comes to 603,550, excluding the Levites, who are appointed to care for the tabernacle and its furnishings.

segments.title: God commands the census
segments.gist: God speaks to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, ordering a count of all Israelite men twenty and older who can serve in war.

segments.title: Leaders named for each tribe
segments.gist: God lists the ancestral leaders who will assist Moses and Aaron in taking the census, one man from each tribe.

segments.title: Moses and Aaron assemble the people
segments.gist: Moses and Aaron gather the congregation and register the people by tribe and family, as God commanded.

segments.title: Census results by tribe
segments.gist: The number of men twenty and older able to go to war is recorded for each tribe, totaling 603,550.

segments.title: Levites exempted for tabernacle service
segments.gist: The Levites are not counted with the others but are appointed to care for the tabernacle, its furnishings, and its camp.

2.summary: God instructs Moses and Aaron to organize the Israelites into four camps around the tabernacle, each under its own standard and leader, with the Levites camped in the middle. The chapter lists the tribes in each camp, their leaders, and their census totals, and describes the order of march when the camp sets out.

segments.title: Camp arrangement commanded
segments.gist: God tells Moses and Aaron that each tribe shall camp by its own standard around the tabernacle.

segments.title: East camp: Judah's group
segments.gist: The tribes of Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun camp on the east under Judah's standard, totaling 186,400.

segments.title: South camp: Reuben's group
segments.gist: The tribes of Reuben, Simeon, and Gad camp on the south under Reuben's standard, totaling 151,450.

segments.title: West camp: Ephraim's group
segments.gist: The tribes of Ephraim, Manasseh, and Benjamin camp on the west under Ephraim's standard, totaling 108,100.

segments.title: North camp: Dan's group
segments.gist: The tribes of Dan, Asher, and Naphtali camp on the north under Dan's standard, totaling 157,600.

segments.title: Summary and obedience
segments.gist: The total census is 603,550, and the Israelites camp and march exactly as God commanded Moses.

3.summary: God commands Moses to bring the tribe of Levi to Aaron to serve as priests' assistants and to take charge of the tabernacle and its furnishings. The chapter lists the sons of Aaron and Levi, counts the Levite males by clan, and describes their camp positions and duties. It concludes with the redemption of the firstborn Israelites by the Levites and a census of the firstborn.

segments.title: Levitical Service and Duties
segments.gist: God instructs Moses to bring the Levites to Aaron to serve the tabernacle and guard its furnishings.

segments.title: Aaron's Sons and Levite Roles
segments.gist: Lists Aaron's sons as priests and assigns the Levites to assist them and keep the tabernacle charge.

segments.title: Levites Taken for Firstborn
segments.gist: God declares the Levites as substitutes for all firstborn Israelites, who belong to Him.

segments.title: Levi's Sons and Clan Heads
segments.gist: Names Levi's sons—Gershon, Kohath, and Merari—and their clans, with Aaron's sons listed.

segments.title: Census and Duties of Levite Clans
segments.gist: Counts the Levite males by clan and describes each clan's camp location and tabernacle duties.

segments.title: Redemption of Firstborn Israelites
segments.gist: God commands a census of firstborn Israelites and their redemption by the Levites, with excess redeemed by money.

4.summary: God instructs Moses to take a census of the Kohathites, Gershonites, and Merarites, the Levite clans eligible for service, specifying their duties for transporting and caring for the tabernacle. The chapter details the age of service, the roles of each clan under the direction of Aaron's sons and Ithamar, and the total number of Levites set apart for this work.

segments.title: Kohathites' census and duties
segments.gist: Moses is told to number the Kohathites from thirty to fifty years old and to assign them the care of the most holy things, with Aaron and his sons overseeing the covering of the sanctuary.

segments.title: Gershonites' census and duties
segments.gist: The Gershonites are numbered and given charge of the tabernacle curtains, coverings, and related items under the direction of Ithamar.

segments.title: Merarites' census and duties
segments.gist: The Merarites are numbered and assigned the frames, bars, pillars, and sockets of the tabernacle, also under Ithamar's supervision.

segments.title: Total number of Levites
segments.gist: Moses and Aaron number the Kohathites, Gershonites, and Merarites, totaling 8,580 Levites from thirty to fifty years old for service in the tabernacle.

5.summary: God instructs Moses to remove ritually unclean persons from the camp of Israel, to have wrongdoers confess and make restitution, and to give a wife suspected of adultery a test of bitter water to determine her guilt or innocence.

segments.title: Unclean persons put out
segments.gist: God commands that lepers, those with discharges, and those defiled by the dead be sent outside the camp so they do not defile it.

segments.title: Confession and restitution
segments.gist: When a person wrongs another, they must confess and repay the wrong plus a fifth; if no kinsman exists, the restitution goes to the priest.

segments.title: Jealousy offering brought
segments.gist: A husband who suspects his wife of adultery brings her and a grain offering of jealousy to the priest.

segments.title: Oath and bitter water
segments.gist: The priest brings the woman near, charges her with an oath, and writes the curses in a book, blotting them into bitter water for her to drink.

segments.title: Drink and its outcome
segments.gist: The priest writes the curses, makes the woman drink the water, and declares that if guilty she will be cursed, but if innocent she will be free and conceive children.

segments.title: Law of jealousy summarized
segments.gist: This is the law of jealousy when a wife goes aside or when a husband is jealous; the husband is guiltless and the woman bears her iniquity.

6.summary: God gives Moses instructions for the Nazirite vow, including its restrictions and the procedure for completing the vow. He also gives the priestly blessing for Aaron and his sons to pronounce over Israel.

segments.title: Nazirite Vow Restrictions
segments.gist: The LORD commands Moses to tell Israel that a man or woman may take a Nazirite vow, abstaining from wine and strong drink and not cutting hair.

segments.title: Defilement and Restitution
segments.gist: If someone dies suddenly near a Nazirite, the Nazirite becomes unclean, must shave and bring offerings, and restart the vow.

segments.title: Completion of the Vow
segments.gist: The law for completing a Nazirite vow: bring offerings, shave the head at the tabernacle, and the priest presents the offerings.

segments.title: The Priestly Blessing
segments.gist: The LORD instructs Aaron and his sons to bless Israel with a threefold blessing, placing His name upon them.

7.summary: On the day Moses finished setting up the tabernacle, the leaders of the twelve tribes brought offerings of wagons and oxen for transport, which Moses distributed to the Levites. Over twelve days, each tribal leader presented identical dedication offerings of silver, gold, and animals, and Moses spoke with God in the tent of meeting.

segments.title: Leaders bring wagons and oxen
segments.gist: After the tabernacle is anointed, tribal leaders bring six wagons and twelve oxen, which Moses gives to the Levites for service.

segments.title: Twelve days of dedication offerings
segments.gist: Each of the twelve tribal leaders presents identical offerings of silver, gold, and animals over twelve consecutive days for the altar's dedication.

8.summary: God instructs Moses to set up the seven lamps of the lampstand so they give light in front of it, and the Levites are cleansed, presented as a wave offering, and set apart for service in the tabernacle in place of Israel's firstborn. The chapter also sets the age limits for Levite service and describes the Levites' dedication and the offerings made for them.

segments.title: Lamps Set Toward the Lampstand
segments.gist: Moses is told to have Aaron arrange the seven lamps so they shine in front of the lampstand, and he does so as commanded.

segments.title: Cleansing and Offering of the Levites
segments.gist: God commands Moses to cleanse the Levites with water and offerings, present them before the tabernacle, and set them apart as a wave offering from Israel.

segments.title: Levites Given to Aaron for Service
segments.gist: After cleansing, the Levites are to serve in the tabernacle as a gift to Aaron and his sons, taking the place of Israel's firstborn.

segments.title: Moses and Aaron Obey
segments.gist: Moses, Aaron, and the congregation carry out all that God commanded concerning the Levites, who are cleansed and serve before Aaron.

segments.title: Age Limits for Levite Service
segments.gist: God sets the Levites' service from twenty-five to fifty years old, after which they assist but no longer perform the work.

9.summary: God commands Israel to keep the Passover in the first month of the second year after the Exodus, and provides a second-month makeup for those defiled by a dead body or on a journey. The chapter then describes the cloud that covered the tabernacle, which guided Israel's journeys and encampments, and ends with the signal of the two silver trumpets.

segments.title: Passover Commanded
segments.gist: God tells Moses to have Israel keep the Passover at its appointed time in the first month.

segments.title: Second Passover Provided
segments.gist: Men defiled by a dead body ask about Passover; God allows a second-month observance for them and for travelers.

segments.title: Cloud Guides Israel
segments.gist: The cloud covers the tabernacle and directs Israel's camp and journeys by lifting or resting.

10.summary: God instructs Moses to make two silver trumpets for summoning the congregation and signaling camp movements. After the Israelites celebrate Passover and follow the cloud, they set out from Sinai in marching order, with Moses inviting Hobab to join them as they journey toward the promised land.

segments.title: Two Silver Trumpets
segments.gist: God commands Moses to make two silver trumpets for calling the assembly, signaling marches, and sounding alarms in battle and festivals.

segments.title: Israel Departs Sinai
segments.gist: The cloud lifts from the tabernacle and the Israelites set out from Sinai in ordered divisions, with the ark leading and the camps advancing.

segments.title: Moses Invites Hobab
segments.gist: Moses asks his brother-in-law Hobab to accompany Israel as a guide, promising him a share in the good that God will do.

segments.title: The Ark Leads the Journey
segments.gist: The ark goes before the people to find resting places, and Moses utters prayers for God to scatter enemies and return with Israel.

11.summary: The Israelites complain about their hardships, and fire from the LORD consumes some at the edge of the camp until Moses intercedes. Moses, overwhelmed by the people's weeping for meat, voices his despair to God, who instructs him to appoint seventy elders and promises a month of quail. The Spirit rests on the elders, and a wind brings quail, but a plague strikes the people while they eat the meat.

segments.title: Complaints and Fire
segments.gist: The people complain, the LORD's fire burns some in the camp, and Moses prays until the fire abates.

segments.title: Weeping for Meat
segments.gist: The mixed multitude and Israelites weep for meat, despise the manna, and Moses hears the people weeping.

segments.title: Moses' Despair
segments.gist: Moses tells God he cannot bear the people alone and asks either for help or to be killed.

segments.title: Seventy Elders Appointed
segments.gist: God instructs Moses to gather seventy elders to share the burden and promises meat for a month.

segments.title: Spirit on the Elders
segments.gist: The Spirit rests on the seventy elders, who prophesy; Eldad and Medad also prophesy, and Moses rebukes Joshua's jealousy.

segments.title: Quail and Plague
segments.gist: A wind brings quail, the people gather them, and a plague strikes while the meat is still in their teeth; Kibroth-hattaavah is named.

12.summary: Miriam and Aaron speak against Moses because of his Ethiopian wife and challenge his unique authority. God summons the three to the tabernacle, rebukes Miriam and Aaron, and strikes Miriam with leprosy. Moses intercedes, and after seven days of exclusion Miriam is healed and the people move on.

segments.title: Miriam and Aaron Challenge Moses
segments.gist: Miriam and Aaron criticize Moses for marrying an Ethiopian woman and question whether God has spoken only through Moses.

segments.title: God Defends Moses' Authority
segments.gist: God summons Moses, Aaron, and Miriam to the tabernacle, descends in a pillar of cloud, and affirms Moses' unique prophetic status.

segments.title: Miriam Struck with Leprosy
segments.gist: God's anger burns, the cloud departs, and Miriam becomes leprous; Aaron pleads with Moses on her behalf.

segments.title: Moses Intercedes and Miriam Healed
segments.gist: Moses cries to God for Miriam's healing; she is shut out seven days, then the people journey from Hazeroth.

13.summary: At God's command, Moses sends twelve spies from the wilderness of Paran to scout Canaan. They return with fruit and a report of a rich land but also of formidable inhabitants, and ten of the spies spread a discouraging account that frightens the people, while Caleb urges immediate action.

segments.title: Spies chosen and sent
segments.gist: The LORD tells Moses to send men to spy out Canaan, and Moses selects twelve leaders, one from each tribe, and sends them from Paran.

segments.title: Instructions for scouting
segments.gist: Moses instructs the spies to assess the land's fertility, the people's strength, the cities' fortifications, and to bring back fruit.

segments.title: Journey through Canaan
segments.gist: The spies travel from the wilderness of Zin to Rehob, come to Hebron, and cut a cluster of grapes at Eshcol before returning after forty days.

segments.title: Mixed report and fear
segments.gist: The spies report a good land but strong inhabitants; Caleb urges conquest, but the others exaggerate the dangers, disheartening the people.

14.summary: After the spies' report, the Israelites rebel and refuse to enter Canaan, threatening to stone Joshua and Caleb. God threatens to destroy them, but Moses intercedes; God forgives but decrees that the adults will die in the wilderness, and the ten spies die of plague. The people then presumptuously attack and are defeated.

segments.title: People weep and murmur
segments.gist: The congregation cries all night and complains against Moses and Aaron, wishing they had died in Egypt.

segments.title: Caleb and Joshua urge trust
segments.gist: Moses and Aaron fall on their faces; Joshua and Caleb tear their clothes and urge the people to trust God, but the congregation threatens to stone them.

segments.title: Moses intercedes for Israel
segments.gist: God threatens to disinherit Israel, but Moses pleads for God's honor and reminds him of his mercy, asking forgiveness.

segments.title: God forgives but judges
segments.gist: God pardons but declares that the adults who murmured will die in the wilderness, while their children will inherit the land.

segments.title: Spies die, Joshua and Caleb live
segments.gist: The ten spies who brought the evil report die of plague, but Joshua and Caleb survive.

segments.title: Presumptuous attack defeated
segments.gist: The people mourn, then go up to fight without God's presence and are defeated by the Amalekites and Canaanites.

15.summary: After the rebellion of the previous generation, God gives Israel laws for offerings and unintentional sins, prescribes a death penalty for a man who gathers sticks on the Sabbath, and commands the people to wear fringes on their garments as a reminder to keep the commandments.

segments.title: Laws for Offerings and Strangers
segments.gist: God instructs Moses to tell Israel about grain, drink, and animal offerings, and to apply the same rules to strangers living among them.

segments.title: Firstfruits of Dough
segments.gist: God commands the people to set aside a cake from the first of their dough as a heave offering throughout their generations.

segments.title: Offerings for Unintentional Sins
segments.gist: God provides atonement for unintentional sins by the congregation or an individual, but prescribes cutting off for those who sin presumptuously.

segments.title: Sabbath Breaker Stoned
segments.gist: A man is found gathering sticks on the Sabbath; God orders him stoned, and the people carry it out.

segments.title: Fringes as Reminder
segments.gist: God commands Israel to wear fringes on their garments to remember and keep all his commandments.

16.summary: Korah, Dathan, Abiram, and 250 leaders rebel against Moses and Aaron's authority; Moses challenges them to a test with incense, and God destroys the rebels by fire and by opening the earth to swallow them. A plague then breaks out among the people, which Aaron stops by offering incense.

segments.title: Korah and company rebel
segments.gist: Korah, Dathan, Abiram, and 250 princes confront Moses and Aaron, claiming the whole congregation is holy.

segments.title: Moses proposes incense test
segments.gist: Moses falls on his face, tells Korah and his company to take censers with fire and incense before the LORD.

segments.title: Dathan and Abiram refuse
segments.gist: Moses summons Dathan and Abiram, who refuse to come and accuse Moses of failing to bring them into a land of milk and honey.

segments.title: Moses warns congregation
segments.gist: Moses tells the congregation to depart from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram, and warns them not to touch anything belonging to these sinners.

segments.title: Earth swallows rebels
segments.gist: The ground opens and swallows Korah, Dathan, Abiram, and their households, and fire from the LORD consumes the 250 men offering incense.

segments.title: Censers made into covering
segments.gist: God commands Eleazar to make the censers into a covering for the altar as a memorial that no outsider should offer incense.

segments.title: Plague and Aaron's atonement
segments.gist: The congregation murmurs, a plague breaks out, and Aaron runs with incense among the people to make atonement and stop the plague.

17.summary: God confirms Aaron's priesthood by having each tribe's leader place a rod before the ark; Aaron's rod buds, blossoms, and yields almonds, while the others remain unchanged. The rods are shown to the people, and Aaron's rod is kept as a sign against rebellion. The chapter ends with the people's fearful cry that they will die if they approach the tabernacle.

segments.title: Rods Collected from Tribes
segments.gist: God instructs Moses to take a rod from each tribal leader, write names on them, and place them in the tabernacle.

segments.title: Aaron's Rod Buds
segments.gist: The next day Aaron's rod has budded, blossomed, and produced almonds, while the other rods remain unchanged.

segments.title: Rod Kept as Sign
segments.gist: God commands Aaron's rod be kept as a sign against rebels, and the people cry out in fear of dying.

18.summary: God assigns the duties of the tabernacle to the priests and Levites, with Aaron's family responsible for the sanctuary and the Levites assisting them. The chapter then details the portions of the offerings and tithes given to the priests and Levites as their inheritance, since they receive no land allotment.

segments.title: Duties of Priests and Levites
segments.gist: God assigns Aaron and his sons to serve in the priesthood and the Levites to assist them, warning that outsiders who approach the sanctuary will die.

segments.title: Priests' Portions from Offerings
segments.gist: God grants the priests a perpetual share of the grain offerings, sin offerings, guilt offerings, and firstfruits brought by the Israelites.

segments.title: Levites Receive the Tithe
segments.gist: The Levites are given the tithe from Israel as their inheritance because they have no land allotment among the people.

segments.title: Levites' Tithe to the Priests
segments.gist: The Levites must offer a tenth of the tithe they receive to the priests and may eat the rest anywhere, but they must not profane the holy offerings.

19.summary: God instructs Moses and Aaron to give Israel the law of the red heifer: a flawless red cow is burned outside the camp, and its ashes mixed with water form a purification water for cleansing from contact with the dead. The chapter details who becomes unclean, how long, and the cleansing ritual on the third and seventh days, ending with a statute about a person who refuses purification.

segments.title: The red heifer offering
segments.gist: God commands Moses and Aaron to have a red heifer burned outside the camp, with cedar, hyssop, and scarlet, and its ashes kept for purification water.

segments.title: Uncleanness from the dead
segments.gist: Anyone who touches a dead body becomes unclean for seven days, and the chapter lists ways uncleanness spreads through a tent or open field.
