segments.title: Cleansing on third and seventh days
segments.gist: The ashes are mixed with running water, and a clean person sprinkles the unclean on the third and seventh days to complete purification.

segments.title: Penalty for refusing purification
segments.gist: Anyone who remains unclean and does not purify himself is cut off from the congregation, and whatever the unclean person touches becomes unclean.

20.summary: In the wilderness of Zin, Miriam dies and is buried. The people complain about the lack of water, and God tells Moses to speak to a rock to bring forth water, but Moses strikes it twice; God says he will not lead the people into the promised land. Moses asks Edom for passage through their land, but Edom refuses. Aaron dies on Mount Hor and Eleazar becomes high priest.

segments.title: Water from the Rock
segments.gist: The people complain about lack of water; God tells Moses to speak to the rock, but Moses strikes it twice and God says he will not enter the land.

segments.title: Edom Refuses Passage
segments.gist: Moses asks Edom for permission to pass through their land, but Edom refuses and comes out against Israel.

segments.title: Aaron's Death
segments.gist: At Mount Hor, Aaron dies and Eleazar is clothed with his garments as the people mourn.

21.summary: The Israelites defeat the Canaanite king of Arad after vowing to destroy his cities. When fiery serpents plague the people for their complaining, Moses makes a bronze serpent on a pole so that those who look at it live. Israel then journeys around Edom, sings a song at a well, and defeats the Amorite kings Sihon and Og, taking possession of their land.

segments.title: Israel defeats king of Arad
segments.gist: Israel vows to destroy the Canaanite cities if God delivers them, and the Lord grants the victory at Hormah.

segments.title: Fiery serpents and bronze serpent
segments.gist: The people complain on the way, fiery serpents bite them, and Moses lifts a bronze serpent so that the bitten may live by looking.

segments.title: Journey to the well and song
segments.gist: Israel travels through Oboth, Ije-abarim, and the valley of Zared, and sings a song at the well God gives them.

segments.title: Defeat of Sihon king of Amorites
segments.gist: Israel asks Sihon for passage, he refuses and attacks, and Israel defeats him and occupies his cities from Arnon to Jabbok.

segments.title: Defeat of Og king of Bashan
segments.gist: Og king of Bashan attacks Israel at Edrei, and the Lord gives Israel victory, and they possess his land.

22.summary: Balak, king of Moab, fearing Israel, sends elders to hire Balaam to curse them. God forbids Balaam to go, but after a second delegation He permits it with a warning. On the journey the angel of the Lord blocks the way, and Balaam's donkey speaks to him. Balaam meets Balak, who offers sacrifices, and Balaam prepares to speak.

segments.title: Balak sends for Balaam
segments.gist: Balak, king of Moab, sees Israel's numbers and sends elders to Balaam to ask him to curse Israel.

segments.title: Balaam refuses first request
segments.gist: Balaam seeks God's word, is told not to curse Israel, and refuses the first delegation.

segments.title: Second delegation and permission
segments.gist: Balak sends more honorable princes; God permits Balaam to go but warns him to speak only what God says.

segments.title: Angel and speaking donkey
segments.gist: The angel of the Lord blocks Balaam's path; the donkey speaks, and Balaam's eyes are opened.

segments.title: Balaam meets Balak
segments.gist: Balak meets Balaam, who insists he can only speak God's words; Balak offers sacrifices.

23.summary: Balak brings Balaam to three different high places to curse Israel, but each time Balaam speaks only the blessing God puts in his mouth, declaring Israel blessed, numerous, and favored by God, to Balak's frustration.

segments.title: Balak's First Sacrifice and Balaam's Instruction
segments.gist: Balak takes Balaam to Bamoth-baal, builds seven altars, and offers sacrifices; Balaam tells Balak to stand by the offering while he meets God.

segments.title: Balaam's First Oracle: Israel Blessed
segments.gist: Balaam declares that he cannot curse whom God has not cursed, describing Israel as a people dwelling alone and numerous as the dust.

segments.title: Balak's Protest and Second Sacrifice
segments.gist: Balak complains that Balaam blessed instead of cursing; they move to Zophim on Pisgah, where Balak again builds seven altars and offers sacrifices.

segments.title: Balaam's Second Oracle: God Does Not Repent
segments.gist: Balaam proclaims that God is not a man that he should lie, that he has blessed Israel and sees no iniquity in Jacob, and that Israel will rise like a lion.

segments.title: Balak's Further Protest and Third Sacrifice
segments.gist: Balak tells Balaam not to curse or bless, then takes him to Peor, where he again builds seven altars and offers sacrifices.

24.summary: Balaam, hired by Balak to curse Israel, instead delivers a series of oracles blessing Israel, declaring that God has not beheld iniquity in Jacob and that a star shall rise out of Jacob. Balak angrily dismisses him, and Balaam prophesies the defeat of Moab, Edom, and other nations before departing to his own place.

segments.title: Balaam's third oracle: Israel blessed
segments.gist: Balaam, filled with the Spirit, blesses Israel, describing their tents as goodly and their strength as that of a unicorn.

segments.title: Balak's anger and dismissal
segments.gist: Balak angrily claps his hands and tells Balaam he has called him to curse Israel but instead he has blessed them thrice; Balaam replies he can only speak what the LORD says.

segments.title: Balaam's fourth oracle: the star of Jacob
segments.gist: Balaam prophesies that a star shall come out of Jacob and a sceptre out of Israel, smiting Moab and Edom and ruling over his enemies.

segments.title: Oracles against Amalek, Kenites, and Asshur
segments.gist: Balaam delivers brief prophecies of destruction for Amalek, the Kenites, and Asshur, then returns to his place while Balak goes his way.

25.summary: While Israel camps at Shittim, the men begin committing whoredom with Moabite women and join in sacrifices to Baal-peor, provoking God's anger. God commands Moses to execute the leaders, and Phinehas kills an Israelite man and a Midianite woman in the act, stopping the plague after 24,000 die. God grants Phinehas a covenant of peace and commands Israel to smite the Midianites.

segments.title: Israel Sins with Moab
segments.gist: Israelite men commit whoredom with Moabite women and join sacrifices to Baal-peor, and God commands Moses to hang the offenders.

segments.title: Phinehas Stops the Plague
segments.gist: Phinehas kills an Israelite man and a Midianite woman in the act, and the plague that had killed 24,000 stops.

segments.title: Covenant of Peace
segments.gist: God praises Phinehas for his zeal and grants him and his descendants a covenant of peace and perpetual priesthood.

segments.title: Names of the Slain
segments.gist: The slain Israelite man is identified as Zimri son of Salu, and the Midianite woman as Cozbi daughter of Zur.

segments.title: Command to Smite Midian
segments.gist: God commands Moses to vex and smite the Midianites because they had deceived Israel with the matter of Peor and Cozbi.

26.summary: After the plague, God commands Moses and Eleazar to take a new census of Israel's men able to bear arms, organized by tribe and ancestral house. The count totals 601,730, and God directs the division of the land according to the size of each tribe. The chapter also records the Levites' separate census and notes that none of the earlier generation except Caleb and Joshua survived.

segments.title: Command to Take Census
segments.gist: God tells Moses and Eleazar to count all Israelite men twenty and older able to go to war, by their fathers' houses.

segments.title: Census Results by Tribe
segments.gist: The tribes are listed with their clans and the number of men counted in each, totaling 601,730.

segments.title: Land Divided by Lot
segments.gist: God instructs that the land be divided by lot according to the number of names in each tribe, with larger tribes receiving more inheritance.

segments.title: Census of the Levites
segments.gist: The Levites are counted separately by their clans, totaling 23,000 males a month old and older, and are not numbered with the rest of Israel.

segments.title: None Survive Except Caleb and Joshua
segments.gist: Moses and Eleazar finish the census, and God notes that none of the previous generation survived except Caleb and Joshua.

27.summary: The daughters of Zelophehad bring their inheritance case before Moses and are granted a possession among their father's brethren. God then tells Moses to view the promised land from Mount Abarim and to appoint Joshua as his successor, which Moses does before Eleazar and the congregation.

segments.title: Daughters of Zelophehad plead
segments.gist: The five daughters of Zelophehad stand before Moses, Eleazar, and the princes, asking for an inheritance because their father died without sons.

segments.title: God grants their request
segments.gist: Moses brings the case before the LORD, who rules that the daughters shall inherit and establishes a statute for inheritance when a man has no son.

segments.title: Moses told to view land
segments.gist: God tells Moses to go up Mount Abarim to see the land, and reminds him he will not enter it because of his disobedience at Meribah.

segments.title: Joshua appointed as successor
segments.gist: Moses asks God to set a leader over the congregation; God directs him to lay hands on Joshua before Eleazar and the people, and Moses does so.

28.summary: God instructs Moses to command the Israelites to present their offerings at their appointed times. The chapter details the daily burnt offering, the weekly Sabbath offering, the monthly new moon offerings, and the annual offerings for Passover and the Feast of Weeks, each with specified animals, grain, and drink offerings.

segments.title: Daily Burnt Offering
segments.gist: God commands Israel to offer two lambs each day, one in the morning and one in the evening, with grain and drink offerings.

segments.title: Sabbath Offering
segments.gist: On the Sabbath, two lambs with grain and drink offerings are added to the regular daily offering.

segments.title: Monthly New Moon Offering
segments.gist: At each new moon, two young bulls, one ram, and seven lambs are offered with grain and drink offerings, plus a goat for sin.

segments.title: Passover and Unleavened Bread
segments.gist: The Passover is on the fourteenth day of the first month, followed by a seven-day feast with specified offerings each day.

segments.title: Feast of Weeks Offering
segments.gist: On the day of firstfruits, a freewill offering of two bulls, one ram, and seven lambs is made with grain and drink offerings and a goat for sin.

29.summary: Numbers 29 continues the instructions for the seventh month, detailing the offerings for the Feast of Trumpets, the Day of Atonement, and the Feast of Tabernacles. It specifies the number of bulls, rams, lambs, and grain and drink offerings for each day of the festivals, with a decreasing number of bulls over the eight days of Tabernacles.

segments.title: Offerings for Feast of Trumpets
segments.gist: On the first day of the seventh month, a holy convocation with trumpet blasts and specified burnt, grain, and sin offerings.

segments.title: Offerings for Day of Atonement
segments.gist: On the tenth day, a holy convocation with affliction of soul and the same offerings as the Trumpets, plus a sin offering.

segments.title: Offerings for Feast of Tabernacles
segments.gist: For the eight days of the feast, decreasing numbers of bulls are offered each day, along with rams, lambs, and grain and drink offerings.

segments.title: Offerings for the Eighth Day
segments.gist: On the eighth day, a solemn assembly with a prescribed set of offerings different from the preceding days.

segments.title: Summary of Vows and Offerings
segments.gist: Moses commands the Israelites to present these offerings at their appointed times, in addition to their vows and freewill offerings.

30.summary: Moses instructs the heads of the tribes about vows made to the LORD, emphasizing that a man's vow is binding but a woman's vow may be annulled by her father if she is young and living at home, or by her husband if she is married. The chapter sets out specific cases for widows and divorced women, whose vows stand.

segments.title: Moses addresses tribal heads on vows
segments.gist: Moses tells the heads of the tribes that when a man makes a vow to the LORD, he must not break his word.

segments.title: Young woman's vow and father's authority
segments.gist: If a young woman in her father's house makes a vow, her father may annul it; if he does not, the vow stands.

segments.title: Married woman's vow and husband's authority
segments.gist: If a married woman makes a vow, her husband may annul it when he hears it; otherwise, it stands.

segments.title: Wife's vow in husband's house
segments.gist: A wife's vow made in her husband's house may be annulled by her husband, but if he does not, it stands.

segments.title: Husband's power to confirm or annul
segments.gist: A husband may confirm or annul his wife's vows, and if he annuls them later, he bears her guilt; these are the statutes Moses received.

31.summary: God commands Moses to take vengeance on the Midianites. Israel's army of 12,000 defeats Midian, kills five kings and Balaam, and brings back captives and spoil. Moses is angry that the women were spared, orders purification, and the spoil is divided between soldiers and congregation, with a portion given to the LORD and to the Levites.

segments.title: Command to attack Midian
segments.gist: The LORD commands Moses to avenge Israel on Midian; Moses sends 12,000 armed men, who kill all Midianite males and five kings, including Balaam.

segments.title: Moses rebukes and orders purification
segments.gist: Moses is angry that the women were spared, orders the killing of male children and non-virgin women, and gives purification rules for soldiers and spoil.

segments.title: Law of purification for spoil
segments.gist: Eleazar the priest instructs how to purify metals and other goods taken from battle, and the soldiers must cleanse themselves and their garments.

segments.title: Division of the spoil
segments.gist: The LORD commands Moses to divide the spoil between soldiers and congregation; the soldiers' half is counted, and a tribute is given to the LORD and to the Levites.

segments.title: Offering of the officers
segments.gist: The officers bring a freewill offering of gold jewelry to make atonement, and Moses and Eleazar bring it into the tabernacle as a memorial.

32.summary: The tribes of Reuben and Gad ask Moses for the land of Jazer and Gilead east of the Jordan, preferring it for their large herds. Moses initially rebukes them for discouraging the other tribes from crossing into Canaan, but they agree to send their warriors ahead to help conquer the land before settling their families and flocks on the east side. Moses grants the request with conditions, and the tribes build cities for their children and folds for their sheep.

segments.title: Reuben and Gad request eastern land
segments.gist: The tribes of Reuben and Gad ask Moses and Eleazar for the land of Jazer and Gilead because of their many cattle.

segments.title: Moses rebukes their request
segments.gist: Moses warns that their refusal to cross the Jordan will discourage the other tribes and provoke God's anger, citing the earlier failure at Kadesh.

segments.title: Tribes offer to fight first
segments.gist: They propose to build shelters for their families and flocks, then send their armed men ahead of Israel until the land is subdued.

segments.title: Moses sets conditions
segments.gist: Moses agrees that if they go armed before the Lord and drive out the inhabitants, they may return and possess the eastern land.

segments.title: Moses assigns the land
segments.gist: Moses commands Eleazar, Joshua, and the tribal leaders to give the land to Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh if they cross armed.

segments.title: Cities built in the east
segments.gist: The tribes of Gad, Reuben, and half of Manasseh rebuild cities and rename them, including Nobah and Jair's towns.

33.summary: Numbers 33 recounts the stages of Israel's journey from Egypt to the plains of Moab, listing the campsites from Rameses to the Jordan. God commands Moses to drive out the Canaanites, destroy their idols, and possess the land, warning that failure to do so will bring trouble.

segments.title: Journey from Rameses
segments.gist: Moses records Israel's departure from Rameses after the firstborn were struck down, with the Egyptians burying their dead.

segments.title: List of camping places
segments.gist: The chapter lists the successive campsites from Succoth through the wilderness to the plains of Moab by the Jordan.

segments.title: Command to possess Canaan
segments.gist: God commands Israel to drive out the Canaanites, destroy their idols and high places, and possess the land, warning that failure will bring trouble.

34.summary: God defines the borders of the land of Canaan that Israel is to inherit, naming the southern, western, northern, and eastern boundaries. He then appoints the leaders who will divide the land among the tribes, listing one prince from each of the nine and a half tribes settling west of the Jordan.

segments.title: Command to divide the land
segments.gist: The LORD instructs Moses to command Israel to divide the land of Canaan as their inheritance.

segments.title: Southern border described
segments.gist: The southern boundary runs from the wilderness of Zin along Edom to the Salt Sea.

segments.title: Northern border described
segments.gist: The northern boundary runs from the Great Sea to Mount Hor and on to Hamath and Zedad.

segments.title: Eastern border described
segments.gist: The eastern border goes from Hazar-enan to the Jordan River and ends at the Salt Sea.

segments.title: Inheritance for nine and a half tribes
segments.gist: Moses states that the land is for the nine and a half tribes, since Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh already received theirs east of the Jordan.

segments.title: Leaders appointed to divide land
segments.gist: The LORD names Eleazar, Joshua, and one prince from each of the nine and a half tribes to divide the land.

35.summary: God commands Israel to give the Levites forty-eight cities, including six cities of refuge where someone who kills a person accidentally can flee from the avenger of blood. The chapter specifies the rules for these cities, distinguishing between intentional murder and unintentional killing, and requires the congregation to judge the case. It also states that a murderer must be put to death and that the land cannot be cleansed except by the blood of the one who shed it.

segments.title: Levites receive cities and suburbs
segments.gist: God commands Israel to give the Levites forty-eight cities with surrounding suburbs, including six cities of refuge.

segments.title: Six cities of refuge appointed
segments.gist: God designates six cities of refuge—three east of Jordan and three in Canaan—for anyone who kills unintentionally to flee to.

segments.title: Intentional murder requires death
segments.gist: If someone strikes another with an iron object, stone, or wood, or pushes or throws something with malice, and death results, the killer is a murderer and must be put to death.

segments.title: Unintentional killing and refuge
segments.gist: If someone kills another without enmity or malice, the congregation shall judge between the killer and the avenger, and the killer must stay in the city of refuge until the high priest dies.

segments.title: Murder and land purification laws
segments.gist: A murderer must be put to death on the testimony of witnesses, and no ransom is allowed; the land cannot be cleansed except by the blood of the murderer.

36.summary: The heads of the Gileadite families of Manasseh raise a concern that if Zelophehad's daughters marry outside their tribe, their inheritance would transfer to another tribe, reducing Manasseh's holdings. Moses rules that the daughters must marry within their father's tribe, and they comply by marrying cousins, so the inheritance stays within the tribe. The chapter closes with a note that these are the commandments given in the plains of Moab.

segments.title: Tribal leaders raise inheritance concern
segments.gist: Heads of Manasseh's families warn Moses that if Zelophehad's daughters marry outside the tribe, their inheritance will be lost to another tribe.

segments.title: Moses rules daughters must marry within tribe
segments.gist: Moses commands that Zelophehad's daughters may marry anyone they choose, but only within their father's tribe, to keep inheritances from transferring between tribes.

segments.title: Daughters marry cousins within tribe
segments.gist: Zelophehad's daughters obey and marry their cousins from the families of Manasseh, so their inheritance remains in their father's tribe.

1.summary: Moses addresses Israel in the plains of Moab, recounting the journey from Horeb and the appointment of judges. He recalls the spies sent from Kadesh-barnea, the people's refusal to enter the land, and God's judgment that the adult generation would die in the wilderness, except Caleb and Joshua.

segments.title: Moses recounts the journey from Horeb
segments.gist: Moses begins his farewell address, reminding Israel of God's command to leave Horeb and take possession of the land promised to their fathers.

segments.title: Appointment of judges and officials
segments.gist: Moses recalls how he appointed wise men as judges over the people to share the burden of leadership and to judge righteously.

segments.title: Spies sent from Kadesh-barnea
segments.gist: Moses recounts sending twelve spies from Kadesh-barnea to scout the land; they returned with fruit and reported that the land was good.

segments.title: Israel's rebellion and God's anger
segments.gist: The people refused to enter the land, murmuring against God; Moses reminds them of God's anger and his own prohibition from entering.

segments.title: Judgment: adults will not enter
segments.gist: God swore that the rebellious generation would die in the wilderness, except Caleb and Joshua; their children would inherit the land.

segments.title: Presumptuous attack and defeat
segments.gist: The people confessed their sin and presumptuously attacked the Amorites without God's presence, and were defeated and wept before the Lord.

2.summary: Deuteronomy 2 recounts Israel's journey through the wilderness, where God instructs them not to provoke the Edomites, Moabites, or Ammonites, whose lands He has given to them. The chapter ends with the defeat of Sihon, king of Heshbon, and the capture of his cities.

segments.title: God's command to pass through Edom
segments.gist: God tells Moses to lead the people through the wilderness, not to meddle with Edom, for He has given Mount Seir to Esau's descendants.

segments.title: Journey past Moab
segments.gist: Israel passes by the children of Esau and crosses the brook Zered; the generation of fighting men is consumed as God swore.

segments.title: Command regarding Ammon
segments.gist: God instructs Israel not to distress the Ammonites, for He has given their land to the children of Lot; the chapter notes earlier inhabitants.

segments.title: Defeat of Sihon
segments.gist: Israel asks Sihon for passage, but he refuses; God delivers him to Israel, who defeats him and takes all his cities.

3.summary: Moses recounts the defeat of Og, king of Bashan, and the allocation of land east of the Jordan to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh. He then charges Joshua not to fear the coming conquest and pleads with God to let him enter the promised land, but God refuses and tells him to prepare Joshua instead.

segments.title: Defeat of Og
segments.gist: Moses recalls how the Israelites defeated Og, king of Bashan, and took all his cities, devoting them to destruction.

segments.title: Land taken from Og
segments.gist: The land east of the Jordan from the Arnon to Mount Hermon is described, including Og's iron bedstead in Rabbah.

segments.title: Allotment to eastern tribes
segments.gist: Moses assigns the conquered land to Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh, specifying boundaries and cities.

segments.title: Conditions for eastern tribes
segments.gist: Moses commands the eastern tribes to send their warriors ahead of Israel until the land is conquered, then they may return to their inheritance.

segments.title: Moses forbidden to enter
segments.gist: Moses pleads with God to enter the promised land, but God refuses and tells him to commission Joshua and not fear.

4.summary: Moses urges Israel to obey God's statutes and remember the covenant at Horeb, warning against idolatry and announcing exile and restoration. He sets apart three cities of refuge east of the Jordan, and the chapter closes by identifying the law Moses set before the people.

segments.title: Exhortation to obedience and wisdom
segments.gist: Moses calls Israel to hear and keep God's statutes, warning against adding or taking away, and cites their nearness to God as unique.

segments.title: Remember Horeb and the covenant
segments.gist: Moses recalls the assembly at Horeb where God spoke from the fire and gave the Ten Commandments, commanding the people to teach their children.

segments.title: Warning against idolatry
segments.gist: Moses warns against making any graven image, reminding Israel that God is a consuming fire and that they saw no form at Horeb.

segments.title: Exile and restoration promised
segments.gist: Moses foretells that if Israel corrupts itself and serves idols, they will be scattered among the nations, but God will be found if they seek Him with all their heart.

segments.title: Appeal to history and exclusive worship
segments.gist: Moses appeals to the unique events of Israel's history and calls them to know and obey the Lord alone, that it may go well with them and their children.

segments.title: Cities of refuge and law introduced
segments.gist: Moses sets apart three cities of refuge east of the Jordan for unintentional killers and begins to declare the law on the plains of Moab.

5.summary: Moses gathers all Israel and recounts the covenant made at Horeb, declaring that God spoke to the people face to face from the fire and gave the Ten Commandments, which Moses received on stone tablets. He then recalls how the people, terrified by the fire and voice, asked Moses to mediate, and how God approved their request and called them to obey all his commands so that they and their children might live long in the land.

segments.title: Moses summons Israel to hear
segments.gist: Moses calls all Israel to hear the statutes and judgments, reminding them of the covenant God made at Horeb with them and their fathers.

segments.title: The Ten Commandments recited
segments.gist: Moses repeats the Ten Commandments spoken by God from the midst of the fire, covering Israel's duties toward God and toward neighbor.

segments.title: People fear the fire and voice
segments.gist: After God speaks, the people are terrified and ask Moses to hear God's words and relay them, promising to obey.

segments.title: God approves and commands obedience
segments.gist: God approves the people's request and tells Moses to teach them all his commandments so they may live long and prosper in the land.

6.summary: Moses calls Israel to obey God's commandments so they may live long in the land, and he gives the central command to love the LORD with all the heart, teaching it diligently to children. He warns against forgetting God in prosperity and against testing Him, urging wholehearted obedience and the passing on of the covenant to the next generation.

segments.title: Moses recounts the command to obey
segments.gist: Moses reminds Israel of the statutes and judgments God commanded him to teach them, so they may fear the LORD and multiply in the land.

segments.title: The Shema: love and teach
segments.gist: Israel is told that the LORD is one and must be loved wholeheartedly, with these words taught diligently to children and bound as signs.

segments.title: Warning against forgetting in prosperity
segments.gist: When God brings them into a good land with abundant provisions, they must not forget the LORD who brought them out of Egypt.

segments.title: Do not test God; do what is right
segments.gist: Israel must not test the LORD as at Massah, but diligently keep His commandments so that it may go well with them.

segments.title: Explaining the covenant to children
segments.gist: When children ask about the meaning of the testimonies, parents are to recount the exodus and God's gift of the land, and obedience is counted as righteousness.

7.summary: Moses instructs Israel to completely destroy the seven Canaanite nations and avoid all alliances or intermarriage with them, because they would lead Israel into idolatry. He reminds the people that God chose them not for their own greatness but out of love and faithfulness to the oath sworn to their fathers, and he promises that obedience will bring blessing and victory over enemies.

segments.title: Command to Destroy Canaanites
segments.gist: Moses commands Israel to conquer and utterly destroy the seven nations, making no covenant or intermarriage with them.

segments.title: Israel Chosen by God's Love
segments.gist: Moses explains that God chose Israel not because of their numbers but out of love and faithfulness to the oath to their fathers.

segments.title: Blessings for Obedience
segments.gist: Moses promises that obedience will bring blessings of fertility, health, and victory, and he repeats the command to destroy the Canaanite nations.

segments.title: Do Not Fear, Remember God's Power
segments.gist: Moses tells Israel not to fear the Canaanites but to remember God's mighty acts in Egypt and trust that He will drive out the nations; he warns against coveting their silver and gold or bringing abominations into their homes.

8.summary: Moses calls Israel to remember and obey all of God's commandments so they may live and multiply and possess the land. He recounts the wilderness years—the manna, the lack of clothing wearing out, and the discipline of hunger—to teach that man does not live by bread alone but by every word from God's mouth. He warns that when they enter the good land and enjoy its wealth, they must not forget the LORD who gave it, lest they say their own power got them the wealth.

segments.title: Remember the wilderness way
segments.gist: Moses urges Israel to keep God's commandments and to remember how God humbled and tested them in the wilderness with manna, teaching that man lives by every word of God.

segments.title: A good land to enjoy
segments.gist: Moses describes the good land with brooks, wheat, vines, olives, and honey, where they will eat and be full and bless the LORD for the good land.

segments.title: Beware forgetting God in plenty
segments.gist: Moses warns that when they are full and wealthy they must not forget the LORD who brought them out of Egypt and gave them the power to get wealth, lest they perish like the nations.

9.summary: Moses reminds Israel that God is driving out the Canaanites because of their wickedness, not because of Israel's righteousness, and recounts their repeated rebellions, especially the golden calf at Horeb, showing God's mercy in not destroying them.

segments.title: Not for Your Righteousness
segments.gist: Moses tells Israel they will dispossess nations greater than they, but not because of their own righteousness; it is because of the Canaanites' wickedness and God's promise to the fathers.

segments.title: The Golden Calf at Horeb
segments.gist: Moses recounts how Israel provoked God at Horeb by making a molten calf, and how he broke the tablets and interceded for them.

segments.title: Rebellions at Other Places
segments.gist: Moses lists other times Israel provoked God: at Taberah, Massah, Kibroth-hattaavah, and Kadesh-barnea, where they refused to enter the land.

segments.title: Moses' Intercession
segments.gist: Moses describes his forty-day intercession, pleading with God not to destroy Israel for His own name's sake and because of His promise to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

10.summary: Moses recounts how God gave him the second set of stone tablets after the first were broken, and how the Levites were set apart to carry the ark and minister before the Lord. He calls Israel to fear, love, and obey God, reminding them that God shows no partiality and executes justice for the fatherless and widow.

segments.title: Second Tablets and the Ark
segments.gist: Moses recalls God's command to hew two stone tablets like the first, which God wrote on and placed in the ark.

segments.title: Levitical Priesthood and Inheritance
segments.gist: The tribe of Levi is set apart to bear the ark and minister before the Lord, having no land inheritance.

segments.title: Moses' Intercession and God's Command
segments.gist: Moses recounts his forty days on the mountain and God's command to arise and lead the people into the land.

segments.title: Call to Fear and Love God
segments.gist: Israel is called to fear, love, and obey God, who shows no partiality and executes justice for the vulnerable.

segments.title: God's Mighty Acts and Promise
segments.gist: Moses recalls God's mighty acts in Egypt and the wilderness, and promises that God will multiply Israel as the stars.

11.summary: Moses calls Israel to love and obey the LORD by remembering His mighty acts, from Egypt to the wilderness, and sets before them the blessing of obedience and the curse of disobedience. He describes the good land they are about to enter and urges them to teach God's words to their children and to choose obedience so that they may dwell long in the land.

segments.title: Love and obey the LORD
segments.gist: Moses commands Israel to love the LORD and keep His charge, statutes, and judgments, and to remember His discipline.

segments.title: Remember the LORD's great acts
segments.gist: Israel is told to keep all the commandments and to remember the LORD's signs and works in Egypt and the wilderness.

segments.title: Blessing for obedience, curse for turning away
segments.gist: If Israel loves and serves the LORD wholeheartedly, He will send rain and grass; but if they turn to other gods, His anger will bring drought and they will perish.

segments.title: Teach these words to your children
segments.gist: Moses urges Israel to bind God's words as signs and teach them to their children, so that they may possess the land and prevail over enemies.

segments.title: Set before you blessing and curse
segments.gist: Moses sets before Israel a blessing on Mount Gerizim and a curse on Mount Ebal, and commands them to observe all the statutes in the land they are entering.

12.summary: Moses commands Israel to destroy all Canaanite places of worship and to bring their offerings to the single place the LORD will choose for His name. He warns against following Canaanite practices, permits meat to be eaten freely except blood, and warns against inquiring after other gods.

segments.title: Destroy Canaanite Worship Places
segments.gist: Israel must utterly destroy all high places, altars, and images where Canaanites worship their gods.

segments.title: Bring Offerings to Chosen Place
segments.gist: Israel must bring tithes, offerings, and sacrifices to the place the LORD chooses, not to every place they see.

segments.title: Slaughter and Eat Meat Freely
segments.gist: Meat may be eaten within their gates as they desire, but blood must not be eaten and holy things must be brought to the chosen place.

segments.title: Rules for Eating Meat and Blood
segments.gist: When the chosen place is far, they may slaughter and eat meat, but must pour out blood and not eat it, so it may go well with them.

segments.title: Avoid Canaanite Religious Practices
segments.gist: Israel must not inquire after the gods of the nations or imitate their worship, but must do only what the LORD commands.

13.summary: Moses warns Israel against being enticed to serve other gods, whether by a prophet or dreamer of dreams, by a close relative or friend, or by an entire city. He commands that such enticers be put to death and that a city that turns to idolatry be utterly destroyed, so that Israel may remain faithful to the LORD.

segments.title: False Prophet Enticement
segments.gist: If a prophet or dreamer of dreams entices Israel to serve other gods, he must be put to death for trying to turn them from the LORD.

segments.title: Family or Friend Enticement
segments.gist: If a close relative or friend secretly entices to idolatry, the people must not consent but must put the enticer to death, and all Israel shall hear and fear.

segments.title: City Enticed to Idolatry
segments.gist: If a city is found to have turned to serve other gods, it must be utterly destroyed with all its spoil, and the LORD will turn from His fierce anger.

14.summary: Moses instructs Israel on mourning customs and clean and unclean animals, reiterates the law of the tithe, and gives instructions for the year of tithing and the care of the Levite, stranger, fatherless, and widow.

segments.title: Mourning customs forbidden
segments.gist: Israel is told not to cut themselves or make baldness for the dead, for they are a holy people.

segments.title: Clean and unclean animals
segments.gist: Moses lists clean and unclean animals, fish, and birds, and forbids eating anything that dies of itself.

segments.title: Tithe and the year of tithing
segments.gist: Israel is commanded to tithe yearly and every third year to support the Levite, stranger, fatherless, and widow.

15.summary: Deuteronomy 15 instructs Israel on the remission of debts every seven years, the release of Hebrew servants in the seventh year, and the consecration of firstborn animals. It emphasizes generosity toward the poor and warns against exploiting the upcoming release year.

segments.title: The Seven-Year Debt Release
segments.gist: Every seven years debts are to be released, and the Lord will bless Israel if they obey.

segments.title: Generosity to the Poor
segments.gist: Israel must not harden their hearts against the poor but lend generously, for the poor will always be among them.

segments.title: Release of Hebrew Servants
segments.gist: Hebrew servants are to be freed in the seventh year and generously supplied, remembering Israel's slavery in Egypt.

segments.title: Firstborn Animals Consecrated
segments.gist: All firstborn male animals are to be consecrated to the Lord and eaten before Him, except those with defects.

16.summary: Deuteronomy 16 instructs Israel to observe the Passover and Feast of Unleavened Bread in the month of Abib, to celebrate the Feast of Weeks seven weeks later, and to keep the Feast of Tabernacles for seven days. It also commands the appointment of judges and officers in every city to judge righteously, and forbids planting groves or setting up pillars beside the altar of the LORD.

segments.title: Passover and Unleavened Bread
segments.gist: Israel must keep the Passover in the month of Abib and eat unleavened bread for seven days, with no leaven found in their homes.

segments.title: Feast of Weeks
segments.gist: Seven weeks after the harvest begins, Israel is to celebrate the Feast of Weeks with a freewill offering and rejoice before the LORD.

segments.title: Feast of Tabernacles
segments.gist: After gathering the harvest, Israel is to keep the Feast of Tabernacles for seven days and rejoice with their households.

segments.title: Three Annual Feasts
segments.gist: All males must appear before the LORD three times a year, each bringing a gift according to the blessing received.

segments.title: Appointment of Judges
segments.gist: Judges and officers are to be appointed in every city to judge with righteous judgment, without partiality or bribes.

segments.title: Forbidden Worship Practices
segments.gist: Israel must not plant groves of trees near the altar of the LORD or set up sacred pillars, which the LORD hates.

17.summary: Deuteronomy 17 sets rules for sacrifices with blemishes, the death penalty for idolatry after careful inquiry, the handling of difficult legal cases by the Levitical priests, and the selection and conduct of a king, who must copy and obey the law.

segments.title: Punishment for Idolatry
segments.gist: If someone serves other gods, the matter must be thoroughly investigated; if true, the idolater is stoned to death on the testimony of two or three witnesses.

segments.title: Appeals to Priests and Judge
segments.gist: Difficult legal cases are brought to the Levitical priests and the judge; anyone who presumes to disobey their verdict must die.

segments.title: Laws Concerning a King
segments.gist: When Israel asks for a king, God will choose him; he must not multiply horses, wives, or silver and gold, and must copy and read the law all his days.

18.summary: Moses instructs Israel that the Levitical priests will have no land inheritance but will live on the offerings brought to the LORD. He forbids the people from adopting the abominable practices of the surrounding nations, such as divination and child sacrifice, and promises that God will raise up a prophet like Moses whom the people must obey.

segments.title: Priests' Portion and Inheritance
segments.gist: The Levitical priests receive no land inheritance; their portion comes from the LORD's offerings and firstfruits.

segments.title: Warning Against Canaanite Abominations
segments.gist: Israel must not learn the detestable practices of the nations, including divination, sorcery, and child sacrifice.

segments.title: Promise of a Prophet Like Moses
segments.gist: God will raise up a prophet like Moses from among the people, and everyone must listen to him.

segments.title: Test of a False Prophet
segments.gist: A prophet who speaks presumptuously or in another god's name must die; a sign of falsehood is an unfulfilled prediction.

19.summary: Deuteronomy 19 sets out laws for Israel: cities of refuge for accidental killers, the case of a deliberate murderer who flees to refuge, protection of landmark boundaries, and rules for witnesses, including the law of retaliation for false accusers.

segments.title: Cities of refuge appointed
segments.gist: Moses instructs Israel to set apart three cities of refuge for those who kill a neighbor unintentionally.

segments.title: Case of accidental killer
segments.gist: An example is given of an accidental killing, and the killer may flee to a refuge city and live.

segments.title: Three more cities added
segments.gist: If God enlarges Israel's borders, three additional cities of refuge are to be added to prevent innocent bloodshed.

segments.title: Deliberate murderer's fate
segments.gist: A murderer who flees to a refuge city must be handed over to the avenger of blood and put to death without pity.

segments.title: Rules for witnesses
segments.gist: A single witness is insufficient; false witnesses are to receive the punishment they intended for the accused, with life for life and eye for eye.

20.summary: Deuteronomy 20 gives Israel laws for warfare: the priest and officers encourage the troops not to fear, exemptions are provided for men with unfinished obligations, and procedures are set for offering peace before attacking a city, for besieging distant cities, and for utterly destroying the cities of the promised land. It also includes a rule about not destroying fruit trees during a siege.

segments.title: Priest's encouragement before battle
segments.gist: When Israel goes to war, the priest tells the people not to fear because the Lord fights for them.

segments.title: Exemptions from military service
segments.gist: Officers send home men who have built a house, planted a vineyard, or become engaged, and those who are fearful.

segments.title: Terms for distant cities
segments.gist: Israel must offer peace to a distant city; if refused, they besiege it, kill the men, and take spoil.

segments.title: Destruction of Canaanite cities
segments.gist: In the cities of the promised land, Israel must utterly destroy all people to prevent idolatry.

segments.title: Preservation of fruit trees
segments.gist: During a siege, Israel must not cut down fruit trees for food, but may use non-fruit trees for siege works.

21.summary: Deuteronomy 21 gives laws for unsolved murders, marrying a captive woman, the rights of a firstborn son in a polygamous family, and the execution of a stubborn and rebellious son. It closes with rules for burying an executed criminal, requiring burial the same day because a hanged man is accursed of God.

segments.title: Unsolved murder atonement
segments.gist: Elders and judges measure to the nearest city, whose elders break a heifer's neck and wash their hands to atone for unknown bloodshed.

segments.title: Marrying a captive woman
segments.gist: A man may take a captive woman as wife after she mourns her parents; if he rejects her, he must let her go free.

segments.title: Firstborn son's double portion
segments.gist: A hated wife's firstborn son still receives the double portion as the firstfruits of his father's strength.

segments.title: Stubborn son stoned
segments.gist: A stubborn and rebellious son who will not obey his parents is brought to the elders and stoned by the men of his city.

segments.title: Burial of hanged criminal
segments.gist: A hanged criminal's body must be buried the same day, for he is accursed of God and must not defile the land.

22.summary: Deuteronomy 22 is a collection of covenant laws covering lost property, clothing and construction safety, sexual purity, and marriage violations. It includes rules on returning a neighbor's stray animal, distinguishing garments, building a parapet, and various cases of sexual immorality with their penalties.

segments.title: Laws on lost property
segments.gist: Israelites must return a neighbor's stray ox or sheep and help lift a fallen animal, not ignoring it.

segments.title: Bird's nest rule
segments.gist: If one finds a bird's nest, they may take the young but must let the mother go, so it may go well with them.

segments.title: Laws on mixtures and tassels
segments.gist: Commands against mixing seeds, plowing with mixed animals, wearing mixed fabrics, and a requirement to wear tassels.

segments.title: Laws on sexual immorality
segments.gist: Various cases of sexual sin are addressed: false accusations, adultery, rape in town and country, and relations with a betrothed woman, with penalties.

23.summary: Deuteronomy 23 is a collection of laws given to Israel concerning exclusion from the congregation, ritual purity in the camp, treatment of escaped servants, cult prostitution, lending at interest, vows, and gleaning. The chapter sets boundaries for who may belong to the assembly and gives rules for daily life in the promised land.

segments.title: Exclusion from the congregation
segments.gist: Laws exclude certain groups from the assembly of the LORD, with specific limits for Edomites and Egyptians.

segments.title: Purity in the camp
segments.gist: Rules for ritual cleanliness in the military camp, including dealing with nocturnal emissions and latrine areas.

segments.title: Protection of escaped servants
segments.gist: A servant who escapes to Israel must not be returned to his master but allowed to live freely.

segments.title: Ban on cult prostitution
segments.gist: Israelites are forbidden to practice or pay for cult prostitution, and such offerings are detestable to the LORD.

segments.title: Laws on interest
segments.gist: Interest may be charged to foreigners but not to fellow Israelites, so that the LORD may bless them.

segments.title: Regulations for vows
segments.gist: Vows made to the LORD must be fulfilled without delay; failure to vow is not sin, but a spoken vow is binding.

segments.title: Gleaning in neighbor's field
segments.gist: Travelers may eat their fill from a neighbor's vineyard or grain field but must not carry any away.

24.summary: Deuteronomy 24 is a collection of covenant laws given by Moses to Israel, covering divorce, pledges, justice for the poor, gleaning, and limits on punishment. It sets out specific rules to protect the vulnerable and maintain fairness in the community.

segments.title: Divorce and Remarriage
segments.gist: A man who divorces his wife and she remarries cannot take her back, for that would be an abomination.

segments.title: Pledges and Kidnapping
segments.gist: A millstone may not be taken as a pledge, and kidnapping a fellow Israelite is a capital offense.

segments.title: Leprosy Regulations
segments.gist: Israel must carefully follow the priests' instructions regarding leprosy, remembering Miriam's punishment.

segments.title: Pledges and Wages
segments.gist: Pledges must be returned before sunset, and poor laborers must be paid their wages daily.

segments.title: Justice for the Vulnerable
segments.gist: Fathers are not to be put to death for children, and gleanings are left for the stranger, fatherless, and widow.

25.summary: Deuteronomy 25 continues Moses' covenant laws, covering limits on corporal punishment, the duty of levirate marriage and the shame of refusal, modesty in fighting, honest weights and measures, and the command to blot out Amalek's memory.

segments.title: Limits on corporal punishment
segments.gist: Judges may order beatings for the guilty but must not exceed forty stripes, lest the offender be humiliated.

segments.title: Levirate marriage and refusal
segments.gist: A brother must marry his childless brother's widow; if he refuses, she removes his shoe and spits, and he is named in Israel.

segments.title: Modesty in a fight
segments.gist: A woman who seizes a man's private parts in a fight must have her hand cut off.

segments.title: Honest weights and measures
segments.gist: Israelites must use just weights and measures; dishonesty is an abomination to the LORD.

segments.title: Command to blot out Amalek
segments.gist: Israel must remember how Amalek attacked the weak rear guard and, after entering the land, blot out Amalek's memory.

26.summary: Moses instructs Israel to present the firstfruits and the tithe of the third year with a spoken declaration of God's past deliverance and present provision, and he concludes the covenant by securing the people's pledge to obey God's statutes and God's promise to make them a holy people.

segments.title: Firstfruits Offering and Declaration
segments.gist: When Israel enters the land, they are to bring firstfruits to the priest and recite how God brought them from Egypt into a land flowing with milk and honey.

segments.title: Third-Year Tithe Declaration
segments.gist: In the third year, the tithe is given to the Levite, stranger, fatherless, and widow, and the offerer declares he has obeyed and asks God to bless the land.

segments.title: Covenant Pledge and Promise
segments.gist: Israel pledges to obey the LORD as their God, and the LORD promises to make them a holy people and set them high above all nations.

27.summary: Moses and the elders of Israel command the people to set up large stones with the law written on them after crossing the Jordan, and to build an altar on Mount Ebal. Moses then directs the tribes to pronounce blessings on Mount Gerizim and curses on Mount Ebal, with the Levites declaring a series of specific curses that all the people must affirm.

segments.title: Command to write the law
segments.gist: Moses and the elders command Israel to set up plastered stones with the law written on them after crossing the Jordan, and to build an altar of unhewn stones.

segments.title: Israel becomes God's people
segments.gist: Moses and the priests declare that Israel has become the people of the LORD and must obey his commandments.

segments.title: Tribes for blessing and cursing
segments.gist: Moses assigns six tribes to stand on Mount Gerizim for the blessing and six on Mount Ebal for the curse.

segments.title: The Levites pronounce the curses
segments.gist: The Levites pronounce twelve curses for specific sins, and all the people respond 'Amen' after each.

28.summary: Moses sets before Israel the blessings that follow obedience to the LORD's voice and the curses that follow disobedience. The curses are described in escalating detail, culminating in the siege of Jerusalem, exile among the nations, and a return to Egypt, as a covenant warning to the people.

segments.title: Blessings for Obedience
segments.gist: If Israel obeys the LORD's voice, blessings will come in the city and field, on offspring and crops, and Israel will be established as a holy people.

segments.title: Curses for Disobedience
segments.gist: If Israel will not obey, curses will come in the city and field, on basket and store, and on offspring and crops.

segments.title: Curses in Daily Life
segments.gist: The LORD will send cursing, vexation, and rebuke in all Israel's undertakings; enemies will defeat them, and they will be scattered and oppressed.

segments.title: Siege and Desperate Straits
segments.gist: Because Israel does not serve the LORD with joy, a nation will besiege them, and they will eat their own children in the desperate straits of the siege.

segments.title: Exile and Return to Egypt
segments.gist: If Israel does not observe all the words of the law, the LORD will bring extraordinary plagues and scatter them among the nations, and they will return to Egypt in bondage.

29.summary: Moses summons Israel in Moab to renew the covenant, recounting God's deliverance from Egypt and wilderness provisions, and warning all present and future generations against turning to other gods. He declares the curses of the broken covenant and the desolation that will follow, while affirming that secret things belong to God and revealed things to Israel and their children.

segments.title: Moses Recounts God's Faithfulness
segments.gist: Moses calls Israel to remember God's works in Egypt and the wilderness, urging them to keep the covenant so they may prosper.

segments.title: All Stand to Enter Covenant
segments.gist: Every person, from leaders to strangers and servants, is gathered to swear the covenant, including future generations.

segments.title: Warning Against Idolatry
segments.gist: Moses warns against turning to the gods of other nations and declares that an idolatrous individual will face God's anger and be singled out for disaster.

segments.title: Desolation of the Land
segments.gist: Future generations and foreigners will see the land's destruction and ask why; the answer will be that Israel forsook the covenant and served other gods.

30.summary: Moses tells Israel that when they return to the LORD and obey Him, He will restore them from exile and circumcise their hearts. He declares the commandment is not too hard or far off, but near in their mouth and heart, and sets before them life and death, blessing and cursing, calling heaven and earth as witnesses and urging them to choose life.

segments.title: Promise of Restoration
segments.gist: Moses promises that if Israel returns to the LORD and obeys, He will gather them from exile and bless them.

segments.title: The Commandment Is Near
segments.gist: Moses says the commandment is not in heaven or beyond the sea, but near in their mouth and heart.

segments.title: Choose Life or Death
segments.gist: Moses sets before Israel life and death, blessing and cursing, and calls heaven and earth to witness as he urges them to choose life.

31.summary: Moses, now 120 years old, publicly commissions Joshua as his successor and delivers the written law to the priests and elders, commanding a public reading every seventh year. God appears at the tabernacle, foretells Israel's future rebellion and idolatry, and gives Moses a song as a witness. Moses writes the song and charges Joshua to be strong and courageous.

segments.title: Moses commissions Joshua publicly
segments.gist: Moses, barred from entering the land, encourages Israel and formally commissions Joshua before the people.

segments.title: Law given; septennial reading commanded
segments.gist: Moses delivers the written law to the priests and elders and commands a public reading every seventh year at the Feast of Tabernacles.

segments.title: God foretells rebellion; song given
segments.gist: At the tabernacle, God predicts Israel's apostasy and gives Moses a song as a witness, then charges Joshua to be strong.

segments.title: Moses writes song; final charge
segments.gist: Moses writes the song, places it with the ark, and assembles Israel to hear his final words and the song.

32.summary: Moses delivers his farewell song to Israel, recounting God's faithfulness and Israel's rebellion, and calls the heavens and earth to witness. After the song, God tells Moses to ascend Mount Nebo to view the promised land from afar, where he will die because of his trespass at Meribah.

segments.title: Call to Hear Moses' Song
segments.gist: Moses calls heaven and earth to witness as he proclaims the name of the Lord and declares His greatness.

segments.title: God's Faithfulness to Israel
segments.gist: Moses praises God as the Rock whose works are perfect, and recounts how He cared for Israel in the wilderness.

segments.title: Israel's Rebellion Against God
segments.gist: Israel grew fat and forsook God, provoking Him with foreign gods and sacrificing to demons.

segments.title: God's Anger and Threat of Judgment
segments.gist: God threatens to scatter Israel and blot out their memory, but restrains His anger for the enemy's sake.

segments.title: Call to Nations and Vindication
segments.gist: Moses calls the nations to rejoice with God's people, for He will avenge the blood of His servants and atone for His land.

segments.title: Moses Commanded to View Canaan
segments.gist: Moses and Joshua speak the song to the people; God tells Moses to ascend Mount Nebo to see the land and die there.

33.summary: Moses, shortly before his death, blesses the tribes of Israel, giving each a distinct blessing and praising God as their refuge and deliverer. The chapter closes with a description of God riding to Israel's help and Israel dwelling in safety.

segments.title: Moses Introduces the Blessing
segments.gist: Moses proclaims God's coming from Sinai and his love for Israel, establishing God as king in Jeshurun.

segments.title: Blessings on Reuben, Judah, Levi
segments.gist: Moses blesses Reuben with survival, Judah with help against enemies, and Levi with faithfulness in teaching and sacrifice.

segments.title: Blessings on Benjamin, Joseph
segments.gist: Benjamin is called the beloved of the Lord, and Joseph receives abundant blessings of land, harvest, and strength.

segments.title: Blessings on Zebulun, Issachar, Gad
segments.gist: Zebulun and Issachar are blessed in their travels and tents, and Gad is praised for executing justice and God's righteousness.

segments.title: Blessings on Dan, Naphtali, Asher
segments.gist: Dan is likened to a lion's whelp, Naphtali is satisfied with favor, and Asher is blessed with iron and brass shoes.

segments.title: God as Israel's Refuge
segments.gist: Moses declares that no god is like Israel's God, who rides the heavens to help and gives Israel safety and victory.

34.summary: Moses goes up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, where God shows him the whole land of Canaan and tells him he will not enter it. Moses dies there at 120 years old and is buried by God in an unknown grave; Israel mourns him for thirty days, and Joshua succeeds him as leader.

segments.title: Moses Views the Promised Land
segments.gist: Moses climbs Mount Nebo, and God shows him the land from Gilead to the western sea, saying he will not cross into it.

segments.title: Death and Burial of Moses
segments.gist: Moses dies at 120 years old with undimmed eyesight; God buries him in an unknown valley, and Israel mourns for thirty days.

segments.title: Joshua Succeeds Moses
segments.gist: Joshua is filled with the spirit of wisdom and obeyed by Israel, and the chapter closes by praising Moses' unique signs and wonders.

1.summary: After Moses' death, God commissions Joshua to lead Israel into the promised land, promising his presence and requiring obedience to the law. Joshua orders the people to prepare to cross the Jordan, and the tribes east of the river agree to help their brothers, pledging loyalty as they did to Moses.

segments.title: God commissions Joshua
segments.gist: God tells Joshua to lead Israel across the Jordan, promising his presence and commanding him to be strong and keep the law.

segments.title: Joshua orders preparations
segments.gist: Joshua instructs the officers to prepare provisions and reminds the eastern tribes of their duty to help conquer the land.

segments.title: Eastern tribes pledge obedience
segments.gist: The tribes east of the Jordan promise to follow Joshua as they followed Moses and warn that anyone who rebels will be put to death.

2.summary: Joshua sends two spies to Jericho, where Rahab hides them and sends the king's men away. She confesses faith in Israel's God and secures a promise of safety for her family, then lets the spies down by a cord through her window. They return to Joshua and report that the land is given into their hands.

segments.title: Spies Lodged with Rahab
segments.gist: Joshua sends two spies from Shittim; they enter Jericho and lodge with Rahab, but the king's men come searching.

segments.title: Rahab's Confession and Request
segments.gist: Rahab tells the spies she knows the LORD has given them the land and asks for a promise to spare her family.

segments.title: Escape by Scarlet Cord
segments.gist: Rahab lets the spies down by a cord and instructs them to hide in the mountains; they agree to spare all in her house marked by the scarlet line.

segments.title: Spies Return to Joshua
segments.gist: The spies hide three days, then return to Joshua and report that the LORD has delivered the land into their hands.

3.summary: Joshua leads Israel to the Jordan River, where the priests carrying the ark step into the water and the river is cut off, allowing the people to cross on dry ground. Twelve men are chosen to take memorial stones from the riverbed, and the chapter ends with the priests standing in the dry riverbed as the nation crosses over.

segments.title: Joshua instructs the people
segments.gist: Joshua tells the people to consecrate themselves and gives instructions for the priests carrying the ark to lead the crossing.

segments.title: God promises to exalt Joshua
segments.gist: The LORD tells Joshua He will exalt him before Israel, and Joshua tells the priests to stand in the Jordan, promising the waters will be cut off.

segments.title: Jordan waters cut off
segments.gist: As the priests' feet touch the water, the Jordan is cut off and the people cross on dry ground while the priests stand firm in the riverbed.

4.summary: After Israel crosses the Jordan, God commands Joshua to set up twelve memorial stones taken from the riverbed. Joshua does so, and the stones are placed at Gilgal as a lasting sign so future generations will remember how the Lord dried up the Jordan before Israel, as he had done at the Red Sea.

segments.title: Twelve Stones Commanded
segments.gist: God instructs Joshua to choose twelve men, one from each tribe, to take twelve stones from the midst of the Jordan as a memorial.

segments.title: Stones Set and Priests Halted
segments.gist: Joshua sets twelve stones in the Jordan and at Gilgal; the priests carrying the ark stand still until all the people finish crossing.

segments.title: Priests Called Out of Jordan
segments.gist: The Lord commands Joshua to tell the priests to come up out of the Jordan, and when they do, the waters return and overflow as before.

segments.title: Gilgal Memorial Explained
segments.gist: The people camp at Gilgal, and Joshua explains that the stones are a sign so future generations may know the Lord dried up the Jordan as he did the Red Sea.

5.summary: When the kings west of the Jordan hear of Israel's crossing, they lose heart. God commands Joshua to circumcise the new generation born in the wilderness, and the people celebrate Passover at Gilgal, eating the produce of the land as the manna ceases. Joshua encounters a man with a drawn sword who identifies himself as the captain of the LORD's host, and Joshua bows in reverence.

segments.title: Circumcision at Gilgal
segments.gist: God commands Joshua to circumcise the Israelite men born in the wilderness, and the place is named Gilgal because God rolled away the reproach of Egypt.

segments.title: Passover and Manna Ceases
segments.gist: Israel keeps Passover at Gilgal and eats unleavened cakes and parched grain; the manna stops the next day as they eat the fruit of Canaan.

segments.title: Joshua Meets the Captain
segments.gist: Joshua sees a man with a drawn sword near Jericho, learns he is the captain of the LORD's host, and is told to remove his sandals on holy ground.

6.summary: Joshua receives instructions from the LORD on how Israel is to conquer Jericho: the armed men are to march around the city once daily for six days, with seven priests carrying trumpets before the ark, and on the seventh day they are to march seven times and shout when the trumpets sound. Joshua relays the plan, and on the seventh day the walls fall after the shout, the city is destroyed with Rahab and her household spared, and Joshua pronounces a curse on anyone who rebuilds Jericho.

segments.title: The LORD's instructions to Joshua
segments.gist: The LORD tells Joshua that Jericho is given into his hand and commands a six-day march with priests blowing trumpets before the ark.

segments.title: Seventh-day march and shout
segments.gist: The LORD commands seven circuits on the seventh day, a long trumpet blast, and a shout that will bring down the walls.

segments.title: Six days of marching
segments.gist: Joshua relays the plan, and Israel marches around Jericho once daily for six days with priests blowing trumpets and the ark following.

segments.title: Walls fall on the seventh day
segments.gist: On the seventh day the people shout, the walls collapse, and the Israelites enter the city and destroy everything except Rahab and her household.

segments.title: Rahab and her family spared
segments.gist: Joshua sends the two spies to bring out Rahab and all her relatives, and she dwells in Israel because she hid the messengers.

segments.title: Curse on rebuilding Jericho
segments.gist: Joshua pronounces a curse on anyone who rebuilds Jericho, and the LORD is with Joshua, whose fame spreads through the land.

7.summary: After Israel's defeat at Ai, Joshua learns that Achan took plunder from Jericho despite the ban. Achan and his family are stoned and burned in the valley of Achor, and God's anger is turned away.

segments.title: Israel Defeated at Ai
segments.gist: Joshua sends men to spy out Ai; they report it is small, so only about three thousand men go up, but they are routed and about thirty-six are killed.

segments.title: Joshua's Lament and God's Answer
segments.gist: Joshua and the elders fall before the ark in grief; God tells Joshua to get up because Israel has sinned by taking of the devoted things.

segments.title: God Explains the Sin
segments.gist: God explains that Israel has taken accursed things, and commands that the guilty be destroyed by fire along with all he has.

segments.title: Achan Identified by Lot
segments.gist: Joshua brings Israel near by tribes, and the lot falls on Achan, who confesses that he took a Babylonian garment, silver, and gold from Jericho.

segments.title: Achan and Family Stoned
segments.gist: Joshua sends messengers who bring the stolen items; Achan and his family are stoned and burned in the valley of Achor, and a heap of stones is raised over him.

8.summary: After Israel's defeat at Ai because of Achan's sin, God directs Joshua to set an ambush and destroy the city; Israel defeats Ai, Joshua builds an altar and reads the law to the people.

segments.title: God commands attack on Ai
segments.gist: God tells Joshua not to fear and to take all the fighting men against Ai, promising victory.

segments.title: Joshua plans ambush
segments.gist: Joshua sends 30,000 men to lie in ambush behind Ai while he leads the main force to draw out the city's defenders.

segments.title: Israel defeats Ai
segments.gist: The men of Ai pursue Israel, the ambush enters and burns the city, and Israel routs the enemy.

segments.title: Ai destroyed and king hanged
segments.gist: Israel kills all the inhabitants of Ai, takes the spoil, and hangs the king of Ai on a tree until evening.

segments.title: Altar and law reading
segments.gist: Joshua builds an altar on Mount Ebal, writes the law, and reads it to all Israel with the ark present.

9.summary: The Gibeonites, hearing of Israel's victories, deceive Joshua and the elders by pretending to be from a distant land, securing a peace treaty. Three days later Israel discovers they are nearby neighbors but honors the oath sworn before the LORD. The Gibeonites are made servants, and Joshua rebukes the congregation for not seeking God's counsel.

segments.title: Gibeonites plan deception
segments.gist: The Gibeonites, alarmed by Israel's conquests, send ambassadors with worn supplies to pretend they come from a far country and seek a treaty.

segments.title: Joshua makes treaty
segments.gist: The men of Israel question them, but Joshua and the elders make peace without consulting the LORD, and the Gibeonites are accepted.

segments.title: Deception discovered
segments.gist: Three days later Israel learns the Gibeonites are neighbors; the congregation murmurs, but the princes uphold the oath sworn to them.

segments.title: Gibeonites made servants
segments.gist: Joshua confronts the Gibeonites, who explain their fear, and he assigns them to be woodcutters and water carriers for the altar.

10.summary: Five Amorite kings besiege Gibeon, so Joshua marches overnight and defeats them with hailstones and the sun standing still over Gibeon. The five kings are trapped in a cave at Makkedah and executed, and Joshua then conquers the southern cities from Makkedah to Debir before returning to Gilgal.

segments.title: Gibeon calls Joshua for help
segments.gist: Adoni-zedek of Jerusalem forms an alliance of five Amorite kings to attack Gibeon for making peace with Israel; the Gibeonites ask Joshua for help.

segments.title: Joshua defeats the Amorites
segments.gist: Joshua marches overnight, routs the Amorites with hailstones, and at his command the sun and moon stand still while Israel prevails.

segments.title: Five kings found in cave
segments.gist: The five kings hide in a cave at Makkedah; Joshua orders the cave sealed and the pursuit continued until the enemy is destroyed.

segments.title: Kings executed at Makkedah
segments.gist: Joshua brings out the five kings, has the captains put their feet on the kings' necks, kills them, and hangs them on trees until evening.

segments.title: Southern cities conquered
segments.gist: Joshua takes Makkedah, Libnah, Lachish, Eglon, Hebron, and Debir, destroying their inhabitants and kings as he had done to Jericho and Ai.

segments.title: Joshua returns to Gilgal
segments.gist: Joshua subdues the whole southern region from Kadesh-barnea to Gaza, leaving no survivors, and returns with Israel to Gilgal.

11.summary: Joshua leads a united Israelite campaign against a northern coalition of Canaanite kings gathered by Jabin of Hazor, defeating them at the waters of Merom and destroying Hazor. The chapter then lists the territories conquered, including the Anakim and the land of the Rephaim, and concludes with a summary of Joshua's obedience and the rest from war.

segments.title: Northern Kings Gather
segments.gist: Jabin of Hazor gathers a vast coalition of northern and eastern kings with horses and chariots to fight Israel.

segments.title: Israel Defeats Coalition
segments.gist: God assures Joshua of victory; Israel routs the coalition at Merom, hamstrings their horses, and burns their chariots.

segments.title: Hazor Destroyed
segments.gist: Joshua captures and burns Hazor, kills its king, and takes the spoil and livestock from other cities, obeying Moses' commands.

segments.title: Conquered Territories Listed
segments.gist: The chapter lists regions conquered from the Negev to Mount Hermon, including Anakim and Rephaim, noting no city made peace except Gibeon.

segments.title: Anakim Destroyed and Land Rests
segments.gist: Joshua destroys the Anakim from the hill country and cities of Judah and Israel, leaving none in Israel's land; the land rests from war.

12.summary: This chapter lists the kings and territories that Israel defeated under Moses east of the Jordan and under Joshua west of the Jordan. It names each defeated king and the land they ruled, concluding with a total count of thirty-one kings.

segments.title: Kings Defeated by Moses
segments.gist: Recounts the kings east of Jordan defeated by Moses and the land given to Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh.

segments.title: Kings Defeated by Joshua
segments.gist: Lists the thirty-one kings west of the Jordan defeated by Joshua and the Israelites.

13.summary: God commands an aged Joshua to divide the remaining unconquered land among Israel, specifying the territories still to be possessed. The chapter then details the inheritance Moses had already assigned to Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh east of the Jordan, and notes that the tribe of Levi received no land inheritance but the offerings of the Lord.

segments.title: God Lists Unconquered Land
segments.gist: God tells Joshua that much land remains to be possessed and enumerates the regions and peoples still to be driven out, promising to drive them out before Israel.

segments.title: Eastern Tribes' Inheritance Recounted
segments.gist: The inheritance given by Moses to Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh east of the Jordan is described, including the kingdoms of Sihon and Og.

segments.title: Reuben's Territory
segments.gist: The territory allotted to the tribe of Reuben is detailed, including cities and villages in the plains of Moab.

segments.title: Gad's Territory
segments.gist: The territory allotted to the tribe of Gad is described, with its cities and villages east of the Jordan.

segments.title: Half-Manasseh's Territory
segments.gist: The territory given to the half-tribe of Manasseh is outlined, including the kingdoms of Og and Sihon, and the chapter concludes with Levi's lack of inheritance reiterated.

14.summary: Joshua 14 recounts Caleb's request to Joshua for the inheritance promised to him by Moses, citing his faithfulness as one of the spies, and Joshua grants him Hebron. The chapter also notes that the land was divided among the nine and a half tribes west of the Jordan, with the Levites receiving no land inheritance.

segments.title: Caleb's Request to Joshua
segments.gist: Caleb, son of Jephunneh, approaches Joshua at Gilgal to remind him of the promise Moses made regarding his inheritance.

segments.title: Caleb Recounts His Faithfulness
segments.gist: Caleb recounts how he and Joshua spied out the land and brought back a faithful report, and how Moses swore to give him the land he trodden.

segments.title: Joshua Grants Hebron to Caleb
segments.gist: Joshua blesses Caleb and gives him Hebron as an inheritance, and the land has rest from war.

15.summary: The chapter records the allotment of land to the tribe of Judah, including its southern, eastern, western, and northern boundaries, the inheritance of Caleb and his family, and a list of the cities belonging to Judah.

segments.title: Judah's Southern and Eastern Boundaries
segments.gist: The lot for Judah is described, with its southern border from the Dead Sea to the Mediterranean and its eastern border along the Dead Sea and Jordan.

segments.title: Caleb Conquers Hebron and Debir
segments.gist: Caleb drives out the Anakim from Hebron, and Othniel captures Debir, winning Caleb's daughter Achsah, who asks for springs of water.

segments.title: Cities of the Negev and Shephelah
segments.gist: The cities of Judah in the south and lowland are listed, including Beersheba, Ziklag, and others with their villages.

segments.title: Cities of the Shephelah and Philistine Plain
segments.gist: More lowland cities are listed, such as Eshtaol, Zorah, Ekron, and Ashdod, with their villages.

segments.title: Cities of the Hill Country
segments.gist: The hill country cities of Judah are listed, including Hebron, Debir, and others with their villages.

segments.title: Cities of the Wilderness and Jerusalem
segments.gist: Wilderness cities like Beth-arabah and Engedi are listed, and the Jebusites in Jerusalem are noted as not being driven out.

16.summary: The chapter describes the inheritance allotted to the tribes of Joseph—Ephraim and Manasseh—giving the southern border of Ephraim's territory from the Jordan to the sea and listing cities within it. It notes that the Canaanites in Gezer remained among Ephraim and were put to forced labor.

segments.title: Joseph's lot and southern border
segments.gist: The lot of Joseph's descendants begins at the Jordan and runs through Bethel and the hill country to the sea.

segments.title: Ephraim's border and cities
segments.gist: Ephraim's territory is bounded on the east and west, with cities listed including Gezer and Tappuah.

segments.title: Separate cities and Canaanite labor
segments.gist: Additional cities are set apart for Ephraim, and the Canaanites in Gezer are subjected to forced labor.

17.summary: The chapter continues the allotment of land to the tribe of Manasseh, including the inheritance of Zelophehad's daughters and the failure of Manasseh to drive out the Canaanites in several cities. The descendants of Joseph complain to Joshua that their portion is too small, and Joshua tells them to clear the forest and drive out the Canaanites despite their chariots of iron.

segments.title: Manasseh's borders and daughters
segments.gist: The lot for Manasseh is described, including the allotment to Zelophehad's daughters, with boundaries listed.

segments.title: Manasseh's territory and unconquered cities
segments.gist: The boundaries of Manasseh's land are detailed, and the chapter notes that Manasseh could not drive out the Canaanites in several cities.

segments.title: Joseph's complaint and Joshua's response
segments.gist: The children of Joseph complain their inheritance is too small, and Joshua tells them to clear the forest and drive out the Canaanites with their iron chariots.

18.summary: The whole congregation of Israel assembles at Shiloh, where the tabernacle is set up, and Joshua challenges the seven tribes that have not yet received their inheritance. He sends out twenty-one men to survey the remaining land, casts lots before the LORD at Shiloh, and apportions the territory to the tribes of Benjamin, Simeon, Zebulun, Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and Dan. The chapter closes with the detailed boundaries and cities of Benjamin's inheritance.

segments.title: Joshua sends surveyors from Shiloh
