segments.gist: Israel gathers at Shiloh; Joshua rebukes seven tribes for delaying and sends men to survey the remaining land before casting lots.

segments.title: Benjamin's lot and boundaries
segments.gist: The lot falls to Benjamin; its territory is described by its borders and the cities within it.

19.summary: The chapter completes the allotment of land to the remaining tribes by lot: Simeon receives cities within Judah's territory, Zebulun, Issachar, Asher, and Naphtali receive their inheritances, and Dan receives a portion with cities listed. The chapter concludes with the Israelites giving Joshua the city of Timnath-serah, which he builds and where he settles.

segments.title: Simeon's Inheritance
segments.gist: The second lot falls to Simeon, whose inheritance is taken from Judah's portion and includes cities like Beersheba and Hormah.

segments.title: Zebulun's Inheritance
segments.gist: The third lot goes to Zebulun; their border extends to Sarid and includes cities such as Bethlehem and Jokneam.

segments.title: Issachar's Inheritance
segments.gist: The fourth lot falls to Issachar; their territory includes Jezreel, Chesulloth, Shunem, and other cities.

segments.title: Asher's Inheritance
segments.gist: The fifth lot goes to Asher; their border includes cities like Helkath, Rehob, and Sidon, extending to the sea.

segments.title: Naphtali's Inheritance
segments.gist: The sixth lot falls to Naphtali; their inheritance includes cities such as Kedesh, Hammoth-dor, and Kartan.

segments.title: Dan's Inheritance and Joshua's Portion
segments.gist: The seventh lot goes to Dan; their cities are listed, and after the land is divided, Joshua receives Timnath-serah, which he builds and inhabits.

20.summary: God instructs Joshua to designate six cities of refuge where someone who kills a person accidentally may flee for protection from the avenger of blood. The chapter lists the cities east and west of the Jordan and describes the legal procedure for the accused to stand trial before the congregation.

segments.title: Cities of refuge appointed
segments.gist: God commands Joshua to appoint cities of refuge for accidental killers to flee from the avenger of blood.

segments.title: Six cities named
segments.gist: The six cities of refuge are listed: three east of the Jordan and three in Canaan west of the Jordan.

21.summary: The heads of the Levite families come to Eleazar the priest and Joshua at Shiloh to request cities to dwell in, as God had commanded through Moses. The children of Israel allot forty-eight cities with their suburbs to the Levites by lot from their inheritances, including the cities of refuge. The chapter concludes by noting that God gave Israel rest and that all His promises were fulfilled.

segments.title: Levites request cities
segments.gist: The Levite leaders remind Eleazar and Joshua that God commanded cities for them to dwell in with their suburbs.

segments.title: Cities allotted by lot
segments.gist: The Israelites give cities and suburbs to the Levites by lot according to their families, including the Kohathites, Gershonites, and Merarites.

segments.title: Cities of Aaron's sons
segments.gist: The cities given to the priests, the sons of Aaron, are listed from Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin, totaling thirteen cities with their suburbs.

segments.title: Cities of Kohath's families
segments.gist: The remaining Kohathite families receive ten cities from Ephraim, Dan, and Manasseh with their suburbs.

segments.title: Cities of Gershon's families
segments.gist: The Gershonite families receive thirteen cities from Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and Manasseh with their suburbs.

segments.title: Cities of Merari's families
segments.gist: The Merarite families receive twelve cities from Zebulun, Reuben, and Gad with their suburbs, totaling forty-eight Levite cities.

segments.title: God's promises fulfilled
segments.gist: The chapter concludes that God gave Israel rest and that all His good promises to Israel came to pass.

22.summary: Joshua summons the Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh, commends them for keeping their promise to help conquer Canaan, and sends them home with spoils and a charge to remain faithful. On their way back they build a large altar by the Jordan, which the other tribes interpret as rebellion and gather for war. A delegation led by Phinehas confronts them, and the eastern tribes explain the altar is a witness of shared faith, not a rival place of sacrifice, averting civil war.

segments.title: Joshua dismisses eastern tribes
segments.gist: Joshua blesses the Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh, praises their obedience, and sends them home with wealth and a warning to stay faithful.

segments.title: Altar by Jordan sparks war threat
segments.gist: The eastern tribes build a large altar near the Jordan, and the other Israelites gather at Shiloh to go to war against them.

segments.title: Phinehas confronts altar builders
segments.gist: Phinehas and ten princes confront the eastern tribes, accusing them of rebellion like Peor and Achan, and urge them not to provoke God's wrath.

segments.title: Eastern tribes defend altar purpose
segments.gist: The eastern tribes explain they built the altar not for sacrifice but as a witness between them and the western tribes, fearing future exclusion from the LORD.

segments.title: Conflict resolved and altar named
segments.gist: Phinehas and the princes accept the explanation, call off the war, and the eastern tribes name the altar Witness, declaring the LORD is God.

23.summary: Joshua, now old, gathers all Israel's elders, heads, judges, and officers to remind them of God's past faithfulness and to warn them against intermarrying with or serving the remaining nations. He urges them to love the LORD and obey all that is written in the law, warning that disobedience will bring God's judgment and drive them from the good land.

segments.title: Joshua recounts God's past deeds
segments.gist: Joshua, old and advanced in years, summons Israel's leaders and reminds them how God fought for them and gave them the land.

segments.title: Exhortation to be steadfast
segments.gist: Joshua urges the people to be courageous, keep the law of Moses, and not turn aside to other gods.

segments.title: Warning against mixing with nations
segments.gist: Joshua warns that God will no longer drive out the remaining nations if Israel intermarries with them, and he calls them to love the LORD.

segments.title: Consequences of disobedience
segments.gist: Joshua declares that if Israel turns away, God's anger will burn and they will perish from the good land.

segments.title: Call to choose faithfulness
segments.gist: Joshua calls the people to fear the LORD and serve him sincerely, warning that he will not forgive their sins if they serve other gods.

24.summary: Joshua gathers all the tribes of Israel at Shechem and recounts God's history with their ancestors from Abraham to the conquest of Canaan. He calls the people to choose whom they will serve, and they twice affirm they will serve the LORD. Joshua makes a covenant with them that day, sets up a stone as a witness, and then sends them away; the chapter closes with Joshua's death and burial, the burial of Joseph's bones, and the death of Eleazar the priest.

segments.title: Joshua recounts God's acts
segments.gist: Joshua assembles Israel at Shechem and recounts God's faithfulness from Abraham through the exodus and the conquest of Canaan.

segments.title: Call to choose whom to serve
segments.gist: Joshua challenges the people to fear the LORD and serve him, and the people affirm they will serve the LORD who brought them out of Egypt.

segments.title: Joshua warns and people affirm
segments.gist: Joshua warns that God is holy and jealous, but the people insist they will serve the LORD, and Joshua calls them to witness against themselves.

segments.title: Covenant and stone of witness
segments.gist: Joshua makes a covenant with the people, writes the words in a book, sets up a great stone as a witness, and sends the people to their inheritances.

segments.title: Death of Joshua and Eleazar
segments.gist: Joshua dies at 110 and is buried, Israel serves the LORD during the elders' lifetime, Joseph's bones are buried, and Eleazar the priest dies.

1.summary: After Joshua's death, the tribes of Israel ask who will go up first to fight the Canaanites; Judah and Simeon join forces and win victories, but the chapter also records failures to drive out inhabitants in several territories, and ends with the tribe of Dan being pressed into the hill country.

segments.title: Judah and Simeon defeat Canaanites
segments.gist: Israel asks who will fight first; Judah and Simeon unite, defeat Adoni-bezek, and take Jerusalem and other cities.

segments.title: Caleb gives Hebron and Debir
segments.gist: Judah takes Hebron and Debir; Caleb promises his daughter Achsah to the conqueror, and she asks for springs of water.

segments.title: Kenites and Benjamin's failure
segments.gist: The Kenites settle in the wilderness of Judah; Judah takes Gaza, Ashkelon, and Ekron, but Benjamin fails to drive out the Jebusites from Jerusalem.

segments.title: House of Joseph takes Bethel
segments.gist: The house of Joseph spies out Bethel, shows mercy to a man who reveals the entrance, and takes the city; the man founds Luz.

segments.title: Manasseh, Ephraim, Zebulun fail
segments.gist: Manasseh, Ephraim, Zebulun, Asher, and Naphtali do not drive out the Canaanites but live among them.

segments.title: Amorites press Dan
segments.gist: The Amorites force the Danites into the hill country and hold their ground from Akrabbim to Aijalon, marking the border of the Amorites.

2.summary: An angel of the LORD rebukes Israel at Bochim for making covenants with the Canaanites, and the people weep. After Joshua's generation dies, Israel forsakes the LORD for Baalim; the LORD allows oppressors to trouble them, yet raises judges to deliver them, but the people repeatedly return to corruption.

segments.title: Angel Rebukes Israel at Bochim
segments.gist: The angel of the LORD recounts Israel's failure to obey and dispossess the Canaanites, and the people weep at Bochim.

segments.title: Joshua's Generation and Apostasy
segments.gist: After Joshua dismisses the people and dies, a new generation arises that does not know the LORD and serves Baalim.

segments.title: Israel Oppressed by Enemies
segments.gist: The LORD's anger burns against Israel, and He delivers them into the hands of spoilers and enemies round about.

segments.title: Judges Raised but People Rebel
segments.gist: The LORD raises judges who deliver Israel, but the people quickly turn back and corrupt themselves more than their fathers.

segments.title: Nations Left to Test Israel
segments.gist: The LORD refuses to drive out the remaining nations, leaving them to test whether Israel will keep His commandments.

3.summary: God tests Israel by leaving enemy nations in the land, and the Israelites intermarry with them and serve their gods. When Israel cries out, God raises up deliverers: Othniel defeats Mesopotamia, Ehud assassinates the Moabite king Eglon, and Shamgar kills Philistines with an ox goad.

segments.title: Nations Left to Test Israel
segments.gist: The LORD leaves several nations to test Israel and teach war, and Israel intermarries with them and serves their gods.

segments.title: Othniel Delivers Israel
segments.gist: Israel serves Mesopotamia for eight years; when they cry out, Othniel judges them and defeats Cushan-rishathaim, and the land rests forty years.

segments.title: Ehud Kills King Eglon
segments.gist: Ehud, a left-handed Benjaminite, brings tribute to Eglon, assassinates him with a hidden dagger, escapes, and leads Israel to defeat Moab, giving the land eighty years of rest.

4.summary: Deborah, a prophetess and judge, summons Barak to lead Israel against Sisera's Canaanite army; Barak insists she go with him, and God gives Israel victory as Sisera's chariots are routed. Sisera flees on foot to the tent of Jael, who kills him with a tent peg, and Deborah and Barak celebrate the fall of Israel's enemy.

segments.title: Israel Sins and Is Oppressed
segments.gist: After Ehud's death, Israel again does evil, and the LORD sells them into the hand of Jabin, king of Canaan, whose captain Sisera oppresses them for twenty years.

segments.title: Deborah Summons Barak
segments.gist: Deborah, a prophetess judging Israel, summons Barak and delivers God's command to draw Sisera to the river Kishon; Barak agrees to go only if Deborah goes with him.

segments.title: Barak Defeats Sisera
segments.gist: Heber the Kenite is introduced; Deborah urges Barak to attack, and the LORD routs Sisera's chariots and army before Barak, who pursues them.

segments.title: Jael Kills Sisera
segments.gist: Sisera flees to Jael's tent, where she gives him milk, covers him, and drives a tent peg through his head; Barak arrives to find Sisera dead.

segments.title: Israel Subdues Jabin
segments.gist: God subdues Jabin before Israel, and the Israelites prevail and destroy him.

5.summary: Deborah and Barak sing a victory song after Israel's defeat of Sisera and the Canaanite army. The song praises God, recounts the battle, honors the tribes who fought, and curses those who held back, ending with the death of Sisera by Jael and a prayer for God's enemies to perish.

segments.title: Praise for Divine Victory
segments.gist: Deborah and Barak call Israel to praise the LORD for leading them and for the earth's response to His coming.

segments.title: Israel's Oppression and Deliverance
segments.gist: The song recalls the days of Shamgar and Jael when roads were deserted, then celebrates leaders who arose and the LORD's righteous acts.

segments.title: Tribes Rally to Battle
segments.gist: Deborah and Barak are called to lead, and the tribes are named—some who risked their lives and others who stayed behind.

segments.title: Kings Defeated, Meroz Cursed
segments.gist: The kings of Canaan fight and are swept away by the Kishon, and the angel of the LORD curses Meroz for not helping.

segments.title: Jael Kills Sisera
segments.gist: Jael is blessed above women; Sisera asks for water, falls asleep, and she strikes a tent peg through his head.

segments.title: Sisera's Mother Waits
segments.gist: Sisera's mother looks through the window, wondering why he delays, while her ladies imagine the spoil; the song ends with a prayer for God's enemies to perish.

6.summary: Israel is oppressed by Midian for seven years, so the LORD sends a prophet to rebuke them and then calls Gideon, who is threshing wheat in hiding. Gideon tests God with a fleece, and God gives him signs to confirm his calling.

segments.title: Israel Oppressed by Midian
segments.gist: Israel does evil, and the LORD delivers them into Midian's hand for seven years; Midian forces them into dens and caves.

segments.title: Prophet Rebukes Israel
segments.gist: The LORD sends a prophet to remind Israel of His deliverance from Egypt and to rebuke them for not obeying His voice.

segments.title: Gideon Called and Given a Sign
segments.gist: The angel of the LORD calls Gideon while he threshes wheat in hiding; Gideon questions God, and after a sign, builds an altar called Jehovah-shalom.

segments.title: Gideon Destroys Baal's Altar
segments.gist: That night Gideon tears down his father's altar to Baal and builds an altar to the LORD; the men of the city want to kill him, but Joash defends him.

segments.title: Midianites Gather for Battle
segments.gist: The Midianites, Amalekites, and children of the east gather, and the Spirit of the LORD comes upon Gideon, who summons Israel to follow him.

segments.title: Gideon Tests God with Fleece
segments.gist: Gideon asks God for a sign with a fleece: first dew on the fleece only, then dew on the ground only; God grants both.

7.summary: Gideon, camped with his army at the spring of Harod, is told by God to reduce his forces from thirty-two thousand to three hundred so that Israel cannot claim credit for the victory. That night Gideon overhears a Midianite's dream of a barley cake overturning the camp, takes courage, and surrounds the Midianite host with trumpets, jars, and torches; the enemy flees in panic, and the Ephraimites capture and kill the fleeing kings Oreb and Zeeb.

segments.title: Gideon's army reduced to three hundred
segments.gist: God tells Gideon to send home the fearful and then the careless, leaving only three hundred men to defeat Midian.

segments.title: Gideon hears the Midianite's dream
segments.gist: Gideon goes down to the enemy camp, overhears a man recount a dream of a barley cake overthrowing Midian, and worships God.

segments.title: Trumpets, jars, and torches
segments.gist: Gideon divides the three hundred into three companies, arms them with trumpets and hidden lamps, and at his signal they blow and shout, causing the Midianites to flee.

segments.title: Ephraimites capture Oreb and Zeeb
segments.gist: Israelites from Naphtali, Asher, and Manasseh pursue Midian, and the Ephraimites seize the fords and kill the princes Oreb and Zeeb.

8.summary: Gideon pacifies the Ephraimites, pursues the Midianite kings across the Jordan, and punishes the men of Succoth and Penuel for refusing him aid. After killing Zebah and Zalmunna, he declines to rule Israel but makes a golden ephod that becomes a snare; the land has rest for forty years until his death, after which Israel again turns to Baal and forgets Gideon's family.

segments.title: Gideon Calms Ephraim's Anger
segments.gist: Ephraimites criticize Gideon for not calling them to battle; he appeases them by saying their gleaning was better than his vintage.

segments.title: Succoth and Penuel Refuse Aid
segments.gist: Gideon and his 300 men cross Jordan pursuing Midianite kings; Succoth and Penuel refuse bread and are threatened with punishment.

segments.title: Gideon Punishes Succoth and Penuel
segments.gist: Gideon captures the kings, teaches Succoth's elders with thorns, and breaks down Penuel's tower, killing its men.

segments.title: Gideon Kills Zebah and Zalmunna
segments.gist: Gideon avenges his brothers' deaths by killing the Midianite kings after his young son refuses; the kings are slain.

segments.title: Gideon's Ephod and Israel's Rest
segments.gist: Gideon refuses to rule but makes a golden ephod that becomes a snare; Israel has rest forty years until his death.

segments.title: Gideon's Death and Israel's Apostasy
segments.gist: Gideon dies and is buried; Israel again worships Baal and forgets Gideon's family despite his kindness.

9.summary: Abimelech, son of Gideon by a concubine, murders his seventy half-brothers and is made king by the men of Shechem. After three years, God stirs up discord between Abimelech and the Shechemites; Jotham's parable of the trees and his curse are fulfilled when Gaal leads a revolt, Abimelech crushes Shechem and burns its tower, and he is finally killed by a millstone dropped by a woman at Thebez.

segments.title: Abimelech's conspiracy in Shechem
segments.gist: Abimelech, son of Jerubbaal by a concubine, persuades the men of Shechem to make him king by appealing to his kinship and by hiring vain fellows to follow him.

segments.title: Jotham's parable and curse
segments.gist: Jotham, the surviving son, tells the parable of the trees choosing a king and pronounces a curse on the men of Shechem and on Abimelech, then flees.

segments.title: God sends evil spirit and treachery
segments.gist: After three years God stirs up enmity between Abimelech and Shechem, and the Shechemites deal treacherously, setting ambushes on the highways.

segments.title: Gaal's revolt and Zebul's warning
segments.gist: Gaal son of Ebed gains the confidence of Shechem and boasts against Abimelech; Zebul, the city ruler, warns Abimelech and helps him ambush Gaal, who is driven out.

segments.title: Abimelech destroys Shechem
segments.gist: Abimelech attacks the people in the field, captures Shechem, kills its inhabitants, and burns the tower where the men and women have taken refuge.

segments.title: Abimelech killed at Thebez
segments.gist: Abimelech besieges Thebez, but a woman drops a millstone on his head; he has his armor-bearer kill him, and God repays his wickedness and the men of Shechem.

10.summary: After Abimelech's death, two minor judges, Tola and Jair, arise in Israel. Israel again turns to foreign gods, and when the Ammonites oppress them, the people cry out to the LORD, who rebukes them but then is moved by their confession and removal of foreign gods.

segments.title: Tola judges Israel
segments.gist: Tola, a man of Issachar, judges Israel for twenty-three years and is buried in Shamir.

segments.title: Jair judges Israel
segments.gist: Jair the Gileadite judges Israel twenty-two years; his thirty sons ride on thirty ass colts and have thirty cities.

segments.title: Israel serves foreign gods
segments.gist: Israel again does evil, serving Baalim, Ashtaroth, and the gods of surrounding nations; the LORD delivers them to the Philistines and Ammonites, who oppress them.

segments.title: Israel cries and repents
segments.gist: Israel cries to the LORD, confessing their sin; the LORD reminds them of past deliverances and refuses to save them, but they put away foreign gods and he is grieved for their misery.

segments.title: Ammonites gather for war
segments.gist: The Ammonites gather and camp in Gilead, and the Israelites assemble and camp at Mizpeh, seeking a leader to fight.

11.summary: Jephthah the Gileadite, an outcast warrior, is recalled by the elders of Gilead to lead them against the Ammonites. After failed negotiations with the Ammonite king over disputed land, Jephthah vows to sacrifice whatever comes out of his house to meet him if God gives him victory; he defeats Ammon, and his daughter comes out first, so he fulfills his vow, and the daughters of Israel mourn her yearly.

segments.title: Jephthah recalled as leader
segments.gist: The Gileadites, oppressed by Ammon, ask the outcast Jephthah to be their captain, and he agrees on condition of lasting leadership.

segments.title: Negotiations with Ammon
segments.gist: Jephthah sends messengers to the Ammonite king, who claims Israel took his land; Jephthah recounts Israel's history and denies the claim.

segments.title: Jephthah's vow and victory
segments.gist: The Spirit of the LORD comes on Jephthah; he vows to sacrifice whatever meets him after victory, then defeats the Ammonites.

segments.title: Jephthah fulfills his vow
segments.gist: Jephthah's daughter comes out to meet him, and after her two months of mourning, he fulfills his vow, and Israel's daughters mourn her yearly.

12.summary: Jephthah's conflict with the Ephraimites escalates into civil war; he defeats them at the Jordan fords, where the password "Shibboleth" exposes fleeing Ephraimites, and forty-two thousand are killed. The chapter closes with Jephthah's death and brief records of the judges Ibzan, Elon, and Abdon.

segments.title: Ephraimites confront Jephthah
segments.gist: The Ephraimites threaten Jephthah for not calling them to fight Ammon, and he replies that he did call but they did not help.

segments.title: Gilead defeats Ephraim
segments.gist: Jephthah gathers the Gileadites, defeats Ephraim, and they mockingly call the Gileadites fugitives of Ephraim.

segments.title: Ibzan judges Israel
segments.gist: Ibzan of Bethlehem judges Israel for seven years, dies, and is buried in Bethlehem.

segments.title: Elon judges Israel
segments.gist: Elon the Zebulunite judges Israel for ten years, dies, and is buried in Aijalon.

segments.title: Abdon judges Israel
segments.gist: Abdon the Pirathonite judges Israel for eight years, dies, and is buried in Pirathon.

13.summary: The Israelites again do evil, so God delivers them to the Philistines for forty years. The angel of the LORD appears to Manoah's barren wife, promising a son who will be a Nazirite and begin to deliver Israel. After the angel repeats the instructions to Manoah and ascends in the flame of the offering, the woman bears Samson.

segments.title: Israel Sins, Philistines Rule
segments.gist: Israel does evil again, and the LORD gives them into Philistine hands for forty years; the angel appears to Manoah's barren wife with a promise of a son.

segments.title: Woman Reports, Angel Returns
segments.gist: The woman tells Manoah about the man of God; Manoah prays, and the angel returns to repeat the Nazirite instructions for the child.

segments.title: Offering and Angel's Ascent
segments.gist: Manoah offers a kid and meal offering; the angel ascends in the flame, and Manoah fears death while his wife reasons God has accepted them.

segments.title: Samson Born and Blessed
segments.gist: The woman bears a son named Samson; the LORD blesses him, and the Spirit begins to move him at Mahaneh-dan.

14.summary: Samson goes down to Timnath and demands a Philistine woman for a wife despite his parents' objections. On the way he kills a young lion with his bare hands, and later finds honey in its carcass, which he turns into a riddle at his wedding feast. When the Philistines threaten his bride, she coaxes the answer from him, and he responds by killing thirty Philistines to pay his debt and leaving in anger.

segments.title: Samson seeks a Philistine wife
segments.gist: Samson goes to Timnath, sees a Philistine woman, and asks his parents to get her for him, despite their objections.

segments.title: Samson kills a lion
segments.gist: On the way to Timnath, Samson kills a young lion with his bare hands, and later finds honey in its carcass and eats it.

segments.title: Samson's wedding feast and riddle
segments.gist: At the wedding feast, Samson poses a riddle about the lion and honey, wagering thirty changes of garments.

segments.title: The bride reveals the answer
segments.gist: The Philistines threaten Samson's bride, who coaxes the answer from him, and they tell him the riddle's solution.

segments.title: Samson pays the wager and leaves
segments.gist: The Spirit of the LORD comes upon Samson; he kills thirty Philistines, gives their garments to the winners, and returns angrily to his father's house.

15.summary: Samson returns to Timnah to visit his wife and is turned away by her father. In revenge he burns the Philistines' fields with foxes and firebrands, then strikes them down after they kill his wife. When the Philistines come to bind him, the Spirit of the LORD enables him to break free and slay a thousand men with the jawbone of an ass, and God brings water from the jawbone to revive him.

segments.title: Samson Burns Philistine Fields
segments.gist: Samson visits his wife but is refused by her father, so he catches foxes, ties firebrands to them, and burns the Philistines' crops.

segments.title: Philistines Demand Samson
segments.gist: The Philistines come to Judah to capture Samson, and the men of Judah bind him with two new cords to hand him over.

segments.title: Samson Slays a Thousand
segments.gist: The Spirit of the LORD comes upon Samson, he breaks the cords, and kills a thousand Philistines with the jawbone of an ass.

segments.title: God Provides Water
segments.gist: Samson, thirsty and near death, cries to God, who brings water from the jawbone, reviving him; he judges Israel twenty years.

16.summary: Samson goes to Gaza and spends the night with a harlot; the men of Gaza lie in wait but he escapes by carrying off the city gates. He then falls in love with Delilah, who is bribed by the Philistine lords to discover the secret of his strength. After three false answers, she presses him until he reveals that his strength lies in his uncut hair; she has his hair cut while he sleeps, and the Philistines seize and blind him. His hair begins to grow again, and at a Philistine feast in the temple of Dagon he prays for strength, pulls down the pillars, and dies with a great multitude of Philistines.

segments.title: Samson Escapes Gaza
segments.gist: Samson visits a harlot in Gaza; the men lie in wait, but he rises at midnight and carries the city gates to Hebron.

segments.title: Delilah Seeks Samson's Secret
segments.gist: The Philistine lords bribe Delilah to find Samson's strength; she asks him, and he gives three false answers that fail.

segments.title: Samson Betrays His Secret
segments.gist: Delilah presses Samson daily until he reveals his uncut hair is his strength; she has it cut, and the Philistines seize and blind him.

segments.title: Samson Destroys the Temple
segments.gist: At a Philistine feast Samson prays for strength, pulls down the temple pillars, and dies with a great multitude of Philistines.

17.summary: Micah, an Ephraimite, confesses to his mother that he stole her silver; she blesses him and dedicates the silver to make a graven image and a molten image, which are placed in his house. Micah installs one of his sons as a priest and later hires a wandering Levite to be his private priest, believing the LORD will bless him because he has a Levite as priest.

segments.title: Micah Confesses Theft to Mother
segments.gist: Micah tells his mother he took her eleven hundred shekels of silver; she blesses him and dedicates the silver to the LORD for a graven image.

segments.title: Micah's House of Gods
segments.gist: Micah makes an ephod and teraphim, consecrates one of his sons as priest, and the text notes there was no king in Israel.

segments.title: Levite Seeks a Home
segments.gist: A young Levite from Bethlehem in Judah leaves the town to find a place to live and comes to Micah's house in Ephraim.

segments.title: Micah Hires the Levite
segments.gist: Micah asks the Levite where he is from; he answers Bethlehem, and Micah hires him as a father and priest for ten shekels and provisions.

segments.title: Levite Becomes Micah's Priest
segments.gist: The Levite agrees to stay, becomes like a son to Micah, and is ordained as priest; Micah expects the LORD to bless him for having a Levite as priest.

18.summary: The tribe of Dan, still without an inheritance, sends five spies who come to Micah's house and recognize the Levite priest there. They ask him to seek God's will, then continue to Laish, find it secure, and return with a report. A large Danite force later comes to Micah's house, takes his carved image and ephod, and persuades the priest to join them. They attack Laish, destroy it, and rename the city Dan, setting up the graven image with Jonathan's descendants as priests.

segments.title: Danites send spies
segments.gist: The Danites, lacking an inheritance, send five men to spy out the land; they lodge at Micah's house in Ephraim.

segments.title: Spies find Laish
segments.gist: The spies recognize the Levite priest, ask him to seek God's counsel, then go to Laish and report its secure and isolated state.

segments.title: Danite army sets out
segments.gist: Six hundred armed Danites journey from Zorah and Mahaneh-dan and camp near Micah's house.

segments.title: Theft of Micah's idols
segments.gist: The spies tell the armed men about Micah's idols; they enter the house, take the image and ephod, and persuade the priest to come with them.

segments.title: Micah pursues and rebuked
segments.gist: Micah and his neighbors chase the Danites, but the Danites warn him off, and Micah returns home.

segments.title: Danites destroy Laish
segments.gist: The Danites attack Laish, burn it, rebuild it as Dan, and set up the graven image with Jonathan's descendants as priests.

19.summary: A Levite from Ephraim takes a concubine from Bethlehem-judah who leaves him and returns to her father's house; he goes to bring her back and is warmly received by her father. On the journey home they stop at Gibeah of Benjamin, where no one offers hospitality except an old man; that night the men of the city surround the house and abuse the concubine to death. The Levite cuts her body into twelve pieces and sends them throughout Israel, demanding a response.

segments.title: Levite's concubine returns to father
segments.gist: A Levite's concubine leaves him for her father's house in Bethlehem-judah; after four months he travels to reconcile and is welcomed by her father.

segments.title: Journey and refusal at Gibeah
segments.gist: The Levite and his concubine leave Bethlehem, bypass Jebus, and arrive at Gibeah of Benjamin, where they sit in the street because no one offers lodging.

segments.title: Old man offers hospitality
segments.gist: An old man from Ephraim living in Gibeah invites the travelers into his house, washes their feet, and provides for them.

segments.title: Men of Gibeah abuse concubine
segments.gist: Men of the city surround the house and demand the Levite; he sends out his concubine, and they abuse her all night until she falls dead at the door.

segments.title: Levite divides body into twelve pieces
segments.gist: The Levite finds his concubine dead, carries her home, cuts her into twelve pieces, and sends them throughout Israel, prompting outrage and a call for action.

20.summary: The tribes of Israel gather at Mizpeh to punish the outrage at Gibeah, where a Levite's concubine was abused to death. After the Benjamites refuse to hand over the offenders, civil war erupts; Israel is twice defeated with heavy losses before a third battle in which they ambush and nearly annihilate Benjamin, leaving only 600 survivors.

segments.title: Israel assembles against Gibeah
segments.gist: The congregation gathers at Mizpeh, hears the Levite's account of the crime, and demands that Benjamin surrender the offenders.

segments.title: Benjamin refuses and musters
segments.gist: Benjamin rejects the demand and assembles 26,000 swordsmen, while Israel numbers 400,000, and the Benjamites are counted.

segments.title: Two defeats for Israel
segments.gist: Israel asks God who should attack first, is defeated twice by Benjamin with heavy losses, and weeps before the LORD.

segments.title: Third battle and ambush
segments.gist: After fasting and sacrifice, Israel sets an ambush and draws Benjamin away from Gibeah, then strikes the city and routs the Benjamites.

segments.title: Benjamin nearly destroyed
segments.gist: The ambush burns Gibeah, Benjamin is surrounded and cut down, and only 600 men escape to Rimmon while Israel devastates their cities.

21.summary: The men of Israel, having sworn not to give their daughters to Benjamin, mourn the near-extinction of the tribe and seek a way to provide wives for the surviving Benjamites. They discover that Jabesh-gilead did not join the assembly, so they destroy that city and give its virgin women to Benjamin. When these are not enough, they instruct the Benjamites to seize wives from the dancing daughters of Shiloh during the feast, and the survivors return to rebuild their towns.

segments.title: Israel Mourns Benjamin's Loss
segments.gist: The Israelites gather at Mizpeh and lament that one tribe is nearly wiped out, but they had sworn not to give their daughters to Benjamin.

segments.title: Inquiry About Missing Tribes
segments.gist: The assembly investigates which tribe failed to come to Mizpeh and finds that no one from Jabesh-gilead had attended.

segments.title: Jabesh-gilead Destroyed
segments.gist: Israel sends twelve thousand men to destroy Jabesh-gilead, killing all inhabitants except four hundred virgins, who are brought to the camp.

segments.title: Peace Offered to Benjamin
segments.gist: The congregation sends peace offerings to the Benjamites at Rimmon, but there are not enough women for all of them, and the people grieve.

segments.title: Plan to Seize Wives at Shiloh
segments.gist: The elders devise a plan for the remaining Benjamites to take wives from the dancing daughters of Shiloh during the feast, with the excuse that they did not give them willingly.

segments.title: Benjamites Rebuild and Return
segments.gist: The Benjamites seize wives from Shiloh, return to their inheritance, rebuild their cities, and the chapter closes noting that everyone did what was right in their own eyes.

1.summary: During a famine in Bethlehem, Elimelech and Naomi move to Moab with their sons, who marry Ruth and Orpah. After the men die, Naomi urges her daughters-in-law to return home; Orpah goes, but Ruth clings to Naomi and vows to stay with her and her God. Naomi and Ruth arrive in Bethlehem, where Naomi laments her bitterness and the town is stirred.

segments.title: Elimelech's family moves to Moab
segments.gist: Because of famine in Bethlehem, Elimelech takes Naomi and their sons to Moab, where the sons marry Ruth and Orpah.

segments.title: Naomi urges daughters-in-law to return
segments.gist: After her husband and sons die, Naomi tells Ruth and Orpah to go back to their mothers, but they weep and refuse to leave her.

segments.title: Ruth's vow to Naomi
segments.gist: Orpah departs, but Ruth clings to Naomi and pledges to stay with her, her people, and her God, sealing her vow.

segments.title: Naomi and Ruth arrive in Bethlehem
segments.gist: The women of Bethlehem greet Naomi, who calls herself Mara because of her bitterness, and Ruth the Moabitess stands with her.

2.summary: Ruth gleans in the fields of Boaz, a wealthy relative of Naomi's late husband. Boaz notices her, protects her, and instructs his workers to leave extra grain for her. Ruth returns home with abundant barley, and Naomi recognizes Boaz as a potential redeemer.

segments.title: Ruth asks to glean
segments.gist: Ruth asks Naomi to let her glean in the fields, and she happens to come to the field of Boaz.

segments.title: Boaz notices Ruth
segments.gist: Boaz arrives from Bethlehem, greets his reapers, and asks about the Moabite woman gleaning.

segments.title: Boaz protects Ruth
segments.gist: Boaz tells Ruth to stay in his field, offers her water, and explains he has heard of her kindness to Naomi.

segments.title: Boaz invites Ruth to eat
segments.gist: Boaz invites Ruth to eat with his workers and instructs his men to leave extra grain for her.

segments.title: Ruth returns with barley
segments.gist: Ruth gleans until evening, beats out about an ephah of barley, and returns to Naomi.

segments.title: Naomi blesses Boaz
segments.gist: Naomi blesses Boaz, explains his kinship, and urges Ruth to stay in his fields for safety.

3.summary: Naomi instructs Ruth to go to Boaz at the threshing floor at night, uncover his feet, and lie down, seeking his protection as kinsman-redeemer. Ruth obeys, and Boaz wakes to find her there; she asks him to spread his skirt over her, and he praises her kindness, promises to act as redeemer if the nearer kinsman declines, and sends her away before dawn with barley.

segments.title: Naomi's plan for Ruth
segments.gist: Naomi tells Ruth to wash, anoint herself, and go to Boaz at the threshing floor, then uncover his feet and lie down, promising to instruct her further.

segments.title: Ruth at the threshing floor
segments.gist: Ruth follows Naomi's instructions, goes to the threshing floor, and lies down at Boaz's feet; at midnight Boaz wakes and asks who she is.

segments.title: Boaz's promise as redeemer
segments.gist: Boaz blesses Ruth for her kindness, agrees to redeem her if the nearer kinsman will not, and tells her to stay until morning.

segments.title: Ruth returns with barley
segments.gist: Ruth leaves before dawn, Boaz gives her six measures of barley, and she returns to Naomi, who tells her to wait for Boaz to settle the matter.

4.summary: Boaz settles the legal matter of redeeming Naomi's land and marrying Ruth at the city gate, securing the kinsman's waiver and the elders' witness. He takes Ruth as his wife, and she bears a son, Obed, who becomes the grandfather of David.

segments.title: Boaz addresses the nearer kinsman
segments.gist: Boaz gathers the nearer kinsman and ten elders at the gate, offering him first right to redeem Naomi's land, which the man initially accepts.

segments.title: Kinsman renounces claim, Boaz redeems
segments.gist: The nearer kinsman declines to redeem lest he mar his inheritance, and Boaz declares before the elders that he has bought the land and taken Ruth as wife.

segments.title: Ruth bears Obed
segments.gist: Boaz marries Ruth, the LORD enables her conception, and she bears a son whom the women name Obed, calling him a restorer for Naomi.

segments.title: Genealogy from Perez to David
segments.gist: The chapter closes with the lineage of Perez down to David, listing Boaz, Obed, Jesse, and David.

1.summary: Elkanah, an Ephraimite with two wives, goes yearly to Shiloh to worship. His barren wife Hannah is provoked by Peninnah and weeps before the LORD, vowing to give a son to God's service. Eli first rebukes her, then blesses her, and Hannah bears Samuel, whom she brings to Shiloh after weaning and leaves with Eli.

segments.title: Elkanah's family and yearly worship
segments.gist: Elkanah, his wives Hannah and Peninnah, and their children go up yearly to Shiloh to worship and sacrifice to the LORD of hosts.

segments.title: Hannah's vow and Eli's blessing
segments.gist: Hannah weeps and vows to give a son to the LORD; Eli mistakes her for drunk, then blesses her after she explains her sorrow.

segments.title: Samuel's birth and weaning
segments.gist: Hannah bears a son and names him Samuel; she stays home until he is weaned, then prepares to go to Shiloh.

segments.title: Hannah gives Samuel to the LORD
segments.gist: Hannah brings Samuel and offerings to Shiloh, presents him to Eli, and declares that she has lent him to the LORD forever.

2.summary: Hannah's prayer exalts God as the one who humbles and exalts, while Eli's sons Hophni and Phinehas sin grievously at Shiloh and are judged by a man of God, and Samuel grows in favor with God and men.

segments.title: Hannah's prayer of praise
segments.gist: Hannah prays, rejoicing in God's holiness and power to reverse fortunes and exalt the humble.

segments.title: Eli's sons sin at Shiloh
segments.gist: Eli's sons take meat by force from worshippers and treat the Lord's offering with contempt.

segments.title: Samuel grows; Hannah's family blessed
segments.gist: Samuel ministers before the Lord, and Hannah is blessed with more children after dedicating Samuel.

segments.title: Eli rebukes his sons
segments.gist: Eli confronts his sons for their sins, but they refuse to listen, and Samuel grows in favor.

segments.title: Judgment on Eli's house
segments.gist: A man of God prophesies the downfall of Eli's priestly line and the rise of a faithful priest.

3.summary: While the boy Samuel serves under Eli at Shiloh, the LORD calls him three times at night; Samuel mistakes the voice for Eli until Eli teaches him to answer. God then tells Samuel of the coming judgment on Eli's house, and Samuel reluctantly reports it to Eli the next morning. The chapter closes with Samuel growing as a prophet and the LORD continuing to appear at Shiloh.

segments.title: Samuel ministers; the LORD calls
segments.gist: The boy Samuel serves before Eli, the word of the LORD is rare, and God calls Samuel, who answers and runs to Eli.

segments.title: Three calls and Eli's instruction
segments.gist: The LORD calls Samuel three times; each time Samuel goes to Eli, until Eli realizes God is calling and tells him how to respond.

segments.title: Judgment announced on Eli's house
segments.gist: The LORD tells Samuel he will bring judgment on Eli's house forever for the iniquity Eli knew about and did not restrain.

segments.title: Samuel tells Eli the vision
segments.gist: Samuel lies down until morning, then reluctantly tells Eli everything; Eli accepts it as from the LORD.

segments.title: Samuel established as prophet
segments.gist: Samuel grows, the LORD is with him, all Israel recognizes him as a prophet, and the LORD continues to appear at Shiloh.

4.summary: Israel goes to battle against the Philistines and, after a first defeat, brings the ark of the covenant from Shiloh to the camp. The Philistines rally, defeat Israel again, capture the ark, and kill Eli's sons Hophni and Phinehas. Eli dies upon hearing the news, and Phinehas's wife dies in childbirth, naming her son Ichabod because the glory has departed from Israel.

segments.title: Israel defeated by Philistines
segments.gist: Israel camps against the Philistines, is defeated in battle, and about four thousand men are killed.

segments.title: Elders send for the ark
segments.gist: The elders of Israel ask why the LORD allowed the defeat and decide to bring the ark from Shiloh to save them.

segments.title: Philistines fear and fight
segments.gist: The Philistines hear the shout at the ark's arrival, fear Israel's God, but rally and defeat Israel, killing thirty thousand.

segments.title: Ark captured, sons killed
segments.gist: The Philistines capture the ark of God, and Hophni and Phinehas, Eli's sons, are killed.

segments.title: Eli dies at news
segments.gist: A Benjamite runs to Shiloh; Eli, aged ninety-eight, hears of the ark's capture and falls backward, breaking his neck.

segments.title: Ichabod born, wife dies
segments.gist: Phinehas's wife dies after bearing a son, naming him Ichabod because the glory has departed from Israel.

5.summary: After capturing the ark of God, the Philistines bring it to Ashdod and set it in the temple of Dagon. The idol falls before the ark, and God's hand brings tumors and destruction on the people of Ashdod, Gath, and Ekron as the ark is moved from place to place.

segments.title: Ark in Dagon's Temple
segments.gist: The Philistines bring the captured ark to Ashdod and place it beside Dagon; the idol falls twice and is broken.

segments.title: Tumors Strike Ashdod
segments.gist: The hand of the Lord brings tumors on Ashdod and its territory, and the men decide to send the ark away.

segments.title: Ark Sent to Gath and Ekron
segments.gist: The ark is sent to Gath, where tumors break out, and then to Ekron, whose people cry out in fear.

segments.title: Ekron's Cry and Tumors
segments.gist: The Ekronites demand the ark be returned, and those who do not die are struck with tumors, and the cry of the city goes up to heaven.

6.summary: After seven months of affliction, the Philistines send the ark back to Israel on a new cart drawn by two milk cows, accompanied by a trespass offering of golden emerods and mice. The ark arrives at Beth-shemesh, where some men are struck down for looking into it, and the people ask who can stand before the LORD. They send messengers to Kiriath-jearim, and the ark is taken to the house of Abinadab, where it remains for twenty years.

segments.title: Philistines Consult Priests and Diviners
segments.gist: The Philistines ask their priests and diviners how to return the ark, and they advise sending it with a trespass offering of golden emerods and mice.

segments.title: Ark Sent on a New Cart
segments.gist: The Philistines place the ark on a new cart with the golden offerings and set two milk cows to draw it toward Beth-shemesh.

segments.title: Ark Arrives at Beth-shemesh
segments.gist: The people of Beth-shemesh reap wheat and rejoice at the ark's arrival; the cart stops by a great stone, and the Levites offer the cows as a burnt offering.

segments.title: Men of Beth-shemesh Struck Down
segments.gist: God strikes down some men of Beth-shemesh for looking into the ark, and the people mourn and ask who can stand before the LORD.

7.summary: The ark remains at Kirjath-jearim for twenty years, and Samuel calls Israel to repentance, putting away foreign gods. When the Philistines attack, Samuel sacrifices and God thunders against the enemy, and Israel routs them. Samuel sets up the Ebenezer stone, and the Philistines are subdued throughout his judgeship as he judges Israel at Mizpeh, Bethel, Gilgal, and Ramah.

segments.title: Ark at Kirjath-jearim; Samuel's Call
segments.gist: The ark stays at Kirjath-jearim twenty years; Samuel urges Israel to return to the LORD and put away foreign gods.

segments.title: Israel Gathers at Mizpeh
segments.gist: Samuel calls all Israel to Mizpeh, where they fast and confess their sin, and he judges them there.

segments.title: Philistines Defeated by Thunder
segments.gist: When the Philistines attack, Samuel sacrifices and cries out; God thunders, the Philistines are routed, and Israel pursues them.

segments.title: Ebenezer Stone and Philistine Subdued
segments.gist: Samuel sets up the Ebenezer stone, and the Philistines are subdued; cities are restored and there is peace with the Amorites.

segments.title: Samuel Judges Israel
segments.gist: Samuel judges Israel all his days, traveling yearly to Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpeh, and returning to Ramah where he builds an altar.

8.summary: When Samuel grows old, the elders of Israel demand a king to judge them like other nations. God tells Samuel that the people are rejecting Him, not Samuel, and instructs him to warn them of a king's rights. The people refuse to listen, and God tells Samuel to give them a king.

segments.title: Elders Demand a King
segments.gist: Samuel's sons are corrupt, so the elders of Israel ask Samuel to appoint a king to judge them.

segments.title: God Explains the Rejection
segments.gist: God tells Samuel the people have rejected Him as king, and instructs Samuel to warn them of a king's ways.

segments.title: Samuel Warns of a King's Rights
segments.gist: Samuel lists what a king will take from the people: sons, daughters, fields, servants, and flocks.

segments.title: People Refuse to Listen
segments.gist: The people insist on a king to be like other nations, and God tells Samuel to give them one.

9.summary: Saul, a tall young man from the tribe of Benjamin, is sent by his father Kish to find lost donkeys. After searching unsuccessfully, he seeks out the prophet Samuel for help. God had already revealed to Samuel that Saul would be the future ruler of Israel, and Samuel privately anoints him, then honors him at a feast and speaks with him on the roof.

segments.title: Saul Searches for Donkeys
segments.gist: Kish sends his son Saul with a servant to find lost donkeys, and they pass through several regions without success.

segments.title: Saul Seeks Samuel's Help
segments.gist: Saul proposes consulting a man of God in the nearby town, and the servant mentions they have a small gift to offer him.

segments.title: God Reveals Saul to Samuel
segments.gist: God had told Samuel the day before that the man to be anointed ruler would come, and when Saul arrives, Samuel invites him to the feast.

segments.title: Samuel Honors Saul at Feast
segments.gist: Samuel gives Saul the choicest portion at the feast and then speaks with him on the roof, preparing to reveal God's word.

10.summary: Samuel privately anoints Saul as captain over Israel and gives him signs to confirm it. Saul meets a band of prophets and prophesies, then is publicly chosen by lot at Mizpah, but some men doubt him.

segments.title: Samuel Anoints Saul
segments.gist: Samuel pours oil on Saul's head, declares him captain over Israel, and tells him to go to Gilgal and wait seven days.

segments.title: Signs Fulfilled and Prophesying
segments.gist: Saul receives a new heart, meets a company of prophets, prophesies, and his uncle questions him about Samuel's words.

segments.title: Saul Publicly Chosen by Lot
segments.gist: Samuel gathers Israel at Mizpah, Saul is chosen by lot and hailed as king, but some men despise him and bring no gifts.

11.summary: Nahash the Ammonite threatens to gouge out the right eyes of the men of Jabesh-gilead, but Saul rallies Israel's tribes and defeats the Ammonites. After the victory, Saul refuses to punish those who had opposed him, and Samuel leads the people to Gilgal to renew the kingdom and confirm Saul as king.

segments.title: Nahash Threatens Jabesh-gilead
segments.gist: Nahash the Ammonite besieges Jabesh-gilead and offers a treaty only on the condition of gouging out every right eye.

segments.title: Saul Rallies Israel
segments.gist: Saul hears the news, is moved by the Spirit, cuts up a yoke of oxen to summon Israel, and musters a large army.

segments.title: Ammonites Defeated
segments.gist: Saul's forces defeat the Ammonites in a morning attack, and the people of Jabesh-gilead are rescued.

segments.title: Saul Refuses Retribution
segments.gist: The people want to kill those who opposed Saul, but Saul forbids it, crediting the LORD with the victory.

segments.title: Kingdom Renewed at Gilgal
segments.gist: Samuel leads the people to Gilgal, where they renew the kingdom and rejoice with Saul as king.

12.summary: Samuel addresses Israel after Saul's confirmation as king, declaring his own integrity and recounting God's righteous acts from the Exodus to the present. He warns that obedience brings blessing but rebellion will bring judgment, and he calls on God to send thunder and rain as a sign. The people confess their sin in asking for a king, and Samuel reassures them, urging them to serve the Lord and promising to pray for them.

segments.title: Samuel Declares His Integrity
segments.gist: Samuel asks the people to testify if he has wronged anyone, and they affirm his innocence before the Lord and His anointed.

segments.title: Samuel Recounts God's Deliverances
segments.gist: Samuel reminds Israel of God's faithfulness from the Exodus through the judges, and how God delivered them from surrounding enemies.

segments.title: Warning About the King
segments.gist: Samuel warns that if the people and their king fear and obey the Lord, it will go well, but if they rebel, God's hand will be against them.

segments.title: Thunder and Rain as a Sign
segments.gist: Samuel calls on the Lord to send thunder and rain as a sign, and the people greatly fear the Lord and confess their sin of asking for a king.

segments.title: Samuel Reassures and Exhorts
segments.gist: Samuel tells the people not to fear but to serve the Lord wholeheartedly, promises to pray for them, and warns that rebellion will lead to destruction.

13.summary: Saul, now king, gathers Israel's army at Gilgal and waits seven days for Samuel, but when Samuel delays, Saul offers the burnt offering himself. Samuel arrives and rebukes Saul, declaring his kingdom will not continue because he disobeyed God's command. Meanwhile, the Philistines gather a massive army, and Israel is left with almost no weapons, forcing them to rely on God.

segments.title: Jonathan Smites Philistine Garrison
segments.gist: Jonathan attacks a Philistine garrison, and Saul summons Israel to Gilgal, where the Philistines gather a huge army.

segments.title: Israelites Hide in Fear
segments.gist: The Philistines assemble a vast force, and the Israelites, terrified, hide in caves and thickets, while some flee across the Jordan.

segments.title: Saul Offers Burnt Offering
segments.gist: Saul waits seven days for Samuel, but when Samuel does not come and the people scatter, Saul offers the burnt offering himself.

segments.title: Samuel Rebukes Saul's Disobedience
segments.gist: Samuel arrives and confronts Saul, who excuses his action; Samuel declares that Saul's kingdom will not continue because he disobeyed God's command.

segments.title: Philistines Raid Israel
segments.gist: Samuel leaves, and the Philistines send raiders in three directions to plunder Israel.

segments.title: Israel Lacks Weapons
segments.gist: No blacksmith exists in Israel, so the Israelites must go to the Philistines to sharpen their tools, leaving only Saul and Jonathan with weapons.

14.summary: Jonathan, with only his armor-bearer, attacks a Philistine garrison and sparks a rout when God sends an earthquake; Saul's rash oath forbids eating until evening, but Jonathan unknowingly eats honey, and after the people eat blood with meat, Saul builds an altar. Saul's pursuit ends when he consults God and receives no answer, the lot exposes Jonathan, and the people ransom him, so Saul's kingship is established over Israel's enemies.

segments.title: Jonathan attacks the Philistine garrison
segments.gist: Jonathan and his armor-bearer climb to a Philistine outpost, kill about twenty men, and God sends an earthquake that panics the Philistine camp.

segments.title: Saul's watchmen see the Philistines flee
segments.gist: Saul's watchmen report the Philistine army melting away, and the Hebrews who had hidden join the pursuit as the Philistines turn on each other.

segments.title: Saul's oath and Jonathan's honey
segments.gist: Saul binds the people with an oath not to eat until evening; Jonathan, unaware, eats honey and is refreshed, while the famished people later eat meat with blood, prompting Saul to build an altar.

segments.title: The lot falls on Jonathan
segments.gist: Saul proposes a night pursuit, but the priest urges consulting God; when God gives no answer, Saul casts lots, Jonathan is taken, and the people ransom him from death.

segments.title: Saul's victories and family
segments.gist: Saul fights Israel's enemies on every side and wins victories, and the chapter closes by listing his family and the commander of his army.

15.summary: Samuel tells Saul that God has rejected him as king because he disobeyed the command to destroy Amalek completely, sparing King Agag and the best of the livestock. After Saul's excuses and Samuel's pronouncement of judgment, Samuel executes Agag and departs, mourning for Saul.

segments.title: Saul Spares Agag and Best
segments.gist: Samuel delivers God's command to destroy Amalek utterly, but Saul defeats them while sparing Agag and the best animals.

segments.title: Saul's Excuse and Samuel's Rebuke
segments.gist: God regrets making Saul king; Saul claims he obeyed and blames the people, but Samuel declares obedience better than sacrifice and announces his rejection.

segments.title: Saul Confesses and Begs Honor
segments.gist: Saul admits his sin, asks forgiveness, and pleads with Samuel to return with him so he can worship and be honored before the elders.

segments.title: Samuel Executes Agag
segments.gist: Samuel brings Agag before the Lord, kills him at Gilgal, and then departs; he mourns for Saul, and God regrets making Saul king.

16.summary: God rejects Saul and sends Samuel to Bethlehem to anoint one of Jesse's sons. After seven older brothers are passed over, David, the youngest, is anointed and the Spirit of the LORD comes upon him. David then enters Saul's service as a harpist to soothe the king when an evil spirit troubles him.

segments.title: God sends Samuel to Bethlehem
segments.gist: God rebukes Samuel's grief for Saul and sends him to anoint a new king from Jesse's sons in Bethlehem.

segments.title: David anointed among his brothers
segments.gist: Jesse's seven older sons are rejected, and David, the youngest, is anointed; the Spirit of the LORD comes upon him.

segments.title: David plays harp for Saul
segments.gist: An evil spirit troubles Saul, and David is brought to play the harp, bringing him relief and favor with the king.

17.summary: The Philistine champion Goliath challenges Israel for forty days while Saul's army cowers. David, a shepherd boy bringing food to his brothers, hears the taunt, refuses Saul's armor, and fells Goliath with a slingstone, then cuts off his head with the giant's own sword. The Philistines flee, David is brought before Saul, and the chapter closes with Saul asking whose son he is.

segments.title: Goliath's Challenge
segments.gist: The Philistines gather for battle, and Goliath, a giant from Gath, shouts his challenge to Israel's army for forty days, terrifying Saul and the people.

segments.title: David Sent to Brothers
segments.gist: Jesse sends David to the camp with food; David hears Goliath's taunt, learns of the reward for killing him, and is rebuked by his brother Eliab.

segments.title: David Refuses Armor
segments.gist: David volunteers to fight Goliath, declines Saul's armor, and takes only his staff, sling, and five smooth stones from the brook.

segments.title: David Kills Goliath
segments.gist: David confronts Goliath in the name of the LORD, strikes him down with a stone, cuts off his head with the giant's sword, and the Philistines flee.

segments.title: Saul Questions David's Lineage
segments.gist: As David returns, Saul asks Abner whose son the youth is, and David answers that he is the son of Jesse the Bethlehemite.

18.summary: After David kills Goliath, Jonathan makes a covenant with him and Saul keeps him at court, but Saul's jealousy is inflamed when women's songs credit David with more kills than the king; Saul repeatedly tries to kill David, and David's growing success and Michal's love for him deepen Saul's fear.

segments.title: Jonathan's covenant with David
segments.gist: Jonathan loves David and makes a covenant with him, giving him his robe and armor; Saul keeps David and will not let him return home.

segments.title: Women's song provokes Saul's jealousy
segments.gist: Women sing that Saul slew thousands and David ten thousands, and Saul becomes angry and suspicious of David.

segments.title: Saul's attempts to kill David
segments.gist: Saul tries to pin David with a spear twice, fears him because the Lord is with David, and makes him a captain over a thousand.

segments.title: Michal offered as a snare
segments.gist: Saul offers his daughter Merab to David, then sets a bride price of a hundred Philistine foreskins, hoping David will fall by the Philistines.

segments.title: David marries Michal; Saul's fear grows
segments.gist: David fulfills the price, marries Michal, and Saul's fear and envy increase as David prospers and is honored.

19.summary: Saul openly seeks to kill David, but Jonathan intercedes and David escapes; when Saul's messengers come to David's house, Michal helps him flee through a window, and later Saul's messengers and Saul himself prophesy when they come to Ramah where David is with Samuel.

segments.title: Jonathan intercedes for David
segments.gist: Saul tells Jonathan he wants David dead; Jonathan warns David and speaks well of him to Saul, who vows not to kill him.

segments.title: Saul tries to kill David
segments.gist: War breaks out again, David defeats the Philistines, and an evil spirit leads Saul to try to pin David to the wall with a spear, but David escapes.

segments.title: Michal helps David escape
segments.gist: Saul sends men to watch David's house; Michal lets David down through a window and deceives the messengers with an image in the bed.

segments.title: Saul prophesies at Ramah
segments.gist: David flees to Samuel at Ramah; Saul sends messengers who prophesy, and Saul himself goes and prophesies naked before Samuel.

20.summary: David flees Saul's court and seeks help from Jonathan, who does not yet know his father means to kill David. The two make a covenant, devise a sign with arrows to reveal Saul's intent, and when Saul's rage is confirmed, Jonathan sends David away in peace while the friends weep together.

segments.title: David and Jonathan's covenant
segments.gist: David flees to Jonathan, protests his innocence, and the two renew their covenant before the LORD.

segments.title: Plan with arrows
segments.gist: Jonathan devises a sign with arrows to tell David whether Saul is hostile, and appeals to David's kindness.

segments.title: Saul's rage at the feast
segments.gist: At the new moon feast Saul notices David's absence, learns of his excuse, and in fury tries to kill Jonathan.

segments.title: Arrows and farewell
segments.gist: Jonathan shoots the arrows as a sign, sends the boy away, and he and David weep and part in peace.

21.summary: David flees from Saul and comes to Nob, where Ahimelech the priest gives him the showbread and the sword of Goliath. He then flees to Gath, but when the Philistines recognize him, he feigns madness to escape.

segments.title: David at Nob
segments.gist: David comes to Ahimelech at Nob, receives the holy bread and Goliath's sword, and learns of Doeg the Edomite's presence.

segments.title: David feigns madness in Gath
segments.gist: David flees to Gath, is recognized as the slayer of Goliath, and pretends to be insane to escape the Philistines.

22.summary: David flees to the cave of Adullam, where his family and about four hundred distressed men join him; he sends his parents to safety in Moab. Saul, at Gibeah, accuses his servants of conspiracy and is told by Doeg the Edomite that Ahimelech the priest helped David. Saul summons Ahimelech and the priests of Nob, condemns them, and has Doeg kill eighty-five priests and destroy the city of Nob; Abiathar escapes and joins David.

segments.title: David at Adullam and Mizpeh
segments.gist: David escapes to the cave of Adullam, gathers his family and about four hundred men, then leaves his parents with the king of Moab.

segments.title: Saul Accuses His Servants
segments.gist: Saul complains to his servants at Gibeah that they have conspired against him and not revealed Jonathan's covenant with David.

segments.title: Doeg Reports Ahimelech's Help
segments.gist: Doeg the Edomite tells Saul that he saw Ahimelech give David provisions and the sword of Goliath.

segments.title: Saul Condemns Ahimelech
segments.gist: Saul summons Ahimelech and the priests of Nob, accuses them of conspiracy, and orders their death, but his guards refuse.

segments.title: Doeg Kills the Priests
segments.gist: Saul orders Doeg to kill the priests; Doeg kills eighty-five priests and then strikes Nob, destroying men, women, children, and animals.

segments.title: Abiathar Escapes to David
segments.gist: Abiathar, son of Ahimelech, escapes and flees to David, who assures him of protection.

23.summary: David rescues the town of Keilah from the Philistines, then flees from Saul's pursuit, moving through the wilderness of Ziph and Maon. Jonathan meets David and strengthens his faith, while the Ziphites betray David's location to Saul. Saul closes in but is forced to withdraw when the Philistines invade, and David escapes to En-gedi.

segments.title: David Rescues Keilah
segments.gist: David inquires of the LORD, then defeats the Philistines and saves the inhabitants of Keilah.

segments.title: David Flees from Keilah
segments.gist: God reveals that Keilah will surrender David to Saul, so David and his men depart.

segments.title: Jonathan Strengthens David
segments.gist: Jonathan meets David in the wilderness and makes a covenant with him, affirming he will be king.

segments.title: Ziphites Betray David
segments.gist: The Ziphites tell Saul where David is hiding, and Saul thanks them and plans to capture David.

segments.title: Saul Pursues, Philistines Attack
segments.gist: Saul closes in on David, but a Philistine invasion forces him to withdraw, and David escapes to En-gedi.

24.summary: After Saul pursues David into the wilderness of Engedi, David has a chance to kill him in a cave but refuses, cutting off a piece of Saul's robe instead. David confronts Saul from a distance, declaring his innocence, and Saul acknowledges David's righteousness, asking for mercy for his descendants before they part.

segments.title: David Spares Saul in the Cave
segments.gist: Saul enters a cave to relieve himself, and David, though urged by his men, refuses to kill him, only cutting off the skirt of his robe.

segments.title: David Confronts Saul
segments.gist: David calls out to Saul, bows before him, and argues his innocence, showing the cut robe as proof he could have killed him but did not.

segments.title: Saul Acknowledges David's Righteousness
segments.gist: Saul weeps, admits David is more righteous, asks the Lord to reward David, and makes David swear he will not destroy his descendants.

25.summary: After Samuel dies, David sends men to ask Nabal of Carmel for provisions, but Nabal insults them. David prepares to attack Nabal, but Nabal's wife Abigail intervenes with gifts and a persuasive speech, and David relents. Abigail tells Nabal, who dies ten days later, and David marries her, while Michal is given to another man.

segments.title: Samuel's death and David in Paran
segments.gist: Samuel dies and is buried; David moves to the wilderness of Paran.

segments.title: Nabal refuses David's request
segments.gist: David sends men to Nabal for provisions, but Nabal insults them and refuses.

segments.title: Abigail intercedes with gifts
segments.gist: Abigail brings gifts to David and persuades him not to take vengeance on Nabal.

segments.title: Nabal dies after Abigail's report
segments.gist: Abigail tells Nabal what happened; he becomes ill and dies ten days later.

segments.title: David marries Abigail and Ahinoam
segments.gist: David marries Abigail and Ahinoam, while Michal is given to Phalti.

26.summary: David again spares Saul's life, this time in the wilderness of Ziph, taking Saul's spear and cruse of water while he sleeps. From a distance David rebukes Abner and Saul, and Saul acknowledges his fault and blesses David, and they part.

segments.title: Ziphites betray David to Saul
segments.gist: The Ziphites tell Saul where David is hiding, and Saul brings three thousand men to seek him.

segments.title: David and Abishai enter Saul's camp
segments.gist: David and Abishai go by night to Saul's sleeping camp; Abishai offers to kill Saul, but David refuses to touch the LORD's anointed.

segments.title: David calls to Abner from the hill
segments.gist: David shouts from a distant hill, rebuking Abner for failing to guard the king, and shows the spear and cruse he took.

segments.title: Saul recognizes David's voice
segments.gist: Saul recognizes David's voice; David questions why Saul pursues him and appeals to the LORD's judgment.

segments.title: Saul confesses and departs
segments.gist: Saul admits he has sinned and blesses David; David returns the spear, and they part ways.

27.summary: David, fearing Saul will eventually kill him, flees to the Philistine city of Gath and serves King Achish. He and his men raid Israel's southern neighbors while telling Achish he has attacked Judah, and Achish comes to trust David completely.

segments.title: David flees to Achish in Gath
segments.gist: David despairs of escaping Saul and takes his 600 men to Gath, where Achish receives him and he dwells in Ziklag.

segments.title: David requests and receives Ziklag
segments.gist: David asks Achish for a separate town and is given Ziklag, which remains a Judean possession.

segments.title: David raids southern tribes and deceives Achish
segments.gist: David raids the Geshurites, Gezrites, and Amalekites, kills all inhabitants, and tells Achish he attacked Judah, so Achish trusts him.

28.summary: With the Philistines gathering for battle, Saul, terrified and unable to get an answer from God, seeks out a medium at Endor despite his own ban on such practices. Disguised, he asks her to bring up Samuel, who announces that Saul and his sons will die and the kingdom will go to David. Saul collapses in fear, and the woman gives him food before he returns to his camp.

segments.title: Philistines gather; Saul fears
segments.gist: The Philistines assemble at Shunem, and Saul, seeing their army, is terrified and inquires of the LORD but receives no answer.

segments.title: Saul seeks medium at Endor
segments.gist: Saul disguises himself and asks a woman at Endor to bring up Samuel, and she sees a spirit rising and cries out.

segments.title: Samuel announces Saul's doom
segments.gist: Samuel tells Saul that the LORD has departed from him, that the kingdom is given to David, and that Saul and his sons will die in battle.

segments.title: Saul collapses; woman feeds him
segments.gist: Saul falls to the ground in fear, and the woman and his servants persuade him to eat, after which he returns to his camp.

29.summary: The Philistines gather their armies at Aphek while David and his men march with Achish in the rear. When the Philistine lords object to David's presence, Achish defends him but sends him back to Ziklag, and David and his men depart early in the morning.

segments.title: Philistines gather at Aphek
segments.gist: The Philistines assemble their forces at Aphek, and David and his men march in the rear with Achish.

segments.title: Philistine lords object to David
segments.gist: The Philistine commanders question why the Hebrews are present and demand that David not go into battle with them.

segments.title: Achish defends David's loyalty
segments.gist: Achish tells David he is as good as an angel of God, but the lords have rejected him.

segments.title: David sent back to Ziklag
segments.gist: David protests, but Achish orders him to return early in the morning with his men.

30.summary: While David and his men are away, the Amalekites raid Ziklag, burn it, and carry off the women and children. David seeks God's direction, pursues the raiders, and recovers all that was taken, then divides the spoil among his men and sends gifts to the elders of Judah.

segments.title: Amalekites Burn Ziklag
segments.gist: The Amalekites attack Ziklag, burn it, and take captive the women and children while David and his men are away.

segments.title: David Inquires of the Lord
segments.gist: David and his men weep, then David seeks God's guidance through Abiathar and is told to pursue the raiders.

segments.title: David Defeats the Amalekites
segments.gist: David and his men attack the celebrating Amalekites, defeat them, and recover all the captives and spoil.

segments.title: Spoil Shared with the Weary
segments.gist: David rejects the demand that only the fighters receive spoil and establishes that the spoil is shared equally with those who stayed behind.

segments.title: Gifts Sent to Judah
segments.gist: David sends portions of the spoil to the elders of Judah and to various towns, strengthening his ties with them.

31.summary: The Philistines fight Israel on Mount Gilboa, killing Saul's sons and wounding Saul, who falls on his own sword to avoid capture; the Philistines find his body, behead it, and fasten it to the wall of Bethshan, while Jabeshgilead men retrieve and bury the bones.

segments.title: Philistines defeat Israel and kill Saul's sons
segments.gist: The Philistines fight Israel at Gilboa, killing Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchi-shua, and wounding Saul, who asks his armor-bearer to kill him.

segments.title: Philistines desecrate Saul's body
segments.gist: The Philistines find Saul's body, strip it, behead it, and fasten it to the wall of Bethshan after sending word to their idols.

segments.title: Jabeshgilead men retrieve and bury the bones
segments.gist: Men of Jabeshgilead retrieve the bodies, burn them, bury the bones under a tree, and fasten a seven-day fast.

1.summary: A messenger from Saul's camp arrives to tell David of the deaths of Saul and Jonathan, and David and his men mourn. David then orders the execution of the Amalekite who claimed to have killed Saul, and he sings a lament for Saul and Jonathan.

segments.title: Messenger reports Saul's death
segments.gist: An Amalekite brings news of Israel's defeat and Saul's death, claiming he killed Saul at his request.

segments.title: David's lament for Saul and Jonathan
segments.gist: David sings a song of mourning for Saul and Jonathan, praising their valor and grieving Jonathan's love.

2.summary: David, after mourning Saul's death, goes up to Hebron and is anointed king over Judah. Meanwhile Abner makes Saul's son Ishbosheth king over Israel, and the two sides clash at Gibeon, where Abner's men are defeated and Asahel is killed.

segments.title: David anointed king in Hebron
segments.gist: David inquires of the LORD, goes to Hebron with his household, and is anointed king over Judah.

segments.title: Ishbosheth made king over Israel
segments.gist: Abner takes Saul's son Ishbosheth and makes him king over Israel, except Judah.

segments.title: Battle at Gibeon
segments.gist: Abner's men and Joab's men meet at Gibeon; after a contest, a fierce battle ensues and Abner's men are defeated.

segments.title: Asahel killed by Abner
segments.gist: Asahel pursues Abner; Abner warns him, then strikes him with the butt of his spear, and Asahel dies.

segments.title: Joab calls off pursuit
segments.gist: Joab and Abishai pursue Abner; Abner appeals to Joab, who sounds the trumpet and stops the pursuit; Asahel is buried, and David's men return to Hebron.

3.summary: During the long war between David's house and Saul's house, Abner, Saul's commander, quarrels with Ish-bosheth and turns to make a covenant with David, sending Michal back to him. Joab and Abishai, seeking revenge for their brother Asahel, murder Abner at Hebron, and David mourns him publicly, distancing himself from the killing.

segments.title: War and Sons Born at Hebron
segments.gist: The war between David and Ish-bosheth drags on, and David's sons born at Hebron are listed.

segments.title: Abner Quarrels with Ish-bosheth
segments.gist: Abner is accused of taking Saul's concubine and angrily threatens to transfer the kingdom to David.

segments.title: Abner's Covenant and Michal's Return
segments.gist: Abner agrees to gather Israel for David, and David demands that Michal be brought back from Paltiel.

segments.title: Abner Persuades Israel and Benjamin
segments.gist: Abner speaks to Israel's elders and Benjamin, then reports to David that he has won them over.

segments.title: Joab Murders Abner
segments.gist: Joab rebukes David, sends messengers after Abner, and kills him at Hebron to avenge Asahel.

segments.title: David Mourns Abner
segments.gist: David commands a public mourning, follows the bier, and laments Abner, and the people are pleased with the king.

4.summary: After Abner's death, two of Saul's captains, Baanah and Rechab, murder Saul's son Ishbosheth in his bed and bring his head to David at Hebron, expecting a reward. David condemns the murder, reminding them he did not spare the man who claimed to kill Saul, and orders their execution; the head of Ishbosheth is buried in Abner's tomb.

segments.title: Ishbosheth's captains plot murder
segments.gist: Saul's son Ishbosheth loses courage when he hears Abner is dead, and two of his captains, Baanah and Rechab, plan to kill him.

segments.title: Ishbosheth murdered in his bed
segments.gist: Baanah and Rechab enter Ishbosheth's house at noon, stab him as he lies on his bed, and cut off his head, escaping by way of the plain.

segments.title: David orders the murderers executed
segments.gist: David swears he did not spare the man who claimed to kill Saul, so he condemns Baanah and Rechab, has them killed and their hands and feet cut off, and buries Ishbosheth's head in Abner's tomb.

5.summary: All the tribes of Israel come to David at Hebron and anoint him king over the united nation. David then captures Jerusalem from the Jebusites and makes it his capital, building up the city with Hiram's help and taking more wives and children. When the Philistines hear of his anointing, they attack, but David defeats them twice after inquiring of the LORD.

segments.title: Israel Anoints David King
segments.gist: Representatives of all Israel come to Hebron, recall David's past leadership, and anoint him king over a united Israel.

segments.title: David Captures Jerusalem
segments.gist: David takes the stronghold of Zion from the Jebusites, makes it his city, and builds around it with help from Hiram.

segments.title: David's Family Grows in Jerusalem
segments.gist: David takes more wives and concubines in Jerusalem and has many sons and daughters born to him there.

segments.title: David Defeats the Philistines Twice
segments.gist: The Philistines attack, and David, after asking God, defeats them at Baalperazim and again at the mulberry trees.
