6.summary: David brings the ark of God from Baale of Judah to Jerusalem with great celebration, but Uzzah is struck dead for touching the ark, which halts the procession and angers David. After the ark rests three months at Obed-edom's house, David successfully transports it to Jerusalem with sacrifices and dancing, and Michal despises him from a window, leading to her barrenness.

segments.title: David fetches the ark
segments.gist: David gathers chosen men and brings the ark from Baale of Judah on a new cart, with rejoicing.

segments.title: Uzzah struck dead
segments.gist: Uzzah touches the ark to steady it and God strikes him dead; David is displeased and fears the Lord.

segments.title: Ark brought to Jerusalem
segments.gist: David brings the ark to Jerusalem with sacrifices and dancing before the Lord.

segments.title: Michal despises David
segments.gist: Michal sees David dancing and despises him; David blesses the people and gives them food.

segments.title: Michal rebukes David
segments.gist: Michal criticizes David's dancing; David defends his humility before the Lord, and Michal remains childless.

7.summary: David, settled in his palace, tells Nathan the prophet he wants to build a house for the ark, and Nathan first approves. That night God speaks to Nathan, refusing David's offer and instead promising to establish David's dynasty forever. David responds with a long prayer of humility and praise, accepting God's covenant.

segments.title: David proposes building a temple
segments.gist: David tells Nathan he lives in a cedar house while the ark remains in a tent, and Nathan initially encourages him.

segments.title: God refuses a house
segments.gist: God's word to Nathan recalls that he has never asked for a cedar house and has moved with Israel in a tent.

segments.title: God's covenant with David
segments.gist: God promises to make David's name great, give Israel rest, and establish David's throne and kingdom forever through his offspring.

segments.title: David's prayer of praise
segments.gist: David sits before the Lord, marvels at God's promises, exalts God's uniqueness, and asks God to confirm the covenant forever.

8.summary: 2 Samuel 8 recounts David's military victories over the Philistines, Moabites, Zobah, Syria, and Edom, and the spoils he dedicates to the LORD. It also records his administrative officials and his justice and equity over Israel.

segments.title: David's victories and spoils
segments.gist: David defeats Philistines, Moabites, and Hadadezer, taking spoils and garrisons.

segments.title: Spoils dedicated to the LORD
segments.gist: David dedicates silver, gold, and brass from conquered nations to the LORD.

segments.title: Edom subdued and garrisons
segments.gist: David gains renown by defeating Edom and placing garrisons throughout the land.

segments.title: David's officials
segments.gist: David reigns with justice; Joab, Jehoshaphat, Zadok, Ahimelech, Seraiah, and Benaiah serve in key roles.

9.summary: David, remembering his covenant with Jonathan, seeks out any surviving descendant of Saul to show kindness for Jonathan's sake. He finds Mephibosheth, Jonathan's lame son, restores to him all of Saul's family land, and invites him to eat at the king's table permanently.

segments.title: David seeks Saul's remnant
segments.gist: David asks if any of Saul's house remain so he can show kindness for Jonathan's sake, and Ziba is brought to him.

segments.title: Mephibosheth brought before David
segments.gist: Mephibosheth, Jonathan's lame son, comes to David and bows, and David reassures him not to fear.

segments.title: Restoration and place at table
segments.gist: David restores Saul's land to Mephibosheth, assigns Ziba and his household to serve him, and decrees that Mephibosheth will eat at the king's table continually.

10.summary: King Nahash of the Ammonites dies, and David sends envoys to comfort his son Hanun, but the Ammonite princes suspect them of spying, so Hanun humiliates the envoys and hires Syrian mercenaries. David's army under Joab defeats the Ammonites and Syrians in two campaigns, and the Syrians make peace with Israel.

segments.title: David's envoys humiliated
segments.gist: Nahash dies; David sends comforters to Hanun, but the Ammonite princes suspect them and Hanun shaves and disfigures them.

segments.title: Ammonites hire Syrians
segments.gist: The Ammonites hire thousands of Syrian mercenaries from Bethrehob, Zoba, Maacah, and Tob to fight Israel.

segments.title: Joab defeats Ammonites and Syrians
segments.gist: Joab divides his army, encourages Abishai, and routs the Syrians and Ammonites, who flee to their cities.

segments.title: Syrians regroup and are defeated
segments.gist: The Syrians gather under Hadarezer, but David defeats them, killing many and making peace with the remaining Syrian kings.

11.summary: While his army besieges Rabbah, David stays in Jerusalem and commits adultery with Bathsheba, Uriah's wife. After she conceives, David recalls Uriah from the front, but Uriah refuses to go home to his wife; David then arranges his death in battle. Uriah is killed, David marries Bathsheba, and the chapter ends noting the Lord's displeasure.

segments.title: David and Bathsheba
segments.gist: David remains in Jerusalem, sees Bathsheba bathing, sends for her, and lies with her; she later tells him she is pregnant.

segments.title: Uriah refuses to go home
segments.gist: David recalls Uriah and tries twice to get him to go home to his wife, but Uriah refuses to enjoy comfort while the ark and army are in tents.

segments.title: David arranges Uriah's death
segments.gist: David sends a letter to Joab ordering Uriah placed in the front line to be killed; Joab complies, Uriah dies, and David sends word that the battle continues.

segments.title: David marries Bathsheba
segments.gist: Bathsheba mourns Uriah, then David takes her as his wife; she bears a son, but the Lord is displeased.

12.summary: Nathan confronts David with a parable of a rich man who took a poor man's lamb, and David condemns himself; Nathan declares God's judgment—the child will die and the sword will not depart from David's house. David repents, the child dies despite his fasting, and Solomon is born. Joab besieges Rabbah and calls David to complete the victory, after which David takes the Ammonite crown and imposes hard labor on the people.

segments.title: Nathan's Parable of the Lamb
segments.gist: Nathan tells David about a rich man who took a poor man's only lamb to feed a guest, and David angrily demands the rich man's death.

segments.title: Nathan Declares God's Judgment
segments.gist: Nathan identifies David as the man and announces that the sword will never leave his house and that his wives will be taken by another.

segments.title: David Repents and Child Stricken
segments.gist: David confesses his sin, Nathan assures him of forgiveness, but the child born to Bathsheba is struck with illness.

segments.title: David Fasts and Child Dies
segments.gist: David fasts and prays for the child; when the child dies, he rises, worships, and explains that he cannot bring the child back.

segments.title: Solomon Born and Loved
segments.gist: Bathsheba bears a son named Solomon, whom the Lord loves, and Nathan calls him Jedidiah.

segments.title: Rabbah Captured and Ammonites Subdued
segments.gist: Joab captures Rabbah's water supply and calls David to finish the siege; David takes the crown and sets the Ammonites to hard labor.

13.summary: Amnon, son of David, becomes infatuated with his half-sister Tamar and, on his cousin Jonadab's advice, lures her to his chambers and rapes her. Tamar's brother Absalom takes her in, harbors hatred for Amnon, and two years later has him killed at a sheep-shearing feast; Absalom then flees to Geshur, while David mourns.

segments.title: Amnon's obsession with Tamar
segments.gist: Amnon, David's son, loves his half-sister Tamar and, advised by Jonadab, feigns illness to request her care.

segments.title: Amnon rapes Tamar
segments.gist: Tamar comes to Amnon's chamber, and despite her pleas, he overpowers and violates her.

segments.title: Tamar sent away in shame
segments.gist: Amnon hates Tamar, orders her out, and she leaves in mourning with ashes and torn garments.

segments.title: Absalom shelters Tamar
segments.gist: Absalom takes Tamar into his house and harbors hatred for Amnon, while David is angry.

segments.title: Absalom plots Amnon's death
segments.gist: At a sheep-shearing feast, Absalom orders his servants to kill Amnon, and they do.

segments.title: Absalom flees to Geshur
segments.gist: David mourns the reported death of all his sons, but Jonadab clarifies only Amnon is dead; Absalom flees to Geshur for three years.

14.summary: Joab sends a wise woman from Tekoa to King David with a parable urging him to bring Absalom back from exile. David relents and allows Absalom to return to Jerusalem, though he refuses to see him for two years. Absalom eventually forces a meeting with Joab and is reconciled to the king, but the chapter closes with hints of his growing ambition.

segments.title: Joab's Plan with the Woman
segments.gist: Joab, knowing David's heart longs for Absalom, sends for a wise woman from Tekoa and instructs her to present a feigned case to the king.

segments.title: The Woman's Parable
segments.gist: The woman tells David a story of two sons, one killed and the other threatened by avengers, pleading that the king protect her remaining son.

segments.title: Woman Applies Parable to Absalom
segments.gist: The woman reveals the parable's intent, urging David to bring Absalom back, and David perceives Joab's hand in her words.

segments.title: David Permits Absalom's Return
segments.gist: David grants Joab's request to bring Absalom back, but orders that Absalom live apart and not see the king's face.

segments.title: Absalom's Appearance and Children
segments.gist: Absalom is described as exceptionally handsome with long hair, and he has three sons and a daughter named Tamar.

segments.title: Absalom Reconciled to David
segments.gist: After two years, Absalom summons Joab to intercede, and David finally kisses Absalom, restoring him to favor.

15.summary: Absalom conspires to win the hearts of Israel, gains permission to go to Hebron, and there launches a rebellion against David with Ahithophel's support. David flees Jerusalem with his household, sends the ark back, and crosses the Kidron, while he arranges for Hushai to return and counter Ahithophel's counsel.

segments.title: Absalom steals Israel's hearts
segments.gist: Absalom stations himself by the gate, greets suppliants, and tells them the king ignores their cases, implying he would judge rightly.

segments.title: Absalom's conspiracy at Hebron
segments.gist: After four years Absalom asks to go to Hebron to pay a vow; from there he sends spies and gathers a growing conspiracy, with Ahithophel among the conspirators.

segments.title: David flees Jerusalem
segments.gist: A messenger reports Israel's hearts are with Absalom; David orders his household to flee, leaving ten concubines, and crosses the Kidron with his servants and six hundred Gittites.

segments.title: Ittai pledges loyalty
segments.gist: David urges Ittai the Gittite to return, but Ittai swears to stay with the king, and David lets him pass with his men and little ones.

segments.title: Ark sent back to Jerusalem
segments.gist: Zadok and Abiathar bring the ark; David tells them to return it, expresses hope in God's will, and sends them back as informants while he camps in the wilderness.

segments.title: Hushai sent to counter Ahithophel
segments.gist: David weeps on the Mount of Olives; he sends Hushai the Archite back to Jerusalem to feign allegiance to Absalom and to thwart Ahithophel's counsel.

16.summary: Ziba meets David with provisions and falsely claims Mephibosheth has betrayed him, so David grants Ziba Mephibosheth's land. Shimei curses and stones David and his men, and David restrains Abishai from killing him. Absalom enters Jerusalem with Ahithophel and, on Ahithophel's advice, publicly takes his father's concubines to secure the claim to the throne.

segments.title: Ziba brings provisions to David
segments.gist: Ziba meets David with donkeys, food, and wine, and falsely claims Mephibosheth has stayed in Jerusalem hoping to reclaim the kingdom.

segments.title: Shimei curses and stones David
segments.gist: Shimei curses David as a usurper and throws stones, and David stops Abishai from killing him, accepting the curse as from God.

segments.title: Absalom and Hushai enter Jerusalem
segments.gist: Absalom arrives in Jerusalem with Ahithophel, and Hushai the Archite comes to him claiming loyalty, though Absalom questions his timing.

segments.title: Ahithophel advises public concubines
segments.gist: Ahithophel advises Absalom to take his father's concubines publicly, and Absalom follows the counsel, which is highly regarded.

17.summary: Absalom follows Ahithophel's counsel to pursue David, but Hushai's counter-advice prevails, giving David time to escape. Ahithophel, seeing his plan rejected, goes home and hangs himself. David crosses the Jordan and is provisioned by loyal supporters, while Absalom's army gathers under Amasa.

segments.title: Ahithophel's counsel to pursue
segments.gist: Ahithophel advises Absalom to let him take twelve thousand men and attack David that night.

segments.title: Hushai's counter-advice prevails
segments.gist: Hushai argues against Ahithophel's plan and proposes a massive nationwide pursuit; Absalom and the elders prefer Hushai's counsel.

segments.title: Hushai warns David to flee
segments.gist: Hushai sends word to David through the priests' sons, who escape and warn David to cross the Jordan quickly.

segments.title: Absalom crosses Jordan with army
segments.gist: Absalom and the Israelites cross the Jordan, with Amasa commanding the army in place of Joab.

segments.title: David provisioned at Mahanaim
segments.gist: Shobi, Machir, and Barzillai bring bedding, food, and supplies for David and his people at Mahanaim.

18.summary: David's forces defeat Absalom's army in the wood of Ephraim, where Absalom is caught in an oak and killed by Joab despite David's orders to spare him. Ahimaaz and Cushi bring news to David, who mourns deeply for his son.

segments.title: David reviews and divides his army
segments.gist: David numbers the people, divides them into three companies under Joab, Abishai, and Ittai, and is persuaded not to go to battle himself.

segments.title: Absalom's army defeated in the wood
segments.gist: The battle spreads through the wood of Ephraim, where David's men defeat Absalom's forces with great slaughter.

segments.title: Absalom caught and killed by Joab
segments.gist: Absalom is caught by his hair in an oak, and Joab, ignoring David's command, strikes him with darts and has him buried in a pit.

segments.title: Ahimaaz and Cushi run to David
segments.gist: Ahimaaz and Cushi race to bring news to David; Ahimaaz arrives first but only reports the victory, while Cushi tells of Absalom's death.

segments.title: David mourns for Absalom
segments.gist: David hears the news, realizes Absalom is dead, and is deeply grieved, crying out in mourning for his son.

19.summary: 2 Samuel 19 describes the aftermath of Absalom's defeat: David mourns deeply, Joab rebukes him and forces him to show himself to the people, and David is restored as king. The chapter then recounts the chaotic return across the Jordan, with Shimei begging forgiveness, Mephibosheth explaining his absence, and Barzillai being honored, while a dispute arises between Israel and Judah over who should escort the king.

segments.title: Joab Rebukes David's Mourning
segments.gist: David's grief over Absalom turns victory into mourning; Joab warns that the people feel shamed and urges David to speak kindly to them.

segments.title: Israel and Judah Debate Return
segments.gist: The tribes argue about bringing David back; David sends Zadok and Abiathar to prompt Judah, and Amasa is promised command to secure Judah's loyalty.

segments.title: Shimei Pardoned by David
segments.gist: Shimei, who cursed David, hurries to meet him with a thousand Benjamites and begs forgiveness; David swears he will not be put to death.

segments.title: Mephibosheth Explains His Absence
segments.gist: Mephibosheth, unkempt since David fled, explains that Ziba deceived him; David divides the land between them, and Mephibosheth asks only for the king's safe return.

segments.title: Barzillai's Kindness and Farewell
segments.gist: Barzillai, who supplied David at Mahanaim, declines to go to Jerusalem due to age; David kisses him, blesses him, and takes Chimham instead.

segments.title: Tribal Quarrel over the King
segments.gist: The men of Israel confront Judah for escorting David privately, and Judah's harsh reply sparks a dispute over their claim to the king.

20.summary: Sheba son of Bichri leads a revolt against David, drawing the men of Israel away while Judah stays with the king. David orders Amasa to muster Judah but Amasa delays, so Abishai pursues Sheba; Joab kills Amasa and besieges Sheba in Abel-beth-maachah, where a wise woman arranges Sheba's death and the city is spared.

segments.title: Sheba's Rebellion
segments.gist: Sheba son of Bichri blows a trumpet and calls Israel to abandon David, and the men of Israel follow him.

segments.title: David's Orders and Amasa's Delay
segments.gist: David returns to Jerusalem, confines his concubines, and orders Amasa to muster Judah within three days, but Amasa delays.

segments.title: Joab Kills Amasa
segments.gist: Joab intercepts Amasa at Gibeon, kills him with a hidden sword, and leaves his body in the road until it is moved aside.

segments.title: Siege of Abel and Sheba's Death
segments.gist: Joab besieges Abel-beth-maachah, and a wise woman persuades the city to cut off Sheba's head and throw it to Joab, ending the siege.

segments.title: David's Officials
segments.gist: A list of David's chief officials: Joab over the army, Benaiah over the Cherethites and Pelethites, and Adoram over tribute.

21.summary: A three-year famine leads David to hand over seven of Saul's descendants to the Gibeonites, who execute them; Rizpah's vigil moves David to bury the bones with Saul and Jonathan. Later, battles against Philistine giants are recounted, including Abishai's rescue of David and the kills by Sibbechai, Elhanan, and David's men.

segments.title: Famine and Gibeonite Revenge
segments.gist: A three-year famine prompts David to ask the Gibeonites what restitution they require for Saul's attempt to destroy them.

segments.title: Seven Descendants Handed Over
segments.gist: David spares Mephibosheth but gives the Gibeonites seven sons of Saul's family, who hang them at Gibeah.

segments.title: Rizpah's Vigil and Burial
segments.gist: Rizpah guards the bodies from birds and beasts; David then gathers the bones of Saul and Jonathan and buries them, and God answers prayer for the land.

segments.title: Abishai Rescues David
segments.gist: In a battle with the Philistines, David grows faint, but Abishai kills the giant Ishbi-benob and David's men swear he will not go out to war again.

segments.title: Victories Over Philistine Giants
segments.gist: Sibbechai, Elhanan, and Jonathan kill other Philistine giants, completing the account of David's men defeating Goliath's relatives.

22.summary: David sings a lengthy song of praise to the LORD for delivering him from all his enemies and from Saul, describing God as his rock and fortress, recounting his cries for help and God's dramatic rescue, and celebrating God's justice, strength, and the exaltation of his king.

segments.title: David's opening praise
segments.gist: David declares his love for the LORD, his rock and fortress, and calls on Him as worthy of praise for salvation from enemies.

segments.title: Distress and divine rescue
segments.gist: David describes being overwhelmed by death and calling to the LORD, who heard from His temple and came in earthquake and fire to rescue him.

segments.title: Reward for righteousness
segments.gist: David affirms that the LORD rewarded him according to his righteousness and dealt with him as he kept the LORD's ways.

segments.title: God equips for battle
segments.gist: David praises God as his strength and shield, who trains his hands for war and gives him victory over his enemies.

segments.title: Closing praise and thanksgiving
segments.gist: David calls the LORD his rock and savior, promises to praise Him among the nations, and credits Him with great deliverance and kindness to His king.

23.summary: The chapter records David's last words, a poem celebrating God's covenant and the justice of his rule, followed by a list of David's mighty warriors and their exploits. It closes with the names of the Thirty and other elite fighters.

segments.title: David's Last Words
segments.gist: David speaks his final oracle, describing the ideal ruler who fears God and the everlasting covenant God made with him.

segments.title: First Three Mighty Men
segments.gist: The exploits of Josheb-basshebeth, Eleazar, and Shammah, who defended Israel against the Philistines.

segments.title: The Well at Bethlehem
segments.gist: Three of the thirty chiefs break through the Philistine camp to fetch water for David, which he pours out as an offering to the Lord.

segments.title: Abishai and Benaiah
segments.gist: Abishai and Benaiah are celebrated for their mighty deeds, though they did not attain the rank of the first three.

segments.title: The Thirty Mighty Men
segments.gist: A list of the thirty elite warriors among David's forces, including Asahel, Uriah, and others.

24.summary: David orders a census of Israel and Judah, which God treats as sin; after Joab carries it out, David repents, and the prophet Gad offers him a choice of punishments. David chooses a pestilence that kills 70,000, and as the angel stretches out his hand over Jerusalem, David intercedes and buys Araunah's threshing floor to build an altar, where the plague is stopped.

segments.title: David orders the census
segments.gist: David commands Joab to number Israel and Judah; Joab objects but obeys, and the count is reported.

segments.title: David repents and chooses punishment
segments.gist: David confesses his sin; Gad offers three punishments, and David chooses pestilence, trusting God's mercy.

segments.title: Plague and David's intercession
segments.gist: The pestilence kills 70,000; as the angel nears Jerusalem, David prays for the people to be spared.

segments.title: Altar on Araunah's threshing floor
segments.gist: Gad tells David to build an altar; David buys Araunah's threshing floor and offers sacrifices, and the plague is stopped.

1.summary: As David is old and bedridden, his son Adonijah exalts himself as king with Joab and Abiathar, while Nathan and Bathsheba urge David to fulfill his oath and make Solomon king. David orders Zadok and Nathan to anoint Solomon at Gihon, and Adonijah's feast breaks up in fear as Solomon takes the throne.

segments.title: David's old age and Abishag
segments.gist: King David is old and cold, so his servants find Abishag the Shunammite to care for him.

segments.title: Adonijah exalts himself
segments.gist: Adonijah, son of Haggith, proclaims himself king with chariots and fifty runners, backed by Joab and Abiathar, but not by Zadok, Benaiah, Nathan, or David's mighty men.

segments.title: Nathan and Bathsheba appeal to David
segments.gist: Nathan instructs Bathsheba to remind David of his oath to make Solomon king, and Nathan confirms Adonijah's feast and conspiracy.

segments.title: David reaffirms Solomon as king
segments.gist: David swears to Bathsheba that Solomon will reign after him, and Bathsheba bows in gratitude.

segments.title: Solomon anointed at Gihon
segments.gist: David orders Zadok, Nathan, and Benaiah to anoint Solomon at Gihon, and the people rejoice with great noise.

segments.title: Adonijah's feast disperses in fear
segments.gist: Adonijah's guests hear the commotion, Jonathan reports Solomon's anointing, and the guests flee; Adonijah clings to the altar and Solomon spares him conditionally.

2.summary: David's final charge to Solomon includes instructions to walk in God's ways and to deal with Joab, Barzillai, and Shimei. After David's death, Solomon secures his throne by executing Adonijah, Joab, and Shimei, and by exiling Abiathar, fulfilling the word of the Lord.

segments.title: David's Charge to Solomon
segments.gist: David instructs Solomon to obey God and to settle accounts with Joab, Barzillai, and Shimei.

segments.title: Adonijah's Request and Death
segments.gist: Adonijah asks for Abishag, and Solomon orders his execution for the request.

segments.title: Abiathar Exiled, Zadok Appointed
segments.gist: Solomon removes Abiathar from the priesthood and makes Zadok priest in his place.

segments.title: Joab and Shimei Executed
segments.gist: Joab is killed at the altar, and Shimei is executed for breaking his oath, securing Solomon's kingdom.

3.summary: Solomon marries Pharaoh's daughter and goes to Gibeon to sacrifice, where God appears to him in a dream and grants his request for a wise and understanding heart. God also promises him riches and honor, and Solomon demonstrates his wisdom by judging between two women who both claim to be the mother of a living child.

segments.title: Solomon's marriage and sacrifice
segments.gist: Solomon marries Pharaoh's daughter and goes to Gibeon to offer a thousand burnt offerings because the high places were still in use.

segments.title: God offers Solomon a request
segments.gist: At Gibeon, God appears to Solomon in a dream and invites him to ask for whatever he wants, and Solomon asks for an understanding heart to judge the people.

segments.title: God grants wisdom and wealth
segments.gist: God is pleased with Solomon's request and promises him a wise heart, plus riches and honor, and Solomon wakes and returns to Jerusalem to sacrifice.

segments.title: Solomon judges the two mothers
segments.gist: Two women come before Solomon, each claiming a living baby after one child died; Solomon orders the baby cut in two, revealing the true mother, and Israel fears his wisdom.

4.summary: This chapter describes Solomon's royal administration: his princes and officers, the twelve district governors who supplied provisions for the king's household, the daily provisions required, and the extent and peace of his kingdom. It closes with a note on Solomon's wisdom, his proverbs and songs, and his knowledge of natural history.

segments.title: Solomon's Princes and Officers
segments.gist: Lists Solomon's chief officials, including priests, scribes, the recorder, the army commander, and the king's friend.

segments.title: Twelve District Governors
segments.gist: Names the twelve officers over Israel who provided food for the king and his household, each for one month a year.

segments.title: Judah and Israel Dwell Safely
segments.gist: Describes the vast population, Solomon's dominion over the region, and the peace and security of Judah and Israel under his rule.

segments.title: Daily Provisions for the Court
segments.gist: Details the daily provisions required for Solomon's household and the barley and straw for his horses.

segments.title: Solomon's Wisdom and Writings
segments.gist: States that God gave Solomon great wisdom, and recounts his three thousand proverbs, thousand and five songs, and knowledge of nature.

5.summary: Solomon arranges with Hiram, king of Tyre, to supply cedar and fir timber from Lebanon for the building of the temple, and in return provides food for Hiram's household. The chapter describes the labor force and the peace and wisdom God gave Solomon.

segments.title: Hiram sends to Solomon
segments.gist: Hiram sends servants to Solomon, and Solomon asks for cedar and fir from Lebanon to build the house of the LORD.

segments.title: Hiram agrees to supply timber
segments.gist: Hiram rejoices and agrees to provide cedar and fir, and Solomon gives wheat and oil for Hiram's household.

segments.title: Solomon's labor force
segments.gist: Solomon raises a levy of thirty thousand men, plus burden bearers and hewers, and prepares stones for the foundation.

6.summary: Solomon begins construction of the temple in the fourth year of his reign, building it according to detailed specifications with stone, cedar, and gold. God promises to dwell among the Israelites if Solomon walks in His statutes. The chapter describes the temple's interior, including the oracle and the cherubim, and concludes with the completion of the building after seven years.

segments.title: Temple Construction Begins
segments.gist: Solomon starts building the temple in the fourth year of his reign, using stone and cedar according to the plans.

segments.title: God's Promise to Solomon
segments.gist: God promises to dwell among the Israelites and not forsake them if Solomon follows His commandments.

segments.title: Interior Overlaid with Gold
segments.gist: Solomon overlays the temple's interior with cedar and pure gold, including the oracle and the altar.

segments.title: Cherubim in the Oracle
segments.gist: Two cherubim of olive wood are made for the oracle, their wings spanning the room.

segments.title: Carved Doors and Walls
segments.gist: The walls and doors are carved with cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers, and overlaid with gold.

segments.title: Completion After Seven Years
segments.gist: The inner court is built with hewn stone, and the temple is completed after seven years of construction.

7.summary: Solomon's palace complex is built over thirteen years, including the Hall of the Forest of Lebanon, the Hall of Pillars, and the Hall of Judgment. Hiram of Tyre casts the bronze pillars Jachin and Boaz, the molten sea, the lavers, and all the temple vessels, which are finally brought into the finished temple.

segments.title: Solomon's palace buildings
segments.gist: Solomon builds his own house, the house of the forest of Lebanon, the hall of pillars, and the hall of judgment over thirteen years.

segments.title: Hiram casts the two pillars
segments.gist: Hiram of Tyre casts the bronze pillars Jachin and Boaz with their capitals, network, and pomegranates.

segments.title: The molten sea and lavers
segments.gist: Hiram makes the molten sea on twelve oxen, ten lavers on wheeled bases, and the pots, shovels, and basins.

segments.title: Inventory of bronze work
segments.gist: The chapter lists the bronze furnishings Hiram made for the temple, noting the great quantity of bronze used.

segments.title: Golden vessels brought in
segments.gist: Solomon makes the golden altar, table, lampstands, and other vessels, and brings in the dedicated treasures to the temple.

8.summary: Solomon assembles Israel to bring the ark into the newly finished temple, and the glory of the LORD fills the house. He then prays a long dedication prayer, blessing God, confessing human frailty, and asking forgiveness for future sins, and finally blesses the people and offers sacrifices, ending with a feast.

segments.title: Ark brought into temple
segments.gist: Solomon gathers Israel's elders and priests carry the ark and holy vessels into the temple, placing them in the most holy place.

segments.title: Solomon blesses the assembly
segments.gist: Solomon blesses the congregation, recalls God's promise to David, and declares that God has chosen Jerusalem and David's line to build the house.

segments.title: Solomon's prayer of dedication
segments.gist: Solomon prays before the altar, praising God's uniqueness and faithfulness, and asks God to hear prayers made toward the temple, including cases of sin, famine, and foreign enemies.

segments.title: Solomon blesses the people
segments.gist: After kneeling in prayer, Solomon stands and blesses the whole assembly, urging them to remain faithful to God's commandments.

segments.title: Sacrifices and feast
segments.gist: The king and people offer abundant sacrifices, and Solomon holds a great feast for fourteen days before sending the people home joyful.

9.summary: God appears to Solomon a second time, promising to establish his throne forever if he walks in integrity, but warning that disobedience will bring destruction and make the temple a byword. Solomon then gives twenty cities in Galilee to Hiram king of Tyre, who is displeased with them, and Solomon builds up various cities and uses a levy of forced labor. The chapter ends with Pharaoh's daughter moving into her own house, Solomon's sacrifices, and his fleet bringing gold from Ophir.

segments.title: God's Second Appearance to Solomon
segments.gist: After the temple is finished, God appears to Solomon, promising to establish his throne if he obeys, but warning that disobedience will bring ruin and make the temple a desolation.

segments.title: Solomon Gives Cities to Hiram
segments.gist: Solomon gives twenty cities in Galilee to Hiram king of Tyre, but Hiram is displeased with them and calls them Cabul.

segments.title: Solomon's Building Projects
segments.gist: Solomon uses a levy of forced labor to build the Millo, the wall of Jerusalem, and various store cities, chariot cities, and other cities.

segments.title: Canaanites Remain as Servants
segments.gist: The remaining Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites are made bondservants, while Israelites serve as soldiers and officers over Solomon's works.

segments.title: Pharaoh's Daughter Moves to Her House
segments.gist: Pharaoh's daughter moves from the city of David to her own house that Solomon built for her, and Solomon offers burnt offerings and peace offerings three times a year.

segments.title: Solomon's Fleet Brings Gold
segments.gist: Solomon builds a fleet at Ezion-geber, and Hiram's servants bring gold from Ophir, amounting to four hundred and twenty talents.

10.summary: The queen of Sheba visits Solomon to test him with hard questions, is overwhelmed by his wisdom and wealth, and blesses the LORD. Solomon's gold, ivory throne, and trading enterprises are described, including his fleet bringing gold, almug wood, and precious stones, and his chariots and horsemen.

segments.title: Queen of Sheba visits Solomon
segments.gist: The queen of Sheba comes to test Solomon, is amazed by his wisdom and wealth, and praises the LORD for making him king.

segments.title: Solomon's gold and ivory throne
segments.gist: Solomon's annual gold income, his ivory throne overlaid with gold, and his gold drinking vessels are described.

segments.title: Solomon's trade and fame
segments.gist: Solomon's fleet brings gold, almug wood, and precious stones; his wealth and wisdom attract visitors from all nations.

segments.title: Solomon's chariots and horsemen
segments.gist: Solomon gathers chariots and horsemen and imports horses and chariots from Egypt and other lands.

11.summary: Solomon's heart turns to foreign gods through his many wives, and God declares the kingdom will be torn from his son. God raises adversaries against Solomon—Hadad, Rezon, and Jeroboam—and Ahijah prophesies to Jeroboam that he will rule ten tribes. Solomon dies and Rehoboam succeeds him.

segments.title: Solomon's wives and idolatry
segments.gist: Solomon loves many foreign women and, in his old age, his wives turn his heart to other gods, so he builds high places and God declares the kingdom will be torn from him.

segments.title: Adversaries Hadad and Rezon
segments.gist: God raises up Hadad the Edomite and Rezon of Zobah as adversaries against Solomon because of his sin.

segments.title: Jeroboam and Ahijah's prophecy
segments.gist: Jeroboam rebels, and the prophet Ahijah tells him God will give him ten tribes, though one tribe remains for David's sake.

segments.title: Solomon's death and burial
segments.gist: The rest of Solomon's acts are recorded, he dies and is buried in the city of David, and his son Rehoboam reigns in his place.

12.summary: After Solomon's death, his son Rehoboam rejects the people's plea for lighter burdens and threatens harsher treatment, prompting ten tribes to revolt under Jeroboam. Rehoboam is restrained from civil war, while Jeroboam sets up golden calves in Bethel and Dan and appoints unauthorized priests and feasts, leading Israel into idolatry.

segments.title: People ask Rehoboam for relief
segments.gist: Jeroboam and the assembly ask Rehoboam to lighten Solomon's heavy yoke, promising to serve him if he does.

segments.title: Rehoboam rejects elders, follows young men
segments.gist: Rehoboam consults old men who advise kindness, but rejects their counsel and follows young advisers who urge harsher treatment.

segments.title: Ten tribes revolt and make Jeroboam king
segments.gist: Israel rejects Rehoboam's rule, stones Adoram, and calls Jeroboam to become king over the northern tribes.

segments.title: God forbids Rehoboam's war
segments.gist: Rehoboam assembles Judah's army to fight Israel, but Shemaiah the prophet declares God's will and the troops disperse.

segments.title: Jeroboam sets up golden calves
segments.gist: Jeroboam fortifies cities, makes two golden calves for Bethel and Dan, appoints non-Levitical priests, and institutes a rival feast.

13.summary: A man of God from Judah prophesies against Jeroboam's altar at Bethel, and it is split as a sign; Jeroboam's hand withers and is restored. An old prophet in Bethel deceives the man of God into disobeying God's command, and he is killed by a lion on the way home. Jeroboam continues his idolatrous practices, and the chapter ends with the old prophet's lament and the fulfillment of the prophecy against the altar.

segments.title: Man of God prophesies at Bethel
segments.gist: A man of God from Judah cries against the altar at Bethel, foretelling Josiah, and gives a sign; Jeroboam's hand withers and is healed.

segments.title: Old prophet deceives the man of God
segments.gist: An old prophet in Bethel lies to the man of God, claiming an angel told him to bring him back, and the man of God eats and drinks in his house.

segments.title: Judgment pronounced and fulfilled
segments.gist: The old prophet declares that the man of God will not be buried in his fathers' tomb; a lion kills him on the road, and his body is left with the donkey and the lion.

segments.title: Old prophet mourns and buries him
segments.gist: The old prophet retrieves the body, mourns, buries him in his own tomb, and confirms the prophecy against the altar at Bethel.

segments.title: Jeroboam's continued idolatry
segments.gist: Jeroboam does not turn from his evil way but makes priests from all the people, bringing sin upon his house.

14.summary: Ahijah the prophet foretells the death of Jeroboam's son and the downfall of Jeroboam's house because of his idolatry. Jeroboam's wife returns to Tirzah and the child dies. Meanwhile in Judah, King Rehoboam leads the people into idolatry, and Shishak king of Egypt invades and plunders the temple and palace. Rehoboam dies and is succeeded by his son Abijam.

segments.title: Jeroboam sends wife to Ahijah
segments.gist: Jeroboam sends his wife disguised to the prophet Ahijah to inquire about their sick son.

segments.title: Ahijah pronounces judgment
segments.gist: Ahijah recognizes the disguise and delivers God's judgment: Jeroboam's house will be cut off and Israel will be scattered.

segments.title: Child dies as foretold
segments.gist: Jeroboam's wife returns to Tirzah, and as she crosses the threshold the child dies and is buried.

segments.title: Jeroboam's reign and death
segments.gist: The rest of Jeroboam's acts are recorded, and he dies and is succeeded by his son Nadab.

segments.title: Rehoboam's idolatry in Judah
segments.gist: Rehoboam rules Judah, which falls into idolatry and builds high places, provoking God's jealousy.

segments.title: Shishak plunders Jerusalem
segments.gist: Shishak king of Egypt attacks Jerusalem and carries off the treasures of the temple and the king's house, including the gold shields.

segments.title: Rehoboam's death and succession
segments.gist: The rest of Rehoboam's reign is recorded, and he dies and is buried, succeeded by his son Abijam.

15.summary: 1 Kings 15 recounts the reigns of Abijam and Asa in Judah and Nadab and Baasha in Israel. Abijam continues in sin, while Asa removes idols and makes a covenant, though he fails to remove the high places. In Israel, Nadab is assassinated by Baasha, who then destroys Jeroboam's house, fulfilling prophecy, but Baasha himself persists in idolatry, leading to ongoing conflict between the two kingdoms.

segments.title: Abijam's Reign in Judah
segments.gist: Abijam reigns wickedly in Judah, yet God preserves the throne for David's sake; he dies and is buried.

segments.title: Asa's Reforms in Judah
segments.gist: Asa does right, removes idols and his grandmother, and brings dedicated gifts into the temple.

segments.title: Asa's Alliance and Death
segments.gist: Asa bribes Ben-hadad to break alliance with Baasha, builds Geba and Mizpah, then dies and is buried.

segments.title: Nadab and Baasha in Israel
segments.gist: Nadab sins and is killed by Baasha, who destroys Jeroboam's house and continues in idolatry and war.

segments.title: Baasha's Evil Reign
segments.gist: Baasha reigns over Israel and follows Jeroboam's sinful ways, provoking God's anger.

16.summary: This chapter records the rapid succession of kings in Israel after Jeroboam: Baasha is condemned by the prophet Jehu and dies, his son Elah is assassinated by Zimri, who then kills all of Baasha's house; Zimri rules seven days before Omri besieges him and he burns himself in the palace. Omri prevails over Tibni, buys Samaria for his capital, and does evil; his son Ahab succeeds him and surpasses all in wickedness by marrying Jezebel and promoting Baal worship, provoking God's anger.

segments.title: Jehu's prophecy against Baasha
segments.gist: The word of the Lord comes to Jehu against Baasha for killing Jeroboam's house and leading Israel into sin, promising to consume his house like Jeroboam's.

segments.title: Elah killed by Zimri
segments.gist: Baasha's son Elah reigns two years; while drinking in Tirzah, his servant Zimri, captain of half his chariots, assassinates him and wipes out all of Baasha's house, fulfilling Jehu's prophecy.

segments.title: Zimri's seven-day reign and suicide
segments.gist: Zimri reigns seven days in Tirzah; when Omri besieges the city, Zimri burns the king's house over himself rather than be captured, and the rest of his acts are recorded.

segments.title: Omri becomes king and builds Samaria
segments.gist: Israel divides between Omri and Tibni; Omri prevails, becomes king, buys the hill of Samaria and builds a city there, but he does evil more than all before him.

segments.title: Ahab's wicked reign and Baal worship
segments.gist: Ahab son of Omri reigns over Israel and surpasses his predecessors in wickedness, marrying Jezebel and promoting Baal worship; in his days Hiel rebuilds Jericho at the cost of his sons, according to Joshua's curse.

17.summary: God sends Elijah to announce a drought to King Ahab, then hides him by the brook Cherith where ravens feed him. When the brook dries up, Elijah stays with a widow in Zarephath; her flour and oil do not run out, and he raises her son from the dead.

segments.title: Elijah announces drought to Ahab
segments.gist: Elijah tells Ahab there will be no rain except by his word, then hides by Cherith where ravens feed him.

segments.title: Elijah and the widow of Zarephath
segments.gist: God sends Elijah to a widow in Zarephath; her flour and oil do not run out during the drought.

segments.title: Elijah raises the widow's son
segments.gist: The widow's son dies; Elijah prays and God restores the child's life, and she believes Elijah is a man of God.

18.summary: In the third year of drought, Elijah meets Obadiah and then confronts King Ahab, challenging the prophets of Baal to a contest on Mount Carmel. After Baal's prophets fail to bring fire, God answers Elijah with fire from heaven, and the people declare the LORD is God. Elijah then prays for rain, and the drought ends.

segments.title: Elijah Meets Obadiah
segments.gist: Elijah appears to Obadiah, who fears for his life but agrees to tell Ahab of Elijah's return.

segments.title: Elijah Confronts Ahab
segments.gist: Ahab accuses Elijah of troubling Israel, but Elijah blames Ahab's idolatry and calls for a contest at Carmel.

segments.title: Elijah Proposes the Contest
segments.gist: Elijah challenges the people and the prophets of Baal to prepare a sacrifice and call on their gods.

segments.title: Baal's Prophets Fail
segments.gist: The prophets of Baal cry out and cut themselves, but there is no response from Baal.

segments.title: God Answers with Fire
segments.gist: Elijah repairs the altar, prays, and fire falls from heaven, leading the people to declare the LORD is God and seize the prophets.

segments.title: Rain Returns
segments.gist: Elijah prays for rain, sends his servant to look, and then runs before Ahab's chariot to Jezreel.

19.summary: Elijah flees from Jezebel into the wilderness, where an angel feeds him and he travels to Horeb; there God speaks to him in a still small voice, gives him new instructions, and assures him of a remnant. He anoints Hazael, Jehu, and Elisha, who immediately follows him.

segments.title: Elijah flees to the wilderness
segments.gist: Elijah flees from Jezebel to Beersheba, then into the wilderness, where an angel feeds him and he travels to Horeb.

segments.title: God speaks at Horeb
segments.gist: At Horeb, God asks Elijah what he is doing there, and Elijah laments that Israel has forsaken the covenant and killed the prophets.

segments.title: God's instructions and remnant
segments.gist: God tells Elijah to anoint Hazael, Jehu, and Elisha, and assures him that seven thousand in Israel have not bowed to Baal.

segments.title: Elisha follows Elijah
segments.gist: Elijah finds Elisha plowing, throws his mantle on him, and Elisha leaves his oxen to follow Elijah.

20.summary: Ben-hadad of Syria besieges Samaria and demands Ahab's silver, gold, wives, and children; Ahab initially yields but refuses the final demand, and with a prophet's assurance Israel routs the Syrians. The next spring the Syrians attack again at Aphek and are defeated, and Ben-hadad surrenders. Ahab spares him and makes a treaty, for which a prophet condemns Ahab and declares that he and his people will die in Ben-hadad's place.

segments.title: Ben-hadad's demands and Ahab's reply
segments.gist: Ben-hadad of Syria besieges Samaria and demands Ahab's silver, gold, wives, and children; Ahab agrees until Ben-hadad sends officers to seize everything.

segments.title: Prophet promises victory and Israel routs Syrians
segments.gist: A prophet tells Ahab God will give him victory, and Israel's young officers defeat the Syrians in a great slaughter.

segments.title: Syrians plan a second attack at Aphek
segments.gist: The prophet warns Ahab to prepare for a spring attack, and Ben-hadad's servants advise him to fight on the plains instead of the hills.

segments.title: Israel defeats Syria at Aphek
segments.gist: The Syrians gather at Aphek, and after a prophet's assurance Israel kills 100,000 Syrian footmen and the wall of Aphek kills 27,000 more.

segments.title: Ben-hadad surrenders and makes a treaty
segments.gist: Ben-hadad's servants plead for mercy, and Ahab calls him brother, spares him, and makes a covenant to restore cities.

segments.title: Prophet condemns Ahab for sparing Ben-hadad
segments.gist: A prophet, disguised, tells Ahab that because he let Ben-hadad go, his life and people will be taken instead, and Ahab goes home displeased.

21.summary: King Ahab covets Naboth's vineyard, and when Naboth refuses to sell, Jezebel orchestrates his death by false accusation so Ahab can seize the land. Elijah confronts Ahab with God's judgment on him and Jezebel, and Ahab's temporary repentance delays the disaster to his son's days.

segments.title: Ahab Covets Naboth's Vineyard
segments.gist: Ahab asks Naboth for his vineyard, but Naboth refuses because it is his family inheritance, leaving Ahab sullen.

segments.title: Jezebel Plots Naboth's Death
segments.gist: Jezebel writes letters in Ahab's name, arranges false witnesses, and has Naboth stoned to death so Ahab can take the vineyard.

segments.title: Elijah Pronounces Judgment
segments.gist: God sends Elijah to confront Ahab in the vineyard, declaring doom on Ahab's house and on Jezebel for their evil.

segments.title: Ahab's Extreme Wickedness
segments.gist: The narrator notes that Ahab sold himself to do evil, urged on by Jezebel, and followed abominable idols.

segments.title: Ahab's Repentance Delays Judgment
segments.gist: Ahab humbles himself, and God tells Elijah that because of this, the disaster will not come in Ahab's days but in his son's.

22.summary: Ahab and Jehoshaphat plan war against Ramoth-gilead; Ahab's prophets promise success, but Micaiah predicts disaster and is imprisoned. Ahab dies in battle despite disguising himself, and Jehoshaphat's reign is summarized. The chapter closes with Ahaziah succeeding Ahab and continuing his father's idolatry.

segments.title: Ahab proposes alliance
segments.gist: Ahab asks Jehoshaphat to join him against Ramoth-gilead, and Jehoshaphat agrees but suggests seeking God's counsel.

segments.title: False prophets promise victory
segments.gist: Ahab's prophets, including Zedekiah, unanimously predict success, and Jehoshaphat asks for a prophet of the Lord.

segments.title: Micaiah predicts defeat
segments.gist: Micaiah foretells Ahab's death and Israel's scattering, explaining a lying spirit in the prophets' mouths; Zedekiah strikes him and Ahab orders his imprisonment.

segments.title: Ahab dies in battle
segments.gist: Ahab disguises himself but is struck by a random arrow; he dies, and his chariot is washed at Samaria's pool as prophesied.

segments.title: Jehoshaphat's reign summarized
segments.gist: Jehoshaphat's righteous reign in Judah is described, including his removal of sodomites and failed naval alliance with Ahaziah.

segments.title: Ahaziah's evil reign
segments.gist: Ahaziah son of Ahab becomes king of Israel and serves Baal, provoking the Lord's anger like his father.

1.summary: After King Ahaziah of Israel is injured, he sends messengers to consult Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron. Elijah intercepts them with a prophecy that the king will die for consulting a foreign god, and when Ahaziah sends soldiers to arrest him, fire from heaven consumes two companies before the third captain pleads for his life. Elijah then delivers the death sentence to Ahaziah in person, and Ahaziah dies and is succeeded by his brother Jehoram.

segments.title: Ahaziah Seeks Baal-zebub
segments.gist: King Ahaziah, injured in a fall, sends messengers to ask Baal-zebub of Ekron whether he will recover; Elijah intercepts them with a prophecy that he will die.

segments.title: Fire Consumes Two Companies
segments.gist: Ahaziah sends a captain and fifty men to arrest Elijah; fire from heaven consumes two such companies, but the third captain pleads and Elijah goes with him to repeat the death sentence.

segments.title: Ahaziah Dies and Jehoram Reigns
segments.gist: Ahaziah dies according to Elijah's word and is succeeded by his brother Jehoram, with a closing reference to the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

2.summary: Elijah and Elisha travel from Gilgal to the Jordan, where Elijah parts the river and is taken up in a whirlwind; Elisha receives a double portion of his spirit, heals Jericho's waters, and calls down a curse on mocking youths.

segments.title: Elijah and Elisha journey
segments.gist: Elijah leads Elisha from Gilgal to Bethel and Jericho, where prophets tell Elisha that Elijah will be taken that day.

segments.title: Elijah parts the Jordan
segments.gist: Fifty prophets watch as Elijah strikes the Jordan with his mantle, the waters divide, and he and Elisha cross on dry ground.

segments.title: Elisha succeeds Elijah
segments.gist: Elisha takes Elijah's mantle, parts the Jordan, and the prophets recognize that Elijah's spirit rests on him.

segments.title: Elisha heals Jericho's waters
segments.gist: The men of Jericho complain of bad water; Elisha casts salt into the spring, and the waters are healed permanently.

segments.title: Elisha curses mocking youths
segments.gist: Boys from Bethel mock Elisha's baldness; he curses them, two bears maul forty-two, and he returns to Samaria.

3.summary: Jehoram of Israel, with Jehoshaphat of Judah and the king of Edom, marches against Moab after Moab rebels. When the allied army runs out of water, Elisha prophesies a miraculous supply and victory, and the Moabites are defeated, though the king of Moab sacrifices his son on the wall.

segments.title: Moab Rebels Against Israel
segments.gist: After Ahab's death, Moab rebels; Jehoram musters Israel and counts his army.

segments.title: Alliance and Water Shortage
segments.gist: Jehoram allies with Jehoshaphat and the king of Edom; after seven days they lack water for the army.

segments.title: Seeking Elisha's Counsel
segments.gist: Jehoram despairs, but Jehoshaphat asks for a prophet; they go to Elisha, who agrees for Jehoshaphat's sake.

segments.title: Elisha Prophesies Water and Victory
segments.gist: Elisha foretells a miraculous supply of water and promises that Moab will be delivered into their hands.

segments.title: Moab Defeated
segments.gist: Water fills the valley; Moab attacks but is routed, and the Israelites destroy their cities and land.

segments.title: Moab's King Sacrifices His Son
segments.gist: The king of Moab, seeing defeat, sacrifices his eldest son on the wall, and great wrath comes upon Israel.

4.summary: Elisha multiplies a widow's oil to pay her debts, promises a Shunammite woman a son who later dies and is raised, purifies a poisoned pot of stew, feeds a hundred men with twenty loaves, and heals Naaman's leprosy (though Naaman's story begins in chapter 5).

segments.title: Widow's Oil Multiplied
segments.gist: A widow cries to Elisha about her husband's debt; he tells her to gather vessels, and the oil multiplies to pay the debt and live on.

segments.title: Shunammite Woman's Son Promised
segments.gist: A Shunammite woman prepares a room for Elisha; he promises her a son, and she bears a child the next year.

segments.title: Elisha Raises the Dead Child
segments.gist: The child dies; the woman seeks Elisha, who prays and stretches himself over the boy, and the child is restored to life.

segments.title: Poisoned Pot Healed
segments.gist: During a famine, sons of the prophets eat a deadly stew; Elisha casts in meal, and the pot becomes safe to eat.

segments.title: Twenty Loaves Feed a Hundred
segments.gist: A man brings twenty barley loaves; Elisha orders them set before a hundred men, and they eat with leftovers, as the LORD promised.

5.summary: Naaman, a Syrian commander afflicted with leprosy, is healed after dipping seven times in the Jordan at Elisha's instruction. He offers gifts, which Elisha refuses, and Gehazi secretly takes them and is struck with leprosy.

segments.title: Naaman's leprosy and the captive girl
segments.gist: Naaman, a mighty Syrian commander, has leprosy; a captive Israelite girl tells his wife of a prophet in Samaria who can heal him.

segments.title: Naaman healed in the Jordan
segments.gist: Elisha tells Naaman to wash seven times in the Jordan; after initial anger, Naaman obeys and is healed.

segments.title: Naaman's confession and Elisha's refusal
segments.gist: Naaman returns to Elisha, confesses faith in the LORD, and offers gifts, which Elisha refuses; Naaman asks for earth for an altar.

segments.title: Gehazi's greed and leprosy
segments.gist: Gehazi runs after Naaman and deceitfully takes gifts; Elisha rebukes him, and Gehazi becomes leprous.

6.summary: Elisha makes a lost axe head float and reveals Syria's battle plans to Israel, prompting the king of Syria to send an army to capture him. Elisha's servant sees the surrounding army, but Elisha prays and the servant sees chariots of fire; Elisha then strikes the Syrians with blindness and leads them to Samaria. Later, Ben-hadad besieges Samaria, causing a severe famine in which two women agree to eat their sons, and the king blames Elisha and sends men to kill him.

segments.title: Elisha Makes Iron Float
segments.gist: The sons of the prophets build a larger dwelling by the Jordan; when a borrowed axe head falls into the water, Elisha throws a stick in and makes the iron float.

segments.title: Elisha Warns Israel's King
segments.gist: Elisha repeatedly reveals the king of Syria's secret plans to the king of Israel, frustrating Syria's strategy; the Syrian king suspects a traitor until told Elisha knows his words.

segments.title: Syrian Army Blinded at Dothan
segments.gist: The king of Syria sends horses and chariots to capture Elisha at Dothan; Elisha prays that his servant may see the mountain full of fiery horses and chariots, then prays the Syrians are struck blind.

segments.title: Elisha Leads Blinded Army to Samaria
segments.gist: Elisha leads the blinded Syrians to Samaria; when their eyes are opened, the king of Israel asks if he should kill them, but Elisha orders a feast and sends them home, ending Syrian raids.

segments.title: Siege and Famine in Samaria
segments.gist: Ben-hadad besieges Samaria, causing a great famine; a woman cries to the king for help because she and another woman agreed to eat their sons, and the king blames Elisha and sends to kill him.

segments.title: King Confronts Elisha
segments.gist: The king arrives at Elisha's house and declares that the evil is from the LORD and asks why he should wait for the LORD any longer.

7.summary: During the Aramean siege of Samaria, four leprous men discover the enemy camp abandoned and report it to the king's household. The Israelites plunder the camp, and the prophet Elisha's earlier prediction that food would be cheap the next day is fulfilled, while the skeptical officer who doubted it is trampled to death at the gate.

segments.title: Elisha Predicts Abundant Food
segments.gist: Elisha says that by the next day a measure of fine flour will sell for a shekel and two measures of barley for a shekel in Samaria.

segments.title: Lepers Decide to Surrender
segments.gist: Four leprous men at the city gate reason that staying means death and going to the Aramean camp may spare them, so they go at twilight.

segments.title: Lepers Find Camp Abandoned
segments.gist: They enter the camp and find it deserted because the Lord caused the Arameans to flee; they eat, drink, and hide plunder.

segments.title: Lepers Report the Good News
segments.gist: The lepers realize they should not keep silent, so they call to the gatekeepers, who report to the king's household.

segments.title: King Investigates and People Plunder
segments.gist: The king sends messengers who confirm the abandoned camp, and the people go out and plunder the Aramean tents.

segments.title: Elisha's Prophecy Fulfilled
segments.gist: Food becomes plentiful as Elisha foretold, and the doubting officer is trampled to death at the gate.

8.summary: 2 Kings 8 concludes the Shunammite woman's land restoration and Elisha's role in Hazael's rise to the Syrian throne, then recounts the reigns of Jehoram and Ahaziah in Judah, including Edom's revolt and Ahaziah's alliance with Joram of Israel.

segments.title: Elisha and the Shunammite's Land
segments.gist: Elisha tells the Shunammite woman to leave during famine; she returns after seven years and the king restores her house and land.

segments.title: Hazael Becomes King of Syria
segments.gist: Elisha visits Damascus, tells Hazael he will become king, and Hazael smothers Ben-hadad and takes the throne.

segments.title: Jehoram's Reign in Judah
segments.gist: Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat reigns wickedly in Judah, Edom revolts, and he dies after eight years.

segments.title: Ahaziah's Reign and Alliance
segments.gist: Ahaziah son of Jehoram reigns in Judah, joins Joram of Israel in war against Hazael, and visits wounded Joram in Jezreel.

9.summary: Elisha sends a young prophet to anoint Jehu king over Israel and to commission him to destroy the house of Ahab. Jehu is proclaimed king by his officers, kills Joram and Ahaziah, and has Jezebel thrown from a window, fulfilling Elijah's prophecy.

segments.title: Elisha sends prophet to anoint Jehu
segments.gist: Elisha sends a young prophet to Ramoth-gilead to anoint Jehu king and command him to strike down the house of Ahab.

segments.title: Jehu proclaimed king by officers
segments.gist: Jehu's fellow officers ask why the prophet came; upon hearing the news, they hastily proclaim Jehu king.

segments.title: Jehu plots against Joram
segments.gist: Jehu conspires against King Joram, instructs his men to keep the city closed, and rides to Jezreel.

segments.title: Jehu kills Joram
segments.gist: Joram and Ahaziah meet Jehu; Jehu shoots Joram and has his body thrown on Naboth's field, fulfilling prophecy.

segments.title: Ahaziah wounded and dies
segments.gist: Ahaziah flees but is wounded by Jehu's men and dies at Megiddo; his servants bury him in Jerusalem.

segments.title: Jezebel killed
segments.gist: Jezebel prepares to meet Jehu, but at his command eunuchs throw her from a window; dogs eat her flesh as prophesied.

10.summary: Jehu writes to the rulers of Jezreel and the guardians of Ahab's seventy sons, challenging them to choose a king; when they submit, he orders the sons killed and their heads piled at the gate. He then kills Ahab's relatives and allies, including the brothers of Ahaziah and the priests of Baal, and destroys the temple of Baal. The chapter concludes with Jehu's partial obedience and the beginning of his reign over Israel.

segments.title: Jehu Orders Ahab's Sons Killed
segments.gist: Jehu challenges Jezreel's rulers to fight for Ahab's seventy sons, but they submit; he then commands the sons be slain and their heads piled at the gate.

segments.title: Ahaziah's Brothers Slain
segments.gist: Jehu encounters the brothers of Ahaziah and orders them killed at the well of Beth-eked, forty-two men.

segments.title: Jehonadab Joins Jehu
segments.gist: Jehu meets Jehonadab, takes him into his chariot, and then kills the remaining relatives of Ahab in Samaria.

segments.title: Baal's Temple Destroyed
segments.gist: Jehu gathers all Baal worshippers under pretense of a great sacrifice, has them killed, and destroys the temple of Baal.

segments.title: Jehu's Partial Obedience
segments.gist: Jehu does not depart from the sins of Jeroboam, and God promises him a dynasty because he executed judgment on Ahab's house.

segments.title: Israel's Territory Lost
segments.gist: In Jehu's days, God begins to cut off parts of Israel, and Hazael takes territory east of the Jordan; Jehu dies and Jehoahaz reigns.

11.summary: Athaliah, mother of Ahaziah, seizes the throne of Judah and kills the royal family, but Jehosheba hides the infant Joash in the temple for six years. In the seventh year, Jehoiada the priest gathers the guards and captains, crowns Joash, and has Athaliah executed. Jehoiada then makes a covenant between the LORD, the king, and the people, and the people destroy the house of Baal.

segments.title: Athaliah usurps the throne
segments.gist: Athaliah, mother of Ahaziah, destroys the royal seed and takes the throne, but Jehosheba hides Joash in the temple.

segments.title: Jehoiada plans the coup
segments.gist: In the seventh year Jehoiada summons the captains and guards, binds them by oath, and shows them the king's son.

segments.title: Guards surround and crown Joash
segments.gist: The guards take their positions around the temple, and Jehoiada crowns Joash and gives him the testimony as the people clap.

segments.title: Athaliah seized and slain
segments.gist: Athaliah cries treason, is led out by the guards, and is killed at the king's house.

segments.title: Covenant and Baal destroyed
segments.gist: Jehoiada makes a covenant, the people destroy Baal's house and kill Mattan, and Joash is seated on the throne.

12.summary: Jehoash (Joash) becomes king of Judah at age seven and reigns forty years, doing right as long as Jehoiada the priest instructs him, though the high places remain. He directs the priests to collect money for temple repairs, and when they are slow, he has a chest placed at the temple gate; the people give gladly, and the funds pay workmen who restore the house of the LORD. Later, Hazael of Syria threatens Jerusalem, and Jehoash buys him off with temple treasures; finally, his servants conspire and kill him, and his son Amaziah succeeds him.

segments.title: Jehoash begins his reign
segments.gist: Jehoash becomes king at seven and reigns forty years in Jerusalem, doing right while Jehoiada the priest instructs him, though the high places remain.

segments.title: Jehoash orders temple repairs
segments.gist: Jehoash tells the priests to collect money for temple repairs from the people, but by the twenty-third year they have not repaired the breaches.

segments.title: Chest and payment for workmen
segments.gist: Jehoiada places a chest at the altar; the people give gladly, and the money is paid to workmen who repair the temple, with no accounting required of them.

segments.title: Hazael threatens Jerusalem
segments.gist: Hazael king of Syria sets his face to attack Jerusalem, and Jehoash gives him all the hallowed things and gold from the temple and palace to turn him away.

segments.title: Conspiracy and death of Jehoash
segments.gist: Jehoash's servants conspire and kill him at the house of Millo, and he is buried with his fathers; Amaziah his son reigns in his stead.

13.summary: Jehoahaz reigns in Israel and does evil, so God gives Israel into the hand of Hazael of Syria; Jehoahaz seeks the LORD and receives a deliverer, but the people continue in sin. His son Jehoash reigns and warms against Judah; Elisha falls sick, and Joash weeps over him. Elisha prophesies three victories over Syria, dies, and a dead man revived by touching his bones. Hazael oppresses Israel, but Jehoash recovers the cities.

segments.title: Jehoahaz's evil reign and oppression
segments.gist: Jehoahaz reigns in Israel, does evil, and is oppressed by Hazael of Syria; he seeks the LORD, who gives a deliverer, yet the people continue in sin.

segments.title: Jehoash reigns in Israel
segments.gist: Jehoash son of Jehoahaz reigns in Israel, does evil, and wars against Amaziah king of Judah; he dies and is buried in Samaria.

segments.title: Elisha's final prophecy to Joash
segments.gist: Elisha falls sick, Joash weeps over him, and Elisha has him shoot arrows and strike the ground, prophesying three victories over Syria.

segments.title: Elisha's death and posthumous miracle
segments.gist: Elisha dies and is buried; a dead man revived when his body touches Elisha's bones.

segments.title: Hazael's oppression and Jehoash's victories
segments.gist: Hazael oppresses Israel, but the LORD is gracious; after Hazael's death, Jehoash recovers the cities from Ben-hadad three times.

14.summary: Amaziah reigns in Judah, executing his father's assassins but sparing their children, then hires Israelite mercenaries whom a prophet warns him to dismiss. He defeats Edom but later challenges King Jehoash of Israel, who crushes Judah, breaks down Jerusalem's wall, and plunders the temple and palace. Amaziah is assassinated in Lachish, and his son Azariah succeeds him. Meanwhile, Jehoash's son Jeroboam II reigns in Israel, restoring Israel's borders and saving the nation despite its sins.

segments.title: Amaziah's Obedience and Edom Victory
segments.gist: Amaziah becomes king, kills his father's assassins but spares their children, and defeats Edom in the Valley of Salt.

segments.title: Amaziah's Challenge to Jehoash
segments.gist: Amaziah hires Israelite mercenaries but dismisses them on a prophet's warning; he then challenges Jehoash, who warns him with a parable but Amaziah insists on battle.

segments.title: Jehoash's Death and Burial
segments.gist: The rest of Jehoash's acts and his burial in Samaria with the kings of Israel are recorded.

segments.title: Judah Defeated and Amaziah Killed
segments.gist: Jehoash defeats Judah, breaks down Jerusalem's wall, plunders the temple and palace, and later Amaziah is assassinated in Lachish; Azariah succeeds him.

segments.title: Jeroboam II's Reign in Israel
segments.gist: Jeroboam II becomes king of Israel, restores Israel's borders as God spoke through Jonah, and saves the nation despite its sins.

15.summary: This chapter records the reigns of several kings of Judah and Israel, including Azariah (Uzziah) of Judah, and a rapid succession of Israelite kings—Zechariah, Shallum, Menahem, Pekahiah, and Pekah—marked by conspiracy and violence. It also notes Jotham's reign in Judah and the beginning of Assyrian incursions under Tiglath-pileser.

segments.title: Azariah's Reign in Judah
segments.gist: Azariah (Uzziah) reigns 52 years in Judah, does right but fails to remove high places, and is struck with leprosy.

segments.title: Zechariah's Brief Reign in Israel
segments.gist: Zechariah son of Jeroboam reigns six months in Israel, does evil, and is killed by Shallum.

segments.title: Shallum and Menahem
segments.gist: Shallum reigns one month before Menahem kills him; Menahem then rules Israel brutally and pays tribute to Assyria.

segments.title: Menahem's Reign and Death
segments.gist: Menahem reigns ten years in Israel, does evil, and dies, leaving the throne to his son Pekahiah.

segments.title: Pekahiah and Pekah
segments.gist: Pekahiah reigns two years and is killed by Pekah, who then rules twenty years in Israel.

segments.title: Pekah's Reign and Hoshea's Conspiracy
segments.gist: Pekah reigns twenty years, does evil, and is killed by Hoshea, who becomes king in his place.

segments.title: Jotham's Reign in Judah
segments.gist: Jotham son of Uzziah reigns sixteen years in Judah, does right, builds the upper gate, and faces attacks from Rezin and Pekah.

16.summary: Ahaz becomes king of Judah and does evil, even sacrificing his son in the fire. When Rezin of Syria and Pekah of Israel attack, Ahaz appeals to Tiglath-pileser of Assyria for help and pays him with temple treasures. Ahaz then copies a Damascus altar in Jerusalem, alters the temple furnishings, and dies, succeeded by Hezekiah.

segments.title: Ahaz's evil reign begins
segments.gist: Ahaz becomes king at twenty and reigns sixteen years, doing evil, sacrificing his son, and worshiping at high places.

segments.title: Syria and Israel attack Judah
segments.gist: Rezin of Syria and Pekah of Israel besiege Ahaz but cannot overcome him, and Rezin recovers Elath for Syria.

segments.title: Ahaz appeals to Assyria
segments.gist: Ahaz sends messengers and temple and palace silver and gold to Tiglath-pileser, asking for help; Assyria attacks Damascus and kills Rezin.

segments.title: Ahaz copies Damascus altar
segments.gist: Ahaz sees an altar in Damascus and has Urijah the priest build a copy; Ahaz offers sacrifices on it and rearranges the temple furnishings.

segments.title: Ahaz strips temple and dies
segments.gist: Ahaz cuts off the temple bases and removes the laver, and he dies and is buried with his fathers; Hezekiah his son reigns.

17.summary: This chapter recounts the fall of the northern kingdom of Israel to Assyria because of the people's persistent idolatry and rejection of God's covenant. It describes how Hoshea became a vassal to Shalmaneser but rebelled, leading to Samaria's three-year siege and the deportation of Israel. The chapter then explains the reasons for the exile and tells how the Assyrian king resettled foreigners in Samaria, who mixed their own religions with a superficial worship of the LORD.

segments.title: Hoshea's Reign and Assyrian Conquest
segments.gist: Hoshea reigns in Israel and becomes a vassal to Shalmaneser of Assyria, but after seeking help from Egypt he rebels, prompting Assyria to besiege Samaria and deport Israel.

segments.title: Reasons for Israel's Exile
segments.gist: The narrator explains that Israel fell because they sinned against the LORD, worshiped other gods, followed pagan customs, and rejected the prophets' warnings.

segments.title: Judah's Continued Disobedience
segments.gist: Judah also failed to keep the LORD's commandments, imitating Israel's practices, so the LORD rejected all Israel and removed them from his presence.

segments.title: Foreigners Settle in Samaria
segments.gist: The king of Assyria brings people from other nations to live in Samaria; the LORD sends lions among them, and a priest is sent back to teach them how to worship the LORD.

segments.title: Mixed Worship of the Settlers
segments.gist: Each foreign group makes its own idols and sets them in the high places, while also fearing the LORD, resulting in a syncretistic religion.

segments.title: Covenant Warning and Continued Idolatry
segments.gist: The chapter recalls the LORD's covenant command to worship only him, but the settlers continue to fear the LORD while serving their own gods, a pattern that persists.

18.summary: Hezekiah becomes king of Judah and reforms the kingdom by removing idolatrous shrines and trusting in the LORD. In the fourteenth year of his reign, Sennacherib of Assyria invades Judah and captures its fortified cities; Hezekiah pays tribute from the temple and palace treasuries. The Assyrian Rabshakeh then confronts Jerusalem's officials with a speech urging the people to surrender, but the people remain silent as instructed.

segments.title: Hezekiah's Good Reign and Reforms
segments.gist: Hezekiah begins to reign at age 25, does right in God's eyes, removes high places and idols, and trusts in the LORD above all other kings of Judah.

segments.title: Assyria Captures Samaria
segments.gist: In Hezekiah's fourth year, Shalmaneser of Assyria besieges Samaria and captures it three years later, deporting Israel to Assyria because they disobeyed the LORD.

segments.title: Sennacherib Invades and Hezekiah Pays Tribute
segments.gist: In Hezekiah's fourteenth year, Sennacherib takes Judah's fortified cities, and Hezekiah pays him silver and gold from the temple and palace treasuries.

segments.title: Rabshakeh's First Speech
segments.gist: Sennacherib sends Rabshakeh to Jerusalem, who delivers a message urging Hezekiah not to trust in Egypt or the LORD, but to make peace and receive Assyrian provisions.

segments.title: Rabshakeh Addresses the People
segments.gist: Rabshakeh speaks directly to the people in Hebrew, warning that the LORD cannot deliver them, and the people remain silent; Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah report to Hezekiah with torn clothes.

19.summary: King Hezekiah of Judah, threatened by Sennacherib of Assyria, seeks the LORD in the temple and sends for the prophet Isaiah, who promises deliverance. Sennacherib sends a blasphemous letter, and Hezekiah spreads it before the LORD in prayer. Isaiah delivers God's oracle against Assyria, and that night the angel of the LORD kills 185,000 Assyrian soldiers; Sennacherib withdraws and is later killed by his sons.

segments.title: Hezekiah Seeks Isaiah's Counsel
segments.gist: Hezekiah mourns Sennacherib's threats, sends officials to Isaiah, and receives a promise that Assyria will fall.

segments.title: Sennacherib's Blasphemous Letter
segments.gist: Sennacherib sends a letter mocking trust in the LORD and boasting of Assyria's conquests over other nations.

segments.title: Hezekiah's Prayer in the Temple
segments.gist: Hezekiah spreads the letter before the LORD and prays for deliverance so all kingdoms may know the LORD alone is God.

segments.title: Isaiah's Oracle Against Assyria
segments.gist: Isaiah declares God's answer: the virgin daughter of Zion despises Assyria, who has mocked the Holy One of Israel.

segments.title: Sign and Promise of Deliverance
segments.gist: God gives a sign to Hezekiah and promises that the remnant of Judah will take root and that Assyria will not enter Jerusalem.

segments.title: Assyrian Army Destroyed; Sennacherib Killed
segments.gist: The angel of the LORD kills 185,000 Assyrians; Sennacherib withdraws and is later slain by his sons in Nineveh.

20.summary: Hezekiah falls gravely ill and is told by Isaiah to set his house in order, but after his prayer and weeping God grants him fifteen more years and a sign of the sundial going back ten degrees. Later, Hezekiah shows all his treasures to envoys from Babylon, and Isaiah prophesies that everything will be carried to Babylon, though peace will last in his days.

segments.title: Hezekiah's Illness and Prayer
segments.gist: Hezekiah is sick unto death; Isaiah tells him to set his house in order, but Hezekiah prays and weeps, and God promises to heal him and add fifteen years.

segments.title: Sign of the Sundial
segments.gist: Hezekiah asks for a sign, and Isaiah offers either the shadow to go forward or back ten degrees; Hezekiah chooses back, and God brings the shadow back ten degrees.

segments.title: Babylonian Envoys Visit
segments.gist: Berodach-baladan sends letters and a present to Hezekiah, who shows the envoys all his treasures and armoury.

segments.title: Isaiah's Prophecy of Exile
segments.gist: Isaiah tells Hezekiah that all his treasures and descendants will be carried to Babylon, and Hezekiah accepts the word as good because of peace in his days.

segments.title: Hezekiah's Death and Succession
segments.gist: The rest of Hezekiah's acts, including the pool and conduit, are recorded; he dies and his son Manasseh reigns.

21.summary: Manasseh becomes king of Judah at twelve and reigns fifty-five years, reversing his father Hezekiah's reforms by restoring high places, building altars to Baal and Asherah, and practicing child sacrifice, so that God declares judgment on Jerusalem and Judah. His son Amon reigns two years, follows the same evil, and is assassinated by his servants, after which the people kill the conspirators and make Josiah king.

segments.title: Manasseh's evil reign
segments.gist: Manasseh, aged twelve, reigns fifty-five years and rebuilds high places, altars to Baal, and Asherah, leading Judah into greater evil than the nations.

segments.title: Prophets announce judgment
segments.gist: God's prophets declare disaster on Jerusalem and Judah, measuring Samaria and wiping Jerusalem like a dish, because of Manasseh's sins.

segments.title: Manasseh's bloodshed and death
segments.gist: Manasseh sheds much innocent blood and is buried in his garden; his son Amon succeeds him.

segments.title: Amon's evil reign
segments.gist: Amon reigns two years in Jerusalem, does evil like his father, forsakes the LORD, and serves idols.

segments.title: Amon assassinated; Josiah king
segments.gist: Amon's servants kill him, the people execute the conspirators, and Amon's son Josiah becomes king.

22.summary: Josiah becomes king of Judah at age eight and reigns righteously. In his eighteenth year he sends Shaphan to repair the temple, and Hilkiah the high priest finds the book of the law. When the king hears it read, he tears his clothes and sends a delegation to the prophetess Huldah, who declares that disaster will come on the nation but that Josiah himself will die in peace because of his humble response.

segments.title: Josiah's righteous reign begins
segments.gist: Josiah becomes king at eight years old and does right in the sight of the LORD, walking in David's ways.

segments.title: Josiah orders temple repairs
