segments.gist: In his eighteenth year Josiah sends Shaphan to Hilkiah to count the temple money and pay the workmen repairing the LORD's house.

segments.title: Book of the law found and read
segments.gist: Hilkiah tells Shaphan he has found the book of the law in the temple; Shaphan reads it to King Josiah.

segments.title: King sends men to inquire of LORD
segments.gist: Josiah tears his clothes and sends Hilkiah, Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan, and Asaiah to the prophetess Huldah to inquire about the words of the book.

segments.title: Huldah's prophecy of judgment and mercy
segments.gist: Huldah says the LORD will bring disaster on Judah for forsaking him, but because Josiah humbled himself, he will be gathered to his grave in peace.

23.summary: King Josiah gathers Judah and reads the book of the law to them, renews the covenant, and destroys idolatrous shrines and priests throughout Judah and Samaria. He reinstitutes the Passover, but God's anger over Manasseh's sins remains. Josiah is killed by Pharaoh Necho at Megiddo, and his sons Jehoahaz and Jehoiakim reign in succession, with Jehoiakim's reign marked by evil.

segments.title: Josiah Reads the Law
segments.gist: King Josiah gathers all Judah to hear the book of the law read, and he renews the covenant before the LORD.

segments.title: Josiah Destroys Idolatry
segments.gist: Josiah removes idolatrous vessels, priests, high places, and altars throughout Judah and Samaria, fulfilling the prophecy.

segments.title: Passover Reinstituted
segments.gist: Josiah commands the people to keep the Passover, and such a Passover had not been kept since the judges.

segments.title: God's Wrath Remains
segments.gist: Josiah cleanses Judah, but God's anger over Manasseh's sins persists, and He decrees Judah's removal.

segments.title: Josiah Killed at Megiddo
segments.gist: Pharaoh Necho kills Josiah at Megiddo, and his son Jehoahaz is made king.

segments.title: Jehoahaz and Jehoiakim
segments.gist: Jehoahaz reigns wickedly and is imprisoned by Pharaoh, who makes Jehoiakim king; Jehoiakim also does evil.

24.summary: Jehoiakim becomes a vassal of Nebuchadnezzar but rebels, so Babylon sends raiders against Judah; Jehoiakim dies and his son Jehoiachin reigns. Jehoiachin surrenders to Babylon, which carries away the temple treasures and the leading people, and Zedekiah is installed as a puppet king who also rebels.

segments.title: Jehoiakim's Vassalage and Rebellion
segments.gist: Nebuchadnezzar makes Jehoiakim his servant, but Jehoiakim rebels, prompting Babylonian, Syrian, Moabite, and Ammonite raids against Judah.

segments.title: Jehoiakim's Death and Burial
segments.gist: The rest of Jehoiakim's acts are recorded, and he dies and is buried with his fathers; his son Jehoiachin succeeds him.

segments.title: Jehoiachin Surrenders to Babylon
segments.gist: Jehoiachin reigns three months, does evil, and surrenders to Nebuchadnezzar, who takes him captive along with his family and officials.

segments.title: Temple Treasures and Exiles Taken
segments.gist: Nebuchadnezzar carries off the temple treasures and deports all Jerusalem's leaders, warriors, craftsmen, and smiths, leaving only the poorest.

segments.title: Zedekiah's Reign and Rebellion
segments.gist: Nebuchadnezzar makes Mattaniah king as Zedekiah, who does evil and rebels against Babylon, provoking the final siege.

25.summary: Nebuchadnezzar besieges Jerusalem, causing famine; Zedekiah flees but is captured, his sons killed, and he is blinded. Nebuzaradan burns the temple and city and carries most people into exile, leaving only the poor. Gedaliah is appointed governor but is assassinated, and the remaining people flee to Egypt. The chapter ends with Jehoiachin released from prison in Babylon.

segments.title: Siege and Zedekiah's Capture
segments.gist: Nebuchadnezzar besieges Jerusalem; famine strikes; Zedekiah flees but is captured, his sons slain, and he is blinded and taken to Babylon.

segments.title: Temple and City Burned
segments.gist: Nebuzaradan burns the temple, palace, and houses of Jerusalem and carries the people captive, leaving only the poorest.

segments.title: Officials Executed at Riblah
segments.gist: The chief priest, officers, and others are taken to Riblah and executed by order of the king of Babylon.

segments.title: Gedaliah Made Governor
segments.gist: Gedaliah is appointed governor over the remnant; he advises submission, but Ishmael assassinates him and the people flee to Egypt.

segments.title: Jehoiachin Released
segments.gist: Evilmerodach king of Babylon releases Jehoiachin from prison and grants him a place of honor among the captive kings.

1.summary: The book opens with a genealogical record from Adam through the sons of Israel, then traces the descendants of Judah down to the family of Caleb, and closes with a list of Caleb's descendants and the line of Jerahmeel.

segments.title: Adam to Noah's sons
segments.gist: The lineage from Adam through Seth, Enosh, Kenan, Mahalalel, Jared, Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech, and Noah, naming Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

segments.title: Japheth's descendants
segments.gist: The sons of Japheth and their descendants, including the coastlands peoples.

segments.title: Ham's descendants
segments.gist: The sons of Ham, including Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan, with Nimrod and the Philistine lines.

segments.title: Shem's descendants
segments.gist: The sons of Shem down to Abraham, and the sons of Abraham's concubines.

segments.title: Abraham to Israel
segments.gist: The line from Shem to Abraham and then through Isaac to Esau and Israel.

segments.title: Judah's descendants
segments.gist: The sons of Judah and the descendants of Perez, Hezron, and Caleb, including the families of Jerahmeel and Caleb's daughter Achsah.

2.summary: This chapter records the sons of Israel, with a focus on Judah's line down to the family of Caleb and the descendants of Jerahmeel. It traces genealogies through Boaz to David and lists the sons of Caleb and the line of Sheshan, closing with the descendants of Caleb's daughter Achsah.

segments.title: Sons of Israel
segments.gist: Lists the twelve sons of Israel, from Reuben to Benjamin and Joseph.

segments.title: Judah's sons and Tamar's
segments.gist: Records the sons of Judah by his wives and the sons born to him by Tamar.

segments.title: Hezron's descendants to David
segments.gist: Traces the line from Hezron through Ram, Amminadab, Nahshon, Salmon, Boaz, Obed, Jesse, and David.

segments.title: Caleb and Hezron's line
segments.gist: Lists the descendants of Caleb son of Hezron and the sons of Hezron by Ephrath and Abiah.

segments.title: Jerahmeel's descendants
segments.gist: Details the sons and descendants of Jerahmeel, including the line through Sheshan and Jether.

segments.title: Caleb's descendants and families
segments.gist: Records the sons of Caleb and the families of scribes and Kenites connected to Judah.

3.summary: This chapter records the descendants of David, beginning with his sons born in Hebron and Jerusalem, then tracing the royal line through Solomon down to the exile and beyond, ending with the sons of Jeconiah and the line to Anani.

segments.title: David's sons born in Hebron and Jerusalem
segments.gist: Lists David's six sons born in Hebron and his sons born in Jerusalem, including Solomon and others by various wives.

segments.title: Kings of Judah from Solomon to Zedekiah
segments.gist: Traces the royal line of Judah from Solomon through the kings down to Zedekiah and his sons.

segments.title: Descendants after the exile to Anani
segments.gist: Records the sons of Jeconiah after the captivity and the line through Pedaiah to Zerubbabel and down to Anani.

4.summary: 1 Chronicles 4 continues the genealogies of Judah, listing descendants of Judah through Pharez, Hezron, and Caleb, along with the families of Ashur, Jabez, and others. It includes Jabez's prayer and God's answer, and concludes with the descendants of Simeon and their territorial expansion.

segments.title: Judah's Descendants and Jabez's Prayer
segments.gist: Genealogy of Judah's sons and descendants, including Jabez who prayed for blessing and God granted his request.

segments.title: Descendants of Caleb and Others
segments.gist: Lists the families of Chelub, Caleb son of Hur, and others, with their sons and trades.

segments.title: Descendants of Shelah
segments.gist: Records the sons of Shelah and their families, including those who worked as potters and lived in the king's service.

segments.title: Simeon's Descendants and Conquests
segments.gist: Genealogy of Simeon's sons and their cities, and their victories over the Hamites and Amalekites.

5.summary: This chapter records the genealogies of Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh east of the Jordan, noting Reuben's loss of birthright to Joseph's sons. It recounts their war against the Hagrites, their cry to God in battle, and their subsequent captivity by Tiglath-pileser for unfaithfulness.

segments.title: Reuben's genealogy and birthright loss
segments.gist: Reuben's descendants are listed, with a note that his birthright was given to Joseph because he defiled his father's bed.

segments.title: Gad's genealogy and chiefs
segments.gist: The descendants of Gad are recorded with their chiefs and families during the reigns of Jotham and Jeroboam.

segments.title: War against the Hagrites
segments.gist: The Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh defeat the Hagrites, crying to God in battle, and occupy their land.

segments.title: Manasseh's half-tribe and exile
segments.gist: The half-tribe of Manasseh east of the Jordan is described, and because of their unfaithfulness God stirs up Tiglath-pileser to carry them into captivity.

6.summary: This chapter records the Levitical genealogies, tracing the lines of Levi's sons—Gershon, Kohath, and Merari—with special emphasis on the priestly descent from Aaron through Eleazar to the Babylonian exile. It also lists the Levitical cities allotted to the clans and the cities of refuge, concluding with the genealogies of the singers and other Levites.

segments.title: Levi's Sons and High Priests
segments.gist: The sons of Levi are listed, and the high priestly line is traced from Aaron through Eleazar to the exile.

segments.title: Levitical Clans and Musicians
segments.gist: The families of Gershon, Kohath, and Merari are recorded, including the singers Heman, Asaph, and Ethan.

segments.title: Duties and Aaron's Descendants
segments.gist: The duties of the Levites in the tabernacle are described, and the descendants of Aaron are listed.

segments.title: Aaron's Priestly Line
segments.gist: The high priests descended from Aaron are listed through Ahimaaz and beyond.

segments.title: Levitical Cities and Refuge
segments.gist: The cities allotted to the Levites, including the cities of refuge, are recorded by clan.

7.summary: 1 Chronicles 7 lists the descendants and clan totals of six northern tribes: Issachar, Benjamin, Naphtali, Manasseh, Ephraim, and Asher. The chapter records genealogies, family heads, and fighting men, with brief notices of Ephraim's sons and the founding of cities.

segments.title: Issachar's Descendants
segments.gist: The sons and clans of Issachar are listed with their valiant men of war numbered by genealogy.

segments.title: Benjamin's Descendants
segments.gist: The sons of Benjamin and their descendants are recorded, including heads of fathers' houses and mighty men.

segments.title: Manasseh's Descendants
segments.gist: The descendants of Manasseh through his concubine and other lines are recorded.

segments.title: Ephraim's Descendants
segments.gist: Ephraim's sons and the story of their deaths and the founding of cities are given.

segments.title: Asher's Descendants
segments.gist: The sons of Asher and their family heads, choice men, and mighty men of war are listed.

8.summary: This chapter records the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, tracing the descendants of Benjamin through several family lines, with special attention to the house of Saul. It lists heads of fathers' houses and noted warriors, concluding with the lineage of Saul and his sons.

segments.title: Benjamin's sons and early descendants
segments.gist: Lists the sons of Benjamin and the descendants of Bela, including heads of fathers' houses and mighty men.

segments.title: Descendants of Shaharaim
segments.gist: Records the sons of Shaharaim by his wives Hushim and Baara, and the descendants of Elpaal.

segments.title: Families of Elpaal and others
segments.gist: Continues the genealogy through the sons of Elpaal, Beriah, and Shema, listing heads of fathers' houses.

segments.title: Gibeon and the house of Saul
segments.gist: Names the father of Gibeon and his sons, including Ner and Kish, leading to Saul's line.

segments.title: Saul's descendants
segments.gist: Lists the sons of Saul and the descendants of Jonathan and Micah, ending with many mighty men.

9.summary: 1 Chronicles 9 lists the returned exiles and their genealogies, focusing on the inhabitants of Jerusalem, especially the priests, Levites, and gatekeepers. It details the duties of the gatekeepers and other Levites, and concludes with the genealogy of Saul, leading into the account of his death.

segments.title: Genealogies of Returned Exiles
segments.gist: The chapter opens with genealogies of Israel and focuses on the residents of Jerusalem, including Judahites, Benjamites, Ephraimites, and Manassehites.

segments.title: Priests in Jerusalem
segments.gist: Lists the priests who lived in Jerusalem, including Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, Jachin, and Azariah, with their duties.

segments.title: Levites and Temple Servants
segments.gist: Names Levites and temple servants residing in Jerusalem, including Shemaiah, Mattaniah, and Obadiah.

segments.title: Gatekeepers and Their Duties
segments.gist: Describes the gatekeepers, their genealogies, and their responsibilities for guarding the thresholds of the tabernacle and later the temple.

segments.title: Other Levite Duties
segments.gist: Details the duties of other Levites over the utensils, fine flour, oil, and other items, and lists the singers and their families.

segments.title: Genealogy of Saul
segments.gist: Records the genealogy of Saul from Jeiel of Gibeon down to his descendants, setting the stage for the account of his reign.

10.summary: 1 Chronicles 10 recounts the defeat of Israel by the Philistines on Mount Gilboa, the deaths of Saul and his sons, and the disrespect shown to Saul's body. It concludes by explaining that Saul died for his trespass against the LORD, specifically for consulting a medium instead of seeking the LORD.

segments.title: Philistines Defeat Israel and Saul
segments.gist: The Philistines battle Israel, kill Saul's sons, and severely wound Saul, who then falls on his own sword.

segments.title: Philistines Desecrate Saul's Body
segments.gist: The Philistines strip Saul, cut off his head, and fasten his body to the wall of Bethshan.

segments.title: Jabesh-gilead Recovers and Buries Bones
segments.gist: Men of Jabesh-gilead retrieve the bodies of Saul and his sons, bury their bones, and fasten a week.

segments.title: Saul's Death Explained
segments.gist: Saul died for his trespass against the LORD, for consulting a medium and not seeking the LORD.

11.summary: The chapter recounts David's anointing as king over all Israel at Hebron and his capture of Jerusalem from the Jebusites, making it his capital. It then lists David's mighty men and highlights three of their exploits, including the drawing of water from the well of Bethlehem.

segments.title: David Anointed King Over Israel
segments.gist: All Israel gathers at Hebron, anoints David king, and he reigns over all Israel.

segments.title: David Captures Jerusalem
segments.gist: David and Israel march to Jerusalem, defeat the Jebusites, and David makes the city his capital.

segments.title: David's Mighty Men Listed
segments.gist: The chief of David's mighty men are listed with their exploits, including Jashobeam and Eleazar.

segments.title: Three Mighty Men Fetch Water
segments.gist: Three mighty men break through the Philistine camp to fetch water from Bethlehem for David, who pours it out to the Lord.

segments.title: Abishai and Benaiah's Exploits
segments.gist: Abishai and Benaiah are praised for their mighty deeds, including Benaiah's slaying of a lion and an Egyptian giant.

segments.title: The Thirty Mighty Men
segments.gist: A list of the thirty mighty men who served David, including Uriah the Hittite.

12.summary: This chapter records the warriors who joined David at Ziklag while he was still avoiding Saul, along with their tribes and numbers, and later the armed men from all Israel who came to Hebron to make David king over all Israel.

segments.title: Benjamite warriors join David at Ziklag
segments.gist: While David was at Ziklag hiding from Saul, Benjaminite kinsmen came to him as mighty helpers in battle.

segments.title: Gadite warriors join David
segments.gist: Men of Gad, skilled warriors and captains, crossed the Jordan to join David in the stronghold.

segments.title: Benjamin and Judah meet David
segments.gist: Men from Benjamin and Judah came to David, and he questioned their loyalty; Amasai answered by the Spirit.

segments.title: Manassite captains defect to David
segments.gist: Some Manassite captains defected to David when he went with the Philistines, and they helped him against raiders.

segments.title: Numbers of armed men at Hebron
segments.gist: The chapter lists the numbers of armed men from each tribe who came to Hebron to make David king.

segments.title: Israel celebrates David's kingship
segments.gist: All the warriors came to Hebron with a perfect heart to make David king, and they held a great feast.

13.summary: David consults his leaders and gathers all Israel to bring the ark of God from Kiriath-jearim to Jerusalem. They transport it on a new cart with celebration, but when Uzzah touches the ark to steady it, God strikes him dead. David is angry and afraid, so the ark is left at the house of Obed-edom, where it blesses his household.

segments.title: David consults and gathers Israel
segments.gist: David seeks the approval of his commanders and all Israel to bring the ark back, and they agree.

segments.title: Ark brought from Kiriath-jearim
segments.gist: David and all Israel bring the ark from Kiriath-jearim on a new cart, celebrating with music and song.

segments.title: Uzzah struck dead; David afraid
segments.gist: Uzzah touches the ark to steady it and God strikes him dead; David is angry and afraid, and leaves the ark at Obed-edom's house.

segments.title: Ark blesses Obed-edom's house
segments.gist: The ark remains at Obed-edom's house for three months, and God blesses his household and all he has.

14.summary: David is anointed king over all Israel and gathers an army. He defeats the Philistines twice, first at Baalperazim and then at the mulberry trees, and his fame spreads. The chapter also lists the children born to him in Jerusalem and records that the ark was not mentioned in this campaign.

segments.title: David Anointed King Over Israel
segments.gist: David is anointed king over all Israel, and he gathers an army to secure his rule.

segments.title: David's Children Born in Jerusalem
segments.gist: A list of the sons born to David in Jerusalem, including Nathan, Solomon, and others.

segments.title: Victory at Baalperazim
segments.gist: The Philistines attack, and David defeats them at Baalperazim, declaring God has broken through.

segments.title: Second Victory Over Philistines
segments.gist: The Philistines attack again, and David follows God's direction to strike them from the mulberry trees, spreading his fame.

15.summary: David prepares a place for the ark in Jerusalem and gathers the Levites, instructing them to carry it properly after the earlier breach. The Levites and singers bring the ark up with music and sacrifice, and it is set in the tent David pitched, with Michal watching from a window.

segments.title: David prepares a place for the ark
segments.gist: David pitches a tent for the ark in the city of David and assembles all Israel to bring it up.

segments.title: Levites gathered and instructed
segments.gist: David gathers the sons of Aaron and the Levites and tells them to sanctify themselves to carry the ark.

segments.title: Levites carry the ark properly
segments.gist: The Levites sanctify themselves and carry the ark on their shoulders with staves, as Moses commanded.

segments.title: Singers and musicians appointed
segments.gist: David appoints Levite singers and musicians with instruments to play as the ark is brought up.

segments.title: Ark brought up with music and sacrifice
segments.gist: David, the elders, and the captains bring the ark with shouting, trumpets, and sacrifices.

16.summary: After the ark is placed in the tent David prepared, David offers burnt and peace offerings and distributes food to the people. He appoints Levites to minister before the ark with music and thanksgiving, and gives a psalm of praise recounting God's covenant and mighty acts. The chapter closes with the establishment of regular worship at Gibeon and Jerusalem, including priests, singers, and gatekeepers.

segments.title: Ark placed and offerings made
segments.gist: David places the ark in the tent, offers sacrifices, blesses the people, and gives each Israelite bread, meat, and wine.

segments.title: Psalm of thanksgiving begins
segments.gist: David appoints Asaph and his brothers to thank the Lord, singing of His wonderful works and covenant with Israel.

segments.title: Psalm calls all nations to praise
segments.gist: The psalm continues, calling all the earth to praise God's glory, declaring His reign, and ending with a blessing and Amen.

segments.title: Levites appointed for regular worship
segments.gist: David assigns Asaph and his brothers to minister daily before the ark, and Obed-edom and others as gatekeepers; he also establishes worship at Gibeon.

17.summary: David, settled in his palace, proposes to build a permanent temple for the ark, but the prophet Nathan first approves and then, after a night vision from God, reverses his counsel. God's covenant through Nathan promises David an everlasting dynasty and a future son who will build the house, prompting David's humble prayer of thanksgiving and praise.

segments.title: David proposes building a temple
segments.gist: David tells Nathan the prophet that he lives in a cedar house while the ark remains under curtains, and Nathan initially approves.

segments.title: God's covenant through Nathan
segments.gist: That night God speaks to Nathan, declining a house from David and promising instead to establish David's dynasty and a son who will build God's house.

segments.title: David's prayer of praise
segments.gist: David sits before the Lord and prays, marveling at God's greatness and recalling what God has done for Israel.

segments.title: David asks for covenant confirmation
segments.gist: David pleads with God to confirm forever the promise made to his house, expressing trust that God's blessing is eternal.

18.summary: David defeats the Philistines, Moabites, Zobah, and Syrians, and secures Israel's borders. He dedicates the spoils to the LORD and administers justice with a list of his chief officials.

segments.title: David Defeats Philistines and Moabites
segments.gist: David smites the Philistines and subdues Moab, and the Moabites become his servants.

segments.title: David Defeats Zobah and Syrians
segments.gist: David defeats Hadadezer of Zobah and the Syrians, taking chariots, horses, and shields.

segments.title: Toi Sends Gifts; David Dedicates Spoils
segments.gist: King Toi sends gifts through Joram, and David dedicates the spoils to the LORD.

segments.title: David's Officials Listed
segments.gist: David reigns over Israel and his chief officials are listed, including Joab and Jehoshaphat.

19.summary: David sends messengers to comfort Hanun, king of Ammon, after his father's death, but Hanun's princes suspect them as spies and humiliate them. When Ammon hires Syrian chariots and armies, David's forces under Joab and Abishai defeat them, and David's army also defeats the Syrians who regroup, bringing them into subjection.

segments.title: David's Messengers Humiliated
segments.gist: David sends servants to comfort Hanun for his father's death, but Hanun's princes accuse them of spying and shame them by shaving and cutting their garments.

segments.title: Ammon Hires Syrian Forces
segments.gist: The Ammonites hire chariots and horsemen from Syria and gather their army at Medeba, prompting David to send Joab with his mighty men.

segments.title: Joab Defeats the Syrians
segments.gist: Joab divides his forces, faces the Syrians and Ammonites, and after a rallying speech, the Syrians flee and the Ammonites retreat into the city.

segments.title: Syrians Defeated Again
segments.gist: The Syrians regroup under Shophach but are defeated by David, who kills many and subdues them, and they make peace with Israel.

20.summary: After the spring campaign when Joab besieged Rabbah, David remained in Jerusalem; Joab captured the city and David took the Ammonite crown and subjected the people to forced labor. Subsequent battles against the Philistines at Gezer saw David's men kill the giants Sippai, Lahmi (Goliath's brother), and a huge man with six fingers and six toes.

segments.title: Siege and Capture of Rabbah
segments.gist: Joab leads the siege of Rabbah while David stays in Jerusalem; Joab captures the city and calls David to take the spoil.

segments.title: Philistine Giants Slain
segments.gist: Battles at Gezer and Gob result in the deaths of Philistine giants: Sippai, Lahmi the brother of Goliath, and a man with twenty-four fingers and toes.

21.summary: Satan incites David to number Israel, and Joab reluctantly carries out the census. God offers David a choice of punishments, and David chooses a plague that kills seventy thousand. As the angel stretches out his hand over Jerusalem, God relents, and David builds an altar on the threshing floor of Ornan, where the plague is stayed.

segments.title: David's Census and Joab's Objection
segments.gist: Satan prompts David to number Israel; Joab protests but obeys, and the count is taken.

segments.title: God's Displeasure and David's Confession
segments.gist: God is displeased with the census, and David confesses his sin and asks for forgiveness.

segments.title: Gad Offers Three Punishments
segments.gist: The prophet Gad presents David with three choices of punishment from God.

segments.title: Plague and the Angel over Jerusalem
segments.gist: A pestilence kills seventy thousand; as the angel threatens Jerusalem, God relents and David pleads for his people.

segments.title: David Builds an Altar on Ornan's Threshing Floor
segments.gist: At Gad's command, David buys Ornan's threshing floor and offers burnt and peace offerings, and the plague is stayed.

segments.title: David Sacrifices There
segments.gist: David continues to sacrifice at the threshing floor because he fears the angel's sword at Gibeon's altar.

22.summary: David gathers materials and workers for building the temple and charges Solomon with the task, praying that God will give him understanding and help him complete it.

segments.title: David Prepares Temple Materials
segments.gist: David declares the temple is for God and assembles stonecutters, iron, brass, cedar, and gold and silver in abundance.

segments.title: David Charges Solomon to Build
segments.gist: David calls Solomon and commands him to build the house of the LORD, promising God's presence and peace.

segments.title: David Prays for Solomon
segments.gist: David blesses Solomon and prays that God will give him wisdom and understanding to keep the law and build the temple.

segments.title: David's Great Provision
segments.gist: David recounts the vast amounts of gold, silver, brass, iron, and timber he has prepared for the temple.

segments.title: David Commands Leaders to Help
segments.gist: David commands all the princes and leaders of Israel to help Solomon and to set their hearts to seek the LORD.

23.summary: David, now old, makes Solomon king over Israel and gathers all the leaders to organize the Levites for temple service. He numbers the Levites from thirty years old and assigns them their duties, dividing them into families and orders for the work of the house of the Lord.

segments.title: David Makes Solomon King
segments.gist: David, old and full of days, makes his son Solomon king over Israel and gathers the princes, priests, and Levites.

segments.title: Numbering and Division of Levites
segments.gist: The Levites from thirty years old are numbered, and David assigns them roles: overseers, officers, judges, gatekeepers, and singers.

segments.title: Duties of Gershon, Kohath, and Merari
segments.gist: David divides the Levites into the families of Gershon, Kohath, and Merari, listing their descendants and their assigned duties.

segments.title: Levites Numbered from Twenty Years
segments.gist: The Levites are numbered from twenty years old and upward, as David's final instructions before his death.

segments.title: Levites' Service in the Temple
segments.gist: The Levites are to assist the priests in the temple, handling showbread, fine flour, and instruments of service.

24.summary: 1 Chronicles 24 records the division of the sons of Aaron into twenty-four priestly courses by lot, with the heads of the families listed. It also describes the corresponding twenty-four courses of the Levites, including the families of Kohath, Merari, and the singers, all organized under David's direction.

segments.title: Divisions of Aaron's Sons
segments.gist: The sons of Aaron are divided into twenty-four courses by lot, with the heads of the families listed.

segments.title: Twenty-Four Priestly Courses
segments.gist: The twenty-four courses of priests are selected by lot, each with its designated head.

segments.title: Levite Courses by Lot
segments.gist: The remaining Levites, including Kohathites and Merarites, are also divided by lot into twenty-four courses.

25.summary: David, with the captains of the army, sets apart the sons of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun to prophesy with harps, psalteries, and cymbals. The chapter lists the twenty-four courses of musicians, each of twelve men, who serve in the house of the LORD, and records the casting of lots to assign their order.

segments.title: Musicians Set Apart for Service
segments.gist: David and the army captains separate the sons of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun, who prophesy with instruments, totaling 288 trained singers.

segments.title: Twenty-Four Courses by Lot
segments.gist: Lots are cast for the twenty-four courses of musicians, each course consisting of twelve men, with their names and order listed.

26.summary: 1 Chronicles 26 organizes the Levite gatekeepers by their divisions and assignments, lists the responsibilities of the treasuries and other officials, and describes the appointment of officers, judges, and scribes for both sacred and civil duties.

segments.title: Gatekeeper Divisions and Assignments
segments.gist: The Korahite and Merarite gatekeepers are listed by family and assigned their gates by lot.

segments.title: Gates Assigned by Lot
segments.gist: The gates are assigned by lot to specific families, including the east, north, south, and west gates and the storehouse.

segments.title: Treasuries and Dedicated Gifts
segments.gist: Levites are put in charge of the treasuries of the house of God and the dedicated gifts from David and the commanders.

segments.title: Officers, Judges, and Scribes
segments.gist: From the Izharites and Hebronites, officers and judges are appointed for civil affairs and for the Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh.

27.summary: 1 Chronicles 27 lists the monthly military divisions of Israel, each of 24,000 men led by a named commander, followed by the tribal leaders, the overseers of the king's treasuries and properties, and David's personal counselors. The chapter closes with David's private advisors and the keeper of his herds.

segments.title: Monthly military divisions
segments.gist: The twelve monthly courses of 24,000 soldiers, each with its commanding officer, are listed in order.

segments.title: Tribal leaders of Israel
segments.gist: The chiefs who governed each tribe of Israel are named, from Reuben to Naphtali.

segments.title: Overseers of David's property
segments.gist: Officials in charge of the king's treasuries, fields, vineyards, olive trees, herds, and camels are listed.

segments.title: David's counselors and officials
segments.gist: David's uncle Jonathan, Ahithophel, Hushai, and Joab are named as counselors and army commander.

28.summary: David assembles all the leaders of Israel in Jerusalem and declares that Solomon, his son, is chosen by God to build the temple, though David himself was not permitted to do so. He hands over the plans for the temple and its furnishings, charges Solomon to be strong and faithful, and prays that God will give Solomon a perfect heart to keep the commandments and build the house of the LORD.

segments.title: David's Assembly and Temple Declaration
segments.gist: David gathers Israel's officials and announces that God has chosen Solomon to build the temple, though David was denied that privilege because of his wars.

segments.title: Charge to Solomon
segments.gist: David charges Solomon to know and serve God with a perfect heart, warning that God searches all hearts and will be found if sought.

segments.title: Plans for the Temple Given
segments.gist: David gives Solomon the detailed plans for the temple, its courts, chambers, and golden furnishings, which he received by the Spirit.

segments.title: Exhortation to Courage
segments.gist: David encourages Solomon and the assembly to be strong and courageous, assuring them that God will not fail or forsake them until all the work is finished.

29.summary: David gathers Israel's leaders and officials, announces that Solomon is chosen to build the temple, and appeals for freewill offerings; the people give generously, and David offers a public prayer of praise and thanksgiving. The next day they sacrifice and feast, anoint Solomon as king, and the chapter closes with David's death and a summary of his reign.

segments.title: David's Charge and Temple Provision
segments.gist: David addresses the assembly, declares Solomon as God's chosen builder, and recounts the preparations and materials gathered for the temple.

segments.title: David's Prayer of Praise
segments.gist: David blesses the LORD before the congregation, exalting His sovereignty and acknowledging that all wealth and honor come from Him.

segments.title: People's Offerings and Rejoicing
segments.gist: The assembly responds with wholehearted freewill offerings, and David and all the people rejoice greatly over the willing gifts.

segments.title: Solomon Anointed and David's Death
segments.gist: They sacrifice and feast, anoint Solomon as king, and the chapter concludes with David's death and a summary of his reign.

1.summary: Solomon travels to Gibeon, where the tabernacle and bronze altar are, and offers a thousand burnt offerings. That night God appears to him and grants him wisdom and knowledge, along with riches and honor because he asked for wisdom rather than wealth. The chapter closes with Solomon's chariots and horsemen and his trade in horses and chariots with Egypt and other lands.

segments.title: Solomon worships at Gibeon
segments.gist: Solomon gathers Israel and goes to Gibeon to seek the LORD at the tabernacle and bronze altar, offering a thousand burnt offerings.

segments.title: God grants Solomon wisdom
segments.gist: God appears to Solomon, promises him wisdom and knowledge because he asked for them, and adds riches and honor.

segments.title: Solomon's chariots and horse trade
segments.gist: Solomon accumulates chariots and horsemen and imports horses and chariots from Egypt and other lands.

2.summary: Solomon assembles Israel's leaders and brings the ark of the covenant into the newly completed temple, placing it in the most holy place under the wings of the cherubims. As the priests and singers praise God, a cloud fills the house, signifying the LORD's presence, and Solomon blesses the people and recounts God's faithfulness in choosing Jerusalem and David's line.

segments.title: Ark Brought into Temple
segments.gist: Solomon gathers Israel's elders and priests to carry the ark and holy vessels into the temple, placing the ark in the most holy place.

segments.title: Cloud Fills the House
segments.gist: As the priests and singers unite in praise, a cloud fills the temple, and the priests cannot stand to minister because of the glory.

segments.title: Solomon Blesses the Assembly
segments.gist: Solomon blesses the congregation and recounts how God fulfilled His promise to David by allowing him to build the temple.

3.summary: 2 Chronicles 3 describes Solomon's construction of the temple in Jerusalem, beginning with the site on Mount Moriah and the dimensions of the building. It details the materials, the inner sanctuary with its cherubim, and the two pillars set up before the temple.

segments.title: Temple site and dimensions
segments.gist: Solomon begins building the temple on Mount Moriah, giving its length and width.

segments.title: Porch and main hall
segments.gist: The porch and the main hall are described with their dimensions and gold overlay.

segments.title: Most holy house
segments.gist: The inner sanctuary is built and overlaid with fine gold.

segments.title: Two cherubim
segments.gist: Two cherubim of image work are made and placed in the most holy house.

segments.title: Two pillars
segments.gist: Two pillars are set before the temple and named Jachin and Boaz.

4.summary: This chapter describes the furnishings Solomon made for the temple: the bronze altar, the molten sea and its oxen supports, the ten lavers and their stands, the golden lampstands and tables, the courts, and the vessels of gold and bronze. It concludes by listing the items Hiram made for King Solomon and noting their placement in the house of God.

segments.title: Altar and Molten Sea
segments.gist: Solomon makes a bronze altar and a large molten sea resting on twelve oxen, holding water for the priests.

segments.title: Lampstands, Tables, and Courts
segments.gist: He makes ten golden lampstands, ten tables, and the courts with doors overlaid with brass.

segments.title: Hiram's Bronze Work
segments.gist: Hiram makes pots, shovels, basins, and the lavers with their stands for King Solomon's temple.

segments.title: Casting in the Jordan Plain
segments.gist: The bronze items are cast in the clay ground of the Jordan plain in such abundance that the weight is not recorded.

segments.title: Golden Vessels and Doors
segments.gist: Solomon makes the golden altar, tables, lampstands, flowers, lamps, tongs, and the golden entry doors.

5.summary: Solomon assembles Israel's elders and the people to bring the ark of the covenant from the city of David up to the newly completed temple. The priests and Levites carry the ark and the holy vessels into the most holy place, and when the ark is set down, the glory of the Lord fills the house so that the priests cannot stand to minister.

segments.title: Solomon gathers Israel to bring up the ark
segments.gist: Solomon assembles the elders and heads of tribes at Jerusalem to bring the ark from Zion to the temple.

segments.title: Priests and Levites carry the ark
segments.gist: The Levites carry the ark and the tabernacle vessels, and Solomon and the congregation sacrifice sheep and oxen without number.

segments.title: Ark placed in the most holy place
segments.gist: The priests set the ark in the inner sanctuary under the cherubim's wings, containing only the two tables of stone.

segments.title: The glory fills the house
segments.gist: As the priests and singers praise together, the cloud fills the house and the priests cannot stand to minister because of the glory.

6.summary: Solomon addresses the assembled Israelites at the dedication of the temple, declaring that God has fulfilled his promise to David by choosing Jerusalem and establishing a house for his name. He then offers a long prayer of dedication, confessing God's uniqueness and faithfulness, and asking God to hear the prayers of his people, including foreigners and those who sin, from this temple.

segments.title: Solomon blesses the assembly
segments.gist: Solomon blesses the congregation, recalls God's promise to David, and declares that he has built the temple for God's name.

segments.title: Solomon's opening prayer
segments.gist: Solomon kneels before the altar and prays, affirming God's uniqueness and faithfulness in fulfilling his promise to David.

segments.title: Prayer for God's presence
segments.gist: Solomon asks whether God will dwell on earth, and pleads that God hear the prayers directed toward the temple.

segments.title: Prayers for justice and forgiveness
segments.gist: Solomon asks God to judge between his people, to forgive them when they sin and turn back, and to teach them the good way.

segments.title: Prayer for foreigners and battles
segments.gist: Solomon prays that foreigners who come to the temple may be heard, and that God may support Israel in battle.

segments.title: Prayer for repentance and restoration
segments.gist: Solomon asks God to forgive and restore his people when they sin and repent, and closes by asking God to remember his mercies to David.

7.summary: After Solomon finishes praying and fire falls from heaven to consume the offerings, God's glory fills the temple and the people worship. God appears to Solomon at night, promising to hear and heal a humbled people, warning against apostasy, and establishing Solomon's throne if he obeys. The chapter closes with Solomon's extensive building projects and the dedication of the temple.

segments.title: Fire and Glory Fill Temple
segments.gist: Fire consumes the offerings, God's glory fills the house, and the people bow in worship.

segments.title: Solomon's Sacrifices and Dedication
segments.gist: Solomon and the people offer abundant sacrifices and keep the feast for seven days.

segments.title: People Sent Home Rejoicing
segments.gist: On the eighth day Solomon sends the people home, joyful for God's goodness to David, Solomon, and Israel.

segments.title: God's Covenant with Solomon
segments.gist: God appears to Solomon, promises to hear a humbled people, and warns against turning to other gods.

segments.title: Conditional Promise and Warning
segments.gist: God reaffirms David's throne if Solomon obeys, but warns that disobedience will bring destruction and mockery.

8.summary: 2 Chronicles 8 recounts Solomon's building projects after the temple: his own house, the cities he fortified, and his labor force. It also describes his administration, the annual sacrifices, and his trade expeditions, concluding with the notice of his death.

segments.title: Solomon's building projects
segments.gist: Solomon builds his house and cities, fortifies places, and uses remaining Canaanites as forced labor.

segments.title: Labor force and officers
segments.gist: Solomon conscripts non-Israelites for labor and appoints Israelite officers over his works.

segments.title: Sacrifices and temple service
segments.gist: Solomon offers sacrifices according to the law and organizes the priests and Levites for temple service.

segments.title: Trade with Ophir
segments.gist: Solomon's ships sail to Ophir and return with gold.

9.summary: The queen of Sheba visits Solomon to test him with hard questions, is overwhelmed by his wisdom and wealth, and blesses the LORD. Solomon's gold, ivory throne, and trade revenues are described, and the chapter ends with his death and Rehoboam's succession.

segments.title: Queen of Sheba visits Solomon
segments.gist: The queen of Sheba comes to Jerusalem with a great caravan, tests Solomon with hard questions, and is amazed by his answers and the splendor of his court.

segments.title: Solomon's gold and ivory throne
segments.gist: Solomon's annual gold revenue, his ivory throne overlaid with gold, and his gold drinking vessels are described, noting silver was not valued in his days.

segments.title: Solomon's wealth and wisdom exceed all
segments.gist: Solomon surpasses all kings in riches and wisdom, and all the earth seeks his presence to hear the wisdom God put in his heart.

segments.title: Solomon's horses and chariot cities
segments.gist: Solomon's horses and chariots, his collectors, and his building projects are summarized, along with his rule over the kings from the Euphrates to Egypt.

segments.title: Solomon's death and Rehoboam's reign
segments.gist: The rest of Solomon's acts are recorded in prophetic writings; he reigns forty years, dies, and is buried in David's city, and Rehoboam his son reigns in his place.

10.summary: Rehoboam succeeds Solomon, and the people ask him to lighten their heavy burden. He rejects the counsel of the older men and follows the young men's advice to increase it, so the northern tribes revolt under Jeroboam, and Rehoboam flees to Jerusalem, leaving only Judah loyal to him.

segments.title: Rehoboam and the people's request
segments.gist: Rehoboam goes to Shechem where all Israel gathers, and they ask him to ease the heavy yoke Solomon imposed.

segments.title: Rehoboam consults two groups
segments.gist: Rehoboam first asks the old men, who advise kindness, then the young men, who advise harsher treatment.

segments.title: Rehoboam's harsh answer
segments.gist: Rehoboam answers the people harshly, following the young men's counsel, and the text notes this turn came from God.

segments.title: Israel revolts and stones Adoram
segments.gist: The people reject Rehoboam's rule, and when he sends Adoram, they stone him; Rehoboam flees to Jerusalem, and Israel remains in revolt.

11.summary: After Rehoboam's kingdom is reduced to Judah and Benjamin, he fortifies cities, receives priests and Levites who migrate from Israel, and secures his rule through family alliances. The chapter describes his building projects, the religious consolidation around Jerusalem, and his many wives and sons.

segments.title: Rehoboam Forbidden to Fight
segments.gist: Rehoboam assembles Judah and Benjamin to fight Israel, but Shemaiah the prophet forbids it, saying the division is from God.

segments.title: Rehoboam Fortifies Cities
segments.gist: Rehoboam builds up fortified cities in Judah and Benjamin, equipping them with supplies and commanders.

segments.title: Priests and Levites Join Rehoboam
segments.gist: Priests and Levites from all Israel move to Judah because Jeroboam rejected them, strengthening Rehoboam's kingdom.

segments.title: Rehoboam's Family
segments.gist: Rehoboam takes many wives, including Maacah, and appoints his sons as rulers throughout Judah.

12.summary: After Rehoboam and Judah abandon the law of the LORD, Shishak king of Egypt invades with a vast army and takes the fortified cities, reaching Jerusalem. The prophet Shemaiah declares that God has left them to Shishak, and the king and princes humble themselves, so the LORD grants them some deliverance but makes them serve Shishak. Rehoboam reigns in Jerusalem, fortifies cities, and is described as doing evil because he did not prepare his heart to seek the LORD.

segments.title: Shishak Invades Judah
segments.gist: Rehoboam and Judah forsake the LORD, so Shishak king of Egypt attacks with a huge army and captures the fortified cities.

segments.title: Shemaiah Announces Judgment
segments.gist: The prophet Shemaiah tells the humbled king and princes that the LORD has left them to Shishak, and they repent.

segments.title: Deliverance and Tribute
segments.gist: The LORD grants partial deliverance but makes Judah serve Shishak; Shishak takes temple and palace treasures, and Rehoboam replaces the gold shields with bronze.

segments.title: Rehoboam's Reign and Death
segments.gist: Rehoboam reigns in Jerusalem, fortifies cities, does evil because he does not seek the LORD, and dies, succeeded by Abijah.

13.summary: Abijah becomes king of Judah and goes to war against Jeroboam of Israel with 400,000 men against 800,000. From Mount Zemaraim he delivers a speech charging Israel with rebellion against the house of David and with illegitimate worship under Jeroboam's golden calves, while Judah keeps the temple service of Aaron. When Judah is ambushed front and rear, the priests sound the trumpets and Judah's men raise a shout; God strikes Jeroboam's army, and Judah wins a great victory, with Abijah pursuing and taking Bethel, Jeshanah, and Ephrain. Jeroboam never recovers, and Abijah grows strong with fourteen wives and twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.

segments.title: Abijah's reign and war begun
segments.gist: Abijah reigns three years in Jerusalem and goes to war against Jeroboam with 400,000 chosen men against 800,000.

segments.title: Abijah's speech from Zemaraim
segments.gist: Abijah charges Israel with rebelling against David's line and with casting out Aaron's priests and serving Jeroboam's calves, while Judah keeps the LORD's service.

segments.title: Ambush turned into victory
segments.gist: Jeroboam ambushes Judah, but the priests sound trumpets, Judah shouts, and God strikes Israel so that Judah wins a great slaughter.

segments.title: Abijah pursues and grows strong
segments.gist: Abijah pursues Jeroboam and takes Bethel, Jeshanah, and Ephrain; Jeroboam never recovers, and Abijah's family and record are noted.

14.summary: Asa becomes king of Judah and does what is good and right in the eyes of the LORD, removing idols and commanding Judah to seek God. When Zerah the Ethiopian attacks with a vast army, Asa prays for divine help, and God defeats the enemy, leading to great spoil and a period of peace.

segments.title: Asa's Early Reforms
segments.gist: Asa reigns in Judah, removes idolatry, and commands the people to seek the LORD and keep the law.

segments.title: Building and Peace
segments.gist: Because the land is quiet, Asa builds fortified cities and equips a large army.

segments.title: Victory over Zerah
segments.gist: Asa prays for help against Zerah the Ethiopian, and God defeats the enemy, bringing much spoil to Jerusalem.

15.summary: The Spirit of God comes upon Azariah, who meets King Asa and the people of Judah and Benjamin, urging them to seek the LORD and promising His presence. Asa responds by removing idols from Judah and Benjamin and the cities he captured, repairs the altar in the temple, and gathers the people at Jerusalem, where they make a covenant to seek the LORD and rejoice greatly. He also deposes his mother Maachah from being queen because of her idolatry, destroys her idol, and brings dedicated gifts into the house of God, with the kingdom enjoying rest.

segments.title: Azariah's Prophecy to Asa
segments.gist: The Spirit of God comes upon Azariah, who tells Asa and Judah that the LORD is with them if they seek Him, urging them to be strong.

segments.title: Asa's Reforms and Covenant
segments.gist: Asa removes idols, repairs the altar, gathers the people, and they make a covenant to seek the LORD, rejoicing with an oath.

segments.title: Maachah Deposed and Treasures Brought
segments.gist: Asa removes Maachah from being queen for idolatry, destroys her idol, and brings dedicated things into the house of God as the kingdom enjoys rest.

16.summary: King Asa of Judah, warned by the prophet Hanani for relying on the king of Syria instead of God, imprisons the prophet and oppresses some of the people. Later afflicted with a severe foot disease, Asa seeks help from physicians rather than the LORD, and he dies and is buried with honor.

segments.title: Asa allies with Syria
segments.gist: Asa pays Ben-hadad of Syria to break his treaty with Baasha of Israel, and the Syrians attack Israel's cities.

segments.title: Hanani rebukes Asa
segments.gist: The prophet Hanani tells Asa he acted foolishly by relying on Syria, and Asa imprisons him and oppresses some people.

segments.title: Asa's disease and death
segments.gist: Asa's reign is recorded; he suffers a severe foot disease, seeks physicians rather than the LORD, dies, and is buried with honor.

17.summary: Jehoshaphat succeeds his father Asa as king of Judah, strengthens the kingdom's defenses and removes idolatry, and sends officials and Levites throughout the land to teach the book of the law. As a result, neighboring nations fear Judah and bring tribute, and Jehoshaphat's power and building projects grow.

segments.title: Jehoshaphat Strengthens Judah
segments.gist: Jehoshaphat becomes king, fortifies cities, and removes high places and groves from Judah.

segments.title: Teaching Tour of the Law
segments.gist: Jehoshaphat sends princes, Levites, and priests to teach the book of the law throughout Judah.

segments.title: Neighboring Nations Bring Tribute
segments.gist: The fear of the LORD falls on surrounding kingdoms, and Philistines and Arabians bring gifts and tribute.

segments.title: Jehoshaphat's Growing Power
segments.gist: Jehoshaphat grows strong, builds fortresses and store cities, and has a large army led by five commanders.

18.summary: Jehoshaphat of Judah allies with Ahab of Israel and agrees to join his campaign against Ramoth-gilead. Ahab's prophets promise success, but Jehoshaphat asks for a prophet of the LORD; Micaiah is summoned and foretells disaster, describing a lying spirit in the mouths of the prophets. Ahab orders Micaiah imprisoned, and the two kings go to battle, where Ahab is struck by a random arrow and dies.

segments.title: Jehoshaphat allies with Ahab
segments.gist: Jehoshaphat makes peace with Ahab and agrees to join him in battle at Ramoth-gilead.

segments.title: Ahab's prophets promise victory
segments.gist: Ahab's prophets unanimously predict success, and Jehoshaphat asks for a prophet of the LORD.

segments.title: Micaiah foretells defeat
segments.gist: Micaiah is summoned and, after initial sarcasm, declares that Israel will be scattered like sheep without a shepherd.

segments.title: Micaiah explains the lying spirit
segments.gist: Micaiah describes a heavenly council where a spirit volunteers to deceive Ahab's prophets, and the LORD permits it.

segments.title: Zedekiah strikes Micaiah
segments.gist: Zedekiah slaps Micaiah and challenges him; Micaiah predicts the outcome and is ordered imprisoned by Ahab.

segments.title: Ahab dies in battle
segments.gist: Ahab disguises himself but is struck by a random arrow and dies at evening, and the army disperses.

19.summary: Jehoshaphat returns safely to Jerusalem and is confronted by the prophet Jehu for allying with wicked Ahab. He repents, reforms the kingdom by sending teachers of the law throughout Judah, and reorganizes the judiciary, appointing judges in the cities and a supreme court in Jerusalem with strict instructions to judge righteously and fear the Lord.

segments.title: Jehu Rebukes Jehoshaphat
segments.gist: Jehoshaphat returns to Jerusalem and the seer Jehu rebukes him for helping the wicked and loving those who hate the Lord, yet promises some good is found in him.

segments.title: Jehoshaphat Reforms Judah
segments.gist: Jehoshaphat dwells in Jerusalem, travels through the land to bring the people back to the Lord, and sends officials and Levites to teach the book of the law in all the cities of Judah.

segments.title: Judges Appointed in Jerusalem
segments.gist: Jehoshaphat appoints Levites, priests, and family heads in Jerusalem to judge for the Lord and settle disputes, charging them to act faithfully and fear the Lord, with Amariah and Zebadiah as leaders.

20.summary: Jehoshaphat faces a vast invading army and proclaims a fast, leading Judah in prayer and trust in God. A prophet assures them of victory, and as the people sing praise, God causes the enemy coalition to destroy itself. Judah gathers the spoil, returns to Jerusalem in thanksgiving, and Jehoshaphat's reign ends with a summary of his rule and a note of his failure to reform the high places.

segments.title: Invasion and Jehoshaphat's Fear
segments.gist: Jehoshaphat learns of a great multitude coming against Judah and responds with fear, seeking the Lord and proclaiming a fast.

segments.title: Jehoshaphat's Prayer in the Temple
segments.gist: Jehoshaphat prays before the assembly, recounting God's past deliverance and asking for help against the invaders.

segments.title: Prophetic Assurance of Victory
segments.gist: The Spirit comes upon Jahaziel, who declares that the battle is God's and instructs Judah to stand still and see the deliverance.

segments.title: Praise and Enemy Self-Destruction
segments.gist: As Judah sings praise, the Lord sets ambushes that turn the enemy against each other until they are all destroyed.

segments.title: Spoil Gathered and Return to Jerusalem
segments.gist: Judah collects the spoil for three days, then returns to Jerusalem with joy and enters the temple to give thanks.

segments.title: Summary of Jehoshaphat's Reign
segments.gist: Jehoshaphat's reign is summarized, noting his failure to remove the high places and his alliance with Ahaziah that ended in shipwreck.

21.summary: Jehoshaphat dies and is succeeded by his son Jehoram, who kills his brothers and leads Judah into idolatry. Elijah sends Jehoram a letter predicting his fatal bowel disease, and after Philistine and Arabian invasions strip him of his family and wealth, he dies unmourned.

segments.title: Jehoram Succeeds and Kills Brothers
segments.gist: Jehoshaphat dies and is buried; his son Jehoram becomes king, kills his brothers, and leads Judah into idolatry.

segments.title: Edom and Libnah Revolt
segments.gist: Edom and Libnah revolt against Judah because Jehoram forsakes the Lord, and he fails to subdue them.

segments.title: Elijah's Letter of Judgment
segments.gist: Elijah writes Jehoram a letter pronouncing a plague on his people, wives, and children, and a fatal bowel disease on him.

segments.title: Philistines and Arabians Invade
segments.gist: The Lord stirs Philistines and Arabians to invade Judah, who carry away all Jehoram's possessions and his sons and wives.

segments.title: Jehoram's Death Without Mourning
segments.gist: Jehoram suffers a painful bowel disease for two years and dies unmourned, not buried in the kings' sepulchres.

22.summary: Ahaziah, son of Jehoram, becomes king of Judah and follows the wicked counsel of his mother Athaliah and the house of Ahab. He joins Jehoram of Israel in war against Hazael of Syria, and later visits the wounded Jehoram, where Jehu kills him in his purge. After Ahaziah's death, Athaliah seizes the throne and kills the royal seed, but Jehoshabeath hides the infant Joash in the temple for six years.

segments.title: Ahaziah's wicked reign in Judah
segments.gist: Ahaziah son of Jehoram becomes king at 22 and rules one year in Jerusalem, walking in the ways of Ahab's house because his mother Athaliah counsels him.

segments.title: Ahaziah joins Jehoram against Syria
segments.gist: Ahaziah follows Ahab's counsel and goes with Jehoram of Israel to battle Hazael of Syria at Ramoth-gilead, where Jehoram is wounded.

segments.title: Jehu kills Ahaziah
segments.gist: Ahaziah visits the wounded Jehoram and is caught by Jehu, who executes God's judgment on the house of Ahab and has Ahaziah slain.

segments.title: Athaliah usurps and Joash is hidden
segments.gist: Athaliah destroys the royal seed and takes the throne, but Jehoshabeath hides the infant Joash and his nurse in the temple for six years.

23.summary: Jehoiada the priest stages a coup in Judah: he gathers the Levites and leaders, crowns the young Joash in the temple, and has Athaliah executed. The people then destroy the temple of Baal and restore the worship of the LORD in the house of God.

segments.title: Jehoiada Organizes the Coup
segments.gist: Jehoiada gathers Levites and leaders, arms them from the temple, and stations guards around the young king Joash.

segments.title: Joash Crowned, Athaliah Killed
segments.gist: The people crown Joash and shout, while Athaliah cries treason and is dragged out and executed at the horse gate.

segments.title: Covenant and Baal's Temple Destroyed
segments.gist: Jehoiada makes a covenant between the people and the king, and the people tear down the temple of Baal and kill its priest Mattan.

segments.title: Temple Worship Restored
segments.gist: Jehoiada restores the priests and Levites to their duties, the people rejoice, and the city is quiet after Athaliah's death.

24.summary: Joash becomes king at seven and repairs the temple, but after the death of Jehoiada the priest he turns to idolatry and murders Jehoiada's son Zechariah. A small Syrian army defeats Judah, and Joash is assassinated by his own servants.

segments.title: Joash Crowned and Temple Repaired
segments.gist: Joash becomes king at seven and later decides to repair the house of the LORD.

segments.title: Temple Repair Completed
segments.gist: Joash collects money and has the temple repaired by skilled workers until it is restored.

segments.title: Death of Jehoiada
segments.gist: Jehoiada the priest dies at 130 and is buried among the kings for his good deeds.

segments.title: Joash's Apostasy and Zechariah's Murder
segments.gist: After Jehoiada's death, Joash and the people turn to idols and kill Zechariah for rebuking them.

segments.title: Syrian Invasion and Defeat
segments.gist: A small Syrian army defeats Judah, executes judgment, and leaves Joash wounded.

segments.title: Joash Assassinated
segments.gist: Joash's servants conspire and kill him, and he is buried without honor; Amaziah succeeds him.

25.summary: Amaziah becomes king of Judah and initially obeys the LORD, but after hiring Israelite mercenaries he is warned by a prophet and dismisses them. He defeats Edom but then brings Edomite gods back to worship, and when a prophet rebukes him he threatens him. Later he challenges King Joash of Israel, is defeated, and Jerusalem is plundered; he is finally assassinated in Lachish.

segments.title: Amaziah's Reign Begins
segments.gist: Amaziah becomes king at twenty-five and does right in the LORD's eyes, though not with a perfect heart, and he executes his father's murderers but spares their children.

segments.title: Mercenaries Hired and Dismissed
segments.gist: Amaziah hires a hundred thousand Israelite mercenaries, but a prophet warns him that Israel is not with the LORD, so he dismisses them despite the loss of money.

segments.title: Edom Defeated, Idols Embraced
segments.gist: Amaziah defeats the Edomites, but then sets up the gods of Edom and worships them; a prophet rebukes him, and Amaziah threatens him.

segments.title: War with Israel and Defeat
segments.gist: Amaziah challenges Joash of Israel, is warned but persists, and is defeated; Joash breaks down Jerusalem's wall and plunders the temple and palace.

segments.title: Amaziah's Death
segments.gist: After Joash's death, Amaziah is conspired against and flees to Lachish, where he is killed; his body is brought back to Jerusalem for burial.

26.summary: Uzziah becomes king of Judah at sixteen and reigns fifty-two years, doing right as long as Zechariah instructs him, and God prospers him. He builds up Judah's army and fortifications and wins victories over the Philistines and others, but his heart becomes proud and he unlawfully burns incense in the temple. When the priests confront him, leprosy breaks out on his forehead, and he lives isolated as a leper until his death, with his son Jotham governing the house.

segments.title: Uzziah's early reign and seeking God
segments.gist: Uzziah begins his fifty-two-year reign at sixteen, does right in God's eyes while Zechariah teaches him, and is prospered by God.

segments.title: Military and building achievements
segments.gist: Uzziah builds up Judah's army, fortifies Jerusalem and the wilderness, digs wells, and gains fame through victories and extensive works.

segments.title: Uzziah's pride and leprosy
segments.gist: Uzziah's heart is lifted up, he unlawfully burns incense in the temple, and when the priests confront him, leprosy breaks out on his forehead.

segments.title: Death and burial as a leper
segments.gist: Uzziah remains a leper until his death, is buried apart from the kings, and his son Jotham succeeds him.

27.summary: Jotham reigns in Jerusalem after his father Uzziah, doing right in the eyes of the Lord but not entering the temple; he builds the high gate and cities in the mountains, defeats the Ammonites, and becomes mighty because he prepares his ways before God. After sixteen years he dies and is buried in the city of David, and his son Ahaz succeeds him.

segments.title: Jotham's accession and building
segments.gist: Jotham begins to reign at twenty-five and builds the high gate of the temple and the wall of Ophel.

segments.title: Jotham's works and wars
segments.gist: He builds cities in the mountains and castles and towers in the forests, and defeats the Ammonites in battle.

segments.title: Ammonites subdued and tribute
segments.gist: The Ammonites give him tribute of silver, wheat, and barley for three years, and he becomes mighty.

segments.title: Jotham's death and succession
segments.gist: The rest of Jotham's acts are recorded; he dies after sixteen years and is buried in the city of David, and Ahaz his son reigns.

28.summary: Ahaz becomes king of Judah and leads the nation into idolatry, even sacrificing his own children. He is defeated by Syria and Israel, who carry away captives, though the prophet Oded secures their release. Ahaz then seeks help from Assyria, which brings him distress, and he further desecrates the temple and promotes idolatry, leaving Judah in ruin.

segments.title: Ahaz's Idolatry and Child Sacrifice
segments.gist: Ahaz reigns wickedly in Judah, making molten images and sacrificing his sons in the valley of Hinnom.

segments.title: Syria and Israel Defeat Judah
segments.gist: God delivers Ahaz into the hands of Syria and Israel, who inflict heavy casualties and take captives.

segments.title: Prophet Oded Secures Captives' Release
segments.gist: The prophet Oded confronts Israel's army, and with support from Ephraim's leaders, the captives are freed and cared for.

segments.title: Ahaz Seeks Assyria's Help
segments.gist: Ahaz appeals to Assyria for aid, but the Assyrian king brings him trouble instead of help.

segments.title: Ahaz's Further Apostasy
segments.gist: In his distress, Ahaz sacrifices to Damascus's gods, cuts up the temple vessels, and builds altars throughout Judah.

segments.title: Ahaz's Death and Burial
segments.gist: Ahaz dies and is buried in Jerusalem but not in the royal tombs; his son Hezekiah succeeds him.

29.summary: Hezekiah becomes king of Judah at twenty-five and immediately reopens and repairs the temple his father Ahaz had closed. He assembles the priests and Levites, calls them to consecrate themselves, confesses the nation's past unfaithfulness, and organizes a full restoration of temple worship, culminating in sacrifices, songs, and the people's renewed joy.

segments.title: Hezekiah's charge to the Levites
segments.gist: Hezekiah opens the temple doors, gathers the priests and Levites, and urges them to consecrate themselves and restore the covenant with God.

segments.title: Levites cleanse the temple
segments.gist: The Levites sanctify themselves, gather their brothers, and spend sixteen days cleansing the temple and restoring its vessels.

segments.title: Morning worship and praise
segments.gist: Hezekiah assembles the city rulers, offers sin offerings, and directs the Levites to sing praises with instruments as the burnt offering is made.

segments.title: Freewill offerings and rejoicing
segments.gist: The congregation brings abundant freewill offerings, the priests are too few to handle them all, and Hezekiah and the people rejoice at the sudden restoration.

30.summary: Hezekiah invites all Israel and Judah to a Passover at Jerusalem, sending couriers throughout the land despite mockery. A great assembly gathers, the temple is cleansed, and though many are ceremonially unclean, Hezekiah prays for them and God heals the people. The feast is kept with joy and extended a second week, and the Levites and priests are blessed before the people return home.

segments.title: Hezekiah's Passover Invitation
segments.gist: Hezekiah sends couriers throughout Israel and Judah urging all to come to Jerusalem for a Passover to the LORD.

segments.title: Mixed Response to Couriers
segments.gist: Some mock the couriers, but many from Asher, Manasseh, and Zebulun humble themselves and come to Jerusalem.

segments.title: Assembly Cleanses the Temple
segments.gist: A great multitude gathers, removes the altars of incense, and the Levites and priests sanctify themselves and the temple.

segments.title: Passover Kept with Prayer
segments.gist: The Passover is killed; many eat without proper cleansing, but Hezekiah prays for them and the LORD heals the people.

segments.title: Feast Extended a Second Week
segments.gist: The people keep the feast with great joy for seven days, then all agree to extend it another seven days with many offerings.

segments.title: Joy and Priestly Blessing
segments.gist: The whole assembly rejoices, the priests and Levites bless the people, and their prayer is heard in heaven.

31.summary: After the Passover, the people of Israel destroy idolatrous shrines throughout Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh. Hezekiah reorganizes the priests and Levites and reinstates the tithes and offerings for their support, and the people respond abundantly. The chapter closes with an account of Hezekiah's faithful administration and the prosperity that followed.

segments.title: Hezekiah reorganizes priests and Levites
segments.gist: Hezekiah assigns the priests and Levites their courses and duties, commands the people to support them, and the people bring tithes and offerings in abundance.

segments.title: Storehouses and faithful distribution
segments.gist: Hezekiah prepares storehouses, appoints overseers, and organizes the equitable distribution of offerings to priests and Levites throughout their cities.

segments.title: Hezekiah's faithfulness and prosperity
segments.gist: Hezekiah acts faithfully in all he does for the house of God, and he prospers because he seeks the Lord with all his heart.

32.summary: After Hezekiah's religious reforms, Sennacherib of Assyria invades Judah and besieges the fortified cities. Hezekiah prepares Jerusalem's defenses and encourages the people to trust in God, but Sennacherib's envoys mock Hezekiah and blaspheme the LORD, urging surrender. Hezekiah and Isaiah pray, and God sends an angel who destroys the Assyrian army, forcing Sennacherib to withdraw and later be killed by his own sons. Hezekiah then falls ill, is healed after a sign, and grows wealthy, though he briefly falters by showing his treasures to Babylonian envoys; the chapter closes with his death and burial.

segments.title: Assyria Invades and Hezekiah Prepares
segments.gist: Sennacherib invades Judah and besieges cities; Hezekiah blocks water sources, repairs walls, and appoints military leaders.

segments.title: Sennacherib's Envoys Mock God
segments.gist: Assyrian envoys threaten Jerusalem, blaspheme the LORD, and urge the people to surrender, but the people remain silent.

segments.title: God Delivers Jerusalem
segments.gist: Hezekiah and Isaiah pray; God sends an angel who destroys the Assyrian army, and Sennacherib withdraws in shame.

segments.title: Hezekiah's Illness and Pride
segments.gist: Hezekiah becomes sick and is healed after a sign, but his heart becomes proud; he and Jerusalem later humble themselves.

segments.title: Hezekiah's Wealth and Folly
segments.gist: Hezekiah grows very wealthy and successful, but he foolishly shows all his treasures to Babylonian envoys, and God tests him.

segments.title: Hezekiah's Death and Burial
segments.gist: Hezekiah dies and is buried with honor; his son Manasseh reigns in his place.

33.summary: Manasseh becomes king of Judah at twelve and leads the nation into extreme idolatry, desecrating the temple and practicing sorcery. Taken captive to Babylon, he humbles himself and prays, and God restores him to Jerusalem, where he fortifies the city and removes the foreign gods. His son Amon reigns wickedly for two years and is killed by his own servants, and the people make eight-year-old Josiah king in his place.

segments.title: Manasseh's Idolatry and Temple Desecration
segments.gist: Manasseh reigns wickedly, rebuilding high places, worshiping idols, and placing a carved image in the temple, leading Judah to do worse than the nations.

segments.title: Manasseh's Captivity and Repentance
segments.gist: God brings Assyrian captains who take Manasseh captive to Babylon; in distress he humbles himself and prays, and God restores him to Jerusalem.

segments.title: Manasseh's Reforms and Fortifications
segments.gist: After his return, Manasseh builds a wall, removes foreign gods and the idol from the temple, restores the altar of the LORD, and commands Judah to serve the LORD.

segments.title: Manasseh's Death and Burial
segments.gist: The rest of Manasseh's acts and his prayer are recorded; he dies and is buried in his own house, and his son Amon reigns.

segments.title: Amon's Wicked Reign and Assassination
segments.gist: Amon reigns wickedly, forsakes the LORD, and is killed by his servants; the people slay the conspirators and make his son Josiah king.

34.summary: Josiah becomes king of Judah at eight years old and seeks the LORD in his youth, purging Judah and Jerusalem of idolatry. In his eighteenth year he repairs the temple, and during the work the book of the law is found and read to him; he humbles himself before God and sends to the prophetess Huldah, who confirms judgment but promises he will die in peace.

segments.title: Josiah Seeks the LORD
segments.gist: Josiah reigns righteously from youth and begins to purge Judah and Jerusalem of idols and altars.

segments.title: Temple Repair Begins
segments.gist: In his eighteenth year Josiah sends officials to repair the house of the LORD and the Levites oversee the work.

segments.title: Book of the Law Found
segments.gist: Hilkiah finds the book of the law, Shaphan reads it to Josiah, who tears his clothes and seeks the LORD's word.

segments.title: Huldah's Prophecy
segments.gist: Huldah declares that judgment will come on Judah but that Josiah will be gathered to his grave in peace.

segments.title: Covenant Renewed
segments.gist: Josiah gathers the people, reads the law, makes a covenant, and removes abominations from Israel.

35.summary: Josiah keeps a Passover in Jerusalem, organizing priests and Levites and providing sacrifices for the people, with the Levites slaughtering the lambs and the singers and gatekeepers at their posts. Later, Pharaoh Necho passes through on his way to Carchemish, and Josiah, ignoring Necho's warning that God is with him, goes out to battle and is fatally wounded by archers; he dies in Jerusalem and is buried with great mourning, and the people make his son Jehoahaz king.

segments.title: Josiah Organizes the Passover
segments.gist: Josiah assigns the priests and Levites to their duties in the temple and commands them to prepare for the Passover.

segments.title: Josiah and Princes Provide Offerings
segments.gist: Josiah and his officials donate thousands of lambs and goats for the Passover, and the Levites slaughter the animals and distribute the offerings.

segments.title: The Passover Kept
segments.gist: The Passover is celebrated with burnt offerings on the altar, and the singers and gatekeepers remain at their posts as the service is completed.

segments.title: Josiah's Battle and Death
segments.gist: Pharaoh Necho warns Josiah not to interfere, but Josiah fights him at Megiddo, is wounded by archers, and dies in Jerusalem.

segments.title: Lamentation and Succession
segments.gist: Jeremiah and all Judah mourn for Josiah, and the people make his son Jehoahaz king in his place.

36.summary: The final chapter of 2 Chronicles recounts the reigns of Judah's last four kings—Jehoahaz, Jehoiakim, Jehoiachin, and Zedekiah—whose repeated evil and rebellion against Babylon lead to the destruction of Jerusalem and the temple. After seventy years of exile, Cyrus king of Persia issues a decree allowing the Jews to return and rebuild.

segments.title: Jehoahaz's brief reign
segments.gist: The people make Josiah's son Jehoahaz king, but Pharaoh Necho deposes him after three months and takes him to Egypt.

segments.title: Jehoiakim's evil reign
segments.gist: Jehoiakim reigns eleven years in Jerusalem, does evil, and is bound by Nebuchadnezzar and carried to Babylon.

segments.title: Jehoiachin's short reign
segments.gist: Jehoiachin reigns three months and ten days, does evil, and is taken to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar.

segments.title: Zedekiah's rebellion and fall
segments.gist: Zedekiah rebels against Nebuchadnezzar and hardens his heart; the people and priests mock God's messengers until there is no remedy.

segments.title: Jerusalem destroyed, exile
segments.gist: God brings the Chaldeans, who destroy the temple and Jerusalem and kill many; survivors are exiled until the land enjoys its sabbaths for seventy years.

segments.title: Cyrus's decree to return
segments.gist: In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, he issues a decree allowing the Jews to return to Jerusalem and rebuild the temple.

1.summary: King Cyrus of Persia issues a proclamation allowing the Jews exiled in Babylon to return to Jerusalem and rebuild the temple, urging their neighbors to support them with gifts. The chapter then lists the temple vessels that Nebuchadnezzar had taken, which Cyrus now releases for the returning exiles to carry back.

segments.title: Cyrus's Proclamation
segments.gist: Cyrus declares that God has given him all kingdoms and charges him to build a temple in Jerusalem, inviting Jews to return.

segments.title: Exiles Prepare to Return
segments.gist: Heads of families from Judah and Benjamin, priests, and Levites rise to go, and neighbors give them silver, gold, goods, and beasts.

segments.title: Temple Vessels Returned
segments.gist: Cyrus brings out the temple vessels taken by Nebuchadnezzar and gives them to Sheshbazzar to carry back to Jerusalem.

2.summary: This chapter records the census of the Jewish exiles who returned from Babylon to Jerusalem and Judah under Zerubbabel. It lists the families, towns, priests, Levites, temple servants, and the descendants of Solomon's servants, along with their totals. It also notes those who could not prove their Israelite ancestry, and describes the freewill offerings given for rebuilding the temple, with the people settling in their towns.

segments.title: Introduction to the Return
segments.gist: Lists the leaders of the return from Babylon to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his own town.

segments.title: Lay Families and Their Numbers
segments.gist: Records the numbers of the Israelite lay families and those identified by ancestral houses.

segments.title: Priests, Levites, Singers, Gatekeepers
segments.gist: Gives the counts of priests, Levites, temple singers, and gatekeepers returning from exile.

segments.title: Temple Servants and Solomon's Servants
segments.gist: Lists the temple servants and the descendants of Solomon's servants with their totals.
