segments.gist: The righteous is like a tree planted by rivers of water, bringing forth fruit and prospering, while the wicked are like chaff driven by the wind.

2.summary: Psalm 2 depicts the nations raging against the LORD and His anointed, but God laughs and establishes His king on Zion. The king recounts the decree of sonship and is promised the nations as inheritance, warning rulers to serve the LORD with fear and take refuge in Him.

segments.title: Nations Rage Against the LORD
segments.gist: The nations and rulers conspire against the LORD and His anointed, but God laughs and speaks in wrath.

segments.title: God Establishes His King
segments.gist: God declares His king on Zion, rebuking the rebellious nations.

segments.title: The Decree of the Son
segments.gist: The king proclaims God's decree: He is God's Son and will inherit and rule the nations.

segments.title: Warning to Rulers
segments.gist: Rulers are warned to serve the LORD with fear and kiss the Son, taking refuge in Him.

3.summary: Psalm 3 is a psalm of David, written when he fled from his son Absalom. David cries out to God about his many enemies who say God will not help him, but he affirms God as a shield and deliverer, sleeps and wakes in safety, and asks God to arise and save him, ending with a blessing on God's people.

segments.title: David's cry and enemies' taunt
segments.gist: David laments that many foes rise against him and say God will not deliver him.

segments.title: God as shield and lifter
segments.gist: David declares God is his shield, his glory, and the one who lifts up his head, and he cries out and is answered.

segments.title: Sleep and waking in safety
segments.gist: David lies down and sleeps and wakes again because the Lord sustains him, and he is not afraid of ten thousands of people.

segments.title: Prayer for deliverance and blessing
segments.gist: David asks God to arise and save him, recalling that God strikes his enemies and breaks their teeth, and he concludes with salvation and blessing for God's people.

4.summary: Psalm 4 is a short evening prayer in which David asks God to hear him, rebukes those who chase after false gods, and expresses quiet trust that God will give him peace and safety. He closes by asking for God's blessing and light, and lies down to sleep in confidence.

segments.title: Rebuke of vain men
segments.gist: He challenges men who love vanity and lies, asking how long they will turn his glory to shame.

segments.title: Call to trust and sacrifice
segments.gist: He urges them to stand in awe, sin not, and offer sacrifices of righteousness while trusting in the Lord.

segments.title: Peace and safety in sleep
segments.gist: David contrasts the many who seek good with his own trust that God will give him peace and safety.

5.summary: Psalm 5 is a morning prayer in which David asks God to hear him and to reject the wicked, then describes the fate of the wicked and asks for guidance and protection, ending with confidence that God will bless the righteous.

segments.title: Morning Prayer for Hearing
segments.gist: David cries out to God in the morning, asking Him to listen to his words and groaning.

segments.title: God Rejects the Wicked
segments.gist: David declares that God takes no pleasure in wickedness and will destroy those who speak lies and shed blood.

segments.title: Entering God's House in Fear
segments.gist: David resolves to enter God's house in reverence and asks for guidance in righteousness because of his enemies.

segments.title: Judgment on the Wicked
segments.gist: David describes the destructive speech of the wicked and asks God to let them fall by their own counsels.

segments.title: Joy and Protection for the Righteous
segments.gist: David calls the righteous to rejoice because God blesses and defends those who love Him.

6.summary: Psalm 6 is a individual lament in which David pleads with God for mercy and healing, asking how long his suffering will last. He describes his physical and emotional anguish, warns evildoers to depart, and expresses confidence that God has heard his weeping and will answer his prayer.

segments.title: Plea for Mercy and Healing
segments.gist: David asks God not to rebuke him in anger but to have mercy and heal him, acknowledging his weakness and troubled bones.

segments.title: How Long, O Lord?
segments.gist: David cries out for God to return and deliver him, asking how long his suffering will last and appealing to God's steadfast love.

segments.title: Wearied with Groaning
segments.gist: David describes his exhaustion from weeping, his bed drenched with tears, and his eyes wasting away because of his foes.

segments.title: Depart from Me, Evildoers
segments.gist: David commands evildoers to depart because God has heard his weeping, and he expresses confidence that God will answer and put his enemies to shame.

7.summary: Psalm 7 is a prayer of David, likely composed concerning the Benjamite Cush, in which he appeals to God for justice against his enemies. He protests his innocence, asks God to arise and judge the peoples, and expresses confidence that God will defend the righteous and bring the wickedness of the wicked to an end.

segments.title: David's Trust in God
segments.gist: David declares his trust in God and asks for deliverance from his persecutors.

segments.title: Plea for Innocence
segments.gist: David asks God to judge him according to his righteousness and not let enemies triumph if he is guilty.

segments.title: Call for God to Arise
segments.gist: David urges God to arise in anger against his foes and to gather the people for judgment.

segments.title: God as Righteous Judge
segments.gist: David asks God to end wickedness and defend the righteous, affirming God as a just judge.

segments.title: The Wicked's Own Destruction
segments.gist: David describes how the wicked conceive mischief and fall into their own traps.

8.summary: Psalm 8 is a hymn of praise to God as Creator, opening and closing with the declaration of His majestic name. The psalmist marvels at the honor God has given to humanity, crowning them with glory and dominion over creation.

segments.title: God's Majestic Name
segments.gist: The psalmist praises God's name and glory, which is set above the heavens and praised by babes.

segments.title: Man's Smallness
segments.gist: The psalmist considers the heavens and wonders why God is mindful of insignificant humanity.

segments.title: Humanity Crowned with Honor
segments.gist: God crowns humanity with glory and honor, giving them dominion over all creation.

9.summary: Psalm 9 is a thanksgiving psalm in which David praises God for judging his cause and destroying the wicked, then calls on God to arise and not let mere mortals prevail, asking that the nations be judged and the needy not be forgotten.

segments.title: Praise with whole heart
segments.gist: David resolves to praise the LORD with his whole heart and to recount all his marvelous works.

segments.title: God judges David's enemies
segments.gist: David describes how his enemies turned back and perished before God, who rebuked the nations and blotted out their name.

segments.title: The LORD reigns as refuge
segments.gist: The LORD sits as king forever, judges the world in righteousness, and is a refuge for the oppressed who trust in him.

segments.title: Call to praise in Zion
segments.gist: David calls Zion to praise the LORD who avenges blood and does not forget the humble, and asks God to lift him from the gates of death.

segments.title: Wicked fall into their own trap
segments.gist: The nations sink into the pit they made, the wicked are snared in their own net, and the needy are not forgotten forever.

segments.title: Prayer for God to arise
segments.gist: David asks the LORD to arise so that man may not prevail, and that the nations may be judged and know they are but men.

10.summary: Psalm 10 is a lament over the apparent triumph of the wicked, who oppress the poor and boast that God does not see. The psalmist pleads for God to arise and break the arm of the wicked, expressing confidence that God hears the humble and will do justice for the fatherless and oppressed.

segments.title: The Wicked's Boast and Oppression
segments.gist: The psalmist describes the wicked who persecute the poor and boast that God has forgotten and will not call them to account.

segments.title: Plea for God to Arise
segments.gist: The psalmist cries out for God to lift his hand and break the arm of the wicked, confident that God sees mischief and will requite it.

segments.title: God's Reign and Justice
segments.gist: The psalmist declares that the Lord is King forever and will hear the desire of the humble and do justice for the fatherless and oppressed.

11.summary: Psalm 11 is a short psalm of trust in which the speaker rejects the advice of those who urge him to flee like a bird to the mountains, because the wicked are secretly shooting at the upright and the foundations of society are being destroyed. He answers that the LORD is in his holy temple and on his heavenly throne, testing the righteous and hating the violent, and that the upright will finally see his face.

segments.title: Counsel to Flee
segments.gist: The psalmist reports the advice to flee to the mountains like a bird, since the wicked secretly aim at the upright and the foundations are destroyed.

segments.title: The LORD Tests and Judges
segments.gist: The LORD tests the righteous and the wicked, and rains snares, fire, and brimstone on the violent as their portion.

12.summary: Psalm 12 is a short lament in which David cries out that the godly and faithful have vanished from among men, while the wicked speak flattering lies and boast of their own tongues. He appeals to the LORD to cut off lying lips, and receives assurance that God will arise and protect the oppressed. The psalm closes with a contrast between the pure words of the LORD and the wicked who strut about while vileness is exalted.

segments.title: The godly have vanished
segments.gist: David cries for help because the faithful have disappeared and the wicked speak lies and flattery.

segments.title: God promises to arise
segments.gist: The LORD declares He will arise to protect the oppressed, and His words are pure and tried.

segments.title: Preserved from the wicked
segments.gist: David trusts the LORD to preserve His people from the wicked who prowl when vileness is exalted.

13.summary: Psalm 13 is a short lament in which David cries out to God four times asking how long he will be forgotten and left to struggle, then pleads for God to answer lest his enemy triumph, and closes with a declaration of trust in God's steadfast love and salvation.

segments.title: Fourfold 'How long?' lament
segments.gist: David repeatedly asks God 'How long?' about being forgotten, hiding his face, enduring sorrow, and being exalted over by his enemy.

segments.title: Plea for answer and light
segments.gist: David asks God to consider and answer him, to enlighten his eyes lest he sleep in death and his enemy rejoice in his fall.

14.summary: Psalm 14 describes the fool who denies God and the corruption of humanity, while affirming that God looks down and finds none who do good. It anticipates God's judgment on evildoers and concludes with a prayer for Israel's salvation and restoration.

segments.title: The Fool Denies God
segments.gist: The psalmist describes the fool who says there is no God, and the corruption of humanity.

segments.title: God Judges Evildoers
segments.gist: God looks down from heaven and sees that all have turned aside; he rebukes those who devour his people.

15.summary: Psalm 15 is a short wisdom psalm in which David asks who may dwell in God's holy hill and answers with a description of the person who lives with integrity, speaks truth, and does no harm to others. It closes with the assurance that such a person will never be moved.

16.summary: Psalm 16 is a short psalm of trust in which David asks God to preserve him, expresses delight in the LORD and in the saints, rejects other gods, and blesses the LORD for guidance. He concludes with confidence that God will not abandon him to the grave but will show him the path of life and joy in His presence.

segments.title: A plea for preservation
segments.gist: David asks God to keep him safe, declares his dependence on the LORD, and separates himself from those who follow other gods.

segments.title: The LORD as inheritance
segments.gist: David describes the LORD as his portion and cup, and expresses contentment with the inheritance assigned to him.

segments.title: Blessing God for counsel
segments.gist: David blesses the LORD for guiding him and sets the LORD always before him as his foundation.

segments.title: Assurance of life and joy
segments.gist: David rejoices in hope that God will not abandon him to the grave but will show him the path of life and eternal joy in His presence.

17.summary: Psalm 17 is a prayer of David asking God to hear his righteous plea and to keep him safe from the wicked who surround him. He appeals for vindication, describes the arrogance and violence of his enemies, and closes with confidence that he will behold God's face and be satisfied when he awakes.

segments.title: Plea for a just hearing
segments.gist: David asks God to listen to his honest prayer and to vindicate him, claiming he has kept his mouth from transgression.

segments.title: Prayer for protection
segments.gist: David calls on God to show his marvelous lovingkindness and to keep him as the apple of the eye from the wicked who oppress him.

segments.title: Description of the wicked
segments.gist: The enemies are portrayed as proud, prosperous, and predatory, like a lion greedy for prey lurking in secret places.

segments.title: Petition for deliverance
segments.gist: David asks God to arise, confront the wicked, and deliver him from men whose portion is in this life and who leave wealth to their children.

18.summary: Psalm 18 is a royal thanksgiving song in which David praises the LORD for delivering him from his enemies and from Saul. He describes his distress, God's dramatic rescue, the LORD's reward for righteousness, and closes with praise and confidence that God will give victory to his king and show mercy to his anointed.

segments.title: David's Love and Praise
segments.gist: David declares his love for the LORD and calls him his rock, fortress, and deliverer.

segments.title: Distress and Divine Rescue
segments.gist: David recounts his near-death distress and describes God's dramatic, earth-shaking intervention to rescue him.

segments.title: Reward for Righteousness
segments.gist: David affirms that the LORD rewards him according to his righteousness and shows himself upright, pure, and saving to those who are faithful.

segments.title: Victory over Enemies
segments.gist: David praises God for strengthening him, enabling him to pursue and destroy his enemies and to be made head over nations.

segments.title: Closing Praise and Thanksgiving
segments.gist: David concludes with a call to praise the living God and expresses confidence that God will show mercy to his anointed forever.

19.summary: Psalm 19 moves from the heavens declaring God's glory to the perfection of the LORD's law, then closes with a prayer for cleansing and acceptance. David praises God's general revelation in creation, extols the specific revelation of Scripture, and asks to be kept from presumptuous sins.

segments.title: The heavens declare God's glory
segments.gist: The heavens, firmament, day, and night proclaim God's handiwork without speech, and the sun runs its course like a bridegroom.

segments.title: The law of the LORD is perfect
segments.gist: The LORD's law, testimony, statutes, commandments, and judgments are perfect, sure, right, pure, and true, more desirable than gold.

segments.title: Prayer for cleansing and acceptance
segments.gist: David asks to be warned and cleansed from secret faults and presumptuous sins, and prays that his words and meditation be acceptable to God.

20.summary: Psalm 20 is a royal psalm in which the congregation prays for the king's success in battle, asking God to answer, protect, and support him. The people express confidence that God will save his anointed, and they conclude with a final prayer for the king's deliverance.

segments.title: Prayer for the King's Success
segments.gist: The congregation asks God to answer the king in trouble, send help from the sanctuary, and grant his heart's desire.

segments.title: Confidence in God's Deliverance
segments.gist: The people declare that God saves his anointed and will answer from heaven, contrasting trust in chariots with trust in God's name.

21.summary: Psalm 21 is a royal thanksgiving psalm in which the congregation praises God for granting the king his heart's desire, victory, and a crown of gold. The king trusts in the LORD and is upheld, and the psalm closes with confidence that God will destroy the king's enemies while the people praise his strength.

segments.title: Thanksgiving for the King's Blessings
segments.gist: The congregation rejoices that the LORD has given the king his heart's desire, victory, and a crown of pure gold.

segments.title: The King's Trust and God's Protection
segments.gist: The king trusts in the LORD and will not be moved; God will find out and destroy all his enemies.

22.summary: Psalm 22 is a lament that moves from abandonment and urgent cries for help to vivid descriptions of the speaker's suffering and enemies, then turns to confident praise and a vision of all nations worshiping the LORD. The psalm closes with a declaration that God's righteousness will be told to future generations.

segments.title: Cry of Abandonment and Trust
segments.gist: The psalmist cries out that God has forsaken him, yet recalls God's holiness and past deliverance, and trusts from birth.

segments.title: Suffering and Enemies Surround
segments.gist: The psalmist describes his physical agony and the hostile crowd that encircles him like bulls, lions, and dogs.

segments.title: Plea for Deliverance
segments.gist: He urgently asks the LORD to be near and to save him from the sword, the dog, and the lion's mouth.

segments.title: Vow to Praise in the Congregation
segments.gist: He promises to declare God's name to his brethren and invites the meek to praise the LORD for answered prayer.

segments.title: All Nations Will Worship
segments.gist: The psalmist envisions all ends of the earth turning to the LORD and future generations serving and proclaiming His righteousness.

23.summary: A short psalm of trust in which the speaker describes the LORD as a shepherd who provides, leads, and restores, then as a host who spreads a table and anoints with oil. Confidence in goodness and mercy follows the speaker through life, ending with the hope of dwelling in the LORD's house forever.

24.summary: Psalm 24 is a liturgical hymn that declares the earth and all it contains belong to the LORD, who dwells on the holy hill. It describes the kind of person who may stand in His holy place—those with clean hands and pure hearts—and then presents a call for the gates to open to the King of glory, identified as the LORD strong and mighty in battle.

segments.title: The Earth Belongs to the LORD
segments.gist: The psalm opens by declaring that the earth and its fullness belong to the LORD, who founded it upon the seas.

segments.title: Who May Ascend the Holy Hill
segments.gist: The psalm asks who may stand in the LORD's holy place and answers that it is those with clean hands and pure hearts, who receive blessing from God.

segments.title: The King of Glory Enters
segments.gist: The gates are commanded to open for the King of glory, identified as the LORD strong and mighty, the LORD of hosts.

25.summary: Psalm 25 is a prayer of David for guidance, forgiveness, and protection, expressing trust in God's mercy and covenant faithfulness. He asks God to remember him despite his sins, seeks deliverance from enemies and distress, and closes with a plea for Israel's redemption.

segments.title: Prayer for Guidance and Trust
segments.gist: David lifts his soul to God, asking for direction and expressing trust in God's salvation.

segments.title: Request for God's Paths
segments.gist: David asks God to teach him His ways and remembers His mercies and lovingkindness.

segments.title: God's Goodness and Forgiveness
segments.gist: God is good and upright, guiding the meek and forgiving those who seek Him.

segments.title: Blessings for Those Who Fear God
segments.gist: Those who fear God will be taught His way and enjoy prosperity and God's covenant.

segments.title: Plea for Mercy in Distress
segments.gist: David asks God to turn to him, forgive his sins, and deliver him from enemies and affliction.

segments.title: Final Prayer for Protection and Redemption
segments.gist: David asks God to preserve him and redeem Israel from all troubles.

26.summary: Psalm 26 is David's prayer for vindication, in which he asks God to examine his integrity, declares his avoidance of the wicked and his love for God's house, and pleads for redemption and mercy.

segments.title: David's Plea for Vindication
segments.gist: David asks God to judge him, test his heart, and declares his trust in the Lord without wavering.

segments.title: Separation from the Wicked
segments.gist: David asserts he does not associate with deceitful or evil people and refuses to join their gatherings.

segments.title: Love for God's House
segments.gist: David describes washing his hands in innocence and going around God's altar with thanksgiving, loving the place where God's honor dwells.

segments.title: Prayer Not to Be Swept Away
segments.gist: David pleads that God not gather his soul with sinners whose hands are full of bribes.

segments.title: Integrity and Praise
segments.gist: David resolves to walk in integrity, asks for redemption and mercy, and vows to praise the Lord in the congregation.

27.summary: Psalm 27 is a psalm of David expressing confident trust in the LORD as his light and salvation, which gives him courage against enemies and a deep desire to dwell in God's house. It moves from praise for God's protection to a prayer for guidance and deliverance, ending with an exhortation to wait on the LORD.

segments.title: The LORD My Light
segments.gist: David declares the LORD as his light and salvation, expressing fearless trust even when enemies attack.

segments.title: Desire to Dwell in God's House
segments.gist: David longs to dwell in the LORD's house, seeking His beauty and protection, confident of being lifted above enemies.

segments.title: Prayer for Guidance and Mercy
segments.gist: David cries out for God's mercy, asking for guidance and deliverance from adversaries, trusting God will not forsake him.

segments.title: Wait on the LORD
segments.gist: David expresses faith to see God's goodness and encourages waiting on the LORD with courage and hope.

28.summary: Psalm 28 is a prayer of David in two movements: he cries out to God not to be silent or to drag him away with the wicked who speak peace while plotting evil, and then he praises God for hearing his plea and for being his strength and shield, closing with a prayer for the salvation and blessing of God's people.

segments.title: Plea for God Not to Be Silent
segments.gist: David cries to God as his rock, asking not to be silent or counted with the wicked who speak peace while harboring evil.

segments.title: Praise for Answered Prayer
segments.gist: David blesses the Lord for hearing his supplication, calling Him his strength, shield, and saving refuge.

29.summary: Psalm 29 is a hymn calling the heavenly beings to ascribe glory and strength to the LORD, then describing the power of his voice as it thunders over the waters, breaks cedars, shakes the wilderness, and strips the forests, while the LORD sits enthroned over the flood and gives strength and peace to his people.

segments.title: Call to Praise the LORD
segments.gist: The psalmist summons the mighty to give the LORD glory and strength, and to worship him in holy attire.

segments.title: The Voice of the LORD
segments.gist: The LORD's voice thunders over waters, breaks cedars, flashes flames, shakes the wilderness, and strips the forests, while all cry 'Glory.'

segments.title: The LORD Enthroned Gives Strength
segments.gist: The LORD sits as king over the flood forever and gives strength and peace to his people.

30.summary: Psalm 30 is a thanksgiving song attributed to David, praising God for healing and deliverance from the grave. The psalmist recalls a time of prosperity when he felt secure, then describes God hiding his face and the distress that followed, and ends with a vow of perpetual praise.

segments.title: Thanksgiving for Deliverance
segments.gist: The psalmist extols the Lord for lifting him up and healing him, so that his enemies do not rejoice over him.

segments.title: Call to Praise
segments.gist: Saints are urged to sing unto the Lord and give thanks at the remembrance of his holiness, for his anger is brief but his favor is lifelong.

segments.title: From Security to Dismay
segments.gist: In prosperity the psalmist felt immovable, but when God hid his face he was troubled.

segments.title: Plea for Mercy
segments.gist: The psalmist cries to the Lord for mercy, arguing that his death would bring no profit to God, for dust cannot praise him.

segments.title: Mourning Turned to Dancing
segments.gist: God has turned mourning into dancing and girded him with gladness, so that his glory may sing praise and not be silent.

31.summary: Psalm 31 is a prayer of David for deliverance from enemies and illness, expressing deep trust in God as his rock and fortress. It moves from urgent pleas for rescue and confessions of distress to praise for God's goodness and a closing exhortation for all the faithful to be strong and take courage.

segments.title: Prayer for Deliverance and Guidance
segments.gist: David asks God to be his rock and fortress, to lead and guide him for his name's sake.

segments.title: Distress and Abandonment
segments.gist: David laments being hated, forgotten, and surrounded by enemies, with fear and sorrow overwhelming him.

segments.title: Trust in God Amidst Enemies
segments.gist: David affirms his trust in God and asks for deliverance and for the wicked to be silenced.

segments.title: Praise for God's Goodness
segments.gist: David praises God for his abundant goodness and for hearing his supplication when he cried out.

segments.title: Exhortation to Love and Courage
segments.gist: David calls all saints to love the Lord and be of good courage, for God preserves the faithful.

32.summary: Psalm 32 is a thanksgiving and wisdom psalm in which the speaker declares the blessedness of the forgiven, recounts how hiding sin brought physical and spiritual distress, and describes confession and divine deliverance. He then exhorts the faithful to trust God and follow His guidance rather than being stubborn like a horse or mule.

segments.title: Blessedness of Forgiveness
segments.gist: The psalmist pronounces blessing on those whose transgression is forgiven and whose sin is covered.

segments.title: Distress and Confession
segments.gist: While silent about sin, the psalmist felt God's hand heavy upon him; after acknowledging his sin, he received forgiveness.

segments.title: Prayer and Hiding Place
segments.gist: The godly are urged to pray while God may be found; God is a hiding place preserving from trouble.

segments.title: Divine Instruction and Warning
segments.gist: God promises to instruct and guide with His eye, warning against being stubborn like a horse or mule.

segments.title: Sorrow and Mercy
segments.gist: The wicked have many sorrows, but mercy surrounds the trusting; the righteous are called to rejoice.

33.summary: Psalm 33 is a hymn of praise calling the righteous to worship the LORD for His creative word and His sovereign rule over the nations. It contrasts the LORD's steadfast love and deliverance of those who fear Him with the futility of trusting in human strength, ending with a declaration of hope in Him.

segments.title: Call to Praise the LORD
segments.gist: The righteous are called to praise the LORD with music and a new song because His word and works are upright and true.

segments.title: The LORD's Creative Word
segments.gist: The LORD's word and breath made the heavens and earth; He gathers the waters and all the earth should fear Him.

segments.title: The LORD Rules the Nations
segments.gist: The LORD frustrates the plans of nations but His own counsel stands forever; blessed is the nation whose God is the LORD.

segments.title: The LORD Watches Over His People
segments.gist: From heaven the LORD observes all people and delivers those who fear Him and hope in His mercy.

segments.title: Hope in the LORD
segments.gist: The psalmist expresses trust in the LORD as help and shield, asking for His mercy according to their hope.

34.summary: Psalm 34 is an acrostic thanksgiving in which David praises God for delivering him from his fears and afflictions, invites the humble to join him in tasting God's goodness, and offers wisdom on the fear of the Lord and righteous living. The psalm alternates between personal testimony, instruction to the congregation, and a general observation on the contrasting fates of the righteous and the wicked.

segments.title: David's Praise for Deliverance
segments.gist: David blesses the Lord at all times and recounts how God answered him and delivered him from his fears and troubles.

segments.title: Taste and See God's Goodness
segments.gist: David invites the congregation to experience God's goodness, promising that those who fear Him lack no good thing.

segments.title: Instruction in the Fear of the Lord
segments.gist: David teaches the fear of the Lord, urging listeners to keep their tongue from evil and pursue peace.

segments.title: The Lord Hears the Righteous
segments.gist: The Lord watches over the righteous, hears their cries, and is near to the brokenhearted, delivering them.

segments.title: Affliction and Final Justice
segments.gist: The righteous may face many afflictions, but the Lord delivers them, while the wicked are condemned.

35.summary: Psalm 35 is a prayer of David asking God to contend with those who fight against him, describing their plots and false accusations, and appealing for divine justice. He recalls his past kindness toward them and asks God not to remain silent, vowing to praise God when vindicated.

segments.title: Prayer for Deliverance from Enemies
segments.gist: David asks God to fight against his adversaries, to shame and turn them back, and to rescue his soul from their destructive plans.

segments.title: Enemies Repay Good with Evil
segments.gist: David laments that false witnesses accuse him of crimes he did not commit and that his enemies repay his kindness with hostility and mockery.

segments.title: Appeal for God to Act
segments.gist: David pleads with God not to stay silent, asks for vindication, and prays that his enemies be put to shame and not triumph over him.

segments.title: Vow to Praise God
segments.gist: David vows that those who favor his cause will rejoice and that he will praise God's righteousness all day long.

36.summary: Psalm 36 contrasts the wicked, who flatter themselves and plot evil, with God's steadfast love and justice, which are pictured as a fountain of life and light. The psalmist prays for God's continued protection and asks that the proud not triumph over the righteous.

segments.title: The Transgression of the Wicked
segments.gist: The psalmist describes the wicked person who flatters himself and speaks deceit, plotting evil even on his bed.

segments.title: God's Steadfast Love and Justice
segments.gist: God's mercy, faithfulness, and righteousness are praised as vast and life-giving, a fountain of life and light.

segments.title: Prayer for Protection from the Proud
segments.gist: The psalmist asks God to continue loving the upright and to prevent the proud from driving him away.

37.summary: Psalm 37 is a wisdom poem in which David counsels the righteous not to fret over evildoers, urging them to trust in the LORD, do good, and wait patiently, while contrasting the brief prosperity of the wicked with the lasting inheritance of the meek. It combines exhortations, promises of God's provision and protection, and observations on the eventual downfall of the wicked.

segments.title: Exhortation to Trust and Wait
segments.gist: David urges the righteous not to envy evildoers but to trust in the LORD, delight in Him, commit their way to Him, and wait patiently, promising that the meek will inherit the earth.

segments.title: Contrast of Wicked and Righteous
segments.gist: The wicked plot against the righteous but their weapons will fail; the LORD upholds the righteous, and the wicked will perish like smoke.

segments.title: Blessing of the Righteous
segments.gist: The wicked borrow and do not repay, but the righteous are generous and blessed; the LORD upholds the steps of the good man and his descendants are a blessing.

segments.title: Depart from Evil and Do Good
segments.gist: David exhorts to depart from evil and do good, promising that the LORD loves justice and will not forsake His saints, while the wicked will be cut off.

segments.title: Wait on the LORD and Be Saved
segments.gist: The psalm closes with a call to wait on the LORD and keep His way, assuring that He will exalt the righteous and be their salvation and strength in trouble.

38.summary: Psalm 38 is a penitential prayer in which David, suffering under God's heavy hand for his sin, describes his physical and spiritual anguish, the abandonment of friends and the hostility of enemies, and pleads for God's forgiveness and help, confessing his iniquity and trusting in the Lord.

segments.title: David's Anguish Under God's Wrath
segments.gist: David cries out that God's arrows and hand press him down, describing his body as full of disease and his soul deeply troubled because of his sin.

segments.title: Abandoned by Friends and Targeted by Enemies
segments.gist: David laments that his loved ones and friends stand aloof from his plague, while enemies plot and speak mischief against him.

segments.title: Confession and Plea for Help
segments.gist: David confesses his sin and sorrow, declares his hope in God, and begs the Lord not to forsake or be far from him, but to hasten to his aid.

39.summary: Psalm 39 is a prayer of David in which he resolves to guard his speech before the wicked, but his pent-up grief breaks out as he reflects on the brevity and vanity of life. He asks God to forgive his sins and to spare him before he dies, acknowledging that all men are but a passing shadow.

segments.title: David's Resolve to Silence
segments.gist: David decides to watch his words and stay silent before the wicked, but his sorrow grows and he finally speaks.

segments.title: Prayer for Knowledge of End
segments.gist: David asks God to reveal his end and the measure of his days, recognizing the fleeting nature of life.

segments.title: Vanity of Life and Plea for Relief
segments.gist: David acknowledges that man's busy life is vain, and he asks God to remove his affliction and not consume him with rebukes.

segments.title: Final Plea for Mercy
segments.gist: David begs God to hear his prayer and spare him, comparing himself to a stranger and sojourner before he passes away.

40.summary: Psalm 40 is a thanksgiving psalm in which David recalls God lifting him from the miry clay and putting a new song in his mouth, then moves into a prayer for mercy and help against the multitude of his enemies and his own sins.

segments.title: God Lifted Him from the Pit
segments.gist: David waits on the Lord, is drawn from the miry clay, and receives a new song of praise.

segments.title: Obedience More Than Sacrifice
segments.gist: God desires an open ear and a willing heart more than sacrifice; David delights to do God's will.

segments.title: Righteousness Declared in the Congregation
segments.gist: David proclaims God's faithfulness and salvation openly among the great congregation.

segments.title: Innumerable Evils Surround Him
segments.gist: David pleads for God's tender mercies and confesses that his sins have overtaken him.

segments.title: Prayer for Deliverance from Enemies
segments.gist: David asks God to confound his enemies and to help and deliver him speedily.

41.summary: Psalm 41 is a prayer of David for mercy and healing while enemies speak falsely against him and a close friend betrays him. He trusts that God will uphold him and closes with praise to the God of Israel.

segments.title: Blessing on the Merciful
segments.gist: The psalm opens by pronouncing blessing on those who consider the poor, promising God's protection and help in trouble.

segments.title: Enemies Speak Against Him
segments.gist: David describes his enemies speaking evil of him, wishing him dead, and even a close friend betraying him.

segments.title: Plea for Restoration
segments.gist: David asks God to raise him up and restore him, confident that God upholds him in his integrity.

42.summary: The psalmist longs for God like a deer panting for water, remembering past worship and feeling taunted by enemies who ask where his God is. He chides his own soul to hope in God, recalling God's steadfast love and promising to praise him again.

segments.title: Longing for God
segments.gist: The psalmist compares his thirst for God to a deer panting for water and recalls leading worship.

segments.title: Despair and Remembrance
segments.gist: He describes his downcast soul and remembers God from the land of Jordan and Hermon.

segments.title: Lament of Enemies
segments.gist: He cries out to God as his rock, asking why he is forgotten and oppressed by enemies.

43.summary: The psalmist, feeling abandoned by God and oppressed by an ungodly nation, cries out for vindication and deliverance. He recalls past worship in the temple and urges his soul to hope in God, confident that he will again praise him.

segments.title: Plea for vindication
segments.gist: The psalmist asks God to judge him and plead his cause against an ungodly nation and deceitful man.

segments.title: Longing for God's guidance
segments.gist: He asks God to send his light and truth to lead him to God's holy hill and dwelling place.

44.summary: Psalm 44 is a communal lament in which the people of Israel recall God's past deliverance and gift of the land, yet now complain that God has rejected and scattered them despite their covenant faithfulness. They appeal to God to awake and redeem them for the sake of His steadfast love.

segments.title: Recalling God's Past Deliverance
segments.gist: The community recounts how God drove out nations and planted their ancestors, giving them the land not by their own sword but by God's right hand.

segments.title: Lament of Present Rejection
segments.gist: They complain that God has now rejected and humbled them, making them a reproach and a byword among the nations.

segments.title: Claim of Covenant Faithfulness
segments.gist: Despite this suffering, they insist they have not forgotten God or turned from His covenant, yet they are killed for His sake all day long.

segments.title: Plea for God to Awake and Redeem
segments.gist: They cry out for God to awake, not hide His face, and to rise up and redeem them for the sake of His steadfast love.

45.summary: Psalm 45 is a royal wedding song, addressed to the king and then to the bride. The poet praises the king's beauty, valor, and justice, describes his enthronement and love of righteousness, and then addresses the princess bride, who leaves her people to join the king's household, closing with a promise of enduring fame.

segments.title: Prologue and Praise of the King
segments.gist: The psalmist introduces his song and declares the king fairer than the children of men, with grace poured into his lips.

segments.title: The King's Might and Conquest
segments.gist: The king is called to gird on his sword and ride prosperously for truth and meekness, with his right hand showing terrible things.

segments.title: The King's Throne and Righteousness
segments.gist: The king's throne is everlasting, he loves righteousness and hates wickedness, and he is anointed with the oil of gladness above his fellows.

segments.title: The Bride's Arrival and Procession
segments.gist: The daughter is called to forget her people and enter the king's palace, and she is brought to him with joy and gladness.

segments.title: The King's Sons and Everlasting Name
segments.gist: The king's sons will be princes in all the earth, and the psalmist promises to make his name remembered forever.

46.summary: Psalm 46 declares God as the refuge and strength of his people, unshaken even when the earth itself gives way. It pictures the nations raging and kingdoms falling before God's voice, then calls the faithful to behold his desolations and to be still, knowing he is exalted among the nations.

segments.title: God Our Refuge and Strength
segments.gist: The psalm opens by naming God as refuge and strength, present help in trouble, so his people need not fear though the earth be removed.

segments.title: River of God Amid Nations Raging
segments.gist: A river gladdens the city of God; though nations rage and kingdoms move, God utters his voice and the earth melts, and the Lord of hosts is with his people.

segments.title: Behold God's Works, Be Still
segments.gist: The call goes out to behold God's desolations and the wars he ends, followed by the command to be still and know that he is God, exalted among the nations.

47.summary: Psalm 47 is a short hymn calling all peoples to clap their hands and shout to God, who is exalted as the great King over all the earth. It celebrates God's rule over the nations and his choice of Israel, and it closes with a repeated call to praise him with understanding.

segments.title: Call to Praise the King
segments.gist: The psalmist summons all peoples to clap and shout to God, who is awesome and subdues nations under his people.

segments.title: God Ascends with Shouting
segments.gist: God goes up with a shout and trumpet sound; the psalmist calls for songs of praise to the King of all the earth.

segments.title: God Reigns Over Nations
segments.gist: God reigns over the nations from his holy throne, and the princes of the earth gather as the people of Abraham's God.

48.summary: Psalm 48 is a song of Zion, praising God as the great king whose presence in Jerusalem makes the city secure against attacking kings. The people are called to walk around Zion, count its towers, and tell the next generation that God is their guide forever.

segments.title: God praised in His city
segments.gist: The psalm opens with praise for God in His holy mountain, Zion, which is beautiful and the joy of the whole earth.

segments.title: Kings flee in terror
segments.gist: Earthly kings gather but are struck with fear and flee, like ships broken by an east wind, because God is in the city.

segments.title: God's praise in the temple
segments.gist: The people recall God's lovingkindness in the temple and rejoice in His judgments, which bring joy to Zion and Judah.

segments.title: Walk about Zion
segments.gist: The people are told to walk around Zion, count its towers, and tell the next generation that God is their guide forever.

49.summary: This psalm is a wisdom meditation addressed to all peoples, declaring that wealth cannot ransom a life from death. The psalmist contrasts the fate of the foolish who trust in riches with the upright, and closes with the assurance that God will redeem the soul from the grave.

segments.title: Universal call to hear wisdom
segments.gist: The psalmist summons all inhabitants of the world, rich and poor, to listen to his words of wisdom and understanding.

segments.title: Wealth cannot ransom from death
segments.gist: The psalmist declares that no one can redeem a life by wealth, and that both wise and foolish perish, leaving their riches to others.

segments.title: Fate of the foolish vs. the upright
segments.gist: The foolish who trust in themselves are likened to sheep for the grave, but God will redeem the psalmist's soul from the power of Sheol.

segments.title: Do not fear the rich
segments.gist: The psalmist counsels against fearing the wealthy, for they take nothing with them at death, and their honor does not save them from darkness.

50.summary: Psalm 50 presents God summoning all the earth to judgment, declaring that He does not need Israel's sacrifices but demands thanksgiving and obedience. He rebukes the wicked who recite His statutes while practicing theft, adultery, and slander, warning them to repent lest He tear them apart.

segments.title: God Summons the Earth
segments.gist: God, the mighty Lord, calls all people from east to west and comes in glory to judge His people.

segments.title: True Sacrifice of Thanksgiving
segments.gist: God testifies against Israel, saying He does not need their sacrifices but desires thanksgiving and obedience in trouble.

segments.title: Rebuke of the Wicked
segments.gist: God rebukes the wicked who speak His laws but practice theft, adultery, and slander, thinking God is like them.

segments.title: Warning and Promise
segments.gist: God warns the forgetful to repent or be torn apart, and promises honor to those who offer thanksgiving.

51.summary: Psalm 51 is David's plea for mercy after his sin with Bathsheba, as he confesses his transgressions and asks God to cleanse and forgive him. He seeks a clean heart and a renewed spirit, promises to teach transgressors God's ways, and asks for restoration of joy and God's favor, closing with a prayer for Jerusalem's welfare.

segments.title: Plea for Mercy
segments.gist: David asks God for mercy and cleansing according to His lovingkindness and tender mercies.

segments.title: Confession of Sin
segments.gist: David acknowledges his transgressions and sin against God, affirming God's righteousness in judgment.

segments.title: Prayer for Cleansing and Renewal
segments.gist: David asks to be purged with hyssop, washed, and given a clean heart and a steadfast spirit.

segments.title: Promise to Teach and Praise
segments.gist: David vows to teach transgressors God's ways and to praise God, noting that God desires a broken spirit.

segments.title: Prayer for Jerusalem
segments.gist: David asks God to build up Jerusalem and accept sacrifices offered in righteousness.

52.summary: Psalm 52 is a rebuke by David against a powerful, boastful enemy who trusts in riches and plots destruction against the godly. David contrasts the wicked man's coming downfall with the righteous, who trust in God's mercy and will praise Him forever.

segments.title: Rebuke of the Boastful Wicked
segments.gist: David confronts a mighty man who boasts of mischief and devises destruction with a sharp tongue.

segments.title: God Will Destroy the Wicked
segments.gist: God will destroy the wicked man forever, and the righteous will fear and mock his failed trust in riches.

segments.title: The Righteous Trust and Praise
segments.gist: David compares himself to a green olive tree in God's house, trusting in mercy and vowing to praise God forever.

53.summary: Psalm 53 is a wisdom psalm describing the corruption of humanity, where the fool denies God and all have turned aside. It anticipates God's judgment on the wicked who oppress His people, and closes with a prayer for Israel's salvation and the restoration of Jacob.

segments.title: The Fool Denies God
segments.gist: The fool says in his heart there is no God; all are corrupt and none do good, as God looks down from heaven.

segments.title: Wicked Overcome by Fear
segments.gist: The workers of iniquity are struck with fear where no fear was, for God scatters their bones and puts them to shame.

54.summary: Psalm 54 is a short prayer of David asking God to save him from violent enemies who seek his life, and expressing confidence that God will repay them and that David will offer a freewill sacrifice in thanks.

segments.title: David's Plea for Deliverance
segments.gist: David asks God to save him by His name and judge him by His strength, because strangers and oppressors seek his life.

segments.title: God as Helper and Upholder
segments.gist: David declares that God is his helper and upholds his soul, and asks God to repay his enemies' evil.

segments.title: Vow of Freewill Offering
segments.gist: David promises to offer a freewill sacrifice and praise God's name, because God has delivered him from trouble.

55.summary: Psalm 55 is David's prayer of distress over betrayal by a close friend, expressing his longing to escape, his appeal for God to confound his enemies, and his trust that God will sustain him and bring the wicked down.

segments.title: David's Anguished Prayer
segments.gist: David cries out to God, overwhelmed by enemy oppression and the terrors of death.

segments.title: Betrayal by a Friend
segments.gist: David laments the treachery of a close companion and asks God to destroy the wicked.

segments.title: Trust in God's Deliverance
segments.gist: David affirms that God will hear and save him from those who oppose him.

segments.title: God Will Bring Down the Wicked
segments.gist: David describes the deceit of the wicked and declares that God will cast them down.

56.summary: Psalm 56 is a prayer of David when the Philistines seized him in Gath. He asks God for mercy against enemies who oppress and plot against him, declares his trust in God despite fear, and vows to praise God for delivering him from death.

segments.title: Prayer for Mercy
segments.gist: David asks God for mercy as enemies trample and fight against him daily.

segments.title: Trust in God
segments.gist: David declares that when afraid, he will trust in God and praise His word.

segments.title: Enemies Plot
segments.gist: David describes enemies who twist his words and plot against him, and asks God to cast them down.

segments.title: God Records Tears
segments.gist: David asks God to remember his tears and trusts that God will answer when he calls.

segments.title: Praise for God's Word
segments.gist: David praises God's word and declares his trust in God, saying he will not be afraid.

segments.title: Vows and Thanksgiving
segments.gist: David vows to pay his vows to God and thanks Him for delivering him from death.

57.summary: David prays for mercy and refuge under God's wings, surrounded by enemies likened to lions and whose words are sharp swords. He calls on God to be exalted above the heavens, describes his foes falling into their own pit, and closes with steadfast praise and a call for God's glory over all the earth.

segments.title: Prayer for Mercy and Refuge
segments.gist: David cries to God for mercy, trusting in the shadow of God's wings until calamity passes.

segments.title: Enemies Like Lions and a Net
segments.gist: David describes foes as lions and their tongues as sharp swords, and asks God to be exalted.

segments.title: Steadfast Heart Awakes to Praise
segments.gist: David declares his heart is fixed and calls his soul and harp to wake and sing praise.

segments.title: Praise Among the Nations
segments.gist: David vows to praise God among the peoples and ends with a call for God's exaltation and glory.

58.summary: Psalm 58 is a psalm of David that condemns unjust rulers and judges who speak and act wickedly, describing them as venomous and destructive from birth. The psalmist calls for God to break their power and bring them to ruin, and he concludes that the righteous will rejoice when God's justice is executed, affirming that there is a reward for the righteous and a God who judges the earth.

segments.title: Rebuke of Unjust Judges
segments.gist: The psalmist challenges rulers and judges who speak wickedness and judge unjustly, asking if their righteousness is genuine.

segments.title: Wickedness from Birth
segments.gist: The wicked are described as estranged from birth, speaking lies and possessing venom like a deaf adder that stops its ears.

segments.title: Call for Judgment
segments.gist: The psalmist appeals to God to break the teeth of the wicked and cause them to melt away like water and snails.

segments.title: Righteous Rejoice in Justice
segments.gist: The righteous will rejoice when God's vengeance is seen, and people will acknowledge that there is a reward for the righteous and a God who judges.

59.summary: Psalm 59 is a prayer of David asking God for deliverance from enemies who lie in wait to kill him, protesting his innocence and calling for God to punish the wicked. He trusts that God will laugh at the nations and be his defense, and he vows to sing of God's strength and mercy in the morning.

segments.title: Prayer for Deliverance from Enemies
segments.gist: David asks God to save him from bloodthirsty enemies who plot evil and lie in wait for his life.

segments.title: Enemies Return Like Dogs
segments.gist: The enemies return at evening, growling like dogs and speaking arrogantly, but God laughs at them.

segments.title: Confidence in God's Defense
segments.gist: David watches for God, his strength and refuge, and asks God to scatter and bring down the wicked in judgment.

segments.title: Enemies Prowl for Food
segments.gist: The enemies return at evening, growling like dogs and wandering for food, unsatisfied.

segments.title: Vow to Sing of God's Strength
segments.gist: David vows to sing of God's power and mercy in the morning, for God has been his defense and refuge.

60.summary: Psalm 60 is a communal lament in which the psalmist recounts God's anger and defeat, pleads for restoration, and recalls divine oracles promising victory over Edom and other enemies. The psalm closes with a request for God's help, expressing confidence that God will grant triumph.

segments.title: Plea for Restoration
segments.gist: The psalmist describes God's anger and the nation's defeat, asking God to restore and save them.

segments.title: God's Oracle of Victory
segments.gist: God speaks in holiness, promising to divide Shechem and measure the valley of Succoth, claiming Ephraim and Judah.

segments.title: Moab and Edom Subdued
segments.gist: Moab is called God's washpot, and Edom is where God will cast his shoe, with Philistia shouting in triumph.

segments.title: Request for Divine Help
segments.gist: The psalmist asks who will lead them to the fortified city and acknowledges that only God can help.

61.summary: Psalm 61 is a short prayer of David in which he cries out to God from a place of weakness and distance, asking to be led to the rock that is higher than he is. He recalls God's past protection and expresses confidence that God will preserve the king and give him a lasting heritage, closing with a vow of praise.

segments.title: Cry from the ends of the earth
segments.gist: The psalmist calls to God from a distant, overwhelmed place, asking to be led to the rock that is higher than he is.

segments.title: God as refuge and shelter
segments.gist: He recalls God as his refuge and strong tower, and longs to dwell in God's tabernacle under the shelter of his wings.

segments.title: Prayer for the king's life
segments.gist: He asks that the king's life be prolonged for many generations and that he abide before God forever.

62.summary: Psalm 62 is a song of trust in God alone, in which David declares that his soul waits silently for God as his rock and salvation, warns against trusting in oppression, riches, or vanity, and calls the people to pour out their hearts to God, closing with the assurance that power and mercy belong to the Lord.

segments.title: Waiting in silence for God
segments.gist: The psalmist declares that his soul waits in silence for God alone, who is his rock, salvation, and defense, and he will not be greatly moved.

segments.title: Exhortation to trust in God
segments.gist: The psalmist repeats his silent waiting for God and urges the people to trust in him at all times and pour out their hearts before him.

segments.title: Vanity of men and riches
segments.gist: Men of low and high degree are vanity, and the psalmist warns against trusting in oppression or riches, concluding that power and mercy belong to God.

63.summary: Psalm 63 is a psalm of David, described as being in the wilderness of Judah, in which he expresses deep thirst for God and confidence in His protection. He contrasts his longing for God with the fate of those who seek his life, and concludes with praise and the assurance that the king will rejoice in God.

segments.title: Thirsting for God in the Wilderness
segments.gist: David declares his earnest longing for God in a dry land, comparing his thirst to physical thirst.

segments.title: Praise for God's Lovingkindness
segments.gist: David recalls seeing God's power and glory in the sanctuary and praises His lovingkindness, lifting up his hands.

segments.title: Meditation in the Night Watches
segments.gist: David remembers God on his bed and meditates through the night, rejoicing under the shadow of God's wings.

segments.title: Destruction of Enemies
segments.gist: David expresses confidence that those seeking his life will go into the lower parts of the earth and fall by the sword.

64.summary: Psalm 64 is a prayer for deliverance from treacherous enemies who plot secretly and attack with words like arrows. The psalmist asks God to strike them down suddenly, and he envisions the righteous rejoicing and taking refuge in God.

segments.title: Prayer for Protection from Plotters
segments.gist: The psalmist asks God to hide him from the secret plots and violent words of the wicked, who aim bitter words like arrows.

segments.title: God's Sudden Judgment
segments.gist: God will shoot at the wicked suddenly, and their own tongues will cause their downfall, leading all who see to fear.

65.summary: Psalm 65 is a hymn of praise to God for His forgiveness, His rule over creation, and His provision of rain and harvest. The psalmist calls all people to worship, describes God's mighty acts, and closes with pictures of abundant pastures and grain.

segments.title: Praise and Forgiveness in Zion
segments.gist: Praise is due to God in Zion; He hears prayer, forgives transgressions, and blesses those He draws near.

segments.title: God's Awesome Deeds and Rule
segments.gist: God answers with awesome deeds, establishes the mountains, calms the seas, and silences distant peoples.

segments.title: God's Provision for the Earth
segments.gist: God waters the earth, enriches it, and crowns the year with bounty, causing pastures and valleys to shout for joy.

66.summary: Psalm 66 is a hymn of praise calling all the earth to shout joyfully to God for His awesome deeds, including His deliverance of Israel through the sea and His refining trials. The psalmist then shifts to personal testimony, describing how he cried out to God and was heard, and he invites the congregation to listen as he declares what God has done for him, vowing to offer sacrifices and pay his vows.

segments.title: Call to Praise God's Deeds
segments.gist: The psalmist summons all the earth to shout joyfully to God and sing of His glorious works and great power.

segments.title: God's Awesome Works Recalled
segments.gist: The people are invited to see God's deeds, especially His turning the sea into dry land and His rule over the nations.

segments.title: Praise for Deliverance Through Trial
segments.gist: The nations are called to bless God for preserving His people, whom He tested and refined but ultimately brought to a place of abundance.

segments.title: Vows and Offerings Promised
segments.gist: The psalmist declares he will enter God's house with burnt offerings to fulfill vows made in distress, including sacrifices of fatlings and bulls.

segments.title: Personal Testimony of Answered Prayer
segments.gist: The psalmist invites all who fear God to hear what He has done for him, recounting that God heard his prayer and did not withhold His mercy.

67.summary: Psalm 67 is a short prayer asking God to be merciful and to bless Israel, so that His way may be known on earth and His saving health among all nations. It calls the peoples to praise God and looks forward to a fruitful harvest and universal fear of Him.

segments.title: Prayer for mercy and blessing
segments.gist: The psalmist asks God to be merciful, bless, and cause His face to shine, so His way may be known on earth.

segments.title: Call for universal praise
segments.gist: The peoples are invited to praise God, who judges righteously and governs the nations.

segments.title: Earth's increase and global fear
segments.gist: The earth yields her increase, God blesses His people, and all ends of the earth fear Him.

68.summary: Psalm 68 is a victory hymn that calls God to arise and scatter his enemies, then recounts his march from Sinai through the wilderness to Zion. It celebrates God as the defender of the vulnerable, the giver of abundant rain and bounty, and the triumphant king who ascends on high and receives gifts from men, ending with a call for all kingdoms to sing praise to him.

segments.title: God Arises, Enemies Scatter
segments.gist: The psalmist calls God to arise and scatter his enemies, while the righteous rejoice and sing praise to his name.

segments.title: God's March Through the Wilderness
segments.gist: God is recalled marching before his people through the wilderness, giving rain and restoring the inheritance.

segments.title: Women Publish the Victory
segments.gist: The Lord gives the word, and women publish the news of kings fleeing while the people divide the spoil.

segments.title: God's Chariots and Ascension
segments.gist: God's mountain is exalted above Bashan; he rides through the heavens and ascends on high, leading captivity captive.

segments.title: God Saves and Wounds Enemies
segments.gist: God is praised for daily benefits and salvation; he will wound the heads of his enemies and bring them from Bashan and the depths.

segments.title: Procession into the Sanctuary
segments.gist: The people's procession into the sanctuary is described, with singers and musicians among the tribes.

segments.title: Prayer for Power over Nations
segments.gist: The psalmist asks God to strengthen his people and rebuke the nations and beasts, so that they submit with tribute.

segments.title: All Kingdoms Called to Praise
segments.gist: All kingdoms are called to sing to God, who rides on the heavens and gives strength and power to his people.

69.summary: Psalm 69 is a lament in which David cries out to God for rescue from enemies who hate him without cause, describing his suffering and asking for deliverance. He appeals to God's mercy, asks for judgment on his adversaries, and vows praise when God answers, while the psalm closes with a call for heaven and earth to praise God and a note that God will save Zion.

segments.title: Cry for Rescue
segments.gist: The psalmist pleads for God to save him from drowning in trouble and from those who hate him without cause.

segments.title: Suffering and Reproach
segments.gist: He confesses his foolishness and describes being mocked and rejected by family and leaders for his zeal for God's house.

segments.title: Prayer for Deliverance
segments.gist: He asks God to answer him in mercy, rescue him from the pit and from enemies, and he recounts his reproach and broken heart.

segments.title: Imprecation on Enemies
segments.gist: He asks God to turn their table into a snare, pour out wrath on them, and blot them from the book of the living.

segments.title: Praise and Promise
segments.gist: He prays for God to lift him up and vows to praise God's name, which pleases God more than sacrifice; the humble will be glad.

segments.title: Creation Called to Praise
segments.gist: He calls heaven, earth, seas, and all creatures to praise God, who will save Zion and let his servants dwell there.

70.summary: Psalm 70 is a short urgent prayer for deliverance, in which David asks God to hurry to his aid, calls for the shame and confusion of those who seek his life, and asks that those who seek God rejoice. It closes with a plea for God not to delay, acknowledging his own lowly and needy state.

71.summary: An elderly psalmist, beset by enemies who claim God has forsaken him, prays for deliverance and refuge, recalls God's faithfulness from his youth, and vows to praise God and declare His righteousness to the next generation.

segments.title: Prayer for Deliverance
segments.gist: The psalmist asks God to rescue him from wicked enemies and be his rock of refuge.

segments.title: Trust from Youth
segments.gist: He recalls trusting God from birth and asks that his life be a praise and example to many.

segments.title: Plea in Old Age
segments.gist: He asks God not to forsake him in old age and prays for his enemies' defeat and shame.

segments.title: Vow of Praise
segments.gist: He vows to hope continually and to recount God's righteousness and salvation all day.

segments.title: Declaring God's Power
segments.gist: He commits to declaring God's power to the next generation and trusts God to revive and comfort him.

segments.title: Song of Praise
segments.gist: He promises to praise God with music and joy, confident that his enemies will be put to shame.

72.summary: Psalm 72 is a royal prayer for the king, asking God to give him justice and righteousness so that he may rule the people fairly, defend the poor, and bring peace. It envisions a reign that extends from sea to sea, with all kings and nations serving him, and it closes with a doxology blessing God's glorious name.

segments.title: Prayer for Righteous Rule
segments.gist: The psalmist asks God to endow the king with justice and righteousness so that he may judge the people fairly and defend the poor.

segments.title: Universal Dominion
segments.gist: The king's dominion will extend from sea to sea and to the ends of the earth, with all kings and nations serving him.

segments.title: Deliverance of the Needy
segments.gist: The king will deliver the poor and needy, have pity on the weak, and redeem their lives from oppression and violence.

segments.title: Blessings and Enduring Name
segments.gist: The king will live, receive gold, and be prayed for; grain will flourish, and his name will endure forever.

segments.title: Doxology and Conclusion
segments.gist: The psalm ends with a blessing to the LORD God of Israel for his wondrous works, and a note that the prayers of Jesse's son are ended.

73.summary: Asaph opens with a confession that his feet nearly slipped when he envied the prosperity of the wicked, who seem to live without trouble and die in peace. He describes their arrogance and the doubts their success stirred in him, until he enters the sanctuary and understands their end. He then repents of his bitterness, acknowledges God's continual guidance, and rests in the nearness of God as his portion.

segments.title: Asaph's confession of near stumbling
segments.gist: Asaph admits that his feet almost slipped when he envied the prosperity of the wicked.

segments.title: The prosperity and arrogance of the wicked
segments.gist: The wicked enjoy ease, health, and wealth, speak proudly, and seem to escape trouble while oppressing others.

segments.title: Doubt resolved in the sanctuary
segments.gist: Asaph questions whether his purity was in vain and finds understanding only when he enters God's sanctuary.

segments.title: The wicked's sudden destruction
segments.gist: God sets the wicked in slippery places and brings them to desolation, which makes Asaph realize his former bitterness and ignorance.

segments.title: Asaph's trust in God's guidance
segments.gist: Asaph affirms that God holds his hand, guides him, and is his portion; he desires nothing on earth besides God and finds nearness to God his good.

74.summary: Psalm 74 is a communal lament in which the psalmist pleads with God to remember his covenant people, who have been devastated by enemies. The sanctuary has been desecrated and burned, and the psalmist appeals to God's past acts of creation and deliverance, asking him to arise and defend his cause against the scoffing foes.

segments.title: Plea for God to Remember
segments.gist: The psalmist cries out for God to remember his people and the Mount Zion where he dwells, asking why his anger burns against his flock.

segments.title: Enemies Desecrate the Sanctuary
segments.gist: The foes roar in the sanctuary, set up their banners, and break down the carved work with axes and hammers, burning the holy place to the ground.

segments.title: No Signs or Prophets Remain
segments.gist: The people see no signs and have no prophet; they ask how long the adversary will blaspheme and why God's hand is withdrawn.

segments.title: God's Past Deliverance Recalled
segments.gist: The psalmist recalls God as king from of old, who divided the sea, crushed Leviathan, and established the sun, moon, and seasons.

segments.title: Appeal for God to Arise
segments.gist: The psalmist asks God to remember how fools reproach him and to arise to defend the poor and his own cause against the enemy.

75.summary: Psalm 75 is a communal thanksgiving and oracle in which the people praise God for His nearness and wondrous works. God Himself speaks, declaring that He will judge with equity and cut off the wicked, while the psalmist warns the boastful and praises God for His righteous judgment.

segments.title: Thanksgiving for God's Nearness
segments.gist: The congregation gives thanks to God, recounting His wondrous works and affirming that His name is near.

segments.title: Warning to the Boastful
segments.gist: The psalmist warns the wicked not to boast or speak with a stiff neck.

segments.title: God Alone Exalts and Judges
segments.gist: God is the one who lifts up and brings down; His cup of judgment is poured out for the wicked.

segments.title: Praise and Promise of Judgment
segments.gist: The psalmist vows to praise God forever and declares that the horns of the wicked will be cut off, while the righteous will be exalted.

76.summary: Psalm 76 is a song of Zion celebrating God's presence in Judah and Jerusalem, where He has broken the weapons of war and is feared by kings and nations. It praises God as the judge who saves the humble and calls all people to bring offerings to Him.

segments.title: God Known in Judah
segments.gist: God is known in Judah and His name is great in Israel; His tabernacle and dwelling are in Salem and Zion.

segments.title: God Breaks Weapons of War
segments.gist: God is glorious and excellent, breaking the arrows, shield, sword, and battle, and defeating the stouthearted.

segments.title: God's Judgment from Heaven
segments.gist: God is feared when He arises to judgment, and He saves the meek of the earth.

segments.title: Vows and Offerings to God
segments.gist: Human wrath praises God, and all are called to vow and bring offerings to the feared Lord who cuts off princes.

77.summary: The psalmist cries out to God in a time of deep distress, recalling God's past deliverance of Israel and wondering whether God has withdrawn his mercy. He resolves to remember the mighty works of God, especially the Exodus and the shepherding of his people.

segments.title: Cry to God in Trouble
segments.gist: The psalmist lifts his voice to God, seeking help in the day of trouble, and meditates on God at night.

segments.title: Doubts and Questions
segments.gist: He lies awake and questions whether God has forgotten to be gracious and whether his promises have failed.

segments.title: Remembering God's Works
segments.gist: He resolves to remember the works of the Lord and meditates on God's mighty deeds and redemption of his people.

segments.title: God's Power in Exodus
segments.gist: He describes God's power over the waters and his leading of his people like a flock through the sea.

78.summary: Psalm 78 recounts Israel's history from Egypt to David's reign, alternating between God's mighty deeds and the people's repeated rebellion. It warns each generation to learn from the past and not repeat the faithlessness of their ancestors, while highlighting God's persistent mercy and choice of David as shepherd.

segments.title: Call to Teach Coming Generations
segments.gist: The psalmist urges Israel to listen and pass down the story of God's works so each generation may trust and obey.

segments.title: Ephraim's Failure and God's Wonders
segments.gist: Ephraim's armed men turned back, despite God's mighty acts: dividing the sea and bringing water from the rock.

segments.title: Rebellion in the Wilderness
segments.gist: The people tested God in the desert, demanding food; God gave manna and quail but struck them down for their greed.

segments.title: God's Mercy Despite Persistent Sin
segments.gist: Though the people kept sinning and doubting, God was merciful, forgiving and remembering they were but flesh.

segments.title: Plagues and Exodus Recounted
segments.gist: The psalm recalls how often Israel rebelled, and how God brought plagues on Egypt and led his people to safety.

segments.title: From Shiloh's Rejection to David's Reign
segments.gist: Israel's continued rebellion led God to reject Shiloh and choose Judah, raising David as shepherd of his people.

79.summary: Psalm 79 is a communal lament over the destruction of Jerusalem and the defilement of the temple. The psalmist describes the dead left unburied and Israel's reproach among the nations, then pleads for God's mercy, forgiveness, and vengeance on the enemies, ending with a vow of praise.

segments.title: Nations Invade and Defile Temple
segments.gist: The nations have invaded God's inheritance, defiled the holy temple, and left Jerusalem in ruins with dead bodies unburied.

segments.title: Plea for Anger to Turn
segments.gist: The psalmist asks how long God will be angry and calls for His wrath to be poured on the nations that do not know Him.

segments.title: Confession and Request for Mercy
segments.gist: The psalmist confesses past sins and asks God to forgive and help, so that His name is not mocked among the heathen.

segments.title: Vengeance on Enemies
segments.gist: The psalmist asks God to hear the prisoners' sighing and repay the neighboring nations sevenfold for their reproach.

80.summary: Psalm 80 is a communal lament in which the psalmist appeals to the Shepherd of Israel to restore his people. The congregation recalls how God brought Israel out of Egypt like a vine and planted it, but now the vine is broken down and its fruit devoured by enemies. The psalm closes with repeated pleas for God to turn again, shine his face, and revive the nation.

segments.title: Plea to the Shepherd of Israel
segments.gist: The psalmist calls on the Shepherd of Israel, enthroned above the cherubim, to shine forth and save his people.

segments.title: Lament over God's Anger
segments.gist: The people ask how long God will be angry against their prayer and describe being fed with tears and made a strife to neighbors.

segments.title: The Vine Brought from Egypt
segments.gist: Israel is pictured as a vine brought out of Egypt, planted and flourishing until its branches reached the sea and the river.

segments.title: The Vine Broken Down
segments.gist: The psalmist laments that the vine's hedges are broken, so passersby and wild beasts devour it, and asks God to return and visit it.

segments.title: Plea for Revival
segments.gist: The psalmist asks God to strengthen the son of man at his right hand and promises not to turn back if revived, repeating the call for God to shine and save.

81.summary: Psalm 81 is a festival song calling Israel to joyful worship, recalling God's deliverance from Egypt and his command against foreign gods. God laments that his people would not listen, so he gave them over to their stubborn hearts, yet he promises to subdue their enemies and feed them with honey from the rock if they would only obey.

segments.title: Call to Festival Praise
segments.gist: The psalmist summons Israel to sing, play instruments, and blow the trumpet at the appointed feast.

segments.title: God Recalls Egypt's Deliverance
segments.gist: God reminds his people how he freed them from burdens and answered them from the secret place of thunder.

segments.title: Exhortation to Hear and Obey
segments.gist: God warns Israel to listen and have no foreign god, recalling how he brought them out of Egypt and promised to fill their mouths.

segments.title: Israel's Refusal and Consequence
segments.gist: God laments that his people would not listen, so he gave them over to their own stubborn hearts and counsels.

segments.title: Promise of Blessing for Obedience
segments.gist: God expresses longing that Israel would walk in his ways, promising to subdue their enemies and feed them with the finest wheat and honey.

82.summary: Psalm 82 is a short psalm in which God is depicted as standing in the divine assembly, rebuking the gods or judges for judging unjustly and showing partiality to the wicked. He calls them to defend the poor and fatherless, and pronounces that they will die like men, after which the psalmist asks God to arise and judge the earth.

segments.title: Rebuke for Unjust Judgment
segments.gist: God rebukes the judges for judging unjustly and favoring the wicked, and calls them to defend the poor and needy.

segments.title: They Shall Die Like Men
segments.gist: Though called gods and children of the Most High, they will die like men and fall like any prince.

83.summary: Psalm 83 is a communal lament in which the psalmist pleads with God not to remain silent while a coalition of surrounding nations plots to destroy Israel and erase its name. The prayer recounts past victories over Midian, Sisera, and Oreb, asking God to make these new enemies like chaff and to bring them to shame so they may seek His name.

segments.title: Plea Against Enemy Plot
segments.gist: The psalmist cries for God not to be silent as enemies conspire against Israel.

segments.title: Nations Conspire Together
segments.gist: A coalition of nations—Edom, Ishmael, Moab, Ammon, and others—forms a covenant against Israel.

segments.title: Remember Past Victories
segments.gist: The psalmist asks God to act as in past defeats of Midian, Sisera, and Oreb.

segments.title: Make Enemies Like Chaff
segments.gist: The prayer asks God to scatter the enemies like chaff and fire, and to bring them to shame so they seek His name.

84.summary: Psalm 84 is a pilgrimage song expressing longing for the courts of the Lord, celebrating the blessedness of those who dwell in and travel to God's house, and concluding with a prayer for God's favor upon the king and the people.

segments.title: Longing for the Lord's Courts
segments.gist: The psalmist expresses deep longing for the courts of the Lord, envying even the sparrow and swallow that nest near the altars.

segments.title: Blessed Pilgrims on the Way
segments.gist: Those whose strength is in God are blessed as they pass through the valley of Baca, making it a place of springs and going from strength to strength.

segments.title: Prayer for the Anointed King
segments.gist: The psalmist prays to the God of hosts to hear his prayer and to look upon the face of the anointed king.

segments.title: Better a Day in God's Courts
segments.gist: The psalmist declares that one day in God's courts is better than a thousand elsewhere, and that the Lord is a sun and shield, giving grace and glory to the upright.
