85.summary: Psalm 85 is a communal prayer for restoration, recalling God's past favor to Israel and asking for renewed mercy and salvation. It closes with a vision of God's salvation near to those who fear Him, where mercy and truth meet and righteousness and peace kiss.

segments.title: Recalling Past Favor
segments.gist: The psalmist recalls how God showed favor to the land and restored the fortunes of Jacob.

segments.title: Plea for Restoration
segments.gist: The people ask God to turn from anger and revive them, that they may rejoice in His mercy.

segments.title: Promise of Peace
segments.gist: The psalmist listens for God's promise of peace and envisions salvation near, with mercy and truth meeting.

86.summary: Psalm 86 is a prayer of David in which he asks God to hear and help him, appealing to God's mercy and his own devotion. He praises God's uniqueness and asks for guidance and a united heart, then requests deliverance from enemies and a sign of God's favor.

segments.title: David's Plea for Mercy
segments.gist: David asks God to hear him, trusts in God, and appeals for mercy and help in his time of trouble.

segments.title: Praise of God's Uniqueness
segments.gist: David declares that no other god compares to the Lord, and all nations will worship Him for His great deeds.

segments.title: Request for Guidance and Thanks
segments.gist: David asks God to teach him His way and unite his heart to fear God's name, then thanks God for His mercy.

segments.title: Deliverance from Enemies
segments.gist: David describes arrogant enemies and asks God for deliverance, appealing to God's mercy and requesting a sign of favor.

87.summary: Psalm 87 is a short song of Zion, declaring that the city God founded on the holy mountains is beloved above all the dwellings of Jacob. It looks forward to the inclusion of foreign nations—Rahab, Babylon, Philistia, Tyre, and Ethiopia—who will be counted as born in Zion, and it praises Zion as the source of all joy.

segments.title: Zion, God's Beloved City
segments.gist: The psalmist declares that God's foundation is in the holy mountains and that He loves Zion's gates more than all the dwellings of Jacob.

segments.title: Nations Counted in Zion
segments.gist: God records Rahab, Babylon, Philistia, Tyre, and Ethiopia as peoples born in Zion, and He establishes Zion itself.

88.summary: A lament attributed to Heman the Ezrahite, in which the psalmist cries out to God from deep distress, feeling abandoned among the dead and under God's wrath. He describes his suffering, the loss of friends, and the darkness that surrounds him, yet he continues to call on God day and night.

segments.title: Cry to God Day and Night
segments.gist: The psalmist appeals to the Lord for help, declaring that he cries out day and night.

segments.title: Overwhelmed and Among the Dead
segments.gist: He describes his soul as full of troubles and himself as counted among those who go down to the pit.

segments.title: Afflicted and Isolated
segments.gist: He laments that his friends have abandoned him and questions whether God's wonders are known in the grave.

segments.title: Darkness and Wrath Surround
segments.gist: He continues to pray at dawn, but feels surrounded by God's wrath and covered by darkness, with loved ones far away.

89.summary: Psalm 89 is a royal lament that recounts God's covenant with David and His promises of enduring dynasty, then abruptly turns to a complaint that God has cast off His anointed and allowed enemies to triumph. The psalmist calls on God to remember His covenant and asks how long His wrath will last, ending with a blessing on the Lord.

segments.title: Praise for God's Faithfulness
segments.gist: The psalmist declares he will sing of God's mercies and faithfulness forever, praising His covenant love.

segments.title: God's Power in Creation
segments.gist: The heavens praise God's wonders; He rules the sea and crushed Rahab, and the people who know Him rejoice.

segments.title: Covenant with David Recounted
segments.gist: God speaks of His covenant with David, promising an enduring dynasty and discipline for his descendants.

segments.title: Complaint of Abandonment
segments.gist: The psalmist laments that God has cast off His anointed, broken the covenant, and let enemies prevail.

segments.title: Plea for God to Remember
segments.gist: The psalmist asks how long God will hide His face and calls on Him to remember His servant's reproach.

90.summary: This psalm is titled 'A Prayer of Moses the man of God.' It contrasts God's eternal nature with human frailty and mortality, acknowledges that human life is brief and marked by sin and divine wrath, and ends with a plea for God to teach wisdom, show compassion, and establish the work of human hands.

segments.title: God's Eternity and Human Frailty
segments.gist: The psalmist declares God as eternal dwelling place and creator, who turns humans back to dust, contrasting divine permanence with human brevity.

segments.title: Human Sin and Divine Wrath
segments.gist: The psalmist acknowledges that humans are consumed by God's anger because of their sins, and asks for wisdom to number their days.

segments.title: Plea for Compassion and Favor
segments.gist: The psalmist pleads with God to return, have compassion, satisfy with mercy, and establish the work of their hands.

91.summary: Psalm 91 is a song of trust in God as a refuge and fortress. It describes deliverance from dangers and plagues, promises angelic protection, and concludes with God's assurance of rescue, honor, and long life to those who love Him.

segments.title: Dwelling in the secret place
segments.gist: The psalmist declares that those who dwell in God's secret place will abide under His shadow and calls Him a refuge and fortress.

segments.title: Deliverance from snares and plagues
segments.gist: God delivers from traps and deadly pestilence; thousands may fall, but the faithful will see the reward of the wicked.

segments.title: Angelic protection for the faithful
segments.gist: Because God is the dwelling place, no evil will befall; angels will guard and bear up the faithful, who will tread on lions and serpents.

segments.title: God's promise to the loving
segments.gist: God promises to deliver, exalt, answer, be with, honor, satisfy with long life, and show salvation to those who love Him.

92.summary: Psalm 92 is a song for the Sabbath that opens with praise for God's steadfast love and faithfulness, then contrasts the wicked who flourish briefly with the righteous who are planted in God's house and flourish forever. The psalmist declares God's works and celebrates the LORD as upright and faithful.

segments.title: Praise in the Morning and Night
segments.gist: The psalmist declares it good to give thanks and sing praise to the LORD, proclaiming His lovingkindness and faithfulness.

segments.title: Rejoicing in God's Works
segments.gist: The psalmist rejoices in the works of the LORD and praises His deep thoughts.

segments.title: The Foolish and Wicked Perish
segments.gist: The senseless do not understand that the wicked flourish only to be destroyed forever, while the LORD is exalted.

segments.title: The Psalmist's Strength and Victory
segments.gist: The psalmist is lifted up like a wild ox and sees the defeat of his enemies.

segments.title: The Righteous Flourish Like Trees
segments.gist: The righteous are compared to palm and cedar trees, planted in the LORD's house, flourishing and declaring His uprightness.

93.summary: Psalm 93 is a short hymn declaring the LORD's kingly reign, portraying Him as robed in majesty and strength, established from everlasting. It contrasts the raging floods and waters with the LORD's might, and concludes that His testimonies are sure and holiness befits His house forever.

segments.title: The LORD reigns in majesty
segments.gist: The LORD is clothed with majesty and strength, and the world is established so it cannot be moved.

segments.title: Waters lift up their voice
segments.gist: The floods and waves roar, but the LORD on high is mightier than all these waters.

94.summary: Psalm 94 is a prayer for God to execute justice against the proud and wicked who oppress His people, contrasting their temporary prosperity with God's sure judgment. It moves from lament and rebuke of the wicked to confidence in the LORD as a refuge, ending with the assurance that He will cut off the wicked and not forsake His heritage.

segments.title: Call for Vengeance on the Proud
segments.gist: The psalmist cries out to God to avenge the proud and wicked who crush His people and kill the helpless.

segments.title: Rebuke to the Foolish
segments.gist: The wicked are rebuked as foolish, reminded that God who made the ear and eye sees and knows their thoughts.

segments.title: Blessed Is the Chastened
segments.gist: The man whom God chastens and teaches is blessed, for God will give him rest and will not cast off His people.

segments.title: The LORD My Help
segments.gist: The psalmist recalls that the LORD helped him against evildoers and upheld him when his foot slipped, giving comfort.

segments.title: God Will Cut Off the Wicked
segments.gist: The psalmist affirms that God will not fellowship with wicked rulers but will bring their iniquity upon them and cut them off.

95.summary: Psalm 95 opens with a call to sing and shout to the LORD as the great God and King above all gods, who holds the earth and sea. It then shifts to a warning, urging the people to hear His voice today and not harden their hearts as at Meribah and Massah, where their fathers tested Him and failed to enter His rest.

segments.title: Call to Worship the Rock
segments.gist: The psalmist invites singing and thanksgiving to the LORD, the great King above all gods, who holds the earth and sea.

segments.title: Worship the Maker and Shepherd
segments.gist: The people are called to bow before the LORD their Maker, for He is God and they are the people of His pasture.

segments.title: Warning Against Hardening Hearts
segments.gist: The psalmist warns not to harden hearts as at Meribah and Massah, where the fathers tested God and were denied His rest.

96.summary: Psalm 96 is a call for all the earth to sing a new song to the LORD, declaring His glory among the nations and His greatness above all gods. It summons the nations to ascribe glory to Him, to worship Him in holiness, and it culminates in a vision of all creation rejoicing because He comes to judge the world in righteousness and truth.

segments.title: Sing a New Song
segments.gist: The psalmist calls all the earth to sing a new song to the LORD, to declare His glory among the nations and His wonders among all people.

segments.title: The LORD Is Great
segments.gist: The LORD is great and greatly praised, above all gods; the gods of the nations are idols, but the LORD made the heavens and is honored in majesty.

segments.title: Ascribe Glory to the LORD
segments.gist: The nations are told to ascribe glory and strength to the LORD, to bring an offering and worship Him in the beauty of holiness.

segments.title: Creation Rejoices at His Coming
segments.gist: The heavens, earth, sea, fields, and trees are called to rejoice before the LORD, for He comes to judge the world with righteousness and truth.

97.summary: Psalm 97 declares the LORD's reign over all the earth, contrasting the downfall of idolaters with the joy of Zion. It calls the righteous to rejoice and to hate evil, promising light and gladness for the upright.

segments.title: The LORD's Majestic Reign
segments.gist: The LORD reigns in majesty, with clouds, fire, and lightning displaying His power as the earth trembles and the heavens declare His righteousness.

segments.title: Idolaters Confounded, Zion Rejoices
segments.gist: All who serve idols are put to shame, while Zion hears and rejoices because the LORD is exalted above all gods.

segments.title: Exhortation to the Righteous
segments.gist: The righteous are called to hate evil, with the promise that the LORD preserves them and gives light and gladness to the upright.

98.summary: Psalm 98 is a hymn calling all the earth to sing a new song to the LORD, celebrating His salvation, righteousness, and faithful love to Israel. It summons the whole creation—sea, rivers, and mountains—to rejoice because He comes to judge the world with righteousness and equity.

segments.title: Sing a new song
segments.gist: The psalmist calls for a new song to the LORD, praising His marvelous works, revealed salvation, and righteousness before the nations.

segments.title: All earth rejoices
segments.gist: All the earth is summoned to make a joyful noise, sing, and praise the LORD with harp and trumpet before the King.

segments.title: Creation joins praise
segments.gist: The sea, the world, the floods, and the hills are called to rejoice together because the LORD comes to judge the earth righteously.

99.summary: Psalm 99 is a hymn declaring the LORD's reign from Zion, exalted above all peoples. It calls for praise of His great and awesome name, recalls His justice through Moses, Aaron, and Samuel who called on Him and were answered, and closes with a call to exalt the LORD and worship at His holy hill.

segments.title: The LORD reigns in Zion
segments.gist: The LORD sits enthroned between the cherubim; let the peoples tremble and praise His great and awesome name.

segments.title: Exalt the just King
segments.gist: The King's strength loves justice; He establishes equity in Jacob, so exalt the LORD and worship at His footstool.

segments.title: God answered His priests
segments.gist: Moses, Aaron, and Samuel called on the LORD and He answered them from the pillar of cloud; exalt Him for He is holy.

100.summary: Psalm 100 is a short call to all the earth to worship the LORD with gladness and singing, because he made his people and cares for them like a shepherd. It closes by urging entry into his gates with thanksgiving, praising him as good, merciful, and faithful to all generations.

segments.title: Call to Joyful Service
segments.gist: All the earth is summoned to shout, serve the LORD with gladness, and come before him with singing.

segments.title: The LORD Made Us
segments.gist: The psalm names the LORD as God and maker, whose people and sheep he is.

101.summary: Psalm 101 is a short royal psalm in which the speaker vows to sing of mercy and judgment and to live with integrity. He resolves to shun the wicked, the proud, and the deceitful, and to surround himself only with the faithful, promising to rid the land of evildoers.

segments.title: Vow to live blamelessly
segments.gist: The psalmist pledges to sing of mercy and judgment and to walk with a perfect heart, setting no wicked thing before his eyes.

segments.title: Rejecting the wicked
segments.gist: He resolves to silence slanderers, reject the proud and deceitful, and surround himself with the faithful of the land.

102.summary: A suffering psalmist, afflicted and wasting away, cries out to God for help and contrasts his own fleeting days with God's eternal nature. He takes comfort that God will arise, rebuild Zion, and be praised by future generations, and he prays for deliverance so he may declare God's praise.

segments.title: The afflicted cry for help
segments.gist: The psalmist pours out his complaint: his days vanish like smoke, his bones burn, enemies reproach him, and he lies awake like a lonely bird.

segments.title: God's eternal rule and Zion's restoration
segments.gist: He contrasts God's everlasting throne with his own frailty, and declares that God will arise, rebuild Zion, and receive the worship of all nations.

segments.title: Prayer for strength and God's unchanging years
segments.gist: He asks God to shorten his suffering and not take him away early, then closes by praising God's eternal existence and the security of his servants' children.

103.summary: Psalm 103 is a hymn of praise in which David calls his own soul and all creation to bless the LORD for His benefits: forgiveness, healing, redemption, steadfast love, and renewal. He contrasts God's mercy and fatherly compassion toward frail humans with His eternal rule, and closes by summoning angels and all His works to join the praise.

segments.title: Call to Bless the LORD
segments.gist: David urges his soul to bless the LORD and remember His benefits: forgiveness, healing, redemption, love, and renewal.

segments.title: The LORD's Mercy and Compassion
segments.gist: The LORD works righteousness and shows mercy to Israel; He is slow to anger and treats His people with fatherly compassion, remembering they are dust.

segments.title: Human Frailty and God's Steadfast Love
segments.gist: Human life is like grass that quickly fades, but the LORD's steadfast love endures forever for those who fear Him and keep His covenant.

segments.title: Universal Praise to the LORD
segments.gist: The LORD's throne is established in the heavens; angels, all His works, and the psalmist's own soul are called to bless Him.

104.summary: Psalm 104 is a hymn praising God as creator and sustainer of the world, describing the heavens, the earth, the sea, and all living things. It celebrates God's provision for every creature and concludes with a prayer that sinners be removed and a vow of lifelong praise.

segments.title: Praise to the Creator
segments.gist: The psalmist blesses the Lord and describes God clothed with honor and light, stretching out the heavens.

segments.title: God Establishes the Earth
segments.gist: God sets the earth on its foundations and controls the waters, which flee at His rebuke.

segments.title: God Waters and Provides
segments.gist: God sends springs and rain to nourish plants and animals, providing food and habitat for all creatures.

segments.title: Sun and Moon Order Time
segments.gist: God appoints the moon for seasons and the sun for days, causing animals to hunt at night and humans to work by day.

segments.title: God Sustains All Creatures
segments.gist: The psalmist marvels at the sea's creatures and declares that all life depends on God's open hand and Spirit.

segments.title: Glory and Praise Forever
segments.gist: The psalmist prays for God's glory to endure, vows to sing praise as long as he lives, and asks for sinners to be removed.

105.summary: Psalm 105 is a historical hymn recounting God's covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and His faithful protection of Israel from the patriarchs through the exodus and the conquest of Canaan. It calls the people to remember God's wondrous works and to praise Him for bringing them out of Egypt with signs and wonders, giving them the land promised to their fathers.

segments.title: Call to Praise and Seek God
segments.gist: The psalmist urges thanksgiving, calling on all to seek the Lord and remember His marvelous works.

segments.title: God's Covenant with the Patriarchs
segments.gist: God's covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob is recalled, promising Canaan as their inheritance.

segments.title: Protection of the Chosen Few
segments.gist: When Israel was few and strangers, God protected them and rebuked kings on their behalf.

segments.title: Joseph Sold and Raised Up
segments.gist: God sent Joseph ahead through slavery and imprisonment, then raised him to govern Egypt.

segments.title: Plagues Strike Egypt
segments.gist: Israel multiplied in Egypt, and God sent plagues and signs to break Pharaoh's resistance.

segments.title: Exodus and Conquest of Canaan
segments.gist: God brought Israel out with silver and gold, provided food and water, and gave them the lands of the nations.

106.summary: Psalm 106 recounts Israel's repeated rebellion against God—from the exodus through the judges and into the monarchy—contrasting God's steadfast mercy with the people's forgetfulness and idolatry. It closes with a plea for God to gather the scattered nation and a doxology of praise.

segments.title: Praise and Prayer for Mercy
segments.gist: The psalmist calls for praise to the LORD and asks to be remembered with the favor shown to God's chosen people.

segments.title: Israel's Rebellion at the Red Sea
segments.gist: The people confess their ancestors' sins in Egypt and at the Red Sea, yet God saved them for his name's sake.

segments.title: Lust in the Wilderness and Idolatry
segments.gist: Israel quickly forgot God's works, craved food, envied Moses, and made a calf at Horeb, provoking God's wrath.

segments.title: Despising the Promised Land
segments.gist: The people despised the pleasant land, murmured in their tents, and joined Baal-peor, bringing plagues and judgment.

segments.title: Failure to Destroy the Nations
segments.gist: Israel failed to destroy the Canaanite nations, fell into idolatry and child sacrifice, and was repeatedly oppressed and delivered.

segments.title: Final Plea and Doxology
segments.gist: The psalmist asks God to gather the scattered people, and the psalm ends with a call to bless the LORD forever.

107.summary: Psalm 107 is a thanksgiving hymn calling the redeemed of the Lord to praise Him for His steadfast love. It presents four portraits of people in distress—wanderers in the desert, prisoners in darkness, fools afflicted by their sins, and sailors in a storm—each crying out to God, who delivers them. The psalm concludes by contrasting the righteous and the wicked and urging the wise to heed these acts of deliverance.

segments.title: Call to Give Thanks
segments.gist: The psalmist urges the redeemed to thank the Lord for His goodness and steadfast love.

segments.title: Wanderers in the Desert
segments.gist: The hungry and thirsty wander in a wasteland; they cry to God, who leads them to a city.

segments.title: Prisoners in Darkness
segments.gist: Those sitting in darkness and chains because of rebellion cry out; God breaks their bonds.

segments.title: Fools Afflicted by Sin
segments.gist: Fools suffering for their sins cry out; God heals them and they offer sacrifices of thanksgiving.

segments.title: Sailors in the Storm
segments.gist: Sailors in a tempest cry out; God calms the storm and brings them to their desired haven.

segments.title: God's Judgment and Mercy
segments.gist: God turns fruitful land into desert and desert into pools; He blesses the hungry and humbles princes.

108.summary: Psalm 108 combines two earlier psalms: it opens with the speaker's resolve to praise God and calls for God to be exalted over all the earth, then shifts to a plea for help against enemies, recalling God's promises over Shechem, Gilead, Moab, and Edom, and ends with a confident request for divine assistance, since human help is vain.

segments.title: Resolve to Praise God
segments.gist: The psalmist declares a steadfast heart and vows to sing and give praise among the peoples, asking God to be exalted above the heavens.

segments.title: Plea for Deliverance
segments.gist: The speaker cries for God to save His beloved people and recounts God's triumphant declarations over Shechem, Succoth, Gilead, Manasseh, Ephraim, and Judah.

segments.title: Confidence in God's Help
segments.gist: The psalmist asks who will lead him against Edom and affirms that God, who seemed to cast them off, will go forth with their armies and give help against the enemy.

109.summary: Psalm 109 is a lament and imprecation in which David asks God to defend him against false accusers, calls down severe curses on his adversary, and pleads for deliverance because of his own weakness and need for God's help. He vows to praise God among the multitude when he is rescued.

segments.title: Plea for God's Help
segments.gist: David asks God not to be silent while wicked and deceitful men speak against him with lying tongues.

segments.title: Imprecation Against the Adversary
segments.gist: David calls for a wicked ruler to oppose his enemy and for curses to fall on his enemy's family and possessions.

segments.title: Plea for Deliverance
segments.gist: David begs God to save him for His name's sake and describes his own weakness, fasting, and reproach.

segments.title: Prayer for Vindication
segments.gist: David asks God to help him and to let his enemies be clothed with shame while he blesses God.

segments.title: Vow of Praise
segments.gist: David promises to praise God greatly and declares that God stands at the right hand of the poor to save them.

110.summary: Psalm 110 is a royal psalm consisting of two divine oracles: the first invites the Davidic king to sit at God's right hand until his enemies are subdued, and the second declares him a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek. The psalm closes with a vision of the king's victorious judgment over the nations.

segments.title: Oracle of Exaltation
segments.gist: The LORD invites the king to sit at his right hand and promises to subdue his enemies, extending his rule from Zion.

segments.title: Victorious King
segments.gist: The Lord at the king's right hand defeats kings and judges nations, while the king drinks from the brook and lifts his head.

111.summary: Psalm 111 is a hymn of praise that begins with a personal resolve to thank the Lord among the congregation. It celebrates the great works of God—His righteousness, grace, and provision—and extols the reliability of His precepts, concluding that the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.

segments.title: Praise for God's Works
segments.gist: The psalmist vows to praise the Lord wholeheartedly and extols His great, honorable, and righteous works.

segments.title: God's Grace and Provision
segments.gist: The Lord is gracious and compassionate, provides food for those who fear Him, and remembers His covenant.

segments.title: Truth and Redemption
segments.gist: God's works are truth and judgment, His precepts are sure, and He sent redemption to His people.

112.summary: Psalm 112 is a wisdom poem praising the blessedness of the person who fears the Lord and delights in His commandments. It describes the prosperity, generosity, and steadfastness of the righteous, contrasting them with the wicked, who will ultimately witness the righteous's exaltation and be consumed by their own envy.

segments.title: Blessedness of the Righteous
segments.gist: The psalm opens with praise and declares the blessings of those who fear the Lord and delight in His commandments, including prosperity and enduring righteousness.

segments.title: Light and Generosity
segments.gist: The righteous are described as lights in darkness, gracious, compassionate, and generous, and they will be remembered and not shaken.

segments.title: Steadfast Trust
segments.gist: The righteous are fearless, trusting in the Lord, with a firm heart, and they will see their enemies defeated.

segments.title: Exaltation and Wicked's Envy
segments.gist: The righteous give generously and are exalted, while the wicked see this and are angry, melting away in their own desire.

113.summary: Psalm 113 is a call to praise the LORD, whose glory is above the heavens and who humbles himself to regard the lowly. He raises the poor and needy and gives the barren woman a home and joy as a mother.

segments.title: Call to Praise the LORD
segments.gist: The psalm opens with a call for servants of the LORD to praise his name from sunrise to sunset.

segments.title: The LORD's Exalted Glory
segments.gist: The LORD is exalted above the heavens, and none can compare to him in his lofty dwelling.

segments.title: The LORD Lifts the Lowly
segments.gist: The LORD raises the poor and needy and gives the barren woman a joyful home as a mother.

114.summary: Psalm 114 is a short hymn recalling Israel's exodus from Egypt, when Judah became God's sanctuary and Israel his dominion. It pictures the sea fleeing, the Jordan turning back, mountains skipping like rams, and the earth trembling at the Lord's presence, who brought water from the rock for his people.

segments.title: Israel Leaves Egypt
segments.gist: When Israel came out of Egypt, Judah became God's sanctuary and Israel his dominion.

segments.title: Sea and Mountains React
segments.gist: The sea fled, the Jordan was driven back, and the mountains and hills skipped like rams and lambs.

segments.title: Rhetorical Questions to Creation
segments.gist: The psalmist asks the sea, Jordan, mountains, and hills why they fled, turned back, and skipped.

segments.title: Earth Trembles Before the Lord
segments.gist: The earth is called to tremble before the Lord, who turned the rock into a pool and flint into a fountain of waters.

115.summary: Psalm 115 contrasts the living God of Israel with the lifeless idols of the nations, calling Israel to trust in the LORD as their help and shield. It declares that the heavens belong to the LORD while the earth is given to humanity, and it calls the living to praise Him rather than the dead.

segments.title: Glory to God's Name
segments.gist: The psalmist asks that glory go not to Israel but to God's name, for His mercy and truth's sake, answering the nations' taunt.

segments.title: Idols Are Silver and Gold
segments.gist: The nations' idols are mere silver and gold made by hands, with mouths, eyes, and ears that cannot function; their makers become like them.

segments.title: Israel, Trust in the LORD
segments.gist: Israel, the house of Aaron, and all who fear the LORD are called to trust Him as their help and shield.

segments.title: The LORD Remembers and Blesses
segments.gist: The LORD remembers and blesses Israel and Aaron, both small and great, and is praised as the maker of heaven and earth.

segments.title: Heavens Belong to the LORD
segments.gist: The heavens belong to the LORD, but the earth He has given to humanity; the dead cannot praise Him, so the living will bless Him forever.

116.summary: Psalm 116 is a thanksgiving song in which the psalmist recounts God's deliverance from a near-death crisis. He describes his prayer, God's gracious response, and his resolve to walk before the Lord and offer sacrifices of praise among God's people.

segments.title: God Hears the Psalmist's Cry
segments.gist: The psalmist declares his love for the Lord, who heard his supplication and delivered him from death and distress.

segments.title: The Lord Is Gracious and Righteous
segments.gist: The psalmist praises God's character—gracious, righteous, and merciful—and recalls how God saved him when he was brought low.

segments.title: Delivered from Death and Tears
segments.gist: The psalmist celebrates being rescued from death and vows to walk before the Lord, even after speaking in haste that all men are liars.

segments.title: Vow to Pay Thank Offerings
segments.gist: The psalmist asks how to repay the Lord and resolves to lift the cup of salvation and pay his vows publicly.

segments.title: Precious Death and Sacrifice of Praise
segments.gist: The psalmist affirms that the death of God's saints is precious, renews his vows, and promises to offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving in the Lord's house.

117.summary: Psalm 117 is a brief call to all nations and peoples to praise the LORD, grounded in His merciful kindness and truth toward Israel, and it closes with a renewed call to praise Him.

118.summary: Psalm 118 is a thanksgiving liturgy that opens and closes with a call to praise God's enduring mercy. It recounts the psalmist's deliverance from distress and hostile nations, declares trust in the Lord rather than in human help, and culminates in a procession to the temple and the rejected stone becoming the cornerstone.

segments.title: Call to Praise God's Mercy
segments.gist: The psalmist invites Israel, the priests, and all who fear the Lord to declare that God's mercy endures forever.

segments.title: Deliverance from Distress
segments.gist: In distress the psalmist called on the Lord and found help, so he trusts God rather than fearful humans or princes.

segments.title: Victory over Surrounding Nations
segments.gist: Though all nations surrounded him, the psalmist cut them off in the Lord's name, and God became his strength and song.

segments.title: Songs of Victory in the Sanctuary
segments.gist: Songs of joy and salvation are sung in the tents of the righteous, and the psalmist describes entering the gates of righteousness to give thanks.

segments.title: The Rejected Stone and the Blessed One
segments.gist: The stone the builders rejected becomes the cornerstone, and the people bless the one who comes in the Lord's name, celebrating the festal sacrifice.

segments.title: Final Thanksgiving and Praise
segments.gist: The psalmist declares God to be his God and gives thanks, closing with a call to praise the Lord for his enduring mercy.

119.summary: Psalm 119 is an acrostic poem of 176 verses, divided into twenty-two stanzas of eight verses each, one for every letter of the Hebrew alphabet. It praises God's law, statutes, and precepts, expressing devotion, longing for understanding, and reliance on God's word amid affliction and opposition. The speaker repeatedly declares love for God's commandments, asks for teaching and deliverance, and affirms that God's word is a lamp to his feet and his heritage forever.

segments.title: Aleph: Blessing of the Undefiled
segments.gist: The psalmist declares blessed those who walk in God's law and asks for steadfastness in keeping His statutes.

segments.title: Beth: Cleansing by God's Word
segments.gist: A young man cleanses his way by God's word; the psalmist seeks God with his whole heart and delights in His statutes.

segments.title: Gimel: Dealing Bountifully
segments.gist: The psalmist asks for open eyes to see wonders in God's law and expresses delight in His testimonies despite princes' opposition.

segments.title: Daleth: Strengthened in Grief
segments.gist: In heaviness, the psalmist asks for strength according to God's word and chooses the way of truth over lying.

segments.title: He: Teach Me Thy Statutes
segments.gist: The psalmist pleads to be taught and inclined to God's testimonies, turning away reproach and longing for His precepts.

segments.title: Waw: Trusting in God's Word
segments.gist: The psalmist trusts in God's word for salvation and will speak of His testimonies before kings without shame.

segments.title: Zayin: Comfort in Affliction
segments.gist: The psalmist finds comfort in God's promise and remembers His judgments, even in the night.

segments.title: Heth: The Lord Is My Portion
segments.gist: The psalmist declares the Lord as his portion and promises to keep His law, rising at midnight to give thanks.

segments.title: Teth: Affliction Teaches Statutes
segments.gist: The psalmist acknowledges that affliction taught him God's statutes and values God's law above gold.

segments.title: Yodh: Hope in God's Judgments
segments.gist: The psalmist asks for understanding and comfort, hoping in God's judgments and fearing Him.

segments.title: Kaph: Fainting for Salvation
segments.gist: The psalmist faints for God's salvation and asks for revival according to His word amid persecution.

segments.title: Lamedh: God's Word Settled Forever
segments.gist: God's word is settled in heaven; the psalmist delights in His law and sees all perfection has an end.

segments.title: Mem: Love for God's Law
segments.gist: The psalmist loves God's law and gains wisdom from His precepts, hating every false way.

segments.title: Nun: A Lamp to My Feet
segments.gist: God's word is a lamp to the psalmist's feet; he swears to keep God's righteous judgments despite affliction.

segments.title: Samekh: Uphold Me
segments.gist: The psalmist hates vain thoughts and asks God to uphold him, while the wicked are trodden down as dross.

segments.title: Ayin: Longing for Salvation
segments.gist: The psalmist asks for safety from oppressors and longs for God's salvation and commandments.

segments.title: Pe: Wonderful Testimonies
segments.gist: God's testimonies are wonderful; the psalmist pants for His commandments and weeps over disobedience.

segments.title: Tsadhe: Righteous Judgments
segments.gist: The psalmist praises God's righteous judgments and asks for understanding to live.

segments.title: Qoph: Crying with Whole Heart
segments.gist: The psalmist cries with his whole heart for God to hear and deliver him, trusting in His word.

segments.title: Resh: Great Tender Mercies
segments.gist: The psalmist asks for deliverance according to God's tender mercies and defends His precepts.

segments.title: Shin: Rejoicing at God's Word
segments.gist: The psalmist rejoices at God's word and praises Him seven times a day for His righteous judgments.

segments.title: Taw: Seeking God's Precepts
segments.gist: The psalmist asks for understanding and deliverance, confessing he has gone astray like a lost sheep.

120.summary: Psalm 120 is a short song of distress in which the speaker recalls crying to the LORD and being answered, then laments living among deceitful and war-loving people. He longs for peace while surrounded by those who are for war.

segments.title: Cry to the LORD answered
segments.gist: The psalmist recalls crying to the LORD in distress and being delivered from lying lips and a deceitful tongue, and asks what will be given to such a tongue.

segments.title: Dwelling among the hostile
segments.gist: The psalmist laments dwelling in Meshech and Kedar, among people who hate peace, and states that when he speaks of peace they are for war.

121.summary: A short pilgrim song in which the speaker looks to the hills and declares that his help comes from the LORD, the maker of heaven and earth. He assures that God neither slumbers nor sleeps, protects his people from all harm by day and night, and guards their going out and coming in forever.

segments.title: Looking to the hills for help
segments.gist: The psalmist lifts his eyes to the hills and confesses that his help comes from the LORD, maker of heaven and earth.

segments.title: God neither slumbers nor sleeps
segments.gist: He affirms that God will not let his foot be moved and that Israel's keeper never slumbers nor sleeps.

segments.title: The LORD as shade by day and night
segments.gist: The LORD is described as a shade at the right hand, so the sun will not strike by day nor the moon by night.

segments.title: Preserved in all ways forever
segments.gist: The psalm closes with the promise that the LORD preserves his people from all evil and their going out and coming in forever.

122.summary: Psalm 122 is a short pilgrim song of ascent, expressing gladness at going to the house of the Lord and standing within Jerusalem's gates. The speaker celebrates Jerusalem as a compact, well-built city where the tribes of Israel gather to give thanks, and where thrones of judgment are set. He calls for prayer for Jerusalem's peace and prosperity, and closes by resolving to seek its good for the sake of brethren and companions.

segments.title: Gladness at entering God's house
segments.gist: The psalmist rejoices when invited to go to the house of the Lord and notes that his feet now stand within Jerusalem's gates.

segments.title: Jerusalem as gathered city
segments.gist: Jerusalem is described as a compact, well-built city where the tribes of Israel go up to give thanks, and where thrones of judgment are set.

segments.title: Prayer for Jerusalem's peace
segments.gist: The psalmist urges prayer for Jerusalem's peace and prosperity, and resolves to seek its good for the sake of brethren and companions.

123.summary: This brief psalm is a prayer for mercy in the face of contempt and scorn. The speaker lifts his eyes to God, comparing a servant's dependence on his master to the worshippers' dependence on the Lord, and asks for mercy because they have had more than enough of the derision of the proud.

segments.title: Eyes Lifted to God
segments.gist: The psalmist lifts his eyes to God, who dwells in the heavens, as a servant looks to his master's hand.

segments.title: Plea for Mercy
segments.gist: He asks the Lord for mercy, acknowledging that they have been filled with contempt and are weary of the scorn of the proud.

124.summary: Psalm 124 is a brief song of thanksgiving in which the community of Israel acknowledges that without the LORD's help, their enemies would have swallowed them alive. They praise God for escaping the trap and declare their trust in the LORD as their maker.

segments.title: If the LORD Had Not Been
segments.gist: The psalmist calls Israel to confess that without the LORD's help, enemies would have swallowed them alive and swept them away.

segments.title: Blessed Be the LORD
segments.gist: The LORD is praised for not giving Israel as prey and for enabling escape like a bird from a snare.

125.summary: Psalm 125 is a short song of trust in the Lord, comparing those who trust in Him to Mount Zion, which cannot be moved. It assures that the wicked will not permanently rule over the righteous, and closes with a prayer for peace upon Israel and a warning to those who turn aside to crooked ways.

segments.title: Trust Like Mount Zion
segments.gist: Those who trust in the Lord are compared to Mount Zion, which stands firm forever, with the Lord surrounding His people.

segments.title: Prayer for Peace and Warning
segments.gist: A prayer for God to do good to the upright, and a warning that those who turn to crooked ways will be led away with evildoers, ending with a blessing of peace upon Israel.

126.summary: Psalm 126 is a brief song of thanksgiving and petition. It recalls how Zion's restoration filled the people with laughter and joy among the nations, then asks God to restore them again like streams in the dry south, and closes with the assurance that those who sow in tears will reap with joy.

segments.title: Joy at Zion's Restoration
segments.gist: The psalmist recalls how the Lord turned again the captivity of Zion, filling the people with laughter and prompting the nations to acknowledge God's great works.

segments.title: Sowing in Tears, Reaping in Joy
segments.gist: The psalm closes with a proverb-like assurance that those who sow in tears will return with rejoicing, bearing their sheaves.

127.summary: Psalm 127 is a short wisdom psalm attributed to Solomon. It teaches that human labor and vigilance are vain without the LORD's blessing, and that children are a heritage and reward from Him, with a full quiver bringing honor.

segments.title: Vain Labor Without the LORD
segments.gist: Unless the LORD builds the house and watches over the city, the builders and watchmen labor in vain.

segments.title: Children as Heritage and Reward
segments.gist: Children are a heritage from the LORD, and a man with a full quiver is blessed and not put to shame.

128.summary: Psalm 128 is a short wisdom psalm describing the blessedness of the man who fears the LORD and walks in His ways. It promises fruitfulness from labor, a fruitful wife and children, and blessing from Zion, concluding with a wish for peace upon Israel.

segments.title: Blessing on the God-fearing man
segments.gist: The psalm opens by pronouncing blessing on everyone who fears the LORD and walks in His ways, promising enjoyment of labor.

segments.title: Family fruitfulness described
segments.gist: The godly man's wife is likened to a fruitful vine and his children to olive plants around his table, confirming blessing.

segments.title: Blessing from Zion and peace
segments.gist: The LORD is asked to bless the man from Zion, let him see Jerusalem's good all his days, and grant him peace upon Israel.

129.summary: Psalm 129 is a brief song of Israel recalling affliction from enemies since youth, yet affirming that they did not prevail. It describes the plowers who plowed on Israel's back, declares the LORD's righteousness in cutting the cords of the wicked, and ends with a curse upon all who hate Zion, wishing them to be like grass on rooftops that withers before it grows.

segments.title: Israel's Affliction and Deliverance
segments.gist: Israel recalls being afflicted from youth but declares that enemies did not prevail; the LORD cut the cords of the wicked.

segments.title: Curse on Zion's Haters
segments.gist: A curse is pronounced on all who hate Zion: they will be like rooftop grass that withers and yields no harvest.

130.summary: Psalm 130 is a penitential song in which the speaker cries to the Lord from deep distress, appeals for forgiveness, and waits for God's redemption with confident hope. He urges Israel to hope in the Lord, who is merciful and will redeem his people from all their iniquities.

segments.title: Cry from the depths
segments.gist: The psalmist calls to the Lord from deep distress and asks him to hear his voice.

segments.title: Forgiveness with the Lord
segments.gist: The psalmist acknowledges that if the Lord marked iniquities none could stand, but with him there is forgiveness and fear.

segments.title: Waiting for the Lord
segments.gist: The psalmist waits for the Lord with his soul, hoping in his word more than watchmen wait for the morning.

segments.title: Israel urged to hope
segments.gist: Israel is called to hope in the Lord, who is merciful and will redeem his people from all their iniquities.

131.summary: Psalm 131 is a short song of quiet trust, in which the speaker disclaims proud ambitions and high aspirations, compares his calm soul to a weaned child resting with its mother, and calls Israel to hope in the LORD forever.

132.summary: Psalm 132 is a prayer asking God to remember David's hardships and his oath to find a dwelling place for the ark of the Lord. It recalls God's promise to David of an enduring dynasty and His choice of Zion as His eternal resting place, concluding with assurances of blessing for Zion and its people.

segments.title: David's Oath to Build
segments.gist: The psalmist asks God to remember David's afflictions and his vow not to rest until he finds a place for the Lord's ark.

segments.title: Procession to the Ark
segments.gist: The people recall hearing of the ark in Ephratah and coming to worship at God's footstool, asking Him to arise to His resting place.

segments.title: Prayer for David's Line
segments.gist: For David's sake, the psalmist pleads that God not reject His anointed, recalling God's conditional promise to David's sons.

segments.title: God's Choice of Zion
segments.gist: God declares He has chosen Zion for His habitation and promises to bless her provisions, clothe her priests with salvation, and establish David's horn.

133.summary: Psalm 133 is a short song of ascent praising the goodness of unity among God's people, comparing it to the precious oil poured on Aaron's head and the dew of Hermon falling on Mount Zion, where the Lord promises blessing and life forevermore.

134.summary: A short pilgrim song calling on the night watchmen of the temple to lift up their hands and bless the LORD in the sanctuary, and answering with a blessing pronounced from Zion by the LORD who made heaven and earth.

135.summary: Psalm 135 is a call to praise the LORD, who chose Israel and rules over all creation. It recounts His mighty acts in nature and in Israel's history, from the exodus to the conquest of Canaan, and contrasts the living God with powerless idols, ending with a blessing on those who fear Him.

segments.title: Call to Praise the LORD
segments.gist: The psalm opens with a summons for the LORD's servants to praise Him, citing His goodness and His choice of Israel.

segments.title: The LORD's Sovereign Power
segments.gist: The psalmist declares the LORD's greatness above all gods and describes His control over creation, weather, and the earth.

segments.title: Deliverance from Egypt to Canaan
segments.gist: The LORD is praised for striking Egypt's firstborn, performing signs and wonders, and defeating kings to give Israel their land.

segments.title: The LORD's Name Endures Forever
segments.gist: The LORD's name and remembrance endure forever, and He will judge His people and have compassion on His servants.

segments.title: The Impotence of Idols
segments.gist: The idols of the nations are silver and gold, made by human hands, unable to speak, see, hear, or breathe; those who make and trust them become like them.

segments.title: Blessing and Final Praise
segments.gist: Israel, the priests, the Levites, and all who fear the LORD are called to bless Him, and the psalm concludes with a call to praise from Zion.

136.summary: Psalm 136 is a litany of thanksgiving that recounts God's mighty acts in creation and in Israel's history, from the exodus to the conquest of Canaan. Each verse is followed by the refrain 'for his mercy endureth for ever,' praising God's steadfast love.

segments.title: Call to Give Thanks
segments.gist: An opening exhortation to give thanks to the Lord, the God of gods and Lord of lords, for His enduring mercy.

segments.title: Praise for Creation
segments.gist: Thanksgiving for God's creative works: the heavens, the earth, the great lights, the sun, moon, and stars.

segments.title: Deliverance from Egypt
segments.gist: Recounting God's deliverance of Israel from Egypt through the plagues, the Red Sea crossing, and guidance in the wilderness.

segments.title: Victory Over Kings
segments.gist: God's defeat of great kings, including Sihon and Og, and the giving of their land as an inheritance to Israel.

segments.title: God's Care and Closing Praise
segments.gist: Acknowledgment of God's remembrance in low estate, rescue from enemies, and a final call to give thanks to the God of heaven.

137.summary: The psalm recalls the Babylonian exile, when the Israelites wept by the rivers of Babylon and hung their harps on the willows, refusing to sing Zion's songs in a foreign land. It ends with a bitter call for vengeance against Babylon and a blessing on anyone who repays it and dashes its children against the stones.

segments.title: Weeping by Babylon's Rivers
segments.gist: The exiles sit and weep by Babylon's rivers, hanging their harps on the willows when their captors ask for songs of Zion.

segments.title: Refusal to Sing Zion's Song
segments.gist: They refuse to sing the Lord's song in a strange land and vow never to forget Jerusalem, preferring their right hand to forget its skill.

segments.title: Call for Vengeance on Babylon
segments.gist: The psalm calls for Babylon to be repaid for its destruction of Jerusalem and blesses anyone who seizes and dashes its little ones against the stones.

138.summary: Psalm 138 is a psalm of David giving thanks and praise to God with his whole heart before the gods. He recalls God's answered prayer and magnified word, expresses confidence that all kings will praise God for His glory, and declares that God regards the lowly while the proud He knows afar off. The psalm closes with assurance of God's help and a plea that He not forsake the work of His own hands.

segments.title: Thanksgiving and Worship
segments.gist: David resolves to praise God with his whole heart, worship toward His holy temple, and give thanks for His lovingkindness and truth.

segments.title: God's Care for the Lowly
segments.gist: God's greatness is acknowledged, yet He regards the lowly and knows the proud from afar.

segments.title: Confidence in God's Help
segments.gist: David trusts God to revive him in trouble, save him from enemies, and perfect His purposes, asking God not to forsake him.

139.summary: David addresses God as the all-knowing searcher of his heart, marveling that God knows his thoughts, words, and ways before they happen. He then reflects on God's omnipresence and creative power in forming him in the womb, and closes with a plea for God to slay the wicked and to search and cleanse his own heart.

segments.title: God knows all my ways
segments.gist: David confesses that God has searched him, knows his thoughts and words, and is acquainted with all his paths.

segments.title: Nowhere to flee from God
segments.gist: David asks where he can go from God's presence and finds that heaven, hell, wings of the morning, and the depths are all within God's reach.

segments.title: Fearfully and wonderfully made
segments.gist: David praises God for forming him in the womb and for the countless thoughts and preciousness of God's purposes toward him.

segments.title: Wicked men and God's enemies
segments.gist: David expresses hatred for those who speak wickedly against God and declares his opposition to God's enemies.

segments.title: Search me and know my heart
segments.gist: David asks God to search him, try him, and lead him in the everlasting way.

140.summary: A psalm of David asking God for rescue from violent, scheming enemies who plot his downfall with sharp tongues and hidden snares. He prays that their own evil would fall back on them, and closes with confidence that God will defend the poor and the upright will give thanks in his presence.

segments.title: Prayer for Deliverance from Evil Men
segments.gist: David asks God to preserve him from violent men who devise mischief and stir up war all day.

segments.title: Enemies Hide Snares and Traps
segments.gist: The proud have hidden a net and snares along his path, and he asks God to hear his plea.

segments.title: Prayer That Their Plots Backfire
segments.gist: David asks that the mischief of his enemies' lips cover them and that evil hunt the violent man to overthrow him.

segments.title: Confidence in God's Justice
segments.gist: David affirms that God maintains the cause of the poor and afflicted, and the righteous will give thanks to his name.

141.summary: Psalm 141 is David's prayer for God to hear him and to guard his words and heart from evil. He asks to be kept from the company of the wicked and welcomes correction from the righteous, while praying that the wicked will fall into their own traps.

segments.title: Prayer for Swift Hearing
segments.gist: David cries out to the Lord, asking that his prayer be set before God like incense and his lifted hands like the evening sacrifice.

segments.title: Guard My Words and Heart
segments.gist: He asks the Lord to set a watch over his mouth and to keep his heart from inclining to evil deeds with wicked men.

segments.title: Wicked Leaders Judged
segments.gist: He describes the downfall of the wicked leaders and the scattering of their bones, affirming that his words are heard.

segments.title: Trust in God for Deliverance
segments.gist: David looks to the Lord for refuge, asking to be preserved from the traps of the wicked while they fall into their own nets.

142.summary: A short psalm of David, titled as his prayer when he was in the cave, in which he cries out to the LORD with his complaint, describes his enemies' trap and his own isolation, and appeals to God as his refuge and portion, asking to be delivered from persecutors who are too strong for him.

segments.title: Cry to the LORD aloud
segments.gist: David says he cries aloud to the LORD and pours out his complaint and trouble before him.

segments.title: Faint spirit and hidden snare
segments.gist: When his spirit is overwhelmed he looks to God, who knows his path, and notes the trap set for him.

segments.title: Thou art my refuge
segments.gist: He cries to the LORD as his refuge and portion, asking deliverance from persecutors and praise for God's bounty.

143.summary: Psalm 143 is David's prayer for deliverance and guidance, in which he pleads for God to hear him not on the basis of his own righteousness but for God's faithfulness and mercy. He recalls God's past works, longs for God's presence like a thirsty land, and asks for instruction, protection from enemies, and the destruction of his foes.

segments.title: Plea for a Hearing
segments.gist: David asks God to hear his prayer and not enter into judgment with him, since no one living is righteous before God.

segments.title: Distress and Longing
segments.gist: David describes his enemies pursuing him and his spirit fainting, then remembers God's past works and stretches out his hands in longing.

segments.title: Prayer for Guidance
segments.gist: David urgently asks God to answer him, show him the way to go, teach him to do God's will, and lead him on level ground.

segments.title: Request for Deliverance
segments.gist: David asks God to preserve his life for his name's sake, bring his soul out of trouble, and cut off his enemies in mercy.

144.summary: Psalm 144 is a royal psalm of David that blends praise for God as a rock and fortress with a request for deliverance from foreign enemies. It contrasts the fleeting nature of human life with God's power, asks for rescue and prosperity, and closes with a blessing on the people whose God is the Lord.

segments.title: Praise to the Rock
segments.gist: David blesses the Lord as his strength, fortress, and deliverer, and marvels that God regards frail humanity.

segments.title: Prayer for Deliverance
segments.gist: David asks God to come down in power and rescue him from foreign enemies whose mouths speak vanity.

segments.title: New Song and Rescue
segments.gist: David vows to sing a new song to God and repeats his plea to be saved from deceitful enemies.

segments.title: Blessing of a Prosperous People
segments.gist: David prays for strong sons, fruitful daughters, abundant harvests, and peace, calling blessed the people whose God is the Lord.

145.summary: Psalm 145 is David's acrostic hymn of praise to God as great King, extolling His mighty acts, gracious character, and providential care for all creation. The psalm moves from personal and communal praise to God's goodness to the needy and His righteous rule, ending with a universal call for all flesh to praise Him.

segments.title: David extols God's greatness
segments.gist: David resolves to praise God daily and declares His greatness beyond search.

segments.title: Generations declare God's works
segments.gist: One generation praises God's mighty acts to another, recounting His goodness.

segments.title: God's gracious character and kingdom
segments.gist: God is gracious, merciful, and good to all; His kingdom is everlasting and glorious.

segments.title: God upholds and provides
segments.gist: The Lord supports the falling, lifts the bowed down, and satisfies all living things.

segments.title: God is righteous and near
segments.gist: The Lord is righteous in all His ways, near to those who call on Him, and preserves those who love Him.

146.summary: Psalm 146 is a hymn of praise that calls for trusting in God rather than in human rulers, celebrating God as Creator and as the helper of the oppressed, hungry, imprisoned, blind, and bowed down. It concludes with the declaration that the LORD reigns forever.

segments.title: Praise and Trust in God
segments.gist: The psalmist vows to praise the LORD throughout his life and urges trust in Him rather than in princes.

segments.title: Breath Departs, Plans Perish
segments.gist: Human beings are frail; when their breath leaves, their plans come to nothing.

segments.title: Blessed Are Those Helped by God
segments.gist: Those whose help is the God of Jacob are blessed; He made heaven and earth and keeps truth, executes justice, and gives food to the hungry.

segments.title: God Lifts the Bowed Down
segments.gist: The LORD opens the eyes of the blind, raises those bowed down, loves the righteous, and watches over strangers and fatherless.

147.summary: Psalm 147 is a hymn of praise calling Jerusalem to extol the LORD for restoring the city, gathering Israel's exiles, healing the brokenhearted, and controlling nature. It contrasts God's care for His people with His disregard for human strength, and closes with His special revelation to Israel.

segments.title: Praise for Restoration and Healing
segments.gist: The psalmist calls for praise because God rebuilds Jerusalem, gathers the outcasts, heals the brokenhearted, and names the stars.

segments.title: Sing with Thanksgiving
segments.gist: God is praised for providing rain and grass for the earth and for taking pleasure in those who fear Him.

segments.title: God's Word and Care for Israel
segments.gist: Jerusalem is called to praise God for His control of weather, His provision for creatures, and His special revelation to Israel.

148.summary: Psalm 148 is a call to all creation—from the heavens and their inhabitants to the earth and its creatures—to praise the Lord. The psalm moves from the celestial realm to the earthly, ending with a call for Israel to praise God for their unique relationship.

segments.title: Heavens Praise the Lord
segments.gist: The psalmist calls on the heavens, angels, sun, moon, and stars to praise the Lord.

segments.title: Earth and Sea Praise
segments.gist: The earth, sea creatures, weather phenomena, mountains, and trees are summoned to praise.

segments.title: All People Praise
segments.gist: Kings, rulers, and all people are called to praise the Lord's excellent name.

149.summary: Psalm 149 is a call for Israel to praise the Lord with song and dance, rejoicing in their King. It celebrates God's pleasure in His people and their honor, and it calls the faithful to execute judgment on the nations with a two-edged sword.

segments.title: Call to Praise
segments.gist: The psalmist calls Israel to sing a new song and rejoice in their Maker and King with dance and music.

segments.title: Judgment on Nations
segments.gist: The faithful are to wield a two-edged sword to execute vengeance and judgment on the nations, as written.

150.summary: Psalm 150 is a doxology that concludes the Book of Psalms, calling for praise of God in His sanctuary and mighty acts, with a list of instruments and a universal summons for all living things to praise the Lord.

segments.title: Praise in Sanctuary and Firmament
segments.gist: The psalmist calls for praise in God's sanctuary and in the firmament of His power, citing His mighty acts.

segments.title: Praise with Instruments
segments.gist: A list of instruments—trumpet, psaltery, harp, timbrel, strings, organs, and cymbals—is given for praising God.

1.summary: Proverbs 1 opens with the title and purpose of the book, then states the fear of the Lord as the foundation of knowledge. It warns against joining violent men, portrays wisdom crying out in public to turn the simple from folly, and closes with the consequence of rejecting wisdom's call.

segments.title: Purpose of the Proverbs
segments.gist: The proverbs of Solomon are given to teach wisdom, instruction, and understanding, and the fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge.

segments.title: Warning Against Sinners
segments.gist: A father warns his son not to consent to violent men who entice him to ambush the innocent for gain, for such greed takes the life of its owner.

segments.title: Wisdom's Public Rebuke
segments.gist: Wisdom cries out in the streets and gates, rebuking the simple who refuse her counsel and warning that those who reject her will face calamity and eat the fruit of their own way.

2.summary: Proverbs 2 is a fatherly instruction urging the reader to seek wisdom and understanding as hidden treasure, promising that the Lord gives wisdom and protects the upright. It describes how wisdom delivers from the ways of evil men and from the seductive adulteress, so that one may walk in righteousness and dwell in the land.

segments.title: Seek wisdom as hidden treasure
segments.gist: The son is urged to receive the father's words and search for wisdom and understanding as for silver and hidden treasure.

segments.title: The Lord gives wisdom and protection
segments.gist: The Lord gives wisdom and knowledge, and he preserves the way of his saints and the upright.

segments.title: Wisdom delivers from evil men
segments.gist: When wisdom enters the heart, discretion preserves from the way of evil men who speak froward things and walk in darkness.

segments.title: Deliverance from the strange woman
segments.gist: Wisdom delivers from the adulteress whose house leads down to death and whose paths lead to the dead.

segments.title: Walk in the way of good men
segments.gist: The upright shall dwell in the land, but the wicked shall be cut off and the transgressors rooted out.

3.summary: Proverbs 3 is a fatherly instruction to a son, urging him to keep wisdom and God's commandments, to trust and honor the Lord, and to embrace correction. It praises wisdom's value and the happiness of those who find it, then moves into warnings against envy and violence, closing with a contrast between the wise and the foolish.

segments.title: Exhortation to trust and honor God
segments.gist: The speaker urges his son to keep his teachings, trust in the Lord, fear Him, honor Him with wealth, and accept His correction.

segments.title: The blessedness of finding wisdom
segments.gist: Wisdom is more precious than rubies; those who find it are happy, and by wisdom the Lord founded the earth.

segments.title: Wisdom brings safety and confidence
segments.gist: Keeping sound wisdom and discretion brings life, safety, and freedom from fear of sudden terror.

segments.title: Warnings against envy and oppression
segments.gist: The son is told not to withhold good, not to devise evil, not to envy the oppressor, for the Lord's curse and blessing are on the wicked and the just.

4.summary: Proverbs 4 presents a father's instruction to his children, urging them to embrace wisdom as the principal thing and to avoid the path of the wicked. He contrasts the shining path of the just with the dark way of evildoers, and closes with a call to guard the heart, mouth, and steps with all diligence.

segments.title: Exhortation to Get Wisdom
segments.gist: A father urges his sons to hear his instruction and prize wisdom, calling it the principal thing that brings promotion and honor.

segments.title: Two Paths: Righteous and Wicked
segments.gist: The father contrasts the straight path of the upright, which shines brighter, with the dark and violent way of the wicked.

segments.title: Guard Your Heart and Ways
segments.gist: The father concludes by telling his son to attend to his words, keep them in his heart, and guard his mouth and steps.

5.summary: Proverbs 5 is a father's instruction warning his son against sexual immorality, urging him to embrace wisdom and avoid the seductive words of a forbidden woman. The chapter describes the bitter consequences of such sin and the importance of fidelity in marriage, concluding with a reminder that God sees all human ways.

segments.title: Warning Against Adulteress
segments.gist: The father urges his son to listen to wisdom and avoid the seductive speech of the forbidden woman, whose end is bitter.

segments.title: Consequences of Folly
segments.gist: The son is warned to stay away from her path, lest he lose his honor and wealth and face ruin and public disgrace.

segments.title: Rejoice in Your Wife
segments.gist: The father encourages the son to find joy and satisfaction in his own wife and to avoid the snare of the forbidden woman.

segments.title: God Sees All Ways
segments.gist: The chapter closes by affirming that God observes every path, and the wicked are trapped by their own sins.

6.summary: Proverbs 6 is a collection of wisdom sayings: it warns against putting up security for a neighbor, urges the lazy to learn from the ant, describes the destructive ways of a wicked man, lists seven things the Lord hates, and closes with a strong warning against adultery, contrasting its ruin with the safety of faithful marriage.

segments.title: Warning against becoming surety
segments.gist: The son is warned not to pledge himself for a neighbor's debt and is urged to escape the trap quickly.

segments.title: Lesson from the ant
segments.gist: The sluggard is told to observe the ant's diligence and to consider how poverty comes through laziness.

segments.title: The wicked man's ways
segments.gist: A worthless and wicked person is described by deceitful speech and gestures, and sudden calamity is said to overtake him.

segments.title: Seven things the Lord hates
segments.gist: A list of seven abominations to the Lord, including pride, lying, murder, and sowing discord.

segments.title: Warning against adultery
segments.gist: The son is urged to keep the commandment and is warned that adultery leads to ruin, disgrace, and inescapable vengeance.

7.summary: Proverbs 7 is a father's instruction to his son to keep his words and treasure wisdom as a safeguard against the seductive adulteress. The chapter narrates a scene of a young man lacking understanding who is lured by a crafty woman into her house, which is described as a path to death. It concludes with a warning to listen and not stray into her ways, for her house leads to destruction.

segments.title: Exhortation to Keep Wisdom
segments.gist: The father urges his son to keep his commandments, treasure wisdom, and bind them as a safeguard against the strange woman.

segments.title: Observation of a Simple Youth
segments.gist: From the window of his house, the father observes a young man void of understanding passing through the street near the woman's corner.

segments.title: The Seductress's Enticement
segments.gist: The woman approaches the youth with a bold face, speaks flattering words, and invites him to a feast in her house, claiming her husband is away.

segments.title: The Youth's Downfall
segments.gist: With her much fair speech she causes him to yield; he follows her as an ox to the slaughter, not knowing it will cost him his life.

segments.title: Final Warning to the Sons
segments.gist: The father concludes by warning his sons to listen and not go after her, for her house is the way to hell and death.

8.summary: Wisdom speaks in her own voice, calling people to listen and learn, and declares her eternal existence and presence with God at creation. She contrasts her value with worldly riches and concludes by promising blessing to those who keep her ways.

segments.title: Wisdom's Call to Listen
segments.gist: Wisdom urges all people to hear her instruction, for she speaks truth and offers knowledge better than silver and gold.

segments.title: Wisdom's Worth and Counsel
segments.gist: Wisdom claims prudence, counsel, and strength, and promises that those who seek her find riches and honor.

segments.title: Wisdom Present at Creation
segments.gist: Wisdom declares she was with God from the beginning, present when the heavens and earth were formed.

segments.title: Blessing for Those Who Keep Wisdom
segments.gist: Wisdom calls her children to listen and promises life and favor to those who find her, but harm to those who hate her.

9.summary: Proverbs 9 contrasts two invitations: Wisdom builds her house and calls the simple to her feast, while the foolish woman, loud and seductive, lures the simple to stolen water and death. Between them, the chapter offers short sayings on the value of reproof, the beginning of wisdom, and the consequences of scorning versus walking in understanding.

segments.title: Wisdom builds and invites
segments.gist: Wisdom builds her house, prepares a feast, and sends maidens to call the simple to eat her bread and drink her wine.

segments.title: Reproof, wisdom, and its rewards
segments.gist: Sayings contrast scorning a mocker with loving reproof, and state that the fear of the LORD begins wisdom and that wisdom rewards those who seek it.

segments.title: Folly's seductive invitation
segments.gist: The foolish woman, loud and ignorant, sits at her door and calls the simple to stolen water, not revealing that her guests are in the depths of hell.

10.summary: Proverbs 10 is a collection of short sayings contrasting the righteous and the wicked, often in pairs. It opens with a title attributing the proverbs to Solomon and then presents a series of observations about wealth, speech, labor, love, and the consequences of wisdom versus folly.

segments.title: Solomon's Proverbs: Righteousness and Diligence
segments.gist: The proverbs of Solomon begin with contrasts between the wise and foolish child, righteous and wicked, and the diligent and slack hand.

segments.title: Blessings and Speech
segments.gist: Blessings come on the righteous, while the wicked are covered with violence; speech and integrity are contrasted.

segments.title: Love, Hatred, and Words
segments.gist: Hatred stirs up strife but love covers sins; the wise store knowledge while the fool's mouth brings ruin.

segments.title: Speech, Wealth, and Security
segments.gist: In many words sin is not lacking, but the tongue of the just is choice silver; the fear of the Lord brings security.

segments.title: Sluggards, Fools, and the Righteous
segments.gist: As vinegar to the teeth, so is the sluggard; the fear of the Lord prolongs days, and the righteous shall never be removed.

11.summary: Proverbs 11 is a collection of sayings contrasting the righteous and the wicked, covering themes such as honesty in business, the power of the tongue, generosity, and the certainty of moral consequences. It emphasizes that integrity, humility, and righteousness lead to life and favor, while wickedness, pride, and deceit lead to ruin.

segments.title: Honesty and Deliverance
segments.gist: Dishonest scales are condemned; pride brings shame, integrity guides the upright, and righteousness delivers from trouble.

segments.title: Words and Neighbors
segments.gist: The hypocrite destroys with his mouth, the righteous escape trouble, and a talebearer and faithful witness are contrasted.

segments.title: Surety and Mercy
segments.gist: Suretyship for strangers brings trouble, a gracious woman retains honor, and the merciful and truthful are rewarded while the wicked face evil.

segments.title: Generosity and Withholding
segments.gist: A fair woman without discretion is like a jewel in a swine's snout; the liberal soul is made fat, while he that withholds grain is cursed.

segments.title: Rewards of Righteousness
segments.gist: He that seeks good obtains favor, but evil comes to the wicked; the righteous flourish like a tree, and the fruit of the righteous is a tree of life.

12.summary: Proverbs 12 is a collection of wise sayings contrasting the righteous and the wicked. It covers topics such as speech, diligence, family life, and the consequences of one's actions, often using vivid imagery and direct comparisons.

segments.title: Contrasts in Speech and Favor
segments.gist: The chapter opens by contrasting the virtuous and wicked, highlighting how speech and actions affect favor and standing.

segments.title: Household and Plans
segments.gist: These verses address the value of a virtuous wife, the importance of righteous thoughts, and the stability of the righteous versus the wicked.

segments.title: Reputation and Compassion
segments.gist: The sayings here discuss how one's wisdom is praised, the danger of pride, and the contrast between the merciful and the cruel.

segments.title: Words and Foolishness
segments.gist: This section focuses on the snare of sinful lips, the fruit of one's words, and the fool's quick anger versus the prudent's patience.

segments.title: Truth and Deceit
segments.gist: These proverbs contrast truthful testimony with false witness, and the value of honest words versus lying lips.

segments.title: Diligence and Life
segments.gist: The final verses contrast the prudent and the foolish, the diligent and the slothful, and highlight the way of righteousness leading to life.

13.summary: Proverbs 13 is a collection of wise sayings contrasting the righteous and the wicked, emphasizing the power of speech, the value of discipline, the pursuit of wisdom, and the outcomes of diligence versus laziness. It touches on themes such as the fruit of one's words, the importance of heeding instruction, and the ultimate reward of righteousness versus the destruction of sin.

segments.title: Wisdom and Speech
segments.gist: A wise son heeds instruction, and the fruit of speech brings good or violence; the righteous hate lying while the wicked cause shame.

segments.title: Wealth and Righteousness
segments.gist: Riches are deceptive, but righteousness delivers from death; the light of the righteous rejoices, and wealth gained by vanity dwindles.

segments.title: Desire and Discipline
segments.gist: Hope deferred sickens the heart, but a fulfilled desire is a tree of life; those who despise instruction suffer, while companions of fools are destroyed.

segments.title: Walk with the Wise
segments.gist: Walking with the wise brings wisdom, but fools inherit folly; the righteous are rewarded with good, while the wicked are overthrown.

14.summary: Proverbs 14 is a collection of wise sayings contrasting the righteous and the wicked, covering topics such as speech, wealth, discipline, and the fear of the Lord. It emphasizes that wisdom builds up while folly tears down, and that a person's end is shaped by their conduct.

segments.title: Wisdom Builds, Folly Tears Down
segments.gist: The wise woman builds her house, but the foolish tears it down; the upright are guided by the fear of the Lord, while the wicked are destroyed by their own words.

segments.title: The Way of the Wise and Foolish
segments.gist: The prudent understand their way, but fools are deceived; the wicked will be repaid, and the righteous find refuge in their integrity.

segments.title: The Simple, the Prudent, and the Foolish
segments.gist: The simple believe every word, but the prudent consider their steps; the wise fear the Lord, while the foolish are rash and quick-tempered.

segments.title: The Reward of the Righteous
segments.gist: The evil bow before the good, the poor are hated even by neighbors, and the rich have many friends; those who despise their neighbor sin, but the merciful are blessed.

segments.title: A True Witness and the Fear of the Lord
segments.gist: A true witness delivers souls, but a deceitful witness speaks lies; in the fear of the Lord is strong confidence, and the righteous have a refuge.

segments.title: Patience, Envy, and the King's Favor
segments.gist: He who is slow to wrath has great understanding, but the envious is foolish; the poor is hated even by his own neighbor, but the rich has many friends.

15.summary: Proverbs 15 is a collection of wise sayings contrasting righteous and wicked speech, attitudes, and actions. It emphasizes the power of gentle words, the value of instruction, the LORD's omniscience, and the blessings of a righteous life versus the destruction of the wicked.

segments.title: The Tongue and the LORD's Omniscience
segments.gist: A soft answer turns away wrath, while harsh words stir anger; the LORD sees all and weighs motives, and the wise receive correction.

segments.title: The Sacrifice and the Heart
segments.gist: The LORD detests the sacrifice of the wicked but delights in the prayer of the upright; he sees all, and a cheerful heart brightens the face.

segments.title: Better a Little with Righteousness
segments.gist: Better is little with the fear of the LORD than great treasure with trouble; a wise son honors his father, and a foolish one despises his mother.

segments.title: Plans and Counsel
segments.gist: Folly brings joy to the foolish, but understanding directs the upright; plans succeed with counsel, and the LORD hears the righteous.

segments.title: The Fear of the LORD
segments.gist: The righteous study before answering, the LORD is far from the wicked but hears the righteous, and humility precedes honor.

16.summary: Proverbs 16 is a collection of wisdom sayings contrasting the righteous and the wicked, emphasizing that God weighs motives and directs human plans. It covers themes of pride and humility, honest speech, righteous leadership, and the fear of the Lord as the path to life.

segments.title: God's Sovereignty Over Human Plans
segments.gist: The Lord weighs hearts, directs steps, and purges iniquity through mercy and truth.

segments.title: Righteous Kings and Just Rule
