36.summary: In the fourteenth year of Hezekiah's reign, Sennacherib of Assyria attacks Judah's fortified cities and sends his chief officer, Rabshakeh, to Jerusalem to demand surrender. Rabshakeh delivers a loud propaganda speech at the conduit of the upper pool, mocking Hezekiah's reliance on Egypt and on the LORD, and claiming that the LORD himself told Assyria to destroy Judah. Hezekiah's officials, Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah, ask Rabshakeh to speak in Aramaic rather than Hebrew so the people on the wall will not understand, but he refuses and continues shouting to frighten Jerusalem into surrender.

segments.title: Assyria invades and sends Rabshakeh
segments.gist: Sennacherib takes Judah's fortified cities and sends Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem to confront Hezekiah.

segments.title: Rabshakeh mocks trust in Egypt and the LORD
segments.gist: Rabshakeh tells Hezekiah's officials that Egypt is a broken reed and that the LORD, whose high places Hezekiah removed, will not help Judah.

segments.title: Officials request Aramaic; Rabshakeh refuses
segments.gist: Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah ask Rabshakeh to speak in Aramaic so the people on the wall will not hear, but he refuses and says the people will suffer.

segments.title: Rabshakeh warns the people not to trust Hezekiah
segments.gist: Rabshakeh shouts in Hebrew that Hezekiah cannot save them, urges them to make peace and receive Assyria's provisions, and claims no god has delivered a land from Assyria's kings.

segments.title: People silent; officials report to Hezekiah
segments.gist: The people hold their peace as commanded, and Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah come to Hezekiah with torn clothes and report Rabshakeh's words.

37.summary: King Hezekiah, upon receiving Sennacherib's threatening letter, spreads it before the LORD in the temple and prays for deliverance. Isaiah assures him that Assyria will fall, and that night the angel of the LORD kills 185,000 Assyrian soldiers; Sennacherib withdraws and is later killed by his own sons.

segments.title: Hezekiah Receives Assyrian Threat
segments.gist: Hezekiah hears Sennacherib's blasphemous message, tears his clothes, and sends officials to Isaiah.

segments.title: Assyrian Letter Demands Surrender
segments.gist: Sennacherib's letter warns Hezekiah not to trust in God, citing other nations Assyria has conquered.

segments.title: Hezekiah's Prayer in the Temple
segments.gist: Hezekiah spreads the letter before the LORD and prays for deliverance so all kingdoms may know God.

segments.title: Isaiah's Prophecy Against Assyria
segments.gist: Isaiah declares that the virgin daughter of Zion despises Assyria and that God will turn Sennacherib back.

segments.title: Sign and Promise of Deliverance
segments.gist: God gives a sign to Hezekiah and promises that the remnant of Judah will take root and that Jerusalem will be defended.

segments.title: Assyrian Army Destroyed and Sennacherib Killed
segments.gist: The angel of the LORD kills 185,000 Assyrians; Sennacherib returns to Nineveh and is slain by his sons.

38.summary: Hezekiah falls gravely ill, and Isaiah tells him he will die; Hezekiah prays, and God promises to add fifteen years to his life and deliver Jerusalem from Assyria. Hezekiah asks for a sign, and the shadow on the sundial goes back ten degrees. He then writes a psalm of thanksgiving for his recovery.

segments.title: Hezekiah's illness and Isaiah's message
segments.gist: Hezekiah is sick unto death; Isaiah tells him to set his house in order, for he shall die.

segments.title: God answers Hezekiah's prayer
segments.gist: Hezekiah prays and weeps; God tells Isaiah to say he has heard his prayer and will add fifteen years and deliver Jerusalem.

segments.title: Hezekiah's psalm of thanksgiving
segments.gist: Hezekiah recounts his despair and God's deliverance, praising God for casting his sins behind his back.

segments.title: Sign of the fig cake
segments.gist: Isaiah prescribes a lump of figs for the boil, and Hezekiah asks for a sign of going up to the house of the Lord.

39.summary: King Hezekiah of Judah receives envoys from Babylon, shows them all his treasures, and is then told by the prophet Isaiah that everything in his house will one day be carried off to Babylon, and that some of his descendants will become eunuchs there. Hezekiah accepts the word as good because he expects peace and truth in his own days.

segments.title: Hezekiah welcomes Babylonian envoys
segments.gist: Merodach-baladan sends letters and a gift to Hezekiah, who welcomes the messengers and shows them his treasures.

segments.title: Isaiah questions Hezekiah
segments.gist: Isaiah asks Hezekiah what the men said and where they came from; Hezekiah answers they came from Babylon.

segments.title: Isaiah foretells Babylonian exile
segments.gist: Isaiah tells Hezekiah that all his treasures and his fathers' will be carried to Babylon, and his sons will serve as eunuchs there.

40.summary: Isaiah 40 opens with a call to comfort Jerusalem because her warfare is ended and her iniquity pardoned. The chapter then presents the voice in the wilderness preparing the way for the Lord, declares the everlasting word of God, and portrays the Lord as the incomparable Creator who does not grow weary and gives strength to the faint.

segments.title: Comfort Jerusalem
segments.gist: God commands comfort for Jerusalem, declaring her warfare ended and her iniquity pardoned.

segments.title: Prepare the Way
segments.gist: A voice cries in the wilderness to prepare the way of the Lord, and the glory of the Lord will be revealed.

segments.title: Fading Flesh, Enduring Word
segments.gist: A voice contrasts fading human flesh with the enduring word of God.

segments.title: Behold Your God
segments.gist: Zion is told to lift up her voice and behold God, who comes with a strong arm and tends his flock like a shepherd.

segments.title: Incomparable Creator
segments.gist: God is described as the incomparable Creator who measures the waters, weighs the mountains, and sits above the earth's circle.

segments.title: Strength for the Weary
segments.gist: God addresses Israel's complaint, declaring that he does not faint and gives strength to the weary.

41.summary: God summons the nations to judgment and reassures Israel of His help, contrasting the fate of idolaters with His care for His servant Jacob, whom He will strengthen and use to thresh mountains. He promises to provide water in the wilderness and calls the idols to prove themselves, declaring that He has raised up a ruler from the north and will give Jerusalem a messenger of good tidings.

segments.title: God Summons the Nations
segments.gist: God calls the coastlands and peoples to silence and judgment, while the idolaters encourage one another and fasten their idols with nails.

segments.title: Israel as God's Servant
segments.gist: God addresses Israel as His chosen servant, promises to strengthen and uphold him, and says his enemies will be ashamed and defeated.

segments.title: Water in the Wilderness
segments.gist: God promises to open rivers and fountains for the poor and needy, planting trees in the desert so all may see His work.

segments.title: Challenge to the Idols
segments.gist: God challenges the idols to declare things to come or do good or evil, but they are nothing and their works are worthless.

segments.title: Ruler from the North
segments.gist: God says He has raised up a ruler from the north who will come upon princes, and He declares that the idols are all vanity and confusion.

42.summary: God presents His servant, in whom He delights and upon whom He puts His Spirit, to bring justice to the nations. The servant is gentle and faithful, and God promises a new song of praise and victory over darkness. Israel is called to listen, but the people are blind and deaf, and God allows them to be plundered for their sins.

segments.title: God's Servant Introduced
segments.gist: God declares His chosen servant, upheld and delighted in, who will bring justice to the nations without breaking a bruised reed.

segments.title: God's Promise to the Servant
segments.gist: God, the creator, calls His servant in righteousness to be a covenant and light, opening blind eyes and freeing prisoners.

segments.title: New Song of Praise
segments.gist: The earth and sea are called to sing a new song to the Lord, who goes forth like a mighty warrior.

segments.title: God's Zeal for His People
segments.gist: God declares He will cry out and destroy His enemies, leading the blind in a new way while they stumble.

segments.title: Israel's Blindness and Judgment
segments.gist: Israel is called to hear despite being blind and deaf; God gives them up to plunder for their sins.

43.summary: God reassures Israel of His protection and love, promising to gather them from all directions and citing their role as His witnesses. He declares that He alone is God, that He blots out their transgressions for His own sake, and He challenges them to remember how they have wearied Him with their sins.

segments.title: God's reassurance to Israel
segments.gist: God tells Israel not to fear, for He has redeemed them, will be with them through trials, and will gather their descendants from afar.

segments.title: Israel as God's witnesses
segments.gist: God calls the blind and deaf people to witness that He alone is God, and that no one can deliver from His hand.

segments.title: God promises a new exodus
segments.gist: God declares He will bring down Babylon and make a way in the wilderness, doing a new thing that will give Him praise.

segments.title: Israel's sins and God's judgment
segments.gist: God rebukes Israel for not calling on Him, for burdening Him with sins, and for forgetting Him, so He will bring judgment on their leaders.

44.summary: God reassures Israel of His choice and protection, promises to pour out His Spirit and blessing on their descendants, and contrasts His exclusive deity with the foolishness of idol-making. He calls Israel to remember these things and promises to blot out their sins and redeem them, culminating in a call for the heavens and earth to sing as He restores Jerusalem.

segments.title: God's Promise to Israel
segments.gist: God reminds Israel of His choice and promises to help, pour out His Spirit, and multiply their descendants.

segments.title: No God Besides Me
segments.gist: God declares His uniqueness and challenges false gods to foretell events, urging Israel not to fear.

segments.title: The Folly of Idolatry
segments.gist: The prophet exposes the absurdity of making idols from wood, using part for fuel and part for worship.

segments.title: Redemption and Joyful Praise
segments.gist: God calls Israel to remember their creation and promises to blot out sins, prompting a call for all creation to sing.

segments.title: God the Creator and Redeemer
segments.gist: God identifies Himself as Creator and Redeemer, who frustrates false prophets and confirms His word through Cyrus.

45.summary: God addresses Cyrus by name, declaring him His anointed instrument to subdue nations and free the exiles, while asserting that He alone is God and there is none beside Him. The chapter contrasts the hidden, sovereign purpose of God with the futility of idols, and closes with a universal call to look to Him for salvation.

segments.title: God's Charge to Cyrus
segments.gist: God promises to go before Cyrus, subdue nations, and give him treasures so he may know that the LORD calls him by name.

segments.title: Righteousness and Creation
segments.gist: God declares He created the earth and made it to be inhabited, and challenges the clay to question its maker.

segments.title: Nations Turn to God
segments.gist: The wealth of Egypt and Cush will come to Israel, and all who make idols will be ashamed, while the LORD speaks openly.

segments.title: Call to Look and Be Saved
segments.gist: God invites all ends of the earth to look to Him and be saved, and every knee will bow and every tongue swear allegiance.

46.summary: The chapter contrasts the powerless Babylonian idols Bel and Nebo, which are carried as burdens by beasts, with the God of Israel, who has carried his people from birth to old age and will save them. God declares that he alone is God, foretells the coming of a bird of prey from the east to execute his purpose against Babylon, and rebukes those who trust in idols.

segments.title: Bel and Nebo humbled
segments.gist: Babylon's idols Bel and Nebo are bowed down, loaded as burdens on weary beasts.

segments.title: God carries his people
segments.gist: God reminds Israel that he has carried them from birth and will continue to sustain them to old age.

segments.title: Idols cannot save
segments.gist: God challenges any comparison, describing how idols of gold are carried and cannot answer or save.

segments.title: God alone declares the end
segments.gist: God calls Israel to remember that he alone declares the end from the beginning and will bring his purpose to pass.

segments.title: Salvation for stubborn hearts
segments.gist: God addresses the stubborn-hearted, promising to bring near his righteousness and salvation to Zion.

47.summary: Isaiah 47 is a prophetic oracle against Babylon, depicting the city as a proud queen who will be humiliated and brought down. The chapter declares that Babylon's trust in sorceries and astrologers will not save her from sudden disaster, and that her arrogance and cruelty to God's people will be repaid.

segments.title: Babylon Humbled
segments.gist: Babylon is called to descend from her throne and sit in the dust, stripped of her royal status and exposed to shame.

segments.title: Judgment for Cruelty
segments.gist: Babylon is told to sit in silence and darkness because of her harsh treatment of God's people, whom she showed no mercy.

segments.title: False Security Exposed
segments.gist: Babylon's claim to be unique and secure is challenged; disaster will come suddenly, and her sorceries cannot avert it.

segments.title: Astrologers Powerless
segments.gist: Babylon is mocked to stand by her enchantments and astrologers, who cannot save her but will themselves be consumed.

48.summary: The LORD addresses the house of Jacob, exposing their stubbornness and idolatry while declaring that He alone has foretold events to come. He calls Israel to flee from Babylon and promises to redeem them, though the wicked have no peace.

segments.title: Israel's Stubbornness Rebuked
segments.gist: God confronts Israel's hypocritical worship and obstinacy, yet declares He will act for His own name's sake.

segments.title: God Alone Foretells and Calls
segments.gist: The LORD identifies Himself as the first and last, the only one who has declared future events, and calls Israel to hear.

segments.title: Redemption and Peace Promised
segments.gist: God promises to teach and lead Israel, to redeem them from Babylon, and warns that the wicked have no peace.

49.summary: The second Servant Song presents the Servant speaking of his call from the womb to be a light to the Gentiles and to restore Israel, though he is despised and seemingly laboring in vain. God answers with promises of protection, covenant, and the gathering of exiles, and the chapter closes with a declaration that Zion is not forgotten and that all flesh will know the LORD's salvation.

segments.title: The Servant's Call and Complaint
segments.gist: The Servant recounts his calling from the womb and laments that his labor seems vain, yet commits his cause to God.

segments.title: A Light to the Gentiles
segments.gist: God answers: the Servant will restore Israel and be a light to the Gentiles, though he is despised and abhorred.

segments.title: Promises of Restoration and Praise
segments.gist: God promises to preserve the Servant as a covenant, free prisoners, and provide for his people, prompting all creation to sing praise.

segments.title: Zion's Complaint and God's Answer
segments.gist: Zion feels forsaken, but God assures her that her children will return and she will be adorned with them.

segments.title: Nations Will Bring Back the Exiles
segments.gist: God declares that nations will bring back Zion's children, and all flesh will know that the LORD is her Savior and Redeemer.

50.summary: The chapter presents a dialogue in which the LORD challenges Israel's claim that He has abandoned them, asserting that their captivity is due to their own sins. The speaker, often understood as the Servant, then describes his obedience to God, his willingness to endure suffering, and his confidence that God will vindicate him, ending with a warning to those who walk in their own light.

segments.title: The LORD's Challenge to Israel
segments.gist: The LORD asks where the bill of divorce is and asserts His power to redeem, explaining that Israel's captivity resulted from their sins.

segments.title: The Servant's Obedience and Suffering
segments.gist: The Servant speaks of being taught by God, not rebelling, and willingly enduring beating and spitting from his adversaries.

segments.title: The Servant's Confidence in Vindication
segments.gist: The Servant expresses firm trust that God will help and vindicate him, so he is not ashamed and his adversaries will perish.

segments.title: Warning to Fearers and Self-Reliant
segments.gist: A call to those who fear the LORD to trust in Him, and a warning to those who kindle their own fire that they will lie down in sorrow.

51.summary: Isaiah 51 calls the faithful to remember their origins in Abraham and Sarah and God's comfort of Zion, while the prophet prays for Jerusalem to awake and drink the cup of God's wrath no more. God answers by promising to defend his people and put his words in their mouths, and the chapter closes with a call to depart from Babylon and a description of the cup of trembling passed to their tormentors.

segments.title: Look to Abraham and Sarah
segments.gist: God calls the righteous to look to the rock from which they were cut, promising to comfort Zion and make her wilderness like Eden.

segments.title: God's law and righteousness
segments.gist: God declares his law and justice a light to the peoples, urges the people to hear him, and contrasts the fading earth with his enduring salvation.

segments.title: Awake, arm of the Lord
segments.gist: A prayer asks God to awake as in days of old, recalling how he dried the sea and promising that the ransomed will return to Zion with singing.

segments.title: God answers with comfort
segments.gist: God replies that he is the one who comforts, asks why the people fear mortal oppressors, and promises to defend them and put his words in their mouths.

segments.title: Jerusalem's cup of trembling
segments.gist: Jerusalem is called to awake from the cup of God's wrath, which has left her with no guide among her sons.

segments.title: Cup taken from Jerusalem
segments.gist: God promises to take the cup of trembling from Jerusalem and give it to her tormentors, who will drink it and fall.

52.summary: God calls Zion to wake up and shake off her bonds, proclaiming that she has been sold for nothing and will be redeemed without money. The chapter announces the good news of peace and salvation, calls Jerusalem to rejoice, and closes with a prophetic description of the servant who will be exalted and marred.

segments.title: Zion Called to Awake
segments.gist: God commands Zion to put on strength and shake off dust, for she will no longer be captive.

segments.title: Sold for Nothing, Redeemed Freely
segments.gist: The Lord declares His people were sold for nothing and will be redeemed without money; He will reveal His name.

segments.title: Beautiful Feet Bring Good News
segments.gist: The prophet celebrates those who bring good tidings of peace and salvation, as the Lord comforts Zion.

segments.title: Depart from Babylon
segments.gist: Israel is called to leave Babylon, purify themselves, and carry the Lord's vessels, with God as their rear guard.

segments.title: The Exalted and Marred Servant
segments.gist: The Lord's servant will be exalted, though many are astonished at his marred appearance; he will sprinkle nations.

53.summary: The chapter presents the Suffering Servant, despised and rejected, who bears the griefs and sins of others and is wounded for their transgressions. He is oppressed, judged, and buried, yet through his suffering he justifies many and is exalted.

segments.title: The Servant Despised
segments.gist: The Servant grows up like a tender plant but is despised and rejected, with no beauty to attract others.

segments.title: Bearing Our Sorrows
segments.gist: He bears our griefs and carries our sorrows, is wounded for our transgressions, and by his stripes we are healed.

segments.title: Oppressed and Buried
segments.gist: He is oppressed and afflicted like a lamb, judged and cut off, buried with the rich though innocent.

segments.title: Satisfied Through Suffering
segments.gist: It pleases the Lord to bruise him; he makes an offering for sin, justifies many, and is exalted.

54.summary: Isaiah 54 is a prophetic address to barren Zion, promising restoration, numerous descendants, and the return of God's compassion. The LORD describes a coming ingathering of exiles, an everlasting covenant of peace, and the sure protection of Jerusalem, contrasting her former affliction with future glory.

segments.title: Barren Zion Called to Sing
segments.gist: The barren woman is told to sing and enlarge her tent, for her desolate days are over and her descendants will multiply.

segments.title: Shame Forgotten, Maker Redeems
segments.gist: Zion is told not to fear, for her Maker and Husband will restore her after a brief moment of anger and forsaking.

segments.title: Everlasting Kindness Like Noah's Oath
segments.gist: The LORD swears that as He swore after the flood, so He will not be angry with Zion, but His kindness and covenant of peace will endure.

segments.title: Afflicted City Rebuilt in Righteousness
segments.gist: The afflicted, storm-tossed city is promised a foundation of sapphires, gates of precious stones, and a future of righteousness and peace.

segments.title: No Weapon Formed Shall Prosper
segments.gist: Any alliance against Zion will fail, and every accusing tongue will be silenced; this is the heritage of the LORD's servants.

55.summary: God invites everyone to come and receive free provision, promising an everlasting covenant with David and urging people to seek Him while He may be found. He declares that His ways and thoughts are higher than ours, and that His word will accomplish its purpose, resulting in joy and peace for those who return to Him.

segments.title: Invitation to the Thirsty
segments.gist: God calls everyone who thirsts to come and buy without money, and promises an everlasting covenant with David.

segments.title: Seek the Lord While Near
segments.gist: The prophet urges people to seek the Lord and forsake wicked ways, for God's thoughts and ways are higher than ours.

segments.title: God's Word Accomplishes Its Purpose
segments.gist: Just as rain and snow water the earth, God's word will not return empty but will accomplish what He desires.

segments.title: Joy and Peace for the Redeemed
segments.gist: Those who go out with joy will be led in peace, and instead of thorns and briers, trees will grow as a memorial to the Lord.

56.summary: God calls for justice and righteousness, promising blessing to foreigners and eunuchs who keep His covenant, and rebuking Israel's blind and greedy leaders who neglect their duties.

segments.title: Exhortation to justice
segments.gist: God urges His people to maintain justice and do righteousness, for His salvation is near.

segments.title: Outsiders welcomed in covenant
segments.gist: Foreigners and eunuchs who keep the Sabbath and hold to God's covenant are promised a place in His house.

segments.title: Condemnation of blind leaders
segments.gist: Israel's watchmen are blind, greedy, and negligent, seeking only their own gain.

57.summary: Isaiah 57 contrasts the fate of the righteous who die in peace with the corrupt idolatrous generation that forsakes God, pursuing idols and foreign alliances. God rebukes their hypocrisy and empty rituals, yet promises to revive the contrite and humble, while the wicked are likened to a restless sea with no peace.

segments.title: The righteous perish unnoticed
segments.gist: The righteous are taken away in peace, spared from coming evil, though others do not understand.

segments.title: Rebuke of idolatrous children
segments.gist: God condemns the children of the sorceress for burning with lust among oaks and slaying children in valleys, making beds on high mountains and setting up memorials.

segments.title: Fear of men versus God
segments.gist: God asks why they fear men and forget Him, and declares that their righteousness and works will not profit them, but those who trust in Him will inherit the land.

segments.title: Prepare the way for the humble
segments.gist: A voice calls to prepare the way for God, who dwells in the high and holy place but also with the contrite and humble to revive them.

segments.title: Wrath and healing
segments.gist: God was angry because of the people's covetousness and hid His face, but He will heal them, lead them, and restore comfort to the mourners.

segments.title: No peace for the wicked
segments.gist: The wicked are like a troubled sea that cannot rest, casting up mire and dirt, and there is no peace for them.

58.summary: God rebukes Israel for fasting while continuing to oppress others, declaring that true fasting is to loose the bonds of wickedness and care for the poor. He promises that if they do this, light will break forth, healing will spring up, and they will be called repairers of the breach, inheriting the land and enjoying God's guidance.

segments.title: God Questions Their Fasting
segments.gist: God asks why Israel fasts but He does not notice, and explains that their fasting is marred by oppression and strife.

segments.title: True Fasting and Its Reward
segments.gist: God defines true fasting as loosing bonds and feeding the poor, and promises light, healing, and guidance if they obey.

segments.title: Honoring the Sabbath
segments.gist: If Israel honors the Sabbath and delights in the Lord, they will ride on the high places and inherit Jacob's heritage.

59.summary: Isaiah 59 describes the people's sins as separating them from God, portraying a society full of injustice and violence. God sees there is no one to intercede, so He arms Himself with righteousness and brings judgment, after which a Redeemer comes to Zion and God's covenant spirit remains with His people.

segments.title: Sins Separate from God
segments.gist: The prophet declares that God's hand is not shortened, but the people's iniquities have separated them from Him, producing lies, violence, and injustice.

segments.title: Confession of Widespread Sin
segments.gist: The people confess their blindness and stumbling, acknowledging transgressions and the lack of justice, with truth fallen in the streets.

segments.title: God Arms Himself for Judgment
segments.gist: Seeing no intercessor, God puts on righteousness and vengeance like armor to repay His adversaries and make His glory known.

segments.title: Redeemer Comes to Zion
segments.gist: A Redeemer comes to Zion and to those who turn from transgression, and God establishes His covenant and Spirit upon them forever.

60.summary: Isaiah 60 is a prophetic vision of Zion's future glory, where God's light rises upon his people, nations and kings stream to Jerusalem with wealth, the city's gates stay open to receive them, and former oppression gives way to peace and prosperity under God's everlasting covenant.

segments.title: Arise, shine; darkness covered
segments.gist: God's light rises on Zion while darkness covers the earth, and nations come to her light.

segments.title: Nations and wealth gather
segments.gist: Zion's sons and daughters return, and the wealth of the nations, including Midian, Ephah, and Sheba, comes to glorify God's house.

segments.title: Foreigners rebuild walls
segments.gist: Foreigners rebuild Zion's walls, kings serve her, and the formerly oppressive nations bow before her.

segments.title: From forsaken to eternal excellency
segments.gist: Zion, once forsaken, becomes an eternal excellency, receiving peace and praise instead of violence and destruction.

segments.title: God as everlasting light
segments.gist: The sun and moon fade as God becomes Zion's everlasting light, her people are righteous, and the small become a strong nation.

61.summary: The prophet speaks of his anointing by the Spirit to bring good tidings to the meek, comfort mourners, and proclaim liberty, describing Zion's restoration with rebuilt ruins, restored honor, and an everlasting covenant. He rejoices in salvation and righteousness, and the chapter closes with a promise that the Lord will cause righteousness and praise to spring forth before all nations.

segments.title: The Spirit's Anointed Mission
segments.gist: The speaker declares the Spirit's anointing to preach good tidings, heal the brokenhearted, proclaim liberty, and comfort mourners.

segments.title: Rebuilt Ruins and Restored Honor
segments.gist: Ancient ruins will be rebuilt, strangers will serve, and Israel will receive double honor and everlasting joy instead of shame.

segments.title: Covenant and Known Offspring
segments.gist: The Lord loves judgment and establishes an everlasting covenant, making Israel's offspring known among the nations.

segments.title: Rejoicing in Salvation
segments.gist: The speaker rejoices in God's salvation, clothed in righteousness, and declares that the Lord will cause righteousness and praise to spring forth.

62.summary: Isaiah 62 is a prophetic declaration of Zion's restoration, where God promises to give Jerusalem a new name, vindicate her before the nations, and establish her as a praise in the earth. The chapter depicts watchmen on the walls who pray without ceasing until Jerusalem is made a praise, and it concludes with a call to prepare the way for the returning exiles and to make the city a place of holiness and worship.

segments.title: Zion's New Name and Glory
segments.gist: God promises Zion a new name, a crown of glory, and vindication before the nations, and she will no longer be called Forsaken or Desolate.

segments.title: Watchmen Pray Without Ceasing
segments.gist: Watchmen are set on Jerusalem's walls to pray day and night until God establishes Jerusalem as a praise, and God swears to give her harvest to her people.

segments.title: Prepare the Way for the Exiles
segments.gist: A call goes out to prepare the way for the returning exiles, and they will be called the Holy People, the Redeemed of the Lord, and the City Not Forsaken.

63.summary: Isaiah 63 begins with a dialogue envisioning the LORD returning from Edom with garments stained red from trampling the nations in judgment. The prophet then recounts God's past mercies to Israel, confesses the people's rebellion, and pleads for God to intervene as their Father and Redeemer.

segments.title: The Warrior from Edom
segments.gist: A watchman asks who comes from Edom with dyed garments, and the LORD answers that he has trodden the winepress of judgment alone.

segments.title: Recalling God's Mercies
segments.gist: The prophet praises the LORD for his past lovingkindness and recounts how he saved, led, and gave rest to Israel despite their rebellion.

segments.title: Plea for Divine Compassion
segments.gist: The people cry out for God to look down from heaven, acknowledge their plight, and act as their Father and Redeemer despite their long estrangement.

64.summary: Isaiah 64 is a communal prayer of petition in which the people plead for God to rend the heavens and come down, acknowledge their sin and God's fatherly discipline, and appeal for mercy so that God will not remember iniquity forever.

segments.title: Plea for God to Come Down
segments.gist: The prophet cries for God to rend the heavens and descend, so that nations may tremble at His presence as in past mighty acts.

segments.title: Confession of Sin and Unworthiness
segments.gist: The people confess that all their righteousness is as filthy rags, that their iniquities carry them away, and that no one calls on God.

segments.title: Appeal to God as Father and Potter
segments.gist: They appeal to God as Father and Potter, asking Him not to be exceedingly angry nor remember iniquity forever.

segments.title: Lament over Zion's Desolation
segments.gist: The prayer laments that the holy cities are a wilderness and the temple is burned, and asks if God will hold His peace and afflict them severely.

65.summary: God answers Israel's apostasy by declaring judgment on those who provoke Him with idolatrous practices, while preserving a remnant of faithful servants. He promises a new creation with a restored Jerusalem, where His people will enjoy peace and prosperity, and the wicked will be judged.

segments.title: God's indictment of rebellious Israel
segments.gist: God describes Israel's persistent idolatry and provocation, saying He was ready to be sought but they rebelled.

segments.title: Remnant preserved, apostates judged
segments.gist: God will preserve a remnant like good grapes, but those who forsake Him will fall by the sword.

segments.title: Servants blessed, rebels cursed
segments.gist: God contrasts the future of His servants, who will eat and rejoice, with His enemies, who will suffer shame.

segments.title: New heavens and new earth promised
segments.gist: God promises a new creation where Jerusalem will be a joy, with long life, security, and harmony among His people.

66.summary: Isaiah 66 closes the book with God's declaration that heaven is his throne and the earth his footstool, rejecting empty temple worship while promising comfort to the humble. It describes the sudden rebirth of Zion, the gathering of nations to see God's glory, and final judgment separating the righteous from the rebellious.

segments.title: True Worship and Judgment
segments.gist: God declares heaven his throne, condemns hypocritical sacrifices, and promises to answer the humble while judging the rebellious.

segments.title: Zion's Sudden Rebirth
segments.gist: Zion gives birth without labor, and God promises to comfort Jerusalem and prosper his servants.

segments.title: Final Judgment and Gathering
segments.gist: God comes in fire to judge the wicked, gathers survivors from all nations to see his glory, and describes the eternal fate of the rebellious.

1.summary: God calls Jeremiah to be a prophet, telling him he was chosen before birth. Jeremiah protests his youth, but God promises to be with him and gives him visions of an almond branch and a boiling pot, signaling judgment and the coming threat from the north.

segments.title: Jeremiah's Call and Divine Knowledge
segments.gist: God tells Jeremiah that He knew and appointed him as a prophet to the nations before his birth.

segments.title: Jeremiah's Protest and God's Assurance
segments.gist: Jeremiah objects that he is too young, but God commands him to speak and promises to be with him and deliver him.

segments.title: Vision of the Almond Branch
segments.gist: God shows Jeremiah an almond branch as a sign that He will watch over His word to fulfill it.

segments.title: Vision of the Boiling Pot
segments.gist: God shows a boiling pot tilting from the north, signaling disaster from northern kingdoms against Judah for their idolatry.

segments.title: God's Commission to Jeremiah
segments.gist: God commands Jeremiah to stand firm and promises to make him a fortified city against his opponents.

2.summary: Jeremiah delivers a prophetic indictment against Judah, recalling the nation's early devotion to God and contrasting it with their current idolatry and abandonment of the Lord. He describes the consequences of their sin, including foreign alliances and impending judgment, while calling them to repent and return to God.

segments.title: God recalls Israel's early devotion
segments.gist: The Lord remembers Israel's youthful love and faithfulness, asking what fault they found in Him to turn away.

segments.title: Accusation of forsaking God
segments.gist: God charges the people with forsaking Him, the fountain of living waters, and turning to worthless idols.

segments.title: Two evils: forsaking and hewing cisterns
segments.gist: The Lord declares two evils: forsaking Him and hewing broken cisterns, and warns of judgment.

segments.title: Consequences of foreign alliances
segments.gist: Israel's alliances with Assyria and Egypt bring shame and punishment, illustrating the cost of forsaking God.

segments.title: Israel's stubborn idolatry
segments.gist: Despite God's goodness, Israel plays the harlot on high hills, forgetting God and turning to idols.

segments.title: Judah's futile trust in others
segments.gist: God questions why Judah contends with Him, and condemns their trust in foreign powers that will fail them.

3.summary: Jeremiah 3 continues the call for Israel to return to God despite her harlotry, contrasting the faithless northern kingdom with treacherous Judah. God promises restoration and a future gathering of his people to Zion under faithful shepherds, and calls for repentance and circumcision of the heart.

segments.title: Call to Return Despite Harlotry
segments.gist: God appeals to Israel, saying she has played the harlot but still invites her to return to him.

segments.title: Faithless Israel and Treacherous Judah
segments.gist: The Lord contrasts backsliding Israel with treacherous Judah, noting Judah did not learn from Israel's example.

segments.title: Promise of Restoration and Shepherds
segments.gist: God promises to bring a remnant back to Zion and give them shepherds after his own heart.

segments.title: Future Gathering Without the Ark
segments.gist: In those days the ark will no longer be remembered, and Israel and Judah will come together from the north.

segments.title: Lament and Call to Repentance
segments.gist: God laments Israel's unfaithfulness, and a voice calls for repentance and circumcision of the heart.

4.summary: Jeremiah calls Israel to return to God and warns that judgment is coming from the north. He describes the invading army and its devastation, and laments the coming destruction of Judah and Jerusalem.

segments.title: Call to Return
segments.gist: God invites Israel to return to Him, promising mercy if they put away their abominations.

segments.title: Warning of Invasion
segments.gist: Jeremiah warns of a lion-like destroyer coming from the north against Judah and Jerusalem.

segments.title: Judgment from the North
segments.gist: The prophet describes the fierce invading army and the coming siege because of Judah's wickedness.

segments.title: Prophet's Anguish
segments.gist: Jeremiah expresses deep sorrow over the destruction and the foolishness of the people.

segments.title: Vision of Desolation
segments.gist: The land is pictured as formless and empty, with cities ruined and the earth mourning under God's anger.

segments.title: Desperate Flight
segments.gist: People flee the horsemen and archers, and Jerusalem is portrayed as a woman in anguish.

5.summary: Jeremiah is commanded to search Jerusalem for one just man, but finds only swearing and refusal to repent. He declares that judgment is coming because the people have forsaken God, ignored his warnings, and turned to idols and adultery, so God will bring a distant nation against them.

segments.title: Search for a Just Man
segments.gist: God tells Jeremiah to search Jerusalem for one just man, but finds only swearing and refusal to repent.

segments.title: Judgment for Forsaking God
segments.gist: Because the people have forsaken God and served other gods, God will bring a nation against them.

segments.title: The People's Willful Rebellion
segments.gist: The people are foolish, rebellious, and wealthy, ignoring God's warnings and oppressing the poor.

segments.title: A Horrible Thing in the Land
segments.gist: Prophets prophesy falsely, priests rule by their own authority, and the people love it.

6.summary: Jeremiah 6 continues the prophet's warning of Jerusalem's coming destruction, calling the people to flee and describing the advancing enemy from the north. The chapter condemns the leaders' greed and false peace, rejects the people's empty temple rituals, and portrays Jeremiah as a tester of the people's ways, with the nation facing ruin for its stubborn rebellion.

segments.title: Call to Flee Jerusalem
segments.gist: Jeremiah urges Benjamin to flee as enemy forces gather against Jerusalem, and God declares the city's destruction.

segments.title: Greed and False Peace
segments.gist: God commands a remnant to be gleaned, and the people's leaders are condemned for greed and falsely claiming peace.

segments.title: Rejection of God's Way
segments.gist: The people refuse to walk in the good way, reject the watchmen's warnings, and face stumbling and disaster.

segments.title: Enemy from the North
segments.gist: A cruel nation from the north advances with weapons, causing anguish and terror in Jerusalem.

segments.title: Jeremiah as Tester
segments.gist: God appoints Jeremiah as a tester of the people, who are found to be stubborn and rejected like impure metal.

7.summary: Jeremiah delivers a temple sermon, calling Judah to amend their ways and not trust in the deceptive slogan 'the temple of the LORD.' He denounces their idolatry and hypocrisy, warns of destruction like Shiloh, and describes the coming judgment on the land and people.

segments.title: Call to Amend Ways
segments.gist: Jeremiah urges Judah to reform their actions and not trust in lying words that the temple will protect them despite their sins.

segments.title: Judgment on Idolatry
segments.gist: God forbids Jeremiah to pray for the people, describing their idolatrous worship and the coming wrath on the land.

segments.title: Obedience Over Sacrifice
segments.gist: God recalls commanding obedience at the exodus, not sacrifice, and laments that the people have not listened but walked in their own counsel.

segments.title: Abominations and Coming Destruction
segments.gist: Jeremiah describes the people's abominations in the temple and the resulting desolation of the land and cities.

8.summary: Jeremiah 8 continues the prophet's indictment of Judah: the people persist in idolatry and refuse to repent, the wise and the priests are confounded, and the prophet laments the coming destruction and the incurable wound of his people.

segments.title: Exposed bones and stubborn impenitence
segments.gist: The bones of Judah's leaders will be exhumed and exposed because the people cling to idolatry and refuse to return to the Lord.

segments.title: No one repents or returns
segments.gist: The Lord contrasts the instinct of birds with Judah's willful backsliding, noting that no one says 'What have I done?'

segments.title: False wisdom and shameful leaders
segments.gist: The wise, the scribes, and the priests are put to shame because they have rejected the word of the Lord and dealt falsely.

segments.title: I will consume them
segments.gist: The Lord declares he will consume Judah like a fig tree with no fruit; the people will face invading horses and serpents.

segments.title: Jeremiah's grief over the wound
segments.gist: The prophet laments the incurable wound of his people and asks whether there is no balm in Gilead.

9.summary: Jeremiah laments the deceit and corruption of Judah, describing the people's lies, treachery, and refusal to know God. He foretells judgment, including the destruction of Jerusalem and the scattering of the people, while warning against trusting in human wisdom or strength and calling for mourning over the coming devastation.

segments.title: Jeremiah's Grief over Judah's Sins
segments.gist: Jeremiah wishes for a lodging place to weep over the people's adultery, lies, and deceit, as they proceed from evil to evil and do not know God.

segments.title: God's Judgment on Deceitful People
segments.gist: The Lord declares He will refine and test the people for their deceit, and will bring destruction upon Jerusalem and the cities of Judah.

segments.title: Reason for the Coming Destruction
segments.gist: The Lord explains that the land will be desolate because the people have forsaken His law and followed their own hearts and Baalim.

segments.title: Call to Mourning and Lamentation
segments.gist: The Lord commands the people to call for mourning women and lament, for death has come and the corpses will fall like dung in the field.

segments.title: True Glory in Knowing God
segments.gist: The Lord says that the wise, mighty, and rich should not glory in their own abilities, but in understanding and knowing Him.

segments.title: Judgment on the Uncircumcised in Heart
segments.gist: The Lord declares He will punish all who are uncircumcised in heart, including Judah, for they are not truly circumcised.

10.summary: Jeremiah contrasts the living God with idols, who are powerless and will perish, and warns of the coming destruction of Judah. He laments the folly of Israel's leaders and the people's fear, and prays for correction and for God's wrath to fall on the nations that have devoured Jacob.

segments.title: Idols are worthless
segments.gist: Israel is told not to learn the way of the heathen, for the customs of the people are vain and their idols cannot speak or walk.

segments.title: The living God is great
segments.gist: The LORD is great and mighty; the nations' idols are brutish and foolish, but the LORD is the true God and everlasting King.

segments.title: God made the earth
segments.gist: The gods that did not make the heavens and earth shall perish; the LORD made the world by his power and is the portion of Jacob.

segments.title: Siege and lament
segments.gist: Jeremiah warns of the coming siege and the sound of war, and laments the destruction of Judah and the folly of the shepherds.

segments.title: Jeremiah's prayer
segments.gist: Jeremiah prays for correction with justice, asks for God's wrath on the wicked nations, and pleads for mercy on Jacob.

11.summary: God commands Jeremiah to announce a curse on anyone who does not obey the covenant made with Israel's ancestors, which they broke despite God's repeated warnings. The people of Judah and Jerusalem plot against Jeremiah's life, and he asks God to punish them, expressing his trust that God will judge rightly.

segments.title: Curse for Breaking the Covenant
segments.gist: God tells Jeremiah to pronounce a curse on those who do not obey the covenant, which God commanded Israel to keep.

segments.title: God's Warning and Rebuke
segments.gist: God reminds Jeremiah that he has warned the people persistently, but they have not listened, and their ancestors broke the covenant.

segments.title: Conspiracy and Coming Disaster
segments.gist: God declares that Judah and Jerusalem have conspired to break the covenant, so disaster will come and their idols will not save them.

segments.title: No Intercession for Judah
segments.gist: God forbids Jeremiah from praying for the people, because their sacrifices and beloved practices cannot avert the coming judgment.

segments.title: Plot Against Jeremiah Revealed
segments.gist: God reveals the plot against Jeremiah's life, and he appeals to God as a righteous judge to take vengeance on his enemies.

segments.title: Judgment on the Men of Anathoth
segments.gist: God pronounces judgment on the men of Anathoth who threatened Jeremiah, promising that their young men will die and a remnant will not remain.

12.summary: Jeremiah questions why the wicked prosper and the treacherous are at ease, asking how long the land will mourn. God answers that judgment is coming, even upon his own household, and that he has forsaken his heritage because of its sins; yet he promises to restore the nations that turn to him.

segments.title: Jeremiah's Complaint
segments.gist: Jeremiah asks why the wicked prosper and the treacherous are at ease, and how long the land will mourn.

segments.title: God's First Answer
segments.gist: God warns that if Jeremiah has grown weary in a peaceful land, he will struggle more in the swelling of Jordan.

segments.title: God's Lament Over His Heritage
segments.gist: God describes forsaking his heritage and giving it into the hands of enemies, resulting in desolation.

segments.title: Promise of Restoration
segments.gist: God promises to restore the nations that learn the ways of his people, but to uproot those that do not listen.

13.summary: Jeremiah is told by God to buy and wear a linen girdle, then hide it by the Euphrates where it becomes marred, as a sign that Judah's pride will be ruined. The chapter pronounces judgment on Judah's drunkenness, captivity, and humiliation, and ends with a warning against self-exaltation, comparing the people to a harlot and depicting their shame.

segments.title: The Linen Girdle Sign
segments.gist: God commands Jeremiah to wear a linen girdle, hide it by the Euphrates, and retrieve it marred, symbolizing Judah's ruined pride.

segments.title: Bottles Filled with Wine
segments.gist: Jeremiah declares that all inhabitants will be filled with drunkenness and dashed against one another as God shows no pity.

segments.title: Call to Give Glory
segments.gist: The people are urged to give glory to God before darkness falls and their feet stumble on the dark mountains.

segments.title: Warning to the King
segments.gist: The king and queen mother are told to humble themselves, for their beautiful flock is taken captive and Judah is carried away.

segments.title: Judah's Shame Exposed
segments.gist: Jerusalem is asked to look at the invading army from the north, and her sins are exposed like a harlot's shame.

14.summary: Jeremiah receives a word from the LORD about a severe drought and famine in Judah, and the people's cry for mercy. The LORD refuses to accept their fasting and offerings because of the people's sins and the false prophets' lies, and Jeremiah laments his own sorrow and the nation's wound.

segments.title: Drought and Famine in Judah
segments.gist: The LORD describes a severe drought: the people mourn, the ground is cracked, and even nobles and farmers suffer for lack of water.

segments.title: Plea for Mercy Despite Sins
segments.gist: The people confess their sins and ask the LORD not to forsake them, calling Him their hope and savior in time of trouble.

segments.title: LORD Refuses Their Fasting
segments.gist: The LORD rejects the people's fasting and offerings, declaring He will consume them by sword, famine, and pestilence because of their sins.

segments.title: False Prophets Condemned
segments.gist: The LORD exposes the false prophets who speak lies in His name, promising peace; He will punish both them and those who listen.

segments.title: Jeremiah's Lament over Judah
segments.gist: Jeremiah is commanded to weep for the people's brokenness, and he describes the devastation of famine and sword throughout the land.

segments.title: Final Plea for the LORD's Sake
segments.gist: Jeremiah pleads with the LORD not to reject Judah utterly, confessing their wickedness and appealing to His covenant and name.

15.summary: Jeremiah is told by God that even Moses and Samuel could not intercede for Judah, whose judgment is fixed; he laments his own persecution and God reassures him of protection and vindication.

segments.title: Judah's Inescapable Judgment
segments.gist: God declares that even Moses and Samuel could not turn away His judgment on Judah, which will come through sword, famine, and captivity.

segments.title: Jeremiah's Complaint and God's Answer
segments.gist: Jeremiah laments his contentious role, and God promises to strengthen him and make his enemies turn to him, though judgment remains.

segments.title: Jeremiah's Prayer for Vindication
segments.gist: Jeremiah asks God to remember and avenge him, expressing pain and confusion over his suffering and the burden of his message.

segments.title: God's Promise of Protection
segments.gist: God tells Jeremiah to repent and speak worthy words, promising to make him a fortified wall and to deliver him from his enemies.

16.summary: God forbids Jeremiah to marry and to attend funerals or feasts as signs of the coming judgment on Judah. He declares that the people will be cast out of the land and served by foreign nations, yet promises a future restoration when they will be brought back and will know the LORD.

segments.title: Jeremiah Forbidden to Marry
segments.gist: God tells Jeremiah not to take a wife or have children in this place because of the disaster coming on families in Judah.

segments.title: No Mourning or Feasting
segments.gist: Jeremiah is barred from funerals and feasts, for God has withdrawn his peace and steadfast love from this people.

segments.title: Reason for Exile
segments.gist: When the people ask why disaster comes, God says their fathers and they have forsaken him for other gods, so they will be cast into a foreign land.

segments.title: Promise of Return
segments.gist: God vows that a day will come when the exodus from Egypt will be eclipsed by the return of Israel from the north and all lands.

segments.title: Double Punishment for Idolatry
segments.gist: God summons fishermen and hunters to catch the people; their iniquity is doubled because they defiled the land with idols.

segments.title: Jeremiah's Prayer and God's Answer
segments.gist: Jeremiah prays that the nations will come to God, and God declares he will make his power and name known to them.

17.summary: Jeremiah is told that Judah's sin is written on their hearts, and the man who trusts in man is cursed while the one who trusts in the LORD is blessed. The chapter moves through prophetic laments, a call to keep the Sabbath holy, and warnings of exile and shame.

segments.title: Sin Inscribed on Judah's Heart
segments.gist: Judah's sin is written on their hearts and altars, and they will lose their heritage.

segments.title: Cursed and Blessed Trust
segments.gist: The man who trusts in man is cursed like a barren shrub, but the one who trusts in the LORD is blessed like a watered tree.

segments.title: Deceitful Heart and Unjust Riches
segments.gist: The heart is deceitful above all things, and gaining riches unjustly leads to loss.

segments.title: Jeremiah's Lament and Plea
segments.gist: Jeremiah appeals to the LORD as his hope and asks for healing and protection from his persecutors.

segments.title: Sabbath Command and Warning
segments.gist: Jeremiah is told to warn the people to keep the Sabbath holy, with blessing for obedience and destruction for disobedience.

18.summary: The LORD sends Jeremiah to the potter's house, where the vessel being reshaped becomes a sign of His authority over Israel and Judah. He warns that a nation turning from evil can be spared and one turning to evil can be uprooted, and He exposes Judah's stubborn refusal to repent. The chapter ends with a plot against Jeremiah's life and his prayer that God would vindicate him and bring disaster on his enemies.

segments.title: Jeremiah Sent to the Potter
segments.gist: The LORD tells Jeremiah to go to the potter's house, where He will reveal His word to him.

segments.title: The Potter's House Lesson
segments.gist: God compares His dealings with nations to the potter reshaping clay, warning that He may relent or bring disaster depending on their response.

segments.title: Judah's Refusal to Repent
segments.gist: The LORD calls Judah to turn from evil, but the people refuse, saying they will follow their own plans.

segments.title: Israel's Unnatural Apostasy
segments.gist: God laments that His people have committed an unheard-of apostasy, forgetting Him and turning to false paths.

segments.title: Plot Against Jeremiah
segments.gist: The people plot to attack Jeremiah and destroy his message, and he prays for God to remember his faithfulness.

segments.title: Jeremiah's Prayer for Vengeance
segments.gist: Jeremiah asks God to bring disaster on his enemies and not forgive their iniquity.

19.summary: The LORD instructs Jeremiah to buy a potter's earthen bottle and proclaim judgment in the valley of Hinnom, because Judah has forsaken Him and burned children to Baal. Jeremiah delivers the message of disaster, then breaks the bottle before the elders as a sign that God will shatter the people and the city, and he repeats the warning in the temple court.

segments.title: Jeremiah buys a potter's bottle
segments.gist: God tells Jeremiah to buy a clay bottle and announce judgment in the valley of Hinnom before the elders and priests.

segments.title: Judah's idolatry and coming disaster
segments.gist: The LORD declares He will bring disaster because Judah has forsaken Him, burned incense to other gods, and sacrificed children to Baal.

segments.title: Breaking the bottle as a sign
segments.gist: Jeremiah breaks the bottle before the men, symbolizing how God will shatter the people and city, making Tophet a burial place.

segments.title: Jeremiah repeats warning in the temple
segments.gist: Jeremiah returns to the temple court and tells all the people that God will bring the announced disaster because they have stiffened their necks.

20.summary: Jeremiah is beaten and put in stocks by Pashur, the priest and chief governor of the temple, for prophesying; after his release he delivers a message of doom against Pashur and Babylon. The chapter then shifts to Jeremiah's anguished complaint, in which he accuses God of deceiving him, describes the mockery and threats he faces, and curses the day of his birth.

segments.title: Pashur Persecutes Jeremiah
segments.gist: Pashur the priest beats Jeremiah and puts him in stocks; after release Jeremiah prophesies that Pashur and Judah will be carried captive to Babylon.

segments.title: Jeremiah's Complaint of Deception
segments.gist: Jeremiah accuses God of deceiving him and laments that he is mocked and surrounded by threats and false friends.

segments.title: Jeremiah Trusts in God's Deliverance
segments.gist: Jeremiah expresses confidence that God will deliver him and punish his persecutors, and he calls for praise to the Lord.

segments.title: Jeremiah Curses His Birth
segments.gist: Jeremiah curses the day he was born and the man who announced his birth, wishing he had died in the womb to avoid a life of sorrow and shame.

21.summary: King Zedekiah sends Pashur and Zephaniah to ask Jeremiah to inquire of the LORD for deliverance from Nebuchadnezzar's siege. Jeremiah answers that the LORD will fight against Jerusalem, that the city will fall, and that the people must choose between death and surrender; he then pronounces judgment on the house of David for injustice.

segments.title: Zedekiah's Envoys Seek Help
segments.gist: King Zedekiah sends Pashur and Zephaniah to ask Jeremiah to inquire of the LORD for deliverance from Nebuchadnezzar.

segments.title: The LORD Will Fight Against Jerusalem
segments.gist: Jeremiah declares that the LORD will turn the weapons of Judah against them and fight against the city with outstretched hand.

segments.title: Choice of Life or Death
segments.gist: The LORD sets before the people the choice of surrender and life or resistance and death by sword, famine, and pestilence.

segments.title: Judgment on the House of David
segments.gist: The LORD calls the house of David to execute justice and warns that he will punish their evil deeds with fire and destruction.

22.summary: Jeremiah delivers a series of oracles against the kings of Judah, beginning with a call for justice and a warning to the house of David, then pronouncing judgment on Shallum (Jehoahaz), Jehoiakim, and Coniah (Jehoiachin), and ending with a lament for the shepherds who scattered God's flock.

segments.title: Call for Justice and Warning
segments.gist: Jeremiah tells the king of Judah to execute justice and righteousness, warning that failure will bring destruction to the palace.

segments.title: Judgment on Shallum
segments.gist: The people are told not to weep for the dead king but for Shallum, who will die in captivity and never return.

segments.title: Woe to Jehoiakim
segments.gist: Jehoiakim is condemned for building his house with injustice and oppression; he will be buried like a donkey and mourned by none.

segments.title: Lament for Jerusalem
segments.gist: Jerusalem is called to cry out from Lebanon and Bashan, for her lovers are destroyed and she will be ashamed.

segments.title: Judgment on Coniah
segments.gist: Coniah is likened to a despised broken vessel, to be cast out and childless, with none of his seed to sit on David's throne.

23.summary: Jeremiah denounces the shepherds who scatter God's flock and promises to gather a remnant and raise up a righteous Branch. He then condemns the false prophets who speak visions of their own heart and lead the people astray with lies, contrasting them with the true word of God.

segments.title: Woe to the Shepherds
segments.gist: God pronounces woe on the shepherds who destroy and scatter His flock, promising to punish them and gather the remnant Himself.

segments.title: The Righteous Branch
segments.gist: God promises to raise up a righteous Branch from David who will reign wisely, and Judah will be saved and dwell safely.

segments.title: Judgment on False Prophets
segments.gist: Jeremiah's heart is broken over the land's adultery and lies; God declares He will feed the false prophets with wormwood and bring disaster on Jerusalem.

segments.title: Do Not Listen to Them
segments.gist: God warns the people not to listen to the false prophets who speak visions of their own heart, not from the LORD's mouth.

segments.title: The LORD's Word Like Fire
segments.gist: God challenges the false prophets who steal His words and prophesy lies, asking if His word is not like fire and a hammer.

segments.title: The Burden of the LORD
segments.gist: God instructs the people to stop using the phrase 'the burden of the LORD' falsely, warning of judgment and everlasting reproach.

24.summary: After Babylon carries King Jeconiah and the craftsmen of Judah into exile, the LORD shows Jeremiah two baskets of figs set before the temple: one very good, the other so rotten it cannot be eaten. The LORD explains that the exiles are like the good figs, whom He will restore and give a heart to know Him, while Zedekiah and those remaining in Jerusalem and Egypt are like the bad figs, destined for ruin and scattering.

segments.title: Two baskets of figs
segments.gist: The LORD shows Jeremiah two baskets of figs set before the temple after Babylon exiles Jeconiah and Judah's craftsmen.

segments.title: Good figs: the exiles
segments.gist: The LORD says the good figs represent the exiles, whom He will bring back, build up, and give a heart to know Him.

segments.title: Bad figs: Zedekiah and remnant
segments.gist: The LORD likens Zedekiah, the remaining Judeans, and those in Egypt to rotten figs, destined for reproach, sword, famine, and pestilence.

25.summary: Jeremiah delivers a word from the LORD to Judah and the surrounding nations, announcing that Babylon will rule over them for seventy years and that they must submit to Nebuchadnezzar or face destruction. After the seventy years, Babylon itself will be judged, and Jeremiah pronounces God's wrath against a long list of nations, ending with a vision of worldwide judgment.

segments.title: Jeremiah's Twenty-Three Year Warning
segments.gist: Jeremiah recounts that for twenty-three years he has spoken God's words to Judah, but the people have not listened or turned from their idols.

segments.title: Seventy Years of Babylonian Rule
segments.gist: Because Judah refused to hear, God will bring Nebuchadnezzar against them and make them serve Babylon for seventy years, after which Babylon will be punished.

segments.title: Cup of Wrath for the Nations
segments.gist: God commands Jeremiah to make the nations drink the cup of His wrath, beginning with Jerusalem and extending to all peoples, so that they may be destroyed.

segments.title: The LORD's Roar Against the Nations
segments.gist: The LORD will roar from on high and bring judgment on all nations, and the shepherds and leaders will wail because their land is laid waste.

26.summary: Jeremiah delivers a temple sermon calling Judah to repent or face destruction like Shiloh, and is seized by priests and prophets who demand his death. He defends his prophecy as from God, and the people spare him; elders recall how Micah was spared and how Urijah was killed, showing divided attitudes toward prophets.

segments.title: Jeremiah's Temple Sermon
segments.gist: God commands Jeremiah to stand in the temple court and call all Judah to repent and obey, warning of destruction like Shiloh.

segments.title: Priests and Prophets Seize Jeremiah
segments.gist: Priests, prophets, and people seize Jeremiah and demand his death for prophesying against the temple and city.

segments.title: Jeremiah's Defense
segments.gist: Jeremiah declares his prophecy is from God, urges the people to repent, and warns that innocent blood will be on them if they kill him.

segments.title: People and Elders Spare Jeremiah
segments.gist: The princes and people defend Jeremiah, and elders recall Micah's similar prophecy and Hezekiah's fear of the Lord, sparing Jeremiah.

segments.title: Urijah Killed for Prophecy
segments.gist: Urijah prophesies similarly, flees to Egypt, is brought back by Jehoiakim's men, and is killed and buried without honor.

27.summary: Jeremiah is commanded to make yokes and send word to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre, and Sidon that God has given all lands into Nebuchadnezzar's hand; nations that submit will live, but those that resist will be destroyed. He warns Zedekiah and the priests not to listen to false prophets who promise the Babylonian yoke will be broken, and declares that the temple vessels will be carried to Babylon until the day God restores them.

segments.title: Yokes sent to neighboring kings
segments.gist: God tells Jeremiah to make yokes and send a message to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre, and Sidon that He has given their lands to Nebuchadnezzar.

segments.title: Submit to Babylon or perish
segments.gist: God declares that any nation refusing to serve Nebuchadnezzar will be punished by sword, famine, and pestilence, while those who submit will remain in their land.

segments.title: Warning to Zedekiah
segments.gist: Jeremiah urges King Zedekiah of Judah to submit to Babylon and warns him not to trust prophets who falsely claim the yoke will be broken.

segments.title: False prophets and temple vessels
segments.gist: Jeremiah tells the priests and people not to believe prophets who say the temple vessels will soon return, and challenges those prophets to intercede so the remaining vessels stay.

segments.title: Vessels to remain in Babylon
segments.gist: God says the remaining vessels of the temple will be carried to Babylon and stay there until the day He visits and restores them to Jerusalem.

28.summary: In the fourth year of Zedekiah, the prophet Hananiah publicly contradicts Jeremiah, declaring that within two years God will break Babylon's yoke, return the temple vessels, and bring back Jeconiah and the exiles. Jeremiah responds that only when a prophet's word comes true is he known to be sent by God. Hananiah then breaks the wooden yoke from Jeremiah's neck, and God sends Jeremiah to announce an iron yoke of Babylonian servitude and to pronounce Hananiah's death that same year.

segments.title: Hananiah's False Prophecy
segments.gist: Hananiah tells Jeremiah that God will break Babylon's yoke and restore the temple vessels and exiles within two years.

segments.title: Jeremiah's Cautious Reply
segments.gist: Jeremiah says he hopes Hananiah's words come true but that a prophet is proven only when his prophecy is fulfilled.

segments.title: Hananiah Breaks the Yoke
segments.gist: Hananiah takes the yoke from Jeremiah's neck, breaks it, and repeats that God will break Babylon's yoke within two years.

segments.title: Yoke of Iron Foretold
segments.gist: God tells Jeremiah to say that Hananiah broke wooden bars but God will replace them with an iron yoke of Babylonian servitude.

segments.title: Hananiah's Death Pronounced
segments.gist: Jeremiah tells Hananiah he has made the people trust a lie and that he will die that year; Hananiah dies in the seventh month.

29.summary: Jeremiah writes to the Jewish exiles in Babylon, urging them to settle, build, and seek the city's welfare because the exile will last seventy years; after that God will restore them. He warns against false prophets who promise a quick return, and he pronounces judgment on those who rebel, including Ahab and Zedekiah, and on Shemaiah for opposing the letter.

segments.title: Jeremiah's letter to the exiles
segments.gist: Jeremiah sends a letter from Jerusalem to the elders, priests, prophets, and people carried away to Babylon.

segments.title: Build and seek Babylon's peace
segments.gist: God commands the exiles to build houses, plant gardens, marry, and seek Babylon's welfare, for in its peace they will find peace.

segments.title: Seventy years then restoration
segments.gist: After seventy years God will visit the exiles, fulfill his promise, and be found by them when they seek him with all their heart.

segments.title: Judgment on the people
segments.gist: Because the people trusted false prophets, God will send sword, famine, and pestilence and make them a horror to all nations.

segments.title: Ahab and Zedekiah judged
segments.gist: God condemns Ahab and Zedekiah for prophesying lies and committing adultery, and they will be delivered to Nebuchadnezzar.

segments.title: Shemaiah's rebuke and doom
segments.gist: Shemaiah writes to oppose Jeremiah; God declares that Shemaiah's family will not see the good he promises to his people.

30.summary: Jeremiah 30 records God's promise to restore Israel and Judah from exile, bringing them back to the land and breaking their yoke of bondage. The chapter contrasts the coming time of trouble with deliverance, healing, and a renewed covenant in which God will be their God and they will be His people.

segments.title: Command to Write Restoration
segments.gist: God tells Jeremiah to write in a book that He will bring His people back from captivity to the land.

segments.title: Terror and Deliverance
segments.gist: God describes the time of Jacob's trouble, but promises to save His people and break their yoke.

segments.title: Healing and Restoration
segments.gist: Though the people's wound is incurable, God promises to heal them and restore their fortunes.

segments.title: Rebuilt City and Covenant
segments.gist: God promises to rebuild the city, multiply the people, and renew the covenant relationship with them.

segments.title: Storm of the Lord
segments.gist: The Lord's anger will come like a whirlwind on the wicked until He has accomplished His purposes.

31.summary: Jeremiah 31 promises restoration for Israel and Judah: God will regather His people, Ephraim will repent, and a new covenant will be made in which God's law is written on hearts and sins are forgiven. The chapter also includes Rachel weeping for her children, the rebuilding of Jerusalem, and assurances of future blessing.

segments.title: God's Love and Restoration
segments.gist: God declares His everlasting love for Israel and promises to rebuild and rejoice with His people.

segments.title: Gathering of the Remnant
segments.gist: God calls for singing and promises to gather the remnant, lead them with weeping, and turn their mourning into joy.

segments.title: Rachel's Weeping and Ephraim's Repentance
segments.gist: Rachel weeps for her children, but God promises hope; Ephraim repents and is restored as a beloved son.

segments.title: Restoration of Judah and Jerusalem
segments.gist: God promises to restore Judah and Jerusalem, and declares that each person will die for their own sin.

segments.title: The New Covenant
segments.gist: God announces a new covenant, writing His law on hearts and forgiving sins, with all knowing Him.

segments.title: Certainty of Israel's Future
segments.gist: God affirms His fixed order of creation and promises that Israel will never cease as a nation, and Jerusalem will be rebuilt.

32.summary: While Jerusalem is under siege, Jeremiah is imprisoned by King Zedekiah for prophesying the city's fall. God instructs Jeremiah to buy his cousin's field in Anathoth as a sign that houses, fields, and vineyards will again be bought in the land. Jeremiah prays, recounting God's mighty acts and the people's disobedience, and God answers, promising a future restoration and a new covenant with a reunited people.

segments.title: Jeremiah Buys Hanamel's Field
segments.gist: While confined in the guard court, Jeremiah receives a word from the LORD and buys his cousin Hanamel's field in Anathoth as a sign of future redemption.

segments.title: Deed Preserved as a Sign
segments.gist: Jeremiah weighs the silver, executes and seals the deed, and gives it to Baruch to preserve, declaring that houses and fields will again be bought in the land.

segments.title: Jeremiah's Prayer of Praise
segments.gist: Jeremiah prays, extolling God's power and steadfast love, recalling Israel's history from Egypt to the present, and questioning why God would command the field's purchase amid siege.

segments.title: God's Indictment of Israel
segments.gist: The LORD answers, declaring that He will give the city to the Babylonians because of Israel and Judah's persistent idolatry and refusal to listen.

segments.title: Promise of Restoration
segments.gist: God promises to gather His people from all lands, bring them back to the land, make an everlasting covenant with them, and restore buying and selling of fields.

33.summary: While Jeremiah is confined in the court of the guard, the word of the LORD comes to him a second time, promising that He will restore Judah and Israel, heal their land, and establish a righteous Branch of David whose name is 'The LORD our righteousness.' The chapter emphasizes God's covenant faithfulness and the future joy of Jerusalem.

segments.title: Promise of Restoration and Healing
segments.gist: God tells Jeremiah that He will restore the fortunes of Judah and Israel, heal their wounds, and rebuild the ruined city, bringing praise and honor.

segments.title: Joy Returns to the Land
segments.gist: The desolate land will again hear voices of joy and thanksgiving, and shepherds will count their flocks in the cities of Judah.

segments.title: The Righteous Branch
segments.gist: God promises to fulfill His good word to Israel and Judah by raising up a righteous Branch from David who will execute justice and righteousness.

segments.title: Davidic and Levitical Continuity
segments.gist: God assures that David will never lack a descendant on the throne and that the Levitical priests will always have offerings to present.

segments.title: Covenant as Fixed as the Cosmos
segments.gist: God compares His covenant with David and the Levites to the fixed order of day and night, which cannot be broken.

segments.title: Reversal of Rejection
segments.gist: God rejects those who despise His people but promises to restore them and have compassion, reversing the apparent rejection of Israel and Judah.

34.summary: Jeremiah delivers God's word to King Zedekiah of Judah while Nebuchadnezzar's army besieges Jerusalem, promising the king a peaceful death but destruction for the city. The chapter then recounts how the people made a covenant to free their Hebrew slaves, only to renege and force them back into bondage, prompting God to declare judgment and the city's fall.

segments.title: Siege and Promise to Zedekiah
segments.gist: While Babylon besieges Jerusalem, God tells Jeremiah to inform King Zedekiah that the city will fall but he will die in peace and be mourned.

segments.title: Covenant to Free Slaves Broken
segments.gist: King Zedekiah and the people make a covenant to free Hebrew slaves, but afterward they force the freed slaves back into bondage.

segments.title: God's Charge of Covenant Breaking
segments.gist: God reminds them of the covenant he made with their fathers to free slaves every seventh year, and accuses them of profaning his name by breaking their recent oath.

segments.title: Proclamation of Judgment
segments.gist: Because they did not proclaim liberty, God proclaims liberty to sword, pestilence, and famine, and declares that the city will be taken and burned by the Babylonians.

35.summary: During Jehoiakim's reign, God tells Jeremiah to bring the Rechabites into the temple and offer them wine. They refuse, citing their ancestor Jonadab's command to abstain from wine and live as nomads. God uses their obedience to shame Judah for disobeying Him, and He promises that Jonadab's line will always have a descendant serving Him.

segments.title: The Rechabites refuse wine
segments.gist: Jeremiah brings the Rechabites to the temple and sets wine before them, but they refuse, citing Jonadab's command to abstain and live in tents.

segments.title: Judah's disobedience contrasted
segments.gist: God contrasts the Rechabites' obedience to their ancestor with Judah's refusal to listen to Him despite repeated warnings.

segments.title: Promise to the Rechabites
segments.gist: Because the Rechabites obeyed Jonadab, God promises that Jonadab will never lack a descendant to serve Him.

36.summary: God tells Jeremiah to write all his prophecies on a scroll, which Baruch reads publicly in the temple and later to the princes. King Jehoiakim, after hearing the scroll read, cuts it up and burns it, so God commands Jeremiah to rewrite it with additions.

segments.title: Jeremiah Dictates Scroll to Baruch
segments.gist: God commands Jeremiah to write his prophecies on a scroll; Jeremiah dictates them to Baruch the scribe.

segments.title: Baruch Reads Scroll Publicly
segments.gist: Baruch reads the scroll in the temple and before the princes, who are alarmed and send for the king.

segments.title: Jehoiakim Burns the Scroll
segments.gist: King Jehoiakim cuts and burns the scroll as it is read, ignoring pleas from his servants.

segments.title: Jeremiah Rewrites Scroll with Additions
segments.gist: God commands Jeremiah to rewrite the scroll with many added words, and Baruch writes them again.

37.summary: King Zedekiah sends messengers to Jeremiah asking him to pray for the city, and Jeremiah answers that Pharaoh's army will retreat and the Chaldeans will return to burn Jerusalem. When Jeremiah tries to leave the city, he is arrested as a deserter, beaten, and imprisoned. Zedekiah later has him brought secretly to ask for a word from the LORD, and Jeremiah repeats that the king will be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon; the king then orders him moved to the court of the prison and given a daily loaf of bread.

segments.title: Zedekiah asks for prayer
segments.gist: King Zedekiah sends Jehucal and Zephaniah to ask Jeremiah to pray for the city, and Jeremiah answers that Pharaoh's army will return to Egypt and the Chaldeans will come back to burn Jerusalem.

segments.title: Jeremiah answers the envoys
segments.gist: Jeremiah tells the envoys that the Chaldeans will return, and even if only wounded men remained, they would rise up and burn the city.

segments.title: Jeremiah arrested at the gate
segments.gist: When Jeremiah tries to leave Jerusalem for Benjamin, Irijah the guard arrests him as a deserter, and the princes beat him and put him in a dungeon.
