segments.title: Zedekiah's secret question
segments.gist: Zedekiah brings Jeremiah secretly to ask for a word from the LORD, and Jeremiah says the king will be given into Babylon's hand; the king then moves him to the court of the prison with a daily loaf of bread.

38.summary: Jeremiah is cast into a miry dungeon by the princes for preaching surrender to Babylon, but Ebed-melech the Ethiopian rescues him. King Zedekiah secretly consults Jeremiah, who again advises surrender; the king protects him but keeps him confined in the court of the prison.

segments.title: Jeremiah Cast into Dungeon
segments.gist: The princes accuse Jeremiah of weakening the people and cast him into a miry dungeon, where he sinks in the mire.

segments.title: Ebed-melech Rescues Jeremiah
segments.gist: Ebed-melech the Ethiopian appeals to King Zedekiah and draws Jeremiah out of the dungeon with ropes and rags.

segments.title: Zedekiah's Secret Consultation
segments.gist: King Zedekiah secretly asks Jeremiah for a word from the Lord; Jeremiah advises surrender to Babylon and warns of the consequences of refusal.

segments.title: Jeremiah Remains in Prison
segments.gist: Zedekiah swears Jeremiah to secrecy about their conversation, and Jeremiah remains in the court of the prison until Jerusalem is taken.

39.summary: Jerusalem falls to Babylon in the tenth month of Zedekiah's ninth year; the king flees but is captured, his sons are killed before him, and he is blinded and taken to Babylon. Nebuchadnezzar orders Jeremiah protected, and God promises to deliver Ebed-melech the Ethiopian for his trust.

segments.title: Fall of Jerusalem
segments.gist: In Zedekiah's ninth year, Nebuchadnezzar besieges Jerusalem, and the city is breached in the eleventh year.

segments.title: Zedekiah Captured and Blinded
segments.gist: Zedekiah flees but is captured, his sons are slain before him, and he is blinded and bound for Babylon.

segments.title: City Burned, People Deported
segments.gist: The Babylonians burn Jerusalem and carry most of the people captive, leaving only the poor to tend the land.

segments.title: Jeremiah Protected
segments.gist: Nebuchadnezzar orders Jeremiah cared for, and he is entrusted to Gedaliah and dwells among the people.

segments.title: Promise to Ebed-melech
segments.gist: God promises Ebed-melech the Ethiopian that he will survive the city's fall because he trusted in God.

40.summary: After being freed by Nebuzaradan at Ramah, Jeremiah is given the choice to go to Babylon or stay in Judah; he joins Gedaliah, whom the Babylonians appoint governor over the remnant in Mizpah. Jews and others gather to Gedaliah, and Johanan warns him of a plot by Ishmael to assassinate him, but Gedaliah refuses to believe it.

segments.title: Jeremiah Freed at Ramah
segments.gist: Nebuzaradan finds Jeremiah bound among captives at Ramah, releases him, and offers him freedom to go to Babylon or stay in the land.

segments.title: Jeremiah Chooses Gedaliah
segments.gist: Jeremiah decides to stay with Gedaliah, the appointed governor, and receives provisions from Nebuzaradan before going to Mizpah.

segments.title: Johanan Warns of Plot
segments.gist: Johanan and other captains warn Gedaliah that Ishmael plans to kill him, but Gedaliah disbelieves and forbids Johanan to act.

41.summary: Ishmael son of Nethaniah assassinates Gedaliah the governor at Mizpah and slaughters his entourage, then takes the remaining people captive. Johanan son of Kareah pursues him and rescues the captives, but Ishmael escapes to the Ammonites. Johanan and the people settle at Chimham near Bethlehem, preparing to flee to Egypt out of fear of Babylonian retaliation.

segments.title: Ishmael Kills Gedaliah
segments.gist: Ishmael son of Nethaniah comes to Mizpah and strikes down Gedaliah and the men with him at the governor's table.

segments.title: Pilgrims Slain and Cast into Pit
segments.gist: Ishmael murders eighty men from Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria and throws their bodies into a pit, sparing ten who promise hidden supplies.

segments.title: Johanan Pursues and Rescues
segments.gist: Johanan and his forces overtake Ishmael, and the captives turn back to Johanan while Ishmael escapes to Ammon.

segments.title: People Settle at Chimham
segments.gist: Johanan leads the rescued people to Chimham near Bethlehem, intending to go to Egypt for fear of the Babylonians.

42.summary: After the murder of Gedaliah, Johanan and the remnant of Judah ask Jeremiah to seek God's direction, promising to obey. Ten days later Jeremiah delivers God's answer: if they stay in the land they will be safe, but if they go to Egypt they will die by sword, famine, and pestilence. The people are warned of their hypocrisy and their plan to flee to Egypt.

segments.title: Remnant asks Jeremiah for guidance
segments.gist: Johanan and the people ask Jeremiah to pray for them, promising to obey whatever God says.

segments.title: God's answer after ten days
segments.gist: After ten days, Jeremiah tells them God says to stay in the land and not fear the king of Babylon.

segments.title: Warning against fleeing to Egypt
segments.gist: God warns that if they go to Egypt, sword, famine, and pestilence will follow them there.

segments.title: Jeremiah exposes their hypocrisy
segments.gist: Jeremiah tells the people they have not obeyed and will die in Egypt if they go.

43.summary: After Gedaliah's assassination, Johanan and the remnant ask Jeremiah to seek God's will, promising obedience. Ten days later Jeremiah delivers God's answer: stay in the land and be protected, or go to Egypt and die by sword, famine, and pestilence. The people accuse him of lying and flee to Egypt, taking Jeremiah and Baruch with them to Tahpanhes, where God foretells that Nebuchadnezzar will conquer Egypt.

segments.title: Johanan and remnant seek Jeremiah
segments.gist: Johanan and the remnant approach Jeremiah, asking him to pray for God's direction, promising to obey whatever God says.

segments.title: Jeremiah delivers God's answer
segments.gist: After ten days, Jeremiah tells them God says to stay in the land and be protected, but going to Egypt means death by sword, famine, and pestilence.

44.summary: Jeremiah delivers a message to the Jews living in Egypt, rebuking them for continuing to burn incense to other gods despite the destruction of Jerusalem. The people defiantly refuse to stop, and Jeremiah announces that disaster will follow them into Egypt, with a remnant returning only as a sign of judgment.

segments.title: Jeremiah recounts past judgments
segments.gist: Jeremiah reminds the Jews in Egypt of the sins that brought destruction on Jerusalem and warns them not to repeat them.

segments.title: People refuse to stop idolatry
segments.gist: The people defiantly answer that they will continue burning incense to the queen of heaven as their ancestors did.

segments.title: Jeremiah denounces their idolatry
segments.gist: Jeremiah responds that their idolatry is the very reason disaster has fallen upon them.

segments.title: Judgment pronounced on Egypt Jews
segments.gist: Jeremiah announces that the Jews in Egypt will be destroyed by sword and famine, with only a few escaping as a sign.

45.summary: Jeremiah delivers a message from the LORD to Baruch, who is discouraged and weary, promising to preserve his life even as judgment falls on Judah.

segments.title: Baruch's Complaint Addressed
segments.gist: Jeremiah tells Baruch that the LORD acknowledges his sorrow and weariness.

segments.title: Promise of Preservation
segments.gist: The LORD declares He will bring disaster on Judah but will spare Baruch's life.

46.summary: The word of the LORD comes to Jeremiah concerning the nations: Egypt's army is routed at the Euphrates, Pharaoh Necho's forces are crushed, and Babylon's king Nebuchadnezzar will strike Egypt. The chapter ends with a word of comfort to Jacob, promising preservation though not exemption from discipline.

segments.title: Egypt's army routed at Euphrates
segments.gist: The LORD describes Egypt's warriors preparing for battle and then fleeing in terror before the sword at the river Euphrates.

segments.title: Nebuchadnezzar to strike Egypt
segments.gist: The word of the LORD announces that Babylon's king will come and smite the land of Egypt, and its people will be put to shame.

segments.title: Egypt punished, then restored
segments.gist: The LORD promises to punish Egypt's gods and kings, delivering them into Nebuchadnezzar's hand, yet afterward Egypt will be inhabited as in days of old.

segments.title: Jacob comforted and preserved
segments.gist: The LORD tells Jacob not to fear, promising to save him from afar and discipline him justly, not utterly destroy him.

47.summary: Jeremiah delivers a prophecy against the Philistines, describing the destruction coming from the north like an overwhelming flood. The sword of the Lord is depicted as sweeping through Philistia, causing terror and mourning, and the chapter ends with a lament over the fallen cities.

segments.title: Flood from the North
segments.gist: Waters rise from the north like a flood, overwhelming the land and causing people to cry out.

segments.title: Philistines Destroyed
segments.gist: The day comes to destroy the Philistines, including those from Tyre and Sidon, and Gaza is shaved and mourns.

segments.title: Sword of the Lord
segments.gist: The sword of the Lord is called to strike, and the people cry out for it to be still, but it will not rest.

48.summary: Jeremiah 48 pronounces judgment on Moab, declaring that its god Chemosh will go into exile and its cities will be destroyed because of Moab's arrogance and taunts against Israel. The chapter describes the ruin of Moab's towns, the lamentation of its people, and the destruction of its vineyards and strongholds, ending with a promise that Moab's captivity will be reversed in the latter days.

segments.title: Judgment on Moab's Cities
segments.gist: The Lord declares the destruction of Moab's cities, with weeping and lamentation, and commands a curse on those who do His work negligently.

segments.title: Moab's Pride and Ruin
segments.gist: Moab has been at ease from youth, but the Lord will send wanderers to empty him; his pride and boasting will be brought low.

segments.title: Lament for Moab's Downfall
segments.gist: Daughter of Dibon is called to come down from glory; the horn of Moab is cut off and his arm is broken, and all his cities are destroyed.

segments.title: Moab Made a Derision
segments.gist: Moab will be made drunk and vomit, becoming a derision; the prophet wails for Moab's broken people and the destruction of their high places.

segments.title: Moab's Captivity and Restoration
segments.gist: The Lord will swoop like an eagle on Moab, and Chemosh's people will be taken captive, yet in the latter days Moab's captivity will be brought back.

49.summary: Jeremiah 49 contains a series of oracles against several nations: Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar and Hazor, and Elam. Each oracle pronounces judgment for pride, violence, or complacency, with vivid images of destruction and scattering, though a few end with a promise of restoration in the latter days.

segments.title: Judgment on Ammon
segments.gist: The Lord condemns Ammon for seizing Israel's land and trusting in treasures, promising that their god Milcom will go into exile and their cities will be destroyed.

segments.title: Judgment on Edom
segments.gist: Edom's pride and self-confidence are condemned; despite their rocky strongholds, they will be brought down, their land made desolate, and they will be scattered like Sodom and Gomorrah.

segments.title: Judgment on Damascus
segments.gist: Damascus will be filled with fear and weakness; its young men will fall in the streets and the city will be set on fire.

segments.title: Judgment on Kedar and Hazor
segments.gist: The Lord commands Nebuchadnezzar to attack the nomadic tribes of Kedar and Hazor, who will be scattered and their tents and flocks taken.

segments.title: Judgment on Elam
segments.gist: Elam will be broken by the Lord's anger, its people scattered to the winds, and its king and princes destroyed, though restoration is promised in the latter days.

50.summary: Jeremiah 50 is a prophetic oracle against Babylon, declaring its imminent destruction by a coalition from the north as judgment for its arrogance and cruelty toward Israel and other nations. The chapter calls God's people to flee Babylon and promises their return to Zion and restoration, while depicting Babylon's complete fall and the shame of its idols.

segments.title: Babylon's Fall Declared
segments.gist: The LORD announces Babylon's destruction by a northern nation, and that Israel and Judah will return to seek Him.

segments.title: Israel and Judah Return
segments.gist: In those days the people of Israel and Judah will come weeping, seek the LORD, and join themselves to Him in an everlasting covenant.

segments.title: Babylon's Arrogance Judged
segments.gist: Because Babylon rejoiced over God's heritage, it will be put to shame; its land will become desolate and its people will fall by the sword.

segments.title: Israel Restored
segments.gist: The LORD will bring Israel back to its pasture, forgive its sins, and punish its oppressors, including the king of Babylon.

segments.title: Babylon's Pride Humbled
segments.gist: The LORD commands a sword against Babylon's treasures and waters; its pride and false gods will not save it from destruction.

segments.title: Redemption and Desolation
segments.gist: The LORD will redeem Israel and bring Babylon's destruction like a sweeping storm, causing the earth to tremble at its fall.

51.summary: Jeremiah 51 continues the oracle against Babylon, declaring God's judgment on the city for its idolatry and cruelty, and promising Israel's restoration. It describes the sudden fall of Babylon, the destruction of its idols, and the reaction of the nations, ending with a symbolic act where Jeremiah writes the judgments in a book and has Seraiah sink it in the Euphrates as a sign that Babylon will sink to rise no more.

segments.title: God's Judgment on Babylon
segments.gist: The LORD declares He will destroy Babylon and its idols, gathering nations against it because of its sins against Israel.

segments.title: Praise to the Creator
segments.gist: A hymn praises God's power in creation and providence, contrasting Him with worthless idols.

segments.title: Babylon as God's Hammer
segments.gist: God describes Babylon as His hammer used to break nations, but now Babylon itself will be broken and desolate.

segments.title: Nations Summoned Against Babylon
segments.gist: A call goes out to gather kingdoms against Babylon; its fall is compared to a threshing floor at harvest time.

segments.title: Israel's Complaint and God's Defense
segments.gist: Israel laments Babylon's devouring, but God promises to plead their cause and punish Babylon and its idols.

segments.title: Exhortation to Flee Babylon
segments.gist: God's people are told to flee Babylon because its judgment is near; Babylon's warriors will fall and its broad walls will be destroyed.

segments.title: Jeremiah's Scroll Sunk in Euphrates
segments.gist: Jeremiah writes Babylon's judgments in a book, and Seraiah reads it and sinks it in the Euphrates as a sign of Babylon's permanent fall.

52.summary: The chapter recounts the fall of Jerusalem: King Zedekiah rebels against Babylon, the city is besieged and captured, the temple and palace are burned, and the people are exiled. It then lists the temple vessels taken to Babylon and records the numbers of exiles deported in three waves, ending with the release of King Jehoiachin from prison in Babylon.

segments.title: Zedekiah's Rebellion and Capture
segments.gist: Zedekiah reigns wickedly, rebels against Babylon, and after a siege is captured, his sons killed, and he is blinded and taken to Babylon.

segments.title: Jerusalem Burned and Plundered
segments.gist: Nebuzaradan burns the temple, palace, and city, deports the people, and carries away the temple vessels and furnishings.

segments.title: Officials Executed at Riblah
segments.gist: Nebuzaradan takes the chief priest, officers, and others to Riblah, where the king of Babylon executes them.

segments.title: Number of Exiles Deported
segments.gist: The chapter lists the numbers of Judeans exiled to Babylon in the seventh, eighteenth, and twenty-third years of Nebuchadnezzar.

segments.title: Jehoiachin Released from Prison
segments.gist: Evilmerodach, king of Babylon, releases Jehoiachin from prison, speaks kindly to him, and gives him a place of honor among the captive kings.

1.summary: Lamentations 1 is a lament over the destruction of Jerusalem, personified as a weeping widow who has lost her children and been deserted by allies. She confesses her sin and acknowledges God's righteous judgment, while calling on him to see her suffering and on her enemies to face the same fate.

segments.title: Jerusalem's Desolation
segments.gist: The prophet describes Jerusalem as a lonely widow, weeping and deserted by friends, her people taken captive and her sanctuary defiled.

segments.title: Zion's Plea for Pity
segments.gist: Jerusalem herself speaks, asking passersby to see her sorrow, which she attributes to God's anger, and she spreads her hands for comfort.

segments.title: Confession and Appeal
segments.gist: Jerusalem confesses her rebellion, calls on God to see her distress, and asks him to deal with her enemies as he has dealt with her.

2.summary: Lamentations 2 is a communal lament over the destruction of Jerusalem, describing God's anger as a cloud and fire that has consumed Zion's defenses, temple, and leaders. The poet weeps day and night, calls the people to cry out to God, and recalls the taunts of enemies, ending with a plea for God to look upon the starving children and slain priests and prophets.

segments.title: God's Anger Against Zion
segments.gist: The Lord in His anger has covered Zion with a cloud, broken down her defenses, and allowed her palaces and temple to be destroyed.

segments.title: Poet's Tears for Children
segments.gist: The poet's eyes fail with tears as infants and children faint and die in the streets from hunger.

segments.title: No Comfort for Jerusalem
segments.gist: The poet declares Jerusalem's wound is incurable and recounts how God has fulfilled His threats, while enemies rejoice and taunt her.

segments.title: Call to Cry Out
segments.gist: The people are urged to cry out to the Lord day and night, pouring out their hearts like water before Him for their starving children.

segments.title: Plea for God to Look
segments.gist: The poet asks God to consider the horrors: women eating their own children, priests and prophets slain in the sanctuary, and enemies invited to terrify on every side.

3.summary: The poet speaks as a man who has seen affliction under God's rod, describing his physical and spiritual suffering in vivid images. In the middle of the chapter he recalls God's mercies and faithfulness, finding hope in waiting quietly for salvation. He calls others to examine their ways and return to God, and ends with a plea for God to see his distress and repay his enemies.

segments.title: Affliction under God's wrath
segments.gist: The speaker describes being driven into darkness, his flesh and bones wasted, and his soul bowed down under bitter hardship.

segments.title: Hope in God's mercies
segments.gist: Recalling that God's mercies are new every morning, the speaker resolves to wait quietly for salvation and accepts both good and ill from God.

segments.title: Call to repentance and lament
segments.gist: The people are urged to examine their ways and return to God, while the speaker laments that God has covered himself with anger and prayer is hindered.

segments.title: Plea for deliverance and vengeance
segments.gist: The speaker recalls God answering from the pit and asks God to judge his cause and repay his enemies according to their deeds.

4.summary: Lamentations 4 describes the devastation of Jerusalem after its fall, contrasting the former glory of the city and its people with their current suffering. The chapter attributes the disaster to the sins of prophets and priests and the iniquity of the people, while expressing hope that Zion's punishment will end and Edom's will be punished.

segments.title: Gold Dimmed and Stones Scattered
segments.gist: The chapter opens by lamenting how the gold has become dim and the precious sons of Zion are esteemed as earthen pitchers.

segments.title: Cruel Conditions in the Siege
segments.gist: Even jackals nurse their young, but the daughter of my people is cruel; children beg for bread, and the punishment of the people's iniquity exceeds that of Sodom.

segments.title: The Lord's Wrath and the Leaders' Guilt
segments.gist: The Lord has accomplished his fury, kindling a fire in Zion; the kings of the earth did not believe it, and the sins of prophets and priests led to their rejection.

segments.title: Vain Help and the Fall of the Anointed
segments.gist: The people looked in vain for help from a nation that could not save, and the anointed of the Lord was taken in their pits.

segments.title: Edom's Joy and Zion's Hope
segments.gist: Edom is told to rejoice now but will also drink of the cup; Zion's punishment is accomplished, and her iniquity will no longer be exiled.

5.summary: The final chapter of Lamentations is a communal prayer in which the people of Judah cry out to God about their suffering after Jerusalem's fall, describing famine, violence, and humiliation. They confess their sins and their fathers' sins, acknowledge God's eternal rule, and end with a plea for restoration, asking why God has forgotten them.

segments.title: Plea and description of suffering
segments.gist: The people ask God to remember their reproach and describe their inheritance being turned to strangers, their orphaned and widowed state, and the dangers and famine they face.

segments.title: Women and leaders humiliated
segments.gist: They lament that women are ravished in Zion, princes are hanged, elders are dishonored, and young men and children stagger under burdens; joy has ceased.

segments.title: Confession and plea for restoration
segments.gist: They confess their sins and acknowledge God's eternal throne, then plead for restoration and ask why God has forgotten them, ending with a request to be turned back to God.

1.summary: In exile by the river Chebar, Ezekiel sees a stormy wind from the north and four living creatures with four faces and four wings, accompanied by wheels full of eyes. Above them is a crystal expanse and a throne, on which sits a figure like a man surrounded by fire and brightness, and Ezekiel falls on his face when he sees the likeness of the glory of the LORD.

segments.title: Stormy Wind from the North
segments.gist: Ezekiel, among the captives by the river Chebar, sees a whirlwind coming from the north with a great cloud and flashing fire.

segments.title: Four Living Creatures
segments.gist: Ezekiel describes four living creatures with human form, four faces, four wings, and feet like calves' feet, moving like lightning.

segments.title: Wheels with Eyes
segments.gist: Ezekiel sees four wheels beside the creatures, full of eyes, moving with the creatures as the spirit directs.

segments.title: Firmament and Voice
segments.gist: Above the creatures is a firmament like crystal, and when they stand still they let down their wings; a voice comes from above the firmament.

segments.title: Throne and Glory
segments.gist: Above the firmament is a sapphire throne, and on it a figure like a man surrounded by fire and brightness, which Ezekiel recognizes as the glory of the LORD and falls on his face.

2.summary: God commissions Ezekiel as a prophet to the rebellious house of Israel, telling him not to fear their words or looks. He gives Ezekiel a scroll to eat and warns that the people are obstinate, but promises to make Ezekiel's face as hard as theirs.

segments.title: God Calls Ezekiel
segments.gist: God addresses Ezekiel as son of man and sends him to the rebellious Israelites.

segments.title: Mission to Rebellious Nation
segments.gist: Ezekiel is sent to a nation of rebels who have transgressed; they may hear or refuse, but will know a prophet has been among them.

segments.title: Do Not Fear Their Looks
segments.gist: God tells Ezekiel not to be afraid of the people's words or looks, though they are like briers and scorpions, and to speak God's words regardless.

segments.title: Scroll of Lamentations
segments.gist: Ezekiel sees a hand stretched out with a scroll written on both sides with lamentations, mourning, and woe.

3.summary: Ezekiel is told to eat the scroll and then commissioned as a watchman over Israel, responsible for warning the wicked. He is then transported by the Spirit to the exiles at Tel-abib, where he sits stunned for seven days before God makes him a silent sign until the time for speech.

segments.title: Eating the Scroll
segments.gist: God tells Ezekiel to eat the scroll and speak his words to Israel, though they will not listen.

segments.title: Commission to a Hard People
segments.gist: Ezekiel is sent to the stubborn Israelites, made hard like them, and told to speak God's words.

segments.title: Spirit Lifts Ezekiel to Exiles
segments.gist: The Spirit lifts Ezekiel, and he goes to Tel-abib by the Chebar, sitting stunned seven days.

segments.title: Watchman's Warning
segments.gist: God appoints Ezekiel as a watchman; if he fails to warn the wicked, their blood is on his hands.

segments.title: Silent Sign in the Valley
segments.gist: In the plain, God commands Ezekiel to shut himself in and be mute until God opens his mouth.

4.summary: God instructs Ezekiel to act out the siege of Jerusalem using a clay tile, then to lie on his side for a total of 430 days to bear Israel's and Judah's iniquity, and finally to bake bread over human dung as a sign of the unclean food the exiles will eat during the famine.

segments.title: Siege of Jerusalem portrayed
segments.gist: Ezekiel is told to draw Jerusalem on a tile, set siege works against it, and use an iron pan as a wall between him and the city.

segments.title: Lying on left and right sides
segments.gist: God commands Ezekiel to lie on his left side for 390 days for Israel's sin and on his right for 40 days for Judah's, with his arm bared against Jerusalem.

segments.title: Defiled bread and famine
segments.gist: Ezekiel is told to bake bread using wheat, barley, beans, and other grains over human dung, symbolizing the unclean food and scarcity the people will endure during the siege.

5.summary: God instructs Ezekiel to shave his head and beard, divide the hair into three parts to symbolize Jerusalem's coming destruction by sword, famine, and scattering, with a small remnant preserved. The chapter then explains that Jerusalem's rebellion exceeded that of the surrounding nations, so God will execute judgments upon her, including famine, sword, and pestilence, making her a desolation and a warning to others.

segments.title: Shaving Hair as a Sign
segments.gist: Ezekiel shaves his head and beard, divides the hair into three parts, and performs symbolic actions with them.

segments.title: Jerusalem's Rebellion and Judgment
segments.gist: God declares that Jerusalem has rebelled more than the nations, so He will execute judgments against her.

segments.title: Famine, Sword, and Scattering
segments.gist: God specifies that a third will die by famine and pestilence, a third by the sword, and a third will be scattered.

segments.title: Desolation and Reproach
segments.gist: God will pour out His fury, making Jerusalem a desolation and a reproach among the nations, with famine and wild beasts.

6.summary: Ezekiel is commanded to prophesy against the mountains of Israel, declaring that God will bring a sword upon the high places, destroy the altars and images, and scatter the people among the nations. A remnant will be left, and those who escape will remember God among the heathen and loathe themselves for their abominations. The chapter closes with a series of judgments—sword, famine, pestilence—so that the slain may fall and the land be made desolate, and the people shall know that the LORD is God.

segments.title: Prophecy Against Mountains and High Places
segments.gist: Ezekiel is told to set his face toward the mountains of Israel and prophesy that God will bring a sword upon the high places, destroying altars and images.

segments.title: A Remnant Will Remember God
segments.gist: God promises to leave a remnant who will escape the sword and remember Him among the nations, loathing themselves for their evils.

segments.title: Judgment by Sword, Famine, and Pestilence
segments.gist: God commands smiting and declares that sword, famine, and pestilence will fall on those in the city, field, and strongholds, leaving the land desolate.

7.summary: Ezekiel 7 announces the imminent end of Israel: God's anger will be poured out without pity, disaster will follow disaster, and the people's wealth, idols, and temple will be destroyed. Those who escape will mourn, and the land will be desolate because of their abominations.

segments.title: The End Has Come
segments.gist: God declares that the end has come upon the land, and He will not spare or pity them.

segments.title: Disaster After Disaster
segments.gist: Evil and disaster follow one another; God will judge according to their ways and repay their abominations.

segments.title: Rod Blossoms, Pride Buds
segments.gist: The day of trouble is near; violence has risen, and neither buyer nor seller will recover their possessions.

segments.title: Wealth Cannot Save
segments.gist: Though they blow the trumpet and prepare for battle, terror comes; their silver and gold cannot deliver them in the day of wrath.

segments.title: Temple Defiled by Idols
segments.gist: They turned God's beautiful ornament into pride and made idols; therefore God will give it to strangers and robbers.

segments.title: Chains and Desolation
segments.gist: God commands chains because the land is full of bloodshed; He will bring the worst of nations, and they will seek peace in vain.

8.summary: In a vision, Ezekiel is brought from Babylon to Jerusalem and shown the abominations being committed in the temple: an idol at the north gate, elders burning incense in a secret chamber, women weeping for Tammuz, and men worshipping the sun. God declares that because of these greater abominations, he will act in fury without pity.

segments.title: Vision of the temple abominations
segments.gist: Ezekiel sees a likeness of fire and is transported in vision to the temple, where an idol provokes God's jealousy.

segments.title: Idol at the north gate
segments.gist: God shows Ezekiel the image of jealousy at the altar gate and asks if the house of Israel's abominations are seen.

segments.title: Elders burning incense
segments.gist: Ezekiel is shown seventy elders in a secret chamber burning incense, saying the Lord has forsaken the earth.

segments.title: Women weeping for Tammuz
segments.gist: At the north gate, Ezekiel sees women weeping for Tammuz, and God calls it a greater abomination.

segments.title: Sun worshippers and God's fury
segments.gist: Men in the inner court worship the sun with their backs to the temple, and God declares he will act in fury without pity.

9.summary: Ezekiel sees six men with slaughter weapons and a man clothed in linen with a writer's inkhorn. The LORD commands the linen-clad man to mark the foreheads of those who grieve over Jerusalem's abominations, and the six men are sent to slay all others without pity, beginning at the sanctuary. Ezekiel protests, and God explains that the iniquity of Israel and Judah is exceedingly great, so his eye will not spare.

segments.title: Six executioners and a scribe
segments.gist: Ezekiel sees six men with slaughter weapons and a man clothed in linen with a writer's inkhorn at the north gate.

segments.title: Mark the mourners
segments.gist: The LORD tells the linen-clad man to mark the foreheads of those who sigh and cry over Jerusalem's abominations.

segments.title: Slay without pity
segments.gist: The LORD commands the six men to slay all others without pity, starting at the sanctuary, and they begin with the elders.

segments.title: Ezekiel's protest and God's reply
segments.gist: Ezekiel protests the destruction of the remnant, and God answers that Israel's iniquity is exceedingly great and he will not spare.

10.summary: Ezekiel sees the glory of the LORD depart from the temple in Jerusalem. The man in linen is commanded to take coals of fire from between the cherubim and scatter them over the city, while the cherubim and the wheels of the chariot-throne are described in detail. The chapter ends with the glory of the LORD moving to the east gate of the LORD's house.

segments.title: Coals taken from cherubim
segments.gist: Ezekiel sees the cherubim and the man in linen is told to take coals of fire from between them and scatter them over the city.

segments.title: Description of wheels and cherubim
segments.gist: The wheels beside the cherubim are described, full of eyes, and the cherubim move with the wheels, their faces and wings detailed.

segments.title: Glory departs to east gate
segments.gist: The glory of the LORD departs from the threshold of the temple and stands over the cherubim, then moves to the east gate of the LORD's house.

11.summary: Ezekiel sees twenty-five leaders of Jerusalem at the east gate, and God tells him they are the city's corrupt counselors who say the city is the pot and the people the meat. God commands Ezekiel to prophesy judgment: the leaders will be dragged out and killed, and the city will not protect them. As Ezekiel protests that the remnant will be destroyed, God promises to gather the exiles, give them a new heart and spirit, and restore them; the chapter ends with the glory of the Lord leaving the city and Ezekiel being carried back to the exiles in Babylon.

segments.title: Vision of the east gate leaders
segments.gist: Ezekiel is brought to the east gate and shown twenty-five men, including Jaazaniah and Pelatiah, who devise mischief in Jerusalem.

segments.title: Judgment on the counselors
segments.gist: God tells Ezekiel to prophesy against the men who say the city is the pot and they are the meat, promising they will be cast out and killed by the sword.

segments.title: Promise of restoration
segments.gist: God answers that though he scattered the people, he will gather them, give them a new heart and spirit, and make them his people.

segments.title: Glory departs and vision ends
segments.gist: The glory of the Lord rises from the city and stands on the mountain east of it, and Ezekiel is carried back to the exiles in Babylon and tells them all the vision.

12.summary: Ezekiel acts out Jerusalem's coming exile by packing his belongings and digging through a wall, then trembles while eating and drinking to portray the people's fear. God answers the proverb that visions fail, declaring that judgment is near and will not be delayed.

segments.title: Ezekiel packs for exile
segments.gist: God tells Ezekiel to prepare baggage and go into exile by day, as a sign to the rebellious house.

segments.title: Digging through the wall
segments.gist: Ezekiel digs through the wall and carries out his belongings at evening, covering his face, portraying the prince's escape and the people's exile.

segments.title: Trembling while eating
segments.gist: Ezekiel eats and drinks with trembling and anxiety, a sign of the desolation coming upon Jerusalem.

segments.title: The proverb of delayed visions
segments.gist: God addresses the proverb that days pass and every vision fails, declaring that no vision will be delayed any longer.

segments.title: The vision will not be delayed
segments.gist: God answers those who say Ezekiel's vision is for many days, affirming that every word will be fulfilled without delay.

13.summary: God condemns the false prophets of Israel who speak from their own hearts and lead the people astray with false visions and divinations, promising peace when there is none. He also denounces the false prophetesses who hunt souls with magic bands and pillows, and declares that He will deliver His people from their lies and that both the false prophets and their followers will fall by the sword and famine.

segments.title: Woe to Foolish Prophets
segments.gist: God tells Ezekiel to prophesy against the prophets of Israel who follow their own spirit and have seen nothing, calling them foolish and comparing them to foxes in the ruins.

segments.title: False Visions and Whitewashed Wall
segments.gist: God declares He is against the false prophets who envision vanity and divine lies, promising peace when there is none, and compares them to a flimsy wall covered with untempered mortar that will fall in the storm.

segments.title: Judgment on False Prophetesses
segments.gist: God condemns the daughters who prophesy out of their own hearts, using magic bands and veils to hunt souls, and vows to tear off their bands and deliver His people from their lies.

14.summary: Ezekiel is approached by certain elders of Israel who have set up idols in their hearts, and God declares through the prophet that He will answer them according to their idolatry unless they repent. The chapter then presents a series of hypothetical scenarios showing that even the righteousness of Noah, Daniel, and Job could not save a rebellious land from God's four severe judgments—sword, famine, beasts, and pestilence—though a remnant would be preserved. It concludes with a promise that the remnant will bring comfort and demonstrate God's justice.

segments.title: Elders with idols confronted
segments.gist: Elders of Israel come to Ezekiel, but God says they have idols in their hearts and will answer them accordingly.

segments.title: Call to repent from idols
segments.gist: God calls Israel to repent and turn from idols, warning that He will judge those who persist in idolatry.

segments.title: Noah, Daniel, Job cannot save
segments.gist: Even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were in a sinful land, they could only save themselves, not the land from God's judgments.

segments.title: Remnant brings comfort and vindication
segments.gist: God will preserve a remnant, and when they come to Babylon, the exiles will be comforted and see God's justice.

15.summary: The word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel comparing Jerusalem to a vine branch, which is useful only as fuel for fire and not for any product. He argues that since a vine branch is worthless even when whole, how much more so when burned at both ends and charred in the middle; thus the inhabitants of Jerusalem will be given to the fire, and the land will become desolate because of their unfaithfulness.

segments.title: Vine Wood Compared to Other Trees
segments.gist: The LORD asks Ezekiel how the wood of a vine compares to other trees, and whether it is useful for any work.

segments.title: Jerusalem as Burned Vine
segments.gist: The LORD declares that as the vine is given to the fire for fuel, so the inhabitants of Jerusalem will be given to the fire, and the land will be desolate.

16.summary: God recounts Jerusalem's origin as an abandoned infant whom He rescued, cleansed, and adorned, making her a queen. She trusted in her beauty, played the harlot with foreign nations, and sacrificed her children to idols, surpassing Samaria and Sodom in wickedness. God therefore promises judgment but also a future restoration and an everlasting covenant.

segments.title: Jerusalem's rescue and adornment
segments.gist: God describes finding Jerusalem as an abandoned newborn, rescuing, cleansing, and adorning her into a beautiful queen.

segments.title: Jerusalem's harlotry and idolatry
segments.gist: Jerusalem trusted in her beauty, committed harlotry with foreign nations, and sacrificed her children to idols.

segments.title: Judgment pronounced on Jerusalem
segments.gist: God announces judgment: Jerusalem will be exposed and stoned for her adultery and bloodshed.

segments.title: Jerusalem worse than Samaria and Sodom
segments.gist: Jerusalem is compared unfavorably to Samaria and Sodom, whose sins were less than hers.

segments.title: Promise of restoration
segments.gist: God promises to restore the fortunes of Sodom, Samaria, and Jerusalem, but Jerusalem will bear her shame.

segments.title: Everlasting covenant
segments.gist: God will remember His covenant, establish an everlasting covenant, and provide atonement for Jerusalem.

17.summary: Ezekiel presents a riddle of two eagles and a vine: the first eagle takes the top of a cedar and plants it in a city of merchants, where it thrives until another eagle lures it to turn toward him. God explains that the king of Babylon took Judah's king and made a covenant with Zedekiah, who rebelled by seeking Egypt's help. Because Zedekiah broke his oath, God declares he will not escape, but God himself will take a tender twig from the cedar's top and plant it on a high mountain, where it will become a noble cedar.

segments.title: Riddle of the Two Eagles
segments.gist: Ezekiel sets forth a riddle: a great eagle takes the top of a cedar and plants it in a city of merchants, where it grows but then turns toward a second eagle.

segments.title: Explanation of the Riddle
segments.gist: God explains that the king of Babylon took Judah's king to Babylon and made a covenant with Zedekiah, who rebelled by sending to Egypt for horses and help.

segments.title: Judgment for Broken Oath
segments.gist: Because Zedekiah despised the oath and broke the covenant, God declares he will not escape but will be caught and judged in Babylon.

segments.title: God Plants a Tender Twig
segments.gist: God promises to take a tender twig from the cedar's top and plant it on a high mountain, where it will become a noble cedar and all trees will know God's power.

18.summary: Ezekiel 18 addresses the proverb that children suffer for their parents' sins, declaring that each person is accountable for their own actions. Through examples of a righteous man, his violent son, and a repentant wicked man, God affirms that the soul that sins shall die, but that He takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked and calls them to turn and live.

segments.title: The Proverb Refuted
segments.gist: God challenges the proverb that fathers eat sour grapes and children's teeth are set on edge, declaring that all souls belong to Him.

segments.title: The Righteous Man Lives
segments.gist: A man who is just, keeps God's laws, and avoids idolatry and oppression shall surely live, says the Lord.

segments.title: The Violent Son Dies
segments.gist: If a righteous man has a violent son who sheds blood and does abominations, that son shall die; his blood is upon him.

segments.title: The Son Who Turns
segments.gist: If the violent son sees his father's sins, fears God, and does not imitate them, he shall not die for his father's iniquity but shall live.

segments.title: Personal Accountability
segments.gist: God explains that the soul who sins shall die; a wicked man who turns from his sins shall live, and a righteous man who turns to wickedness shall die.

segments.title: Call to Repentance
segments.gist: God defends His justice, urges Israel to repent and get a new heart, and declares He has no pleasure in the death of the wicked.

19.summary: Ezekiel delivers a lamentation for the princes of Israel, using two allegories: a lioness and her cubs, depicting the exile of Israel's leaders, and a vine that is uprooted and withered, symbolizing Jerusalem's destruction. The chapter concludes with a warning that no strong branch remains to rule.

segments.title: Lioness and Her Cubs
segments.gist: The prophet takes up a lamentation, portraying Israel as a lioness whose cubs are taken and led to distant lands.

segments.title: The Withered Vine
segments.gist: Israel is compared to a vine planted by waters, but it is plucked up and burned, leaving no strong branch for a scepter.

20.summary: Certain elders of Israel come to inquire of the LORD, and God refuses to be consulted by them, recounting Israel's repeated rebellions from Egypt onward and His repeated mercy for His name's sake. He declares He will purge out the rebels, bring the people into the wilderness of the peoples, and eventually restore a remnant to His holy mountain, while the fire of judgment falls on the south.

segments.title: Elders inquire, God refuses
segments.gist: Elders of Israel come to seek the LORD, but God tells Ezekiel He will not be inquired of by them.

segments.title: Rebellion in Egypt
segments.gist: God recounts choosing Israel in Egypt and bringing them out, but they rebelled, and He acted for His name's sake.

segments.title: Rebellion in the wilderness
segments.gist: God gave statutes and sabbaths in the wilderness, yet the people rebelled, so He withheld judgment for His name's sake.

segments.title: Children rebel in the land
segments.gist: The next generation also rebelled, defiling God's sabbaths, so He gave them over to statutes that were not good.

segments.title: Blasphemy in the land
segments.gist: God recounts Israel's high places and idolatrous offerings, and refuses to be inquired of by such a people.

segments.title: Purge and restoration
segments.gist: God will purge out rebels, bring the people into the wilderness, and restore a remnant to serve Him on His holy mountain.

segments.title: Fire in the south
segments.gist: The word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel: He will kindle a fire in the south that shall not be quenched.

21.summary: Ezekiel is commanded to prophesy against Jerusalem and the land of Israel, announcing that God will draw His sword against both the righteous and the wicked, and that the king of Babylon will use divination to choose Jerusalem for attack. The chapter also includes a prophecy against the Ammonites, who will be destroyed and remembered no more.

segments.title: Sword Against Jerusalem
segments.gist: Ezekiel is told to set his face toward Jerusalem and prophesy that God will draw His sword against the land.

segments.title: Sighing and the Sword
segments.gist: Ezekiel sighs before the people, and God declares the sword will strike both righteous and wicked, and the people will faint.

segments.title: Sword Sharpened for Slaughter
segments.gist: The sword is sharpened and polished for slaughter, and God says He will clap His hands and satisfy His fury.

segments.title: King of Babylon Divines
segments.gist: The king of Babylon uses divination to decide whether to attack Jerusalem or Ammon, and Jerusalem is chosen.

segments.title: Iniquity Remembered
segments.gist: Because of Jerusalem's iniquity, God will overturn the kingdom until He whose right it is comes.

segments.title: Prophecy Against Ammon
segments.gist: The Ammonites are told their sword is drawn for slaughter, and they will be destroyed and remembered no more.

22.summary: Ezekiel delivers a series of oracles against Jerusalem, cataloging the city's bloodshed, idolatry, and social injustices—especially the failure of its leaders, priests, prophets, and people. God declares that He will gather the exiles for judgment, refining them like silver in a furnace, and that no righteous person can stand in the gap for the land.

segments.title: City of Bloodshed Condemned
segments.gist: Ezekiel is told to pronounce judgment on Jerusalem as a city guilty of bloodshed and idolatry, bringing its day of reckoning.

segments.title: Princes and People Charged
segments.gist: The princes, people, and leaders are accused of violence, idolatry, sexual sins, and economic exploitation.

segments.title: God's Wrath and Cleansing
segments.gist: God declares He will strike His hands at Jerusalem's unjust gain, scatter the people, and purge away their uncleanness.

segments.title: Refined Like Silver
segments.gist: Israel is compared to dross and gathered into Jerusalem to be melted in the furnace of God's wrath.

segments.title: No One Found in the Gap
segments.gist: Prophets, priests, princes, and people all fail; God finds no one to stand in the gap, so He pours out His indignation.

23.summary: The chapter presents a parable of two sisters, Oholah (Samaria) and Oholibah (Jerusalem), who played the harlot with foreign nations. Oholah was given over to Assyria, and Oholibah, worse than her sister, lusted after Assyria, Babylon, and Egypt. Therefore God decrees judgment on Oholibah through the Babylonians and calls for her to be stoned and slain, ending with a warning against lewdness.

segments.title: Two Sisters' Harlotries
segments.gist: Ezekiel recounts the origins of two sisters, Oholah and Oholibah, who became harlots in Egypt and bore sons and daughters.

segments.title: Oholah's Lust and Judgment
segments.gist: Oholah lusted after Assyrian warriors and played the harlot with them, so God delivered her into their hands, and she was slain.

segments.title: Oholibah's Greater Whoredoms
segments.gist: Oholibah was more corrupt, lusting after Assyrians, Babylonians, and Egyptians, multiplying her harlotries and defiling herself.

segments.title: Judgment on Oholibah
segments.gist: God summons Oholibah's lovers against her to execute judgment, and she will drink the cup of her sister's ruin.

segments.title: Adulteries and Idolatries Exposed
segments.gist: God charges Ezekiel to condemn the sisters' adulteries and idolatries, including child sacrifice and incense in the temple.

segments.title: Punishment for Lewdness
segments.gist: God declares that the sisters will be stoned and slain for their lewdness, and the land will be cleansed of adultery.

24.summary: Ezekiel is told to record the parable of the boiling pot to announce Jerusalem's siege and destruction, then his wife dies as a sign that the exiles will lose their temple and children without mourning. The chapter ends with a promise that Ezekiel will become a sign and a fugitive will bring news of the fall.

segments.title: Parable of the Boiling Pot
segments.gist: God commands Ezekiel to set a pot on the fire and pile meat and bones into it, portraying Jerusalem under siege.

segments.title: Woe to the Bloody City
segments.gist: The city is condemned for its bloodshed; its pieces are emptied out and the fire is kindled to purge it.

segments.title: Fire of Judgment
segments.gist: God declares the bloody city will be burned and its filth consumed, and He will not relent from His anger.

segments.title: Death of Ezekiel's Wife
segments.gist: God tells Ezekiel his wife will die, and he must not mourn; her death becomes a sign for the exiles.

segments.title: Sign of the Exiles' Loss
segments.gist: Ezekiel explains that the temple and the exiles' children will fall, and they will mourn without outward signs.

segments.title: Promise of a Fugitive's News
segments.gist: When the fugitive arrives with news of the fall, Ezekiel's mouth will be opened and he will be a sign to them.

25.summary: God's word comes to Ezekiel against four neighboring nations: Ammon, Moab, Edom, and Philistia. Each is judged for mocking or taking revenge on Judah when Jerusalem fell, and each is told that they will be destroyed and know that the LORD is God.

segments.title: Judgment on Ammon
segments.gist: Because Ammon rejoiced over the desecration of God's sanctuary and Judah's ruin, God will give them to the men of the east and destroy them.

segments.title: Judgment on Moab and Edom
segments.gist: Moab and Seir said Judah is like all other nations, so God will expose their flank and destroy them, giving Moab to the eastern peoples.

segments.title: Judgment on Edom
segments.gist: Because Edom took revenge on Judah, God will stretch out his hand against Edom and lay it waste by the hand of Israel.

segments.title: Judgment on Philistia
segments.gist: Because the Philistines acted in revenge with spiteful hearts, God will cut off the Cherethites and destroy the remnant of the seacoast.

26.summary: Ezekiel prophesies that Tyre will be destroyed by many nations because it rejoiced over Jerusalem's fall. The city will become a bare rock and a place for spreading nets, and its wealth and commerce will end in the depths of the sea.

segments.title: Prophecy Against Tyre
segments.gist: Because Tyre rejoiced over Jerusalem's destruction, God will bring many nations against her like waves of the sea.

segments.title: Nebuchadnezzar's Siege
segments.gist: Nebuchadnezzar will besiege Tyre with horses, chariots, and a great army, destroying her walls and making her a bare rock.

segments.title: Coastlands Mourn Tyre's Fall
segments.gist: The princes of the sea will tremble and lament when Tyre falls, mourning the loss of her commerce and renown.

segments.title: Tyre Descends to the Pit
segments.gist: God will bring Tyre down to the pit with the nations of old, and she will never be found again.

27.summary: Ezekiel takes up a lamentation over Tyre, portraying it as a magnificent merchant ship that traded with many nations. The chapter describes Tyre's commercial network and the wealth it brought, then foretells its sudden destruction and the dismay of its trading partners.

segments.title: Lamentation for Tyre
segments.gist: The word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel, commanding him to take up a lamentation for Tyre, the gateway to the sea.

segments.title: Tyre as a Ship
segments.gist: Tyre is depicted as a ship built of fine woods, with oars, masts, and skilled sailors from various places.

segments.title: Tyre's Trade and Wealth
segments.gist: The chapter lists many nations and goods that traded with Tyre, describing its vast commerce and riches.

segments.title: Shipwreck and Desolation
segments.gist: Tyre's ship is wrecked by the east wind, its wealth lost, and the merchants and nations mourn its sudden fall.

28.summary: The word of the Lord comes to Ezekiel with a lamentation over the prince of Tyre, who in his pride claims to be a god but will be brought down to death. It then pronounces judgment on the king of Tyre, describing him as the anointed cherub in Eden who was cast out for iniquity. The chapter closes with a prophecy against Sidon and a promise that Israel will be restored and dwell securely.

segments.title: Judgment on the Prince of Tyre
segments.gist: The prince of Tyre boasts of being a god, but God will bring strangers against him and he will die the deaths of the uncircumcised.

segments.title: Lamentation for the King of Tyre
segments.gist: The king of Tyre is portrayed as the anointed cherub in Eden, perfect until iniquity was found in him, and he is cast out and destroyed.

segments.title: Prophecy Against Sidon
segments.gist: God declares judgment on Sidon, promising that it will no longer be a pricking brier to Israel, and that God will be glorified in her.

segments.title: Promise of Israel's Restoration
segments.gist: God promises to gather Israel from the peoples and restore them to their land, where they will dwell safely and know that He is the Lord.

29.summary: The word of the Lord comes to Ezekiel in the tenth year, tenth month, twelfth day, condemning Pharaoh king of Egypt for claiming the Nile as his own and promising to drag him and his fish out of the river. Egypt will be made desolate for forty years and its people scattered, then restored after forty years but as a lowly kingdom. Nebuchadnezzar will be given Egypt as wages for his army's labor against Tyre, and Egypt will never again be Israel's confidence.

segments.title: Judgment on Pharaoh and Egypt
segments.gist: God addresses Pharaoh, the great dragon in the Nile, who claims the river as his own, and vows to drag him and his fish out and leave them in the wilderness.

segments.title: Egypt a broken reed
segments.gist: When Israel leaned on Egypt, it splintered and tore their shoulder; therefore Egypt will become desolate because Pharaoh said, 'The river is mine.'

segments.title: Egypt made desolate
segments.gist: God will make Egypt waste from Migdol to Syene, uninhabited for forty years, and scatter the Egyptians among the nations.

segments.title: Egypt restored but diminished
segments.gist: After forty years God will gather Egypt back, but it will be a lowly kingdom, no longer a source of confidence for Israel.

segments.title: Egypt as wages for Babylon
segments.gist: In the twenty-seventh year God declares that Nebuchadnezzar will take Egypt as wages for his army's labor against Tyre, and Israel will be restored.

30.summary: Ezekiel 30 contains a series of prophecies against Egypt and its allies. The word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel declaring a day of doom for Egypt, and the LORD promises to scatter the Egyptians and lay waste the land and its cities, including Thebes and Memphis, and to break the arms of Pharaoh and Babylon's king.

segments.title: Wailing for the day of the LORD
segments.gist: The LORD commands Ezekiel to wail for the day of the LORD, a day of clouds and doom for Egypt and the nations.

segments.title: Egypt's allies fall
segments.gist: The LORD declares that Egypt's supporters from Ethiopia to Libya will fall by the sword, and messengers will trouble Ethiopia.

segments.title: Babylon despoils Egypt
segments.gist: The LORD says he will use Nebuchadnezzar and his army to destroy Egypt and sell its land to the wicked.

segments.title: Cities of Egypt laid waste
segments.gist: The LORD will destroy idols and cities like Memphis, Thebes, and Pelusium, and set fire to Egypt and execute judgments.

segments.title: Pharaoh's arms broken
segments.gist: The LORD will break Pharaoh's arms and strengthen Babylon's king, scattering the Egyptians among the nations.

31.summary: Ezekiel delivers a prophecy against Pharaoh and Egypt, comparing Egypt's former greatness to a cedar in Lebanon that towered above all trees and was envied by the trees of Eden. Because it exalted itself, God declares it will be cut down and delivered to a mighty nation, and it will descend to the grave with the uncircumcised, serving as a warning to other trees not to exalt themselves.

segments.title: Egypt Compared to a Cedar
segments.gist: Ezekiel asks Pharaoh who he is like in greatness, then describes Assyria as a cedar in Lebanon with fair branches, deep roots, and waters that made it tall.

segments.title: Cedar's Pride and Fall Declared
segments.gist: Because the cedar exalted itself, God says it will be cut down and delivered to a mighty nation, so no other tree will exalt itself.

segments.title: Descent to the Grave
segments.gist: God describes the day the cedar goes down to the grave, causing the deep to mourn and the trees of Eden to be comforted in the lower parts of the earth.

32.summary: In the twelfth year of exile, Ezekiel delivers a lamentation over Pharaoh and Egypt, describing their fall to Babylon as a lion's capture and a cosmic darkening. The chapter then lists Egypt's descent to the pit alongside other fallen nations—Assyria, Elam, Meshech, Tubal, Edom, and the princes of the north—each slain by the sword and lying in shame.

segments.title: Lamentation for Pharaoh
segments.gist: Ezekiel is told to take up a lamentation for Pharaoh, comparing him to a lion and a sea monster whose destruction will darken the heavens and trouble the nations.

segments.title: Babylonian Sword and Desolation
segments.gist: The sword of Babylon will fall on Egypt, and the land will be left desolate, prompting lamentation among the nations.

segments.title: Egypt Descends to the Pit
segments.gist: Egypt is to be cast down to the pit among the uncircumcised, greeted by the mighty who speak from Sheol.

segments.title: Nations in the Pit
segments.gist: Assyria, Elam, Meshech, Tubal, Edom, and the princes of the north are described as lying in shame in the pit, and Pharaoh will see them and be comforted.

33.summary: Ezekiel is appointed as a watchman for Israel, responsible for warning the wicked to turn from their ways. The exiles in Babylon receive word that Jerusalem has fallen, and God explains that the land's desolation is due to the people's continued sins. The chapter ends with the people hearing Ezekiel's words but not putting them into practice.

segments.title: Ezekiel Appointed as Watchman
segments.gist: God appoints Ezekiel as a watchman to warn Israel; if he fails to warn the wicked, their blood is on his hands.

segments.title: Individual Responsibility for Sin
segments.gist: God affirms that the wicked who turn from sin will live, while the righteous who sin will die; each person is judged individually.

segments.title: Jerusalem's Fall Reported
segments.gist: A fugitive from Jerusalem arrives in Babylon and reports that the city has been struck down.

segments.title: Judgment on Those in the Land
segments.gist: God declares that those remaining in the land of Israel will fall by sword, famine, and pestilence because of their abominations.

segments.title: People Hear but Do Not Obey
segments.gist: The people listen to Ezekiel's words but do not practice them; when judgment comes, they will know a prophet was among them.

34.summary: God condemns the shepherds of Israel who feed themselves instead of the flock, leaving the sheep scattered and preyed upon. He promises to rescue His sheep, judge between them, and set over them one shepherd, His servant David, in a covenant of peace.

segments.title: Condemnation of selfish shepherds
segments.gist: God indicts the shepherds who feed themselves, fail to strengthen the weak, and scatter the flock, so He will hold them accountable.

segments.title: God promises to rescue His sheep
segments.gist: God declares He will search for His scattered sheep, gather them from all places, feed them in good pasture, and bind up the injured.

segments.title: Judgment between fat and lean sheep
segments.gist: God will judge between the sheep, rebuking the strong who push and butt the weak away from the pasture and waters.

segments.title: One shepherd, David, over them
segments.gist: God promises to set up one shepherd, His servant David, over the flock, and He Himself will be their God.

segments.title: Covenant of peace and blessing
segments.gist: God establishes a covenant of peace, removes harmful beasts, showers blessings, and assures the house of Israel that He is with them.

35.summary: The word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel against Mount Seir (Edom) because of its enduring hatred and violence against Israel, especially its gloating over Jerusalem's fall and its attempt to seize the land. God declares that Edom will be desolated and its cities made waste, and that He will be known through His judgment, while Israel will be restored and multiply.

segments.title: Prophecy Against Mount Seir
segments.gist: God tells Ezekiel to set his face against Mount Seir and prophesy that He is against Edom because of its ancient enmity.

segments.title: Edom's Hatred and Judgment
segments.gist: Because Edom pursued Israel with hatred and bloodshed, God will make Edom a desolation and its cities perpetual wastes.

segments.title: Edom's Claim on the Land
segments.gist: Edom said it would possess the two nations and the land of Israel, and blasphemed against God, so God will judge it accordingly.

segments.title: Edom's Desolation and God's Glory
segments.gist: God declares that as Edom rejoiced over Israel's desolation, so it will be desolated, and God will be known through His judgment.

36.summary: Ezekiel is told to prophesy to the mountains of Israel that God will restore the land and multiply its people, not for their sake but for the honor of His holy name, which they profaned among the nations. God promises to cleanse Israel with clean water, give them a new heart and a new spirit, and cause them to obey Him and dwell in the land. The chapter closes with a promise that the ruined cities will be rebuilt and the desolate land will become like the garden of Eden, and the nations will know that the Lord has done it.

segments.title: Prophecy to the Mountains of Israel
segments.gist: Ezekiel prophesies to the mountains of Israel that God will restore the land, multiply its people, and no longer let the nations devour them.

segments.title: Israel's Defilement and God's Concern
segments.gist: God explains that Israel defiled the land by their ways and were scattered among the nations, but He will act to vindicate His holy name.

segments.title: Promise of Cleansing and New Heart
segments.gist: God promises to gather Israel, cleanse them with clean water, give them a new heart and spirit, and cause them to obey Him.

segments.title: Restoration of the Land
segments.gist: God promises to rebuild the ruined cities, make the land like the garden of Eden, and let the nations know that He has done it.

segments.title: Promise to Multiply the Flock
segments.gist: God declares that He will multiply the people like a flock, and the ruined cities will be filled with flocks of people.

37.summary: Ezekiel is shown a valley of dry bones that come to life when he prophesies, symbolizing Israel's national resurrection from exile. God then commands Ezekiel to join two sticks, one for Judah and one for Joseph, into one, signifying the reunification of the divided kingdom under one shepherd, David, with a new covenant of peace and God's sanctuary among them forever.

segments.title: Valley of Dry Bones
segments.gist: Ezekiel prophesies to dry bones; they become a vast living army, representing Israel's restoration from the grave.

segments.title: Two Sticks Become One
segments.gist: Ezekiel joins two sticks for Judah and Joseph, symbolizing the reunification of Israel and Judah under one king.

segments.title: David as Shepherd King
segments.gist: God promises one shepherd, David, a covenant of peace, and His sanctuary among them forever.

38.summary: The word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel against Gog, of the land of Magog, who will lead a vast coalition against Israel in the latter days. God declares that He will bring Gog against His people as a judgment, but will then destroy Gog's forces on the mountains of Israel, sending fire and pestilence and displaying His glory among the nations.

segments.title: Prophecy Against Gog
segments.gist: God commands Ezekiel to set his face against Gog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, and declares He will turn him back and put hooks in his jaws.

segments.title: Gog's Great Coalition
segments.gist: Gog is described as gathering a vast army from many nations, including Persia, Ethiopia, and Libya, to come against the land of Israel like a cloud.

segments.title: Gog's Evil Plan
segments.gist: In the latter days Gog will devise an evil thought to attack the unwalled villages of Israel and take spoil, but God asks if he is not the one spoken of by the prophets.

segments.title: God's Wrath and Judgment
segments.gist: God declares that His fury will rise against Gog, bringing earthquake, pestilence, bloodshed, and fire upon him and his armies, so the nations will know He is the LORD.

39.summary: Ezekiel 39 continues the oracle against Gog, declaring God's judgment on Gog and his armies, with their weapons burned and bodies buried in the valley of Hamongog. It describes the gathering of Israel from exile, the restoration of the land, and God's promise never again to hide His face from His people.

segments.title: God's Judgment on Gog
segments.gist: God declares He is against Gog, will turn him around, and will give his armies to the birds and beasts as prey.

segments.title: Burning Weapons and Burying the Dead
segments.gist: Israel burns Gog's weapons for seven years and buries the dead in the valley of Hamongog, cleansing the land.

segments.title: Call to the Birds and Beasts
segments.gist: God summons the birds and beasts to a sacrificial feast on the flesh and blood of Gog's fallen warriors.

segments.title: God's Glory Among the Nations
segments.gist: God will display His glory among the nations, and Israel will know that their captivity was due to their sins.

segments.title: Restoration of Israel
segments.gist: God promises to restore Jacob, gather Israel from exile, and pour out His Spirit upon them, never hiding His face again.

40.summary: In the twenty-fifth year of the exile, Ezekiel is brought in a vision to a high mountain in Israel, where he sees a structure like a city. A man with a measuring reed guides him to measure the temple complex, beginning with the east gate, then the outer court, the north and south gates, the inner court, and the temple building itself, recording dimensions throughout.

segments.title: Vision of the measuring man
segments.gist: Ezekiel is brought to a high mountain and sees a man with a measuring reed standing in a gateway.

segments.title: Measuring the east gate
segments.gist: The man measures the wall and the east gate's thresholds, chambers, and posts.

segments.title: Outer court and pavement
segments.gist: Ezekiel is brought into the outer court, where he sees chambers and a paved area, and the man measures its dimensions.

segments.title: North and south gates measured
segments.gist: The man measures the north gate and the south gate of the outer court, including their chambers and arches.

segments.title: Inner court gates measured
segments.gist: The man measures the inner court's south, east, and north gates with their chambers and posts.

segments.title: Chambers and temple porch
segments.gist: Chambers for washing and singers are described, and the man measures the temple porch and its pillars.

41.summary: Ezekiel is shown the inner temple, including the nave and most holy place with their measurements, the side chambers, the altar of wood, and the carved decorations of cherubims and palm trees throughout the house.

segments.title: Measuring the Temple and Most Holy Place
segments.gist: The man measures the temple's walls, the nave, and the most holy place, giving their dimensions.

segments.title: Side Chambers and Their Structure
segments.gist: The side chambers around the temple are described, with their three stories, increasing width, and entrances.

segments.title: The Separate Place and Building Measurements
segments.gist: The separate place and the building facing it are measured, along with the galleries and inner temple.

segments.title: Carved Cherubims and Palm Trees
segments.gist: The temple's interior is decorated with carved cherubims and palm trees, each cherub having two faces.

segments.title: The Altar of Wood and Door Posts
segments.gist: The wooden altar is described, along with the temple's doors, windows, and carved decorations.

42.summary: Ezekiel is shown the chambers of the inner court and the dimensions of the temple's outer walls and courts. The measurements emphasize the holiness and separation of the temple area from the profane.

segments.title: Chambers and Measurements
segments.gist: The prophet is brought to the outer court and measures the chambers, including their galleries and doors.

segments.title: Outer Wall Dimensions
segments.gist: The man measures the outer wall of the temple on all four sides, a square of five hundred reeds.

43.summary: Ezekiel is brought to the east gate and sees the glory of the God of Israel return to fill the temple. The LORD declares this as His dwelling place and gives ordinances for the altar, its consecration, and the offerings to be made upon it.

segments.title: Glory Returns to the Temple
segments.gist: Ezekiel is brought to the east gate and sees the glory of the LORD come from the east and fill the house.

segments.title: LORD Speaks from the Temple
segments.gist: The LORD speaks from the temple, declaring it His throne and dwelling, and rebukes Israel's past defilements.

segments.title: Measurements of the Altar
segments.gist: The dimensions and structure of the altar are given, including its base, ledges, and horns.

segments.title: Consecration of the Altar
segments.gist: Ordinances for consecrating the altar are given: sin offerings, burnt offerings, and the seven days of purification.

44.summary: Ezekiel is brought back to the outer gate of the sanctuary and sees it shut, with the glory of the Lord filling the house. The Lord rebukes Israel's past profanation of the temple and gives ordinances for the priests and Levites, distinguishing the faithful Zadokites from those who went astray. The chapter closes with regulations for the priests' dress, conduct, and portions.

segments.title: The shut east gate
segments.gist: Ezekiel is brought to the outer east gate, which is shut because the Lord entered by it, and it shall remain closed.

segments.title: Glory fills the house
segments.gist: Ezekiel is brought by the north gate before the house, sees the glory of the Lord fill it, and is told to mark well what he sees.

segments.title: Rebuke for profaning the temple
segments.gist: The Lord recounts Israel's abominations, including admitting foreigners uncircumcised in heart and flesh into the sanctuary, and declares they shall no longer do so.

segments.title: Levites who went astray
segments.gist: Levites who ministered before idols and caused Israel to stumble are demoted to serve as gatekeepers and helpers in the house, bearing their iniquity.

segments.title: Zadokite priests restored
segments.gist: The sons of Zadok, who kept charge of the sanctuary when Israel strayed, shall come near to minister before the Lord and stand before him.

segments.title: Ordinances for the priests
segments.gist: Regulations are given for the priests' linen garments, marriages, teaching, judgments, mourning, food, and inheritance portions.

45.summary: Ezekiel 45 describes the division of the land in the millennial kingdom, with a holy district for the sanctuary and the priests, a portion for the Levites, and the city's possession. It also gives ordinances for the prince's offerings and the people's worship, including the Passover and other feasts, and instructions for just weights and measures.

segments.title: The Holy District
segments.gist: When the land is divided, a holy portion 25,000 reeds long and 10,000 wide is set apart for the sanctuary and the priests.

segments.title: The Prince's Portion
segments.gist: The prince receives land on both sides of the holy district and the city's possession, extending to the borders.

segments.title: Justice for the Prince
segments.gist: The princes are told to stop violence and execute justice; honest scales and measures are required.

segments.title: Offerings for the Prince
segments.gist: The people give a fixed portion of grain, oil, and sheep to the prince, who provides the offerings for Israel.

segments.title: Feasts and Offerings
segments.gist: Regulations for the prince's sin offerings at the new year and Passover, and for the daily and feast offerings.

46.summary: Ezekiel 46 continues the vision of the millennial temple, giving regulations for the prince's offerings, the people's worship, and the orderly use of the temple courts. It specifies the east gate's opening on sabbaths and new moons, the prince's burnt and peace offerings, and the inheritance laws for the prince and people. It also details the kitchens where the priests boil and bake the offerings.

segments.title: The East Gate and Prince's Offerings
segments.gist: The east gate is shut on six working days but opened on the sabbath and new moon for the prince's offerings.

segments.title: Rules for Worship and Daily Offering
segments.gist: The people must enter and exit by opposite gates, and the prince provides a daily morning burnt offering.

segments.title: Laws of the Prince's Inheritance
segments.gist: The prince may give gifts to his sons, but he must not take the people's inheritance by oppression.

segments.title: The Temple Kitchens
segments.gist: The prophet is shown the kitchens where the priests boil the trespass and sin offerings and bake the meat offering.

47.summary: Ezekiel is shown a river flowing from the temple that brings life and healing wherever it goes, and the boundaries of the land are described for the twelve tribes, with provisions for strangers to inherit land among them.

segments.title: The Life-Giving River
segments.gist: A man leads Ezekiel through waters that flow from the temple, deepening from ankles to a river, bringing life to all it touches.

segments.title: Boundaries of the Land
segments.gist: The Lord defines the borders of the land for the twelve tribes, including the northern, eastern, southern, and western limits.

48.summary: Ezekiel 48 closes the book by allotting the tribal inheritances in the restored land, setting aside a holy district for the sanctuary, priests, Levites, and the city, and describing the city's gates and dimensions. The chapter ends with the name of the city: 'The LORD is there.'

segments.title: Tribal portions from north to south
segments.gist: Seven tribes receive strips of land from the north border down to the holy district.

segments.title: The holy oblation for priests and Levites
segments.gist: A sacred district is set apart for the sanctuary, the priests, and the Levites as a perpetual possession.

segments.title: The city portion and its produce
segments.gist: The remaining strip beside the holy district is for the city, its dwellings, and common use, with produce for the city's workers.

segments.title: The prince's land on both sides
segments.gist: The prince receives land flanking the holy district and the city, between the tribal portions of Judah and Benjamin.

segments.title: Portions for the remaining tribes
segments.gist: The remaining five tribes receive strips of land from the east to the west side, ending at the south border.

segments.title: The city's gates and its name
segments.gist: The city's four sides and twelve gates are described, and the city is named 'The LORD is there.'

1.summary: Daniel and other young men of Judah are taken to Babylon and trained for royal service. Daniel resolves not to defile himself with the king's food, and God gives him and his friends favor and superior wisdom. When tested before Nebuchadnezzar, they surpass all the magicians and wise men.

segments.title: Exiles chosen for training
segments.gist: Nebuchadnezzar orders young men of Judah, including Daniel and his friends, to be trained for three years in Babylon.

segments.title: Daniel refuses king's food
segments.gist: Daniel resolves not to defile himself with the king's meat and wine, and after a test of ten days, he and his friends are allowed vegetables.

segments.title: God gives wisdom and favor
segments.gist: God gives the four young men knowledge and wisdom, and when brought before the king, they surpass all the magicians and wise men.

2.summary: King Nebuchadnezzar dreams of a great image and demands that his wise men tell him both the dream and its interpretation, threatening death if they fail. Daniel seeks mercy from God, receives the dream and its meaning in a night vision, and interprets it as four successive kingdoms ending with an everlasting kingdom set up by God. The king honors Daniel and his companions and promotes Daniel to rule over Babylon.

segments.title: Nebuchadnezzar Demands Dream and Interpretation
segments.gist: Nebuchadnezzar has a troubling dream and demands the wise men reveal both the dream and its meaning, threatening death for failure.

segments.title: Daniel Seeks and Receives Revelation
segments.gist: Daniel asks for time, prays with his companions, and receives a night vision revealing the dream and its interpretation, prompting him to praise God.

segments.title: Daniel Presents Himself Before the King
