segments.gist: Daniel tells the king that no wise man could reveal the secret, but God in heaven reveals mysteries, and he will now declare the dream and its meaning.

segments.title: The Dream and Its Interpretation
segments.gist: Daniel describes the great image with its head of gold, breast of silver, belly of brass, legs of iron, and feet of iron and clay, and interprets it as successive kingdoms destroyed by an everlasting kingdom.

segments.title: The King Honors Daniel
segments.gist: Nebuchadnezzar falls before Daniel, acknowledges his God, gives him many gifts, and makes him ruler over Babylon and chief of the wise men.

3.summary: King Nebuchadnezzar sets up a golden image and commands all peoples to worship it, but three Jewish men—Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego—refuse. Enraged, the king has them thrown into a fiery furnace, where they are preserved, and he witnesses a fourth figure in the fire and blesses their God.

segments.title: Nebuchadnezzar's Golden Image
segments.gist: King Nebuchadnezzar makes a golden image and commands all peoples to fall down and worship it when the music plays.

segments.title: Accusation Against the Three Jews
segments.gist: Certain Chaldeans accuse Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego of refusing to worship the golden image, and they are brought before the king.

segments.title: The Three Refuse to Worship
segments.gist: Nebuchadnezzar threatens them with the fiery furnace, but the three men declare that their God can deliver them and that they will not serve other gods.

segments.title: Cast into the Fiery Furnace
segments.gist: The king, furious, orders the furnace heated seven times hotter, and the three men are bound and cast into the fire, which kills the executioners.

segments.title: The King Sees Four Men
segments.gist: Nebuchadnezzar is astonished to see four men loose and walking in the fire, and he calls the three servants of God to come out.

segments.title: The King Blesses God
segments.gist: Nebuchadnezzar blesses the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego and promotes the three men in the province of Babylon.

4.summary: King Nebuchadnezzar issues a proclamation to all peoples recounting how the Most High humbled him: after his pride over Babylon, he was driven from men to eat grass like an ox until he acknowledged God's dominion, whereupon his reason and kingdom were restored and he praised the King of heaven.

segments.title: Nebuchadnezzar's Proclamation
segments.gist: Nebuchadnezzar addresses all peoples and nations, declaring the signs and wonders the Most High God has shown toward him.

segments.title: The Dream of the Great Tree
segments.gist: Nebuchadnezzar recounts his dream of a great tree cut down by a watcher, leaving a stump bound with iron and brass, and Daniel's interpretation that it signifies the king's coming humiliation.

segments.title: Daniel Interprets the Dream
segments.gist: Daniel explains that the tree is Nebuchadnezzar, who will be driven from men to dwell with beasts until he knows the Most High rules, and urges the king to break off his sins by righteousness.

segments.title: The Dream Fulfilled
segments.gist: Twelve months later, while boasting of Babylon's greatness, Nebuchadnezzar is driven from men, eats grass like an ox, and his hair and nails grow until his understanding returns.

segments.title: Nebuchadnezzar Praises God
segments.gist: Nebuchadnezzar lifts his eyes to heaven, praises the Most High as eternal and sovereign, is restored to his kingdom, and confesses that God humbles the proud.

5.summary: Belshazzar, king of Babylon, holds a great feast and drinks from the gold and silver vessels taken from the Jerusalem temple, praising idols. A disembodied hand writes mysterious words on the palace wall, terrifying the king. Daniel is brought in, interprets the writing as a divine judgment against Belshazzar for his pride, and that very night Babylon falls and Belshazzar is slain.

segments.title: Belshazzar's Feast and Temple Vessels
segments.gist: King Belshazzar gives a great feast for a thousand nobles and orders the sacred temple vessels brought so he and his guests can drink from them.

segments.title: The Writing on the Wall
segments.gist: A hand appears and writes on the palace wall; the king's face changes and he calls loudly for the wise men of Babylon.

segments.title: Daniel Summoned Before the King
segments.gist: The queen advises the king to call Daniel, who is brought in and promised rewards if he can read and interpret the writing.

segments.title: Daniel Rebukes Belshazzar's Pride
segments.gist: Daniel refuses the gifts, recounts God's dealings with Nebuchadnezzar, and charges Belshazzar with pride and idolatry despite knowing this history.

segments.title: The Interpretation of the Writing
segments.gist: Daniel reads the words MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN and explains that God has numbered Belshazzar's kingdom, weighed him, and will divide it to the Medes and Persians.

segments.title: Belshazzar Slain and Babylon Falls
segments.gist: Belshazzar honors Daniel, but that night he is killed and Darius the Mede takes the kingdom.

6.summary: King Darius promotes Daniel to a high office, prompting jealous officials to trap him through his prayer life. They persuade the king to outlaw petitions to anyone but himself, and Daniel is thrown into a lions' den for praying to God. The king spends a sleepless night, finds Daniel unharmed the next morning, and issues a decree honoring Daniel's God.

segments.title: Daniel's Promotion and Enemies' Plot
segments.gist: Darius sets 120 princes and three presidents over the kingdom, with Daniel preferred above them; jealous officials seek grounds against him but find none, so they scheme regarding his prayer life.

segments.title: Daniel Prays and Is Accused
segments.gist: Daniel continues praying three times daily before his window toward Jerusalem; the officials catch him and report to the king, who reluctantly agrees Daniel must be cast into the lions' den.

segments.title: Daniel Cast into the Lions' Den
segments.gist: Daniel is thrown into the den with a stone sealed over it; the king fasts and cannot sleep, then finds Daniel alive and unharmed, and has his accusers and their families cast in and destroyed.

segments.title: Darius's Decree Honoring God
segments.gist: Darius writes to all peoples praising the God of Daniel as the living God who delivers and works signs, and Daniel prospers in the kingdom.

7.summary: Daniel recounts a night vision of four great beasts rising from the sea, representing four kingdoms, followed by the appearance of the Ancient of Days and the coming of the Son of Man to receive everlasting dominion. An angel explains the vision to Daniel, identifying the beasts as successive kingdoms and the saints of the Most High as the ones who will ultimately possess the kingdom, though they will first face persecution. Daniel is troubled by the vision, especially the fourth beast with ten horns and the little horn that speaks great things.

segments.title: Vision of the Four Beasts
segments.gist: Daniel sees four beasts rise from the sea: a lion, a bear, a leopard, and a terrifying fourth beast with iron teeth and ten horns.

segments.title: The Ancient of Days and Son of Man
segments.gist: The Ancient of Days takes His throne, the beast is slain, and one like the Son of Man comes with the clouds to receive everlasting dominion.

segments.title: Daniel Seeks Interpretation
segments.gist: Daniel is troubled and asks the meaning of the vision; he is told the four beasts are four kings, but the saints will possess the kingdom forever.

segments.title: The Fourth Beast and the Horn
segments.gist: Daniel asks specifically about the fourth beast, its iron teeth and ten horns, and the little horn that makes war against the saints until the Ancient of Days comes.

segments.title: Explanation of the Fourth Kingdom
segments.gist: The angel explains that the fourth kingdom will devour the earth, its ten horns are ten kings, and a little horn will speak against the Most High and persecute the saints until judgment gives them the kingdom.

8.summary: Daniel sees a vision of a ram with two horns and a goat with a prominent horn; the goat defeats the ram, but its horn breaks and four horns arise, from one of which a little horn grows and desecrates the sanctuary. The angel Gabriel explains that the vision concerns the latter time of the kingdoms of Media-Persia and Greece, and the fierce king who will oppose the holy people, but Daniel is told to seal the vision because it is for many days.

segments.title: Vision of the Ram
segments.gist: Daniel sees a ram with two horns, one higher than the other, which becomes great and does as it pleases.

segments.title: Goat Defeats the Ram
segments.gist: A goat with a notable horn charges the ram, breaks its two horns, and becomes very great.

segments.title: Little Horn Desecrates Sanctuary
segments.gist: A little horn grows exceedingly, exalts itself against the host of heaven, and casts down the sanctuary and the daily sacrifice.

segments.title: Gabriel Explains the Vision
segments.gist: Gabriel is commanded to make Daniel understand the vision, explaining that the ram and goat represent the kings of Media-Persia and Greece.

segments.title: Meaning of the Horns
segments.gist: Gabriel details the two-horned ram, the goat's great horn, the four horns, and the fierce king who will destroy many and stand against the Prince of princes.

9.summary: Daniel reads Jeremiah's prophecy that Jerusalem would lie desolate seventy years and prays a long confession of Israel's sins, pleading for God's mercy. While he is still praying, the angel Gabriel arrives to give him the answer: seventy weeks are determined upon the people and the holy city, marking out the coming of Messiah and the destruction to follow.

segments.title: Daniel reads the seventy years
segments.gist: Daniel understands from Jeremiah's writings that the desolation of Jerusalem is to last seventy years.

segments.title: Daniel's confession of sin
segments.gist: Daniel prays to the Lord, confessing Israel's rebellion and the shame that has come upon the nation.

segments.title: Plea for mercy on Jerusalem
segments.gist: Daniel asks God to turn away his anger and to hear and forgive for the sake of his city and his name.

segments.title: Gabriel arrives with the answer
segments.gist: While Daniel is still praying, the angel Gabriel comes to him and announces that he has been sent to give understanding.

segments.title: The seventy weeks prophecy
segments.gist: Gabriel explains the seventy weeks: the coming of Messiah, the cutting off of the anointed one, and the destruction of the city.

10.summary: Daniel sees a vision of a glorious man beside the river Hiddekel after three weeks of mourning. The appearance terrifies him and his companions flee, but the messenger strengthens him, explains that he was delayed twenty-one days by the prince of Persia, and tells Daniel he has come to show him what will befall his people in the latter days.

segments.title: Daniel mourns three weeks
segments.gist: In the third year of Cyrus, Daniel mourns for three full weeks, eating no pleasant bread and using no ointment.

segments.title: Vision of the glorious man
segments.gist: By the river Hiddekel Daniel sees a man clothed in linen with a face like lightning and eyes like fire; his companions flee in terror.

segments.title: Messenger strengthens and explains delay
segments.gist: A hand touches Daniel and a voice strengthens him, explaining that the prince of Persia withstood the messenger twenty-one days until Michael came to help.

segments.title: Daniel overwhelmed and strengthened
segments.gist: Daniel is speechless and weak, but the one like the sons of men touches his lips and strengthens him again.

segments.title: Messenger promises to show the future
segments.gist: The messenger strengthens Daniel, asks why he has come, and says he will show what is written in the scripture of truth, though he must soon return to fight the prince of Persia.

11.summary: Daniel receives a detailed prophecy of future empires and conflicts, beginning with the Persian and Greek kingdoms and focusing on the wars between the Seleucid and Ptolemaic dynasties. The prophecy culminates in the rise of a contemptible king who profanes the sanctuary, sets up the abomination of desolation, and persecutes the faithful, though many will be purified and a final deliverance is promised.

segments.title: Persia and Greece Foretold
segments.gist: The angel foretells the rise of the Persian empire and its wealth, followed by the conquest by a mighty Greek king whose kingdom will be divided.

segments.title: Wars of the Kings of the South and North
segments.gist: The angel describes repeated conflicts between the king of the south and the king of the north, including alliances, betrayals, and shifting fortunes.

segments.title: Rise of a Contemptible King
segments.gist: A contemptible king arises through flattery and deceit, gaining power and plotting against the wealthy and the covenant people.

segments.title: Campaign Against the South
segments.gist: The king of the north campaigns against the king of the south with a great army, but his plans fail and he returns to his land.

segments.title: Profanation of the Sanctuary
segments.gist: The king returns, profanes the sanctuary, sets up the abomination of desolation, and persecutes the faithful, leading to their purification.

segments.title: The King Exalts Himself
segments.gist: The king exalts himself above all gods, prospers until the time of wrath, and meets his end with no one to help him.

12.summary: Daniel is told of the time of trouble and the resurrection of the dead, with the wise shining like stars. He sees two angels discussing the duration of these wonders and is told to seal the words until the end. Daniel is given a final word about the purification of the wise and his own rest until the end.

segments.title: Time of Trouble and Resurrection
segments.gist: Michael stands up, a time of trouble comes, and many who sleep in the dust awake to everlasting life or shame.

segments.title: Angels Ask About the End
segments.gist: Two angels ask the man in linen how long until the wonders end, and he swears it will be for a time, times, and a half.

segments.title: Daniel Told to Seal the Words
segments.gist: Daniel does not understand, and is told the words are sealed until the end, when the wicked will not understand but the wise will.

segments.title: Final Numbers and Daniel's Rest
segments.gist: From the taking away of the daily sacrifice, 1290 and 1335 days are given; Daniel is told to go his way and rest until the end.

1.summary: God commands Hosea to marry a promiscuous woman as a sign of Israel's unfaithfulness, and Hosea's children are given names that announce judgment and the reversal of God's mercy. The chapter ends with a promise that Israel will one day be restored and called God's people.

segments.title: Hosea's marriage commanded
segments.gist: God tells Hosea to take a wife of whoredoms as a symbol of Israel's departure from the Lord.

segments.title: Jezreel born
segments.gist: Hosea's wife bears a son named Jezreel, marking the coming judgment on Jehu's house and Israel's kingdom.

segments.title: Lo-ruhamah born
segments.gist: A daughter is named Lo-ruhamah, signifying that God will no longer show mercy to Israel but will save Judah.

segments.title: Lo-ammi born
segments.gist: A son is named Lo-ammi, meaning 'not my people,' declaring Israel's broken relationship with God.

segments.title: Promise of restoration
segments.gist: Despite judgment, God promises that Israel will multiply and be called sons of the living God, reunited under one head.

2.summary: Hosea 2 presents God's indictment of Israel for spiritual adultery, His promise to strip and expose her, and His subsequent restoration: He will allure her into the wilderness, betroth her forever, and renew the covenant with creation.

segments.title: Plead with Your Mother
segments.gist: God calls the children to contend with their mother Israel, threatening to strip her naked and make her like a wilderness for her harlotry.

segments.title: Hedge Her Way with Thorns
segments.gist: God will block Israel's paths, withhold grain and wine, and expose her lovers, punishing her for forgetting Him and serving Baal.

segments.title: Allure Her into the Wilderness
segments.gist: God promises to woo Israel back, give her vineyards, and betroth her forever in righteousness, lovingkindness, and faithfulness.

segments.title: I Will Hear the Heavens
segments.gist: In that day God will answer the heavens, earth, grain, and wine, sow Israel in the land, and call her beloved who was not beloved.

3.summary: At the LORD's command, Hosea buys back his adulterous wife for fifteen pieces of silver and a homer and a half of barley, symbolizing God's love for Israel despite their unfaithfulness. The chapter then describes Israel's coming period without king, prince, sacrifice, or ephod, after which they will return and seek the LORD and David their king.

segments.title: Hosea Redeems His Wife
segments.gist: The LORD tells Hosea to love an adulteress again, so he buys her back for silver and barley and confines her for many days.

segments.title: Israel's Exile and Return
segments.gist: Israel will remain many days without king, prince, sacrifice, or ephod, but afterward they will return and seek the LORD and David their king.

4.summary: God brings a formal charge against Israel for lack of faithfulness, knowledge, and obedience, detailing the corruption of priests, prophets, and people. The chapter warns that their idolatry and harlotry will lead to judgment, and even Judah is cautioned not to follow the same path.

segments.title: The Lord's Controversy
segments.gist: The Lord charges Israel with no truth, mercy, or knowledge of God, and warns of judgment on the land.

segments.title: Priests and People Rejected
segments.gist: The people and priests are condemned for rejecting knowledge and committing harlotry, and they will eat but not be satisfied.

segments.title: Harlotry and Idolatry
segments.gist: Harlotry, wine, and idolatry take away understanding; the people consult stocks and commit adultery, so God will not punish their daughters.

segments.title: Warning to Judah
segments.gist: Israel is stubborn like a heifer; Judah is warned not to follow Israel's idolatry, and a whirlwind will wrap them in shame.

5.summary: Hosea 5 announces God's judgment on Israel's priests, people, and leaders for their idolatry and arrogance, and on Judah for following the same course. Because they persist in sin and refuse to seek the Lord, God withdraws his presence and will carry them into exile until they acknowledge their guilt and seek him in distress.

segments.title: Judgment on priests and people
segments.gist: God indicts the priests, Israel, and the king's household for leading the nation into idolatry and warns that their sacrifices will not save them.

segments.title: War and desolation declared
segments.gist: The prophet sounds the alarm for Benjamin and Ephraim, declaring that God's wrath will pour out like water and that Judah's leaders will be like those who move boundary stones.

segments.title: God withdraws until repentance
segments.gist: Ephraim turns to Assyria for help in vain, so God will be like a lion to them, tearing and withdrawing until they seek his face in their affliction.

6.summary: Hosea calls Israel to return to the LORD, who has torn but will heal, and laments that the people's love is as fleeting as morning mist. God indicts both Israel and Judah for covenant unfaithfulness, comparing their cities to places of bloodshed and their priests to robbers, and warns that judgment is appointed for them.

segments.title: Call to Return to the LORD
segments.gist: Hosea urges the people to return to the LORD, who has torn but will heal and revive them after two days.

segments.title: God Desires Mercy, Not Sacrifice
segments.gist: The LORD laments that Israel's love is like morning mist, and declares he desires mercy and knowledge of God rather than sacrifice.

segments.title: Cities and Priests Charged with Bloodshed
segments.gist: The LORD compares Gilead and Shechem to places of violence, and the priests to robbers who murder on the way.

segments.title: Judgment Appointed for Israel and Judah
segments.gist: The LORD declares that he has appointed a harvest of judgment for Israel and Judah because of their whoredom and unfaithfulness.

7.summary: Hosea 7 describes Israel's persistent unfaithfulness despite God's desire to heal them. Their kings and princes fall amid drunkenness and intrigue, and they turn to foreign nations and idols instead of to God, who nevertheless remembers their wickedness and will punish them.

segments.title: God Would Have Healed Israel
segments.gist: God laments that when he would have healed Israel, Ephraim's iniquity and Samaria's lies were exposed.

segments.title: Kings Fall Through Wickedness
segments.gist: The people make kings glad with their wickedness; adulterers and drunkards consume rulers, and all are hot as an oven in their plotting.

segments.title: Ephraim as a Cake Not Turned
segments.gist: Ephraim mixes with the nations and is like a cake not turned; strangers devour his strength, yet he does not return to the Lord.

segments.title: Like a Silly Dove
segments.gist: Ephraim is like a silly dove without heart, calling to Egypt and Assyria; God will spread his net and bring them down for their rebellion.

segments.title: They Return Not to the Most High
segments.gist: They cry not to God but howl on their beds for corn and wine, and though God chastens them, they return not to the Most High.

8.summary: Hosea 8 declares Israel's impending judgment for breaking God's covenant and rejecting what is good. The people have set up kings and idols without God's approval, and their sacrifices are unacceptable; they will return to Egypt and Assyria will oppress them. The chapter ends with a vivid image of Israel as a useless vessel and a wild ass, and with the assurance that their sins will be punished.

segments.title: Israel Cries but Not to God
segments.gist: The prophet calls for a trumpet blast because Israel has transgressed God's covenant and cries out to God without sincerity.

segments.title: Kings and Idols Without God
segments.gist: Israel set up kings and idols without God's approval; their sacrifices are unacceptable, and they will reap the whirlwind.

segments.title: Israel Swallowed Among Nations
segments.gist: Israel is swallowed up among the nations like a useless vessel; they have hired lovers and will be gathered for judgment.

segments.title: Altars for Sin and Forgetfulness
segments.gist: Ephraim multiplied altars for sin and forgot their Maker; judgment will fall on their cities and palaces.

9.summary: Hosea announces Israel's coming exile and the end of their festivals and sacrifices because of their persistent sin and idolatry. He recalls the nation's corruption from Gibeah and Baal-peor, declares that Ephraim's glory will fly away like a bird, and warns that they will be wanderers among the nations.

segments.title: No Joy in Exile
segments.gist: Hosea warns Israel not to rejoice, for they will soon be driven from the Lord's land and eat unclean food in Assyria and Egypt.

segments.title: Prophet Called a Fool
segments.gist: The prophet is dismissed as a fool, and the people are deeply corrupt, as in the days of Gibeah.

segments.title: Ephraim's Glory Departs
segments.gist: Ephraim's glory will fly away, with no birth, pregnancy, or conception, and the children will be slain.

segments.title: Cast Out for Disobedience
segments.gist: Because of their wickedness at Gilgal, God will cast them out, and they will be wanderers among the nations.

10.summary: Hosea 10 portrays Israel as a luxuriant vine that has multiplied altars and idols, leading to God's judgment. The chapter condemns the people's empty oaths, their reliance on military might, and their calf-idol worship at Beth-aven, announcing that their fortresses will be destroyed and their king cut off.

segments.title: Israel's Empty Vine
segments.gist: Israel is a fruitful vine that has used its prosperity to multiply altars and idols, provoking God's anger.

segments.title: No King and Broken Oaths
segments.gist: The people say they have no king and make empty promises, so judgment springs up like poisonous weeds.

segments.title: Calf of Beth-aven Destroyed
segments.gist: The inhabitants of Samaria mourn over the calf-idol of Beth-aven as it is carried away to Assyria, and the high places are destroyed.

segments.title: Punishment for Double Iniquity
segments.gist: God recalls Israel's sin since Gibeah and will punish them for their double iniquity when He desires.

segments.title: Call to Break Fallow Ground
segments.gist: Ephraim is a trained heifer, but God calls them to sow righteousness and break up their fallow ground, yet they have plowed wickedness.

segments.title: Destruction of Fortresses
segments.gist: God announces that a tumult will arise among the people and their fortresses will be destroyed, and the king of Israel will be cut off.

11.summary: God recounts His tender care for Israel from Egypt onward, describing Ephraim as a child He taught to walk and fed, yet Israel turned to idols and to Assyria. Because of their refusal to return, judgment by sword and exile is pronounced, though God's compassion wrestles with His anger and He vows not to destroy Ephraim utterly but to roar and bring His children trembling from the west.

segments.title: God's love for Ephraim
segments.gist: God recalls calling Israel out of Egypt and teaching Ephraim to walk, but they turned to Baalim and did not know He healed them.

segments.title: Refusal to return brings sword
segments.gist: Because Israel refuses to return to God, the sword falls on their cities and they are bent on backsliding despite God's call.

segments.title: God's compassion restrains wrath
segments.gist: God's heart is troubled within Him and His repentings are kindled together; He will not execute the fierceness of His anger nor destroy Ephraim again.

segments.title: Roar and return from exile
segments.gist: God will roar like a lion, and His children shall come trembling from the west and from Egypt and Assyria to their homes.

12.summary: Hosea presents God's case against Ephraim and Judah, recalling Jacob's early struggles and God's care, and condemning the people's deceit, wealth, and reliance on Assyria and idols. The chapter warns that their sin will bring judgment and that God's words will be fulfilled.

segments.title: God's Controversy with Ephraim
segments.gist: God charges Ephraim with lies and violence, recalls Jacob's birth and struggle with God, and calls the people to return to their God.

segments.title: Ephraim's Wealth and Idolatry
segments.gist: Ephraim boasts of wealth and denies iniquity, but God will make them dwell in tents again and exposes their altars as sin.

segments.title: Jacob's Flight and God's Judgment
segments.gist: Jacob fled to Syria and Israel was preserved, but Ephraim's provocation will bring bloodshed and reproach from God.

13.summary: Hosea recounts how Ephraim's exalted status turned to idolatry and how God will therefore scatter them like chaff and destroy them as a lion; yet he promises to ransom them from the grave and calls them to return, while Samaria's guilt brings certain judgment.

segments.title: Ephraim's idolatry and fading glory
segments.gist: Ephraim exalted himself but sinned with Baal, and now their glory will vanish like morning mist and chaff.

segments.title: God's fierce judgment like a lion
segments.gist: God declares he is the LORD who brought them from Egypt, and he will tear them like a lion and devour them.

segments.title: Israel's destruction and kingship removed
segments.gist: Israel is destroyed for opposing God; their king is given in anger and taken away in wrath.

segments.title: Iniquity bound up and ransom promised
segments.gist: Ephraim's iniquity is stored up, but God promises to ransom them from the grave and redeem them from death.

segments.title: Samaria's guilt and judgment
segments.gist: Though Ephraim is fruitful, an east wind will come, and Samaria will fall for rebelling against God.

14.summary: Hosea closes with a call for Israel to return to the LORD, promising restoration from stumbling and healing from backsliding. The chapter contrasts Ephraim's former arrogance with a renewed confession and the LORD's promise to be like dew to Israel, leading to a final wise saying about the LORD's right ways.

segments.title: Call to Return and Promise
segments.gist: Israel is urged to return to the LORD with words, and the LORD promises to heal their backsliding and love them freely.

segments.title: Ephraim's Confession and Renunciation
segments.gist: Ephraim confesses that idols and Assyria cannot save, and the LORD promises to be like dew, causing Israel to blossom.

1.summary: Joel opens with a call to hear about a devastating locust plague that has stripped the land bare, leaving no grain, wine, or oil. He summons the drunkards, farmers, and priests to mourn and wail, declares the day of the Lord near, and calls for a fast and assembly as the beasts and even the fire of the wilderness cry out in want.

segments.title: Call to Hear the Locust Plague
segments.gist: Joel addresses all inhabitants, telling them to pass the news of the locusts to future generations and describing the successive waves of locusts that have devoured the land.

segments.title: Drunkards and Farmers Mourn
segments.gist: Drunkards are told to weep because the wine is cut off, and farmers are called to lament because the harvest is destroyed and the fields are laid waste.

segments.title: Lament Like a Virgin
segments.gist: The people are told to mourn like a young widow; the grain and drink offerings are cut off from the house of the Lord, and the priests mourn.

segments.title: Farmers and Vinedressers Wail
segments.gist: Farmers and vinedressers are called to wail because the wheat and barley are destroyed and the vine, fig tree, and other trees are withered.

segments.title: Call to Fast and Assembly
segments.gist: Priests are told to gird themselves and lament, to sanctify a fast and call a solemn assembly, gathering the elders and all inhabitants to the house of the Lord.

segments.title: Day of the Lord and Cry for Help
segments.gist: The day of the Lord is proclaimed near, bringing destruction; fire has devoured the pastures, beasts cry out, and the prophet cries to the Lord as even the rivers are dried up.

2.summary: Joel calls for trumpet-blown alarm and fasting as the day of the LORD approaches, describing an invading army and urging repentance; God then promises restoration, the defeat of the northern enemy, and the outpouring of His Spirit on all flesh, with signs in heaven and earth before the great day.

segments.title: Alarm and the invading army
segments.gist: A trumpet sounds warning of a vast, disciplined army advancing like fire and horsemen, causing anguish and cosmic signs.

segments.title: Call to repentance
segments.gist: The LORD urges turning to Him with fasting and weeping, for He is gracious and may relent and bless again.

segments.title: Promise of restoration
segments.gist: God promises to drive away the northern army, restore the years lost to locusts, and bless His people with plenty and safety.

segments.title: Outpouring of the Spirit
segments.gist: God promises to pour His Spirit on all flesh, with prophetic dreams and cosmic signs before the great day of the LORD.

3.summary: The chapter presents God's judgment on the nations gathered in the valley of Jehoshaphat for their mistreatment of Israel, followed by promises of restoration for Judah and Jerusalem. It closes with a vision of Zion's security and blessing, contrasting the desolation of God's enemies.

segments.title: Judgment on the Nations
segments.gist: God declares judgment on the nations for scattering His people and dividing His land, promising to gather them and repay their deeds.

segments.title: Call to Battle and Harvest
segments.gist: The nations are summoned to war and to the valley of Jehoshaphat, where the harvest is ripe and God's judgment is near.

segments.title: Zion's Refuge and Blessing
segments.gist: The LORD roars from Zion, providing refuge for His people while Egypt and Edom become desolate, and Judah dwells in safety forever.

1.summary: Amos opens with God's roar from Zion and a series of judgments against Israel's neighbors—Damascus, Gaza, Tyre, Edom, Ammon, and Moab—each condemned for specific atrocities. The chapter ends by turning to Judah and then Israel, announcing that their own sins will not go unpunished.

segments.title: The LORD roars from Zion
segments.gist: Amos declares that the LORD will roar from Zion and judge, causing the pastures and Carmel to wither.

segments.title: Judgment on Damascus
segments.gist: Damascus is condemned for threshing Gilead, and God will send fire and exile its people.

segments.title: Judgment on Gaza
segments.gist: Gaza is judged for delivering captives to Edom, and fire will destroy its cities and Philistine remnant.

segments.title: Judgment on Tyre
segments.gist: Tyre is condemned for delivering captives to Edom and breaking a covenant, so fire will consume its walls.

segments.title: Judgment on Edom
segments.gist: Edom is judged for pursuing his brother with the sword and casting off pity, so fire will devour Teman.

segments.title: Judgment on Ammon
segments.gist: Ammon is condemned for ripping open pregnant women in Gilead, and its king and people will go into exile.

2.summary: Amos continues his oracles against the nations, pronouncing judgment on Moab, Judah, and finally Israel. He details Israel's sins—oppressing the poor, sexual immorality, and ingratitude toward God's past acts—and declares that their strength will not save them from destruction.

segments.title: Judgment on Moab
segments.gist: Moab is condemned for burning the bones of Edom's king, and God will send fire upon Moab.

segments.title: Judgment on Judah
segments.gist: Judah is judged for rejecting God's law and following lies, and fire will consume Jerusalem.

segments.title: Israel's sins listed
segments.gist: Israel is condemned for selling the righteous, oppressing the poor, and sexual immorality at altars.

segments.title: Ingratitude for God's acts
segments.gist: God recounts destroying the Amorites, bringing Israel out of Egypt, and raising prophets and Nazirites, yet Israel led the Nazirites astray.

segments.title: Certain destruction
segments.gist: God will crush Israel; the swift, strong, and mighty will not escape, and the bravest will flee naked.

3.summary: God declares that He has chosen Israel alone among all families of the earth, so their sins will bring unique punishment. He reminds them of past acts and warns that disaster is coming, with only a remnant to be saved, and that the altars of Bethel will be destroyed.

segments.title: God's unique judgment on Israel
segments.gist: God declares that He has known only Israel among all families, so He will punish their iniquities.

segments.title: Cause and effect in prophecy
segments.gist: Through a series of rhetorical questions, Amos shows that every effect has a cause, and the prophet speaks because God has spoken.

segments.title: Call to witness oppression
segments.gist: God summons Ashdod and Egypt to witness the oppression in Samaria, and declares that an adversary will surround the land.

segments.title: Remnant saved, altars destroyed
segments.gist: God promises to save a remnant like a shepherd rescuing pieces from a lion's mouth, and warns that the altars of Bethel and the luxurious houses will be destroyed.

4.summary: Amos addresses the luxury-loving women of Samaria, foretells their captivity, and recounts Israel's repeated failures to return to God despite famine, drought, and plague. The chapter ends with a call to prepare to meet God, who is the LORD of hosts.

segments.title: Judgment on Samaria's Women
segments.gist: Amos calls the wealthy women of Samaria 'cows of Bashan' and swears by his holiness that they will be taken away with hooks.

segments.title: Empty Religious Rituals
segments.gist: The people are sarcastically invited to transgress at Bethel and Gilgal, multiplying sacrifices and tithes, yet their religion is empty.

segments.title: Refusal to Return
segments.gist: God recounts past judgments—famine, drought, blight, locusts, pestilence, and overthrow—yet the people did not return to Him.

segments.title: Prepare to Meet God
segments.gist: Because of Israel's persistent rebellion, God warns them to prepare to meet Him, the Creator who controls all nature.

5.summary: Amos delivers a lamentation over Israel, declaring that the nation will fall and only a remnant will survive. He calls the people to seek the Lord and live, condemns their perversion of justice and their empty religious rituals, and warns that the day of the Lord will bring darkness and exile because they have rejected reproof and oppressed the poor.

segments.title: Lament over Fallen Israel
segments.gist: Amos sings a funeral song for Israel, saying the virgin is fallen and only a tenth will remain.

segments.title: Seek the Lord and Live
segments.gist: The Lord calls Israel to seek Him and live, warning that He will break out like fire and that He is the Almighty Creator.

segments.title: Condemnation of Injustice
segments.gist: The Lord rebukes those who hate reproof, oppress the poor, and pervert justice, so the prudent keep silent.

segments.title: Call to Seek Good
segments.gist: The prophet urges seeking good and not evil so the Lord may be with them, but warns of wailing in all streets because of judgment.

segments.title: Woe to Those Desiring the Day
segments.gist: Woe to those who long for the day of the Lord, for it will be darkness and not light, like fleeing a lion and meeting a bear.

segments.title: Rejection of Empty Rituals
segments.gist: The Lord rejects Israel's feasts and offerings, calls for justice to flow, and declares they will be exiled beyond Damascus for their idolatry.

6.summary: Amos pronounces woe upon those in Zion and Samaria who live in luxury and false security, ignoring the coming day of judgment. He describes their feasts, beds of ivory, and songs, then declares that God abhors their pride and will deliver them into exile, with a vivid depiction of a house struck by disaster and the remnant fleeing.

segments.title: Woe to the Complacent
segments.gist: Amos warns the wealthy leaders of Zion and Samaria who feel secure and oppress the poor, asking if they are better than other nations.

segments.title: Luxury and Coming Exile
segments.gist: The prophet describes their lavish feasts, music, and anointing, then declares they will be the first to go into exile.

segments.title: God's Oath Against Pride
segments.gist: The Lord swears against Jacob's pride, will deliver up the city, and a remnant will flee, with houses struck and destroyed.

segments.title: Futility of Justice and Coming Nation
segments.gist: Amos questions the perversion of justice, then declares God will raise a nation to oppress Israel from Hamath to the Arabah.

7.summary: Amos receives three visions of judgment: locusts, fire, and a plumbline, each showing God's impending punishment on Israel, with Amos interceding for the first two. The chapter ends with the priest Amaziah opposing Amos, accusing him of conspiracy and telling him to flee to Judah, to which Amos responds by asserting his divine call and pronouncing judgment on Amaziah and Israel.

segments.title: Vision of Locusts
segments.gist: God shows Amos a swarm of locusts devouring the land's crops; Amos pleads for forgiveness and God relents.

segments.title: Vision of Fire
segments.gist: God calls for a judgment by fire that consumes the deep and the land; Amos again intercedes, and God relents.

segments.title: Vision of the Plumbline
segments.gist: God shows Amos a plumbline and declares He will set it among Israel, no longer passing by them; the high places and sanctuaries will be destroyed.

segments.title: Amaziah Accuses Amos
segments.gist: The priest Amaziah sends word to King Jeroboam that Amos is conspiring against him and tells Amos to flee to Judah and prophesy there.

segments.title: Amos's Response and Judgment
segments.gist: Amos defends his prophetic call and pronounces judgment on Amaziah: his wife will be a harlot, his children slain, and Israel will be taken captive.

8.summary: Amos is shown a basket of summer fruit, and God declares that the end has come upon Israel. The chapter pronounces judgment on those who exploit the poor and long for the holy days to end so they can resume selling, and it foretells a famine of hearing the word of the Lord, with people fainting while seeking it.

segments.title: Vision of Summer Fruit
segments.gist: God shows Amos a basket of summer fruit and says the end has come upon Israel; He will not pass by them again.

segments.title: Judgment on Exploiters
segments.gist: Amos condemns those who swallow the needy and cheat with false balances and dishonest measures.

segments.title: Earth Trembles and Mourning
segments.gist: The Lord swears never to forget their works; the land will tremble, and songs will turn to wailing and mourning.

segments.title: Famine of the Word
segments.gist: A famine of hearing the Lord's word will come; people will wander seeking it and fall, and the young will faint for thirst.

9.summary: Amos's final chapter presents five visions of judgment: the LORD standing by the altar, the destruction of the sinful kingdom, the filtering of Israel among the nations, and the restoration of David's fallen tabernacle with future prosperity.

segments.title: Vision at the Altar
segments.gist: The LORD stands by the altar, commanding destruction from top to bottom, with no escape for the wicked.

segments.title: Hymn to the Sovereign LORD
segments.gist: A doxology praises God who melts the earth, builds His chambers in the heavens, and pours out waters.

segments.title: Israel Judged Among Nations
segments.gist: The LORD declares Israel like the Ethiopians, yet He will sift them and slay the sinners who deny disaster.

segments.title: David's Tabernacle Restored
segments.gist: In that day God will raise up David's fallen tabernacle and rebuild it, so that Israel may possess Edom and all nations.

segments.title: Promise of Prosperity
segments.gist: The days come when harvest follows plowing, mountains drip wine, and God plants Israel in their land forever.

1.summary: Obadiah delivers a prophecy against Edom for its pride and its violence against Jacob in the day of Jerusalem's fall, declaring that Edom will be brought down and that the day of the LORD is near for all nations. The book closes with the promise that mount Zion will be delivered and the kingdom shall be the LORD's.

segments.title: Judgment on Edom's Pride
segments.gist: The LORD declares judgment on Edom for its pride and false security, promising to bring it down despite its lofty dwelling.

segments.title: Edom's Violence Against Jacob
segments.gist: Edom is condemned for standing aloof and participating in the plunder and slaughter of Jerusalem's people.

segments.title: Day of the LORD for All Nations
segments.gist: The day of the LORD is near for all nations, and as Edom has done, so it shall be done to it.

segments.title: Deliverance and the LORD's Kingdom
segments.gist: Mount Zion shall be delivered and become holy, and the kingdom shall be the LORD's.

1.summary: God commands Jonah to preach against Nineveh, but Jonah flees by ship toward Tarshish. A violent storm threatens the ship, and after casting lots the sailors throw Jonah overboard; the sea calms, and a great fish swallows Jonah.

segments.title: Jonah Flees from God
segments.gist: God tells Jonah to cry against Nineveh, but Jonah rises to flee to Tarshish, going down to Joppa and boarding a ship.

segments.title: Storm and Sailors' Fear
segments.gist: God sends a great wind and a mighty tempest; the sailors fear and cry to their gods while Jonah sleeps below deck.

segments.title: Lots Expose Jonah
segments.gist: The sailors cast lots, the lot falls on Jonah, and he confesses he is a Hebrew fleeing from the Lord, causing the men to fear greatly.

segments.title: Jonah Cast into the Sea
segments.gist: Jonah tells the sailors to throw him overboard to calm the sea; after trying to row to land, they do so, the sea calms, and the men fear the Lord.

2.summary: From inside the fish, Jonah prays to the LORD, describing his descent into the deep and his cry for help, and ends by acknowledging that salvation belongs to the LORD. The LORD then speaks to the fish, which vomits Jonah onto dry land.

segments.title: Distress and Descent Recounted
segments.gist: Jonah describes crying out in distress, being cast into the deep, and feeling cut off from God's sight.

segments.title: Fainting Yet Remembering the LORD
segments.gist: Jonah recalls fainting but remembering the LORD, and contrasts those who forsake mercy with his own sacrifice and vow.

3.summary: God sends Jonah a second time to Nineveh, and Jonah obeys, proclaiming that the city will be overthrown in forty days. The people of Nineveh believe God, proclaim a fast, and put on sackcloth, and the king issues a decree calling everyone to turn from evil. God sees their repentance and relents from the disaster he had threatened.

segments.title: Jonah Preaches in Nineveh
segments.gist: God commands Jonah to go to Nineveh and preach; Jonah obeys and declares the city will be overthrown in forty days.

segments.title: Nineveh Repents and King Decrees Fast
segments.gist: The people believe God, fast, and wear sackcloth; the king issues a decree for all to turn from evil.

4.summary: Jonah is furious that God spared Nineveh after his warning, and he complains that God's mercy is why he fled in the first place. He leaves the city, builds a booth, and God teaches him a lesson through a gourd that grows and then withers, ending with God's question about pity for Nineveh.

segments.title: Jonah's anger at mercy
segments.gist: Jonah is greatly displeased and angry that Nineveh is spared, and prays to God citing his flight as proof of God's graciousness.

segments.title: The gourd and the worm
segments.gist: God prepares a gourd to shade Jonah, then a worm to wither it, and Jonah faints and wishes to die.

segments.title: God's lesson about pity
segments.gist: God questions Jonah about his anger over the gourd, then contrasts Jonah's pity for a plant with God's concern for Nineveh's people and cattle.

1.summary: Micah opens with a prophetic summons to all nations to hear the LORD's case against Israel and Judah. He announces judgment on Samaria for idolatry and then laments the coming invasion that will reach even Jerusalem, calling the people to mourn.

segments.title: The LORD's summons to all peoples
segments.gist: Micah calls all nations to hear the LORD's witness against them as He comes from His holy temple in judgment.

segments.title: Judgment on Samaria for idolatry
segments.gist: The LORD declares Samaria's sins and promises to destroy the city, its idols, and its wealth.

segments.title: Micah laments the coming invasion
segments.gist: Micah mourns and warns the cities of Judah that invasion will reach Jerusalem, calling them to mourn and prepare for exile.

2.summary: Micah pronounces woe on those who devise iniquity and covet fields and houses, taking them by violence. He declares that God will bring disaster upon them, and the people will taunt them with a lament. The chapter condemns false prophets who preach peace for gain, and it ends with a promise that God will gather the remnant of Israel like sheep in a fold.

segments.title: Woe to Oppressors
segments.gist: Micah denounces those who plot evil and seize fields and houses, and announces God's judgment upon them.

segments.title: False Prophets Rebuked
segments.gist: The people reject true prophecy, and Micah condemns prophets who preach peace for reward while opposing those who do not feed them.

segments.title: Remnant Gathered
segments.gist: God promises to gather the remnant of Israel like sheep in a fold, with their king leading them.

3.summary: Micah addresses the leaders and prophets of Israel and Judah, condemning their injustice, greed, and false assurances. He declares that because they have abused their power and misled the people, Zion will be plowed like a field and the temple mount become a wooded hill.

segments.title: Judgment on unjust rulers
segments.gist: Micah indicts the heads of Jacob who hate good and love evil, devouring the people like flesh, and warns that God will not answer them in their distress.

segments.title: Prophets who mislead
segments.gist: Micah condemns prophets who cry peace for gain and declare war on those who do not feed them, contrasting them with his own empowerment by the Spirit to declare Jacob's transgression.

segments.title: Zion to be plowed
segments.gist: Because rulers judge for bribes, priests teach for hire, and prophets divine for money while claiming the Lord's support, Micah declares that Zion will be plowed as a field and the mountain of the house become high places of a forest.

4.summary: Micah 4 describes the future exaltation of Mount Zion as the house of the Lord, where many nations will gather to learn God's ways and swords will be beaten into plowshares. It contrasts this peace with the present suffering of Jerusalem, promising that the captive daughter of Zion will be rescued and that God will reign in Mount Zion forever.

segments.title: Mountain of the Lord Exalted
segments.gist: In the last days, the mountain of the Lord's house will be established, and many nations will flow to it to learn God's ways.

segments.title: Remnant Gathered to Zion
segments.gist: God will gather the afflicted and outcast remnant, and the kingdom will come to the daughter of Jerusalem.

segments.title: Travail and Captivity Foretold
segments.gist: The daughter of Zion will cry out in pain and go into captivity, but there the Lord will redeem her from enemies.

segments.title: Nations Gathered Against Zion
segments.gist: Many nations gather against Zion, but they do not know the Lord's plan to gather them like sheaves and thresh them.

5.summary: Micah foretells a ruler to come from Bethlehem, describes God's care for the remnant of Israel, and promises deliverance from Assyria and other enemies, ending with a declaration that God will execute vengeance on disobedient nations.

segments.title: Ruler from Bethlehem
segments.gist: A ruler from Bethlehem will shepherd Israel, and the people will be delivered from Assyria.

segments.title: Remnant Among Nations
segments.gist: The remnant of Jacob will be like dew and a lion among the nations, and enemies will be cut off.

segments.title: God's Vengeance on Nations
segments.gist: God will remove Israel's horses, cities, and idols, and will execute vengeance on disobedient nations.

6.summary: God brings a covenant lawsuit against Israel, recounting his saving acts and asking what offering could satisfy him, then declares what he requires: justice, mercy, and humble walking with God. The chapter denounces the city's dishonest commerce and violence, pronounces judgment on its wealth and idols, and ends with the land left desolate.

segments.title: God's Controversy with Israel
segments.gist: The Lord summons the mountains as witnesses and recounts his faithful acts from Egypt to Gilgal while Israel questions how God has wearied them.

segments.title: What the Lord Requires
segments.gist: The people ask what offerings would please God, from rams to firstborn sons, and the prophet answers: do justly, love mercy, and walk humbly with God.

segments.title: Dishonest Scales and Violence
segments.gist: The Lord cries out against the city's deceitful balances, false weights, rich men full of violence, and inhabitants who speak lies.

segments.title: Judgment on Wealth and Idols
segments.gist: Because of their sins, God will make them sick and desolate; their stored wealth will not save them, and they will bear the reproach of following Omri and Ahab's statutes.

7.summary: Micah laments the corruption and faithlessness of his people, resolving to wait on God for salvation. He expresses confidence that God will forgive, restore, and shepherd his remnant, ending with a hymn of praise to the God who delights in mercy.

segments.title: Micah Laments Widespread Corruption
segments.gist: Micah grieves that the godly have perished and everyone lies in wait for blood, with rulers and judges demanding bribes.

segments.title: Micah Waits for God's Salvation
segments.gist: Micah resolves to wait for God, trusting that though he falls he will rise, and his enemies will see God's vindication.

segments.title: Promise of Restoration and Desolation
segments.gist: God promises a day when walls will be rebuilt and people will come from afar, but the land will be desolate for its sins.

segments.title: Prayer for Shepherd's Care
segments.gist: Micah asks God to shepherd his people, and nations will see and be ashamed, licking the dust like a serpent.

segments.title: Hymn of Praise to Merciful God
segments.gist: Micah praises God, who forgives sin, delights in mercy, and will fulfill his promises to Jacob and Abraham.

1.summary: Nahum opens with an oracle describing the LORD as a jealous and avenging God, slow to anger but great in power, who controls the seas, mountains, and storms. He announces judgment on Nineveh and deliverance for Judah, declaring that the wicked will be cut off and the yoke broken.

segments.title: The LORD's Character Described
segments.gist: The LORD is jealous, avenging, slow to anger, great in power, and controls nature.

segments.title: The LORD is Good
segments.gist: The LORD is a stronghold in trouble and cares for those who trust Him.

segments.title: Judgment on Nineveh
segments.gist: The LORD will make an end of Nineveh's plots and cut off the wicked counselor.

segments.title: Deliverance for Judah
segments.gist: Though afflicted, Judah will be freed from Assyria's yoke, and Nineveh will be destroyed.

2.summary: Nahum describes the advance of an attacking army against Nineveh, the city's defenses failing and its people fleeing. The chapter ends with a taunt that Nineveh's destruction is final, with no one to comfort her.

segments.title: The attacker advances against Nineveh
segments.gist: A destroyer comes against Nineveh; the prophet describes the siege, the flashing weapons, and the rushing chariots.

segments.title: Nineveh's defenses collapse
segments.gist: The city's gates are opened, the palace is dissolved, and the people flee while the enemy plunders silver and gold.

segments.title: The lion's den is destroyed
segments.gist: Nahum taunts Nineveh as a lion's den that will be burned, and declares that God will end its prey and silence its messengers.

3.summary: Nahum pronounces woe on Nineveh, the bloody city, describing its violence, its coming shame, and the destruction of its fortresses and princes. The chapter ends with the nations rejoicing over Nineveh's fall, for its endless cruelty had touched everyone.

segments.title: Woe to the Bloody City
segments.gist: Nahum denounces Nineveh as a city of blood, lies, and endless prey, and declares God's judgment against it.

segments.title: No Escape from Judgment
segments.gist: Nineveh is compared to No, whose fall shows that its own strength and allies cannot save it.

segments.title: Siege and Devouring Locusts
segments.gist: The city is told to prepare for siege, but fire and sword will consume it like devouring locusts.

segments.title: Kings and People Scattered
segments.gist: Nineveh's rulers and people are scattered, and its wound is incurable; all who hear rejoice.

1.summary: Habakkuk complains to God about the violence and injustice in Judah, and God answers by raising up the Chaldeans as his instrument of judgment. Habakkuk then protests that the Chaldeans, who are even more wicked, seem to be allowed to swallow up the righteous without restraint.

segments.title: Habakkuk's Complaint
segments.gist: Habakkuk cries out to God about violence, iniquity, and strife in the land, asking why God tolerates wrongdoing.

segments.title: God's Answer: The Chaldeans
segments.gist: God tells Habakkuk to look at the nations and be amazed, for he is raising up the bitter and hasty Chaldeans to conquer and take captives.

segments.title: Habakkuk's Second Complaint
segments.gist: Habakkuk questions why God, who is of purer eyes than to behold evil, allows the treacherous Chaldeans to swallow up the righteous like fish in a net.

2.summary: Habakkuk waits for God's answer to his complaint, and God replies that the vision will surely come at its appointed time and that the proud will fail while the just shall live by faith. God then pronounces five woes against the arrogant Chaldean oppressor—for plundering nations, heaping up unjust gain, building cities by bloodshed, and idolatry—declaring that the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the Lord's glory.

segments.title: Habakkuk Waits for God's Answer
segments.gist: Habakkuk stations himself on the watchtower to see what God will say, and God tells him to write the vision plainly because it will surely come at the appointed time.

segments.title: First Woe: Plundering Nations
segments.gist: God pronounces woe on the proud Chaldean who heaps up what is not his and plunders many nations, who will themselves become plunder.

segments.title: Second Woe: Unjust Gain
segments.gist: Woe to him who builds his house by unjust gain to set his nest on high, for the stone and beam of his house will cry out against him.

segments.title: Third Woe: Cities Built by Blood
segments.gist: Woe to him who builds a town with bloodshed, for the Lord's glory will fill the earth as the waters cover the sea.

segments.title: Fourth Woe: Drunken Shame
segments.gist: Woe to him who makes his neighbor drunk to expose his shame, for the cup of the Lord's right hand will turn against him and cover him with disgrace.

segments.title: Fifth Woe: Idols Are Silent
segments.gist: Woe to him who trusts in dumb idols that cannot speak, for the Lord is in his holy temple and all the earth should keep silence before him.

3.summary: Habakkuk prays for God to revive His work and recalls the LORD's mighty deliverance of Israel from Egypt and His conquest of the nations, ending with a confession of trust and joy in God despite total agricultural ruin.

segments.title: Habakkuk's Prayer for Revival
segments.gist: Habakkuk asks God to revive His work in the midst of the years and to remember mercy in wrath.

segments.title: The LORD's Coming from Teman
segments.gist: God comes from Teman and Paran, His glory covers the heavens, and pestilence and mountains yield before Him.

segments.title: The LORD's Chariots and Arrows
segments.gist: The LORD rides upon horses and chariots of salvation, His arrows and spear divide the earth and sun stand still.

segments.title: The LORD's Deliverance of His People
segments.gist: The LORD goes forth for the salvation of His people, striking the head of the wicked and dividing the sea.

segments.title: Joy in God Despite Ruin
segments.gist: Though the fig tree and crops fail, Habakkuk rejoices in the LORD and trusts Him for strength and sure footing.

1.summary: Zephaniah opens with a sweeping announcement of judgment: God will utterly consume all things from the land, cutting off idolatrous priests and those who have turned from Him. The day of the LORD is described as a day of wrath, distress, and darkness, a swift destruction that will come upon Judah and Jerusalem because of their sins.

segments.title: Universal Judgment Declared
segments.gist: God declares He will utterly consume all things from the land, including people, beasts, and idols, and will cut off those who worship the host of heaven and turn from Him.

segments.title: Day of the LORD's Sacrifice
segments.gist: The day of the LORD is near; God prepares a sacrifice and punishes princes, those wearing foreign apparel, and those who leap over the threshold, while searching Jerusalem with lamps.

segments.title: Great Day of Wrath
segments.gist: The great day of the LORD is described as a day of wrath, trouble, distress, darkness, and desolation, when neither silver nor gold can deliver people from God's fierce anger.

2.summary: Zephaniah calls the humble of the land to seek the LORD before judgment falls, then pronounces oracles against surrounding nations—Philistia, Moab, Ammon, Cush, and Assyria—declaring that their lands will be desolated and the remnant of Judah will possess them.

segments.title: Call to Seek the LORD
segments.gist: The nation is urged to gather and seek the LORD before the day of judgment comes.

segments.title: Judgment on Philistia
segments.gist: Gaza, Ashkelon, Ashdod, and Ekron are doomed; the coastland will become pasture for Judah's remnant.

segments.title: Judgment on Moab and Ammon
segments.gist: Moab and Ammon are condemned for taunting Judah; their lands will become like Sodom and Gomorrah.

segments.title: Judgment on Assyria and Nineveh
segments.gist: The LORD will stretch out his hand against the north, making Nineveh a desolate waste and a mockery.

3.summary: Zephaniah pronounces woe on Jerusalem for its corrupt leaders and prophets, then promises a purified remnant and the LORD's presence among them. The chapter closes with a call to rejoice because God will gather the outcast and restore his people.

segments.title: Woe to rebellious Jerusalem
segments.gist: Jerusalem is condemned for not obeying the LORD, with its princes, prophets, and priests described as corrupt and unjust.

segments.title: Promise of a purified remnant
segments.gist: The LORD will gather the nations, purify the speech of the peoples, and leave a humble remnant who trust in his name.

segments.title: Call to rejoice in restoration
segments.gist: Zion is told to sing because the LORD has taken away judgment and will gather the outcast and make them praised.

1.summary: In the second year of Darius, the LORD rebukes the returned exiles through Haggai for living in paneled houses while His temple lies in ruins, and He sends drought and scarcity as a consequence. The people obey, and the LORD stirs up Zerubbabel, Joshua, and the remnant to begin rebuilding the temple.

segments.title: Rebuke for Neglecting the Temple
segments.gist: The LORD challenges the people for saying the time has not come to rebuild His house while they dwell in paneled houses.

segments.title: Consider Your Ways
segments.gist: The LORD calls the people to consider their ways: they sow much but bring in little, and earn wages to put into a bag with holes.

segments.title: Command to Rebuild the Temple
segments.gist: The LORD tells them to go up to the mountain, bring wood, and build the house, promising to take pleasure in it and be glorified.

segments.title: Drought as Consequence
segments.gist: Because they run to their own houses while the temple lies waste, the LORD calls for a drought upon the land and its produce.

segments.title: People Obey and Begin Work
segments.gist: Zerubbabel, Joshua, and all the remnant obey the LORD's voice, and the LORD stirs their spirits to begin work on the temple.

2.summary: Haggai addresses the people's discouragement over the modest new temple, promising God's Spirit and future glory greater than the former. He then answers the priests about ritual holiness and defilement to show the people's uncleanness, but declares blessing from the day the foundation was laid. The chapter closes with a promise to Zerubbabel that God will overthrow the nations and make him a signet ring.

segments.title: Encouragement for the Temple
segments.gist: God asks who remembers the former temple's glory, tells the people to be strong, and promises His Spirit and greater glory for the new house.

segments.title: Priests Question Holiness
segments.gist: Haggai asks the priests whether holy meat makes other food holy and whether a dead body defiles; they answer no and yes, and he applies it to the people's uncleanness.

segments.title: Blessing from Foundation Day
segments.gist: God tells the people to consider the time before the temple's foundation was laid, when harvests failed, and promises blessing from this day forward.

segments.title: Promise to Zerubbabel
segments.gist: God speaks a second time to Haggai, promising to shake the nations and make Zerubbabel a signet ring, His chosen servant.

1.summary: Zechariah opens with a call for Judah to return to the LORD, followed by a night vision of a horseman among myrtle trees reporting that the earth is at rest. After the angel intercedes for Jerusalem, Zechariah sees four horns that scattered Judah and four craftsmen who come to terrify them.

segments.title: Call to Return
segments.gist: The LORD calls Israel to return to Him and warns them not to repeat their fathers' disobedience.

segments.title: Horseman Among Myrtles
segments.gist: Zechariah sees a man on a red horse among myrtle trees with other horses, who report the earth is at rest.

segments.title: Intercession and Promise
segments.gist: The angel asks how long the LORD will withhold mercy from Jerusalem, and the LORD answers with comforting promises of restoration.

segments.title: Four Horns and Craftsmen
segments.gist: Zechariah sees four horns that scattered Judah and four craftsmen who come to terrify and cast down those horns.

2.summary: Zechariah's third vision shows a young man measuring Jerusalem, with an angel declaring the city will overflow with people and God will be a wall of fire around it. The LORD calls the exiles to flee Babylon and promises to dwell among them, and the chapter closes with a summons for all flesh to be silent before the LORD, who has roused himself from his holy habitation.

segments.title: Man with a measuring line
segments.gist: Zechariah sees a man with a measuring line going to measure Jerusalem, and an angel goes to meet him.

segments.title: Jerusalem will overflow
segments.gist: An angel tells the first angel that Jerusalem will be inhabited as villages without walls because of the multitude of people and cattle, and the LORD will be a wall of fire around it.

segments.title: Flee from Babylon
segments.gist: The LORD calls the exiles to flee from the land of the north and from Babylon, promising to dwell among them and that many nations will join the LORD.

3.summary: In a vision, Zechariah sees Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the LORD with Satan accusing him; the LORD rebukes Satan and has Joshua's filthy garments replaced with clean ones. The LORD then charges Joshua to walk in His ways and promises the coming Branch, with the removal of iniquity and the stone with seven eyes.

segments.title: Joshua and the Accuser
segments.gist: Zechariah sees Joshua the high priest before the angel of the LORD, with Satan standing at his right hand to resist him.

segments.title: Filthy Garments Replaced
segments.gist: The LORD rebukes Satan, orders Joshua's filthy garments removed, and clothes him with clean garments and a fair mitre.

segments.title: Charge to Joshua
segments.gist: The angel of the LORD charges Joshua: if he walks in God's ways and keeps His charge, he will judge God's house and have access among those standing by.

segments.title: Promise of the Branch
segments.gist: The LORD promises to bring forth His servant the Branch, remove iniquity in one day, and set a stone with seven eyes, with everyone inviting his neighbor under vine and fig tree.

4.summary: Zechariah receives a vision of a golden lampstand with seven lamps and two olive trees beside it, and the interpreting angel explains that the work will be accomplished not by might but by God's Spirit. The angel assures Zerubbabel that he will complete the temple, and the chapter closes with the promise that the two anointed ones stand by the Lord of all the earth.

segments.title: Vision of the Lampstand
segments.gist: The angel wakes Zechariah and shows him a golden lampstand with seven lamps and two olive trees beside it, and Zechariah asks what it means.

segments.title: Not by Might
segments.gist: The angel explains that the work is done not by might or power but by God's Spirit, and that Zerubbabel will level the mountain and bring forth the headstone.

segments.title: Zerubbabel to Finish the Temple
segments.gist: The word of the Lord says that Zerubbabel's hands laid the foundation and will finish the house, and that the seven eyes of the Lord rejoice to see the plumbline in his hand.

segments.title: The Two Olive Trees
segments.gist: Zechariah asks about the two olive trees and the two branches, and the angel says they are the two anointed ones who stand by the Lord of all the earth.

5.summary: Zechariah's sixth vision shows a flying scroll that brings a curse on thieves and perjurers, followed by a seventh vision of a woman named Wickedness sealed in an ephah basket and carried by two women with stork wings to Shinar, where a house is built for it.

segments.title: The Flying Scroll
segments.gist: Zechariah sees a flying scroll twenty cubits by ten, which the angel says is the curse going over the whole earth against thieves and false swearers.

segments.title: The Ephah and the Woman
segments.gist: The angel shows Zechariah an ephah basket, and a woman named Wickedness is cast into it and covered with a lead weight.

segments.title: Wickedness Carried to Shinar
segments.gist: Two women with stork wings lift the ephah and carry it to the land of Shinar, where a house is built and the basket set on its base.

6.summary: Zechariah sees a vision of four chariots emerging from between two bronze mountains, representing the four spirits of heaven going out to patrol the earth. The word of the Lord then commands him to take silver and gold from the exiles and make crowns for Joshua the high priest, symbolizing the Branch who will build the temple and sit as priest on his throne. The chapter closes with a promise that those far off will help build the temple.

segments.title: Vision of Four Chariots
segments.gist: Zechariah sees four chariots with horses of different colors coming from between two bronze mountains, and the angel explains they are the four spirits of heaven going to patrol the earth.

segments.title: Command to Make Crowns
segments.gist: The Lord tells Zechariah to take silver and gold from Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah who came from Babylon, and to make crowns and set them on Joshua the high priest.

segments.title: Prophecy of the Branch
segments.gist: The Lord declares that the man called the Branch will build the temple, bear the glory, and sit as a priest on his throne, with a counsel of peace between the two offices.

segments.title: Crowns as a Memorial
segments.gist: The crowns are to be a memorial in the temple for Heldai, Tobijah, Jedaiah, and Josiah son of Zephaniah, and those far off will come to build the temple, confirming that the Lord has sent Zechariah.

7.summary: In the fourth year of King Darius, the people of Bethel send men to ask the priests and prophets whether they should continue mourning and fasting in the fifth month, as they have done for years. The LORD answers through Zechariah, challenging whether their fasts were truly for him, and calls them to remember the words of the former prophets about justice, mercy, and care for the vulnerable, which their ancestors ignored, leading to exile.

segments.title: Bethelites ask about fasting
segments.gist: In the fourth year of Darius, Bethel sends Sharezer and Regemmelech to entreat the LORD's favor and ask the priests and prophets if they should continue mourning and fasting in the fifth month.

segments.title: The LORD challenges their motives
segments.gist: The LORD asks whether their seventy years of fasting was truly for him, and whether their eating and drinking was not for themselves.

segments.title: Call to justice and mercy
segments.gist: The LORD commands them to execute true judgment, show mercy and compassion, and not oppress widows, orphans, strangers, or the poor.

segments.title: Disobedience brought exile
segments.gist: Their ancestors refused to listen, so the LORD scattered them among nations and made the land desolate, because they did not heed the words of the former prophets.

8.summary: God promises through Zechariah to return to Zion and dwell in Jerusalem, restoring the city and its people. He declares a future of peace, truth, and blessing for the remnant of Judah, and answers a question about fasting by turning fast days into joyful feasts. The chapter ends with a vision of many nations seeking the Lord in Jerusalem.

segments.title: God's Zeal for Zion
segments.gist: God declares His return to Zion and promises to dwell in Jerusalem, restoring old men and children to its streets.

segments.title: Exhortation to Build
segments.gist: The people are urged to be strong and finish the temple, with promises of prosperity and blessing instead of curse.

segments.title: Promises of Peace and Truth
segments.gist: God promises to do good to Jerusalem and calls the people to speak truth and practice justice.

segments.title: Fasts Become Feasts
segments.gist: The fasts of the fourth, fifth, seventh, and tenth months will become times of joy and gladness for Judah.

segments.title: Nations Seek the Lord
segments.gist: Many peoples and strong nations will come to seek the Lord in Jerusalem, and ten men will grasp a Jew's garment.

9.summary: Zechariah delivers an oracle of judgment on surrounding nations and on Tyre and Ashkelon, then announces the coming of Zion's humble king riding on a donkey and the restoration of Israel as God's flock under his care.

segments.title: Judgment on surrounding nations
segments.gist: The LORD's word comes against Hadrach, Damascus, Hamath, Tyre, Sidon, and the Philistine cities, which will be humbled and incorporated into Israel.

segments.title: Zion's king comes riding a donkey
segments.gist: Zion is called to rejoice because her righteous, lowly king comes riding on a donkey, and his dominion will extend to the ends of the earth.

segments.title: Prisoners released from the pit
segments.gist: The LORD declares that because of the blood of the covenant he will free the prisoners from the waterless pit and calls them to return to their stronghold.

segments.title: Judah and Ephraim as God's weapons
segments.gist: The LORD will use Judah and Ephraim like a warrior's bow and sword against Greece, and he will protect and vindicate his people.

segments.title: The LORD saves his flock
segments.gist: The LORD will save his flock and they will shine like jewels in his land, with abundant grain and new wine for the young people.

10.summary: Zechariah calls on the people to ask the LORD for rain and exposes the false shepherds and idols that mislead them. The LORD promises to strengthen and restore Judah and Ephraim, gathering them from exile and making them mighty in battle under His care.

segments.title: Ask the LORD for Rain
segments.gist: The prophet urges the people to petition the LORD for spring rain, who gives showers and vegetation.

segments.title: Judah as a Battle Horse
segments.gist: The LORD's anger burns against false shepherds, and He makes Judah like a proud horse in battle.

segments.title: Strengthen Judah and Ephraim
segments.gist: The LORD promises to strengthen Judah and save Ephraim, bringing them back and causing them to rejoice.

segments.title: Gather Them from Exile
segments.gist: The LORD whistles for His people, gathers them from Egypt and Assyria, and brings them into Gilead and Lebanon.

segments.title: Victory Through the LORD
segments.gist: The LORD will pass through the sea and subdue nations, while His people walk in His name.

11.summary: Zechariah is told to shepherd a flock doomed for slaughter, portraying the rejection of God's shepherd. He breaks two staffs, Favor and Union, and the people value his wages at thirty pieces of silver, which he throws to the potter. The chapter then shifts to a foolish shepherd who will neglect and devour the flock.

segments.title: Command to shepherd doomed flock
segments.gist: The prophet is told to tend a flock marked for slaughter, whose owners kill them without guilt.

segments.title: Shepherd tends flock, removes three shepherds
segments.gist: The shepherd tends the flock and cuts off three shepherds in one month, but the flock detests him.

segments.title: Staff Favor broken
segments.gist: The shepherd breaks the staff called Favor, annulling the covenant with the peoples.

segments.title: Thirty pieces of silver and staff Union broken
segments.gist: The shepherd is paid thirty pieces of silver, throws them to the potter, and breaks the staff Union.

segments.title: Foolish shepherd raised up
segments.gist: God raises a foolish shepherd who will neglect the flock, and a woe is pronounced on him.

12.summary: This chapter begins with an oracle declaring God's future deliverance of Jerusalem, describing how He will make the city a cup of trembling and a burdensome stone for surrounding peoples and will destroy attacking nations. It then shifts to a promise of spiritual renewal: God will pour out a spirit of grace and supplication on the house of David and Jerusalem's inhabitants, and they will look upon Him whom they pierced and mourn bitterly, as for an only son, with families mourning separately.

segments.title: God's oracle and Jerusalem's defense
segments.gist: The LORD identifies Himself as creator and promises to make Jerusalem a cup of trembling and a burdensome stone for all surrounding peoples.

segments.title: Judah's leaders and Jerusalem's strength
segments.gist: God promises to strengthen the governors of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, making them like a firepot and a torch to devour enemies, and He will seek to destroy all nations that come against Jerusalem.

segments.title: Mourning for the pierced one
segments.gist: God will pour out a spirit of grace and supplication, and the people will look on Him whom they pierced and mourn with great bitterness, each family mourning separately.

13.summary: Zechariah 13 describes a future cleansing from sin and idolatry, the striking of the shepherd and the scattering of the sheep, and the refining of a remnant who will call on the Lord's name.

segments.title: Cleansing from sin and idols
segments.gist: A fountain will cleanse from sin, and idols and false prophets will be removed from the land.

segments.title: False prophets rejected
segments.gist: False prophets will be disowned by family and ashamed of their visions, no longer wearing prophetic garb.

segments.title: Shepherd struck, remnant refined
segments.gist: The shepherd is struck and the sheep scattered; two-thirds are cut off, but the remaining third is refined and called God's people.

14.summary: Zechariah describes a future day when Jerusalem is attacked and plundered, but the Lord intervenes, stands on the Mount of Olives, and brings deliverance. The chapter then portrays the Lord as king over all the earth, with living waters flowing from Jerusalem, and calls for the nations to worship him or face judgment.

segments.title: Jerusalem Attacked, Lord Delivers
