segments.gist: The city is taken and spoiled, but the Lord goes forth to fight against the nations and stands on the Mount of Olives.

segments.title: Living Waters and Universal Reign
segments.gist: In that day living waters flow from Jerusalem, the Lord is king over all the earth, and the land is safely inhabited.

segments.title: Plague on Jerusalem's Enemies
segments.gist: The Lord strikes the peoples who fought against Jerusalem with a consuming plague and confusion, and Judah also fights.

segments.title: Nations Required to Worship
segments.gist: The survivors among the nations must go up to worship the King in Jerusalem; those who refuse receive no rain and are plagued.

segments.title: Holiness to the Lord
segments.gist: In that day even the bells on horses and common pots are holy to the Lord, and no Canaanite remains in the house of the Lord.

1.summary: God declares His love for Israel, contrasting it with His rejection of Esau, and rebukes the priests for offering polluted sacrifices and despising His name, warning that His name will be great among the Gentiles.

segments.title: God's Love for Jacob
segments.gist: God asserts His love for Israel, contrasting Jacob and Esau and promising judgment on Edom.

segments.title: Priests Despise God's Name
segments.gist: God challenges the priests who despise His name by offering polluted bread and blind animals.

segments.title: Cursed Deceitful Offerings
segments.gist: God rejects their offerings and curses those who vow and sacrifice blemished animals, for His name is great among the Gentiles.

2.summary: God rebukes the priests for failing to honor Him and for corrupting the covenant of Levi, then condemns Judah's treachery against the wife of their youth and their weariness with God's standards.

segments.title: Rebuke to the priests
segments.gist: God addresses the priests, warning that if they do not honor Him, He will curse their blessings.

segments.title: Covenant with Levi
segments.gist: God recalls His covenant of life and peace with Levi, contrasting the faithful priest with the corrupt priests who have caused many to stumble.

segments.title: Judah's treachery
segments.gist: Judah is accused of breaking faith with one another and profaning the covenant of their fathers by marrying foreign women.

segments.title: Treachery against wives
segments.gist: The Lord rejects the offerings of those who deal treacherously with the wife of their youth, whom He made one with them.

3.summary: God announces that he will send a messenger to prepare the way, then suddenly come to his temple to purify the sons of Levi and judge the wicked. The people are accused of robbing God in tithes and offerings, and are challenged to bring the full tithe so that blessings may follow. A remnant who fear the Lord are written in a book of remembrance, and the chapter closes with a promise that the day of the Lord will distinguish the righteous from the wicked.

segments.title: Messenger and Refiner's Fire
segments.gist: God promises to send a messenger to prepare the way, and the Lord will suddenly come to his temple to purify the sons of Levi like a refiner's fire.

segments.title: Robbing God in Tithes
segments.gist: The people are accused of robbing God in tithes and offerings and are challenged to bring the full tithe so that God may open the windows of heaven and rebuke the devourer.

segments.title: Stout Words Against God
segments.gist: The people speak stout words against God, saying it is vain to serve him and that the proud are called happy while evildoers prosper.

segments.title: Book of Remembrance
segments.gist: Those who fear the Lord speak often to one another, and a book of remembrance is written for them; God promises to spare them as a man spares his own son.

4.summary: Malachi describes the coming day of judgment as a burning furnace that will consume the proud and wicked, while the sun of righteousness will bring healing to those who fear God's name. The prophet calls Israel to remember the law of Moses and promises to send Elijah the prophet before the great and dreadful day of the LORD to turn hearts and avert a curse.

segments.title: The Day of Judgment
segments.gist: The proud and wicked will be burned like stubble, but those who fear God's name will be healed under the sun of righteousness.

segments.title: Elijah's Coming
segments.gist: God promises to send Elijah before the great day of the LORD to turn hearts and prevent the land from being cursed.

1.summary: Matthew opens with the genealogy of Jesus from Abraham through Joseph, then recounts how Joseph, a righteous man, plans to divorce Mary quietly after learning she is pregnant, but an angel in a dream tells him the child is from the Holy Spirit and will save his people. Joseph obeys, takes Mary as his wife, and names the child Jesus, fulfilling the prophecy of Immanuel.

segments.title: Genealogy from Abraham to Joseph
segments.gist: Matthew lists Jesus' ancestry from Abraham through David to the Babylonian exile and down to Joseph, Mary's husband.

segments.title: Joseph's dilemma over Mary's pregnancy
segments.gist: Mary is found pregnant before marriage, and Joseph, a just man, plans to divorce her quietly to avoid public shame.

segments.title: Angel reassures Joseph in a dream
segments.gist: An angel tells Joseph not to fear taking Mary as his wife, for the child is from the Holy Spirit and will save his people.

segments.title: Prophecy of Immanuel fulfilled
segments.gist: Matthew cites the prophet Isaiah: a virgin will bear a son called Immanuel, meaning God with us.

segments.title: Joseph obeys and names Jesus
segments.gist: Joseph wakes, takes Mary as his wife, keeps her a virgin until the birth, and names the child Jesus.

2.summary: Wise men from the east follow a star to Jerusalem and Bethlehem, worship the young child Jesus, and give him gold, frankincense, and myrrh, while warning Joseph in a dream to flee to Egypt to escape Herod's slaughter of the infants in Bethlehem. After Herod's death, Joseph brings his family back and settles in Nazareth.

segments.title: Wise men arrive in Jerusalem
segments.gist: Wise men from the east come to Jerusalem asking where the King of the Jews is born, having seen his star.

segments.title: Herod sends them to Bethlehem
segments.gist: Herod and Jerusalem are troubled; he learns from priests and scribes that Bethlehem is the prophesied place and sends the wise men to find the child.

segments.title: Wise men worship and give gifts
segments.gist: The star leads the wise men to the house, where they worship the young child and offer gold, frankincense, and myrrh, then depart warned in a dream.

segments.title: Joseph flees to Egypt
segments.gist: An angel warns Joseph in a dream to take Mary and Jesus to Egypt, fulfilling the prophecy out of Egypt.

segments.title: Herod kills the infants
segments.gist: Herod, realizing he was mocked, orders the slaughter of all boys two years old and under in Bethlehem, fulfilling Jeremiah's prophecy.

segments.title: Return and settle in Nazareth
segments.gist: After Herod's death, Joseph is told to return, but fearing Herod's son he settles in Nazareth, fulfilling the prophecy that Jesus would be called a Nazarene.

3.summary: John the Baptist preaches repentance in the wilderness of Judaea, baptizing people in the Jordan and confronting the Pharisees and Sadducees. He announces that one mightier than he will come to baptize with the Holy Ghost and with fire. Jesus comes from Galilee to be baptized by John; after the Spirit descends like a dove and a voice from heaven declares him the beloved Son.

segments.title: John Preaches in the Wilderness
segments.gist: John the Baptist appears in the wilderness of Judaea, preaching repentance and baptizing in the river Jordan as people from Jerusalem and all Judaea come to him.

segments.title: John Rebukes Pharisees and Sadducees
segments.gist: John confronts Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his baptism, calling them a generation of vipers and urging them to bring fruits meet for repentance.

segments.title: John Announces the Mightier One
segments.gist: John declares that one mightier than he will come, baptizing with the Holy Ghost and with fire, with his fan in his hand to purge the floor.

segments.title: Jesus Is Baptized by John
segments.gist: Jesus comes from Galilee to the Jordan to be baptized by John; after his baptism the Spirit of God descends like a dove and a voice from heaven calls him the beloved Son.

4.summary: After his baptism, Jesus is led into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil, who challenges him three times and is refused with scripture. Jesus then begins his ministry in Galilee, calls Peter, Andrew, James, and John to follow him, and travels through the region teaching, preaching, and healing all kinds of diseases among the people.

segments.title: Temptation in the Wilderness
segments.gist: Jesus fasts forty days, is tempted three times by the devil, answers each with scripture, and angels minister to him.

segments.title: Jesus Begins Ministry in Galilee
segments.gist: Jesus withdraws to Galilee, dwells in Capernaum, and from that time preaches repentance because the kingdom of heaven is at hand.

segments.title: Calling of Four Fishermen
segments.gist: Jesus calls Peter and Andrew, then James and John, to follow him, and they immediately leave their nets and boat.

segments.title: Healing and Great Fame
segments.gist: Jesus travels through Galilee teaching and healing every disease, and great multitudes from many regions follow him.

5.summary: Jesus opens the Sermon on the Mount by pronouncing blessings on the poor in spirit, the meek, the merciful, and the persecuted, then calls his disciples salt and light. He insists he came to fulfill the law, and sets a higher standard for anger, lust, divorce, oaths, retaliation, and love of enemies, ending with the call to be perfect as the Father is perfect.

segments.title: Beatitudes and salt and light
segments.gist: Jesus blesses the humble, mourning, meek, hungry, merciful, pure, peacemakers, and persecuted, then calls his followers salt and light.

segments.title: Salt and light
segments.gist: Jesus tells his disciples they are the salt of the earth and the light of the world, urging good works that glorify the Father.

segments.title: Fulfilling the law
segments.gist: Jesus says he came not to destroy the law but to fulfill it, and warns that righteousness must exceed that of the scribes and Pharisees.

segments.title: Teaching on anger
segments.gist: Jesus equates anger and insults with judgment, urging reconciliation with an adversary quickly before it is too late.

segments.title: Teaching on lust
segments.gist: Jesus says looking at a woman with lust is adultery in the heart, and advises drastic measures to avoid sin.

segments.title: Teaching on divorce
segments.gist: Jesus permits divorce only for fornication, and says marrying a divorced woman commits adultery.

segments.title: Teaching on oaths
segments.gist: Jesus forbids swearing oaths by heaven, earth, or one's head, and says let your yes be yes and no be no.

segments.title: Teaching on retaliation
segments.gist: Jesus tells his followers not to resist evil, but to turn the other cheek, give the cloak, go the second mile, and lend without refusal.

segments.title: Teaching on love of enemies
segments.gist: Jesus commands love for enemies and prayer for persecutors, so as to be children of the Father, and calls for perfection.

6.summary: Jesus continues the Sermon on the Mount, teaching about genuine piety: giving alms, prayer (including the Lord's Prayer), and fasting done secretly before God rather than for human praise. He then warns against storing earthly treasure, calls for wholehearted devotion to God over money, and urges trust in God's provision instead of anxious worry.

segments.title: Secret Almsgiving
segments.gist: Jesus warns against doing righteousness for show and instructs giving alms secretly, with God rewarding what is done in secret.

segments.title: Secret Prayer
segments.gist: Jesus contrasts hypocritical public prayer with private prayer to the Father, who sees in secret.

segments.title: The Lord's Prayer and Forgiveness
segments.gist: Jesus gives a model prayer and emphasizes that forgiving others is tied to receiving God's forgiveness.

segments.title: Secret Fasting
segments.gist: Jesus instructs fasting without outward display, so that only the Father who sees in secret knows.

segments.title: Treasure and Single Devotion
segments.gist: Jesus urges storing treasure in heaven, warns that the eye affects the whole body, and says no one can serve both God and money.

segments.title: Do Not Worry
segments.gist: Jesus tells his followers not to be anxious about food, drink, or clothing, pointing to God's care for birds and lilies and urging seeking God's kingdom first.

7.summary: Jesus concludes the Sermon on the Mount with a series of teachings: judging others, persistence in prayer, the golden rule, the narrow gate, false prophets, and the importance of doing God's will. He ends with the parable of the wise and foolish builders, contrasting those who hear and obey His words with those who do not.

segments.title: Judging Others and Helping Brothers
segments.gist: Jesus warns against hypocritical judgment and encourages helping others after removing one's own faults.

segments.title: Ask, Seek, Knock
segments.gist: Jesus teaches persistence in prayer and the golden rule, emphasizing God's willingness to give good gifts.

segments.title: The Narrow Gate
segments.gist: Jesus urges entering through the narrow gate that leads to life, contrasting it with the broad way to destruction.

segments.title: Warning Against False Prophets
segments.gist: Jesus warns about false prophets, saying they are known by their fruits, and that not all who call Him Lord will enter the kingdom.

segments.title: Parable of the Two Builders
segments.gist: Jesus compares those who hear and obey His words to a wise builder on rock, and those who do not to a foolish builder on sand.

segments.title: Response of the Crowds
segments.gist: The crowds are astonished at Jesus' teaching because He speaks with authority, unlike the scribes.

8.summary: Matthew 8 presents a series of miracles and encounters that demonstrate Jesus' authority: he cleanses a leper, heals a centurion's servant and Peter's mother-in-law, calms a storm, casts out demons, and forgives and heals a paralytic. The chapter also includes would-be followers and the healing of many at evening.

segments.title: Jesus Cleanses a Leper
segments.gist: A leper worships Jesus and is healed; Jesus tells him to show himself to the priest.

segments.title: Centurion's Servant Healed
segments.gist: A centurion asks Jesus to heal his paralyzed servant; Jesus marvels at his faith and heals the servant remotely.

segments.title: Peter's Mother-in-law and Many Healed
segments.gist: Jesus heals Peter's mother-in-law and many others, fulfilling Isaiah's prophecy.

segments.title: Two Would-Be Followers
segments.gist: Jesus speaks to a scribe and a disciple about the cost of following him.

segments.title: Storm Calmed
segments.gist: Jesus rebukes the winds and sea, calming a storm while his disciples marvel.

segments.title: Demons Cast into Pigs
segments.gist: Jesus casts demons out of two men into a herd of pigs, and the townspeople ask him to leave.

9.summary: Jesus forgives and heals a paralytic, calls Matthew from the tax booth, and defends his fellowship with sinners. He raises Jairus's daughter, heals a woman with an issue of blood, restores sight to two blind men, casts out a demon, and moves through the cities teaching and healing, moved with compassion for the crowds.

segments.title: Healing and forgiving the paralytic
segments.gist: Jesus tells a paralytic his sins are forgiven, answers scribes who call it blasphemy, and heals him to prove his authority.

segments.title: Call of Matthew and defense
segments.gist: Jesus calls Matthew from the tax booth, dines with sinners, and tells Pharisees he came to call sinners, not the righteous.

segments.title: Question about fasting
segments.gist: John's disciples ask why Jesus's disciples do not fast; he answers with bridegroom, cloth, and wineskin parables.

segments.title: Jairus's daughter and the woman
segments.gist: A ruler asks Jesus to raise his dead daughter; on the way a woman touches his garment and is healed, then the girl is raised.

segments.title: Two blind men and a mute demoniac
segments.gist: Jesus heals two blind men who call him Son of David, then casts a demon out of a mute man, amazing the crowds.

segments.title: Compassion for the crowds
segments.gist: Jesus travels teaching and healing; seeing the scattered crowds, he tells his disciples to pray for laborers for the harvest.

10.summary: Jesus commissions his twelve apostles, giving them authority over unclean spirits and diseases and sending them to Israel with the message that the kingdom of heaven is at hand. He instructs them to rely on hospitality, warns of persecution and family division, and calls for fearless confession, ending with the promise of reward for those who receive his messengers.

segments.title: The Twelve Commissioned
segments.gist: Jesus gives the twelve apostles authority over unclean spirits and diseases and names them.

segments.title: Instructions for the Mission
segments.gist: Jesus sends the twelve to Israel, telling them to heal freely, rely on hospitality, and warn of judgment.

segments.title: Warning of Persecution
segments.gist: Jesus foretells arrests, trials, and family betrayal, urging endurance and caution.

segments.title: Fearless Confession
segments.gist: Jesus tells the disciples not to fear those who kill the body but to confess him before men.

segments.title: Division and Taking the Cross
segments.gist: Jesus says he brings a sword and division, and that whoever does not take up his cross is not worthy.

segments.title: Reward for Receiving Messengers
segments.gist: Jesus promises that those who receive his messengers and give even a cup of cold water will be rewarded.

11.summary: John the Baptist sends disciples to ask Jesus if he is the coming one; Jesus praises John and denounces the unrepentant cities. Jesus then thanks the Father for revealing truth to the simple and invites the weary to take his yoke.

segments.title: John's disciples question Jesus
segments.gist: John in prison sends disciples to ask if Jesus is the expected Messiah, and Jesus answers by pointing to his healing works.

segments.title: Jesus praises John the Baptist
segments.gist: Jesus tells the crowds that John is a prophet and more, the messenger preparing his way, and calls them to heed.

segments.title: Parable of children in the marketplace
segments.gist: Jesus compares his generation to children who reject both John's austerity and his own sociability, yet wisdom is justified by her deeds.

segments.title: Woes on unrepentant cities
segments.gist: Jesus denounces Chorazin, Bethsaida, and Capernaum for not repenting despite mighty works, saying Sodom will fare better.

segments.title: Jesus thanks the Father
segments.gist: Jesus prays, thanking the Father for hiding truth from the wise and revealing it to babes, and declares all things are given to him.

segments.title: Invitation to the weary
segments.gist: Jesus invites all who labor and are heavy laden to take his yoke and learn from him, promising rest.

12.summary: Jesus defends his disciples for plucking grain on the Sabbath and heals a man's withered hand, prompting the Pharisees to plot against him. He withdraws, heals many, and fulfills Isaiah's prophecy; he then casts out a demon and warns that blasphemy against the Holy Spirit is unforgivable, rebukes the demand for a sign, and teaches that the heart's overflow defiles a person. When told his mother and brothers are outside, he declares that whoever does the will of his Father is his true family.

segments.title: Sabbath grain and withered hand
segments.gist: Jesus defends his disciples for plucking grain on the Sabbath and heals a man's withered hand, angering the Pharisees.

segments.title: Withdrawal and Isaiah's prophecy
segments.gist: Jesus withdraws, heals many, and fulfills Isaiah's prophecy of the chosen servant who will not break a bruised reed.

segments.title: Blasphemy against the Holy Spirit
segments.gist: Jesus casts out a demon, refutes the Pharisees' charge of Beelzebub, and warns that blasphemy against the Holy Spirit is unforgivable.

segments.title: Sign of Jonah and empty house
segments.gist: Jesus rebukes the demand for a sign, promising only the sign of Jonah, and warns of the unclean spirit returning to an empty house.

segments.title: Jesus' true family
segments.gist: When told his mother and brothers are outside, Jesus declares that whoever does the will of his Father is his true family.

13.summary: Jesus teaches the crowds in parables about the kingdom of heaven, including the sower, the wheat and tares, the mustard seed, and the leaven. He explains why he speaks in parables and interprets the sower and the wheat and tares to his disciples. The chapter ends with his rejection at Nazareth.

segments.title: Parable of the Sower
segments.gist: Jesus tells of a sower whose seed falls on four types of ground, yielding different results.

segments.title: Why Jesus Speaks in Parables
segments.gist: Jesus explains to his disciples that parables reveal truth to some but hide it from others, fulfilling prophecy.

segments.title: Explanation of the Sower
segments.gist: Jesus interprets the parable: the seed is the word, and the soils represent different responses to it.

segments.title: Parable of Wheat and Tares
segments.gist: Jesus tells of a man who sows good seed, but an enemy sows tares; both grow until the harvest.

segments.title: Mustard Seed and Leaven
segments.gist: Jesus compares the kingdom to a mustard seed and leaven, both of which grow from small beginnings.

segments.title: Explanation of Wheat and Tares
segments.gist: Jesus explains that the good seed are the righteous and the tares are the wicked, separated at the end of the age.

segments.title: Parables of Hidden Treasure, Pearl, and Net
segments.gist: Jesus likens the kingdom to a hidden treasure, a costly pearl, and a net that gathers fish of every kind.

segments.title: Rejection at Nazareth
segments.gist: Jesus returns to his hometown, where the people take offense at him, and he does few miracles because of their unbelief.

14.summary: Herod hears of Jesus and fears he is John the Baptist risen from the dead, recalling how he had John beheaded. Jesus withdraws by ship, feeds five thousand men with five loaves and two fish, walks on the sea to his disciples, and heals the sick in Gennesaret.

segments.title: Herod Fears Jesus and Recalls John
segments.gist: Herod hears of Jesus' fame and fears he is John the Baptist risen; he recounts how he had John beheaded after a birthday feast.

segments.title: Feeding the Five Thousand
segments.gist: Jesus withdraws by ship, has compassion on the crowd, and feeds five thousand men with five loaves and two fish, leaving twelve baskets full.

segments.title: Jesus Walks on the Sea
segments.gist: Jesus walks on the sea to his disciples, Peter walks on the water and is saved from sinking, and the wind ceases when Jesus enters the ship.

segments.title: Healing in Gennesaret
segments.gist: Jesus and his disciples cross over to Gennesaret, where the sick are brought to him and healed by touching the hem of his garment.

15.summary: Pharisees and scribes from Jerusalem challenge Jesus over his disciples eating with unwashed hands; Jesus rebukes their tradition that nullifies God's commandment and teaches that defilement comes from the heart. He heals the Canaanite woman's daughter after her persistent faith, then feeds four thousand men with seven loaves and a few fish, and dismisses the crowd.

segments.title: Tradition versus commandment
segments.gist: Pharisees ask why disciples break tradition; Jesus cites Isaiah and the command to honor parents, accusing them of voiding God's word.

segments.title: What defiles a man
segments.gist: Jesus teaches the crowd that what enters the mouth does not defile, but what comes out of the heart does; he explains to Peter.

segments.title: Canaanite woman's faith
segments.gist: A Canaanite woman pleads for her daughter; after Jesus' silence and words about children's bread, her reply prompts him to heal her daughter.

segments.title: Feeding four thousand
segments.gist: Jesus heals many by the sea, has compassion on the crowd, multiplies seven loaves and a few fish, and sends them away.

16.summary: Pharisees and Sadducees demand a sign from heaven, but Jesus refuses and warns his disciples about their teaching. At Caesarea Philippi, Peter confesses Jesus as the Christ, and Jesus foretells his death and resurrection, rebuking Peter for opposing God's will. The chapter ends with Jesus' teaching on taking up one's cross and the promise that some will not taste death before seeing the Son of Man coming in his kingdom.

segments.title: Pharisees and Sadducees Demand a Sign
segments.gist: The Pharisees and Sadducees ask Jesus for a sign from heaven, but he refuses, calling them a wicked and adulterous generation that can discern the weather but not the times.

segments.title: Jesus Warns of Leaven
segments.gist: Jesus warns his disciples about the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees, and they misunderstand, thinking he speaks of bread, until he reminds them of the feedings.

segments.title: Peter Confesses Jesus as Christ
segments.gist: At Caesarea Philippi, Jesus asks who people say he is, and Peter confesses him as the Christ, the Son of the living God; Jesus blesses Peter and promises to build his church.

segments.title: Jesus Foretells His Death
segments.gist: Jesus begins to show his disciples that he must go to Jerusalem, suffer, be killed, and be raised again; Peter rebukes him, and Jesus rebukes Peter as a stumbling block.

segments.title: Take Up Your Cross
segments.gist: Jesus teaches that following him means denying oneself and taking up one's cross, and that the Son of Man will come in his Father's glory to reward each according to his deeds.

17.summary: Jesus is transfigured before Peter, James, and John, and a voice from a bright cloud declares him the beloved Son. After healing a demon-possessed boy whom the disciples could not cure, Jesus again foretells his death and resurrection, and he provides the temple tax money from a fish's mouth.

segments.title: The Transfiguration
segments.gist: Jesus is transfigured before Peter, James, and John; Moses and Elijah appear, and a voice from a cloud declares Jesus the beloved Son.

segments.title: Healing the Demoniac Boy
segments.gist: A man asks Jesus to heal his son, whom the disciples could not cure; Jesus rebukes the demon and the boy is healed.

segments.title: Jesus Foretells His Death
segments.gist: Jesus tells his disciples that he will be killed and raised on the third day, and they are deeply grieved.

segments.title: The Temple Tax
segments.gist: Peter is asked about the temple tax; Jesus teaches that he is free but provides a coin from a fish's mouth to avoid offense.

18.summary: Jesus teaches his disciples about humility and care for the vulnerable, using a child as an example and warning against causing others to stumble. He tells the parable of the lost sheep and gives instructions for restoring a brother who sins, ending with the parable of the unforgiving servant who is punished for refusing to forgive.

segments.title: Who Is Greatest in Heaven
segments.gist: Jesus calls a child, says one must become humble like a child to enter heaven, and welcomes little ones in his name.

segments.title: Warning Against Causing Stumbling
segments.gist: Jesus warns that causing a little one to stumble brings severe judgment and says to cut off offending hands or feet.

segments.title: Parable of the Lost Sheep
segments.gist: Jesus tells of a shepherd leaving ninety-nine sheep to find one lost, showing the Father's will that none perish.

segments.title: Steps to Restore a Sinning Brother
segments.gist: Jesus instructs: confront a sinning brother privately, then with witnesses, then before the church; agreement in prayer is affirmed.

segments.title: Parable of the Unforgiving Servant
segments.gist: Peter asks about forgiveness; Jesus tells of a servant forgiven much who refuses to forgive a little and is handed to tormentors.

19.summary: Jesus leaves Galilee for Judea, where Pharisees test him on divorce and he teaches on marriage, celibacy, and welcoming children. A rich young man asks about eternal life but turns away when told to sell his possessions, prompting Jesus' teaching on the difficulty of riches and the reward of following him. He closes with the parable of the laborers in the vineyard and a third prediction of his death, and answers the mother of Zebedee's sons about greatness and service.

segments.title: Teaching on Divorce and Celibacy
segments.gist: Jesus answers the Pharisees' test on divorce by appealing to creation, and teaches that celibacy is a gift for some.

segments.title: Jesus Blesses Little Children
segments.gist: Jesus rebukes his disciples for hindering children and welcomes them, saying the kingdom belongs to such as these.

segments.title: The Rich Young Man's Question
segments.gist: A rich young man asks about eternal life but goes away sorrowful when Jesus tells him to sell his possessions and follow him.

segments.title: Teaching on Riches and Reward
segments.gist: Jesus tells his disciples how hard it is for the rich to enter the kingdom and promises reward to those who follow him.

20.summary: Jesus tells the parable of the laborers in the vineyard, foretells his death and resurrection, teaches that greatness means service, and heals two blind men near Jericho.

segments.title: Parable of the laborers
segments.gist: A householder hires laborers at different hours and pays all the same, illustrating that the last will be first.

segments.title: Jesus foretells his death
segments.gist: Jesus takes the twelve aside and predicts his betrayal, condemnation, crucifixion, and resurrection.

segments.title: Request for James and John
segments.gist: The mother of Zebedee's sons asks for her sons to sit beside Jesus, and Jesus teaches that greatness comes through service.

segments.title: Two blind men healed
segments.gist: Two blind men cry out to Jesus for mercy, and he heals them because of his compassion.

21.summary: Jesus enters Jerusalem on a donkey as crowds hail him, cleanses the temple, and curses a fig tree. He defends his authority through parables of the two sons and the wicked husbandmen, and answers challenges from the chief priests and Pharisees.

segments.title: Triumphal Entry into Jerusalem
segments.gist: Jesus sends disciples for a donkey and rides into Jerusalem while crowds spread garments and cry Hosanna.

segments.title: Cleansing the Temple
segments.gist: Jesus drives out money changers and heals the blind and lame while children praise him in the temple.

segments.title: Cursing the Fig Tree
segments.gist: Jesus curses a barren fig tree, it withers, and he teaches about faith and prayer.

segments.title: Parable of the Two Sons
segments.gist: Jesus tells of a father asking two sons to work; the one who first refused but obeyed is likened to tax collectors entering the kingdom.

segments.title: Parable of the Wicked Husbandmen
segments.gist: Jesus tells of a vineyard owner whose servants and son are killed by tenants, and the chief priests seek to arrest him.

22.summary: Jesus tells the parable of the marriage feast, where invited guests refuse and a man without a wedding garment is cast out. Religious leaders try to trap him with questions about tribute to Caesar, the resurrection, and the greatest commandment, and he answers each. He then asks them whose son the Christ is, and no one dares question him further.

segments.title: Parable of the Marriage Feast
segments.gist: A king invites guests to his son's wedding, but they refuse and kill his servants; he destroys them and invites all to the feast.

segments.title: Question about Tribute to Caesar
segments.gist: The Pharisees and Herodians ask Jesus whether it is lawful to pay tribute to Caesar; he answers, 'Render unto Caesar the things that are Caesar's.'

segments.title: Question about the Resurrection
segments.gist: The Sadducees pose a scenario of a woman married to seven brothers; Jesus says they err, not knowing the scriptures, and God is God of the living.

segments.title: The Greatest Commandment
segments.gist: A lawyer asks which is the great commandment; Jesus names love of God and love of neighbor, on which hang all the law and prophets.

segments.title: Jesus Questions the Pharisees
segments.gist: Jesus asks the Pharisees whose son the Christ is; they say David's, and he asks how David in spirit calls him Lord, and no one answers.

23.summary: Jesus warns the crowds and his disciples about the scribes and Pharisees, condemning their hypocrisy and heavy burdens, and pronounces seven woes against them for their false teaching and persecution of prophets. He concludes with a lament over Jerusalem for rejecting God's messengers.

segments.title: Warning against hypocritical leaders
segments.gist: Jesus tells the crowds and disciples to follow the Pharisees' teaching but not their example, condemning their burdensome rules and love of honor.

segments.title: Seven woes on scribes and Pharisees
segments.gist: Jesus pronounces seven woes against the scribes and Pharisees for shutting the kingdom, making proselytes, swearing falsely, neglecting justice, and persecuting prophets.

segments.title: Lament over Jerusalem
segments.gist: Jesus grieves over Jerusalem's refusal to accept God's messengers and declares that they will not see him again until they bless his coming.

24.summary: Jesus leaves the temple and predicts its destruction, then answers his disciples' questions on the Mount of Olives about the signs of his coming and the end of the age. He warns of false christs, wars, persecution, and the abomination of desolation, and describes his glorious return. He concludes with parables and sayings urging watchfulness and faithful service, because the day and hour are unknown.

segments.title: Jesus Foretells Temple Destruction
segments.gist: Jesus leaves the temple and tells his disciples that not one stone will be left upon another.

segments.title: Signs of the End
segments.gist: On the Mount of Olives, Jesus warns of false christs, wars, famines, earthquakes, persecution, and the need to endure to the end.

segments.title: Great Tribulation and Coming of Son
segments.gist: Jesus describes the abomination of desolation, great tribulation, false signs, and his visible coming with power and great glory.

segments.title: Lesson of the Fig Tree
segments.gist: Jesus says the powers of heaven will be shaken and the Son of Man will come; the fig tree lesson assures that his words will not pass away.

segments.title: Exhortation to Watch
segments.gist: Jesus says no one knows the day or hour and compares his coming to the days of Noah and to a thief, urging watchfulness.

segments.title: Parable of Faithful and Evil Servants
segments.gist: Jesus contrasts the faithful servant who is rewarded with the evil servant who is punished when the master returns unexpectedly.

25.summary: Jesus tells three parables about readiness and judgment: the ten virgins, where five are wise and five foolish; the talents, where servants are rewarded or condemned based on their stewardship; and the sheep and goats, where the Son of Man separates people based on how they treated the needy. The chapter emphasizes watchfulness, faithful use of what is entrusted, and compassionate action.

segments.title: Parable of the Ten Virgins
segments.gist: Ten virgins await the bridegroom; five wise with oil enter the wedding, five foolish shut out.

segments.title: Parable of the Talents
segments.gist: A man entrusts talents to servants; two trade and are rewarded, one buries his and is condemned.

segments.title: Judgment of the Nations
segments.gist: The Son of Man separates sheep and goats, rewarding those who helped the needy and punishing those who did not.

26.summary: Matthew 26 covers the final events before Jesus' crucifixion: He predicts His death, is anointed at Bethany, eats the Passover with His disciples, institutes the Lord's Supper, predicts Peter's denial, prays in Gethsemane, is betrayed by Judas and arrested, is tried before Caiaphas and the Sanhedrin, and is denied by Peter.

segments.title: Plot, Anointing, and Betrayal
segments.gist: Religious leaders plot to kill Jesus; a woman anoints Him at Bethany; Judas agrees to betray Him for thirty pieces of silver.

segments.title: Passover and Lord's Supper
segments.gist: Jesus eats the Passover with His disciples, identifies Judas as the betrayer, and institutes the Lord's Supper with bread and wine.

segments.title: Peter's Denial Predicted
segments.gist: Jesus foretells that all disciples will stumble and that Peter will deny Him three times before the rooster crows.

segments.title: Agony in Gethsemane
segments.gist: Jesus prays in Gethsemane, asking for the cup to pass, while His disciples sleep; He submits to the Father's will.

segments.title: Betrayal and Arrest
segments.gist: Judas arrives with a crowd, betrays Jesus with a kiss; Jesus is arrested, rebukes the use of force, and the disciples flee.

segments.title: Trial and Peter's Denial
segments.gist: Jesus is condemned by the Sanhedrin for blasphemy, mocked, and denied three times by Peter, who weeps bitterly.

27.summary: Matthew 27 recounts Jesus' trial before Pilate, Judas's remorse and suicide, the release of Barabbas, and the mocking and crucifixion of Jesus. After darkness and Jesus' death, the temple veil is torn, a centurion confesses, and Jesus is buried in a tomb guarded by soldiers.

segments.title: Jesus Delivered to Pilate
segments.gist: Jesus is bound and handed to Pilate; Judas repents, returns the silver, and hangs himself.

segments.title: Pilate Questions and Releases Barabbas
segments.gist: Pilate questions Jesus, yields to the crowd's demand for Barabbas, and hands Jesus over to be crucified.

segments.title: Soldiers Mock and Crucify Jesus
segments.gist: Soldiers mock Jesus, crucify him between two thieves, and passersby and priests revile him.

segments.title: Jesus Dies and Veil Is Torn
segments.gist: Darkness covers the land, Jesus cries out and dies, the temple veil is torn, and a centurion confesses.

segments.title: Jesus Buried and Tomb Guarded
segments.gist: Joseph of Arimathea buries Jesus in a new tomb, and the chief priests and Pharisees set a guard.

28.summary: After the Sabbath, women come to Jesus' tomb at dawn and find it empty, with an angel announcing his resurrection. The risen Jesus meets them, and later the guards are bribed to spread a false story. In Galilee Jesus commissions the eleven disciples to make disciples of all nations, promising his presence to the end.

segments.title: Women find empty tomb
segments.gist: Women arrive at the tomb, an angel announces Jesus is risen, and the risen Jesus meets them.

segments.title: Guards bribed to lie
segments.gist: The guards report to the chief priests, who bribe them to claim the disciples stole the body.

segments.title: Great Commission in Galilee
segments.gist: The eleven disciples meet Jesus in Galilee, and he commissions them to baptize and teach all nations.

1.summary: Mark opens with John the Baptist preparing the way in the wilderness and baptizing Jesus, who is then driven into the wilderness to be tempted. Jesus begins preaching in Galilee, calls his first disciples, teaches with authority in the synagogue at Capernaum, heals many, and withdraws to preach in surrounding towns.

segments.title: John Prepares the Way
segments.gist: John the Baptist preaches repentance and baptizes in the wilderness, announcing that one mightier than he is coming.

segments.title: Jesus Baptized and Tempted
segments.gist: Jesus is baptized by John, the Spirit descends, a voice declares him the Son, and he is tempted in the wilderness.

segments.title: Jesus Calls Four Fishermen
segments.gist: Jesus preaches in Galilee and calls Simon, Andrew, James, and John, who immediately leave their nets and follow him.

segments.title: Teaching and Exorcism in Capernaum
segments.gist: In the synagogue Jesus teaches with authority and casts out an unclean spirit, and his fame spreads throughout Galilee.

segments.title: Healings at Simon's House
segments.gist: Jesus heals Simon's mother-in-law and many others who are sick or demon-possessed, though he does not permit the demons to speak.

segments.title: Jesus Preaches in Galilee
segments.gist: Jesus rises early to pray in a solitary place, then goes throughout Galilee preaching in synagogues and casting out demons.

segments.title: A Leper Is Cleansed
segments.gist: A leper begs Jesus to make him clean, Jesus touches and heals him, and the man's testimony causes Jesus to stay outside towns.

2.summary: In Capernaum, Jesus forgives and heals a paralytic lowered through a roof, then calls Levi (Matthew) from the tax booth and eats with sinners, sparking disputes about fasting and Sabbath observance when his disciples pluck grain and he heals a man's withered hand on the Sabbath.

segments.title: Healing and forgiving the paralytic
segments.gist: Four men lower a paralytic through a roof; Jesus forgives his sins and heals him, claiming authority to forgive sins.

segments.title: Call of Levi and dinner with sinners
segments.gist: Jesus calls Levi from the tax booth and dines at his house with tax collectors and sinners, saying he came to call sinners.

segments.title: Question about fasting
segments.gist: When asked why his disciples do not fast, Jesus replies that the bridegroom's guests cannot fast while he is present, and gives new wine and old wineskins sayings.

segments.title: Disciples pluck grain on Sabbath
segments.gist: Jesus defends his disciples for plucking grain on the Sabbath by citing David eating showbread, and declares the Son of man is Lord of the Sabbath.

3.summary: In Mark 3, Jesus heals a man's withered hand on the Sabbath, provoking the Pharisees, and then withdraws to heal many and appoint the twelve apostles. He confronts scribes who accuse him of casting out demons by Beelzebub, warning of the unforgivable sin against the Holy Spirit, and redefines his true family as those who do God's will.

segments.title: Healing on the Sabbath
segments.gist: Jesus heals a man's withered hand in the synagogue on the Sabbath, angering the Pharisees who plot with the Herodians to destroy him.

segments.title: Crowds and Healings
segments.gist: Jesus withdraws to the sea with a great multitude; he heals many and commands unclean spirits not to reveal his identity.

segments.title: Appointing the Twelve
segments.gist: Jesus goes up a mountain, appoints twelve apostles to preach and have authority to heal, and lists their names including Judas Iscariot.

segments.title: Beelzebub Controversy
segments.gist: Scribes accuse Jesus of casting out demons by Beelzebub; he refutes them with parables and warns that blasphemy against the Holy Spirit is unforgivable.

segments.title: Jesus' True Family
segments.gist: When told his mother and brothers are outside, Jesus declares that those who do God's will are his true family.

4.summary: Jesus teaches a crowd by the sea in parables: the sower, the growing seed, and the mustard seed. He explains the sower privately to his disciples, then calms a storm on the lake, rebuking the wind and waves while the disciples marvel who he is.

segments.title: Parable of the Sower
segments.gist: Jesus tells of seed falling on four kinds of ground, with only the good soil bearing fruit.

segments.title: Why Jesus Teaches in Parables
segments.gist: Jesus explains to his disciples that parables reveal truth to insiders and hide it from outsiders, then interprets the sower.

segments.title: Lamp and Measure
segments.gist: Jesus says a lamp is meant to be seen and that the measure you give will be measured to you.

segments.title: Growing Seed and Mustard Seed
segments.gist: Jesus compares the kingdom to seed that grows secretly and to a mustard seed that becomes a great shrub.

segments.title: Jesus Calms the Storm
segments.gist: A great storm arises; Jesus rebukes the wind and sea, and the disciples wonder who he is.

5.summary: Jesus crosses the sea to the country of the Gadarenes, where he frees a man possessed by a legion of demons, sending them into a herd of swine. After returning, he raises Jairus's daughter from the dead and heals a woman who touches his garment.

segments.title: Demoniac Healed in Gadara
segments.gist: Jesus casts a legion of demons out of a man into a herd of swine, which rush into the sea and drown.

segments.title: Jairus Pleads for Daughter
segments.gist: Jairus, a ruler of the synagogue, falls at Jesus's feet, begging him to heal his dying daughter.

segments.title: Woman Healed by Touch
segments.gist: A woman with a twelve-year bleeding condition touches Jesus's garment and is healed; Jesus tells her her faith has made her whole.

segments.title: Jairus's Daughter Raised
segments.gist: Jesus ignores news of the girl's death, enters the house, takes her by the hand, and raises her to life.

6.summary: Jesus is rejected at Nazareth, sends out the Twelve to preach and heal, and hears of Herod's fear that he is John the Baptist risen. After the feeding of the five thousand and walking on the sea, he heals many at Gennesaret.

segments.title: Jesus Rejected at Nazareth
segments.gist: Jesus teaches in his hometown synagogue, but the people take offense at him, and he marvels at their unbelief.

segments.title: The Twelve Sent Out
segments.gist: Jesus sends the Twelve out in pairs with authority over unclean spirits, instructing them to travel light and shake off dust as a testimony.

segments.title: Herod Fears and John Beheaded
segments.gist: Herod hears of Jesus and fears John the Baptist has risen; he later has John beheaded to please Herodias and her daughter.

segments.title: Feeding the Five Thousand
segments.gist: The apostles return, and Jesus has the crowd sit in groups; he blesses five loaves and two fish and feeds five thousand men.

segments.title: Jesus Walks on the Sea
segments.gist: Jesus sends the disciples ahead by boat, prays on a mountain, then walks on the sea and calms the wind, and they are amazed.

segments.title: Healings at Gennesaret
segments.gist: After crossing over, Jesus is recognized at Gennesaret, and many are healed as they touch the hem of his garment.

7.summary: Mark 7 recounts Jesus' dispute with Pharisees over tradition and defilement, his healing of a Gentile woman's daughter and a deaf-mute man, and his teaching that what comes from within defiles a person.

segments.title: Tradition versus commandment
segments.gist: Pharisees question Jesus about unwashed hands; he rebukes them for setting aside God's commandment to keep human tradition.

segments.title: What defiles a person
segments.gist: Jesus teaches the crowd that defilement comes from within, from the heart, not from what enters a person from outside.

segments.title: Syrophoenician woman's faith
segments.gist: A Gentile woman begs Jesus to cast a demon out of her daughter; after a exchange about children's bread, Jesus grants her request.

segments.title: Healing a deaf-mute man
segments.gist: Jesus heals a man who is deaf and has a speech impediment, using his fingers and spit, and the crowd is astonished.

8.summary: Jesus feeds four thousand people with seven loaves and a few fish, refuses the Pharisees' demand for a sign, and warns his disciples against their leaven. At Caesarea Philippi Peter confesses Jesus as the Christ, Jesus foretells his death and rebukes Peter, and then teaches that following him means denying oneself and taking up the cross. The chapter ends with the transfiguration, the healing of a demon-possessed boy, a second prediction of his death, and Jesus' teaching on greatness and tolerance.

segments.title: Feeding the Four Thousand
segments.gist: Jesus has compassion on a hungry crowd and feeds four thousand with seven loaves and a few fish, taking up seven baskets of leftovers.

segments.title: Pharisees Demand a Sign
segments.gist: The Pharisees seek a sign from heaven; Jesus refuses and warns his disciples about the leaven of the Pharisees and Herod.

segments.title: Blind Man Healed at Bethsaida
segments.gist: Jesus heals a blind man at Bethsaida in two stages, first seeing men as trees, then clearly.

segments.title: Peter Confesses Jesus as Christ
segments.gist: At Caesarea Philippi Peter confesses Jesus as the Christ; Jesus foretells his death and rebukes Peter for opposing God's will.

segments.title: Take Up the Cross
segments.gist: Jesus teaches the crowd that following him means denying oneself, taking up the cross, and not being ashamed of him.

9.summary: Jesus is transfigured before Peter, James, and John, then casts out a mute spirit from a boy after the disciples fail. He again foretells his death and resurrection, teaches that greatness means service, and warns against causing others to stumble.

segments.title: The Transfiguration
segments.gist: Jesus is transfigured on a mountain, Moses and Elijah appear, and a voice from the cloud declares him the beloved Son.

segments.title: Healing a Boy with a Mute Spirit
segments.gist: A father brings his possessed son to Jesus; after the disciples fail, Jesus casts out the spirit, stressing the need for prayer.

segments.title: Jesus Foretells His Death
segments.gist: Jesus predicts his betrayal, death, and resurrection, but the disciples do not understand and are afraid to ask.

segments.title: Teaching on True Greatness
segments.gist: Jesus teaches that whoever wants to be first must be last and servant of all, and welcomes a child in his name.

segments.title: The Unknown Exorcist
segments.gist: John reports someone casting out demons in Jesus' name; Jesus says not to forbid him, for whoever is not against them is for them.

segments.title: Warnings about Stumbling Blocks
segments.gist: Jesus warns against causing little ones to stumble, speaks of cutting off offending members, and calls his followers to be salted with fire and at peace.

10.summary: Jesus travels toward Jerusalem, teaching on divorce, blessing children, and the cost of discipleship. He predicts his death, answers James and John's request for glory, and heals blind Bartimaeus.

segments.title: Teaching on Divorce
segments.gist: Jesus answers the Pharisees about divorce, appeals to creation, and says Moses allowed it for hardness of heart.

segments.title: Jesus Blesses Children
segments.gist: Jesus rebukes his disciples for hindering children and blesses them, saying the kingdom belongs to such.

segments.title: The Rich Young Ruler
segments.gist: A rich man asks about eternal life but goes away sorrowful; Jesus teaches on the difficulty of riches and the reward of discipleship.

segments.title: Jesus Predicts His Death
segments.gist: Jesus tells the twelve plainly that he will be condemned, mocked, scourged, killed, and rise again.

segments.title: Request for Glory
segments.gist: James and John ask to sit at Jesus' right and left; Jesus teaches that greatness comes through service and gives his life as a ransom.

segments.title: Blind Bartimaeus Healed
segments.gist: Blind Bartimaeus cries out to Jesus, is called, and receives his sight, then follows Jesus.

11.summary: Jesus rides into Jerusalem on a colt as crowds hail him, curses a fig tree, and cleanses the temple. He teaches about faith and forgiveness, and when the chief priests question his authority, he answers with a question about John the Baptist.

segments.title: Triumphal Entry into Jerusalem
segments.gist: Jesus sends disciples for a colt, rides into Jerusalem as crowds shout Hosanna, and enters the temple.

segments.title: Jesus Curses the Fig Tree
segments.gist: Jesus curses a fig tree for having no fruit, saying no one will eat from it again.

segments.title: Cleansing of the Temple
segments.gist: Jesus drives out buyers and sellers, overturns tables, and teaches that the temple should be a house of prayer.

segments.title: Lesson from the Withered Fig Tree
segments.gist: Jesus teaches about faith, prayer, and forgiving others when the disciples see the fig tree withered.

segments.title: Questioning Jesus' Authority
segments.gist: Chief priests and scribes question Jesus' authority, and he replies by asking about the baptism of John.

12.summary: Jesus tells the parable of the wicked husbandmen, answers questions about tribute to Caesar, the resurrection, and the greatest commandment, warns against the scribes, and observes a widow giving two mites.

segments.title: Parable of the Wicked Husbandmen
segments.gist: Jesus tells of a vineyard owner whose servants and son are killed by the tenants, who will be destroyed.

segments.title: Question About Tribute to Caesar
segments.gist: Pharisees and Herodians ask about paying tribute; Jesus says render to Caesar and to God.

segments.title: Question About the Resurrection
segments.gist: Sadducees pose a scenario of seven brothers; Jesus affirms resurrection and God of the living.

segments.title: The Greatest Commandment
segments.gist: A scribe asks for the greatest commandment; Jesus names love of God and neighbor.

segments.title: Jesus Questions David's Son
segments.gist: Jesus asks how Christ is David's son and warns against the scribes' hypocrisy.

segments.title: The Widow's Two Mites
segments.gist: Jesus observes a poor widow giving two mites and says she gave more than the rich.

13.summary: On the Mount of Olives, Jesus foretells the destruction of the temple and answers his disciples' questions about the signs of the end, warning of false christs, persecution, and the coming desolation. He describes the tribulation, the cosmic signs preceding the Son of man's return, and insists that no one knows the day or hour. The chapter closes with parables urging watchfulness and faithfulness.

segments.title: Jesus Foretells Temple Destruction
segments.gist: Jesus predicts that not one stone of the temple will be left upon another, prompting the disciples to ask privately when these things will happen.

segments.title: Warnings of Deception and Persecution
segments.gist: Jesus warns of false christs, wars, earthquakes, and famines, and tells his followers they will be persecuted and testify before rulers.

segments.title: The Abomination and Great Tribulation
segments.gist: Jesus describes the abomination of desolation, instructs flight to the mountains, and warns of unprecedented tribulation and false prophets.

segments.title: Cosmic Signs and the Son of Man
segments.gist: Jesus foretells cosmic disturbances and the coming of the Son of man in clouds with great power and glory to gather his elect.

segments.title: Parable of the Fig Tree
segments.gist: Jesus uses the fig tree to teach that when these signs appear, his return is near, and assures that his words will not pass away.

segments.title: Exhortation to Watch
segments.gist: Jesus declares that no one knows the day or hour, not even the angels or the Son, and commands his followers to watch and be ready.

14.summary: Mark 14 recounts the plot to arrest Jesus, His anointing at Bethany, the Last Supper with the institution of the Lord's Supper and Peter's denial predicted, the agony in Gethsemane, Judas's betrayal and Jesus's arrest, the trial before the council with Peter's threefold denial.

segments.title: Plot and Anointing
segments.gist: Chief priests plot to kill Jesus; a woman anoints Him at Bethany; Judas agrees to betray Him.

segments.title: Last Supper Instituted
segments.gist: Jesus eats the Passover with His disciples, institutes the bread and cup, and predicts His betrayer.

segments.title: Peter's Denial Predicted
segments.gist: Jesus foretells the disciples' scattering and Peter's threefold denial before the cock crows twice.

segments.title: Agony in Gethsemane
segments.gist: Jesus prays in Gethsemane for the cup to pass, submits to God's will, and finds His disciples sleeping.

segments.title: Betrayal and Arrest
segments.gist: Judas betrays Jesus with a kiss; Jesus is arrested, a bystander cuts off a servant's ear, and a young man flees naked.

segments.title: Trial and Peter's Denial
segments.gist: Jesus is condemned by the council; Peter denies Him three times and weeps.

15.summary: Jesus is brought before Pilate, who condemns him to crucifixion despite finding no fault in him. He is mocked, crucified at Golgotha, and dies after darkness covers the land, with the temple veil torn and a centurion confessing him as the Son of God. Joseph of Arimathaea buries him in a rock tomb, and two women observe where he is laid.

segments.title: Jesus before Pilate
segments.gist: Pilate questions Jesus, who answers little; the crowd demands Barabbas and cries for Jesus to be crucified.

segments.title: Soldiers mock Jesus
segments.gist: Soldiers dress Jesus in purple, crown him with thorns, hail him as King of the Jews, and lead him out to be crucified.

segments.title: Crucifixion and mockery
segments.gist: Jesus is crucified at Golgotha; passersby and chief priests mock him, and two thieves also revile him.

segments.title: Darkness and death
segments.gist: Darkness covers the land; Jesus cries out and dies, the temple veil tears, and a centurion confesses him as the Son of God.

segments.title: Joseph buries Jesus
segments.gist: Joseph of Arimathaea asks Pilate for Jesus' body and lays it in a rock tomb, with two women watching.

16.summary: Three women come to Jesus' tomb at dawn to anoint his body and find the stone rolled away and a young man in white announcing that Jesus is risen. The risen Jesus appears to Mary Magdalene, to two disciples on the road, and finally to the eleven, commissioning them to preach the gospel to every creature before he ascends into heaven.

segments.title: Women find the empty tomb
segments.gist: Three women bring spices to anoint Jesus, find the stone rolled away, and hear a young man in white declare that Jesus is risen.

segments.title: Jesus appears to Mary Magdalene
segments.gist: The risen Jesus appears first to Mary Magdalene, who tells the mourning disciples, but they do not believe her.

segments.title: Jesus appears to two disciples
segments.gist: Jesus appears in another form to two disciples walking in the country, and they report it to the rest, who do not believe.

segments.title: Great Commission to the eleven
segments.gist: Jesus rebukes the eleven for unbelief, commands them to preach the gospel to every creature, and promises signs to those who believe.

segments.title: Ascension and continued preaching
segments.gist: After speaking to them, Jesus ascends to heaven and sits at God's right hand, while the disciples go out preaching with the Lord's confirming signs.

1.summary: Luke opens with a formal preface to Theophilus, then recounts two angelic announcements: Gabriel tells Zacharias that his aged wife Elisabeth will bear John, and later tells Mary that she will conceive Jesus. The chapter includes Mary's Magnificat, the birth of John the Baptist, Zacharias's prophecy over his son, and closes with John growing in the wilderness.

segments.title: Luke's Preface to Theophilus
segments.gist: Luke explains that he has carefully investigated the events and writes an orderly account so Theophilus may know the truth.

segments.title: Gabriel Announces John's Birth
segments.gist: The angel Gabriel appears to Zacharias in the temple and promises a son, John, who will prepare the people for the Lord.

segments.title: Gabriel Announces Jesus to Mary
segments.gist: Gabriel visits Mary in Nazareth, tells her she will conceive Jesus by the Holy Spirit, and she submits to God's will.

segments.title: Mary Visits Elisabeth and Sings
segments.gist: Mary visits Elisabeth, who blesses her, and Mary responds with a song praising God for lifting up the humble.

segments.title: Birth of John and Zacharias's Prophecy
segments.gist: Elisabeth bears John, Zacharias regains his speech and prophesies about John's role, and the child grows in the wilderness.

2.summary: Luke 2 recounts the birth of Jesus in Bethlehem, the angelic announcement to shepherds, the presentation of Jesus in the temple where Simeon and Anna recognize him, and the only biblical account of Jesus' boyhood, when he is found in the temple at age twelve.

segments.title: Jesus Born in Bethlehem
segments.gist: A decree from Caesar Augustus brings Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem, where Mary gives birth to Jesus and lays him in a manger.

segments.title: Angels Announce to Shepherds
segments.gist: An angel announces the Savior's birth to shepherds, a heavenly host praises God, and the shepherds find the baby in the manger.

segments.title: Circumcision and Presentation
segments.gist: Jesus is circumcised on the eighth day and presented in the temple, with offerings according to the law.

segments.title: Simeon and Anna Prophesy
segments.gist: Simeon blesses God and prophesies over Jesus and Mary, and the prophetess Anna speaks of the child to all awaiting redemption.

segments.title: Return to Nazareth
segments.gist: The family returns to Nazareth, where Jesus grows and becomes strong in spirit and wisdom.

segments.title: Boy Jesus in the Temple
segments.gist: At twelve, Jesus stays behind in Jerusalem and is found in the temple among teachers, then returns home with his parents and grows in favor.

3.summary: Luke sets the historical context of John the Baptist's ministry, who preaches repentance and baptizes in the Jordan, calling the crowds to bear fruits of repentance. John is imprisoned by Herod, and Jesus is baptized, with the Holy Spirit descending on him and a voice from heaven declaring him God's beloved Son. The chapter closes with a genealogy tracing Jesus' lineage back to Adam.

segments.title: John Begins Ministry
segments.gist: Luke lists the political and religious rulers of the time and describes John the Baptist receiving God's word in the wilderness, preaching baptism of repentance for remission of sins, and fulfilling Isaiah's prophecy.

segments.title: John Preaches Repentance
segments.gist: John calls the crowds a generation of vipers, warns of coming wrath, and tells them to bring forth fruits of repentance; he gives specific ethical instructions to the people, tax collectors, and soldiers.

segments.title: John Denies Being Christ
segments.gist: As the people wonder if John is the Christ, he clarifies that he baptizes with water but one mightier is coming who will baptize with the Holy Ghost and fire, and he preaches many other things to the people.

segments.title: Herod Imprisons John
segments.gist: Herod the tetrarch, rebuked by John for his sins including taking his brother's wife, adds to his evils by shutting John up in prison.

segments.title: Jesus Is Baptized
segments.gist: After all the people are baptized, Jesus is baptized and prays; the heaven opens, the Holy Ghost descends like a dove, and a voice from heaven declares Jesus to be God's beloved Son.

segments.title: Genealogy of Jesus
segments.gist: Luke records Jesus' genealogy, beginning with Jesus at about thirty years old and tracing his lineage through Joseph back to Adam, the son of God.

4.summary: Luke 4 recounts Jesus' temptation in the wilderness, where he resists the devil's offers; his rejection at Nazareth when he reads Isaiah in the synagogue and the townspeople try to kill him; his move to Capernaum, where he teaches with authority, casts out a demon, and heals Simon's mother-in-law and many others; and his withdrawal to preach in other synagogues.

segments.title: Temptation in the Wilderness
segments.gist: Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, is led into the wilderness and tempted by the devil for forty days, but he resists each temptation with Scripture.

segments.title: Rejection at Nazareth
segments.gist: Jesus teaches in the synagogue at Nazareth, reads from Isaiah, claims the prophecy is fulfilled, and the townspeople, enraged, try to throw him off a cliff.

segments.title: Teaching and Exorcism in Capernaum
segments.gist: Jesus teaches with authority in the synagogue at Capernaum and casts out an unclean demon, amazing the crowd.

segments.title: Healings at Simon's House
segments.gist: Jesus heals Simon's mother-in-law of a fever and then heals many others who are sick or possessed as the sun sets.

segments.title: Preaching in Other Synagogues
segments.gist: Jesus withdraws to a deserted place, but the crowds seek him; he says he must preach the kingdom of God to other towns and does so in the synagogues of Galilee.

5.summary: Jesus calls his first disciples after a miraculous catch of fish, heals a leper and a paralytic, calls Levi the tax collector, and defends his disciples for eating grain on the Sabbath and for not fasting like others.

segments.title: Miraculous catch and call of disciples
segments.gist: Jesus teaches from Simon's boat, directs a great catch of fish, and calls Simon, James, and John to follow him.

segments.title: Jesus heals a leper
segments.gist: A leper begs to be cleansed; Jesus touches and heals him, then withdraws to pray as his fame spreads.

segments.title: Jesus forgives and heals a paralytic
segments.gist: Friends lower a paralytic through the roof; Jesus forgives his sins and heals him, astonishing the scribes and crowd.

segments.title: Call of Levi and dinner with sinners
segments.gist: Jesus calls the tax collector Levi, dines with sinners, and says he came to call sinners to repentance.

segments.title: Question about fasting
segments.gist: Jesus explains that his disciples cannot fast while he is present and gives parables of new wine and old garments.

6.summary: In Luke 6, Jesus defends his disciples for plucking grain on the Sabbath and heals a man's withered hand, then withdraws to pray and chooses twelve apostles. He teaches a large crowd, pronouncing blessings and woes, commanding love for enemies, warning against judging others, and illustrating that a tree is known by its fruit and that a house must be built on a rock by hearing and doing his words.

segments.title: Sabbath controversies
segments.gist: Jesus defends his disciples for plucking grain on the Sabbath and heals a man's withered hand, angering the scribes and Pharisees.

segments.title: Choosing the twelve
segments.gist: Jesus spends the night in prayer and then selects twelve apostles from among his disciples.

segments.title: Blessings and woes
segments.gist: Jesus teaches the crowd, pronouncing blessings on the poor, hungry, weeping, and persecuted, and woes on the rich, full, laughing, and praised.

segments.title: Love enemies and judge not
segments.gist: Jesus commands love for enemies, the golden rule, and generous giving, warning against judging and condemning others.

segments.title: Parables of tree and heart
segments.gist: Jesus uses parables about blind guides, specks and beams, and trees bearing fruit to show that the heart determines one's words and actions.

segments.title: Hearing and doing
segments.gist: Jesus compares those who hear and do his words to a man building a house on a rock, which stands against floods.

7.summary: Luke 7 recounts Jesus healing a centurion's servant and raising a widow's son at Nain, then answering John the Baptist's disciples and praising John before rebuking the crowd. The chapter closes with a sinful woman anointing Jesus' feet at a Pharisee's house, where Jesus tells a parable about forgiveness and declares her sins forgiven.

segments.title: Centurion's Servant Healed
segments.gist: A centurion sends elders to ask Jesus to heal his servant, and Jesus marvels at his faith, healing the servant from afar.

segments.title: Widow's Son Raised at Nain
segments.gist: Jesus meets a funeral procession at Nain, raises the widow's only son, and the crowd glorifies God.

segments.title: John's Disciples and Jesus' Testimony
segments.gist: John's disciples ask if Jesus is the coming one; Jesus heals many and praises John, then rebukes the crowd for rejecting both John and the Son of Man.

segments.title: Sinful Woman Anoints Jesus
segments.gist: At a Pharisee's house, a sinful woman washes Jesus' feet with tears and anoints them; Jesus tells a parable of two debtors and forgives her sins.

8.summary: Luke 8 gathers Jesus' parable of the sower and its explanation, followed by a series of miracles: he calms a storm, casts out a legion of demons from a man in Gadara, heals a woman with an issue of blood, and raises Jairus' daughter from the dead. The chapter emphasizes hearing and keeping God's word, the authority of Jesus over nature, demons, disease, and death, and the varied responses of faith and fear.

segments.title: Women Accompany Jesus
segments.gist: Jesus travels through cities and villages preaching, accompanied by the twelve and several women healed of evil spirits and infirmities.

segments.title: Parable of the Sower
segments.gist: Jesus tells the parable of the sower and later explains its meaning to his disciples, identifying the seed as the word of God and the soils as different responses.

segments.title: Light and True Family
segments.gist: Jesus teaches that nothing hidden will remain secret, urges careful hearing, and declares that those who hear and do God's word are his true family.

segments.title: Jesus Calms the Storm
segments.gist: While sailing, Jesus rebukes the wind and waves, calming the storm, and questions his disciples' faith; they marvel at his authority.

segments.title: Healing the Gadarene Demoniac
segments.gist: Jesus casts a legion of demons out of a man into a herd of swine; the townspeople ask him to leave, but the healed man proclaims what Jesus did.

segments.title: Jairus' Daughter and the Woman
segments.gist: On the way to heal Jairus' daughter, a woman with a hemorrhage is healed by touching Jesus' garment; Jesus then raises Jairus' daughter from the dead.

9.summary: Jesus sends out the twelve apostles to preach and heal, feeds five thousand with five loaves and two fishes, is confessed by Peter as the Christ, and is transfigured before Peter, James, and John. He foretells his death, rebukes a sectarian spirit, and teaches on humility and cost of discipleship.

segments.title: Mission of the Twelve
segments.gist: Jesus gives the twelve power and authority, sends them to preach and heal, and Herod is perplexed about who Jesus is.

segments.title: Feeding the Five Thousand
segments.gist: Jesus welcomes the crowd, teaches them, and multiplies five loaves and two fishes to feed about five thousand men.

segments.title: Peter's Confession and Passion Foretold
segments.gist: Peter confesses Jesus as the Christ, Jesus foretells his death and resurrection, and calls his followers to take up their cross daily.

segments.title: The Transfiguration
segments.gist: Jesus is transfigured on a mountain before Peter, James, and John, appearing with Moses and Elijah as a voice from the cloud declares him God's beloved Son.

segments.title: Healing a Boy and Foretelling Death
segments.gist: Jesus heals a demon-possessed boy after his disciples fail, and again foretells his betrayal and death while the disciples fail to understand.

segments.title: Teaching on Humility and Tolerance
segments.gist: Jesus teaches that the least is greatest and rebukes the disciples for forbidding an outsider who casts out demons in his name.

10.summary: Jesus appoints seventy disciples and sends them out to heal and proclaim the kingdom, then rejoices that the Father has revealed these things to the simple. A lawyer tests him with the question of eternal life, prompting the parable of the good Samaritan, and Jesus visits Martha and Mary, where Mary chooses the better part.

segments.title: The Seventy Sent Out
segments.gist: Jesus appoints seventy disciples, sends them ahead in pairs, and warns them of rejection while giving them authority to heal.

segments.title: The Seventy Return Rejoicing
segments.gist: The seventy return with joy that demons submit to them; Jesus rejoices in spirit and praises the Father for revealing truth to babes.

segments.title: Parable of the Good Samaritan
segments.gist: A lawyer asks who is his neighbor; Jesus tells of a wounded man ignored by priest and Levite but helped by a Samaritan.

segments.title: Martha and Mary
segments.gist: Jesus visits Martha, who is busy serving, while Mary sits at his feet; Jesus says Mary has chosen the good part.

11.summary: Luke 11 contains Jesus' teaching on prayer, including the Lord's Prayer and parables on persistence, followed by controversy over his healing a mute man and his rebuke of the Pharisees and lawyers, ending with his warning against hypocrisy and his lament over Jerusalem.

segments.title: Teaching on Prayer
segments.gist: Jesus gives the Lord's Prayer and parables on persistence and the Father's willingness to give the Holy Spirit.

segments.title: Controversy Over Beelzebub
segments.gist: Jesus heals a mute man, refutes the charge of casting out demons by Beelzebub, and warns of the returning unclean spirit.

segments.title: Blessing on Hearers
segments.gist: A woman blesses Jesus' mother, but Jesus says blessed are those who hear and keep God's word.

segments.title: Sign of Jonah and Light
segments.gist: Jesus condemns the demand for a sign, citing Jonah and the queen of Sheba, and teaches about the light of the body.

segments.title: Woes to Pharisees and Lawyers
segments.gist: At a Pharisee's dinner, Jesus pronounces woes on the Pharisees and lawyers for hypocrisy and burdening others, leading to their opposition.

12.summary: Jesus warns his disciples against hypocrisy and fear of men, tells the parable of the rich fool to expose greed, and urges trust in God's provision. He then calls for watchful readiness for his return, speaks of division his coming brings, and ends by urging the crowds to discern the present time and settle with their accuser.

segments.title: Warning Against Hypocrisy and Fear
segments.gist: Jesus tells his disciples to fear God rather than those who kill the body, and promises the Holy Spirit's help before authorities.

segments.title: Parable of the Rich Fool
segments.gist: Jesus refuses to arbitrate an inheritance dispute and tells of a rich man whose stored wealth is demanded of him that night.

segments.title: Do Not Worry About Provisions
segments.gist: Jesus urges his disciples not to worry about food or clothing, pointing to ravens and lilies as evidence of God's care.

segments.title: Parable of the Watchful Servants
segments.gist: Jesus calls for readiness like servants waiting for their master, and describes the faithful and unfaithful stewards' rewards.

segments.title: Division and Discerning the Time
segments.gist: Jesus says he brings division on earth, rebukes the crowds for not discerning the time, and urges them to settle with their accuser.

13.summary: Jesus calls for repentance, heals a crippled woman on the Sabbath, and teaches about the kingdom of God through parables of the mustard seed and leaven. He answers a question about who will be saved, laments over Jerusalem, and warns Herod's threat.

segments.title: Call to Repentance
segments.gist: Jesus uses the deaths of Galileans and others to urge repentance, warning of perishing otherwise.

segments.title: Parable of the Barren Fig Tree
segments.gist: A fig tree is given one more year to bear fruit before being cut down.

segments.title: Healing on the Sabbath
segments.gist: Jesus heals a crippled woman on the Sabbath, defends the act, and the crowd rejoices.

segments.title: Parables of Mustard Seed and Leaven
segments.gist: Jesus compares the kingdom of God to a mustard seed and to leaven.

segments.title: Teaching on the Narrow Door
segments.gist: Jesus urges entry through the narrow door and describes the exclusion of many.

segments.title: Lament over Jerusalem
segments.gist: Jesus is warned about Herod, replies, and laments over Jerusalem's rejection.

14.summary: Jesus heals a man with dropsy on the Sabbath and teaches on humility and inviting the poor to feasts. He tells the parable of the great supper, where invited guests make excuses and the poor and outcast are brought in. He then speaks of the cost of discipleship and the value of salt.

segments.title: Healing on the Sabbath
segments.gist: Jesus heals a man with dropsy on the Sabbath and defends the act by asking if any would not rescue a son or ox on the Sabbath.

segments.title: Parable of the Lowest Seat
segments.gist: Jesus tells a parable about taking the lowest seat at a wedding feast, so that the host may exalt you rather than shame you.

segments.title: Invite the Poor
segments.gist: Jesus instructs the host to invite the poor, maimed, lame, and blind, who cannot repay, promising repayment at the resurrection.

segments.title: Parable of the Great Supper
segments.gist: A man gives a great supper, but invited guests make excuses; the master then invites the poor and outcast, and compels others to come in.

segments.title: Cost of Discipleship
segments.gist: Jesus teaches that disciples must hate family and life, carry the cross, and count the cost, using parables of a tower and a king going to war; salt without savor is worthless.

15.summary: The chapter contains three parables Jesus tells in response to Pharisees who complain about him receiving sinners: the lost sheep, the lost coin, and the lost son. Each parable emphasizes the joy in heaven over one repentant sinner, culminating in the father's forgiveness of his younger son and the resentment of his older brother.

segments.title: Parable of the Lost Sheep
segments.gist: Jesus tells of a shepherd leaving ninety-nine sheep to find one lost, and the joy when it is found.

segments.title: Parable of the Lost Coin
segments.gist: A woman searches for a lost coin and rejoices with friends when she finds it, illustrating joy over repentance.

segments.title: Parable of the Lost Son
segments.gist: A younger son squanders his inheritance, returns in repentance, and is welcomed by his father with a feast.

segments.title: The Older Brother's Resentment
segments.gist: The older brother refuses to join the celebration and complains, but the father explains his joy over the repentant son.

16.summary: Jesus tells two parables about money and judgment: the unjust steward who secures his future by forgiving debts, and the rich man and Lazarus, where the rich man's neglect of the beggar leads to eternal reversal and a warning that Scripture is sufficient.

segments.title: Parable of the Unjust Steward
segments.gist: Jesus tells of a steward who, facing dismissal, reduces debts owed to his master to secure his future, and commends his shrewdness.

segments.title: Teachings on Money and Law
segments.gist: Jesus rebukes the Pharisees for justifying themselves before men and teaches on the law, divorce, and serving God rather than mammon.

segments.title: Rich Man and Lazarus
segments.gist: A rich man ignores the beggar Lazarus, and after death their fates are reversed; Abraham refuses to send a warning, saying Scripture is enough.
