17.summary: Jesus teaches his disciples about forgiveness, faith, and duty, heals ten lepers of whom only one returns to give thanks, and answers the Pharisees about the coming of the kingdom of God, describing the sudden separation that will occur when the Son of man is revealed.

segments.title: Forgiveness and Increase of Faith
segments.gist: Jesus warns against causing little ones to stumble, commands repeated forgiveness, and tells the apostles to increase their faith.

segments.title: Parable of the Unprofitable Servant
segments.gist: Jesus illustrates that servants who simply do their duty should not expect thanks but should say they are unprofitable servants.

segments.title: Cleansing of Ten Lepers
segments.gist: Jesus heals ten lepers on the way to Jerusalem, but only a Samaritan returns to thank him, prompting Jesus to note the foreigner's gratitude.

segments.title: The Kingdom of God Within You
segments.gist: Jesus tells the Pharisees the kingdom of God comes not with observation but is within you, and warns his disciples of his coming rejection.

segments.title: Days of the Son of Man
segments.gist: Jesus compares his coming to the days of Noah and Lot, describing sudden separation and urging readiness, with a warning about where the body will be gathered.

18.summary: Jesus tells a parable about persistent prayer, welcomes little children, challenges a rich ruler to give up his wealth, foretells his death, heals a blind beggar, and contrasts a proud Pharisee with a humble tax collector in prayer.

segments.title: Parable of the Persistent Widow
segments.gist: Jesus tells a parable about a widow who persistently demands justice from an unjust judge, teaching that God will avenge his elect who cry out to him.

segments.title: Parable of the Pharisee and Publican
segments.gist: Jesus contrasts a proud Pharisee's self-righteous prayer with a humble tax collector's plea for mercy, declaring the humble one justified.

segments.title: Jesus Welcomes Little Children
segments.gist: People bring infants to Jesus, and he rebukes his disciples, saying the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.

segments.title: The Rich Ruler's Question
segments.gist: A rich ruler asks Jesus what he must do to inherit eternal life; Jesus tells him to sell all and follow him, and the ruler goes away sorrowful.

segments.title: Jesus Foretells His Death
segments.gist: Jesus takes the twelve aside and predicts his betrayal, death, and resurrection, but they do not understand.

segments.title: Healing of the Blind Beggar
segments.gist: As Jesus approaches Jericho, a blind beggar cries out for mercy, and Jesus restores his sight, prompting the man to follow him and glorify God.

19.summary: Jesus encounters Zacchaeus and announces salvation for his house, tells a parable of ten pounds about a nobleman's servants, then enters Jerusalem to crowds hailing him as king. He weeps over the city, cleanses the temple, and teaches there daily while the chief priests plot against him.

segments.title: Zacchaeus repents and is saved
segments.gist: Jesus calls the tax collector Zacchaeus down from a sycamore tree, and Zacchaeus promises to give half his goods to the poor and repay fourfold.

segments.title: Parable of the ten pounds
segments.gist: Jesus tells of a nobleman who gives ten servants a pound each, and on returning rewards the faithful and punishes the rebellious.

segments.title: Triumphal entry into Jerusalem
segments.gist: Jesus sends disciples to fetch a colt, rides into Jerusalem as crowds spread garments and praise God, and answers Pharisees who ask him to rebuke them.

segments.title: Jesus weeps over Jerusalem
segments.gist: Jesus laments over the city, foretelling its destruction because it did not recognize the time of its visitation.

segments.title: Cleansing the temple and teaching
segments.gist: Jesus drives out the merchants from the temple, teaches daily there, and the chief priests seek to destroy him but fear the people.

20.summary: In the temple, Jesus is confronted by the chief priests and elders demanding to know the source of his authority; he answers with a question about John's baptism and then tells the parable of the wicked husbandmen. Later, spies question him about paying tribute to Caesar, Sadducees ask about the resurrection, and a scribe asks which is the greatest commandment. Jesus then poses a question about David's son and warns his disciples about the scribes.

segments.title: Questioned About Authority
segments.gist: The chief priests and elders ask Jesus by what authority he acts; he replies by asking whether John's baptism was from heaven or men.

segments.title: Parable of the Wicked Husbandmen
segments.gist: Jesus tells of a vineyard owner who sends servants and finally his son, whom the husbandmen kill, and warns of judgment on them.

segments.title: Question About Tribute to Caesar
segments.gist: Spies ask if it is lawful to pay tribute to Caesar; Jesus asks for a coin and says to render to Caesar and to God what is theirs.

segments.title: Sadducees Ask About Resurrection
segments.gist: Sadducees pose a scenario of a woman married to seven brothers; Jesus says the resurrected do not marry and that God is God of the living.

segments.title: Jesus Asks About David's Son
segments.gist: Jesus asks how the scribes say Christ is David's son, yet David calls him Lord, and says the common people hear him gladly.

segments.title: Warning Against the Scribes
segments.gist: In the hearing of all, Jesus warns his disciples to beware of scribes who seek honor and devour widows' houses while making long prayers.

21.summary: Jesus observes a poor widow giving two mites, declaring her gift greater than the rich donors'. He then foretells the temple's destruction, warns of persecution and false messiahs, and describes cosmic signs and the coming of the Son of man, urging watchfulness.

segments.title: The Widow's Two Mites
segments.gist: Jesus sees a poor widow cast two mites into the treasury and says she gave more than all the rich.

segments.title: Temple Destruction Foretold
segments.gist: When people admire the temple, Jesus predicts that not one stone will be left upon another.

segments.title: Warnings of Persecution
segments.gist: Jesus warns of false christs, wars, earthquakes, and persecution, promising to give his disciples words and endurance.

segments.title: Jerusalem's Siege and Fall
segments.gist: Jesus describes Jerusalem surrounded by armies, the days of vengeance, and the city's fall by the sword.

segments.title: Signs and the Son of Man
segments.gist: Jesus foretells signs in the sun and stars, the Son of man coming in a cloud, and says his words will not pass away.

segments.title: Exhortation to Watch
segments.gist: Jesus warns against surfeiting and drunkenness, urges watchfulness and prayer, and teaches daily in the temple.

22.summary: Luke 22 recounts the plot of the chief priests and scribes to kill Jesus, Judas's agreement to betray him, and the preparation and observance of the Passover supper. During the supper Jesus institutes the Lord's Supper, predicts his betrayal and Peter's denial, and teaches about servanthood and the coming kingdom. After singing a hymn, Jesus goes to the Mount of Olives, where he prays in agony, is betrayed by Judas, arrested, and brought before the council, where Peter denies him three times.

segments.title: Plot and Betrayal Agreement
segments.gist: The chief priests and scribes seek to kill Jesus, and Judas agrees with them to betray him for money.

segments.title: Preparation for Passover
segments.gist: Jesus sends Peter and John to prepare the Passover meal, and they find the guest room as he instructed.

segments.title: Passover Supper and Institution
segments.gist: Jesus eats the Passover with his apostles, institutes the bread and cup of the new covenant, and predicts his betrayal.

segments.title: Teaching on Servanthood
segments.gist: The disciples argue about greatness, and Jesus teaches that the greatest must serve, promising them places at his table.

segments.title: Predictions of Denial and Trial
segments.gist: Jesus warns Peter of Satan's sifting and his denial, and tells the disciples to prepare for coming hardship.

segments.title: Agony, Betrayal, and Arrest
segments.gist: Jesus prays in agony on the Mount of Olives, is betrayed by Judas with a kiss, and is arrested by the crowd.

segments.title: Peter's Denial
segments.gist: Peter follows Jesus to the high priest's house and denies knowing him three times before the cock crows.

segments.title: Mocking and Council Trial
segments.gist: The men holding Jesus mock and beat him, and the council demands to know if he is the Christ, which he affirms.

23.summary: Jesus is brought before Pilate and Herod, condemned though declared innocent, and crucified between two thieves; he forgives his executioners, promises paradise to a penitent thief, and dies as the centurion confesses him. Joseph of Arimathaea buries him, and the women observe the tomb.

segments.title: Jesus before Pilate
segments.gist: The chief priests accuse Jesus before Pilate, who finds no fault in him and sends him to Herod.

segments.title: Pilate yields to the crowd
segments.gist: Pilate again declares Jesus innocent but releases Barabbas and delivers Jesus to be crucified.

segments.title: Crucifixion and two thieves
segments.gist: Jesus is crucified, mocked, and forgives his executioners; one thief reviles him while the other receives a promise of paradise.

segments.title: Darkness and death of Jesus
segments.gist: Darkness covers the land, the temple veil is rent, Jesus commends his spirit to God and dies as a centurion glorifies God.

segments.title: Burial by Joseph
segments.gist: Joseph of Arimathaea asks for Jesus' body, lays it in a new tomb, and the women from Galilee observe the burial and prepare spices.

24.summary: On the first day of the week, women find Jesus' tomb empty and are told by angels that he is risen; Peter checks and finds the linen cloths. Jesus joins two disciples on the road to Emmaus, explains the scriptures, and is recognized in the breaking of bread. He appears to the gathered disciples, eats broiled fish, opens their understanding of the scriptures, and ascends at Bethany while they return to Jerusalem with joy.

segments.title: Women find the empty tomb
segments.gist: Women bring spices to the tomb, find the stone rolled away and the body gone, and are told by two angels that Jesus is risen; they report to the eleven.

segments.title: Road to Emmaus
segments.gist: Jesus joins two disciples on the road to Emmaus, explains the scriptures, and is recognized by them in the breaking of bread.

segments.title: Jesus appears to the eleven
segments.gist: Jesus appears among the gathered disciples, shows his hands and feet, and eats broiled fish and honeycomb to prove he is not a spirit.

segments.title: Opens their understanding
segments.gist: Jesus reminds them that the law, prophets, and psalms foretold his suffering and resurrection, opens their understanding of the scriptures, and promises the Father's promise and power from on high.

segments.title: Ascension at Bethany
segments.gist: Jesus leads the disciples to Bethany, blesses them, and is carried up into heaven; they worship him and return to Jerusalem with great joy, praising God in the temple.

1.summary: John opens by identifying Jesus as the eternal Word who was with God, was God, and became flesh. John the Baptist testifies that Jesus is the Lamb of God, and the chapter ends as Jesus calls his first disciples, who begin to follow him after Andrew brings Simon Peter and Philip brings Nathanael.

segments.title: The Word Made Flesh
segments.gist: The eternal Word, who was with God and was God, becomes flesh and dwells among humanity, bringing grace and truth.

segments.title: John Baptist Denies Being Christ
segments.gist: John the Baptist tells priests and Levites he is not the Christ but a voice crying in the wilderness, and identifies himself as unworthy to untie the Messiah's sandal.

segments.title: John Calls Jesus Lamb of God
segments.gist: John the Baptist sees Jesus, calls him the Lamb of God who takes away the world's sin, and testifies that the Spirit descended on him.

segments.title: First Disciples Follow Jesus
segments.gist: Two of John's disciples follow Jesus, and Andrew brings his brother Simon to Jesus, who renames him Cephas.

segments.title: Philip and Nathanael Called
segments.gist: Jesus calls Philip, who brings Nathanael; Jesus tells Nathanael he saw him under the fig tree and promises greater things.

2.summary: Jesus attends a wedding in Cana, where he turns water into wine; he then goes to Jerusalem for Passover and drives the money changers and merchants out of the temple, and many believe in him because of his signs.

segments.title: Water into wine at Cana
segments.gist: At a wedding in Cana, Jesus turns water into wine after his mother's request, and his disciples believe in him.

segments.title: Cleansing the temple
segments.gist: At Passover in Jerusalem, Jesus drives out the money changers and sellers from the temple, declaring it a house of merchandise.

segments.title: Sign of the temple
segments.gist: When asked for a sign, Jesus says to destroy the temple and he will raise it in three days, referring to his body.

segments.title: Many believe in Jerusalem
segments.gist: Many believe in Jesus because of his signs, but he does not entrust himself to them, knowing what is in man.

3.summary: Nicodemus, a Pharisee, visits Jesus at night and is told that one must be born again to see the kingdom of God; Jesus explains God's love in giving his Son and John the Baptist testifies that Jesus must increase while he himself must decrease.

segments.title: Nicodemus Visits Jesus at Night
segments.gist: Nicodemus, a Pharisee and ruler, comes to Jesus by night and is told that one must be born again to see the kingdom of God.

segments.title: Jesus Explains New Birth and God's Love
segments.gist: Jesus explains being born of water and the Spirit, compares himself to the lifted serpent, and declares God's love in giving his Son.

segments.title: Jesus and John Baptize in Judea
segments.gist: Jesus and his disciples baptize in Judea while John also baptizes at Aenon; a dispute arises about purification.

segments.title: John the Baptist Testifies About Jesus
segments.gist: John says he is not the Christ but the friend of the bridegroom, and that Jesus must increase while he must decrease.

4.summary: Jesus travels through Samaria and meets a Samaritan woman at a well, offering her living water and revealing her past; many Samaritans believe through her testimony. He then returns to Galilee and heals a nobleman's son at Capernaum from a distance.

segments.title: Jesus at Jacob's Well
segments.gist: Jesus, tired from his journey, sits by Jacob's well in Samaria while his disciples go into the city to buy food.

segments.title: Living Water and the Woman
segments.gist: Jesus speaks with a Samaritan woman about living water, her past, and true worship, revealing himself as the Messiah.

segments.title: Disciples Return; Harvest Talk
segments.gist: The disciples return and marvel, while Jesus teaches them about the harvest of souls and the labor of others.

segments.title: Samaritans Believe
segments.gist: Many Samaritans believe because of the woman's testimony, and more believe after hearing Jesus themselves.

segments.title: Jesus Returns to Galilee
segments.gist: Jesus goes to Galilee, where the people welcome him because they had seen his works in Jerusalem.

segments.title: Healing the Nobleman's Son
segments.gist: A nobleman begs Jesus to heal his dying son; Jesus says the son lives, and the man and his household believe.

5.summary: At a feast in Jerusalem, Jesus heals a man who had been lame for thirty-eight years at the pool of Bethesda, then defends the healing when the Jews persecute him for doing it on the Sabbath. He claims God as his Father and his own authority to give life and judge, citing the witness of John the Baptist, his works, the Father, and the Scriptures.

segments.title: Healing at Bethesda
segments.gist: Jesus finds a lame man at the pool of Bethesda and heals him on the Sabbath.

segments.title: Sabbath Controversy
segments.gist: The Jews object to the man carrying his bed on the Sabbath, and Jesus defends his work.

segments.title: Jesus Claims Divine Authority
segments.gist: Jesus says the Son does only what the Father does, gives life, and will judge.

segments.title: Witnesses to Jesus
segments.gist: Jesus cites John the Baptist, his own works, and the Father as witnesses to his mission.

segments.title: Scriptures and Moses
segments.gist: Jesus says the Scriptures testify of him, but his hearers refuse to come to him for life.

6.summary: Jesus feeds five thousand people with five loaves and two fish, walks on the Sea of Galilee, and teaches that he is the bread of life. Many disciples take offense at his teaching about eating his flesh and drinking his blood and stop following him, while Peter confesses that Jesus has the words of eternal life.

segments.title: Feeding the Five Thousand
segments.gist: Jesus multiplies five loaves and two fish to feed a great multitude, with twelve baskets of fragments left over.

segments.title: Jesus Walks on the Sea
segments.gist: The disciples set out by boat; Jesus walks on the water, and they receive him into the boat.

segments.title: Jesus the Bread of Life
segments.gist: Jesus teaches that he is the true bread from heaven, and that whoever believes in him has eternal life.

segments.title: Eating the Flesh of the Son
segments.gist: Jesus insists that unless one eats his flesh and drinks his blood, there is no life, causing dispute among the Jews.

segments.title: Many Disciples Depart
segments.gist: Many disciples turn back from following Jesus; Peter confesses that Jesus has the words of eternal life.

7.summary: Jesus' brothers urge him to go to the Feast of Tabernacles in Judea, but he stays in Galilee until going up privately. At the feast he teaches in the temple, debates with the Jews about his origin and authority, and confronts the chief priests and Pharisees, who try to arrest him. The chapter ends with Nicodemus questioning the Pharisees' judgment and the crowd divided over whether Jesus is the Christ.

segments.title: Brothers urge Jesus to go to feast
segments.gist: Jesus' brothers tell him to go to Judea to show his works, but he says his time is not yet come and stays in Galilee.

segments.title: Jesus goes secretly to the feast
segments.gist: Jesus goes up to the feast in secret; the Jews seek him, and the crowd murmurs about whether he is good or a deceiver.

segments.title: Jesus teaches in the temple
segments.gist: In the midst of the feast Jesus teaches, defends his doctrine as from God, and challenges the Jews who seek to kill him.

segments.title: Debate about Jesus' origin
segments.gist: Some Jerusalemites question whether Jesus is the Christ; Jesus declares his divine origin, and the Jews try to seize him but cannot.

segments.title: Living water and division
segments.gist: On the last day of the feast Jesus invites the thirsty to come to him and promises the Spirit; the crowd is divided.

segments.title: Officers return and Nicodemus speaks
segments.gist: The officers sent to arrest Jesus return empty-handed, the Pharisees rebuke them, and Nicodemus questions judging him without a hearing.

8.summary: Jesus teaches in the temple, declaring himself the light of the world and engaging in escalating disputes with the Pharisees over his testimony, his origin, and their claim to be Abraham's children. The confrontation ends with Jesus asserting his eternal identity and narrowly escaping being stoned.

segments.title: Jesus forgives the adulterous woman
segments.gist: The scribes and Pharisees bring a woman caught in adultery to Jesus, testing him; he challenges the sinless to cast the first stone, and they leave.

segments.title: Jesus declares himself the light
segments.gist: Jesus calls himself the light of the world; the Pharisees dispute his testimony, but he defends it and speaks of his Father.

segments.title: Jesus warns of dying in sin
segments.gist: Jesus tells the Pharisees they will die in their sins unless they believe in him, and predicts his crucifixion and their misunderstanding.

segments.title: Jesus confronts claims of Abraham's lineage
segments.gist: Jesus tells believers that truth will free them; they claim never to have been slaves, but he exposes their desire to kill him and their true father the devil.

segments.title: Jesus asserts pre-existence and escapes stoning
segments.gist: The Jews accuse Jesus of being a Samaritan and demon-possessed; he affirms his eternal existence before Abraham and is nearly stoned but escapes.

9.summary: Jesus heals a man born blind by making clay with his spit and sending him to wash in the pool of Siloam. The Pharisees investigate the healing, quarrel over whether Jesus can be from God, and expel the man from the synagogue. Jesus later finds him and he believes, while the Pharisees are told their claimed sight leaves them in sin.

segments.title: Jesus heals the blind man
segments.gist: Jesus answers his disciples, makes clay with spit, anoints the blind man's eyes, and sends him to wash in Siloam.

segments.title: Neighbors question the healed man
segments.gist: Neighbors and others debate whether the seeing man is the same beggar, and he tells them Jesus healed him.

segments.title: Pharisees investigate the healing
segments.gist: The man is brought to the Pharisees; they split over whether a Sabbath healer can be from God, and he calls Jesus a prophet.

segments.title: Parents questioned about their son
segments.gist: The Jews summon the man's parents, who confirm he was born blind but defer to him for fear of being expelled from the synagogue.

segments.title: Man expelled after defending Jesus
segments.gist: The Pharisees press the man again; he argues no sinner could open blind eyes, and they cast him out.

segments.title: Jesus finds him; belief and judgment
segments.gist: Jesus finds the expelled man, reveals himself as the Son of man, receives his worship, and says the blind see while the seeing are blind.

10.summary: Jesus tells the parable of the shepherd and the sheep, declaring Himself the good shepherd who lays down His life for the sheep, in contrast to hirelings. He is confronted by the Jews at the Feast of Dedication, asserts His unity with the Father, and escapes an attempt to stone Him, withdrawing beyond Jordan where many believe on Him.

segments.title: Parable of the Sheepfold
segments.gist: Jesus describes the true shepherd who enters by the door, calls his sheep by name, and leads them out.

segments.title: Jesus the Door
segments.gist: Jesus declares Himself the door of the sheep, contrasting Himself with thieves and hirelings who destroy.

segments.title: The Good Shepherd
segments.gist: Jesus explains that He is the good shepherd who lays down His life for the sheep and has power to take it up again.

segments.title: Division Among the Jews
segments.gist: The Jews are divided over Jesus' words, some calling Him demon-possessed and others defending Him.

segments.title: Feast of Dedication Discourse
segments.gist: At the Feast of Dedication, Jesus tells the Jews that His sheep hear His voice and that He and the Father are one.

segments.title: Attempt to Stone Jesus
segments.gist: The Jews try to stone Jesus for blasphemy, but He escapes and goes beyond Jordan, where many believe on Him.

11.summary: Jesus receives word that Lazarus is sick, delays two days, then travels to Bethany where Lazarus has died. He raises Lazarus from the dead after four days, leading many to believe but prompting the chief priests and Pharisees to plot to kill Jesus.

segments.title: Lazarus's Sickness and Jesus' Delay
segments.gist: Jesus hears of Lazarus's illness, delays two days, then tells his disciples they will go to Judea despite danger.

segments.title: Jesus Comforts Martha and Mary
segments.gist: Jesus arrives at Bethany, speaks with Martha about resurrection, and sees Mary and others weeping.

segments.title: Jesus Raises Lazarus
segments.gist: Jesus goes to the tomb, prays, calls Lazarus out, and Lazarus emerges alive.

segments.title: Plot to Kill Jesus
segments.gist: Many believe, but some report to the Pharisees, who plot to kill Jesus; he withdraws, and the Passover approaches.

12.summary: At a supper in Bethany, Mary anoints Jesus' feet with costly ointment, and Judas objects. Jesus enters Jerusalem to a crowd waving palm branches, and Greeks seek him; he speaks of his coming death and calls for faith. Despite many signs, most do not believe, as Isaiah foretold, but some rulers believe secretly.

segments.title: Mary Anoints Jesus at Bethany
segments.gist: At a supper in Bethany, Mary anoints Jesus' feet with costly ointment; Judas objects, and many Jews believe because of Lazarus.

segments.title: Triumphal Entry into Jerusalem
segments.gist: Jesus enters Jerusalem on a young donkey as crowds wave palm branches and shout hosanna, fulfilling prophecy; the Pharisees despair.

segments.title: Greeks Seek Jesus; He Speaks of Death
segments.gist: Greeks ask to see Jesus; he speaks of his coming death as a grain of wheat, calls for self-denial, and urges faith in the light.

segments.title: Isaiah's Prophecy of Unbelief
segments.gist: Despite many signs, most do not believe, fulfilling Isaiah's prophecy of blindness; some rulers believe secretly but fear the Pharisees.

segments.title: Jesus' Final Public Appeal
segments.gist: Jesus cries out that believing in him is believing in the Father; he came as light, and his words will judge on the last day.

13.summary: At the Last Supper, Jesus washes his disciples' feet, foretells his betrayal by Judas, and gives the new commandment to love one another. He predicts Peter's denial, marking the close of the supper before his passion.

segments.title: Jesus washes the disciples' feet
segments.gist: Jesus rises from supper, washes his disciples' feet, and explains that only the washed are clean, though not all.

segments.title: Jesus explains the foot washing
segments.gist: Jesus teaches that servants are not greater than their master and that receiving him is receiving the one who sent him.

segments.title: Jesus identifies Judas as betrayer
segments.gist: Jesus declares that one of them will betray him, identifies Judas with a sop, and Judas leaves into the night.

segments.title: The new commandment of love
segments.gist: After Judas leaves, Jesus speaks of his glorification and commands his disciples to love one another as he has loved them.

segments.title: Jesus predicts Peter's denial
segments.gist: Peter asks where Jesus is going and vows to lay down his life, but Jesus foretells that Peter will deny him three times.

14.summary: Jesus comforts his disciples before his death, telling them he goes to prepare a place for them and that he is the way, the truth, and the life. He promises the Holy Spirit as a Comforter and teaches that love is shown through obedience, ending with a call to rise and go.

segments.title: Jesus prepares a place
segments.gist: Jesus tells his disciples not to be troubled, that he goes to prepare a place for them and will come again.

segments.title: Jesus the way to the Father
segments.gist: Jesus says he is the way, the truth, and the life, and that whoever has seen him has seen the Father.

segments.title: Promise of the Comforter
segments.gist: Jesus promises to ask the Father to send the Holy Spirit, who will abide with believers forever.

segments.title: Manifestation and abiding
segments.gist: Jesus explains that he and the Father will make their abode with those who love him and keep his word.

segments.title: Peace and the prince of this world
segments.gist: Jesus gives his peace, foretells his going to the Father, and says the prince of this world comes but has nothing in him.

15.summary: Jesus tells his disciples he is the true vine and they are the branches, urging them to remain in him and bear fruit through love and obedience. He commands them to love one another as he has loved them, warns them of the world's hatred, and promises the coming of the Comforter who will testify of him.

segments.title: The True Vine
segments.gist: Jesus declares himself the true vine, his Father the husbandman, and urges branches to abide in him to bear fruit.

segments.title: Abide in My Love
segments.gist: Jesus commands his disciples to keep his commandments and love one another as he has loved them, calling them friends.

segments.title: The World's Hatred
segments.gist: Jesus warns that the world will hate his disciples because it hated him first, fulfilling the law's word.

segments.title: The Comforter's Testimony
segments.gist: Jesus promises the Comforter, the Spirit of truth, who will testify of him along with the disciples.

16.summary: Jesus continues his farewell discourse to his disciples, warning them of coming persecution and the Holy Spirit's work, promising his return after a brief sorrow that will turn to joy, and concluding with the assurance of his victory over the world.

segments.title: Persecution and the Comforter
segments.gist: Jesus warns his disciples of expulsion and killing, but promises that the Comforter will come and convict the world.

segments.title: The Spirit's Ministry
segments.gist: Jesus explains that the Holy Spirit will convict the world of sin, righteousness, and judgment, and will guide believers into all truth.

segments.title: Sorrow Turned to Joy
segments.gist: Jesus tells of his departure and return, comparing the disciples' sorrow to a woman's labor that turns to joy at childbirth.

segments.title: Ask in My Name
segments.gist: Jesus instructs the disciples to ask the Father in his name and promises that the Father loves them for their faith in him.

segments.title: Peace in Tribulation
segments.gist: Jesus acknowledges the disciples' belief, predicts their scattering, and assures them of peace and his victory over the world.

17.summary: Jesus prays to the Father, first for himself and the glory he had before the world, then for his disciples whom he has kept and who are hated by the world, and finally for all future believers, asking that they be one as he and the Father are one.

segments.title: Jesus Prays for Himself
segments.gist: Jesus lifts his eyes to heaven, asks the Father to glorify him, and declares that eternal life is knowing the true God and Jesus Christ.

segments.title: Jesus Prays for His Disciples
segments.gist: Jesus says he has manifested the Father's name to the men given to him, kept them in the Father's name, and now prays for them rather than for the world.

segments.title: Jesus Prays for Their Sanctification
segments.gist: Jesus asks the Father to keep his disciples from the evil one, to sanctify them through the truth, and to send them into the world as he was sent.

segments.title: Jesus Prays for Future Believers
segments.gist: Jesus prays for all who will believe through the disciples' word, asking that they may be one, see his glory, and know the Father's love.

18.summary: Jesus is arrested in the garden of Gethsemane after Judas leads soldiers and officers to him; he is brought before Annas and then Caiaphas, where Peter denies him three times. Pilate interrogates Jesus about his kingship, finds no fault in him, and offers to release him for the Passover, but the crowd demands Barabbas instead.

segments.title: Betrayal and Arrest in Garden
segments.gist: Jesus goes with his disciples to a garden, where Judas arrives with soldiers; Jesus identifies himself and is arrested.

segments.title: Jesus Brought to Annas
segments.gist: Jesus is led first to Annas, the father-in-law of Caiaphas, the high priest that year.

segments.title: Peter's First Denial
segments.gist: Peter follows Jesus and, when questioned by the maid at the door, denies being a disciple.

segments.title: High Priest Questions Jesus
segments.gist: The high priest questions Jesus about his disciples and teaching; Jesus answers and is struck by an officer.

segments.title: Peter Denies Twice More
segments.gist: Peter denies Jesus two more times, and immediately a rooster crows.

segments.title: Jesus Before Pilate
segments.gist: Pilate questions Jesus about his kingship, finds no fault, and offers to release him, but the crowd demands Barabbas.

19.summary: Pilate has Jesus scourged and mocked, but the crowd demands crucifixion; Jesus is handed over and crucified at Golgotha, where he commends his mother to John, gives up his spirit, and is pierced. Joseph of Arimathaea and Nicodemus then bury him in a new tomb.

segments.title: Pilate Scourges and Mocks Jesus
segments.gist: Pilate has Jesus flogged; soldiers crown him with thorns, robe him in purple, and hail him King of the Jews.

segments.title: Pilate Yields to the Crowd
segments.gist: Pilate declares Jesus innocent, but the Jews insist he must die; Pilate tries to release him, then fears Caesar and hands him over.

segments.title: Pilate Delivers Jesus to Be Crucified
segments.gist: Pilate sits on the judgment seat at Gabbatha and delivers Jesus to be crucified; the Jews accept no king but Caesar.

segments.title: Crucifixion and the Title on the Cross
segments.gist: Jesus is crucified at Golgotha between two others; Pilate writes a title in Hebrew, Greek, and Latin, and refuses to change it.

segments.title: Soldiers Divide Garments; Jesus Cares for Mary
segments.gist: Soldiers cast lots for Jesus' seamless coat; Jesus entrusts his mother to the beloved disciple, who takes her home.

segments.title: Death, Piercing, and Prophecy Fulfilled
segments.gist: Jesus says 'It is finished' and gives up his spirit; a soldier pierces his side, and scripture is fulfilled.

segments.title: Joseph and Nicodemus Bury Jesus
segments.gist: Joseph of Arimathaea and Nicodemus take Jesus' body, wrap it in spices and linen, and lay it in a new tomb.

20.summary: Mary Magdalene finds Jesus' tomb empty and tells Peter and the beloved disciple, who run to see the linen clothes and believe. Mary weeps at the tomb and encounters the risen Jesus, who sends her to tell the disciples. That evening Jesus appears to the disciples, shows his wounds, and breathes the Holy Spirit on them; Thomas, absent, refuses to believe until a week later Jesus invites him to touch his wounds, prompting his confession. The chapter closes with the purpose of the written signs: that readers may believe and have life.

segments.title: Empty tomb discovered
segments.gist: Mary Magdalene finds the stone removed, tells Peter and the beloved disciple, who run to the tomb, see the linen clothes, and believe.

segments.title: Mary meets the risen Jesus
segments.gist: Mary weeps at the tomb, sees two angels and then Jesus, whom she recognizes when he calls her name; he sends her to tell the disciples.

segments.title: Jesus appears to the disciples
segments.gist: On the evening of the first day, Jesus appears to the disciples, shows his hands and side, and breathes the Holy Spirit on them.

segments.title: Thomas believes
segments.gist: Thomas doubts until a week later Jesus invites him to touch his wounds; Thomas confesses Jesus as Lord and God, and Jesus blesses those who believe without seeing.

segments.title: Purpose of the signs
segments.gist: The narrator states that many signs are not recorded, but these are written so readers may believe Jesus is the Christ and have life.

21.summary: The risen Jesus appears to seven disciples by the Sea of Tiberias, directs them to a miraculous catch of fish, and eats with them. He restores Peter three times, foretells his martyrdom, and speaks about the beloved disciple's future.

segments.title: Jesus appears by the sea
segments.gist: Peter and six others fish all night with no catch; Jesus tells them to cast on the right side, and they haul in 153 fish.

segments.title: Jesus restores Peter
segments.gist: Jesus asks Peter three times if he loves him; Peter affirms, is told to feed his sheep, and learns he will die a martyr.

segments.title: The beloved disciple's fate
segments.gist: Peter asks about the beloved disciple; Jesus says his will is not Peter's concern, and the book closes with a note about many unwritten deeds.

1.summary: The book of Acts opens with Luke's preface to Theophilus, recalling Jesus' resurrection appearances and his command to wait in Jerusalem for the Holy Spirit. After Jesus ascends, the disciples return to the upper room, and Matthias is chosen by lot to replace Judas Iscariot among the twelve.

segments.title: Luke's Preface and Promise
segments.gist: Luke addresses Theophilus, summarizing Jesus' works and his command to wait for the Holy Spirit.

segments.title: Ascension and Angelic Promise
segments.gist: Jesus ascends into heaven after answering about Israel's kingdom, and angels promise his return.

segments.title: Disciples Gather in Prayer
segments.gist: The disciples return to Jerusalem and devote themselves to prayer with Mary and other believers.

segments.title: Peter Addresses Judas's Fate
segments.gist: Peter recounts Judas's betrayal and death, citing scripture that another must take his place.

segments.title: Matthias Chosen by Lot
segments.gist: Two candidates are proposed, and Matthias is chosen by lot to join the eleven apostles.

2.summary: On the day of Pentecost the Holy Spirit descends on the disciples with a sound from heaven and tongues of fire, enabling them to speak in other languages. Peter explains to the amazed crowd that this fulfills Joel's prophecy and preaches that Jesus, crucified and raised, is both Lord and Christ. About three thousand are baptized and join the believers, who devote themselves to teaching, fellowship, breaking bread, and prayer, sharing their possessions with gladness.

segments.title: The Spirit descends at Pentecost
segments.gist: A sound from heaven and tongues of fire appear, and the disciples speak in other languages as the Spirit enables them, amazing the crowd.

segments.title: Peter explains the prophecy
segments.gist: Peter denies drunkenness and quotes Joel's prophecy about the Spirit being poured out and the day of the Lord.

segments.title: Peter preaches Jesus crucified and raised
segments.gist: Peter proclaims Jesus' miracles, death, and resurrection, citing David's words and declaring Jesus both Lord and Christ.

segments.title: Three thousand are baptized
segments.gist: The crowd is pricked in heart and asks what to do; Peter calls them to repent and be baptized, and about three thousand are added.

segments.title: The believers' communal life
segments.gist: The new believers devote themselves to teaching, fellowship, breaking bread, and prayer, sharing possessions and praising God with gladness.

3.summary: Peter and John heal a lame man at the temple gate, and Peter explains to the amazed crowd that the healing was done by faith in Jesus, calling them to repent.

segments.title: Lame man healed at gate
segments.gist: Peter and John heal a man lame from birth at the temple gate, and he leaps and walks, praising God.

segments.title: Peter explains the healing
segments.gist: Peter tells the amazed crowd that the healing was not by their own power but through faith in Jesus, whom God glorified.

segments.title: Peter calls the crowd to repent
segments.gist: Peter urges the people to repent and turn to God so their sins may be blotted out and times of refreshing may come.

4.summary: Peter and John are arrested after healing a lame man and preaching in the temple, and are brought before the Sanhedrin. Peter boldly declares that salvation is only through Jesus, and the council, unable to punish them, warns them to stop preaching. The believers then pray for boldness, and the place is shaken as they are filled with the Holy Spirit; the chapter ends with the early church sharing all things in common.

segments.title: Peter and John Arrested
segments.gist: While Peter and John speak to the people, the priests, captain of the temple, and Sadducees arrest them and put them in custody until the next day.

segments.title: Peter Preaches to the Council
segments.gist: Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, tells the rulers that the lame man was healed by the name of Jesus Christ, and that salvation is found in no other name.

segments.title: Council Warns Them to Stop
segments.gist: The council marvels at Peter and John's boldness, commands them not to speak in Jesus' name, and releases them because of the people who glorified God for the healing.

segments.title: Believers Pray for Boldness
segments.gist: The believers pray together, quoting Psalm 2, and ask for boldness; the place is shaken, and they are all filled with the Holy Spirit.

segments.title: Early Church Shares All Things
segments.gist: The multitude of believers are of one heart and soul, sharing their possessions, and the apostles testify with great power; Barnabas is cited as an example of generosity.

5.summary: Ananias and Sapphira lie to the Holy Spirit about the price of their land and are struck dead. The apostles perform many signs, are arrested, freed by an angel, and boldly preach; after being beaten, they rejoice to suffer for Christ's name.

segments.title: Ananias and Sapphira Die
segments.gist: Ananias and Sapphira each lie about keeping part of the land sale proceeds and fall dead at Peter's rebuke.

segments.title: Apostles Heal Many
segments.gist: The apostles perform many signs, and multitudes bring the sick and possessed, who are all healed.

segments.title: Arrested, Angel Frees Apostles
segments.gist: The high priest and Sadducees arrest the apostles, but an angel opens the prison doors and tells them to preach in the temple.

segments.title: Apostles Defend Obedience to God
segments.gist: The apostles tell the council they must obey God rather than men and proclaim Jesus as Prince and Saviour.

segments.title: Gamaliel Advises Caution
segments.gist: Gamaliel warns the council to leave the apostles alone, citing past failed movements, lest they fight against God.

segments.title: Apostles Beaten and Rejoice
segments.gist: The apostles are beaten and commanded not to preach, but they rejoice and continue teaching and preaching Jesus daily.

6.summary: As the number of disciples grows, Greek-speaking widows are neglected in the daily distribution, so the apostles direct the disciples to choose seven men to handle the matter while they devote themselves to prayer and the word. Stephen, one of the seven, performs great wonders and disputes with members of the synagogue of the Freedmen, who stir up false accusations against him and bring him before the council, where his face appears like an angel's.

segments.title: Widows neglected and seven chosen
segments.gist: Hellenistic Jews complain that their widows are overlooked in daily distribution, so the apostles instruct the disciples to select seven men to oversee the task.

segments.title: Stephen disputes with the synagogue
segments.gist: Stephen, full of faith and power, performs wonders and disputes with members of the synagogue of the Freedmen, who cannot resist his wisdom.

segments.title: Stephen accused and brought before council
segments.gist: They secretly instigate men to accuse Stephen of blasphemy, seize him, and bring him before the council, where false witnesses testify and his face appears like an angel's.

7.summary: Stephen, on trial before the Jewish council, delivers a long speech retelling Israel's history from Abraham to Solomon to show that God's presence is not confined to the temple, and he accuses the leaders of resisting the Holy Spirit and murdering the Messiah. The crowd, enraged, stones him to death while he commits his spirit to Jesus and prays for his killers; Saul of Tarsus looks on approvingly.

segments.title: Stephen recounts Abraham's call
segments.gist: Stephen begins his defense by recalling God's call to Abraham, the covenant of circumcision, and the promise of land.

segments.title: Joseph and the patriarchs in Egypt
segments.gist: Stephen tells how Joseph was sold into Egypt, rose to power, and brought Jacob's family there, where they died and were buried.

segments.title: Moses' early life and flight
segments.gist: Stephen recounts Israel's growth in Egypt, Moses' birth and upbringing, his killing of an Egyptian, and his flight to Midian.

segments.title: Moses, the exodus, and Israel's rebellion
segments.gist: Stephen describes Moses' call at the burning bush, the exodus, the giving of the law, and Israel's idolatry with the golden calf and beyond.

segments.title: Tabernacle, temple, and God's true dwelling
segments.gist: Stephen notes the tabernacle and Solomon's temple, then declares that the Most High does not dwell in temples made with hands.

segments.title: Stephen's accusation and martyrdom
segments.gist: Stephen accuses the council of resisting the Holy Spirit and betraying the Messiah; they stone him while he prays for forgiveness, and Saul consents.

8.summary: Persecution scatters the Jerusalem church, and Philip preaches in Samaria, where many believe and Simon the sorcerer is rebuked for trying to buy the Holy Spirit. An angel sends Philip to a desert road, where he explains Isaiah to an Ethiopian eunuch and baptizes him.

segments.title: Saul Persecutes the Church
segments.gist: Saul ravages the church, and scattered believers preach the word wherever they go.

segments.title: Philip Preaches in Samaria
segments.gist: Philip proclaims Christ in Samaria; crowds believe and are baptized, and Simon the sorcerer also believes.

segments.title: Peter and John in Samaria
segments.gist: Peter and John pray for Samaritans to receive the Holy Spirit; Simon is rebuked for offering money and asks for prayer.

segments.title: Philip and the Ethiopian Eunuch
segments.gist: An angel sends Philip to a desert road; he explains Isaiah to an Ethiopian eunuch, baptizes him, and is caught away.

9.summary: Saul, breathing threats against the disciples, is struck down by a light from heaven on the road to Damascus and hears Jesus speak; blinded, he is healed by Ananias and baptized. Peter then travels through Lydda and Joppa, healing Aeneas and raising Tabitha (Dorcas) from the dead, and many believe.

segments.title: Saul's Conversion on the Road
segments.gist: Saul obtains letters to persecute Christians in Damascus but is confronted by a light and the voice of Jesus, leaving him blind.

segments.title: Ananias Obeys and Heals Saul
segments.gist: The Lord sends Ananias to restore Saul's sight, and Ananias obeys despite his fears, baptizing Saul.

segments.title: Saul Preaches and Escapes
segments.gist: Saul immediately proclaims Jesus in Damascus, escapes a plot to kill him, and the church enjoys peace and growth.

segments.title: Peter Heals Aeneas in Lydda
segments.gist: Peter travels to Lydda and heals the paralyzed Aeneas, causing many in Lydda and Sharon to turn to the Lord.

segments.title: Peter Raises Tabitha in Joppa
segments.gist: Peter goes to Joppa, prays for the deceased Tabitha (Dorcas), raises her to life, and stays with Simon the tanner.

10.summary: Peter, staying in Joppa, receives a vision of unclean animals and is told by God to call nothing unclean; meanwhile, Cornelius, a Roman centurion in Caesarea, is directed by an angel to send for Peter. Peter goes to Cornelius's house, preaches to the gathered Gentiles, and while he is speaking the Holy Ghost falls on them, leading Peter to baptize them.

segments.title: Cornelius's Vision
segments.gist: Cornelius, a devout centurion, sees an angel who tells him his prayers are heard and to send for Peter in Joppa.

segments.title: Peter's Vision and the Messengers
segments.gist: Peter sees a sheet of unclean animals and is told to call nothing unclean; the Spirit sends him with Cornelius's messengers.

segments.title: Peter Meets Cornelius
segments.gist: Peter arrives in Caesarea, explains that God has shown him not to call any man common, and Cornelius recounts his vision.

segments.title: Peter's Sermon
segments.gist: Peter preaches that God is no respecter of persons, proclaims Jesus as Lord and judge, and offers forgiveness of sins through him.

segments.title: Gentiles Receive the Spirit
segments.gist: The Holy Ghost falls on the Gentile listeners, and Peter commands them to be baptized in the name of the Lord.

11.summary: Peter defends his fellowship with Gentiles before the Jerusalem church, recounting his vision and Cornelius's conversion, and they glorify God. Later, Barnabas brings Saul from Tarsus to Antioch, where disciples are first called Christians, and relief is sent to Judea during a famine.

segments.title: Peter Recounts His Vision
segments.gist: Peter explains to the Jerusalem brethren his vision of clean and unclean animals and the Spirit's command to go with Cornelius's messengers.

segments.title: Barnabas Sent to Antioch
segments.gist: The church in Jerusalem sends Barnabas to Antioch, where he sees God's grace and encourages the disciples to remain faithful.

segments.title: Saul Brought to Antioch
segments.gist: Barnabas brings Saul from Tarsus, and for a year they teach the disciples in Antioch, where they are first called Christians.

segments.title: Famine Relief Sent to Judea
segments.gist: Prophets foretell a famine, and the disciples in Antioch send relief to Judea by the hands of Barnabas and Saul.

12.summary: Herod Agrippa kills James the brother of John and imprisons Peter, intending to execute him after Passover. An angel frees Peter from prison, and he returns to a prayer gathering at Mary's house. Herod later dies at Caesarea after accepting divine honors, and the church continues to grow.

segments.title: Herod Kills James and Imprisons Peter
segments.gist: Herod kills James and arrests Peter during Passover, intending to bring him before the people after the feast.

segments.title: Angel Frees Peter from Prison
segments.gist: An angel appears in Peter's cell, chains fall off, and he leads Peter past the guards and out of the prison.

segments.title: Peter Returns to Prayer Gathering
segments.gist: Peter knocks at Mary's house, the praying believers are astonished, and Herod later executes the guards.

segments.title: Herod's Death and Church Growth
segments.gist: Herod dies at Caesarea after accepting divine praise, while the word of God grows and Barnabas and Saul return to Antioch.

13.summary: The church at Antioch sets apart Barnabas and Saul for missionary work, and they travel through Cyprus and Pisidian Antioch. There Paul preaches in the synagogue, recounting Israel's history and proclaiming Jesus as the promised Savior, which draws mixed reactions from Jews and Gentiles. Opposition arises, and the missionaries turn to the Gentiles before being expelled from the region.

segments.title: Barnabas and Saul Sent Out
segments.gist: The church at Antioch fasts and prays, then sends Barnabas and Saul on a mission by the Holy Spirit.

segments.title: Ministry in Cyprus
segments.gist: Barnabas and Saul preach in Cyprus, confront the sorcerer Elymas, and convert the proconsul Sergius Paulus.

segments.title: Arrival at Pisidian Antioch
segments.gist: Paul and his companions travel to Pisidian Antioch and are invited to speak in the synagogue.

segments.title: Paul Recounts Israel's History
segments.gist: Paul reviews God's dealings with Israel from Egypt to David and John the Baptist, leading up to Jesus.

segments.title: Paul Proclaims Jesus as Savior
segments.gist: Paul declares Jesus as the promised Savior, crucified and risen, and warns his hearers against unbelief.

segments.title: Mixed Response and Opposition
segments.gist: Many Gentiles believe, but Jewish leaders oppose Paul and Barnabas, who turn to the Gentiles and are expelled.

14.summary: Paul and Barnabas preach in Iconium, where many believe but opposition forces them to flee to Lystra and Derbe. In Lystra, Paul heals a lame man, and the crowd tries to worship them as gods; Jews from Antioch and Iconium turn the crowd against Paul and stone him, but he survives and continues with Barnabas, strengthening disciples and appointing elders before returning to Antioch in Syria.

segments.title: Paul and Barnabas in Iconium
segments.gist: They preach in the synagogue, many believe, but opposition divides the city and they flee.

segments.title: Healing at Lystra and mistaken worship
segments.gist: Paul heals a lame man; the crowd calls them gods, but they restrain them and preach the living God.

segments.title: Paul stoned and survives
segments.gist: Jews from Antioch and Iconium persuade the crowd to stone Paul, but he revives and leaves with Barnabas.

segments.title: Strengthening disciples and appointing elders
segments.gist: They preach in Derbe, then return through the cities, encouraging believers and appointing elders in each church.

segments.title: Return to Antioch and report
segments.gist: They pass through Pisidia and Pamphylia, sail to Antioch, and report all God had done with them.

15.summary: The Jerusalem council settles the question of whether Gentile converts must be circumcised, with Peter, Paul, Barnabas, and James arguing that salvation is by grace; a letter is sent to Antioch. Later, Paul and Barnabas separate over John Mark, and Paul takes Silas through Syria and Cilicia.

segments.title: Dispute over circumcision
segments.gist: Men from Judea teach that circumcision is necessary for salvation, prompting sharp debate between them and Paul and Barnabas.

segments.title: Peter and the apostles speak
segments.gist: Peter recounts God's acceptance of Gentiles by faith, and Paul and Barnabas report the signs and wonders God did among the Gentiles.

segments.title: James gives judgment
segments.gist: James cites the prophets and proposes not troubling Gentile converts, but writing them to abstain from pollutions of idols, fornication, things strangled, and blood.

segments.title: Letter to Gentile believers
segments.gist: The apostles and elders send Judas and Silas with Paul and Barnabas, carrying a letter that frees Gentiles from circumcision while urging abstinence from idolatry, blood, things strangled, and fornication.

segments.title: Antioch rejoices and Paul stays
segments.gist: The assembly at Antioch reads the letter and rejoices; Judas and Silas encourage the believers, and Paul and Barnabas remain teaching.

segments.title: Paul and Barnabas separate
segments.gist: Paul proposes revisiting the churches; a sharp disagreement over John Mark leads Barnabas to sail to Cyprus with Mark, while Paul takes Silas through Syria and Cilicia.

16.summary: Paul and Silas travel through Derbe, Lystra, and Phrygia, where Timothy joins them and they are redirected by the Spirit to Macedonia. In Philippi, Lydia believes, a slave girl is freed from a spirit of divination, and Paul and Silas are beaten and imprisoned, but an earthquake opens the doors and the jailer and his household are baptized. After being released and encouraging the believers, they depart.

segments.title: Timothy Joins Paul and Silas
segments.gist: Paul and Silas travel through Derbe and Lystra, where Timothy is well reported of and joins them; they deliver the decrees to the churches.

segments.title: Spirit Redirects to Macedonia
segments.gist: The Holy Spirit forbids preaching in Asia, and a vision of a Macedonian man leads Paul to conclude God has called them to preach there.

segments.title: Lydia Believes in Philippi
segments.gist: In Philippi, Lydia, a seller of purple, hears Paul and her heart is opened; she and her household are baptized and she urges them to stay at her house.

segments.title: Paul and Silas Beaten and Imprisoned
segments.gist: Paul casts a spirit of divination out of a slave girl, angering her masters; they drag Paul and Silas before the magistrates, who beat and imprison them.

segments.title: Earthquake and Jailer's Conversion
segments.gist: At midnight, an earthquake opens the prison doors; the jailer, about to kill himself, is stopped by Paul, believes, and is baptized with his household.

segments.title: Release and Departure from Philippi
segments.gist: The magistrates send to release Paul and Silas, but Paul demands they come themselves; they are brought out, encouraged, and depart after visiting Lydia.

17.summary: Paul and Silas preach in Thessalonica, where Jason is dragged before the rulers; they then go to Berea, where many search the Scriptures daily, but trouble follows and Paul goes to Athens. There he addresses the Areopagus, proclaiming the unknown God and the resurrection, and some mock while others believe.

segments.title: Paul Preaches in Thessalonica
segments.gist: Paul reasons in the synagogue for three sabbaths, some believe, but jealous Jews set the city in an uproar and assault Jason's house.

segments.title: Bereans Search the Scriptures
segments.gist: Paul and Silas go to Berea, where the people receive the word eagerly and search the Scriptures daily; Jews from Thessalonica stir up trouble, so Paul departs.

segments.title: Paul in Athens
segments.gist: Paul waits in Athens, disputes in the synagogue and marketplace, and is brought to the Areopagus by philosophers curious about his new teaching.

segments.title: Paul's Areopagus Speech
segments.gist: Paul proclaims the unknown God as creator and judge, calls for repentance, and speaks of the resurrection; some mock, some delay, and a few believe.

18.summary: Paul leaves Athens for Corinth, where he works as a tentmaker with Aquila and Priscilla and preaches in the synagogue until opposition drives him to the Gentiles. He stays eighteen months, is brought before the governor Gallio (who dismisses the charge), then travels to Ephesus, Jerusalem, and Antioch before returning to Galatia and Phrygia. The chapter closes with Apollos, an eloquent but partially instructed preacher, being corrected by Aquila and Priscilla and sent on to Achaia.

segments.title: Paul joins Aquila and Priscilla
segments.gist: Paul arrives in Corinth, stays with the tentmakers Aquila and Priscilla, and works alongside them.

segments.title: Paul preaches and turns to Gentiles
segments.gist: Paul testifies in the synagogue, is opposed, shakes off his garments, and moves to Justus's house, where many Corinthians believe; the Lord encourages him in a vision.

segments.title: Gallio dismisses the charge
segments.gist: The Jews bring Paul before the governor Gallio, who refuses to judge a matter of their law and drives them from the judgment seat; Sosthenes is beaten.

segments.title: Paul's journey to Antioch and back
segments.gist: Paul sails with Aquila and Priscilla, cuts his hair at Cenchrea, greets the church in Ephesus, goes to Jerusalem and Antioch, then travels through Galatia and Phrygia strengthening disciples.

segments.title: Apollos instructed and sent out
segments.gist: Apollos, an eloquent Alexandrian, preaches boldly in Ephesus but knows only John's baptism; Aquila and Priscilla instruct him, and he goes to Achaia to refute the Jews publicly.

19.summary: Paul arrives in Ephesus, where he re-baptizes disciples of John with the Holy Spirit and teaches daily in the school of Tyrannus for two years, so that many are healed and repent. A confrontation with itinerant Jewish exorcists and the burning of magic books shows the gospel's power, but a riot led by the silversmith Demetrius over the loss of trade in Diana's shrines forces Paul to leave for Macedonia.

segments.title: Paul Re-baptizes John's Disciples
segments.gist: Paul finds disciples of John in Ephesus, explains baptism into Christ, and they receive the Holy Spirit with tongues and prophecy.

segments.title: Paul Teaches Daily in Ephesus
segments.gist: Paul preaches boldly in the synagogue for three months, then teaches daily in the school of Tyrannus for two years.

segments.title: Miracles and Magic Books Burned
segments.gist: Special miracles occur through Paul, itinerant exorcists are overpowered, and believers burn their magic books, advancing the gospel.

segments.title: Paul Plans to Travel
segments.gist: Paul resolves to go to Jerusalem via Macedonia and Achaia, and sends Timothy and Erastus ahead to Macedonia.

segments.title: Riot of the Silversmiths
segments.gist: Demetrius stirs a riot against Paul for threatening the trade in Diana's shrines, and the town clerk quiets the assembly.

20.summary: Paul travels through Macedonia and Greece, raises Eutychus after he falls from a window during a long sermon in Troas, and then journeys to Miletus. There he summons the Ephesian elders, recounts his ministry among them, warns of coming trials and false teachers, and commits them to God before a tearful farewell.

segments.title: Paul's Journey Through Macedonia and Greece
segments.gist: Paul travels through Macedonia and Greece, encouraging believers, then plans to return through Macedonia toward Jerusalem.

segments.title: Eutychus Raised at Troas
segments.gist: During a long sermon in Troas, Eutychus falls from a window and dies, but Paul embraces him and he is revived.

segments.title: Journey to Miletus
segments.gist: Paul travels by ship from Troas to Miletus, skipping Ephesus to save time before Pentecost.

segments.title: Paul Recounts His Ministry
segments.gist: Paul tells the Ephesian elders how he served among them with humility and tears, teaching publicly and house to house.

segments.title: Warning and Commendation
segments.gist: Paul warns the elders of false teachers, commends them to God, and reminds them of his selfless labor.

segments.title: Farewell at Miletus
segments.gist: Paul kneels and prays with the elders, who weep and embrace him, sorrowing most that they will not see him again.

21.summary: Paul and his companions sail from Miletus to Tyre and Caesarea, where disciples repeatedly warn him by the Spirit not to go to Jerusalem. Despite their pleas, Paul insists on going, and in Jerusalem he is seized by a mob in the temple, leading to his arrest by Roman soldiers.

segments.title: Voyage from Miletus to Tyre
segments.gist: Paul and his companions sail from Miletus, passing Cos, Rhodes, and Patara, and find a ship going to Phoenicia.

segments.title: Disciples in Tyre Warn Paul
segments.gist: In Tyre, disciples urge Paul through the Spirit not to go to Jerusalem, but he insists, and they say, 'The Lord's will be done.'

segments.title: Journey to Caesarea
segments.gist: Paul and his company travel from Tyre to Caesarea and stay with Philip the evangelist.

segments.title: Agabus's Prophecy and Paul's Resolve
segments.gist: Agabus binds his own hands and feet with Paul's belt, prophesying the Jews will bind Paul in Jerusalem; Paul refuses to be dissuaded.

segments.title: Paul Seized in the Temple
segments.gist: Jews from Asia stir up a mob against Paul, drag him out of the temple, and beat him until Roman soldiers rescue him.

segments.title: Paul Requests to Speak
segments.gist: As he is carried into the castle, Paul asks the chief captain for permission to speak to the people.

22.summary: Paul addresses the crowd in Jerusalem from the temple stairs, recounting his former persecution of Christians and his dramatic conversion on the road to Damascus. He describes his vision in the temple and his commission to preach to the Gentiles, which provokes the crowd to demand his death. The chief captain then orders Paul to be brought into the castle and examined by scourging, but Paul reveals his Roman citizenship, causing the captain to fear and halt the proceedings.

segments.title: Paul speaks to the crowd
segments.gist: Paul stands on the stairs, gestures for silence, and addresses the crowd in Hebrew, identifying himself as a Jew from Tarsus.

segments.title: Paul recounts his conversion
segments.gist: Paul describes his persecution of Christians, his journey to Damascus, and his encounter with the risen Jesus, including Ananias's role.

segments.title: Paul's temple vision and commission
segments.gist: Paul tells of his vision in the temple where Jesus sent him to preach to the Gentiles far away.

segments.title: Crowd demands Paul's death
segments.gist: The crowd erupts in anger, demanding Paul's death, and the chief captain orders him brought into the castle to be scourged.

segments.title: Paul reveals Roman citizenship
segments.gist: Paul asserts his Roman citizenship, causing the centurion and chief captain to fear and stop the examination.

23.summary: Paul defends himself before the Jewish council, causing a dispute between Pharisees and Sadducees. A plot to kill him is uncovered by his nephew, and the chief captain sends him under guard to Caesarea to appear before Governor Felix.

segments.title: Paul before the council
segments.gist: Paul declares his good conscience, is struck by order of the high priest, and rebukes the injustice.

segments.title: Pharisees and Sadducees dispute
segments.gist: Paul identifies as a Pharisee, causing a division over resurrection, and the captain rescues him from the uproar.

segments.title: Plot to kill Paul
segments.gist: Jews bind themselves to kill Paul, but his nephew reports the plot to the chief captain.

segments.title: Paul sent to Felix
segments.gist: The captain sends Paul with a large guard to Caesarea and writes a letter to Governor Felix explaining the case.

segments.title: Paul arrives in Caesarea
segments.gist: Paul is brought to Caesarea, and Felix orders him kept in Herod's judgment hall until his accusers arrive.

24.summary: Paul is brought before Felix the governor in Caesarea, where the high priest Ananias and the lawyer Tertullus accuse him of sedition and profaning the temple. Paul defends himself, denying the charges and explaining his faith and visit to Jerusalem. Felix postpones a decision, keeps Paul in custody, and later hears him again with his wife Drusilla, hoping for a bribe, but leaves him imprisoned for two years until Festus succeeds him.

segments.title: Tertullus Accuses Paul Before Felix
segments.gist: The high priest Ananias and elders bring charges against Paul through the lawyer Tertullus, accusing him of sedition and profaning the temple.

segments.title: Paul's Defense Before Felix
segments.gist: Paul denies the charges, explains his visit to Jerusalem to bring alms and offerings, and declares his hope in the resurrection.

segments.title: Felix Postpones Decision
segments.gist: Felix, familiar with the Way, defers judgment until Lysias the chief captain comes, and orders Paul kept under guard with some liberty.

segments.title: Felix and Drusilla Hear Paul
segments.gist: Felix and his wife Drusilla listen to Paul speak of faith in Christ, but Felix trembles, hopes for a bribe, and leaves Paul imprisoned for two years.

25.summary: Paul, held in Caesarea, is tried before the new governor Festus, who hears the Jewish leaders' charges and Paul's defense. Festus, seeking to please the Jews, asks if Paul will go to Jerusalem for trial, but Paul appeals to Caesar. Festus then presents Paul's case to King Agrippa, who agrees to hear Paul the next day.

segments.title: Festus hears Jewish charges
segments.gist: Festus arrives in the province, and the chief priests and Jewish leaders present their case against Paul, asking for him to be brought to Jerusalem.

segments.title: Paul defends before Festus
segments.gist: Festus convenes the court, the Jews accuse Paul, and Paul denies wrongdoing against the law, the temple, or Caesar.

segments.title: Paul appeals to Caesar
segments.gist: Festus asks if Paul will go to Jerusalem for trial; Paul refuses and appeals to Caesar, and Festus grants the appeal.

segments.title: Festus presents case to Agrippa
segments.gist: Festus explains Paul's case to King Agrippa, and Agrippa agrees to hear Paul the next day.

26.summary: Paul, brought before King Agrippa and Bernice, recounts his life as a Pharisee, his former persecution of Christians, and his dramatic conversion on the road to Damascus, insisting he is on trial for hoping in God's promise to the fathers. He presses Agrippa to believe, but Agrippa dismisses him, and the officials agree he could have been freed had he not appealed to Caesar.

segments.title: Paul before Agrippa
segments.gist: Agrippa invites Paul to speak, and Paul begins his defense, expressing gratitude for the opportunity.

segments.title: Paul's former life
segments.gist: Paul recounts his strict Pharisaic upbringing and his active persecution of Christians, including imprisonment and consent to death.

segments.title: Damascus road conversion
segments.gist: Paul describes seeing a heavenly light and hearing Jesus, who commissions him to turn Gentiles from darkness to light.

segments.title: Paul's obedience and trial
segments.gist: Paul explains he obeyed the heavenly vision, preaching repentance to Jews and Gentiles, and that this hope in the resurrection is why he is accused.

segments.title: Agrippa's response
segments.gist: Festus calls Paul mad, and Paul appeals to Agrippa, who asks if Paul expects to make him a Christian; Paul expresses his wish that all would believe.

segments.title: Verdict of innocence
segments.gist: The king and officials withdraw, agree Paul has done nothing deserving death, and note he could have been freed if he had not appealed to Caesar.

27.summary: Paul, a prisoner, is sent by ship toward Rome. After a warning from Paul, the ship is caught in a violent storm for many days, and all hope is lost. Paul encourages the crew with a promise from God that everyone will survive, though the ship will be lost. The ship runs aground and all 276 people on board reach land safely.

segments.title: Paul's voyage begins
segments.gist: Paul and other prisoners are put under Julius and sail along the coast, stopping at Sidon and Myra.

segments.title: Paul warns of danger
segments.gist: Paul advises against sailing, but the centurion and shipmaster decide to continue.

segments.title: Storm and despair
segments.gist: A violent storm strikes, the ship is driven and lightened, and all hope of survival is lost.

segments.title: Paul's encouraging vision
segments.gist: Paul tells the crew an angel promised him that all lives would be saved, though the ship would be lost.

segments.title: Sailors attempt to escape
segments.gist: Sailors try to flee in the boat, but Paul warns that they must stay, and soldiers cut the boat away.

segments.title: Shipwreck and safe landing
segments.gist: Paul urges everyone to eat, they lighten the ship, it runs aground and breaks up, and all 276 reach land safely.

28.summary: Paul and his companions are shipwrecked on Malta, where Paul is bitten by a viper but unharmed, and he heals the island's sick. After three months they resume the journey to Rome, where Paul, under house arrest, preaches to the Jews and then to the Gentiles for two years.

segments.title: Paul Bitten by Viper
segments.gist: The shipwrecked survivors land on Malta; Paul is bitten by a viper but shakes it off unharmed, and the islanders call him a god.

segments.title: Paul Heals the Sick
segments.gist: Paul heals Publius's father and many others on the island, and the islanders honor the group with gifts.

segments.title: Journey to Rome
segments.gist: After three months, the group sails to Rome via Syracuse, Rhegium, and Puteoli, where Paul meets brethren and is allowed to stay alone with a guard.

segments.title: Paul Addresses Roman Jews
segments.gist: Paul calls the Jewish leaders together, explains his imprisonment and appeal to Caesar, and they agree to hear his views on the sect.

segments.title: Mixed Response to Paul's Preaching
segments.gist: Paul preaches Jesus from the Law and Prophets all day; some believe, others reject, and Paul declares that salvation has been sent to the Gentiles.

segments.title: Paul Preaches in Rome
segments.gist: Paul remains two years in his own hired house, boldly preaching the kingdom of God and teaching about Jesus without hindrance.

1.summary: Paul opens his letter to the Romans by identifying himself as a servant of Jesus Christ and summarizing the gospel he preaches. He expresses his desire to visit Rome to strengthen the believers there, then declares that the gospel is God's power for salvation to everyone who believes. He then describes the downward spiral of humanity: despite knowing God through creation, people turned to idolatry, and God gave them over to degrading passions and a reprobate mind, listing various sins.

segments.title: Paul's Greeting and Gospel Summary
segments.gist: Paul introduces himself as a servant of Christ, called to be an apostle, and summarizes the gospel concerning God's Son, promised through the prophets.

segments.title: Paul's Desire to Visit Rome
segments.gist: Paul thanks God for the Roman believers' faith and expresses his longing to visit them to impart spiritual gifts and preach the gospel, acknowledging his obligation to all people.

segments.title: The Power of the Gospel
segments.gist: Paul declares the gospel is God's power for salvation to everyone who believes, revealing God's righteousness from faith to faith, as the just shall live by faith.

segments.title: Humanity's Suppression of Truth
segments.gist: Paul describes how people suppress the truth about God, who is evident in creation, and instead turn to idolatry, worshiping created things rather than the Creator.

segments.title: God Gives Them Over to Sin
segments.gist: Because of their idolatry, God gives people over to unclean desires, dishonorable passions, and a reprobate mind, resulting in a catalog of sins and approval of those who practice them.

2.summary: Paul argues that God's judgment is impartial, falling equally on Jews and Gentiles who do evil and rewarding those who do good. He insists that hearing the law does not justify anyone; only doing it does, and that true Jewishness is inward, not merely external.

segments.title: God's impartial judgment
segments.gist: Paul condemns those who judge others while doing the same things, warning that God's judgment is according to truth and will render to every person according to their deeds.

segments.title: Law and conscience
segments.gist: Paul explains that those without the law perish without it, while those under the law are judged by it, and that Gentiles who do the law by nature show it written on their hearts.

segments.title: The Jew's hypocrisy
segments.gist: Paul challenges the Jew who boasts in the law but breaks it, causing God's name to be blasphemed among the Gentiles.

segments.title: True circumcision
segments.gist: Paul argues that circumcision is valuable only if one keeps the law, and that true Jewishness is inward, of the heart, not merely outward in the flesh.

3.summary: Paul argues that both Jews and Gentiles are under sin and accountable to God, quoting scripture to show universal guilt. He then explains that righteousness comes through faith in Jesus Christ, apart from the law, and that justification is by grace through redemption in Christ.

segments.title: Jewish Advantage and Universal Guilt
segments.gist: Paul acknowledges the Jews' advantage in having God's oracles but declares that all, Jews and Gentiles, are under sin.

segments.title: Scripture Declares All Under Sin
segments.gist: Paul strings together Old Testament quotations to prove that no one is righteous and that the law brings only the knowledge of sin.

segments.title: Righteousness Through Faith in Christ
segments.gist: God's righteousness is now revealed apart from the law, available through faith in Jesus Christ to all who believe, who are justified freely by his grace.

segments.title: Boasting Excluded by Faith
segments.gist: Paul concludes that boasting is excluded because justification is by faith, not works, and that God justifies both Jews and Gentiles through faith, upholding the law.

4.summary: Paul uses Abraham as the central example to prove that justification comes by faith rather than by works or circumcision. He argues from Scripture and David's testimony that righteousness is credited apart from works, and that the promise to Abraham's seed is sure only through faith, not the law.

segments.title: Abraham justified by faith
segments.gist: Paul asks what Abraham gained by works, shows that his faith was counted for righteousness, and cites David's blessing on the forgiven.

segments.title: Circumcision a seal of faith
segments.gist: Paul explains that Abraham's righteousness was credited before circumcision, making him the father of all who believe, circumcised or not.

segments.title: Promise through faith, not law
segments.gist: The promise to Abraham and his seed came through the righteousness of faith, not the law, so that it might be by grace and sure to all his seed.

segments.title: Abraham's faith and our justification
segments.gist: Abraham believed God's promise against hope, being fully persuaded of God's power, and his faith was credited as righteousness, written also for our justification through Christ's death and resurrection.

5.summary: Paul describes how believers, justified by faith, have peace with God and access to grace, and he traces the chain from tribulation to hope through the love of God poured out by the Holy Spirit. He contrasts Adam, through whom sin and death entered the world, with Christ, whose obedience brings justification and life to many.

segments.title: Peace with God through faith
segments.gist: Being justified by faith, believers have peace with God, access to grace, and rejoice in hope of God's glory.

segments.title: Christ died for the ungodly
segments.gist: Paul declares that Christ died for the ungodly and sinners, proving God's love, and now believers are saved from wrath and reconciled.

segments.title: Sin and death through Adam
segments.gist: Sin entered the world through one man, Adam, bringing death to all, and death reigned even over those who did not sin as Adam did.

segments.title: Grace abounds through Christ
segments.gist: The free gift through Christ is far greater than Adam's trespass, bringing justification and reigning in life to those who receive it.

segments.title: Righteousness and life in Christ
segments.gist: Through one man's disobedience many were made sinners, but through Christ's obedience many are made righteous, and grace reigns unto eternal life.

6.summary: Paul answers the objection that grace encourages sin, insisting that believers who are baptized into Christ's death are dead to sin and alive to God. He urges them to present their members as instruments of righteousness, and explains that freedom from sin under grace leads to sanctification and eternal life, while sin's wage is death.

segments.title: Dead to Sin in Baptism
segments.gist: Paul rejects the idea that grace permits sin, asking how those who died to sin can live in it, and points to baptism into Christ's death.

segments.title: Buried and Raised with Christ
segments.gist: Believers are buried and raised with Christ so they may walk in newness of life, and their old man is crucified to free them from sin.

segments.title: Do Not Let Sin Reign
segments.gist: Paul commands believers not to let sin rule in their mortal bodies or yield their members to unrighteousness, since they are under grace.

segments.title: Slaves of Righteousness
segments.gist: Paul contrasts slavery to sin, which leads to death, with slavery to righteousness, which leads to sanctification and eternal life through Christ.
