7.summary: Paul illustrates the believer's release from the law through the analogy of a wife freed from her husband by his death, then describes the law's role in revealing sin and his own inner struggle between the desire to do good and the power of sin dwelling in him, ending with a cry for deliverance through Jesus Christ.

segments.title: Released from the Law
segments.gist: Paul uses the example of a woman bound to her husband by law until his death to show believers are freed from the law to belong to Christ.

segments.title: The Law Reveals Sin
segments.gist: Paul argues that the law is not sin but reveals sin, using the commandment against coveting to show how sin sprang to life and brought death.

segments.title: The Inner Struggle
segments.gist: Paul describes the conflict between the law of God in his mind and the law of sin in his members, lamenting his condition and thanking God for deliverance through Jesus Christ.

8.summary: Romans 8 declares that there is no condemnation for those in Christ Jesus, who walk after the Spirit and are set free from sin and death. It contrasts life in the flesh with life in the Spirit, affirms believers as children and heirs of God, and describes creation's groaning for redemption. The chapter concludes with a triumphant assurance that nothing can separate believers from the love of God in Christ.

segments.title: No Condemnation in Christ
segments.gist: Those in Christ are free from condemnation because the law of the Spirit of life has set them free from sin and death.

segments.title: Life in the Spirit vs Flesh
segments.gist: Paul contrasts minds set on the flesh, which leads to death, with minds set on the Spirit, which brings life and peace.

segments.title: Led by the Spirit as Heirs
segments.gist: Believers are debtors not to the flesh but to the Spirit, and as children of God they are heirs with Christ.

segments.title: Creation's Groaning for Redemption
segments.gist: Creation waits for the revealing of God's children and groans for freedom, while believers eagerly await their adoption.

segments.title: The Spirit's Intercession
segments.gist: The Spirit helps in weakness and intercedes for believers according to God's will, working all things for good.

segments.title: Nothing Can Separate Us
segments.gist: Paul triumphantly declares that God is for us and nothing can separate believers from the love of God in Christ Jesus.

9.summary: Paul expresses deep sorrow for Israel and affirms God's sovereign election, showing that not all physical descendants of Abraham are true children of promise. He cites Old Testament examples of God's sovereign choice and explains that righteousness comes by faith, not by works, while Israel stumbled over the stumbling stone.

segments.title: Paul's Sorrow for Israel
segments.gist: Paul declares his great sorrow and unceasing anguish for his kinsmen according to the flesh, wishing himself accursed for their sake.

segments.title: God's Sovereign Election
segments.gist: Paul shows that God's word has not failed, illustrating with Isaac and Jacob that the children of promise, not merely physical descendants, are counted as seed.

segments.title: God's Mercy and Hardening
segments.gist: Paul defends God's justice, explaining that He has mercy on whom He wills and hardens whom He wills, using Pharaoh as an example and the potter and clay imagery.

segments.title: Prophecies of Inclusion
segments.gist: Paul cites Hosea and Isaiah to show that God calls both Jews and Gentiles, and that a remnant of Israel will be saved.

segments.title: Righteousness by Faith
segments.gist: Paul explains that Gentiles attained righteousness by faith, while Israel, seeking it by works, stumbled over the stumbling stone, Christ.

10.summary: Paul expresses his desire for Israel's salvation, contrasting the righteousness of faith with the righteousness of the law. He explains that Christ is the end of the law and that salvation comes through confessing Jesus as Lord and believing in His resurrection, which is available to all. He then asks whether Israel has heard and understood the gospel, citing scripture to show that Israel's rejection was foretold and that God extends salvation to the Gentiles.

segments.title: Paul's Desire for Israel's Salvation
segments.gist: Paul expresses his heartfelt desire and prayer for Israel's salvation, acknowledging their zeal for God but lack of knowledge.

segments.title: Righteousness by Faith vs. Law
segments.gist: Paul contrasts the righteousness of the law with the righteousness of faith, explaining that salvation comes through confessing Jesus and believing in His resurrection.

segments.title: The Necessity of Preaching the Gospel
segments.gist: Paul argues that people must hear the gospel to believe, and preachers must be sent, concluding that faith comes by hearing the word of God.

segments.title: Israel's Disobedience and God's Reach to Gentiles
segments.gist: Paul asks if Israel has heard and known the gospel, citing scripture to show that God will provoke Israel to jealousy through Gentiles and that Israel remains disobedient.

11.summary: Paul argues that God has not rejected Israel, using himself and the remnant as proof. He explains that Israel's stumbling is temporary and that Gentiles' inclusion will provoke Israel to jealousy, leading to Israel's eventual restoration. The chapter ends with a doxology praising God's unsearchable wisdom.

segments.title: God Has Not Cast Away Israel
segments.gist: Paul denies that God rejected Israel, citing the remnant and Elijah's complaint, and says the elect obtained righteousness while others were blinded.

segments.title: Israel's Fall and Gentile Grafting
segments.gist: Paul explains that Israel's stumbling brought salvation to Gentiles to provoke Israel to jealousy, and warns Gentiles grafted in not to boast but to fear.

segments.title: All Israel Shall Be Saved
segments.gist: Paul reveals the mystery that Israel's blindness is temporary until the fullness of the Gentiles, after which all Israel will be saved, for God's gifts and calling are irrevocable.

segments.title: Doxology of God's Wisdom
segments.gist: Paul praises the depth of God's wisdom and knowledge, declaring that all things are from Him and to Him be glory forever.

12.summary: Paul urges believers to present their bodies as living sacrifices and to be transformed by renewed minds, then describes the humble, loving conduct of a Christian community, including blessings on persecutors and peace with all.

segments.title: Living Sacrifice and Renewed Mind
segments.gist: Paul appeals to believers to offer their bodies as living sacrifices and to be transformed by the renewing of their minds.

segments.title: Humility and Diverse Gifts
segments.gist: Paul warns against thinking too highly of oneself and describes the varied gifts given to members of the body of Christ.

segments.title: Marks of Genuine Love
segments.gist: Paul lists characteristics of sincere love, including abhorring evil, clinging to good, and being devoted to one another.

segments.title: Blessing Persecutors and Living Humbly
segments.gist: Paul instructs believers to bless those who persecute them, to rejoice and weep with others, and to live in harmony.

segments.title: Overcoming Evil with Good
segments.gist: Paul urges believers to repay no one evil for evil, to live peaceably, and to overcome evil with good.

13.summary: Paul calls believers to submit to governing authorities as ordained by God, to owe no debt but love, and to live awake and honestly because salvation is near. He urges putting on the Lord Jesus Christ and making no provision for the flesh.

segments.title: Submission to Governing Authorities
segments.gist: Paul instructs believers to be subject to civil rulers, who are God's ministers for order and justice, and to pay taxes and respect.

segments.title: The Debt of Love
segments.gist: Paul says the only ongoing debt is to love one another, for love fulfills the law and does no harm to a neighbor.

segments.title: Wake and Put On Christ
segments.gist: Knowing salvation is near, Paul urges believers to cast off works of darkness, live honestly, and put on the Lord Jesus Christ.

14.summary: Paul addresses disputes among Roman believers over matters of conscience, particularly food and the observance of days. He urges the strong to welcome the weak without passing judgment, insisting that each person answers to the Lord and that love and peace should govern their mutual conduct.

segments.title: Welcome the weak in faith
segments.gist: Paul tells believers to receive those weak in faith without arguing over disputable matters, since God has accepted them.

segments.title: Each accountable to the Lord
segments.gist: Paul explains that whether one regards a day or eats or abstains, all should do so to the Lord, for Christ died and rose to be Lord of both dead and living.

segments.title: Stop judging your brother
segments.gist: Paul warns against despising or judging a brother, since all will stand before God's judgment seat, and urges believers to stop putting stumbling blocks in each other's way.

segments.title: Nothing unclean in itself
segments.gist: Paul affirms that nothing is unclean in itself, but it becomes unclean to one who thinks so; the kingdom of God is righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.

segments.title: Pursue peace and build up
segments.gist: Paul urges believers to pursue peace and mutual edification, to avoid destroying another's faith over food, and to keep their own convictions before God.

15.summary: Paul urges the strong in faith to bear with the weak and to please others rather than themselves, citing Christ's example and the Scriptures. He prays for unity among Jews and Gentiles, grounds his ministry to the Gentiles in prophecy, and outlines his travel plans to visit Rome on his way to Spain after delivering a collection to Jerusalem.

segments.title: Bear with the weak
segments.gist: Paul calls believers to bear the infirmities of the weak, please neighbors, and follow Christ's example of not pleasing himself.

segments.title: Unity and hope
segments.gist: Paul prays that God would grant unity and hope, and that Jews and Gentiles would glorify God together.

segments.title: Paul's ministry to Gentiles
segments.gist: Paul describes his calling as a minister to the Gentiles, citing Old Testament prophecies to justify his mission.

segments.title: Plans to visit Rome
segments.gist: Paul explains his long-standing desire to visit Rome and his plan to stop there on his way to Spain after delivering aid to Jerusalem.

segments.title: Request for prayer
segments.gist: Paul asks the Roman believers to pray for his deliverance from unbelievers in Judea and for the acceptance of his service in Jerusalem.

16.summary: Paul commends Phoebe and greets a long list of believers in Rome, warning them against those who cause divisions and closing with greetings from his companions and a doxology.

segments.title: Commendation of Phoebe
segments.gist: Paul commends Phoebe, a servant of the church at Cenchrea, and asks the Romans to receive her and assist her.

segments.title: Greetings to Roman Believers
segments.gist: Paul sends greetings to many named individuals and households in Rome, including Priscilla and Aquila, and asks them to greet one another with a holy kiss.

segments.title: Warning Against Divisions
segments.gist: Paul warns the Romans to mark and avoid those who cause divisions and offenses contrary to the doctrine, and assures them God will bruise Satan under their feet.

segments.title: Greetings from Companions
segments.gist: Paul conveys greetings from Timothy, Lucius, Jason, Sosipater, and others, including Tertius who wrote the epistle.

segments.title: Closing Doxology
segments.gist: Paul closes with a doxology to God, who is able to establish them according to the gospel and the revelation of the mystery, to whom be glory forever.

1.summary: Paul opens his letter to the church at Corinth with thanksgiving for their gifts and a plea for unity, because reports say they are divided into factions claiming loyalty to different leaders. He contrasts the wisdom of the world with the foolishness of the cross, and reminds them that God chose the weak and lowly, so that their boasting might be in the Lord.

segments.title: Greeting and Thanksgiving
segments.gist: Paul greets the church at Corinth and thanks God for their gifts and calling.

segments.title: Plea for Unity
segments.gist: Paul urges the Corinthians to be united and reports that they are divided into factions.

segments.title: Wisdom of the Cross
segments.gist: Paul contrasts the world's wisdom with the message of the cross, which is foolishness to some but God's power.

segments.title: God Chooses the Weak
segments.gist: Paul reminds the Corinthians that God chose the weak and lowly so that no one might boast before Him.

2.summary: Paul explains that his preaching in Corinth was not with eloquence or human wisdom but in demonstration of the Spirit and power, so that faith would rest in God. He contrasts the wisdom of this world with the hidden wisdom of God revealed by the Spirit, which the natural man cannot receive but the spiritual man discerns.

segments.title: Paul's preaching in weakness
segments.gist: Paul recalls that he came to Corinth without excellence of speech or human wisdom, determined to know only Christ crucified, and his message was in demonstration of the Spirit and power.

segments.title: God's hidden wisdom
segments.gist: Paul speaks wisdom among the mature, yet not the wisdom of this world, but God's hidden wisdom ordained before the world for our glory, which none of the rulers understood.

segments.title: The Spirit reveals God's depths
segments.gist: God has revealed these things by his Spirit, for the Spirit searches all things, even the deep things of God, and believers have received the Spirit to know what God has freely given.

segments.title: Spiritual discernment
segments.gist: Paul contrasts unspiritual and spiritual teaching: the natural man does not accept the things of the Spirit, but the spiritual man judges all things and has the mind of Christ.

3.summary: Paul confronts the Corinthians' jealousy and strife, showing they are still spiritual infants. He explains that he and Apollos are only servants through whom God works, and that Christ is the only foundation. He warns that each person's work will be tested by fire, and that the church is God's temple, which must not be destroyed.

segments.title: Paul Addresses Divisions
segments.gist: Paul tells the Corinthians they are carnal because of envy and strife, and he points out their party slogans.

segments.title: Servants and God's Work
segments.gist: Paul explains that he and Apollos are only ministers through whom God gives the increase, and they are fellow workers with God.

segments.title: Building on the Foundation
segments.gist: Paul warns that each person must build carefully on the foundation of Christ, because their work will be tested by fire.

segments.title: The Church as God's Temple
segments.gist: Paul declares that the church is God's temple and that anyone who destroys it will be destroyed by God.

segments.title: True Wisdom in Christ
segments.gist: Paul urges the Corinthians to become fools for Christ, warning against boasting in human leaders, and reminds them that all things belong to them in Christ.

4.summary: Paul urges the Corinthians to regard him and Apollos as servants and stewards of God's mysteries, judging nothing before the Lord comes. He contrasts the Corinthians' boasting with the apostles' suffering, and appeals to them as a father to imitate him, sending Timothy and warning that he will come to test the proud.

segments.title: Stewards of God's Mysteries
segments.gist: Paul says he and Apollos are servants and stewards, and that the Lord alone judges faithfulness.

segments.title: Warning Against Pride
segments.gist: Paul warns the Corinthians not to boast in one leader over another, since all they have is received.

segments.title: Apostles' Suffering Contrasted
segments.gist: Paul contrasts the Corinthians' self-satisfaction with the apostles' suffering, weakness, and dishonor.

segments.title: Paul as Spiritual Father
segments.gist: Paul appeals to them as a father, urges them to imitate him, and sends Timothy to remind them of his ways.

segments.title: Paul's Coming and Warning
segments.gist: Paul warns the arrogant that he will come soon and test not their words but their power.

5.summary: Paul confronts the Corinthian church about a case of sexual immorality that they have tolerated and even boasted about, instructing them to remove the offender from their fellowship. He explains that a little leaven leavens the whole lump, calls for cleansing and celebration of the Passover with sincerity and truth, and clarifies that his command to separate from immoral people applies to those within the church, not to outsiders.

segments.title: Reported Immorality and Church Pride
segments.gist: Paul reports a case of sexual immorality in the church and rebukes the congregation for being proud instead of mourning.

segments.title: Deliver the Offender to Satan
segments.gist: Paul, though absent, judges the offender and instructs the church to deliver him to Satan for the destruction of the flesh.

segments.title: Leaven and Passover Cleansing
segments.gist: Paul uses the metaphor of leaven to urge the church to purge out the old leaven and keep the feast with sincerity and truth.

segments.title: Separate from Immoral Brethren
segments.gist: Paul clarifies his earlier command: separate from immoral people within the church, not from outsiders, and judge those inside.

6.summary: Paul rebukes the Corinthian believers for taking their disputes to secular courts instead of settling them within the church, and warns that the unrighteous will not inherit God's kingdom. He then addresses sexual immorality, arguing that the body is meant for the Lord and is a temple of the Holy Spirit, so believers should glorify God with their bodies.

segments.title: Lawsuits Before Unbelievers
segments.gist: Paul confronts the Corinthians for taking legal disputes before unjust judges rather than settling them among the saints, who will judge the world.

segments.title: The Unrighteous Will Not Inherit
segments.gist: Paul lists various sinners who will not inherit God's kingdom, reminding the Corinthians that they were washed and sanctified in Christ.

segments.title: Glorify God in Your Body
segments.gist: Paul argues that the body is for the Lord, not for fornication, and that believers' bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit, so they should glorify God.

7.summary: Paul answers the Corinthians' questions about marriage and sexual relations, advising marriage as a remedy against fornication while allowing celibacy for those with the gift. He then addresses mixed marriages, the permanence of marriage, and the priority of peace, before turning to virgins, widows, and the principle that circumstances should not distract from serving the Lord.

segments.title: Marriage and Celibacy
segments.gist: Paul advises marriage to avoid fornication, commands mutual conjugal duty, and permits temporary abstinence for prayer, while acknowledging celibacy as a gift.

segments.title: Mixed Marriages
segments.gist: Paul instructs that a believing spouse should not divorce an unbelieving partner, for the unbeliever is sanctified and may be saved through the believer.

segments.title: Abide in Your Calling
segments.gist: Paul teaches that believers should remain in the social position in which they were called, whether circumcised or not, slave or free, because they are Christ's servants.

segments.title: Advice to Virgins
segments.gist: Paul gives his judgment that, given the present distress, it is good for virgins to remain unmarried, though marriage is not sin; he desires undivided devotion to the Lord.

segments.title: Fathers and Widows
segments.gist: Paul allows a father to give his virgin daughter in marriage without sin, affirms that a widow may marry a believer, but says she is happier if she remains single.

8.summary: Paul addresses the Corinthian believers' question about eating food offered to idols. He agrees that idols are nothing and God is one, but warns that knowledge must be tempered by love, and that exercising one's liberty can harm a weaker brother for whom Christ died.

segments.title: Knowledge vs. Love
segments.gist: Paul contrasts knowledge that puffs up with love that builds up, and notes that true knowledge of God is coupled with being known by Him.

segments.title: One God and One Lord
segments.gist: Paul affirms that an idol is nothing and there is one God, the Father, and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things exist.

segments.title: Weak Conscience and Food
segments.gist: Not all have this knowledge; some, formerly accustomed to idols, eat as if it were sacrificed to an idol, and their weak conscience is defiled, though food itself does not commend us to God.

segments.title: Warning Against Stumbling Others
segments.gist: Paul urges the strong to beware lest their liberty become a stumbling block to the weak, and declares he will abstain from meat forever rather than cause a brother to stumble.

9.summary: Paul defends his apostleship and his right to receive material support from the churches, using his own example of willingly giving up those rights for the sake of the gospel. He explains his flexible approach to different groups in order to win them, and he compares the Christian life to a race requiring self-discipline.

segments.title: Paul's Rights as an Apostle
segments.gist: Paul asserts his freedom and apostleship, and argues from Scripture and common practice that he has the right to material support.

segments.title: Paul's Voluntary Restraint
segments.gist: Paul explains that he has not used these rights, and that he preaches the gospel freely, not seeking payment.

segments.title: Paul's Flexible Approach
segments.gist: Paul describes how he adapts to different groups—Jews, Gentiles, and the weak—in order to win them for the gospel.

segments.title: The Race and Self-Discipline
segments.gist: Paul compares the Christian life to a race, urging self-control and discipline so as not to be disqualified after preaching to others.

10.summary: Paul warns the Corinthians against presumption by recalling Israel's wilderness failures—idolatry, sexual immorality, testing God, and grumbling—which brought judgment despite their privileges. He assures them that temptation is common and God provides a way out, then addresses the practical limits of Christian liberty regarding food offered to idols, urging them to seek God's glory and the good of others.

segments.title: Israel's Wilderness Failures as Warnings
segments.gist: Paul recounts Israel's privileges and their failures in the wilderness, warning the Corinthians that these examples were written to deter them from the same sins.

segments.title: Flee Idolatry; The Lord's Table
segments.gist: Paul commands fleeing idolatry, arguing that participating in the Lord's Supper and in pagan sacrifices cannot be done together without provoking the Lord.

segments.title: Limits of Christian Liberty
segments.gist: Paul explains that while all things are lawful, not all are helpful; believers should consider others' consciences when eating food sold in the market or served by unbelievers.

segments.title: Do All to God's Glory
segments.gist: Paul concludes that all actions should be done for God's glory, giving no offense to Jews, Greeks, or the church, and seeking others' profit for salvation.

11.summary: Paul commends the Corinthians for remembering his teachings but then addresses head coverings and gender roles in worship, arguing from creation and nature. He then rebukes divisions at the Lord's Supper, where some go hungry while others are drunk, and recalls the institution of the supper, warning that unworthy participation brings judgment. He concludes by instructing them to wait for one another and to eat at home if hungry.

segments.title: Head Coverings and Order in Worship
segments.gist: Paul commends the Corinthians, then teaches that women should cover their heads and men should not, based on creation order and nature.

segments.title: Divisions at the Lord's Supper
segments.gist: Paul rebukes the Corinthians because their gatherings cause divisions, with some going hungry while others are drunk.

segments.title: Institution of the Lord's Supper
segments.gist: Paul recounts what he received from the Lord: Jesus took bread and the cup, gave thanks, and told his disciples to do this in remembrance of him.

segments.title: Warning Against Unworthy Participation
segments.gist: Paul warns that anyone who eats and drinks unworthily is guilty of the body and blood of the Lord, and should examine themselves.

12.summary: Paul explains that spiritual gifts, though diverse, all come from the same Spirit and are given for the common good. He compares the church to a body with many members, each necessary and interdependent, and urges members to care for one another without envy or division.

segments.title: Criteria for Spiritual Gifts
segments.gist: Paul reminds the Corinthians that no one speaking by the Spirit of God calls Jesus accursed, and no one can say Jesus is Lord except by the Holy Spirit.

segments.title: Diversity of Gifts from One Spirit
segments.gist: Paul lists various gifts, services, and workings, emphasizing that the same Spirit distributes them to each person as He wills for the common good.

segments.title: The Church as One Body
segments.gist: Paul compares the church to a body with many members, each essential and interdependent, so that there should be no division and all members care for one another.

segments.title: God's Ordering of Members
segments.gist: Paul states that God has appointed various roles in the church and asks rhetorical questions to show that not everyone has the same gift, while encouraging the pursuit of greater gifts.

13.summary: Paul describes the necessity of charity (love) above all spiritual gifts, showing that without it even the most impressive gifts are worthless. He then details the nature of charity and its eternal permanence compared to the temporary gifts of prophecy, tongues, and knowledge.

segments.title: Without Charity, Gifts Are Nothing
segments.gist: Paul declares that even the most extraordinary spiritual gifts and sacrifices are worthless without charity.

segments.title: The Nature of Charity
segments.gist: Paul lists the qualities of charity: it is patient, kind, humble, unselfish, and enduring.

segments.title: Charity Never Fails
segments.gist: Paul contrasts the temporary nature of spiritual gifts with the eternal permanence of charity, faith, and hope.

14.summary: Paul instructs the Corinthians to prioritize prophecy over tongues for the edification of the church, because tongues without interpretation are unintelligible and do not build up others. He gives guidelines for orderly worship, including limits on speaking in tongues and prophecy, and insists that all things be done decently and in order.

segments.title: Prophecy Superior to Tongues
segments.gist: Paul urges the pursuit of love and spiritual gifts, especially prophecy, since tongues without interpretation do not edify the church.

segments.title: Need for Intelligibility
segments.gist: Paul illustrates with musical instruments and the mind that uninterpreted tongues are useless; he will pray and sing with understanding.

segments.title: Tongues as a Sign
segments.gist: Tongues are a sign for unbelievers, prophecy for believers; an unbeliever hearing prophecy is convicted and worships God.

segments.title: Order in Worship
segments.gist: Each should contribute for edification; tongues must be limited and interpreted, and prophets should speak in turn for order.

segments.title: Women, Order, and Conclusion
segments.gist: Women should keep silent in church and ask husbands at home; all things must be done decently and in order.

15.summary: Paul defends the reality of Christ's resurrection, recounting the eyewitness appearances and arguing that if Christ is not raised, faith is vain and the dead are lost. He explains the resurrection body as a transformed, imperishable body, and concludes with a call to steadfastness in light of the final victory over death.

segments.title: The Gospel and Eyewitnesses
segments.gist: Paul reminds the Corinthians of the gospel he preached, listing Christ's death, burial, resurrection, and appearances to Peter, the twelve, and many others.

segments.title: Consequences if No Resurrection
segments.gist: Paul argues that if Christ is not raised, preaching and faith are vain, and believers are still in their sins.

segments.title: Christ the Firstfruits
segments.gist: Christ is risen as the firstfruits; in Adam all die, in Christ all shall be made alive, and he will reign until all enemies are subdued.

segments.title: Why Suffer for the Dead?
segments.gist: Paul questions the practice of baptism for the dead and his own daily peril, arguing that if the dead rise not, one might as well live for the moment.

segments.title: The Resurrection Body
segments.gist: Paul explains that the resurrection body differs from the natural body as a seed differs from the plant, contrasting the first Adam with the last Adam.

segments.title: Victory Over Death
segments.gist: Flesh and blood cannot inherit God's kingdom; the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and the saying will be fulfilled: Death is swallowed up in victory.

16.summary: Paul closes his letter with practical instructions: a collection for the saints in Jerusalem, his travel plans involving Timothy and Apollos, and final exhortations to watchfulness, love, and steadfastness. He sends greetings from the churches of Asia and from Priscilla and Aquila, and signs off with a curse on those who do not love the Lord and a prayer for grace.

segments.title: Collection for the Saints
segments.gist: Paul instructs the Corinthians to set aside money weekly so a collection for the saints in Jerusalem can be ready when he arrives.

segments.title: Paul's Travel Plans
segments.gist: Paul explains he will stay in Ephesus until Pentecost because a great door of opportunity is open, then plans to visit Corinth for an extended stay.

segments.title: Instructions about Timothy and Apollos
segments.gist: Paul asks the Corinthians to receive Timothy without fear and explains that Apollos was unwilling to come now but will visit later.

segments.title: Final Exhortations and Greetings
segments.gist: Paul urges watchfulness, steadfastness, love, and submission to fellow workers, and mentions the household of Stephanas and other laborers.

segments.title: Greetings and Closing
segments.gist: Paul sends greetings from the churches of Asia and from Priscilla and Aquila, and closes with a curse on those who do not love the Lord and a prayer for grace.

1.summary: Paul opens his second letter to the Corinthians by blessing God as the source of all comfort, who consoles him in affliction so he can comfort others. He explains that his recent severe troubles in Asia taught him to trust not in himself but in God, who delivers. He then defends his change of travel plans, insisting his word to them was not fickle and that all God's promises are yes in Christ, and he explains that he spared them a painful visit out of love, not dominance.

segments.title: Greeting and blessing
segments.gist: Paul greets the church at Corinth and blesses God as the Father of mercies and God of all comfort.

segments.title: Comfort in affliction
segments.gist: Paul explains that God comforts him in all his troubles so that he can comfort others with the same comfort.

segments.title: Deliverance from despair
segments.gist: Paul recounts a severe affliction in Asia that brought him to despair, but God delivered him and he trusts God will continue to deliver.

segments.title: Paul's sincere conduct
segments.gist: Paul boasts that his conduct toward the Corinthians has been in holiness and sincerity, not by fleshly wisdom, and he hopes they will fully understand him.

segments.title: Defense of travel plans
segments.gist: Paul defends his change of plans, denying fickleness and affirming that God's promises are yes in Christ, who seals and anoints believers.

segments.title: Spared to spare them
segments.gist: Paul explains he did not return to Corinth to spare them, not to lord over their faith, but as a helper of their joy.

2.summary: Paul explains why he changed his travel plans and did not return to Corinth, clarifying that his earlier letter caused pain but was written out of love. He describes the comfort God gives in affliction and the joy of hearing that the Corinthians had repented and forgiven the offender, and he affirms his sincerity and sufficiency in Christ.

segments.title: Paul's Changed Plans
segments.gist: Paul explains his decision not to visit Corinth again, to spare them grief and to show his love.

segments.title: The Painful Letter
segments.gist: Paul acknowledges the sorrow his previous letter caused but says it was written to show his abundant love.

segments.title: Paul's Sincerity Defended
segments.gist: Paul defends his sincerity and consistency, denying that he makes plans lightly or says yes and no at once.

3.summary: Paul defends his apostolic ministry, calling the Corinthian believers his letter of recommendation written by the Spirit. He contrasts the old covenant of the letter, which brings death and was glorious, with the new covenant of the Spirit, which brings righteousness and freedom, and he describes how believers behold the Lord's glory with unveiled faces and are transformed into the same image.

segments.title: Corinthians as Paul's Letter
segments.gist: Paul says he needs no letters of commendation because the Corinthians themselves are his letter, written by the Spirit on hearts.

segments.title: Sufficiency from God
segments.gist: Paul affirms his sufficiency comes from God, who made him a minister of the new covenant of the Spirit, not the letter.

segments.title: Glory of the Old Covenant
segments.gist: Paul argues that if the ministry of death was glorious, the ministry of the Spirit is far more glorious.

segments.title: Veil over Moses and Israel
segments.gist: Paul compares Israel's veiled understanding to Moses' veil, saying the veil is removed in Christ but remains for those who do not turn to the Lord.

segments.title: Liberty and Transformation
segments.gist: Paul declares that where the Spirit of the Lord is there is liberty, and believers with unveiled faces are transformed into the Lord's glory.

4.summary: Paul declares that his ministry is open and truthful, not veiled, and that he preaches Christ Jesus as Lord rather than himself. He describes the gospel as light shining in darkness and explains that the treasure of this message is carried in fragile human vessels so that the power may be seen as God's. He closes by contrasting present affliction with an eternal weight of glory.

segments.title: Paul's Open Ministry and the Veiled Gospel
segments.gist: Paul says he renounces hidden and dishonest methods, commending himself by plain truth, and notes that the gospel is veiled only to those who are perishing.

segments.title: Light of Christ in Earthen Vessels
segments.gist: Paul describes the light of the knowledge of God's glory in Christ shining in hearts, and says this treasure is held in fragile vessels so the power belongs to God.

segments.title: Faith in Spite of Affliction
segments.gist: Paul cites the psalmist's words of faith and describes being troubled yet not forsaken, carrying Christ's death so his life may appear, all for the sake of the Corinthians and God's glory.

segments.title: Inner Renewal and Eternal Glory
segments.gist: Paul says the outward man decays but the inward man is renewed daily, and present light affliction produces an eternal weight of glory for those who look at things unseen.

5.summary: Paul contrasts the earthly tent with the eternal building from God and the judgment seat of Christ, then declares that Christ's love compels him to persuade others and that in Christ God reconciles the world, making the reconciled into ambassadors of reconciliation.

segments.title: Earthly Tent and Eternal Building
segments.gist: Paul describes the longing to be clothed with the heavenly dwelling and to be present with the Lord.

segments.title: Walking by Faith and Judgment Seat
segments.gist: Paul speaks of walking by faith, pleasing the Lord, and appearing before Christ's judgment seat.

segments.title: Christ's Love Compels Us
segments.gist: Paul explains that the love of Christ constrains him because Christ died for all, so he no longer regards anyone according to the flesh.

segments.title: New Creation and Ministry of Reconciliation
segments.gist: Paul declares that in Christ there is a new creation and that God has given the ministry of reconciliation.

segments.title: Ambassadors for Christ
segments.gist: Paul appeals as an ambassador for Christ to be reconciled to God, for God made Christ to be sin for us.

6.summary: Paul appeals to the Corinthians to receive God's grace without delay, describing his hardships and endurance as a minister of God. He calls for separation from unbelievers and unclean things, promising God's welcome as a Father to his children.

segments.title: Appeal for Grace
segments.gist: Paul urges the Corinthians not to receive God's grace in vain, citing the acceptable time of salvation.

segments.title: Hardships and Endurance
segments.gist: Paul lists his sufferings and virtues as proof of his ministry, commending himself by endurance and godly character.

segments.title: Open Heart Appeal
segments.gist: Paul speaks openly to the Corinthians, asking for equal affection in return for his love.

segments.title: Call to Separation
segments.gist: Paul commands believers to separate from unbelievers, quoting God's promise to dwell with and receive his people.

7.summary: Paul urges the Corinthians to cleanse themselves and make room for him in their hearts, then describes his comfort at Titus's arrival and the good news of the Corinthians' repentance and longing for him. He contrasts godly sorrow that leads to repentance with worldly sorrow that brings death, and rejoices that Titus was refreshed by them.

segments.title: Paul's Affection and Confidence
segments.gist: Paul affirms his love for the Corinthians, expresses his great boldness and comfort in them, and says he is filled with joy despite affliction.

segments.title: Comfort at Titus's Coming
segments.gist: Paul describes his affliction in Macedonia but finds comfort in Titus's arrival and the report of the Corinthians' earnest desire and mourning for him.

segments.title: Godly Sorrow vs Worldly Sorrow
segments.gist: Paul explains that his previous letter caused sorrow, but he rejoices that it led to godly repentance, contrasting it with the sorrow of the world that brings death.

segments.title: Rejoicing in Titus's Refreshment
segments.gist: Paul rejoices that Titus was refreshed by the Corinthians, and expresses his confidence and joy in them, noting that his boasting to Titus was not in vain.

8.summary: Paul urges the Corinthians to complete their collection for the poor saints in Jerusalem, citing the Macedonians' generous example and Christ's self-impoverishment. He explains the principle of giving according to ability, commends Titus and others who will handle the funds, and emphasizes transparency and sincerity in the administration of the gift.

segments.title: Macedonian Example of Generosity
segments.gist: Paul tells how the churches of Macedonia gave generously out of deep poverty, urging the Corinthians to abound in this grace also.

segments.title: Christ's Example and Giving According to Ability
segments.gist: Paul appeals to Christ's poverty that made believers rich, and teaches that giving should be according to what one has, with equality as the goal.

segments.title: Commendation of Titus and Messengers
segments.gist: Paul commends Titus and two other brothers who will carry the collection, emphasizing their earnestness and the need for transparency.

9.summary: Paul explains that he has boasted to the Macedonians about the Corinthians' readiness to give, and he urges them to finish the collection before he arrives so that it is ready as a willing gift, not as an exaction. He then expands on the principle that God loves a cheerful giver, promising that God will supply and multiply their seed, enrich them for generosity, and produce thanksgiving to God through their service.

segments.title: Paul Urges Completion of Collection
segments.gist: Paul says it is superfluous to write about the collection, but he is sending brothers to ensure the Corinthians' readiness, so his boasting about them is not in vain.

segments.title: Cheerful Giving and God's Provision
segments.gist: Paul states that sparing sowing reaps sparingly, God loves a cheerful giver, and God is able to make all grace abound so they may abound in good works.

segments.title: God Multiplies Seed and Increases Fruits
segments.gist: Paul prays God will supply seed to the sower and increase their fruits, enriching them for generosity, which produces thanksgiving to God through the service of this ministry.

10.summary: Paul defends his apostolic authority against critics in Corinth, insisting that his bold letters match his presence and that his boasting is measured by God's standards. He warns that he will deal firmly with disobedience once the Corinthians' obedience is complete, and he grounds his ministry in the Lord's commendation rather than self-praise.

segments.title: Paul's Meekness and Authority
segments.gist: Paul appeals by the meekness of Christ, asking the Corinthians not to force him to be bold against those who accuse him of walking according to the flesh.

segments.title: Letters vs. Bodily Presence
segments.gist: Paul addresses the charge that his letters are weighty but his bodily presence weak, warning that his actions will match his words.

segments.title: Boasting Within God's Measure
segments.gist: Paul refuses to compare himself with self-commending critics, insisting that boasting must be within the measure God has assigned.

11.summary: Paul defends his apostolic authority against rival teachers in Corinth, expressing his jealousy for the church's purity and warning against false apostles. He recounts his sufferings and hardships as proof of his ministry, and ironically boasts in his weaknesses, concluding with his escape from Damascus.

segments.title: Paul's Jealousy and Warning
segments.gist: Paul expresses godly jealousy for the Corinthians and warns them against being deceived by false teachers, as Eve was deceived.

segments.title: Paul's Defense of His Ministry
segments.gist: Paul defends his refusal to take financial support, asserting he preached the gospel freely and will continue to do so to expose false apostles.

segments.title: Paul's Reluctant Boasting
segments.gist: Paul reluctantly boasts as a fool, comparing himself to his opponents who boast in worldly credentials.

segments.title: Paul's Sufferings as Proof
segments.gist: Paul lists his hardships, labors, imprisonments, beatings, and daily concern for the churches, proving his apostolic credentials.

segments.title: Paul Boasts in Weakness
segments.gist: Paul declares he will boast in his weaknesses, and recounts his escape from Damascus as an example of God's deliverance.

12.summary: Paul defends his apostleship by recounting a visionary experience and a thorn in the flesh, then expresses his concern for the Corinthian church and his fear that his upcoming visit may reveal unresolved problems.

segments.title: Paul's Vision and Thorn
segments.gist: Paul describes being caught up to paradise and the thorn in the flesh given to keep him humble, through which Christ's strength is perfected in weakness.

segments.title: Signs of an Apostle
segments.gist: Paul asserts he is not inferior to other apostles and points to the signs, wonders, and mighty deeds he performed among the Corinthians.

segments.title: Plans for a Third Visit
segments.gist: Paul explains his intention to visit Corinth a third time, not to burden them but to seek their spiritual growth, and defends his conduct and that of Titus.

segments.title: Fear of Unresolved Problems
segments.gist: Paul expresses fear that his visit will expose quarrels, jealousy, and moral failures among the Corinthians, and that he will have to grieve over their unrepentant state.

13.summary: Paul closes his second letter to the Corinthians by warning that his upcoming visit will bring decisive discipline to unrepentant sinners, urging the church to examine and prove their own faith, and expressing his hope for their restoration. He ends with a series of brief exhortations and a benediction.

segments.title: Paul's Third Visit Warning
segments.gist: Paul announces his third visit and warns that he will not spare those who have sinned, citing the testimony of two or three witnesses.

segments.title: Examine Yourselves
segments.gist: Paul urges the Corinthians to examine and prove their own faith, and expresses his prayer that they do no evil and become complete.

segments.title: Final Exhortations and Benediction
segments.gist: Paul gives final commands to rejoice, be perfect, be of one mind, and live in peace, closing with a Trinitarian benediction.

1.summary: Paul opens his letter to the Galatians by asserting his apostolic authority from God, then rebukes the churches for quickly turning to a different gospel and pronounces a curse on anyone who preaches another message. He recounts his former life as a persecutor of the church and how God revealed His Son in him, after which he went to Arabia and later met Peter and James in Jerusalem, concluding that he was unknown by face to the churches of Judea, which glorified God because of him.

segments.title: Paul's Greeting and Authority
segments.gist: Paul identifies himself as an apostle not from men but through Jesus Christ and God the Father, and greets the Galatian churches with grace and peace.

segments.title: No Other Gospel
segments.gist: Paul expresses astonishment that the Galatians are turning to a different gospel and declares that anyone preaching another gospel should be accursed.

segments.title: Paul's Former Life and Call
segments.gist: Paul recounts his former life in Judaism, his persecution of the church, and how God revealed His Son in him, after which he went to Arabia and returned to Damascus.

segments.title: Paul Visits Jerusalem and Judea
segments.gist: Three years later Paul went to Jerusalem to see Peter and James, then traveled to Syria and Cilicia, and the churches of Judea glorified God because of him.

2.summary: Paul recounts his visit to Jerusalem fourteen years after his conversion, where he defended the gospel of grace against false brethren and was acknowledged by the church leaders. Later, at Antioch, he publicly rebuked Peter for withdrawing from Gentile believers out of fear, insisting that a person is justified by faith in Christ and not by works of the law.

segments.title: Paul's Jerusalem Visit and Approval
segments.gist: Paul describes going to Jerusalem with Barnabas and Titus, defending the gospel against false brethren, and being acknowledged by James, Cephas, and John.

segments.title: Paul Rebukes Peter at Antioch
segments.gist: Paul confronts Peter publicly for withdrawing from Gentile meals out of fear, calling his behavior inconsistent with the truth of the gospel.

segments.title: Justified by Faith, Not Works
segments.gist: Paul argues that Jews and Gentiles alike are justified by faith in Christ, not by works of the law, and that Christ's death would be in vain if righteousness came through the law.

3.summary: Paul confronts the Galatians for turning from faith to law-keeping, reminding them that Abraham was justified by faith and that the law was a temporary tutor until Christ came. He argues that all who believe, Jew and Gentile alike, are Abraham's heirs and sons of God through faith in Christ.

segments.title: Rebuke for Turning from Faith
segments.gist: Paul asks the Galatians who has bewitched them, reminding them that Christ was crucified before their eyes and that they received the Spirit by faith, not works.

segments.title: Abraham Justified by Faith
segments.gist: Paul cites Abraham's belief being counted for righteousness and says that Gentiles who believe are blessed with faithful Abraham.

segments.title: Law Brings Curse, Christ Redeems
segments.gist: Paul argues that those under the law are under a curse, but Christ redeemed believers from the curse by becoming a curse, so the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles.

segments.title: Promise Precedes the Law
segments.gist: Paul compares the law to a human covenant, explaining that the promise to Abraham and his seed was confirmed by God and cannot be annulled by the law that came later.

segments.title: Purpose of the Law as Tutor
segments.gist: Paul explains that the law was added because of transgressions until Christ came, and that it served as a schoolmaster to bring people to faith, so that after faith comes they are no longer under it.

segments.title: Sons of God Through Faith
segments.gist: Paul declares that all who are baptized into Christ have put on Christ, are one in him, and as Abraham's seed are heirs according to the promise.

4.summary: Paul argues that believers, though heirs, were held in bondage under the law until God sent his Son to redeem them and give them adoption as sons. He appeals to the Galatians not to return to weak and beggarly elements, reminds them of their former reception of him, and uses an allegory of Hagar and Sarah to show that the Jerusalem above is free and that believers are children of promise, not of the bondwoman.

segments.title: Heirs in Bondage Until Adoption
segments.gist: Paul explains that an heir, while a child, is no different from a servant until the appointed time, when God sent his Son to redeem those under the law and give them adoption.

segments.title: Warning Against Returning to Bondage
segments.gist: Paul warns the Galatians not to turn back to weak and beggarly elements after knowing God, expressing fear that his labor was in vain.

segments.title: Remember Your Former Reception
segments.gist: Paul reminds the Galatians how they received him as an angel of God despite his illness, and asks why their attitude has changed.

segments.title: Zeal of False Teachers
segments.gist: Paul contrasts the zeal of false teachers who want to exclude the Galatians with his own desire to see Christ formed in them.

segments.title: Allegory of Hagar and Sarah
segments.gist: Paul uses the two women, Hagar and Sarah, as an allegory of the two covenants, showing that believers are children of the free woman and of promise.

5.summary: Paul declares that Christ has set believers free from the law, warning that circumcision and legalism cut them off from grace. He contrasts the works of the flesh with the fruit of the Spirit, urging believers to walk in the Spirit and fulfill the law of love.

segments.title: Stand Fast in Liberty
segments.gist: Paul urges believers to stand firm in the freedom Christ gives and warns that submitting to circumcision for justification separates them from Christ and grace.

segments.title: Warning Against False Teachers
segments.gist: Paul warns that false teachers are hindering the Galatians and that their influence will be judged, expressing confidence that believers will remain steadfast.

segments.title: Serve One Another in Love
segments.gist: Paul calls believers to use their freedom to serve one another in love, summarizing the law as loving one's neighbor as oneself.

segments.title: Works of the Flesh
segments.gist: Paul lists the works of the flesh and warns that those who practice such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.

segments.title: Fruit of the Spirit
segments.gist: Paul describes the fruit of the Spirit and calls believers to live and walk in the Spirit, not in conceit or envy.

6.summary: Paul instructs the Galatians to restore those overtaken in faults gently, to bear one another's burdens, and to examine their own work. He contrasts sowing to the flesh with sowing to the Spirit, urges perseverance in doing good, and closes with a final warning against those who glory in circumcision, boasting only in the cross of Christ and the new creation.

segments.title: Restore the Fallen Gently
segments.gist: Paul tells the spiritual to restore the fallen meekly, bear burdens, and examine their own work.

segments.title: Sowing to the Spirit
segments.gist: Paul urges sharing with teachers, warns against mocking God, and encourages persistent good works.

segments.title: Boast Only in the Cross
segments.gist: Paul contrasts false teachers' circumcision boast with his own boast in the cross and new creation.

segments.title: Final Blessing and Peace
segments.gist: Paul asks that no one trouble him, citing his scars for Jesus, and pronounces a blessing on Israel.

1.summary: Paul opens his letter to the Ephesians by greeting the saints and blessing God for the spiritual blessings given in Christ, including election, redemption, and the sealing of the Holy Spirit. He then reports his prayer that they may know God's calling, inheritance, and the greatness of His power, which was demonstrated in raising Christ and exalting Him above all things as head of the church.

segments.title: Greeting to the Ephesians
segments.gist: Paul identifies himself as an apostle of Jesus Christ and greets the faithful saints in Ephesus with grace and peace.

segments.title: Blessing God for Spiritual Blessings
segments.gist: Paul blesses God for choosing believers in Christ, redeeming them through His blood, and sealing them with the Holy Spirit.

segments.title: Prayer for Knowledge and Power
segments.gist: Paul prays that believers may know God's calling, inheritance, and the surpassing power shown in Christ's resurrection and exaltation.

2.summary: Paul describes how God made believers alive with Christ even while they were dead in sins, saved them by grace through faith, and united Jewish and Gentile believers into one new body, breaking down the dividing wall and building them together as a dwelling place for God.

segments.title: Dead in Sins Made Alive
segments.gist: Paul recalls that believers were once dead in trespasses and sins, following the world and the prince of the power of the air.

segments.title: Saved by Grace Through Faith
segments.gist: God, rich in mercy, made believers alive with Christ and saved them by grace through faith, not by works, creating them for good works.

segments.title: Gentiles Once Far Off
segments.gist: Paul reminds Gentile believers that they were once aliens from Israel and strangers to the covenants, but are now brought near by Christ's blood.

segments.title: Christ Our Peace and Access
segments.gist: Christ is the peace who broke down the middle wall, reconciled Jew and Gentile into one body through the cross, and gives both access to the Father by one Spirit.

segments.title: Built Together as God's Dwelling
segments.gist: Gentile believers are no longer strangers but fellow citizens with the saints, built upon the apostles and prophets with Christ as the cornerstone, growing into a holy temple where God dwells.

3.summary: Paul explains that the mystery of Christ—that Gentiles are fellow heirs in the church—was revealed to him by revelation and is now made known through his ministry. He prays that the Ephesians would be strengthened by the Spirit and rooted in love, so that they might comprehend the vast dimensions of Christ's love and be filled with the fullness of God, closing with a doxology to God who is able to do exceeding abundantly above all that we ask or think.

segments.title: Paul's Stewardship of the Mystery
segments.gist: Paul states that the mystery of Christ was made known to him by revelation, that Gentiles are fellow heirs and partakers of the promise, and that he was made a minister of this gospel.

segments.title: Paul's Ministry to the Gentiles
segments.gist: Paul describes his commission to preach the unsearchable riches of Christ to the Gentiles and to make all see the fellowship of the mystery, so that the manifold wisdom of God might be known through the church.

segments.title: Prayer for Spiritual Strength
segments.gist: Paul bows his knees to the Father, praying that believers would be strengthened by the Spirit, rooted and grounded in love, and able to comprehend the breadth, length, depth, and height of Christ's love.

segments.title: Doxology to God
segments.gist: Paul concludes with a doxology to God, who is able to do exceeding abundantly above all that we ask or think, giving glory in the church by Christ Jesus throughout all ages.

4.summary: Paul urges the Ephesians to walk worthy of their calling with humility and unity, emphasizing one body, one Spirit, and one Lord. He describes how Christ gave gifts to equip the saints for ministry and maturity, then calls believers to put off the old man and put on the new, rejecting vices like lying, stealing, and corrupt speech in favor of kindness and forgiveness.

segments.title: Unity of the Spirit
segments.gist: Paul exhorts believers to live with humility and unity, preserving the bond of peace as one body and one Spirit.

segments.title: Gifts for Maturity
segments.gist: Christ gives gifts to equip the saints for ministry, so the church may grow into maturity and avoid being tossed by false doctrine.

segments.title: Put Off the Old Man
segments.gist: Paul urges the Gentiles to no longer walk in vanity but to put off the old man and put on the new man in righteousness.

segments.title: Rules for New Life
segments.gist: Paul gives specific commands: speak truth, control anger, stop stealing, speak edifying words, and forgive as God forgave.

5.summary: Paul calls the Ephesians to imitate God as beloved children, walking in love and light rather than in the sins of their former life. He instructs them to be filled with the Spirit, to live wisely, and to order their households in mutual submission, including specific roles for wives and husbands, children and fathers, and servants and masters.

segments.title: Walk in Love, Not Uncleanness
segments.gist: Paul urges believers to imitate God, walk in love as Christ did, and avoid fornication, covetousness, and filthy talk.

segments.title: Walk as Children of Light
segments.gist: Paul calls them to walk as children of light, exposing the unfruitful works of darkness rather than participating in them.

segments.title: Be Filled with the Spirit
segments.gist: Paul instructs them to walk circumspectly, redeem the time, be filled with the Spirit, and submit to one another.

segments.title: Wives and Husbands
segments.gist: Paul sets forth the duties of wives to submit to their husbands and of husbands to love their wives as Christ loved the church.

6.summary: Paul instructs children to obey their parents and fathers to nurture their children, then addresses servants and masters. He describes the whole armor of God for spiritual warfare and asks for prayer to proclaim the gospel boldly. He commends Tychicus, who is being sent to encourage the believers, and closes with a benediction of peace and grace.

segments.title: Children and Fathers
segments.gist: Children are to obey and honor their parents; fathers are to nurture and admonish their children.

segments.title: Servants and Masters
segments.gist: Servants are to serve sincerely as to Christ; masters are to treat servants fairly, knowing they have a Master in heaven.

segments.title: The Whole Armor of God
segments.gist: Believers are to put on God's armor—truth, righteousness, peace, faith, salvation, and the word of God—to stand against spiritual enemies.

segments.title: Tychicus and Final Blessing
segments.gist: Paul sends Tychicus to comfort the Ephesians and closes with a prayer for peace, love, faith, and grace.

1.summary: Paul writes to the Philippians from prison, thanking God for their partnership in the gospel and expressing confidence that God will complete the good work begun in them. He explains that his imprisonment has advanced the gospel and that he rejoices despite opposition, then urges the church to live worthy of the gospel and to stand united in faith, suffering for Christ's sake.

segments.title: Paul's Thanksgiving and Prayer
segments.gist: Paul greets the Philippians, thanks God for their partnership in the gospel, and prays that their love may abound in knowledge and discernment.

segments.title: Imprisonment Advances the Gospel
segments.gist: Paul explains that his chains have helped spread the gospel and that he rejoices that Christ is preached, even from wrong motives.

segments.title: Hope in Christ Alone
segments.gist: Paul expresses confidence that he will be delivered through prayer and the Spirit, and declares that to live is Christ and to die is gain.

segments.title: Live Worthy of the Gospel
segments.gist: Paul urges the Philippians to live worthy of the gospel, stand united in one spirit, and not be frightened by opponents, since suffering for Christ is a gift.

2.summary: Paul urges the Philippians to unity through humility, pointing to Christ's self-emptying and exaltation as the model, and calls them to work out their salvation without grumbling. He commends Timothy and Epaphroditus as examples of selfless service.

segments.title: Exhortation to Unity and Humility
segments.gist: Paul appeals for unity, humility, and regard for others, citing encouragement in Christ and fellowship of the Spirit.

segments.title: Christ's Humiliation and Exaltation
segments.gist: Paul presents Christ's self-emptying, obedience to death, and subsequent exaltation by God as the model for believers.

segments.title: Work Out Salvation Without Grumbling
segments.gist: Paul calls believers to obey and work out their salvation without complaining, shining as lights in a crooked world.

segments.title: Timothy's Commendation
segments.gist: Paul hopes to send Timothy, who genuinely cares for the Philippians and seeks Christ's interests above his own.

segments.title: Epaphroditus's Service and Return
segments.gist: Paul explains that Epaphroditus, who risked his life for the gospel, will be sent back to the Philippians.

3.summary: Paul sets aside his own impressive religious credentials, counting them as loss for the sake of knowing Christ and being found in him. He presses toward the goal of God's upward call, urging the Philippians to follow his example rather than those who live as enemies of the cross.

segments.title: Paul's Former Confidence
segments.gist: Paul warns against confidence in the flesh and lists his own Jewish credentials and past zeal.

segments.title: All Things Loss for Christ
segments.gist: Paul counts all his former gains as loss and dung for the excellency of knowing Christ and his resurrection.

segments.title: Pressing Toward the Mark
segments.gist: Paul says he has not attained but presses forward, forgetting things behind and reaching for the prize of God's call.

segments.title: Warning About Enemies of the Cross
segments.gist: Paul urges the Philippians to follow his example and warns of those whose end is destruction, while our citizenship is in heaven.

4.summary: Paul closes his letter to the Philippians with a series of exhortations: stand firm, resolve a dispute between Euodias and Syntyche, rejoice and pray with thanksgiving, and focus on virtuous things. He thanks the church for their renewed financial support, describes his contentment in any circumstance through Christ, and ends with greetings and a benediction.

segments.title: Stand fast and help coworkers
segments.gist: Paul urges the Philippians to stand firm and asks Euodias and Syntyche to agree, requesting help for his fellow laborers.

segments.title: Rejoice, pray, and think on good
segments.gist: Paul commands rejoicing and prayer with thanksgiving, promises God's peace, and lists virtues to think about.

segments.title: Contentment in every circumstance
segments.gist: Paul rejoices in the Philippians' care, says he has learned contentment in all situations, and can do all things through Christ.

segments.title: Philippians' support and God's supply
segments.gist: Paul recalls the Philippians' financial support and promises that God will supply all their needs according to His riches.

segments.title: Final greetings and benediction
segments.gist: Paul sends greetings from the brethren and Caesar's household and closes with a benediction of grace.

1.summary: Paul greets the Colossian believers and gives thanks for their faith, love, and the hope laid up for them in heaven. He prays for their spiritual growth and then celebrates Christ's preeminence in creation and redemption, describing his work of reconciliation. Paul concludes by describing his own ministry as a steward of this mystery, rejoicing in his sufferings for the church and laboring to present everyone perfect in Christ.

segments.title: Greeting and Thanksgiving
segments.gist: Paul greets the Colossians and gives thanks for their faith in Christ and love for all the saints, grounded in the hope of the gospel.

segments.title: Prayer for Spiritual Growth
segments.gist: Paul prays that the Colossians may be filled with the knowledge of God's will, walk worthy of the Lord, and give thanks for redemption.

segments.title: The Preeminence of Christ
segments.gist: Paul describes Christ as the image of the invisible God, creator and sustainer of all things, and the head of the church who reconciles all things through his blood.

segments.title: Reconciliation Through Christ
segments.gist: Paul explains that the Colossians, once alienated, are now reconciled through Christ's death to be presented holy and blameless, if they continue in the faith.

segments.title: Paul's Ministry and Labor
segments.gist: Paul rejoices in his sufferings for the church and describes his commission to make known the mystery of Christ, laboring to present everyone perfect in him.

2.summary: Paul warns the Colossians against being deceived by persuasive but hollow philosophy and human tradition, urging them to remain rooted in Christ, in whom the fullness of deity dwells bodily. He explains that believers, having been buried and raised with Christ in baptism, are made alive and forgiven, and that the written ordinances against them have been blotted out and nailed to the cross. He therefore tells them not to submit to regulations about food, drink, festivals, or ascetic practices, which have only an appearance of wisdom.

segments.title: Paul's Concern for the Colossians
segments.gist: Paul describes his struggle for the Colossians and others, desiring their hearts be comforted and united in love and full assurance of understanding.

segments.title: Walk Rooted in Christ
segments.gist: Paul urges believers to walk in Christ as they received him, rooted, built up, established in the faith, and abounding in thanksgiving.

segments.title: Beware of Philosophy and Tradition
segments.gist: Paul warns against being spoiled through philosophy, vain deceit, and human tradition rather than Christ, in whom the fullness of the Godhead dwells bodily.

segments.title: Alive with Christ Through Baptism
segments.gist: Paul explains that believers are circumcised in Christ, buried and raised with him in baptism, made alive, forgiven, and triumphant over principalities and powers.

segments.title: Freedom from Ascetic Regulations
segments.gist: Paul says no one should judge believers regarding food, drink, festivals, or sabbaths, which are shadows, and warns against false humility and worship of angels.

segments.title: Dead to Worldly Ordinances
segments.gist: Paul asks why believers, dead with Christ to worldly principles, submit to human commandments and ascetic rules that lack true value.

3.summary: Paul calls believers to set their minds on things above because they have been raised with Christ, and to put to death earthly vices while putting on virtues of the new self. He instructs households—wives, husbands, children, fathers, servants—to live in mutual duty and service as unto the Lord.

segments.title: Seek Things Above
segments.gist: Since believers are risen with Christ, they should seek and set their affection on things above, where Christ sits at God's right hand.

segments.title: Put Off the Old Man
segments.gist: Paul lists sins to mortify and urges putting off the old man with its deeds, putting on the new man renewed in knowledge after Christ.

segments.title: Put On Christian Virtues
segments.gist: As God's elect, believers are to put on mercy, kindness, humility, meekness, longsuffering, forgiveness, and above all love, letting Christ's peace rule and His word dwell richly.

segments.title: Household Duties: Wives, Husbands, Children, Fathers
segments.gist: Wives are to submit to their husbands, husbands to love their wives, children to obey their parents, and fathers to avoid provoking their children.

segments.title: Duties of Servants
segments.gist: Servants are to obey their earthly masters sincerely as serving the Lord, knowing that they will receive an inheritance from the Lord and that wrongdoers will be repaid.

4.summary: Paul closes his letter to the Colossians with instructions for masters and servants, a call to persistent prayer, and requests for prayer for his ministry. He then sends greetings from his companions and gives final instructions to share the letter with the church at Laodicea.

segments.title: Exhortation to prayer and conduct
segments.gist: Paul urges continual prayer, thanksgiving, and wise conduct toward outsiders, with speech seasoned with grace.

segments.title: Commendation of Tychicus and Onesimus
segments.gist: Paul introduces Tychicus and Onesimus as faithful messengers who will report his situation and comfort the church.

segments.title: Greetings from companions
segments.gist: Paul sends greetings from Aristarchus, Mark, Justus, Epaphras, Luke, and Demas, noting Epaphras's fervent prayer for the Colossians.

segments.title: Instructions for Laodicea and Archippus
segments.gist: Paul asks to greet the Laodicean church and Nymphas, to exchange letters, and to tell Archippus to fulfill his ministry.

1.summary: Paul, writing with Silvanus and Timotheus, greets the church at Thessalonica and thanks God for their faith, labor of love, and steadfast hope. He recalls how the gospel came to them in power and how they turned from idols to serve the living God, becoming examples to believers throughout Macedonia and Achaia as they await God's Son from heaven.

segments.title: Greeting and Thanksgiving
segments.gist: Paul, Silvanus, and Timotheus greet the Thessalonian church and thank God for their faith, love, and hope.

segments.title: Gospel Received in Power
segments.gist: Paul recalls how the gospel came to them in power and the Holy Ghost, and how they became examples to all believers.

segments.title: Turned from Idols to God
segments.gist: The Thessalonians' faith is spread abroad; they turned from idols to serve God and wait for His Son from heaven.

2.summary: Paul recounts his recent visit to Thessalonica, defending his conduct as gentle and blameless among them and reminding them how he worked night and day to avoid burdening them. He gives thanks that they received his preaching as God's word and expresses his longing to see them again, though Satan hindered him, calling them his glory and joy.

segments.title: Paul's Visit Not in Vain
segments.gist: Paul reminds the Thessalonians that his visit to them was not ineffective despite the suffering and shame he had faced.

segments.title: Blameless Conduct and Gentle Care
segments.gist: Paul defends his motives, saying he spoke to please God, used no flattery or greed, and was gentle as a nurse among them.

segments.title: Labor and Fatherly Example
segments.gist: Paul recalls working night and day to avoid burdening them and urges them to walk worthy of God as a father would.

segments.title: Thanksgiving for Received Word
segments.gist: Paul thanks God that the Thessalonians received his preaching as God's word and describes the suffering they endured from their own countrymen.

segments.title: Longing to See Them Again
segments.gist: Paul expresses his eager desire to visit the Thessalonians, hindered by Satan, and calls them his hope, joy, and crown.

3.summary: Paul recounts how he sent Timothy to strengthen and encourage the Thessalonians during his forced absence, and how Timothy's good report of their faith and love comforted Paul in his distress. Paul expresses his longing to see them again and prays that God would direct his way to them and make their love abound, so that their hearts would be established blameless in holiness at the coming of Christ.

segments.title: Paul Sends Timothy
segments.gist: Paul explains that he sent Timothy to establish and comfort the Thessalonians in their faith and to prevent them from being shaken by afflictions.

segments.title: Timothy's Good Report
segments.gist: Timothy returns with news of the Thessalonians' faith and love, bringing Paul comfort in his distress.

segments.title: Paul's Thanksgiving and Longing
segments.gist: Paul gives thanks for the Thessalonians and expresses his earnest desire to see them and complete what is lacking in their faith.

segments.title: Paul's Prayer for Them
segments.gist: Paul prays that God will direct his way to them, make their love abound, and establish their hearts blameless in holiness at Christ's coming.

4.summary: Paul urges the Thessalonians to keep growing in the moral instruction they already received, especially sexual purity and brotherly love, and then answers their question about believers who have died, assuring them that the dead in Christ will rise first and both groups will meet the Lord together.

segments.title: Exhortation to Holiness and Purity
segments.gist: Paul urges the Thessalonians to abound more in the conduct they were taught, stressing that God's will is their sanctification and that they abstain from fornication.

segments.title: Brotherly Love and Quiet Living
segments.gist: Paul commends their love for all brethren and urges them to increase it, to aspire to a quiet life, mind their own business, and work with their hands.

segments.title: The Dead in Christ Will Rise
segments.gist: Paul comforts the church about deceased believers, declaring that the Lord will descend and the dead in Christ will rise first, then the living will be caught up to meet him.

5.summary: Paul closes his letter to the Thessalonians by addressing the timing of Christ's return, urging watchfulness and faith rather than date-setting. He then gives a rapid series of instructions on church life, prayer, and gratitude, and ends with a prayer for sanctification and greetings to be shared with the whole congregation.

segments.title: Day of the Lord and watchfulness
segments.gist: Paul says the day of the Lord comes like a thief, so believers should stay awake, sober, and armed with faith, hope, and love, encouraging one another.

segments.title: Instructions for church life
segments.gist: Paul gives a rapid series of commands: honor leaders, be patient, do good, rejoice, pray, give thanks, test prophecies, and avoid evil.

segments.title: Prayer for sanctification
segments.gist: Paul prays that God will sanctify the Thessalonians completely and keep their spirit, soul, and body blameless until Christ's return, trusting God's faithfulness.

segments.title: Final greetings and charge
segments.gist: Paul asks for prayer, greets the brothers with a holy kiss, charges them to read the letter to all, and closes with a blessing.

1.summary: Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy greet the church at Thessalonica and give thanks for their growing faith and love amid persecution, pointing to God's righteous judgment and the coming rest for believers and vengeance on their persecutors. He prays that God will count them worthy of their calling and glorify Jesus in them.

segments.title: Greeting to the Thessalonians
segments.gist: Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy greet the church of the Thessalonians in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

segments.title: Thanksgiving for Growing Faith
segments.gist: Paul thanks God for the Thessalonians' growing faith and love, and boasts of their patience in persecution.

segments.title: God's Righteous Judgment
segments.gist: Paul describes God's righteous judgment: rest for afflicted believers and vengeance on persecutors when Jesus returns.

segments.title: Prayer for Worthiness and Glory
segments.gist: Paul prays that God will count them worthy of their calling and glorify Jesus in them.

2.summary: Paul corrects the Thessalonians' alarm that the day of Christ had already come, explaining that a falling away and the man of sin must appear first before the Lord destroys him at his coming. He thanks God for their election and calls them to stand fast in the traditions they were taught.

segments.title: Not shaken by false reports
segments.gist: Paul urges the Thessalonians not to be troubled by claims that the day of Christ is at hand.

segments.title: Falling away and man of sin
segments.gist: Paul explains that a falling away and the man of sin, who exalts himself in the temple, must come first.

segments.title: Mystery of iniquity and judgment
segments.gist: The mystery of iniquity already works but is restrained until the wicked one is revealed and destroyed by Christ's coming.

segments.title: Thanksgiving and call to stand fast
segments.gist: Paul thanks God for choosing the Thessalonians and exhorts them to hold the traditions they were taught.

segments.title: Prayer for comfort and stablishment
segments.gist: Paul prays that the Lord Jesus and God the Father would comfort their hearts and establish them in every good word and work.

3.summary: Paul asks the Thessalonians to pray for the spread of the gospel and for deliverance from wicked men, then prays for their own stability. He commands them to withdraw from idle, disorderly believers, citing his own example of working night and day, and directs that those who refuse to work be noted and admonished as brothers, closing with a benediction.

segments.title: Prayer for the Word
segments.gist: Paul asks for prayer that the word may spread and that he be delivered from unreasonable men, and prays for the Thessalonians' stability.

segments.title: Withdraw from the Disorderly
segments.gist: Paul commands withdrawal from idle brethren and points to his own example of working night and day so as not to burden them.

segments.title: Admonish the Idle as Brothers
segments.gist: Paul tells them not to grow weary in well doing and to note and admonish the disobedient as brothers, not enemies.

segments.title: Benediction and Signature
segments.gist: Paul prays for peace and the Lord's presence, gives his personal greeting as a sign, and closes with grace.

1.summary: Paul opens his first letter to Timothy by reminding him of the charge to stay in Ephesus and oppose false teachers who promote endless genealogies and misuse the law.
