He contrasts this with the true purpose of the law for sinners and recounts his own conversion as an example of Christ's patience, closing with a doxology and a renewed charge to Timothy to fight the good fight and hold to faith and a good conscience.

segments.title: Charge Against False Teachers
segments.gist: Paul urges Timothy to remain in Ephesus and command certain men not to teach false doctrines or endless genealogies.

segments.title: Purpose of the Law
segments.gist: Paul explains that the law is good if used lawfully, aimed at lawless and disobedient people, in contrast to sound doctrine.

segments.title: Paul's Conversion and Doxology
segments.gist: Paul thanks Christ for mercy, recounts his former blasphemy and persecution, and praises God as eternal King.

segments.title: Charge to Timothy
segments.gist: Paul renews his charge to Timothy to fight the good fight, holding faith and a good conscience, and mentions Hymenaeus and Alexander.

2.summary: Paul urges that prayers and thanksgivings be made for all people, especially rulers, so that believers may live peaceful and godly lives, and he grounds this in God's desire for all to be saved through the one mediator, Christ Jesus. He then addresses the conduct of men and women in worship, calling men to pray without anger and women to dress modestly and learn quietly, with a closing statement about women's role in teaching and authority.

segments.title: Prayer for all people
segments.gist: Paul instructs that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for all people, including kings and those in authority, so believers may live peaceful and godly lives.

segments.title: One God and mediator
segments.gist: Paul affirms there is one God and one mediator between God and humanity, the man Christ Jesus, who gave himself as a ransom for all, and he was appointed a preacher and apostle to testify to this.

segments.title: Men and women in worship
segments.gist: Paul desires men to pray everywhere without wrath or doubting, and women to adorn themselves modestly with good works rather than elaborate hairstyles, gold, pearls, or costly clothing.

segments.title: Women's learning and role
segments.gist: Paul instructs women to learn quietly and not to teach or usurp authority over men, citing Adam and Eve and the fall, yet says women will be saved through childbearing if they continue in faith, love, holiness, and sobriety.

3.summary: Paul describes the qualifications for bishops (overseers) and deacons, emphasizing moral integrity and household management, and explains that he writes so believers know how to conduct themselves in God's church, concluding with a short creed-like statement about the mystery of godliness.

segments.title: Qualifications for Bishops
segments.gist: Paul lists the moral and domestic requirements for an overseer, including being blameless, temperate, hospitable, and able to manage his own household.

segments.title: Qualifications for Deacons
segments.gist: Paul gives similar qualifications for deacons, stressing dignity, sound faith, and proven character, and mentions their wives and household management.

segments.title: Conduct in God's Church
segments.gist: Paul explains his purpose in writing so believers know how to behave in the church, the pillar of truth, and cites a hymn about the mystery of godliness.

4.summary: Paul warns Timothy that in later times some will abandon the faith and follow deceiving spirits, forbidding marriage and certain foods. He instructs Timothy to reject such teachings, to train himself in godliness, and to set an example for believers in speech, conduct, love, faith, and purity. Paul encourages him to devote himself to reading, exhortation, and teaching, and to persevere in his ministry.

segments.title: Warning Against Deceptive Teachings
segments.gist: Paul foretells that some will depart from the faith, forbidding marriage and foods that God created to be received with thanksgiving.

segments.title: Train Yourself in Godliness
segments.gist: Timothy is told to reject profane fables and exercise himself unto godliness, which holds promise for this life and the next.

segments.title: Set an Example and Persevere
segments.gist: Paul urges Timothy to be an example in word and conduct, to devote himself to reading and teaching, and to continue in doctrine for salvation.

5.summary: Paul instructs Timothy on how to treat older men and women, younger men and women, and widows, distinguishing between widows who should be enrolled for church support and those who should be cared for by family. He gives rules for elders, especially those who preach and teach, and concludes with personal advice about Timothy's health and a warning about sins that are sometimes obvious and sometimes hidden.

segments.title: Exhortation on treating age groups
segments.gist: Paul tells Timothy to treat older men as fathers, younger men as brothers, older women as mothers, and younger women as sisters with purity.

segments.title: Instructions about widows
segments.gist: Paul gives detailed rules for honoring widows, distinguishing those truly in need from those with family, and setting criteria for enrolling widows.

segments.title: Rules for elders
segments.gist: Paul says elders who rule well, especially those who preach and teach, deserve double honor and protection from accusations unless confirmed by witnesses.

segments.title: Charge to Timothy
segments.gist: Paul solemnly charges Timothy to keep these instructions without partiality and not to share in others' sins.

segments.title: Sins and good works revealed
segments.gist: Paul notes that some sins are obvious and lead to judgment, while others are hidden, and likewise good works are sometimes hidden but cannot remain so.

6.summary: Paul addresses masters and servants, warns against false teachers who promote gain, and teaches that godliness with contentment is great gain. He charges Timothy to flee covetousness, fight the good fight of faith, and keep the commandment until Christ's appearing. The chapter closes with instructions to the rich to trust in God and to Timothy to guard the deposit of faith.

segments.title: Duties of servants to masters
segments.gist: Servants are to honor their masters, especially believing ones, so that God's name and doctrine are not blasphemed.

segments.title: Warning against false teachers
segments.gist: Paul describes false teachers who promote strife and suppose godliness is a means of financial gain.

segments.title: Godliness with contentment
segments.gist: Paul teaches that godliness with contentment is great gain, warning that the love of money is the root of all evil.

segments.title: Charge to fight the good fight
segments.gist: Paul charges Timothy to flee evil, pursue righteousness, and keep the commandment until Christ's appearing.

segments.title: Instructions to the rich
segments.gist: The rich are commanded not to trust in wealth but in God, to do good, and to lay hold on eternal life.

segments.title: Guard the deposit of faith
segments.gist: Paul urges Timothy to guard what has been entrusted to him and avoid profane babblings and false knowledge.

1.summary: Paul opens his second letter to Timothy by affirming his love and prayers, recalling Timothy's sincere faith and the legacy of his mother and grandmother. He urges Timothy to rekindle God's gift and to boldly share in suffering for the gospel, not being ashamed of Paul's chains. Paul contrasts the saved and called with the power of God, and describes the desertion of many in Asia, while highlighting Onesiphorus's faithful ministry in Rome.

segments.title: Paul's Thanksgiving for Timothy
segments.gist: Paul greets Timothy, thanks God for him, and recalls his tears and sincere faith inherited from Lois and Eunice.

segments.title: Stir Up the Gift
segments.gist: Paul urges Timothy to rekindle God's gift and to share in suffering for the gospel by God's power.

segments.title: Called to a Holy Calling
segments.gist: Paul describes God's saving purpose and grace, and his own appointment as preacher, for which he suffers but is not ashamed.

segments.title: Hold Fast the Sound Words
segments.gist: Paul tells Timothy to keep the pattern of sound words and guard the good deposit by the Holy Spirit.

segments.title: Onesiphorus's Faithfulness
segments.gist: Paul mentions those in Asia who turned away and praises Onesiphorus for his diligent service in Rome.

2.summary: Paul charges Timothy to be strong in grace, to entrust the gospel to faithful men, and to endure hardship as a good soldier of Jesus Christ. He uses metaphors of soldier, athlete, and farmer, reminds Timothy of Jesus risen from the dead, and encourages him to rightly divide the word of truth while shunning vain babblings and pursuing holiness.

segments.title: Be Strong and Endure
segments.gist: Paul urges Timothy to be strong in grace, to pass on the teaching to faithful men, and to endure hardship like a good soldier.

segments.title: Remember Jesus Christ
segments.gist: Paul calls Timothy to remember Jesus risen from the dead, to suffer for the gospel, and cites a faithful saying about dying and reigning with Christ.

segments.title: Rightly Divide the Word
segments.gist: Paul instructs Timothy to remind believers, to shun vain babblings, and to name Hymenaeus and Philetus who erred concerning the resurrection.

segments.title: Vessel unto Honour
segments.gist: Paul compares believers to vessels in a great house, urging purification for noble use, and describes the servant of the Lord as gentle and apt to teach.

3.summary: Paul warns Timothy about the perilous times of the last days, describing the wicked character of false teachers and hypocrites. He contrasts his own persecution and doctrine with the deceptive practices of evil men, and urges Timothy to continue in the Scriptures, which are inspired by God and sufficient for equipping believers.

segments.title: Perilous Times and Wicked Men
segments.gist: Paul describes the last days as perilous because people will be self-loving, boastful, blasphemous, and hypocritical, having a form of godliness but denying its power.

segments.title: Paul's Example and Persecution
segments.gist: Paul reminds Timothy of his doctrine, manner of life, and persecutions, affirming that all who live godly will suffer persecution while evil men grow worse.

segments.title: Continue in the Scriptures
segments.gist: Paul urges Timothy to continue in what he has learned from the Holy Scriptures, which are inspired by God and profitable for teaching, reproof, correction, and equipping for every good work.

4.summary: Paul charges Timothy to preach the word faithfully, endure hardship, and fulfill his ministry, citing his own imminent death and the reward awaiting him. He then reports on his companions and opponents, asks Timothy to come to him and bring Mark and his cloak and books, warns about Alexander the coppersmith, and closes with a report of his first defense, confidence in the Lord's deliverance, greetings, and a final benediction.

segments.title: Charge to Preach the Word
segments.gist: Paul solemnly charges Timothy to preach the word in season and out of season, reprove, rebuke, and exhort with patience, and to endure afflictions and do the work of an evangelist.

segments.title: Paul's Departure and Reward
segments.gist: Paul declares that he is now ready to be offered, has fought the good fight and kept the faith, and anticipates the crown of righteousness from the Lord.

segments.title: Personal Requests and Warning
segments.gist: Paul urges Timothy to come quickly, reports that Demas has forsaken him and only Luke is with him, asks for Mark and his cloak and books, and warns about Alexander the coppersmith.

segments.title: First Defense and Deliverance
segments.gist: Paul recounts that at his first defense no one stood with him, but the Lord strengthened him and delivered him, and he expresses confidence of final salvation.

segments.title: Greetings and Benediction
segments.gist: Paul sends greetings to Prisca, Aquila, and the household of Onesiphorus, reports on Erastus and Trophimus, urges Timothy to come before winter, and closes with greetings and a blessing.

1.summary: Paul opens his letter to Titus by asserting his apostleship and the hope of eternal life, then instructs Titus on appointing elders in Crete, listing the qualifications for overseers and the need to silence false teachers, especially those promoting Jewish myths and commandments for financial gain. He concludes by quoting a Cretan prophet about the people's character and urging Titus to rebuke them sharply so they may be sound in the faith.

segments.title: Paul's Greeting to Titus
segments.gist: Paul introduces himself as a servant and apostle of God, writing to Titus about faith, truth, and the hope of eternal life.

segments.title: Appointing Elders in Crete
segments.gist: Paul instructs Titus to appoint elders in every city and lists the qualifications for an overseer, including being blameless and holding to sound doctrine.

segments.title: Silencing False Teachers
segments.gist: Paul warns of rebellious deceivers, especially those of the circumcision, who must be silenced because they teach false doctrines for dishonest gain, as even a Cretan prophet testified.

segments.title: Pure and Defiled
segments.gist: Paul contrasts the pure who see all things as pure with the defiled whose minds and consciences are corrupted, claiming to know God but denying Him by their works.

2.summary: Paul instructs Titus to teach sound doctrine to various groups in the church—older men, older women, younger women, younger men, and slaves—so that their behavior adorns the gospel. He grounds this ethical teaching in the grace of God that brings salvation and in the hope of Christ's return, urging believers to live godly lives as a peculiar people.

segments.title: Instructions for older men and women
segments.gist: Paul tells Titus to teach older men to be sober and sound in faith, and older women to be reverent, not slanderers, teaching younger women to love their families.

segments.title: Instructions for younger men and Titus
segments.gist: Paul urges younger men to be sober-minded and Titus to set an example of good works and sound speech that cannot be condemned.

segments.title: Instructions for servants
segments.gist: Servants are told to be obedient and faithful to their masters so that they adorn the doctrine of God in all things.

segments.title: Grace and the blessed hope
segments.gist: The grace of God has appeared, teaching believers to deny ungodliness and live soberly while awaiting the blessed hope and glorious appearing of Christ, who gave himself to redeem a peculiar people.

3.summary: Paul reminds Titus to be subject to rulers and ready for good works, recalling that believers were once foolish and sinful but were saved by God's mercy through washing and renewal of the Holy Spirit. He insists on good works and warns against divisive people, closing with personal instructions and greetings.

segments.title: Submission to Authorities
segments.gist: Paul instructs Titus to remind believers to be subject to rulers and authorities, obedient, and ready for every good work.

segments.title: Saved by Mercy
segments.gist: Paul recalls believers' former sinful state and declares that God saved them by His mercy through the washing of regeneration and renewal of the Holy Spirit.

segments.title: Maintain Good Works
segments.gist: Paul affirms that believers should maintain good works and instructs Titus to avoid foolish questions, genealogies, and divisive people after admonition.

segments.title: Final Instructions and Greetings
segments.gist: Paul gives personal instructions about Artemas, Tychicus, Zenas, and Apollos, and closes with greetings and a blessing.

1.summary: Paul writes to Philemon, appealing on behalf of Onesimus, a runaway slave who has become a Christian through Paul's ministry. Paul asks Philemon to receive Onesimus not as a slave but as a beloved brother, offering to repay any debt and expressing confidence in Philemon's obedience.

segments.title: Greeting from Paul and Timothy
segments.gist: Paul and Timothy greet Philemon, Apphia, Archippus, and the church that meets in Philemon's house.

segments.title: Thanksgiving for Philemon's Love
segments.gist: Paul thanks God for Philemon's love and faith toward Jesus and all saints, and prays that his generosity may be effective.

segments.title: Paul's Appeal for Onesimus
segments.gist: Paul appeals for Onesimus, his spiritual son, asking Philemon to receive him as a beloved brother rather than a slave.

segments.title: Request to Receive and Repay
segments.gist: Paul asks Philemon to receive Onesimus as he would Paul, offers to repay any debt, and expresses confidence in Philemon's obedience.

segments.title: Final Greetings and Blessing
segments.gist: Paul sends greetings from Epaphras and other companions, and closes with a blessing of grace.

1.summary: The opening of Hebrews declares that God, who spoke through prophets in the past, now speaks through his Son, who is the heir of all things and the exact image of God's glory. The Son is shown to be far superior to the angels, who are merely ministering spirits, and the chapter closes with a contrast between the Son's eternal throne and the angels' role as servants.

segments.title: God Speaks Through His Son
segments.gist: God, who spoke through prophets, now speaks through his Son, who is heir of all things, creator, and the brightness of God's glory.

segments.title: Son Superior to Angels
segments.gist: The Son is shown to be superior to angels because God never called any angel his Son, but angels are made spirits and ministers.

segments.title: The Son's Eternal Throne
segments.gist: The Son is addressed as God with an eternal throne, loving righteousness and hating iniquity, anointed above his fellows.

segments.title: The Son as Creator
segments.gist: The Son is credited with creating the heavens and the earth, which will perish, but he remains the same forever.

segments.title: Angels as Ministering Spirits
segments.gist: No angel was ever invited to sit at God's right hand; angels are ministering spirits sent to serve those who will inherit salvation.

2.summary: The author urges his readers to pay close attention to the gospel they have heard, since it was confirmed by the Lord and by signs and wonders, and since neglecting it brings just punishment. He then shows that God subjected the world to come not to angels but to man, quoting Psalm 8, and explains that Jesus was made lower than the angels for a little while so that by tasting death for everyone he might be crowned with glory and honor. Because the children share flesh and blood, Christ also took on flesh and blood, destroying the devil's power over death and becoming a merciful and faithful high priest who can help those who are tempted.

segments.title: Warning to heed the gospel
segments.gist: The author urges careful attention to what was heard, since the message spoken through angels proved steadfast and every transgression received just recompense.

segments.title: The world to come and Psalm 8
segments.gist: God did not subject the world to come to angels; Psalm 8 says man was made lower than angels but crowned with glory, and Jesus was made lower than angels for a little while to taste death for all.

segments.title: Christ brings many sons to glory
segments.gist: It was fitting for God, for whom all things exist, to perfect the captain of salvation through sufferings and to bring many sons to glory, for Christ and his people are all of one, so he is not ashamed to call them brethren.

segments.title: Christ partakes of flesh and blood
segments.gist: Since the children share flesh and blood, Christ likewise took part of the same, so that through death he might destroy the devil and deliver those in bondage, becoming a merciful and faithful high priest able to help the tempted.

3.summary: Hebrews 3 compares Jesus to Moses, arguing that Christ is worthy of greater glory as the builder of God's house, while Moses was a faithful servant within it. The chapter then warns believers against hardening their hearts as Israel did in the wilderness, urging them to hold fast their confidence and not fall through unbelief.

segments.title: Jesus Greater Than Moses
segments.gist: The author calls Jesus the apostle and high priest of our profession, faithful as was Moses, but worthy of more glory as the builder of the house.

segments.title: Warning Against Hardening Hearts
segments.gist: A quotation of Psalm 95 warns against hardening hearts as Israel did in the wilderness, provoking God and failing to enter His rest.

segments.title: Exhortation to Hold Fast
segments.gist: Believers are urged to beware of an evil heart of unbelief, to exhort one another daily, and to hold firm their confidence to the end.

segments.title: Israel's Unbelief and Exclusion
segments.gist: The author recalls that those who provoked God were the Israelites who came out of Egypt and fell in the wilderness, unable to enter God's rest because of unbelief.

4.summary: Hebrews 4 continues the warning from chapter 3, urging believers to enter God's rest while the promise remains, and explains that the gospel was preached to Israel but did not profit them because of unbelief. It identifies the rest as God's own rest from creation, still available today, and describes the word of God as living and powerful, discerning the heart. The chapter closes by presenting Jesus as the great high priest who sympathizes with human weakness and invites believers to come boldly to the throne of grace.

segments.title: Warning to Enter God's Rest
segments.gist: The promise of entering God's rest remains, so believers should fear falling short through unbelief.

segments.title: Believers Enter God's Rest
segments.gist: Believers enter God's rest, while unbelievers do not, as God's works were finished from the foundation of the world.

segments.title: The Rest Still Remains
segments.gist: The rest remains for some to enter, and God sets a day, showing that Joshua did not give final rest and that a sabbath rest remains for God's people.

segments.title: The Living Word of God
segments.gist: Believers should labor to enter that rest, for the word of God is living and powerful, discerning the thoughts and intentions of the heart.

segments.title: Jesus the Great High Priest
segments.gist: Since Jesus is a great high priest who sympathizes with weaknesses, believers should come boldly to the throne of grace.

5.summary: Hebrews 5 contrasts the high priest's role of offering sacrifices for himself and the people with Christ's appointment as high priest after the order of Melchizedek. The chapter chides the readers for their spiritual immaturity, noting they still need milk rather than solid food and are unskilled in the word of righteousness.

segments.title: High Priest's Role and Weakness
segments.gist: Every high priest is chosen to offer gifts and sacrifices for sins and can deal gently with the ignorant, since he himself is beset with weakness.

segments.title: Christ Appointed High Priest
segments.gist: Christ did not glorify himself but was appointed by God as high priest after the order of Melchizedek, and he learned obedience through suffering.

segments.title: Warning of Spiritual Immaturity
segments.gist: The readers are dull of hearing and still need milk, not solid food, being unskilled in the word of righteousness and immature.

6.summary: The writer urges his readers to move past foundational teachings and press on to maturity, warning that those who have fully experienced God's blessings yet fall away cannot be restored again. He expresses confidence in better things for them, reminding them of God's unchanging promise and oath to Abraham, which gives strong encouragement and an anchor of hope for the soul.

segments.title: Exhortation to Maturity
segments.gist: The author urges leaving elementary doctrines and going on to perfection, not relaying foundations again.

segments.title: Warning Against Falling Away
segments.gist: Those who were enlightened and tasted heavenly gifts but fell away cannot be renewed to repentance, crucifying Christ afresh.

segments.title: Confidence of Better Things
segments.gist: The writer expresses confidence in better things for his readers, reminding them of their past labor of love and urging continued diligence.

segments.title: God's Unchangeable Promise
segments.gist: God's promise and oath to Abraham provide strong consolation and an anchor of hope for believers, secured by Jesus as high priest.

7.summary: The chapter presents Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God, who blessed Abraham and received tithes from him, and argues that Christ's priesthood is after Melchizedek's order rather than Aaron's. It contrasts the temporary, repeated sacrifices of the Levitical priests with the permanent, once-for-all priesthood and sacrifice of Jesus, who lives forever to intercede.

segments.title: Melchizedek blesses Abraham
segments.gist: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God, meets Abraham, blesses him, and receives tithes from him.

segments.title: Levi paid tithes through Abraham
segments.gist: The author argues that the Levitical priesthood, being descended from Abraham, paid tithes to Melchizedek and was thus inferior.

segments.title: A new priesthood needed
segments.gist: If perfection came through the Levitical priesthood, no other priest would be needed; but a priest like Melchizedek from Judah arises, requiring a change in the law.

segments.title: Jesus, priest by oath
segments.gist: Jesus became a priest by God's oath, not by lineage, and holds a permanent priesthood, able to save completely those who come to God through him.

segments.title: A perfect high priest
segments.gist: Jesus is a sinless high priest who offered himself once for all, unlike the Levitical priests who offered repeated sacrifices.

8.summary: The writer of Hebrews presents the central point of his argument: the true high priest sits at the right hand of God in the heavenly sanctuary, not in the earthly tabernacle. He then cites Jeremiah's prophecy of a new covenant, in which God will write His laws on hearts and forgive sins, showing that the old covenant is obsolete.

segments.title: The Main Point
segments.gist: The writer states the core of his message: we have a high priest seated at God's right hand in heaven.

segments.title: Heavenly Sanctuary Ministry
segments.gist: Every high priest offers gifts and sacrifices, so Christ also must have something to offer, serving in the true tabernacle set up by God.

segments.title: First Covenant Fault
segments.gist: If the first covenant had been faultless, no second would be needed; God finds fault with the people and promises a new covenant.

segments.title: New Covenant Promises
segments.gist: God promises to put His laws in minds and hearts, be their God, and forgive their sins, remembering them no more.

9.summary: Hebrews 9 contrasts the earthly tabernacle and its repeated animal sacrifices with the superior sacrifice of Christ, who entered the heavenly sanctuary once for all and obtained eternal redemption. It explains that the old covenant rituals could not perfect the conscience, while Christ's death inaugurates the new covenant and secures the forgiveness of sins.

segments.title: Earthly Tabernacle and Its Ordinances
segments.gist: The first covenant had an earthly sanctuary with furnishings and rituals, but these were only outward regulations until the time of reformation.

segments.title: Christ's Superior Sacrifice
segments.gist: Christ, as high priest of the greater tabernacle, entered once with his own blood, obtaining eternal redemption and purifying the conscience.

segments.title: Mediator of the New Covenant
segments.gist: Christ is the mediator of the new covenant; his death redeems transgressions, and a testament requires the death of the testator, as the law's rituals involved blood.

segments.title: Once for All in Heaven
segments.gist: Christ entered heaven itself to appear before God, not to offer himself repeatedly, but once to put away sin and to bring salvation to those who wait for him.

10.summary: Hebrews 10 explains that the law's sacrifices are a shadow, not the reality, and that Christ's once-for-all offering perfects believers. It urges believers to hold fast and assemble together, warns that willful sin leaves no sacrifice, and closes with a call to persevere in faith rather than shrink back.

segments.title: The Law's Shadow and Christ's Offering
segments.gist: The law's repeated sacrifices cannot perfect worshippers, but Christ's once-for-all offering sanctifies believers.

segments.title: Christ's Single Sacrifice Perfected Believers
segments.gist: Christ's one offering perfects believers forever, and the Holy Spirit confirms sins are remembered no more.

segments.title: Exhortation to Draw Near and Hold Fast
segments.gist: Believers are urged to draw near to God, hold fast their hope, and provoke one another to love and good works.

segments.title: Warning Against Willful Sin
segments.gist: Willful sin after receiving the truth leaves no sacrifice, only fearful judgment and vengeance from God.

segments.title: Call to Endure and Not Shrink Back
segments.gist: The author recalls the readers' former endurance and urges them to persevere in faith rather than draw back.

11.summary: Hebrews 11 is a sustained exposition of faith, defined as the substance of things hoped for and the evidence of things not seen. The chapter recounts how figures from Abel to the prophets lived and died by faith, enduring hardship and obtaining divine approval, though they did not receive the promises in their lifetime because God had provided something better for them together with us.

segments.title: Faith Defined
segments.gist: Faith is the substance of things hoped for and the evidence of things not seen; by it the elders obtained a good report.

segments.title: Abel, Enoch, Noah
segments.gist: By faith Abel offered a better sacrifice, Enoch was translated, and Noah built the ark and became heir of righteousness.

segments.title: Abraham and Sarah
segments.gist: By faith Abraham obeyed and sojourned in the promised land, and Sarah received strength to conceive, leading to a multitude of descendants.

segments.title: Strangers and Pilgrims
segments.gist: These all died in faith, confessing they were strangers and pilgrims on earth, desiring a better heavenly country that God has prepared.

segments.title: Isaac to Rahab
segments.gist: By faith Abraham offered Isaac, Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau, Jacob blessed Joseph's sons, Joseph gave commandment about his bones, Moses was hid and chose to suffer with Israel, and Rahab perished not with the unbelievers.

segments.title: Gideon to the Prophets
segments.gist: Time would fail to tell of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and the prophets, who through faith subdued kingdoms, endured trials, and obtained a good report, though they received not the promise.

12.summary: Hebrews 12 presents Jesus as the ultimate example of endurance, urging believers to run their race with patience and to accept God's chastening as a father's discipline. It contrasts the terror of Mount Sinai with the joy of Mount Zion and the heavenly Jerusalem, warning against refusing God's voice and reminding them that His kingdom cannot be shaken.

segments.title: Run with Patience
segments.gist: Believers are called to lay aside every weight and sin, looking to Jesus, who endured the cross for the joy set before Him.

segments.title: Endure God's Chastening
segments.gist: The author cites Proverbs to show that God disciplines His children as a father, and such chastening yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness.

segments.title: Lift Up Drooping Hands
segments.gist: Readers are urged to strengthen the weak, pursue peace and holiness, and avoid the bitter root of Esau's profanity.

segments.title: Sinai vs. Zion
segments.gist: The terrifying, untouchable mountain of the old covenant is contrasted with the joyful assembly at Mount Zion and the heavenly Jerusalem.

segments.title: A Kingdom That Cannot Be Shaken
segments.gist: A final warning not to refuse God's voice, since He will shake all things, and a reminder that we receive an unshakable kingdom.

13.summary: The closing chapter of Hebrews gives practical instructions for Christian living: love, hospitality, care for prisoners, purity in marriage, contentment, and loyalty to sound teaching. It calls believers to obey their leaders, offers a benediction, and ends with personal greetings and a final blessing.

segments.title: Exhortations to Love and Purity
segments.gist: The author urges brotherly love, hospitality, remembrance of prisoners, honor in marriage, and contentment without covetousness.

segments.title: Loyalty to Christ and Sacrifices
segments.gist: Believers are told to follow faithful leaders, avoid strange doctrines, and offer spiritual sacrifices through Jesus.

segments.title: Obedience to Leaders and Prayer Request
segments.gist: The author asks for obedience to leaders and requests prayer for himself and others.

segments.title: Benediction
segments.gist: A blessing is pronounced through the blood of the everlasting covenant, asking God to perfect believers in every good work.

segments.title: Final Greetings and Blessing
segments.gist: The author appeals for patience, shares news of Timothy, sends greetings, and closes with a blessing.

1.summary: James opens his letter by addressing scattered believers, urging them to find joy in trials and to ask God for wisdom without doubting. He contrasts the lowly and the rich, traces temptation to human desire rather than God, and calls for pure religion shown in speech, care for the needy, and moral purity.

segments.title: Greeting and Joy in Trials
segments.gist: James greets the twelve tribes and tells them to count trials as joy because testing produces endurance.

segments.title: Ask God for Wisdom
segments.gist: Believers lacking wisdom should ask God, who gives generously, but must ask in faith without doubting.

segments.title: The Lowly and the Rich
segments.gist: The lowly believer should glory in being exalted, while the rich should glory in being humbled, for wealth fades like a flower.

segments.title: Temptation and God's Goodness
segments.gist: James pronounces a blessing on those who endure temptation and clarifies that temptation comes from human desire, not from God, who gives only good gifts.

segments.title: Hearers and Doers of the Word
segments.gist: Believers should be quick to hear and slow to speak, putting away anger and receiving the implanted word, not merely hearing it but doing it.

segments.title: Pure Religion Defined
segments.gist: True religion means controlling one's tongue and caring for orphans and widows while keeping oneself unstained by the world.

2.summary: James warns against showing partiality to the rich over the poor, arguing that favoritism breaks the royal law of loving one's neighbor and that faith in Christ is incompatible with such discrimination. He then insists that faith without works is dead, illustrating with the examples of Abraham and Rahab to show that a person is justified by works and not by faith alone.

segments.title: Partiality to the Rich Condemned
segments.gist: James rebukes believers for honoring the rich man while despising the poor man, calling such favoritism evil and inconsistent with faith in Christ.

segments.title: The Royal Law and Partiality
segments.gist: James calls the command to love one's neighbor the royal law, shows that partiality is a transgression of the whole law, and urges mercy over judgment.

segments.title: Faith Without Works Is Dead
segments.gist: James argues that faith without works cannot save, illustrating with a needy brother or sister left unhelped, and declares that faith apart from works is dead.

segments.title: Abraham and Rahab Justified by Works
segments.gist: James cites Abraham offering Isaac and Rahab hiding the spies to prove that faith is made perfect by works and that a person is justified by works, not faith alone.

3.summary: James warns that teachers face stricter judgment and that the tongue, though small, can set a whole life on fire and is untamable. He contrasts bitter envy and strife with the wisdom from above, which is pure, peaceable, and gentle.

segments.title: Warning to Teachers
segments.gist: James cautions that many should not become teachers, since they will be judged more strictly for their words.

segments.title: The Tongue's Power
segments.gist: The tongue is small but boasts great things, like a bit in a horse's mouth or a rudder on a ship, and can ignite a great fire.

segments.title: Untamable Tongue
segments.gist: Every kind of beast has been tamed, but no one can tame the tongue; it is a restless evil, and blessing and cursing come from the same mouth.

segments.title: Two Kinds of Wisdom
segments.gist: True wisdom is shown by good conduct; bitter envy brings confusion, while wisdom from above is pure, peaceable, gentle, and full of mercy.

4.summary: James rebukes his readers for their quarrels, which spring from selfish desires, and calls them to humble submission to God. He warns against judging others and against presumptuous boasting about tomorrow, urging them instead to do the good they know.

segments.title: Quarrels from selfish desires
segments.gist: James traces fights and conflicts to lusts that war within and to prayers made only to satisfy selfish wants.

segments.title: Friendship with the world
segments.gist: He calls them adulterers, says friendship with the world is enmity with God, and cites Scripture on God resisting the proud but giving grace to the humble.

segments.title: Submit to God, resist devil
segments.gist: He commands submission to God, resistance to the devil, drawing near to God, cleansing hands and hearts, and humbling oneself before the Lord.

segments.title: Do not speak evil of others
segments.gist: James forbids speaking evil of or judging a brother, arguing that such a person judges the law and usurps the place of the one lawgiver and judge.

segments.title: Boasting about tomorrow
segments.gist: He rebukes those who plan business for tomorrow without acknowledging God, reminds them life is a vapor, and says that to know good and not do it is sin.

5.summary: James warns the rich about coming judgment and calls believers to patience until the Lord's return, citing the prophets and Job as examples. He gives instructions on prayer, healing, and restoring the wandering, emphasizing confession and prayer's power.

segments.title: Woe to the Rich
segments.gist: James denounces wealthy oppressors whose riches are corrupted and who have defrauded laborers, warning of impending judgment.

segments.title: Be Patient Until Coming
segments.gist: Believers are called to patience like farmers awaiting rain, and to endure suffering as the prophets and Job did.

segments.title: Prayer and Healing
segments.gist: The sick are told to call for elders to pray and anoint them, and Elijah's example shows prayer's power.

segments.title: Restore the Wanderer
segments.gist: Whoever turns a sinner from error saves a soul and covers many sins.

1.summary: Peter greets the scattered elect and praises God for a living hope through Christ's resurrection, calling believers to holy conduct and sincere love as they live in reverent fear during their earthly exile, having been redeemed by Christ's blood and born again through the enduring word of God.

segments.title: Greeting to the Elect
segments.gist: Peter addresses the scattered elect, chosen according to God's foreknowledge and sanctified by the Spirit for obedience and sprinkling of Christ's blood.

segments.title: Praise for Living Hope
segments.gist: God is praised for a living hope through Christ's resurrection and for an incorruptible inheritance kept in heaven for believers.

segments.title: Joy Through Trials
segments.gist: Believers rejoice despite trials that test their faith, which is more precious than gold, leading to praise and salvation.

segments.title: Prophets and Angels Inquire
segments.gist: Prophets searched diligently for the time and manner of Christ's sufferings and glory, and angels desire to look into these things.

segments.title: Call to Holiness
segments.gist: Believers are called to holy conduct, remembering their redemption by Christ's blood and their new birth through the living word of God.

segments.title: Love One Another Sincerely
segments.gist: Having purified their souls, believers are urged to love one another fervently, being born again by the enduring word of God.

2.summary: Peter calls believers to lay aside malice and hypocrisy and to crave spiritual milk, describing them as living stones built into a spiritual house on Christ the cornerstone. He then urges submission to authorities, patient suffering for doing good after Christ's example, and addresses servants, closing with Christ's sinless suffering and bearing of sins on the tree.

segments.title: Crave Pure Spiritual Milk
segments.gist: Believers are told to put away malice, guile, hypocrisies, envy, and evil speakings, and to desire the sincere milk of the word.

segments.title: Living Stones and Royal Priesthood
segments.gist: Christ is the living cornerstone; believers as living stones are built into a spiritual house and called a chosen generation and royal priesthood.

segments.title: Abstain from Fleshly Lusts
segments.gist: As strangers and pilgrims, believers are urged to abstain from fleshly lusts and maintain honest conversation among the Gentiles.

segments.title: Submit to Every Ordinance
segments.gist: Believers are commanded to submit to human authorities for the Lord's sake, to honour all men, love the brotherhood, fear God, and honour the king.

segments.title: Servants Suffer Patiently
segments.gist: Servants are told to be subject to masters, enduring grief and suffering wrongfully with patience, for this is acceptable with God.

segments.title: Christ's Example of Suffering
segments.gist: Christ suffered for believers, leaving an example; He did no sin, bore sins on the tree, and by His stripes believers are healed and returned to the Shepherd.

3.summary: Peter instructs wives and husbands on their conduct in marriage, urging wives to win unbelieving husbands by their behavior and husbands to honor their wives as heirs of grace. He then calls all believers to unity, compassion, and a readiness to give an answer for their hope with meekness, reminding them that it is better to suffer for doing good than for evil, as Christ suffered once for sins, the just for the unjust, and was put to death in the flesh but quickened by the Spirit, preaching to spirits in prison and now exalted at God's right hand.

segments.title: Wives' conduct toward husbands
segments.gist: Wives are told to be submissive to their husbands, especially unbelieving ones, so that they may be won by the wives' chaste behavior and inner adornment of a meek and quiet spirit.

segments.title: Call to unity and blessing
segments.gist: All believers are called to be of one mind, compassionate, loving, and not returning evil for evil, but blessing others, with a quotation from Psalm 34 about the Lord's favor on the righteous.

segments.title: Suffering for righteousness
segments.gist: Believers are encouraged to suffer for righteousness' sake without fear, always ready to give a meek and reverent answer for their hope, keeping a good conscience so that those who slander them may be ashamed.

segments.title: Christ's suffering and exaltation
segments.gist: Christ suffered once for sins, the just for the unjust, was put to death in the flesh but quickened by the Spirit, preached to spirits in prison, and is now exalted at God's right hand with angels and authorities subject to him.

4.summary: Peter calls believers to arm themselves with Christ's suffering mindset, ceasing from sin and living for God's will rather than worldly lusts. He urges sober prayer, fervent love, and joyful service with God's gifts amid persecution, and encourages suffering believers to entrust themselves to God while doing good.

segments.title: Live for God's Will
segments.gist: Believers should adopt Christ's suffering mindset, cease from sin, and live for God's will rather than Gentile lusts, remembering they will give account to God.

segments.title: Sober, Loving, Serving
segments.gist: Peter urges watchful prayer, fervent love covering sins, hospitality, and stewardship of gifts for God's glory through Christ.

segments.title: Suffering as a Christian
segments.gist: Believers should not be surprised by fiery trials but rejoice in sharing Christ's sufferings, ensuring their suffering is for Christ and not for wrongdoing.

5.summary: Peter addresses elders, urging them to shepherd God's flock willingly and humbly, and younger members to submit to them, with all called to humility and casting anxiety on God. He warns that the devil prowls like a roaring lion, calls for resistance and steadfastness in suffering, and closes with a benediction and greetings from Babylon and Mark.

segments.title: Exhortation to Elders
segments.gist: Peter urges elders to feed the flock willingly, not for gain, and to be examples, promising a reward.

segments.title: Humility and Casting Care
segments.gist: Younger members are told to submit to elders; all are called to humility, casting anxiety on God.

segments.title: Resist the Devil
segments.gist: Peter warns that the devil prowls like a lion; believers must resist him and trust God to restore them.

segments.title: Final Greetings
segments.gist: Peter commends Silvanus, sends greetings from Babylon and Mark, and tells them to greet one another.

1.summary: Peter opens his second letter by greeting believers and reminding them that God's divine power has given them everything needed for life and godliness through precious promises. He urges them to add virtue to faith and make their calling and election sure, then explains his intention to remind them of these truths before his death, citing the Transfiguration and the prophetic word as sure foundations.

segments.title: Greeting and blessing
segments.gist: Peter introduces himself as a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ and greets those who have obtained like precious faith.

segments.title: Divine power and promises
segments.gist: God's divine power has given believers all things pertaining to life and godliness through great and precious promises.

segments.title: Add to your faith
segments.gist: Peter lists virtues to add to faith and urges diligence to make calling and election sure, promising an abundant entrance into Christ's kingdom.

segments.title: Reminder before departure
segments.gist: Peter says he will not neglect to remind them of these things, knowing his death is near, and will ensure they remember after his departure.

segments.title: Eyewitness of majesty
segments.gist: Peter affirms they did not follow cunningly devised fables but were eyewitnesses of Christ's majesty at the Transfiguration.

segments.title: The sure prophetic word
segments.gist: Peter calls the prophetic word more sure, comparing it to a light in darkness, and explains that prophecy came by the Holy Spirit, not human will.

2.summary: Peter warns that false teachers will arise among the believers, denying the Lord and leading many into destructive heresies, and he describes their coming judgment by recalling the fallen angels, the flood, and Sodom and Gomorrah. He then exposes their greedy, arrogant, and immoral character, comparing them to Balaam and to dogs returning to their vomit, and declares that their end is worse than if they had never known the way of righteousness.

segments.title: False Teachers and Their Destruction
segments.gist: Peter warns that false teachers will secretly bring in destructive heresies, denying the Lord and bringing swift destruction upon themselves.

segments.title: Judgment on the Wicked
segments.gist: God's past judgments on fallen angels, the ancient world, and Sodom and Gomorrah show that He reserves the unjust for punishment while delivering the godly.

segments.title: Character of the False Teachers
segments.gist: The false teachers are described as arrogant, greedy, and immoral, following the way of Balaam and feasting with the believers while deceiving them.

segments.title: Their End and Return to Corruption
segments.gist: These teachers are empty and promising freedom while enslaved to corruption; their latter end is worse than the beginning, like a dog returning to its vomit.

3.summary: Peter warns that scoffers will come in the last days denying Christ's return, but God's promise is certain and his delay is patience, not slackness. He describes the day of the Lord as a sudden, fiery dissolution of the heavens and earth, and urges believers to live holy lives as they await it, growing in grace and guarding against error.

segments.title: Peter's second epistle reminder
segments.gist: Peter writes this second letter to stir up pure minds by way of remembrance, recalling the words of the prophets and the commandment of the apostles.

segments.title: Scoffers deny Christ's return
segments.gist: Scoffers will come in the last days, walking after their own lusts and asking where the promise of Christ's coming is, forgetting that the world was destroyed by water.

segments.title: Day of the Lord dissolution
segments.gist: The day of the Lord will come as a thief, dissolving the heavens and earth with fire, and believers look for new heavens and a new earth wherein dwelleth righteousness.

segments.title: Exhortation to holy living
segments.gist: Believers are urged to be diligent, found in peace without spot, and to count God's long-suffering as salvation, as Paul also wrote, while beingware of being led away by error.

1.summary: The opening of 1 John declares the apostolic testimony about the Word of life, then states that God is light and that walking in darkness while claiming fellowship with him is a lie. It contrasts confession of sin with denial, promising cleansing through Christ's blood and forgiveness to those who confess.

segments.title: The Word of Life Declared
segments.gist: The author testifies to the eternal Word of life that was from the beginning, seen and handled, so that readers may share fellowship with the Father and Son.

segments.title: God Is Light
segments.gist: The message is that God is light; walking in darkness while claiming fellowship with him is a lie, but walking in the light brings fellowship and cleansing by Christ's blood.

segments.title: Confession and Forgiveness
segments.gist: Claiming sinlessness is self-deception, but confessing sins brings forgiveness and cleansing, while denying sin makes God a liar.

2.summary: John addresses his little children, reminding them that Christ is their advocate and propitiation, and that keeping his commandments is the evidence of knowing him. He contrasts the old commandment of love with the new, warns against loving the world, and identifies antichrists who deny the Father and the Son. He assures believers of their anointing and abiding in Christ, and urges them to continue in the truth so they may have confidence at his coming.

segments.title: Christ our advocate and propitiation
segments.gist: John writes so believers may not sin, but if they do, Jesus Christ is their advocate with the Father and the propitiation for the whole world.

segments.title: Old and new commandment of love
segments.gist: The commandment to love is old yet new in Christ; whoever loves abides in the light, while whoever hates walks in darkness and blindness.

segments.title: Address to little children, fathers, young men
segments.gist: John addresses little children, fathers, and young men, affirming their forgiveness, knowledge of God, and victory over the wicked one.

segments.title: Do not love the world
segments.gist: John warns against loving the world or the things in it, because the world's lusts pass away, but those who do God's will abide forever.

segments.title: Antichrists deny the Father and Son
segments.gist: John identifies the last hour and many antichrists who deny that Jesus is the Christ, warning that whoever denies the Son does not have the Father.

segments.title: Abide in Christ and his anointing
segments.gist: John urges believers to let the truth abide in them, assures them of the anointing that teaches all things, and calls them to abide in Christ so they may have confidence at his coming.

3.summary: 1 John 3 describes God's love in making believers His children, the hope of future transformation, and the ethical demand to live righteously and love one another. It contrasts the children of God with the children of the devil, and concludes with assurance of answered prayer and the commandment to believe in Jesus and love one another.

segments.title: God's Love Makes Us Children
segments.gist: The Father's love calls believers His children, and the world does not know them because it did not know Him; their future likeness to Christ is yet to be revealed.

segments.title: Righteousness vs. Sin
segments.gist: Sin is lawlessness, Christ appeared to take away sins, and whoever abides in Him does not sin; the children of God are manifest by doing righteousness, while the children of the devil practice sin.

segments.title: Love One Another
segments.gist: The message from the beginning is to love one another, unlike Cain who murdered his brother; believers have passed from death to life by loving, and love is shown in deed and truth, not just words.

segments.title: Assurance and Answered Prayer
segments.gist: By loving in truth we assure our hearts before God, receive whatever we ask because we keep His commandments, and know He abides in us by the Spirit He has given us.

4.summary: 1 John 4 warns believers to test the spirits because many false prophets have gone out into the world, and gives the confession that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh as the test of truth. It then grounds love in God's own nature and his sending of his Son, so that whoever loves God must also love his brother, and it closes with the confidence believers have in the day of judgment because perfect love casts out fear.

segments.title: Test the spirits
segments.gist: Believers are told not to trust every spirit but to test them, since many false prophets are in the world; the spirit that confesses Jesus Christ come in the flesh is of God.

segments.title: Love is of God
segments.gist: Love comes from God, and God showed his love by sending his only Son so that we might live through him.

segments.title: Abiding in love
segments.gist: Believers know they abide in God by the Spirit he gave them, and whoever confesses Jesus as the Son of God abides in love.

segments.title: Perfect love casts out fear
segments.gist: Love is made perfect so that believers have boldness in the day of judgment, because perfect love casts out fear.

segments.title: Love your brother
segments.gist: Whoever claims to love God but hates his brother is a liar, and this commandment comes from God: love God and love your brother.

5.summary: 1 John 5 closes the letter by grounding love for God in obedience and faith in Jesus as the Son of God, then presents the testimony of water, blood, and the Spirit. It contrasts the assurance of eternal life with the sin unto death, and ends with confidence that God hears prayer and that the whole world lies in wickedness while believers are kept by the true God.

segments.title: Faith Overcomes the World
segments.gist: Love for God is shown by keeping his commandments, and faith in Jesus as the Son of God gives victory over the world.

segments.title: The Threefold Testimony
segments.gist: The Spirit, water, and blood testify that Jesus is the Son of God, and God's testimony about his Son is greater than human testimony.

segments.title: Assurance and Prayer
segments.gist: Believers can know they have eternal life and be confident that God hears their prayers, including prayers for a brother sinning not unto death.

segments.title: Kept by the True God
segments.gist: Those born of God are kept from the wicked one, the world lies in wickedness, and believers are to keep themselves from idols.

1.summary: The elder writes to an elect lady and her children, expressing love for them in the truth and joy that some walk in truth. He urges them to love one another and to keep the commandment, warns against deceivers who deny Christ's incarnation, and instructs them not to receive false teachers into their homes. He hopes to visit soon and closes with greetings from the children of her elect sister.

segments.title: Greeting to the Elect Lady
segments.gist: The elder greets the elect lady and her children, whom he loves in the truth, and rejoices that some walk in truth.

segments.title: Commandment to Love One Another
segments.gist: He asks that we love one another, defining love as walking according to God's commandments.

segments.title: Warning Against Deceivers
segments.gist: Many deceivers deny that Jesus Christ came in the flesh; those who do not abide in Christ's teaching have no part with God.

segments.title: Do Not Receive False Teachers
segments.gist: If anyone brings a different doctrine, do not receive him or greet him, lest you share in his evil deeds.

segments.title: Closing and Greetings
segments.gist: He hopes to speak face to face and sends greetings from the children of her elect sister.

1.summary: The elder writes to Gaius, commending his hospitality to traveling missionaries and his faithful walk in the truth. He contrasts this with Diotrephes, who rejects the elder's authority and refuses to welcome brethren, and commends Demetrius as a good example.

segments.title: Greeting and prayer for Gaius
segments.gist: The elder greets Gaius, prays for his health and prosperity, and rejoices that he walks in the truth.

segments.title: Commendation for hospitality
segments.gist: The elder praises Gaius for supporting traveling brethren and urges him to continue helping such workers.

segments.title: Warning about Diotrephes
segments.gist: The elder condemns Diotrephes for rejecting his authority and refusing to welcome brethren, and urges Gaius to imitate good, not evil.

segments.title: Closing remarks and greeting
segments.gist: The elder hopes to visit soon and sends greetings from the friends.

1.summary: Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ and brother of James, writes to warn believers about ungodly men who have crept into the church, turning grace into license and denying Christ. He reminds them of past judgments on unbelieving Israel, fallen angels, and Sodom, describes the corrupt character of these intruders, and urges believers to contend for the faith, keep themselves in God's love, and rescue others, closing with a doxology to God.

segments.title: Greeting and Purpose
segments.gist: Jude greets the called, sanctified, and preserved, and says he writes to urge them to contend for the faith once delivered.

segments.title: Examples of Judgment
segments.gist: Jude reminds readers that the Lord destroyed unbelieving Israel, bound fallen angels, and condemned Sodom and Gomorrah for fornication.

segments.title: Description of the Intruders
segments.gist: Jude depicts the dreamers as defiling the flesh, rejecting authority, and following the way of Cain, Balaam, and Korah, described as hidden spots and wandering stars.

segments.title: Enoch's Prophecy
segments.gist: Jude quotes Enoch's prophecy of the Lord's coming with ten thousands of saints to judge and convict the ungodly for their hard speeches.

segments.title: Exhortation to Believers
segments.gist: Jude tells believers to remember the apostles' warnings, build themselves up in faith, keep in God's love, and save others with fear.

segments.title: Doxology
segments.gist: Jude closes with praise to God, who is able to keep believers from falling and present them faultless before his glory.

1.summary: John, exiled on Patmos, addresses seven churches in Asia and recounts a vision of the risen Christ. He describes the command to write what he sees and the majestic appearance of the Son of Man among seven lampstands.

segments.title: Prologue and Blessing
segments.gist: The revelation of Jesus Christ is given to John, who pronounces a blessing on those who read and keep the prophecy.

segments.title: Greeting to the Seven Churches
segments.gist: John greets the seven churches in Asia with grace and peace from the triune God and from Jesus Christ, the faithful witness and ruler of kings.

segments.title: John's Vision on Patmos
segments.gist: John, exiled on Patmos for his testimony, receives a command to write what he sees and send it to the seven churches.

segments.title: The Son of Man Among Lampstands
segments.gist: John sees seven golden lampstands and, among them, one like the Son of Man, whose majestic appearance is described.

segments.title: Christ's Assurance and Command
segments.gist: Jesus identifies Himself as the living one who died and is alive forever, and commands John to write the mystery of the lampstands.

2.summary: Christ dictates messages to four of the seven churches in Asia: Ephesus, commended for labor but warned to repent and recover its first love; Smyrna, encouraged to remain faithful under persecution and poverty; Pergamos, rebuked for tolerating false teaching and idolatry; and Thyatira, praised for works but warned about a prophetess leading believers into immorality.

segments.title: Message to Ephesus
segments.gist: Christ commends Ephesus for labor and patience but calls it to repent for leaving its first love.

segments.title: Message to Smyrna
segments.gist: Christ encourages the persecuted and poor church in Smyrna to be faithful unto death.

segments.title: Message to Pergamos
segments.gist: Christ rebukes Pergamos for holding false doctrine and idolatry, calling it to repent.

segments.title: Message to Thyatira
segments.gist: Christ praises Thyatira's works but warns of judgment for tolerating Jezebel's teaching and immorality.

3.summary: Christ dictates letters to the churches at Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea. Sardis is warned to watch and strengthen what remains; Philadelphia is praised for keeping the word and promised an open door; Laodicea is rebuked as lukewarm and counseled to buy gold tried in the fire. Each letter ends with a promise to the one who overcomes.

segments.title: Letter to Sardis
segments.gist: Christ rebukes Sardis for having a name but being dead, and calls them to watch and repent.

segments.title: Letter to Philadelphia
segments.gist: Christ praises Philadelphia for keeping his word and promises an open door and protection.

segments.title: Letter to Laodicea
segments.gist: Christ rebukes Laodicea as lukewarm and counsels them to buy gold tried in the fire and open the door.

4.summary: John is shown an open door in heaven and is called up to see things to come. He sees a throne set in heaven with one sitting on it, surrounded by a rainbow, twenty-four elders, and four living creatures who worship continually. The chapter focuses on the majesty and worthiness of the one on the throne.

segments.title: Open Door and Invitation
segments.gist: John sees an open door in heaven and hears a voice like a trumpet inviting him to come up and see future events.

segments.title: Description of the Throne
segments.gist: The one on the throne appears like jasper and sardine stone, with a rainbow around the throne and twenty-four elders seated on thrones.

segments.title: Four Living Creatures
segments.gist: Four beasts full of eyes before and behind, each with six wings, rest not day or night saying, 'Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty.'

segments.title: Elders Worship the Creator
segments.gist: The twenty-four elders fall before the throne and cast their crowns, saying, 'Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power.'

5.summary: John sees a book in the right hand of God on the throne, sealed with seven seals, and no one is found worthy to open it, causing John to weep. One of the elders tells him the Lion of Judah has prevailed, and John sees a Lamb standing as if slain, who takes the book. The four living creatures and twenty-four elders fall down in worship, singing a new song, and then a great multitude of angels joins in praise to the Lamb.

segments.title: The Sealed Book and the Weeping
segments.gist: John sees a book with seven seals in God's right hand, and no one is found worthy to open it, so John weeps.

segments.title: The Lamb Takes the Book
segments.gist: An elder says the Lion of Judah has prevailed, and John sees a slain Lamb who takes the book from God's hand.

segments.title: Worship by the Living Creatures and Elders
segments.gist: The four living creatures and twenty-four elders fall before the Lamb, singing a new song of redemption.

segments.title: Angelic Praise and Universal Worship
segments.gist: Many angels join the living creatures and elders in praising the Lamb, and all creation worships God and the Lamb.

6.summary: The Lamb opens the first six seals of the scroll, each accompanied by a vision: four horsemen (white, red, black, pale), martyrs crying for vengeance, and cosmic upheaval as the sixth seal brings terror to kings and people hiding from the wrath of the Lamb.

segments.title: First Seal: White Horse
segments.gist: The Lamb opens the first seal, and a rider on a white horse with a bow and crown goes forth conquering.

segments.title: Second Seal: Red Horse
segments.gist: The second seal brings a rider on a red horse who takes peace from the earth, causing men to kill one another.

segments.title: Third Seal: Black Horse
segments.gist: The third seal reveals a rider on a black horse with balances, and a voice announces prices for wheat and barley while sparing oil and wine.

segments.title: Fourth Seal: Pale Horse
segments.gist: The fourth seal brings a rider on a pale horse named Death, with Hell following, given power over a fourth of the earth to kill by sword, famine, pestilence, and beasts.

segments.title: Fifth Seal: Martyrs' Cry
segments.gist: Under the altar, martyred souls cry for vengeance; they are given white robes and told to rest until more are killed.

segments.title: Sixth Seal: Cosmic Upheaval
segments.gist: The sixth seal causes a great earthquake, the sun turns black, the moon becomes blood, stars fall, and kings and people hide from the wrath of the Lamb.

7.summary: John sees four angels holding back the winds of judgment until the servants of God are sealed on their foreheads, and he hears the number of the sealed—144,000 from the tribes of Israel. Then he sees a great multitude from every nation standing before the throne in white robes, and an elder explains that they have come out of great tribulation and that God will dwell with them and wipe away every tear.

segments.title: Four Angels Restrain Winds
segments.gist: Four angels stand at the earth's corners holding the winds, and another angel commands them not to harm the earth until God's servants are sealed.

segments.title: Sealing of the 144,000
segments.gist: John hears the number of those sealed from the tribes of Israel: 144,000, with 12,000 from each of the listed tribes.

segments.title: Great Multitude Before Throne
segments.gist: John sees an innumerable multitude from all nations in white robes with palms, crying out salvation to God and the Lamb, joined by angels and elders in worship.

segments.title: Elder Explains White Robes
segments.gist: An elder explains that the multitude came out of great tribulation and washed their robes in the Lamb's blood; God will shelter them, and the Lamb will shepherd them and wipe away every tear.

8.summary: When the Lamb opens the seventh seal, silence falls in heaven for half an hour, and seven angels receive trumpets. An angel offers incense with the prayers of the saints, then casts fire to the earth, and the first four trumpets sound, bringing hail and fire, a burning mountain into the sea, a falling star that bitterens the waters, and a darkening of sun, moon, and stars.

segments.title: Seventh Seal and Seven Trumpets
segments.gist: The Lamb opens the seventh seal; silence in heaven for half an hour, and seven angels receive seven trumpets.

segments.title: Angel Offers Incense and Fire
segments.gist: An angel offers incense with the prayers of the saints, fills a censer with fire, and casts it to the earth amid thunderings.

9.summary: The fifth and sixth angels sound their trumpets, releasing a plague of locusts from the bottomless pit that torments those without God's seal, and then four bound angels at the Euphrates who lead an army of 200 million horsemen to kill a third of mankind. Despite these plagues, the surviving people refuse to repent of their idolatry and sins.

segments.title: Fifth Trumpet: Locusts from the Pit
segments.gist: A star falls from heaven, opens the bottomless pit, and releases locusts that torment unsealed people for five months under their king, Abaddon.

segments.title: Sixth Trumpet: Four Angels Released
segments.gist: A voice from the golden altar commands the sixth angel to release four angels bound at the Euphrates, who lead a vast army of horsemen to kill a third of mankind.

segments.title: Unrepentant Idolatry
segments.gist: The surviving people do not repent of their idolatry, murders, sorceries, fornication, or thefts.

10.summary: A mighty angel descends from heaven wrapped in a cloud with a rainbow over his head, holding a little book. He cries out with a lion's roar, and seven thunders utter their voices, which John is told to seal up and not write. The angel swears that at the sounding of the seventh trumpet the mystery of God will be finished, and John is commanded to take the little book and eat it, which is sweet in his mouth but bitter in his belly. He is then told he must prophesy again before many peoples, nations, tongues, and kings.

segments.title: Mighty Angel with Little Book
segments.gist: John sees a mighty angel come down from heaven clothed with a cloud, a rainbow on his head, face as the sun, feet as pillars of fire, holding a little book open, and he sets his right foot on the sea and his left on the earth.

segments.title: Angel Swears Mystery Finished
segments.gist: The angel lifts his hand to heaven and swears by the eternal Creator that there will be no more delay, but in the days of the seventh trumpet the mystery of God will be finished as declared to the prophets.

segments.title: John Eats the Little Book
segments.gist: A voice from heaven tells John to take the little book from the angel; he eats it, it is sweet in his mouth but bitter in his belly, and he is told he must prophesy again before many peoples and kings.

11.summary: John is given a reed to measure the temple and its worshippers, while the outer court is left for the Gentiles to tread for forty-two months. Two witnesses prophesy in sackcloth, are killed by the beast, and after three and a half days are raised and taken up to heaven, followed by an earthquake. The seventh trumpet sounds, proclaiming God's kingdom, and the twenty-four elders worship as the temple in heaven opens and the ark is seen amid lightning and hail.

segments.title: Measure the Temple
segments.gist: John is told to measure the temple and altar and count the worshippers, but to leave the outer court out.

segments.title: Two Witnesses Prophesy
segments.gist: Two witnesses are given power to prophesy for 1,260 days, with fire and plagues as their defense.

segments.title: Witnesses Killed and Displayed
segments.gist: The beast kills the two witnesses, and people celebrate, exchanging gifts because the prophets tormented them.

segments.title: Witnesses Raised and Taken Up
segments.gist: After three and a half days, the witnesses are revived, called up to heaven, and an earthquake destroys part of the city.

segments.title: Seventh Trumpet and Heavenly Worship
segments.gist: The seventh trumpet sounds, proclaiming God's reign; the elders worship, and the heavenly temple opens with lightning and hail.

12.summary: A great sign appears in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun gives birth to a man child while a dragon waits to devour him; the child is caught up to God and the woman flees to the wilderness. Michael and his angels defeat the dragon, who is cast to earth and pursues the woman, but she is given wings and protection, and the dragon turns to make war with the remnant of her seed.

segments.title: The Woman and the Dragon
segments.gist: A woman clothed with the sun cries out in birth pangs while a seven-headed dragon stands ready to devour her child; she brings forth a man child who is caught up to God, and she flees to the wilderness.

segments.title: War in Heaven
segments.gist: Michael and his angels fight the dragon and his angels; the dragon is cast out of heaven with his angels, and a loud voice proclaims salvation and the kingdom of God, while the accuser is overcome by the blood of the Lamb.

segments.title: The Dragon Pursues the Woman
segments.gist: The dragon persecutes the woman, who is given eagle's wings to escape to the wilderness; he spews water after her, but the earth helps her, and he goes to make war with the remnant of her seed who keep God's commandments and hold the testimony of Jesus.

13.summary: The dragon stands on the sand of the sea and brings forth a beast with ten horns and seven heads, which blasphemes God and makes war on the saints for forty-two months. A second beast arises from the earth, performs miracles, and forces all people to worship the first beast and receive its mark. The chapter closes with a call for wisdom to calculate the number of the beast, 666.

segments.title: The Beast from the Sea
segments.gist: John sees a beast rise from the sea with ten horns and seven heads, to whom the dragon gives his power, throne, and authority.

segments.title: The Beast Blasphemes and Makes War
segments.gist: The beast blasphemes God and makes war on the saints, and all who dwell on earth worship him except those written in the Lamb's book of life.

segments.title: The Beast from the Earth
segments.gist: A second beast rises from the earth, performs great miracles, and deceives people into worshipping the first beast.

segments.title: The Mark of the Beast
segments.gist: The second beast forces all people to receive a mark on their right hand or forehead, and John gives the number of the beast as 666.

14.summary: The Lamb stands on Mount Zion with 144,000 sealed followers, and three angels announce judgment on Babylon and the beast's worshippers. A voice from heaven pronounces blessing on those who die in the Lord, and two harvests—grain and grapes—depict the earth's reaping and God's wrath.

segments.title: The Lamb and the 144,000
segments.gist: The Lamb stands on Mount Zion with 144,000 sealed followers who sing a new song before the throne.

segments.title: Three Angels Announce Judgment
segments.gist: Three angels proclaim the eternal gospel, the fall of Babylon, and warning against the beast's mark.

segments.title: Blessing on the Faithful Dead
segments.gist: A voice from heaven declares blessing on those who die in the Lord and rest from their labors.

segments.title: The Harvest of the Earth
segments.gist: One like the Son of Man reaps the earth's harvest with a sharp sickle.

segments.title: The Grapes of Wrath
segments.gist: Another angel gathers grapes and treads them in the winepress of God's wrath, with blood flowing.

15.summary: John sees a great sign in heaven: seven angels with the seven last plagues, and a sea of glass mingled with fire where the victorious stand singing the song of Moses and the Lamb. The temple in heaven opens, and the seven angels come out with golden vials full of the wrath of God, and smoke fills the temple so that no one can enter until the plagues are finished.

segments.title: The Sea of Glass
segments.gist: John sees a sign in heaven: seven angels with the seven last plagues, and a sea of glass where the victorious stand with harps.

segments.title: The Temple Opens
segments.gist: The temple in heaven opens, and the seven angels with the plagues come out clothed in pure white linen with golden girdles.

16.summary: Seven angels pour out the seven vials of God's wrath upon the earth, bringing plagues, darkness, and destruction. The sixth vial dries up the Euphrates and gathers the kings of the earth to Armageddon, while the seventh vial brings voices, thunders, an earthquake, and great hail, with a voice from the throne declaring 'It is done.'

segments.title: First Vial: Sores
segments.gist: The first angel pours his vial on the earth, causing grievous sores on those with the mark of the beast.

segments.title: Second to Fourth Vials
segments.gist: The second vial turns the sea to blood, the third turns rivers and fountains to blood, and the fourth scorches men with fire.

segments.title: Fifth Vial: Darkness
segments.gist: The fifth vial brings darkness over the beast's kingdom, and men blaspheme God because of their pains and sores.

segments.title: Sixth Vial: Euphrates Dried
segments.gist: The sixth vial dries up the Euphrates, and unclean spirits gather the kings of the earth to Armageddon.

segments.title: Seventh Vial: It Is Done
segments.gist: The seventh vial brings voices, thunders, a great earthquake, and hail, and a voice from the throne says, 'It is done.'

17.summary: A woman named Babylon the Great, dressed in purple and scarlet and riding a scarlet beast, is shown to John in the wilderness. She is drunk with the blood of saints, and the beast with seven heads and ten horns, along with the ten kings, turns against her to destroy her. The chapter ends by identifying the woman as the great city that rules over the kings of the earth.

segments.title: The Woman on the Beast
segments.gist: John is carried in the Spirit to see a woman sitting on a scarlet beast, arrayed in purple and gold, with a golden cup and a blasphemous name.

segments.title: The Beast and the Kings
segments.gist: The angel explains the beast's seven heads and ten horns, and the ten kings who give their power to the beast and make war with the Lamb.

segments.title: The Waters and the Woman
segments.gist: The angel identifies the waters as peoples and nations, and the ten horns as those who will hate the harlot, destroy her, and give their kingdom to the beast.

18.summary: An angel announces the fall of Babylon the great, describing her sins and the judgments that come upon her. A voice from heaven calls God's people to flee from her, and kings, merchants, and shipmasters lament her destruction, while heaven and the saints rejoice over her fall.

segments.title: Angel Announces Babylon's Fall
segments.gist: An angel with great authority declares that Babylon the great is fallen and has become a habitation of demons and unclean spirits.

segments.title: Call to Flee Babylon
segments.gist: A voice from heaven commands God's people to come out of Babylon to escape her plagues, for her sins have reached heaven and God remembers her iniquities.

segments.title: Kings and Merchants Lament
segments.gist: The kings of the earth, merchants, and shipmasters mourn and weep over Babylon's destruction, fearing her torment and losing their wealth.

segments.title: Mighty Angel Declares Finality
